title: Squad commander, combat soldier killed in West Bank terror attack, IDF confirms
body: Staff Sergeant Ron Yonatan Roytman, aged 23, from Ashkelon, and Sergeant Yuval Shai Svilem, aged 20, from Hod Hasharon, were killed in a West Bank terror attack on Friday, the military announced. Roytman was a squad commander, and Slivem was a combat soldier in the Ari Battalion (775), Search and Rescue Brigade, according to the IDF. Both fell in combat at the Judea Junction when two terrorists traveling in a car with an M4 machine gun and a pistol opened fire on four soldiers who were on site. The attackers had originally intended to go past the junction and carry out a larger attack on heavily traveled Route 35, IDF sources estimated, before realizing they would not get through.Roytman's uncle, Dani, described him as "always smiling, with a great sense of humor, and a mature young man." "This is a terrible tragedy, and we are still trying to come to terms with it," he said. Speaking from the site of the attack later on Friday, IDF Chief of General Staff Eyal Zamir said, "I extend my deepest condolences to the families of SSGT Ron Yonatan Roytman and SGT Yuval Shai Svilem, who fell while defending Israeli civilians and preventing an even more serious attack. I also wish the wounded a speedy recovery.”Three additional soldiers from the battalion were lightly injured and evacuated to receive medical treatment, the military said, and their families have been notified. Bluth commends IDF bravery, announces 'significant counterterrorism operation'Commander of the Central Command Maj.-Gen. Avi Bluth commended the "bravery of IDF soldiers" at the scene of the attack later on Friday. Commander of the Central Command Maj.-Gen. Avi Bluth at the scene of a West Bank terror attack that killed two soldiers, October 23, 2026.“This morning, a grave terror attack against Israeli civilians was thwarted," he said. "Unfortunately, we paid a heavy price during the encounter, and two combat soldiers fell in battle. I wish to extend my condolences to their families."Bluth called the IDF the "protective shield" of Israeli citizens. Today, IDF soldiers put their lives on the line to prevent a grave terror attack against civilians," he said. He also announced a "significant counterterrorism operation alongside imposing a cordon on the areas of Hebron and Halhul." "We will bring all terrorists to justice and dismantle terrorist infrastructure of all kinds," he pledged. Zamir vowed that the military would "act decisively, pursue and reach all those involved in the attack."“The outcome of the encounter with the terrorist cell is painful," he said, "but the initial inquiry indicates that the troops' actions prevented a serious attack against Israeli civilians. “We are at the highest level of readiness and alert across all fronts," he continued. "Our primary mission is to thwart terrorism and ensure security and stability for Israeli civilians. We will continue to strike and take proactive action wherever necessary, while acting with composure. We will not be drawn into provocations or allow our enemies to influence our actions, particularly as we enter this sensitive week."Zamir held a situational assessment alongside Bluth, Commander of the 98th Division Brig.-Gen. Meni Liberty, Acting Head of the Civil Administration Brig.-Gen. (Res) Ilan Malka, the commander of the Judea Regional Brigade, the commander of the Judea and Samaria Border Police, representatives of the Israel Security Agency (ISA), and additional senior commanders."Based on the situational assessment, we prepared for the possibility of escalation in Judea and Samaria, reinforced our troops, and deployed the 98th Division headquarters and numerous additional troops to the area," he said. "Our troops' operations in the area have prevented and thwarted numerous attacks in recent weeks. We will act decisively and pursue all those involved in the attack. Anyone who attempts to harm us should know that we will reach them."Zamir added that the IDF is at its "highest level of readiness and alert across all fronts.""Our primary mission is to thwart terrorism and ensure security and stability for Israeli civilians. We will continue to strike and take proactive action wherever necessary, while acting with composure. We will not be drawn into provocations or allow our enemies to influence our actions, particularly as we enter this sensitive week. We will also conduct an inquiry into this attack to learn from it and draw lessons for the future," he said.Yonah Jeremy Bob, Tzvi Jasper, and Amichai Stein contributed to this report.

title: Austria foreign ministry expels four Russian diplomats from Vienna over suspected espionage
body: Austria's foreign ministry said on Friday it was expelling four Vienna-based Russian diplomats over "activities incompatible with their diplomatic status," a term usually used for spying."Based on findings by the Austrian security authorities, the Austrian foreign ministry has taken measures against four Russian diplomats in Vienna," it said in a statement, adding that they had been declared personae non gratae and ordered to leave the country.Three of them worked at Russia's embassy to Austria and one at the Russian delegation to the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) on military security and arms control, the ministry said.Russia will respond to the expulsions, Russian news agencies cited a foreign ministry official as saying soon after Friday's announcement, without elaborating.The move brings to 18 the number of Russian diplomats Austria has expelled since 2020. While Austria is a neutral country, politically its governments have sided with Ukraine since Russia launched its all-out invasion in 2022.While Austria does not usually comment on the specifics of such expulsions, during the last round in May, when it expelled three Russian diplomats, it said it was because of an "antenna forest" on the roofs of Russian diplomatic buildings that could be used for spying.Vienna is major diplomatic center for OSCE, UN organizationsVienna is a major diplomatic center, hosting the OSCE and United Nations organizations such as the International Atomic Energy Agency.Larger countries like Russia and the United States often have separate ambassadors to Austria, the OSCE, and UN organizations, each running an embassy or mission.Vienna, which was divided into Allied sectors after World War Two, has long had a reputation as a den of spies. The large diplomatic presence offers the opportunity to station intelligence agents there under cover of diplomatic immunity.

title: Police clarify AFP photographer had no suspected advance knowledge of West Bank terror attack
body: Israel Police officials clarified on Friday that there was no suspicion that a Palestinian photographer working with the French news agency AFP had advance knowledge of a shooting attack near Hebron earlier in the day, Walla learned, following reports that the photographer had prior information about the incident.The clarification came after professional photographs of the terrorists at the scene were published, reportedly taken by the photographer in real time, according to foreign media reports.Meanwhile, the IDF told Walla in response that "The entire incident is under investigation."Following a situational assessment led by Judea and Samaria District Police Commander Maj.-Gen. Moshe Pinchi, the investigation into the attack was assigned to the district's Minorities Division, part of its Central Investigations Unit. Police will also assist the Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency) in investigating the incident.During the assessment, attended by the commander of the Hebron area police and senior district officers, officials presented preliminary findings from the scene and reviewed the actions taken by police officers who assisted IDF troops.Police to increase enforcement against vehicles used in terrorismPinchi instructed investigators to place particular emphasis on the use of a vehicle that had been taken off the road and was used in the attack. Known in Hebrew as a mashtuba, the vehicle was no longer legally permitted to operate on public roads.He stressed the need to combat the use of such vehicles for terrorism and criminal activity throughout the West Bank.Following the attack, district police will step up operations along major roads, including inspections of vehicles and suspects and the seizure of vehicles that have been taken off the road. Operational cooperation with IDF troops in the area will also be increased.Police also addressed the timing of a statement distributed to the media earlier in the day and expressed regret over its release.The statement said that even when an investigation is conducted professionally and independently, authorities must exercise judgment, demonstrate sensitivity to developments on the ground, and understand the public implications of when information is released.Two terrorists killed following shooting attack near HebronA shooting attack took place on Friday morning near the Yehuda Junction, close to Hebron. Following a manhunt, IDF troops killed two terrorists involved in the shooting.Five people were wounded in the attack, including two who were reported to be in critical condition.The terrorists arrived at a scrapyard in the area in a vehicle bearing Israeli license plates and observed the soldiers before carrying out the attack.According to the IDF's preliminary investigation, the attackers were two terrorists from Hebron who arrived carrying a large quantity of ammunition, an M4 rifle, and a handgun.They reached the area of the Yehuda Junction, where an IDF squad-level outpost belonging to the Ari Battalion had been established two months earlier.The deployment was the soldiers' first operational assignment.Following a situational assessment, the soldiers set out to establish a checkpoint and prevent terrorists from accessing Routes 35 or 60 to carry out an attack. Similar precautions were taken at other junctions in the area.

title: IDF, Defense Ministry drafting resolution to protect reservists and families' benefits through 2027
body: The IDF and Defense Ministry are drafting a government resolution to protect the benefits and entitlements of reservists and their families whose service spans 2026 and 2027, following a Walla investigation that exposed gaps in eligibility, Walla learned on Thursday.Alongside the government resolution, the IDF and Defense Ministry are advancing legislation in the Knesset, which they hope to expedite after the elections, during the Knesset's first session.The move follows Walla's revelation that reservists could lose benefits and entitlements despite serving for extended periods. Because their reserve duty is divided between two calendar years, some soldiers fail to meet the minimum number of service days required to qualify for grants and benefits in either year.As a result, a reservist serving nearly 100 consecutive days could fail to meet the eligibility requirements, despite having completed a substantial period of service.The IDF and Defense Ministry are pursuing two parallel approaches: drafting a government resolution to regulate the calculation of reserve duty days and eligibility for benefits, while also advancing legislation in the Knesset.While the legislative process is expected to take longer, the government resolution is intended to allow eligibility issues to be resolved sooner, subject to government approval.Despite these efforts, the wives of reservists have criticized the proposed timetable. They argue that there is no justification for forcing families to wait until the legislative process is completed while soldiers continue accumulating reserve duty days and their families contend with the financial and personal consequences of prolonged service.They are demanding that the IDF and Defense Ministry bridge the eligibility gaps during the interim period, providing assistance similar to that available to families of reservists who accumulate a large number of service days within a single calendar year.Tank battalion reservists face loss of benefitsAt the center of the controversy are soldiers from Battalion 363 of an armored brigade, some of whom have been called up for their fifth or sixth round of reserve duty since the start of the war.As Walla previously reported, the soldiers received orders for 99 days of reserve duty beginning November 22, 2026, with 40 days falling in 2026 and another 59 days in 2027.The division between the two years could affect their eligibility for various benefits, including reimbursements for mental health treatment, grants related to extending maternity leave, student grants, and vacation vouchers.Some benefits require 45 to 50 days of reserve duty per year, while others require 60 days or more.In response, the soldiers' wives sent a letter to IDF Personnel Directorate head Maj.-Gen. Dado Bar Kalifa and Chief Reserve Officer Brig.-Gen. Benny Ben Ari, demanding a solution to prevent their families from losing their entitlements."It is unacceptable that families who continue to shoulder the burden time and again should be harmed because of bureaucracy and dates over which they have no control," the women wrote.They also emphasized that the benefits were not luxuries but assistance intended to help families cope with the price they pay for prolonged reserve duty.IDF promises eligibility will not be affectedIn response to an inquiry from Walla, the IDF Spokesperson's Unit said the issue was known and being addressed, and that reservists' eligibility for benefits would not be harmed because their service was divided between calendar years.The IDF said the military and Defense Ministry were finalizing a draft government resolution concerning benefits for reservists.Once the process is completed, the resolution will be submitted for government approval, after which the IDF will work to implement the entitlements in accordance with the approved framework.Regarding battalions whose reserve duty spans two calendar years, particularly Battalion 363, the IDF clarified that service days completed in 2026 and those scheduled for 2027 would be taken into account under the framework to be established.For a battalion that accumulated 40 days of reserve duty in 2026 and continues serving in 2027, service days will be calculated across both years, allowing eligibility for benefits in 2027 to be assessed based on the total number of service days and the provisions ultimately approved.The IDF also clarified that reservists who have already exercised their eligibility for benefits based on service in 2026 and perform additional reserve duty in 2027 will remain eligible for benefits under the conditions to be established.The proposed framework also addresses eligibility for emotional support and treatment when reserve duty is calculated across calendar years.The IDF is preparing to advance the government resolution to allow reservists to receive their benefits as soon as possible.At the same time, a dedicated briefing will be held for commanders and relevant personnel. The briefing will outline the assistance currently available, clarify the eligibility mechanism, and provide answers to reservists' questions.Despite the IDF's commitment that reservists' rights will not be affected, the government resolution has yet to be approved, and the legislative process remains ahead.Reservists' wives are demanding an interim solution to ensure that their families are not left without the benefits and assistance to which they are entitled.Wives say no solution has been provided for 2026The wives of reservists serving in Battalion 363 responded to the IDF Spokesperson's Unit's statement, arguing that despite the impression that a solution had been found, they had yet to receive an answer concerning their entitlements for 2026.According to the women, the battalion is preparing for its sixth round of reserve duty after hundreds of days of service, during which their husbands are expected to be away from home for 99 consecutive days.The women described the difficulties of raising children, working, and managing their households alone."We are not looking for special treatment, but are asking to receive support and assistance from the IDF and the state in dealing with our situation," they said.According to the women, they even requested that the call-up be brought forward by five days to preserve their entitlements.They are demanding a clear commitment that no benefits or rights belonging to reservists and their families will be affected in either 2026 or 2027.

title: More Ontario police forces pause Crime Stoppers use after cyber breach
body:
Several Ontario police forces are suspending their use of Crime Stoppers as concerns grow over a cybersecurity breach that potentially exposed identifying information included in some anonymous tips.
Police in Halton, Peel and York regions, London, Hamilton and Kingston have announced suspensions after Toronto Crime Stoppers paused its phone, online and app-based tip intake .
“Crime Stoppers’ brand as we know it is essentially dead,” tech analyst Carmi Levy told Global News.
“This is catastrophic. If you called in information on any crime at all, and you assumed that information would be held confidential, that has now been blown up.”
In March, hackers stole data from P3, the tip-management software Toronto Crime Stoppers has used since 2018, Chair Sean Sportun said in a statement Wednesday.
Navigate360, which provides the P3 platform, “repeatedly” assured Toronto Crime Stoppers the system was secure, Sportun said. A month after the attack, the provider said some Canadian data had been stolen but that Toronto submissions were not affected, he added.
Sportun said the organization was told in June tips submitted to the platform between January 2022 and November 2025 were affected. A month later, it pegged the figure at 176,859 tips affected, adding 12,392 of them may contain personal information.
“We never ask for your name, and we don’t want it. But people sometimes include details to explain what they saw,” Sportun said.
“Before a tip goes to investigators, our practice is to remove those details. It has come to light that some of those original tips containing potentially identifying information were stolen from P3.”
In September and October, Navigate360 gave Toronto Crime Stoppers a list of 14,973 names found in the breach. However, Sportun said the list “lacks detail necessary to measure the risk involved” because it did not identify who the names belonged to.
Toronto Crime Stoppers continues to press Navigate360 for details.
Navigate360 did not immediately return Global News’ request for comment.
Sportun added that “anonymously sourced information” reported this week had not been shared with Toronto Crime Stoppers. An investigation by CBC published Wednesday reported that more than 1.5 million Canadian Crime Stoppers tips were affected.
Sean Sparling, a former deputy chief of the Sault Ste. Marie Police Service, told Global News officers across Canada use Crime Stoppers “on a daily basis.”
He said he relied on Crime Stoppers for many of his own investigations.
“Knowing Crime Stoppers and how well it’s organized, how well it works and its importance to the law enforcement community and the safety of our communities, I fully expect they’re going to recover from this,” Sparling said.
Crime Stoppers programs in Peel and Hamilton said in separate statements Thursday they continue to press Navigate360 for more information.
Police forces in Kingston, York and Halton regions said they’re assessing the impact of the breach on their operations.
Toronto police said Wednesday the service is temporarily suspending its use of Crime Stoppers while it assesses new safeguards and other measures.
Each police force said members of the public can submit information through existing police reporting channels, though those methods are not anonymous.
Anyone facing an immediate emergency should call 911.
“Until we have a safer way to protect you, please do not send us tips by phone, online or through the app,” Sportun said.
“Pausing our program means that option isn’t available now, and we did not make this decision lightly. We are pausing because those people deserve a system we can fully stand behind.”

title: 45 seconds of voting in the Lviv Oblast Council sparked a new dispute with Poland: Warsaw says Kyiv promised the UPA year decision will not take effect
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); On 20 October, the Lviv Oblast Council voted to declare 2027 the year of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA), its commander Roman Shukhevych, and Oleh Olzhych, a poet and member of the Organization of Ukrainian Nationalists (OUN). The vote on the UPA and Shukhevych took 45 seconds, Ukrainska Pravda reported , citing the council's online broadcast. It reopened a dispute Kyiv and Warsaw had only just settled. In May, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy gave a special operations unit the honorary name "Heroes of the UPA," and Polish President Karol Nawrocki later stripped him of the Order of the White Eagle in response. Poland is the main hub for Western aid to Ukraine, and that role rests on Polish trust, which every new fight over the two nations' shared past erodes. Since 2022, Poland has also paid for nearly 30,000 Starlink terminals for Ukraine, Rzeczpospolita reported . The sorest point is the UPA. Poland recognizes the UPA's 1943 Volhynia massacres of Poles as genocide, a classification Ukraine disputes, pointing to the broader Polish-Ukrainian conflict of World War II, in which both sides killed civilians. A batch vote, then a "catastrophe" The resolution honoring the UPA commander and his fighters passed with 52 of the 55 deputies who voted, none against. The one on Olzhych passed 49 of 54. A source in the council told Ukrainska Pravda that, after a lunch break and an air raid alert, deputies voted through 30 to 40 minor items one after another without discussion, and the UPA year passed among them. A source in the Office of the President called the situation a " catastrophe ." " Ukraine looks irrational. We only just settled the previous crisis, and now this. Everyone knew it was not allowed, the head of the oblast knew about it personally. But the chase for cheap one-day hype won out. The consequences are already here, and they will only grow ," the source told Ukrainska Pravda. The same source said the decision put the next Polish military aid package at risk. Polish Defense Ministry spokesperson Janusz Sejmej said this was " not true ," and Deputy Defense Minister Cezary Tomczyk said Poland would keep helping Ukraine. Ukraine's Foreign Ministry called the decision counterproductive, noted that oblast deputies are not subordinate to central authorities, and urged Poland to refrain from sharp steps that could hinder the normalization of relations. " Only Russia stands to gain from tension in our relations with Poland ," Iryna Vereshchuk, deputy head of the Office of the President, wrote . Explore further “Heroes of UPA” unit will keep its name, Budanov’s office says despite Polish pressure Warsaw holds Kyiv to its word, but Lviv won't budge Polish Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz called the decision unacceptable. Deputy Foreign Minister Marcin Bosacki told Polsat News on 21 October that it was hard to imagine a worse decision for Polish-Ukrainian relations. He said Zelenskyy's aides had assured Warsaw it would not take effect, and that the resolution had disappeared from the council's website after Poland intervened, which he called promising. Warsaw would hold the Ukrainian authorities to their word, he added. The council itself does not plan to revoke or revise the decision, its representatives told Liga on 21 October. On 23 October, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said he had received a signal from Zelenskyy that he " will in no way support this decision " if further steps depend on him. " Ukraine will simply have very serious problems with integration if it does not also respect our sensitivity ," Tusk said. Poland bans proposal's initiator, who took part in search in Łasków, from Schengen Area Poland has barred Sviatoslav Sheremeta, the Lviv Oblast Council deputy who initiated the decision, from entering the Schengen Area for five years, until 20 October 2031. Polish Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński announced the ban on 21 October at the request of Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski. Sikorski described Sheremeta as a reenactor of the Galizien Waffen-SS division. Sviatoslav Sheremeta (center), initiator of the proposal to declare a Year of the UPA in Lviv Oblast, with his team during a search for the remains of Ukrainians killed in 1944 in the village of Łasków, Lublin Voivodeship, Poland, October 2026. Photo: Ukrainian Institute of National Memory Before the ban was announced, Sheremeta told Zaxid.Net that he had never taken part in military-historical reenactment, and noted that Sikorski's post had at first named a "P. Sheremeta." He found Polish officials' reaction strange, since Lviv and other oblast councils had declared years of the UPA and Shukhevych before. " This is nothing new ," he said. He added that the decision was not aimed at anyone, least of all Poles or Poland, and that a ban would hurt the two countries' cooperation on commemoration. Ukrainians have the right to choose their own heroes and honor them, Sheremeta believes. He suggested that recent statements by Polish officials may be linked to the discovery of Ukrainian civilians killed by Polish armed groups in Łasków in 1944. Human remains, likely belonging to a Ukrainian killed in 1944 in the village of Łasków, Lublin Voivodeship, Poland, October 2026. Photo: Ukrainian Institute of National Memory Sheremeta also directs Dolia, a memorial search center. In October, Dolia carried out a search in Łasków, a village in Poland's Lublin Voivodeship, and found the remains of more than 40 Ukrainians, including women and children. The Ukrainian Institute of National Memory, which commissioned the search, says they were killed by units of the Polish Home Army and the Peasants' Battalions in an attack on 10 March 1944 in which more than 300 people died. Exhumation is planned for spring 2027. The dispute over shared memory has shaped relations between Kyiv and Warsaw for a decade. After local authorities in Hruszowice removed a UPA monument in 2017, Ukraine's Institute of National Memory halted exhumations of Poles in Ukraine. Despite a 2019 pledge by the institute to stop blocking them, the first exhumation took place only in April 2025, in Puzhnyky, after Tusk announced a breakthrough. title: High winds from Subtropical Storm Josephine nix N.S.-P.E.I. ferry crossings
body:
The ferry service that links Nova Scotia with eastern P.E.I. cancelled all crossings this morning because of high winds generated by the remnants of Subtropical Storm Josephine.
Gale warnings remain in effect for the eastern side of the Northumberland Strait.
Environment Canada says winds from the north are gusting at 65 kilometres per hour and are expected to diminish to 45 kilometres per hour by midnight.
Northumberland Ferries says the company will provide an update on the afternoon sailings no later than 1 p.m.
The centre of the storm was more than 400 kilometres southeast of Halifax by 10 a.m. Atlantic time.
On Sable Island, about 300 kilometres southeast of Halifax, Environment Canada recorded a northeast gust reaching 122 kilometres per hour at 7 a.m.

title: UBA commences contempt proceedings against WEMPCO directors over alleged disobedience of court order
body:
The Federal High Court, presided over by Justice Aluko, has granted an application by United Bank for Africa (UBA) Plc for substituted service of Form 49 on directors of Wempco named as alleged contemnors in the case of UBA v. Wempco.
The application forms part of proceedings seeking to determine whether the named individuals disobeyed an order of the court and whether they should be committed to prison for contempt.
The directors named as alleged contemnors are Lewis Shui Ngor Tung, Phillip Shui Chei Tung, M.A. Ola Yusuf, Tung Lawrence Blake, Aali Aare Hadji Tokunbo, Paul Shui Po Tung, Tung Robert, C.L. Ip and Taiwo Alli.
In advancing the application, counsel to UBA argued that service of Form 49 on the alleged contemnors was necessary to enable them to appear before the court and show cause why an order of committal should not be made against them.
He also argued that the Directors of Wempco and some members of staff took illegal steps in an attempt to disobey the Order of Court.
The court’s decision to grant substituted service provides a procedural step towards bringing the notice to the attention of the individuals concerned in accordance with the court’s directions.
Form 49 is a notice requiring an alleged contemnor to show cause why an order of committal to prison should not be made against them for alleged disobedience of a court order.
The Federal High Court had earlier made an Order of Mareva Injunction and appointed a Receiver/Manager over some of the Assets of Wempco following the indebtedness of Wempco to UBA in the sum of N61,445,695,993.76 (Sixty One Billion FourHundred and Forty-Five Million Six Hundred and Ninety Five Thousand, Nine Hundred and Ninety Three Naira, Seventy Six Kobo).

title: Russia may stage sabotage in Eastern Europe, but wants Kyiv blamed, Ukraine’s Intelligence warns
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Ukraine’s Defense Intelligence (HUR) warned that Russia may stage sabotage in Central and Eastern Europe, including the Baltic states, and blame Ukraine for the attacks, in a Telegram post on 23 October. The warning comes three days after The Wall Street Journal reported that US intelligence traces Europe’s sabotage wave to Putin’s personal order. If Russia stages new attacks and pins them on Ukraine, as HUR warns, European anger could turn on Kyiv rather than the Kremlin. This goes further than HUR’s statement on 2 October, which named potential Russian targets in Europe but did not mention a plan to blame Ukraine for attacks. HUR says Moscow wants to discredit Ukraine’s army Russia is stepping up its hybrid strategy to destabilize the European Union, according to HUR. The agency identified two aims: reducing foreign support for Ukraine by discrediting its Defense Forces, and intimidating European governments and societies. The accusations would be spread through Russian propaganda channels and international platforms accessible to the Kremlin. Potential targets include infrastructure and Russian Orthodox Church sites HUR listed several potential targets for Russian provocations: critical infrastructure and areas bordering Russia; the Kaliningrad exclave; areas of EU countries with Russian-speaking populations; Kremlin-controlled sites, including properties belonging to the Russian Orthodox Church network; historical sites associated with Russia. The list reflects HUR’s assessment of potential targets, not confirmation that attacks at these locations are planned. Earlier warnings and reported sabotage On 2 October, HUR said Russian intelligence services had been ordered to increase activity in EU and NATO countries. It named military facilities, critical infrastructure, communications systems, and Starlink ground stations as potential targets and said it had alerted partners. Warnings of Russian false flags on NATO’s eastern flank predate HUR’s. In August, Bloomberg reported , citing an unnamed European intelligence official, that Russia might expand hybrid attacks against Poland and the Baltic states, including false-flag attacks. A European government official separately told the agency that the CIA had warned countries in the region of a possible Russian attack. Lithuania’s military intelligence had warned earlier in August that Moscow might reassemble captured Ukrainian drones for false-flag strikes on critical infrastructure in the Baltic region. Meanwhile, The Wall Street Journal reported on 20 October that US intelligence agencies believe the attempted drone attack on Leipzig-Halle Airport in Germany in early August was among the opening shots of a sabotage campaign ordered by Russian President Vladimir Putin. The Journal cited European officials briefed on the intelligence findings. According to the newspaper, at least three drones carrying military-grade Semtex explosives were involved. One struck an Antonov cargo plane used to transport military aid to Ukraine but failed to explode. Another collided with a different aircraft, while a third detonated near the airport perimeter. German newspaper Welt am Sonntag has since named two suspects , citing German investigation files . Earlier German media reports described the sequence differently. The Journal also reported sabotage attacks on Starlink stations in Poland, Lithuania, and Bulgaria in recent weeks. In August, Slovak authorities said they had foiled a planned arson attack on a Ukrainian drone factory, the Journal reported. Russia denies involvement in sabotage in Europe. Responding to Berlin’s accusations over the Leipzig incident in early September, Putin asked where the evidence was. title: Kwame Sefa Kayi backs Andre Ayew for GFA Presidency
body: Renowned broadcast journalist Kwame Sefa Kayi has thrown his support behind Andre Ayew to become president of the Ghana Football Association (GFA). Sefa Kayi has publicly revealed he would back the former Black Stars captain if he were to run for the presidency seat at the GFA as pressure mounts on the Kurt Okraku-led administration. According to the ace journalist, Ghana football deserves a new direction with regard to leadership as the sport continues to decline. “If he has not declared, then I am declaring for him. If Dede [Ayew] decides to contest, I will support him, and I wish everybody would do the same so that there will be changes,” he said in a light-hearted conversation with Dan Kwaku Yeboah on Peace FM. “For this, I have declared that I am not saying I am biased. For this, I have an interest.” Despite hinting that there have been several calls from ‘football people’ for him to run for the seat, Ayew is yet to publicly declare his intent to run for the position as GFA President.

title: France to field twelve SAMP/T NG air defence units
body: France has ordered four additional SAMP/T NG firing units, taking its total order for the ground-based air and missile defence system to twelve, according to eurosam. The Organisation for Joint Armament Cooperation, known as OCCAR, placed the contract on behalf of France with eurosam, the Franco-Italian grouping formed by MBDA France, MBDA Italy and Thales. The units will be delivered to the French Air and Space Force in a multi-layer configuration combining Aster and MICA VL missiles. The company said: “This order is an additional step towards the renewal of the European Long-Range Air and Missile Defence ground capabilities, following the SAMP/T NG development launched in 2021.” It added: “OCCAR-EA, eurosam and its members, MBDA and Thales will continue to lead the way in state of the art and sovereign air and Missile defence systems for the benefit of European defence. These advanced air defence systems are crucial in the current global context to respond to increasingly challenging threats.” A SAMP/T NG firing unit holds up to forty-eight Aster missiles ready to fire, carried across up to six launcher modules of eight rounds each, alongside a multi-function radar and identification module able to detect and identify targets beyond 350km, and an engagement module. The whole system is mobile and eurosam says it can be operational in under thirty minutes, offering 360-degree coverage and engaging targets beyond 150km. The system is designed around the Aster 30 B1 and the newer Aster B1NT. The B1NT uses a Ka-band seeker and new interception algorithms to give what the company describes as a hit-to-kill capability against short and medium range ballistic missiles, low manoeuvring targets and hypersonic missiles. Britain has a stake in the wider programme, since the United Kingdom is a participant in the FSAF-PAAMS arrangement that OCCAR manages, and the fourteenth amendment to that contract, signed in Paris in January 2024, covered supplementary procurement of equipment allowing Britain to carry out mid-life upgrades to its own Aster missiles. Aster is the weapon carried by the Royal Navy’s Type 45 destroyers as part of the Sea Viper system, which HMS Diamond used against Houthi missiles and drones in the Red Sea. France and Italy have supplied SAMP/T systems to Ukraine, where the type has engaged Russian ballistic missiles. The order lands while Britain has no ground-based long-range air defence system assigned to the defence of the United Kingdom. Luke Pollard, the Minister of State for Defence, confirmed this week that a further £790 million will be invested in homeland integrated air and missile defence, covering enhanced command and control, improved sensing and radar systems, counter-drone capabilities and more effective layered defences. The Defence Committee reported yesterday that anti-strike capabilities for shooting down ballistic, hypersonic and cruise missiles and drones are among the capabilities European NATO members lack in sufficient numbers, and that replacing American military capabilities with European weapons has been costed by the Kiel Institute at an extra €50 billion each year over the next decade. Sky Sabre gives the British Army a medium range ground-based system, currently deployed in Poland and the Falkland Islands. This publication has reported on continuing work on the potential of British destroyers in the ballistic missile defence role and on when those destroyers will receive their missile upgrades . The post France to field twelve SAMP/T NG air defence units first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Ex-Deputy Economy Minister Mikautadze’s Jail Sentence Reduced to 3 Years in Plea Deal
body: The prison term of Georgia’s former First Deputy Economy Minister Romeo Mikautadze, previously sentenced to ten years in prison on abuse of office and money laundering charges, was reduced to three years after reaching a plea agreement, the Prosecutor’s Office of Georgia announced on October 23. According to the agreement, already approved by Tbilisi’s Court of Appeals, Mikautadze was sentenced to three years of imprisonment and a two-year suspended sentence. He was also fined GEL 1 million (USD 385 thousand), banned from holding a public office for three years, and will have multiple assets with a total worth of GEL 5.54 million (USD 2,1 million) confiscated. “Convicted former First Deputy Minister of Economy and Sustainable Development Romeo Mikautadze admitted to the crimes committed, cooperated with the investigation, expressed remorse, compensated for the damages, and requested a plea agreement,” the Prosecutor’s Office said in a statement. The plea agreement follows reports by the prosecutors that Mikautadze testified in the proceedings of jailed former State Security Service Chief Grigol Liluashvili, including by confirming that he facilitated a bribe for Liluashvili. Liluashvili was subsequently sentenced to 13 years in jail after the court found him guilty in four episodes related to alleged bribery. The confiscated assets include an apartment in Madrid, Spain, a country house in Tserovani, Mtskheta Municipality, a 15% stake in Nakhiduri Hydropower Plant company, three luxury vehicles, a Mercedes-Benz G 63 AMG, a Land Rover Range Rover, and a Lexus ES 250, as well as four watches, gold bars, and coins. Mikautadze also fully compensated damage inflicted on Tbilservice Group LLC amounting to GEL 114,658 (USD 44,200), the statement said. Mikautadze was sentenced to ten years in prison on March 16 after a court found him guilty on multiple counts of abuse of office and money laundering. He was arrested on June 21, 2025, accused, among other things, of abusing his official authority for personal gain in the energy sector, including by receiving shares in energy companies and unlawfully arranging the employment of individuals in state or private organizations in exchange for material benefits. The State Security Service said his wealth had increased by “millions” of GEL following his tenure in public office. Mikautadze held several senior government positions between 2017 and 2024, including serving as First Deputy Economy Minister under Levan Davitashvili from 2022 to 2024 and Deputy Economy Minister under Natia Turnava from 2021 to 2022. Mikautadze’s prosecution comes amid Georgian Dream’s broader crackdown on its former associates and senior officials under the declared anti-corruption drive. Among the prominent figures sentenced to prison are former Prime Minister Irakli Garibashvili , former head of Georgia’s State Security Service Grigol Liluashvili , and former Defense Minister Juansher Burchuladze. title: Our best tips for using the iPhone Duo
body:
The Duo is an entirely new kind of iPhone, so it comes with a bit of a learning curve. That’s a wild thing to imagine, since the iPhone has had very few fundamental changes since its inception. But the Duo is built different. If you won the preorder lottery and managed to get your hands on one today, you’ll see what that means. You’ll laugh, you’ll cry, you’ll lose track of the volume buttons as you turn the thing around.
We’ve learned a few tricks over the past week of flipping and folding the Duo as much as we could. Here are our favorite tips and hacks for newly minted Duo owners.
You can set orientation lock on each screen independently
I learned this one when someone on Threads asked about it. Normally, I keep screen orientation lock enabled because I hate it when everything flips unintentionally. But the Duo is built to be used in different orientations. So, throughout my first week with the phone, I just left it unlocked and didn’t think twice about it. But it turns out that if you lock orientation on the outer screen to preserve your sanity, you can leave it unlocked for the inner screen, which you are much more likely to want to rotate. And even with orientation locked on the cover screen, videos will still rotate automatically if you prop it up in tent mode.
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/IMG_3192.png?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/Screenshot-2026-10-22-at-4.50.34-PM.png?quality=90&strip=all]
You can automatically remap the volume buttons to match orientation
The iPhone Duo is a phone that you sometimes end up using upside down. It happened to us a lot; you flip open the screen, and for some reason it feels natural to rotate the screen clockwise. But this orients the volume controls so that the bottom button turns the volume up and the top one turns it down. You can change this setting. Go to Settings > Sounds & Haptics > Fixed Position Volume Controls and toggle it off. Now, when you rotate the inner screen clockwise, you’ll press the top button to increase the volume. Why isn’t this the default behavior? Great question.
You can tap the Wi-Fi status icon to bring up Control Center
Now that Apple has three shortcuts mapped to swipes from the top of the iPhone screen — swipe from the top left for notifications, the middle for Siri, and the top right for Control Center — it’s easy to miss whatever you were going for on the first try. All three shortcuts appear on the Duo as well, but there’s another way to pull up the Control Center — just tap the new, unified Wi-Fi / battery status icon. This will fully reveal the Control Center and expand the status icon into its independent parts. It’s a small thing, but anything that makes the phone easier to use one-handed is welcome in my book.
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/IMG_3189.png?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/IMG_3190.png?quality=90&strip=all]
You should register a bunch of fingers with Touch ID
You might be tempted to speed through setup and just register one finger for Touch ID, but it’s worth doing a few more while you’re at it. Once again, the Duo is a phone you’re going to flip around and reorient by its nature. So while your right-hand thumb makes sense for unlocking the cover screen, it requires an awkward maneuver to use that finger once you’ve opened the phone and rotated it. Your left-hand index finger will be closer to the Touch ID sensor if you rotate the phone counterclockwise the way Apple CEO John Ternus seemingly intended. And it sounds silly, but enrolling your right-hand pinky is a good move for those occasions when you turn the inner screen clockwise.
You can watch a video and open an app below it in portrait orientation, but it’s complicated
The iPhone Duo very much only wants you to multitask with two apps side by side in landscape mode using the inner screen. There’s no window resizing, no additional apps. And if you turn the phone to portrait orientation, one of those apps flies away and you’re down to one. But there is technically a way to get two apps going in this orientation — it’s just wonky.
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/268762_iPhone_Duo_AKrales_0756.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
Start playing a video in an app like Prime Video, then tap the picture-in-picture (PiP) icon to move it to a PiP window. Swipe away to get to the homescreen, open another app, then rotate the phone to portrait. An icon to stack the video on top of the open app will appear in the PiP window.
You might want a PopSocket
I picked up a PopSocket habit while using the Google Pixel 10 Pro Fold, and it makes a tremendous difference when you’re holding such a heavy phone for a long time. It’s especially appealing on the Pro Fold and the Duo because they both have magnets built into the back panel. You can thwack it onto the phone when you want it and just take it off when you don’t. The MagSafe PopSocket I’ve been using with the Duo has been more than strong enough to support the phone’s weight.
If you’re picking up a Duo today and discover a neat trick as you use your new phone, drop it in the comments below. We’re all learning together here.

title: CBN outlines market infrastructure supporting Nigeria–China financial flows at Beijing investor forum
body:
BEIJING — The Central Bank of Nigeria is developing financial-market infrastructure to support transactions between Nigeria and China and strengthen investor confidence in cross-border financial flows, a CBN official told an investor forum in Beijing.
Dr Okey Umeano, Deputy Director, Financial Markets, said the work extended beyond bilateral swap arrangements to the markets and mechanisms banks need to conduct transactions.
He identified fixed-income market development and work on repurchase agreements, or repos, among the measures supporting the financial infrastructure for RMB–naira activity.
“Even with the policies that are in place, we’re also building infrastructure to support what the market is doing,” Umeano said.
His remarks placed market functioning at the centre of the discussion about deeper financial ties. The objective, he explained, was to give both direct and portfolio investors confidence in their ability to move funds through the financial system.
Umeano said the CBN was building the infrastructure around its policy framework to support continuity and provide confidence over longer investment horizons.
Banking executive Kayode Solola of Standard Bank Group reinforced the importance of efficient payment infrastructure. He said reliable connections between financial systems would give businesses greater certainty about how transactions would be processed and completed.
Solola also highlighted the work required to develop financial flows in both directions. Exporters accustomed to earning dollars would need to consider receiving renminbi, helping build the corresponding flows that could support wider RMB use.
He described those discussions as ongoing, indicating that broader adoption would depend on changes in commercial practice alongside improvements in financial infrastructure.
Flutterwave CEO Olugbenga Agboola provided an example of private-sector payment arrangements already serving the corridor. He said the company had developed a model through which Nigerian businesses could pay participating Chinese suppliers in naira.
Agboola linked adoption to trust in the payment provider, confirmation that funds had been paid and greater exchange-rate predictability.
The discussion connected the CBN’s market-development work with the practical requirements of banks, investors and businesses. It also highlighted the distinct roles of policy, financial markets and payment providers in supporting transactions across the corridor.
For Umeano, the longer-term objective was a financial framework that continued to function reliably beyond the officials implementing it, giving investors confidence that the arrangements supporting their transactions would endure.

title: Man United goalie Onana rushed to hospital after car accident in Turkey
body: Manchester United goalkeeper Andre Onana was taken to hospital following a car accident in Turkey after Trabzonspor’s 2-0 victory over Hearts in the Conference League on Thursday. The Cameroon international was reportedly rear-ended by another vehicle, with images from the scene appearing to show debris from the collision. Onana was taken to hospital for medical checks but was later discharged after the results came back clear. Trabzonspor president Ertugrul Dogan confirmed the incident while providing an update on the goalkeeper’s condition. “Andre Onana was involved in a road traffic accident earlier this evening. There are no problems with him, and we wish him a speedy recovery,” as reported by GOAL. Onana has made an impressive start to life at the Turkish club, where he is spending a second spell on loan from Manchester United. The 30-year-old started Thursday’s victory over Hearts, which followed Trabzonspor’s 4-2 win over Finnish side KuPS. The result also marked his fourth clean sheet in five games for the club. Trabzonspor have enjoyed a strong run of form in recent weeks, defeating Turkish heavyweights Besiktas and Galatasaray by an aggregate score of 6-0. The team will return to league action against Rizespor next Monday, giving Onana time to rest and recover before the fixture, depending on his condition following the accident. Onana joined Manchester United from Inter Milan in the summer of 2023 for £43.8 million but struggled to establish himself consistently during his time at Old Trafford. His position at the club came under pressure following the arrival of goalkeeper Senne Lammens, prompting his temporary move to Trabzonspor. During his previous spell at Manchester United, Onana made 42 appearances and kept six clean sheets. However, his return to Trabzonspor has offered signs of improvement, with the goalkeeper already approaching that clean-sheet tally as his side continues its positive start to the season.
