title: Civilian cargo ship sinks off coast of Romania after Russian drone strike, authorities say
body:
Editor's note: An earlier version of this article said the ship was sailing under the flag of the Cayman Islands. This information has since been corrected
A civilian cargo ship sank after being struck by a Russian drone near Romania's Black Sea coast on Oct. 23, Romanian authorities reported.
The attack is the latest in a series of brazen Russian strikes on civilian shipping in the Black Sea, part of a broader escalation in Russia's economic warfare against Ukraine this year.
The ship, Khoryv, was sailing from Turkey under the flag of the Comoros and was crewed by Ukrainian and Azerbaijani nationals.
According to Romanian President Nicusor Dan, one person was confirmed dead and three others were missing from the 14-member crew.
Ukraine's Foreign Ministry later confirmed that a Ukrainian crew member on board the Khoryv was killed. Four other Ukrainian nationals, including the ship's captain, were hospitalized, while two Ukrainian crew members did not require medical assistance.
The ministry said the vessel had sunk near the Romanian city of Constanta with 14 crew members on board. According to preliminary information, a drone strike may have caused the sinking.
Ukraine's Embassy in Romania is working to establish the circumstances of the incident, as well as the whereabouts and condition of the rescued Ukrainian nationals, while remaining in contact with Romanian authorities, the ministry said.
"This attack is a new example of the tragic consequences of Russia’s aggression against Ukraine," Dan wrote on social media .
"It is time for Russia to take the peace initiatives proposed by the United States and Europe seriously, accept the ceasefire proposals and end the war."
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen condemned the attack , describing it as another Russian escalation in the Black Sea.
"These reckless attacks target innocent lives and openly defy international law," von der Leyen wrote on X.
Romania's Interior Ministry later confirmed that nine crew members had been rescued, publishing a video showing the keel of the overturned ship barely protruding above the water's surface.
In response to a series of attacks on civilian shipping, NATO plans to increase its military presence in the Black Sea by deploying additional maritime patrol aircraft, radar systems, and drones.
The announcement came after NATO's main decision-making body, the North Atlantic Council, met at the alliance's headquarters in Brussels on Oct. 20 to discuss security in the Black Sea.

title: TUC not part of FG talks, issued no ultimatum, NLC clarifies
body: By Victor Ahiuma-Young The Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, has clarified that the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria, TUC, neither issued an ultimatum to the Federal Government nor participated in the dialogue between the government and the NLC held on October 22, 2026. The clarification follows media reports that mentioned the TUC in connection with the ultimatum and the meeting, prompting the NLC to set the record straight and absolve the sister labour centre of any involvement in the specific engagement. In a statement signed by its Acting General Secretary, Comrade Benson Upah, the NLC said the TUC’s name was erroneously included in some newspaper reports, while acknowledging that a greater number of publications correctly attributed the statement to the NLC alone. The statement reads: “The Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) wishes to clarify that the Trade Union Congress (TUC) did not issue an ultimatum to the government and was not part of the dialogue between the NLC and Federal Government yesterday, 22nd October 2026 even as the TUC side of Joint Health Workers Union of Nigeria, JOHESU and Joint Public Service Negotiating Council, JPSNC were represented at the dialogue. “TUC’s name featured in error in a paper or two but we note that a greater number of the papers appropriately attributed the statement to NLC only. “This is to categorically state that only the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) was present at the meeting. “The TUC is completely exonerated from the purports of this specific dialogue. We urge the public and media to take note of this correction, please.” The post TUC not part of FG talks, issued no ultimatum, NLC clarifies appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Seven killed as gunmen open fire near Christian church in Jordan — TV
body:
BEIRUT, October 23. /TASS/. At least seven people were killed in a terrorist attack on a funeral procession near a Christian church in the Jordanian city of Al-Karak, a source in the kingdom’s security service told Al Mamlaka television channel.
"Gunmen opened fire from a vehicle at people gathered near the church. Seven people were killed and around 10 were injured, some of them in critical condition," the source told the television channel.
Two masked gunmen were shooting at the crowd for several minutes and then fled the scene, the television channel cited witnesses. They did not get inside the church where more than 150 people has gathered.
Security forces have blocked all entry roads to Al-Karak and are combing city quarters.

title: FG Targets March 2027 for Completion of 132/33kV Substation in Katsina
body: • Unveils 132/33kV power transformers The Federal Government has fixed March 2027 for the completion of a new 132/33kV transmission substation in Mashi Local Government Area of Katsina State, as part of efforts to strengthen electricity supply and boost economic activities across the state. The Minister of Power, Mr. Joseph Olasunkanmi Tegbe, disclosed this on Friday during the groundbreaking ceremony for the project in Garo, Mashi LGA, noting that compensation for affected properties had been fully paid before the commencement of construction. The project, being executed through the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN), comprises 2x60MVA transformers, providing a combined transmission capacity of 120MVA, equivalent to 96 megawatts. The minister also unveiled 2×60MVA, 132/33kV power transformers in Kankia Local Government Area of the state, as part of efforts to strengthen electricity infrastructure in the state. He also inspected the 2x100MVA, 132/33kV GIS transmission substation project at Katsina 330/132/33kV substation alongside Governor Dikko Umaru Radda and other top federal and state governments officials. Speaking at the groundbreaking ceremony in Garo, Tegbe said the Mashi substation would enhance the transmission network’s capacity to deliver available electricity to Katsina and its environs upon completion. “The Federal Government, through the Transmission Company of Nigeria, is providing this new 2×60MVA, 132/33kV transmission substation. “On completion, it will provide 120MVA of transmission capacity, equivalent to 96 megawatts. This will strengthen the network’s ability to deliver available electricity within Katsina and its environs and support productive activity and household welfare,” he said. Tegbe urged TCN, the contractor and supervising engineers to ensure strict adherence to the March 2027 completion deadline, while maintaining high standards of workmanship and safety throughout the construction process. He stressed that every phase of the project, including equipment manufacturing, civil works, installation and testing, must comply with the required technical standards to prevent defects and ensure the facility’s long-term reliability. The minister described the substation as part of the Federal Government’s commitment to providing critical infrastructure to support enterprise, employment generation and economic prosperity. He commended President Bola Tinubu for supporting investments in the power sector, adding that dependable infrastructure was essential to achieving the country’s economic development objectives. He called on residents of Mashi to cooperate with the construction team, protect the facility and report suspicious activities around the project site to safeguard the infrastructure and facilitate its timely completion. He urged all institutions involved to ensure that the groundbreaking ceremony translated into measurable progress, while keeping the host community informed throughout the construction and inauguration process. In his remarks, Governor Radda commended President Tinubu for approving three transmission substation projects in the state to strengthen electricity transmission and supply to the growing population. Radda described the projects as significant investments in the state’s economic development and expressed appreciation to the president for extending critical infrastructure to the state. He said the Federal Government’s intervention demonstrated its commitment to improving electricity infrastructure and supporting economic growth.

title: World’s largest passenger jet cannot land in Moscow due to restrictions
body:
MOSCOW, October 23. /TASS/. The world's largest passenger jet A380 en route from Dubai to Moscow cannot land in Moscow's Domodedovo Airport due to safety restrictions, a source in the air industry told TASS.
"The airplane is now circling in the Penza Region, waiting for the resumption of Moscow airports' operations or the decision to fly to an alternate airfield," the source said. The airplane flight data are also confirmed by air traffic online monitoring services.
Moscow airports are closed for inbound and outbound flights, the Russian Federal Air Transport Service, Rosaviatsiya, said earlier.

title: Bawumia engages Pharmaceutical Society on making Ghana West Africa’s pharmaceutical hub
body: Former Vice President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia has held discussions with the leadership of the Pharmaceutical Society of Ghana (PSGH) on strategies to position Ghana as a leading pharmaceutical production hub in West Africa and across the continent. The meeting, held at the PSG House in Accra, focused on boosting local production of medicines, improving regulatory efficiency and strengthening public-private partnerships to expand the country’s pharmaceutical sector. Dr Bawumia said the engagement formed part of his ongoing stakeholder consultations aimed at shaping policies to drive Ghana’s sustainable development. In a post on Friday, October 23, he said discussions also covered workforce entry and conditions of service for pharmacists, as part of efforts to address issues affecting the profession and support the growth of the pharmaceutical industry. He expressed appreciation to the current leadership, past presidents and executives of the society for their contributions to the discussions and their commitment to healthcare development. Dr Bawumia said strengthening domestic pharmaceutical production would contribute to building a resilient and self-reliant economy, while creating jobs and safeguarding the health of Ghanaians. The engagement comes amid broader efforts to strengthen Ghana’s domestic productive capacity and improve the country’s position in the regional pharmaceutical market.

title: INEC unveils plans to improve safety, participation of PWDs during elections
body:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has outlined plans to improve the safety, accessibility and participation of persons with disabilities (PWDs) during the 2027 general elections.
The plans include adopting disability-inclusive election security protocols, training security personnel on disability rights, improving coordination among election security agencies and establishing accessible channels for reporting incidents involving voters with disabilities.
INEC Chairman, Joash Amupitan, announced the priorities at an event on disability-inclusive election security and protection protocols organised by The All-Rights Foundation (TAF Africa) on Friday.
Mr Amupitan said election credibility goes beyond counting votes; it means ensuring every eligible citizen can vote freely, safely, and without discrimination.
“An election cannot be considered inclusive if persons with disabilities or other vulnerable groups face intimidation, insecurity or other barriers to exercising their rights,” he said.
Mr Amupitan identified five priorities for the 2027 elections, including adopting clear, disability-inclusive election security protocols aligned with INEC’s 2026 regulations and guidelines.
He said the commission would also pursue targeted training for police officers on disability rights and accessible communication to enable security personnel to respond appropriately to the needs of voters with different disabilities.
Other priorities include effective coordination among INEC, the police, and other security agencies; accessible reporting mechanisms and prompt responses to incidents involving persons with disabilities; and sustained engagement with organisations of persons with disabilities.
Mr Amupitan said disability inclusion must be integrated into election security planning, personnel training, deployment and incident response through the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES).
He also announced that INEC would soon convene another security summit involving the Inspector-General of Police, the National Security Adviser, the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps and other paramilitary agencies.
According to him, security personnel must understand the specific needs of voters with different disabilities. People with hearing impairments may require visual accommodation, while those with visual impairments may need verbal guidance. Voters with limited mobility also require accessible polling units.
He stressed that assistance must preserve voters with disabilities’ independence and privacy.
“We must not sabotage the voters’ independence or privacy. It must be respectful and proportionate assistance,” he said.
The INEC chairman said the commission had 232,000 registered voters with disabilities, representing 0.23 per cent of the voter register.
He said the registered voters fell into 10 disability categories, described the figure as too low, and said INEC was working to improve registration through online voter registration.
“When I took over, one of my primary conditions was to have online registration,” he said.
Mr Amupitan cited the 1999 Constitution, the Electoral Act, the Discrimination Against Persons with Disabilities (Prohibition) Act and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities as legal frameworks supporting inclusive elections.
However, he said implementing these protections remained a challenge.
He directed INEC’s Director of Gender and Inclusivity to make copies of the commission’s Regulations and Guidelines for the Conduct of Elections 2026 available, noting that clauses 19, 21, 27 and 28 provide for priority access and assistance for persons with disabilities.
“The duty to protect voters extends well beyond election day. It includes voter registration, campaigns, rallies, polling stations and periods after the election,” he said.
“Our duty is to ensure that no citizen is prevented from exercising their right to vote through avoidable circumstances such as insecurity, discrimination or institutional neglect.”
Mr Amupitan also commended TAF Africa and the European Union for their efforts to advance electoral participation among persons with disabilities and internally displaced persons.

title: One killed, four injured in Paris shooting as France braces for another round of violent protests
body: A gunman killed one person and wounded five others, including a 12-year-old girl, in a shooting in a Paris suburb that French President Emmanuel Macron described as a "terrorist and racist" attack."What happened today is, I am telling you, a turning point, because it is the first time we have had a terrorist act that was planned to kill our compatriots, our children, based on the color of their skin or their religion," Macron told reporters.Macron later retracted his statement after criticism of his claim that this was France's first terrorist attack based on race or religion. "Our country has experienced attacks in recent years that have struck Christians because they were Christians and Jews because they were Jews," Macron acknowledged in a post on X/Twitter.Ce soir, la Nation est en deuil après l'attentat terroriste qui a frappé Trappes et La Verrière. Nous sommes confrontés à un acte d'une gravité extrême et qui par son caractère raciste avéré marque un tournant pour notre pays. Monsieur Pengo Bossio Wangi a perdu la vie. Cinq autres personnes sont en urgence absolue, dont une petite fille qui lutte pour survivre. Nous pensons à chacune et chacun d'entre eux, à leurs proches, à leurs familles. Nous leur devons le soutien, l'affection et la solidarité de toute la Nation. Ce qui s'est passé aujourd'hui nous oblige. J'ai redit ce soir le soutien de la Nation à toutes les victimes et à leurs familles. J'ai également rappelé notre détermination absolue à poursuivre le combat contre le racisme, sous toutes ses formes. Je veux aussi rappeler une vérité essentielle et éviter toute polémique : notre pays a connu, ces dernières années, des attentats qui ont frappé des chrétiens parce qu'ils étaient chrétiens et des juifs parce qu'ils étaient juifs. Aucune de ces victimes ne doit être oubliée. Aucune douleur ne doit être hiérarchisée. Et je veux que rien, ce soir, ne vienne ajouter à la peine des familles, à la tristesse du pays et au recueillement de la nation. Notre combat est celui de l'universalisme, celui de la République, celui de notre unité et de notre cohésion. Il n'y a rien de plus important ce soir. Une France unie qui pleure ses enfants, qui accompagne les victimes et leurs proches. Une France qui combat le racisme, l'antisémitisme et toutes les formes de haine et de persécution fondées sur la religion ou la couleur de peau. C'est cette France que nous devons défendre. C'est pour son unité, pour la sécurité de chacune et de chacun, et pour les valeurs qui nous rassemblent que je me battrai jusqu'au bout.— Emmanuel Macron (@EmmanuelMacron) October 23, 2026"None of these victims deserve to be forgotten. No pain deserves to be graded. And I want nothing, tonight, to add to the pain of the families, to the sadness of the country, and to the concentration of the nation's prayer."A united France that mourns its children, that stands by the victims and their loved ones. A France that combats racism, antisemitism, and all forms of hatred and persecution based on religion or skin color. This is the France we must defend," Macron said.The shooting happened earlier on Friday when the gunman fired an automatic weapon at a petrol station, a medical center and a children's playground in Trappes, on the Paris outskirts.Officials said a 39-year-old suspect, whom they named as Kevin T, had been arrested. His family surname was not given, as is common practice in such criminal inquiries in France.The anti-terrorism prosecutor's office has taken over the caseThe shooting comes at a moment of particular tension in France, after nationwide protests turned violent last Saturday and before further demonstrations this coming weekend.Some far-right politicians have blamed immigration for looting and vandalism in a number of French cities on October 17.Macron said the gunman had deliberately chosen not to fire upon some people due to their skin color and appearance.The anti-terrorism prosecutor's office, known as PNAT, formally opened an investigation into the shooting.PNAT can take over any criminal investigation it believes meets the criteria for terrorism, including violence inspired by far-right ideas. Terrorism sentences are tougher, and counter-terrorism forces have greater investigative powers.Broadcaster BFM said the wounded girl had been hit eight times and was in serious condition.Mayor calls for collective condemnationTrappes Mayor Ali Rabeh, whose parents came from Morocco, said the shooting was "racist" and "Islamophobic.""The people targeted today could just as easily have been my mother, my brothers or my sisters-in-law," said Rabeh.Rabeh called for a collective condemnation of rhetoric that "ideologically arms those capable of carrying out such acts."Nicolas Dainville, the mayor of nearby La Verriere, said the suspect was "of a European type." Rabeh said two of the victims were of African and North African origin, respectively, and did not provide details about the backgrounds of the other victims.Video images showed the suspect's car riddled with bullets.

title: Dambazau, Business Leaders Put Payments, Export Finance, Investment At Centre of CBN Roundtable
body: Nigeria’s Ambassador to China, Lt Gen Abdulrahman Bello Dambazau (rtd), has outlined practical financial priorities for deeper bilateral ties, including reliable cross-border payments, export finance and long-term investment. Speaking at the Central Bank of Nigeria’s ‘Strengthening the Nigeria–China Financial Corridor’ roundtable in Beijing, Dambazau said financial cooperation should deliver measurable benefits for businesses and citizens in both countries. “For businesses, financial cooperation has a practical meaning. It means paying a supplier reliably, receiving export earnings promptly, securing affordable working capital, and obtaining long-term finance for a viable investment,” he said. “Our task is to make these transactions easier, more transparent and more accessible.” The Ambassador’s contribution opened a discussion in which Nigerian and Chinese businesses connected the financial corridor’s wider ambitions with their experience of settlement, investment and access to financial services. Dambazau emphasised the importance of clear information on payment channels, transaction costs and settlement times. Stronger commercial-bank relationships, supported by effective engagement between regulators, could help resolve operational difficulties and reduce uncertainty, he said. “Payment delay can become a shipment delay, a production interruption or a lost business opportunity,” he said. On local-currency settlement, he said the bilateral swap framework’s value to businesses depended on access, adequate liquidity, competitive pricing and a clear understanding of how the arrangements worked. Settlement in local currencies should remain a commercial choice supported by transparent terms and sound risk management. He also called for financial cooperation that supported Nigerian production and exports. “Export finance, letters of credit, credit insurance, and working capital facilities can help businesses turn market opportunities into completed transactions,” he said. Dambazau advocated stronger financial flows in both directions, connecting finance with the practical requirements of supplying the Chinese market. He also highlighted patient capital for productive investment and safeguards that protected legitimate commerce while allowing smaller businesses to participate. The embassy, he said, stood ready to facilitate connections and bring commercial concerns to the appropriate institutions. CIG Motors Chairman Diana Chen reinforced the importance of predictability from the perspective of a Chinese business with an established operating presence in Nigeria. She described the company’s factories and employment of Nigerian engineers, technicians and managers as evidence of a relationship extending beyond imports into production and skills development. “What we ask for today is not grand architecture. It is continuity, predictability, and the right confidence that when we commit capital, we will one day be able to bring our returns home in good order,” she said. Chen said the financial system should keep pace with Chinese businesses’ evolution in Nigeria, including their need for patient capital alongside short-term trade finance. Nigerian businessman, Festus Mbisiogu, welcomed the opportunity for operators in China to explain payment difficulties directly to the CBN leadership. He described uncertainty over settlement routes, suppliers requesting RMB payments and transactions delayed within banking channels. Flutterwave CEO, Olugbenga Agboola, credited improvements in Nigeria’s compliance infrastructure and international credibility with strengthening the environment in which Nigerian financial businesses engaged foreign counterparts. He commended CBN Governor Olayemi Cardoso and his team for implementing their policy direction. Contributions from Fincra and XTransfer focused on bringing more transactions into formal, visible channels and using payment infrastructure to serve businesses at scale. XTransfer’s representative also highlighted smaller merchants’ exposure to fraud and their limited capacity to manage complex payment-verification requirements. A Nigerian student extended the discussion beyond commerce, describing difficulties with tuition payments and transfers between Nigeria and China, including high charges and exposure to fraudulent intermediaries. Responding to the contributions, Cardoso said the delegation had come to understand and address the financial difficulties businesses and Nigerians in China encountered. He described the CBN’s role as catalytic, with banks central to delivering many of the services discussed, and committed the institution to following through on the issues raised. “We want to ensure that whatever it is we discuss, we are able to ensure that we can execute on it,” Cardoso said. The governor reaffirmed the bank’s commitment to consistent policy, transparency and a functioning foreign-exchange market. He also acknowledged the need for clearer communication about instruments such as the bilateral swap. Cardoso said the CBN had taken detailed notes of stakeholders’ contributions, including concerns about business payments and students’ transfers, to inform its work on strengthening financial connectivity between the two economies.

title: Tsunami warning issued for Sicily following tremors — newspaper
body:
ROME, October 23. /TASS/. An orange tsunami alert was declared for Sicily on Friday after a series of undersea tremors struck the Italian island, the most powerful reaching a magnitude of 5.5, according to an update from the National Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology.
Several schools in the Sicilian capital of Palermo were ordered to evacuate as a precaution, Il Messaggero reported. Residential areas on the Aeolian Islands reportedly lie closest to the epicenter. While no injuries or damage have been reported, rescue services and the Civil Protection Department are reassessing the situation. Residents in coastal areas of Palermo, Trapani and Messina have been advised to stay indoors amid the tsunami warning.

title: FSB Orders Critical Infrastructure Operators to Shutter Websites Over PHP Bug – RBC
body:
The FSB security service’s cybersecurity division has told Russia’s critical infrastructure operators to temporarily take down websites if they cannot immediately patch critical flaws in the PHP programming language that were uncovered using AI, the RBC outlet reported Thursday.
Operators were ordered to apply emergency software patches, run full antivirus scans and report any suspicious activity.
“Consider temporarily restricting external access to vulnerable web servers up to and including shutting them down,” the security alert reportedly stated.
The FSB order applies to communication networks and information systems across government agencies, as well as financial, energy, transportation, medical and other companies.
Its directive mirrors that of the U.S. National Security Agency, as well as authorities from the EU and China, after PHP programmers released a fix for the critical vulnerability on Wednesday.
The flaws had been reported privately to PHP’s developers and kept confidential while a fix was prepared.
Global firms and governments rushed on Thursday to patch PHP flaws as cloud firms reported a surge of hacking attempts after the vulnerabilities were disclosed.
As companies and governments deployed patches and suspended websites as a precaution, hacking attempts surged into the millions, according to cloud services firm Cloudflare and Amazon.
Tech experts warned in comments to RBC that “tens or hundreds of thousands” of Russian websites remain vulnerable to cyberattacks due to widespread reliance on PHP across the country.
More than 90% of Russian-language websites and almost 70% of the web globally run on PHP, according to the W3Techs platform.

These actions are direct attempts to silence independent journalism in Russia. The authorities claim our work "discredits the decisions of the Russian leadership." We see things differently: we strive to provide accurate, unbiased reporting on Russia.

title: Nigeria vs North Korea: Five players who could decide World Cup showdown
body:
Nigeria’s Flamingos face a major test of their ambitions at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup when they meet defending champions North Korea in their final Group B fixture on Friday, with a place in the knockout stage at stake.
Head coach Akeem Busari’s side must find a way to contain an opponent that has scored 12 goals in its opening two matches, dismantling Puerto Rico 6-0 before producing an even more emphatic 6-1 victory over Poland.
Nigeria, meanwhile, bounced back from their opening 2-1 defeat to Poland with a 2-0 win over Puerto Rico, courtesy of goals from Oluwakemi Adegbuyi and Precious Oscar. That victory has kept the Flamingos in contention, but they will need another strong performance to overcome one of the tournament’s most dangerous teams.
With North Korea’s attacking firepower posing a serious threat, Nigeria will have to be disciplined at the back while making their own opportunities count. Individual brilliance could prove decisive, making the contributions of these five players particularly important when the teams meet at the Mohammed VI Football Complex in Rabat.
If Nigeria need a reminder of the threat posed by North Korea’s attack, Yu Jong-hyang’s performances in the opening two fixtures provide it.
Like Kim, Yu has scored four goals, registering two against Puerto Rico and another brace against Poland. Her ability to find the net in consecutive matches makes her one of the leading attacking threats the Flamingos must contain.
Yu also enters the contest with an impressive reputation from the previous edition of the competition, where she won the Golden Ball and Golden Boot at the 2025 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup.
That pedigree, combined with her current form, makes her a player Nigeria cannot afford to overlook. She has demonstrated the ability to convert opportunities and influence matches, while her movement and composure in front of goal make her particularly dangerous when opponents allow her time to turn or attack space.
For Busari’s side, the challenge will be to deny Yu the service she needs and ensure that North Korea’s attacking players do not repeatedly find themselves in one-on-one situations around the Nigerian penalty area.
With four goals already to her name, Yu will be eager to continue her scoring run, and Nigeria’s defensive organisation could determine how much influence she has on the contest.
For Nigeria, Oluwakemi Adegbuyi is one of the players who could make a significant difference as the Flamingos attempt to upset the defending champions and strengthen their chances of reaching the knockout stage.
The Robo Queens forward provided an important response to Nigeria’s opening defeat to Poland, scoring the first goal in the 2-0 victory over Puerto Rico on 20 October.
Adegbuyi struck in the 25th minute to give the Flamingos the lead before Precious Oscar sealed the result in stoppage time. Her performance earned her the Player of the Match award, recognising her contribution to a victory that restored confidence within the Nigerian camp.
Her goal was important not only because it put Nigeria ahead but also because it helped ease the pressure on a team that needed a positive result to keep its qualification hopes alive.
Against North Korea, Adegbuyi’s ability to take chances will be particularly important. The Asian champions have conceded just once in their first two matches, meaning Nigeria may not enjoy the same number of clear opportunities they had against Puerto Rico.
The Flamingos will need their forwards to be sharp when openings emerge, and Adegbuyi could be central to that effort. Her confidence after scoring in the previous match should provide encouragement as Nigeria prepare for a much more demanding defensive challenge.
If the Nigerian attack can find ways to exploit spaces behind North Korea’s defence, Adegbuyi’s movement and finishing could offer Busari’s side a route to goal.
With four goals in the team’s opening two matches, Kim Won-sim has emerged as one of North Korea’s most dangerous attacking weapons at the tournament.
The forward announced herself with a brace in the 6-0 demolition of Puerto Rico before repeating the feat against Poland, underlining her ability to deliver consistently against different opponents.
Her finishing has been a major part of North Korea’s impressive start, and the Flamingos cannot afford to give her the freedom to operate in dangerous areas around the penalty box.
Kim’s movement and eye for goal will demand constant attention from Nigeria’s defenders, who must remain compact and prevent the forward from receiving possession in positions where she can punish even the smallest defensive lapse.
For the Flamingos, limiting Kim’s influence could be one of the most important assignments of the evening. Allowing her to settle into the game would give North Korea another avenue to extend their remarkable scoring run.
Precious Oscar completes the list after delivering a crucial contribution off the bench in Nigeria’s victory over Puerto Rico.
The forward scored the Flamingos’ second goal in stoppage time, putting the result beyond doubt and ensuring Nigeria collected their first three points of the tournament.
Her late strike demonstrated the importance of maintaining attacking intensity until the final whistle, particularly in a competition where goal difference and qualification permutations could become decisive.
Oscar’s contribution also gives Nigeria another attacking option to consider against North Korea. Whether she starts or is introduced during the match, her ability to make an impact in the final third could be valuable in a fixture where the Flamingos may need to take advantage of limited opportunities.
The challenge for Nigeria will be to create enough openings to bring their attacking players into dangerous positions. Against a North Korean side that has scored freely and conceded only once, the Flamingos cannot afford to waste chances.
Oscar will be hoping to build on her goal against Puerto Rico and provide another important contribution as Nigeria pursue a place in the knockout rounds.
Her previous impact also offers Busari an option if the game requires fresh attacking energy in the second half, particularly if Nigeria are chasing a goal or need to change the rhythm of the contest.
While much of the attention has centred on Kim and Yu, Ri Ye-rim is another North Korean attacker who deserves close monitoring after her performances in the group stage.
Ri scored in the 6-0 victory over Puerto Rico and found the net again against Poland, demonstrating that North Korea’s threat extends well beyond their two leading scorers.
Her contribution is particularly significant for Nigeria because it highlights the difficulty of preparing to face an attack with several players capable of delivering goals. Concentrating exclusively on Kim and Yu could leave other members of the North Korean forward line with the space to make the difference.
Ri’s involvement in the scoring against both opponents also reflects the attacking depth that has helped the defending champions record 12 goals in two games.
Nigeria’s defenders and midfielders must therefore remain alert to runners arriving from different areas of the pitch rather than allowing their attention to become fixed on the most prominent names.
If Ri receives the freedom to attack the penalty area, she could become another major problem for the Flamingos. Her performances so far make her a genuine threat as North Korea look to complete the group stage with another victory.
Friday’s meeting is more than just another group-stage fixture for Nigeria. With qualification at stake, the Flamingos must produce a disciplined performance against a North Korean side that has looked formidable in front of goal.
Kim Won-sim and Yu Jong-hyang headline the defending champions’ attacking threat, while Ri Ye-rim’s contribution underlines the depth of their forward line. Nigeria will need to be alert across the pitch to prevent North Korea from dictating the contest.
At the other end, Adegbuyi and Oscar have already shown that they can make decisive contributions, and the Flamingos will need their attacking players to deliver again if they are to challenge the champions.
Busari’s team have demonstrated resilience by recovering from their defeat to Poland, but the next step is to prove they can compete with the strongest sides in the tournament.
For Nigeria, the formula is clear: defend with discipline, remain composed under pressure and take the chances that come their way. If the Flamingos can execute that plan, they have an opportunity to turn a difficult assignment into a defining moment in their World Cup campaign.

title: Casualties Feared As Multi-Storey Building Collapses In Nairobi
body: A multi-storey building collapsed mid-construction in the Kenyan capital on Friday, the Red Cross said, with reports from local media of casualties and looting at the site. Videos spreading online showed a dramatic crash and huge clouds of dust as the building — thought to have been around 18 storeys high — came down in a densely populated business and residential area of Eastleigh. AFP journalists at the scene saw the building had been reduced to a pile of rubble as a small number of search and rescue teams arrived on the scene. “There were some businesses in the basement, and workers who were busy building,” said local resident Abdi Aziz, 25. “But as it was (the Friday prayer), a lot of them were at the mosque. I think few people died because no one was living there,” he told AFP. Asked if he could see obvious flaws in the construction process, he said: “Everyone rushes to build in this neighbourhood.” This aerial view shows personnel from the Kenya Defence Forces Disaster Response Battalion inspecting the rubble of a collapsed residential building that was still under construction in the Eastleigh neighbourhood of Nairobi on October 23, 2026. (Photo by TONY KARUMBA / AFP) | TONY KARUMBA / AFP Local media reported looting and possible casualties trapped beneath the rubble, with images showing large crowds gathered at the site immediately after the incident, which happened around lunchtime. AFP saw police use tear gas to disperse crowds gathering near the site. Rescue operations had yet to begin when AFP arrived, with the site hemmed in by high-rise buildings, complicating efforts. Nairobi is undergoing a rapid construction boom, with high-rise buildings appearing all over the city, particularly in Eastleigh which is known for its busy market areas and as a hub for the Somali community. There have been many concerns over safety. There were 86 building collapses between 2009 and 2019, killing an estimated 200 people, according to a report by the Kenya Institute for Public Policy Research and Analysis. An audit of almost 15,000 buildings by the National Building Inspectorate found that 4.8 percent were very dangerous, 72.3 percent were classified as unsafe, the report said. The number of buildings completed annually in Nairobi has risen from 20,025 in 2022 to 25,090 last year, according to its statistics bureau, as east Africa’s leading business hub sucks in people from rural areas and neighbouring countries. The post Casualties Feared As Multi-Storey Building Collapses In Nairobi appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Russia cannot ignore EU’s growing militarization — Russian ambassador to Montenegro
body:
MOSCOW, October 23. /TASS/. Russia cannot ignore the European Union’s ongoing militarization and its provocative anti-Russian measures, Russian Ambassador to Montenegro Alexander Lukashik told TASS.
Montenegro’s accession to the European Union "is the country’s sovereign choice," he noted. "But we cannot turn a blind eye to the ongoing militarization of this alliance, its focus on escalating the confrontation with Russia, its military aid to the Kiev regime, the further tightening of anti-Russian sanctions, and its provocative actions, which bring the prospect of a large-scale armed conflict closer."
Lukashik said these factors "come to the fore when Russia assesses the European Union's expansion through the admission of new members that will automatically undertake an additional burden of responsibility for the deterioration of relations with our country."
The diplomat told TASS earlier that Podgorica plans to join the European Union in 2028. Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova, in turn, emphasized that the process of integration into the European Union, in connection with which Montenegro had decided to impose visa requirements on Russians, "in no way implies that new members will be able to retain their neutral status."

title: Melania Trump secures ceasefire for aid delivery to Oleshky - White House
body:
US First Lady Melania Trump has secured a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine covering the city of Oleshky, the White House has said.
"Both countries have agreed to temporarily suspend all military operations in Oleshky to ensure the delivery of humanitarian aid and prepare for the evacuation of civilians through a designated safe corridor," the statement said.
The local ceasefire will take effect on October 29, 2026.
"The situation in Oleshky is dire. Oleshky is a front-line war city on the brink of disaster. Oleshky’s remaining population is comprised primarily of elderly residents who urgently need medical attention, medicine, food, and clean water,” said First Lady Melania Trump. “The people of Oleshky have limited electricity, live amid mined roads, and endure regular military attacks. It was abundantly clear that without my intervention, the possibility to bring humanitarian aid into the city and to evacuate the elderly would be impossible," Trump said.
Melania Trump and her representative worked directly with Russian and Ukrainian leadership to determine the terms of the localized ceasefire, the statement said. Acting in an official role as exclusive mediator, the first lady initiated talks with both countries and coordinated the objectives of the agreement, technical procedures, timelines, processes and conditions.
"Non-military, civilian leaders from both countries will work together to visit Oleshky residents in their homes and determine the level of assistance they require. Residents who wish to evacuate will receive coordinated support and transportation to their preferred destination. I anticipate some will want to go to Russia, and some to Ukraine," Trump said.
She added that an impartial American media organization would accompany Russian and Ukrainian teams on the ground.
"This will play an important role in ensuring that each family’s wishes are strictly respected," she said.

title: Trump, the peacemaker, can make peace in Israel - opinion
body: If the polls are close to being right, voting stations across the country will close on Tuesday night at 10 p.m. without answering the most important question facing the country: Where does Israel go from here?Neither political bloc will have a majority – neither Benjamin Netanyahu nor Gadi Eisenkot – and Israel will once again face the prospect of political paralysis and potentially another election.In that scenario, much of the responsibility would fall on President Isaac Herzog. He would meet with the different party leaders, hear their recommendations, and decide who should receive the mandate to try to form a government.He might also attempt to bring the sides together, hoping to find a formula that could prevent Israel from returning to the destructive cycle of elections as we had in the years before October 7.But there is another president whose role in this process could be just as consequential: Donald Trump.Trump's endorsement of Netanyahu this week was interesting not only because of its timing – just days before Israelis go to the polls – but because of the reasoning behind it. Trump made clear that his support for Netanyahu was tied to Iran.Netanyahu, he said, is the partner he needs to finish the job and topple the Iranian regime. With someone else in power, Trump warned, America might have to finish the job alone, and that is something he does not want to do.Whether that is true is a good question. But the endorsement revealed something else about how Trump sees what happens next. For him, the Israeli election is not only about who wins in Israel. It is also about what the US will do when it comes to Iran.Imagine the following scenario: The election here ends without a decisive victory for either side, and amid attempts to build a minority coalition or attract defectors from one side to the other, Trump invites Netanyahu and Eisenkot to the White House.Netanyahu would happily accept. Eisenkot would be less enthusiastic, knowing what he would be walking into. But he would not be able to refuse the invitation. The two Israeli politicians would arrive in Washington, and Trump would present them with a proposition: I need both of you to form a government so we can finish the job in Iran.For Netanyahu, it would be a dream come true, while for Eisenkot, the political cost would be huge. The Yashar leader promised just on Wednesday that he would not agree to a rotation agreement with Netanyahu.Trump could guarantee an agreementBut Trump could offer him something that might force him to reconsider: a national unity government built around a shared strategic objective of taking on Iran, alongside Trump serving as the guarantor that Netanyahu would honor a future transfer of power.Could Trump actually enforce such an agreement? Not legally. But if Netanyahu were to break a commitment made at the White House, he would risk not only embarrassing Trump but also damaging his relationship with a president whose support he considers essential to Israel's security.What Trump could do is force Netanyahu to agree to only 18 months as prime minister. That would leave Trump roughly another six months in office to exert pressure if Netanyahu tried to block the transition.Is this imaginary scenario difficult to see happening, considering the personal animosity and broken trust between Netanyahu and Eisenkot? Yes. But is it impossible? No.For this to happen, though, Israelis would need to be able to trust their leaders, something that is very hard right now as Netanyahu beats the war drums on a daily – and even hourly – basis with just days left to the election. His threats reached a point this week that raised concerns that Israel might attack Iran at any moment or might even be trying to provoke Iran to attack first.On the one hand, there is no question that the danger is real. Iran's pursuit of nuclear weapons and its development of long-range ballistic missiles pose a grave threat to Israel. The question is not whether this needs to be confronted but rather whether it needs to be confronted right now.The public does not know the answer, and neither do most members of Israel's political establishment. Only a handful of people have access to the intelligence needed to determine what Iran is actually doing, how immediate the threat is, and whether military action can wait.If Iran is actively building a nuclear bomb and intelligence indicates that it is approaching a point of no return, Israel may have no choice but to act, regardless of the election. But if the threat is likely to be essentially the same in a few weeks or months, then the current government needs to exercise extreme caution.If Netanyahu decides to attack, even for the best and most legitimate of reasons, most Israelis will suspect that his motives are political. Even if the attack is entirely justified, people will believe that its timing was designed to influence the outcome of the election.This brings us to the heart of the problem. Israel is suffering from a deep crisis of trust. An operation that might genuinely be necessary to strengthen the country's security could end up further undermining public confidence in the government and even the IDF, simply because so many Israelis would not believe that it had to happen.This is where Trump could play another important role.If the US decides to participate in another military operation against Iran, that would provide Israelis with an indication that the threat is serious and that the decision is not simply a political move by Netanyahu. American participation would not eliminate the questions, but it would give the decision a level of credibility that Netanyahu cannot provide on his own.There is another person whose voice could be even more important to Israelis: IDF Chief of Staff Lt.-Gen. Eyal Zamir.Zamir was appointed under Netanyahu, but he is not seen as a political loyalist and has already proven that he is ready to challenge the cabinet when he believes that Israel's security interests are in jeopardy.A public address by Zamir, explaining what he can about the danger, its urgency, and the military considerations behind any decision to act, would provide assurances that are currently missing. It is obviously not Zamir's job to endorse Netanyahu's political arguments, but he is responsible for protecting the IDF and preserving public trust in it.Without that trust, even the right decisions can come at a terrible cost.The writer is a co-founder of the MEAD policy forum, a senior fellow at the Jewish People Policy Institute, and a former editor-in-chief of The Jerusalem Post. His newest book is While Israel Slept.

title: Breaking: Russia, Ukraine agree to Oleshky ceasefire mediated by Melania Trump, White House says
body:
Editor's note: This story is being updated.
U.S. First Lady Melania Trump has mediated a localized ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in and around the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky in Kherson Oblast to allow the safe evacuation of civilians and delivery of humanitarian aid, Ukrainian human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets confirmed on Oct. 23.
The move comes amid increased attention to the worsening humanitarian crisis in the city, which over the past weeks has gained international attention, including from Pope Leo XIV.
According to the press release from the White House press service, the First Lady "initiated discussions with both nations and aligned the parties on the agreement's objectives, technical procedures, timing, processes, and terms, in her formal role as Exclusive Intermediary."
The ceasefire is scheduled to begin on 3:00 a.m. on October 27th, Kyiv time, according to Ukraine's General Staff.
Lubinets, confirmed the agreement in a video statement on Telegram later on Oct. 23.
"I personally thank Melania Trump and her team for their efforts, leadership, and coordination between the two negotiating groups of Ukraine and the Russian Federation in reaching agreements," Lubinets said.
Under the agreement, a ceasefire will be put in place, humanitarian cargo will be delivered to Oleshky, and civilians will be allowed to leave the city freely, according to Lubinets.
"The operation will take place gradually. It is extremely difficult to implement," he said. He will keep the Ukrainian public informed and show the results of the operation, he said. He also asked the public to be careful about spreading information on the mission.
Lubinets added that he had led the negotiations on the Ukrainian side and that Russia's human rights commissioner, Yana Lantratova, had led them on the Russian side.
Ukraine's General Staff said on Oct. 23 that Ukrainian forces would implement the decisions of the country's commander-in-chief to facilitate the humanitarian mission in Oleshky.
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov also welcomed Melania Trump's role, saying she had "made a significant contribution to agreeing on the humanitarian operation" in Oleshky, Russian pro-Kremlin media outlet Ura.ru reported. Peskov said the sides are working to agree on a ceasefire in the area so that residents can be evacuated.
State-aligned Russian media RBK reported Russia's General Staff had announced a ceasefire from 04:00 a.m. local time on Oct. 27, citing Valeriy Gerasimov, Chief of the General Staff of the Russian Armed Forces.
Gerasimov added that to ensure the safety of people and the delivery of vital supplies, engineering reconnaissance will be conducted.
Oleshky , located just across the Dnipro River from Kherson , has been effectively blockaded by Russian forces in the area, who prevent humanitarian aid from entering. Civilians attempting to flee via the only roads in and out of the city are frequently targeted by drones.
"Non-military, civilian leaders from both countries will work together to visit Oleshky residents in their homes and determine the level of assistance they require," Melania Trump was quoted as saying in the press release.
"Residents who wish to evacuate will receive coordinated support and transportation to their preferred destination. I anticipate some will want to go to Russia, and some to Ukraine."
According to the document, an "impartial American media organization" will visit the area to document the work of both sides in the area.
Later in the day, Ukrainian lawmaker David Arakhamiia, leader of the Servant of the People faction and close associate of President Zelensky, said that the "process of unblocking the city of Oleshky and its outskirts will begin very soon."
"To achieve this goal, a ceasefire will be achieved in the near future, as announced by the First Lady of the United States, Melania Trump," Arakhamiia wrote on Telegram.
"This has been a long process, in which many people at different political levels have participated. We would like to especially note the role of the Pope and the First Lady of the United States, Melania Trump."
While several localized and temporary "ceasefires" have been announced throughout the course of the war, their implementation and enforcement on the ground has been patchy at best.
"I, like all of us, am hoping that people will be saved, preferably all who want to, and not just those who have time. But I am wary that there will be provocations, blackmail, a route through the Russian Federation (which many people will not agree to), and PR for those who manage to get out," said Stefan Vorontsov, a volunteer coordinator with the NGO Humanity, which helps evacuate civilians from occupied territories, to the Kyiv Independent.
"God willing, we will be able to set a precedent where Russia admits what they did in the occupied territories, and we will be able to organize the first official evacuation from there, then maybe the rest of us will be able to do it too. But again, I have little faith."
Even if the reported ceasefire agreement is upheld by both sides, the nature of the situation in Oleshky means actually carrying out evacuations on the ground will still be particularly challenging.
"I don't think anything (about the news), people were abandoned and no one is going to save them," said a woman from Oleshky, who declined to reveal her name for security reasons, to the Kyiv Independent.
"There is no food delivery there because all the roads are mined, the orcs (Russians) are eating our dogs because they are hungry themselves. In order to bring a bus there, all the roads need to be demined, and there is no one there to do it"
The intervention of the White House in the situation in Oleshky comes at a time of fraught relations between Kyiv and Washington, after the Trump administration agreed to waive sanctions on Russia and buy Russian diesel fuel, while the artificial throttling of Starlink terminals on Ukrainian drones continues.
On Oct. 13, U.S. President Donald Trump unilaterally announced an "energy ceasefire" between Russia and Ukraine, which soon turned out not to exist in practice.
Yuliia Taradiuk contributed to reporting.

title: Von der Leyen condemns Russian attack on vessel off Romanian coast
body:

title: Senior Russian diplomat says West seeks to undermine independent centers of power
body:
MOSCOW, October 23. /TASS/. Western countries are seeking to destroy independent centers of power and erase the identity of other cultures to maintain their dominance, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Mikhail Galuzin said.
"Today, we are witnessing again how, in an attempt to preserve their own dominance, Western countries are seeking to destroy independent centers of power, erase the identity of other cultures under the motto of promoting so-called European values," the senior Russian diplomat said in an address to the Second International Scientific and Practical Conference "Genocide of Slavic Peoples in the 20th Century."
According to Galuzin, Russia’s Foreign Ministry pays "the most serious attention to the protection of the rich culture shared by the Slavic world and the memory of numerous tragic pages of Slavic history." "This is of tantamount importance for Russian citizens living abroad as it serves as confirmation of our country’s readiness to reliably ensure their legitimate rights and interests," he concluded in the address released on the Russian Foreign Ministry’s website.

title: Russia-Africa summit establishes regular cooperation with African nations — expert
body:
MOSCOW, October 23. /TASS/. The second Russia-Africa Summit contributed to establishing regular and structured interaction between the sides, Andrey Maslov, Director of the Center for African Studies at the HSE University, said at the Valdai International Discussion Club. He was speaking during a panel discussion titled "Russia and Africa: Is it for the Long Haul?"
The expert noted that after the first Russia-Africa Summit in Sochi in 2019, the pandemic disrupted regular engagement, causing a COVID-related slump in activity.
"However, we moved forward to the second summit in St. Petersburg, which took place in 2023. It demonstrated a completely different level of interaction, because since the St. Petersburg event, Moscow and Russia as a whole have hosted as many African heads of state as attended the summit itself. This means that a consistent, structured interaction, balanced across various regions and levels, has been established," Maslov pointed out.
"We now have partner countries with whom quite diverse mechanisms of interaction are in place, along with sector-specific tracks. In a number of ministries, the respective deputy ministers in charge of international relations are now deeply engaged in African issues. They don't just remember Africa when a summit comes around. They regularly keep African files on their desks and maintain - what is crucial -working, informal, and direct contacts with their counterparts in several countries," the expert emphasized.

title: Russia-US dialogue focuses not only on Ukraine — Russian diplomat
body:
MOSCOW, October 23. /TASS/. Moscow’s dialogue with Washington is not focused solely on ways of settling the Ukrainian conflict, as it also covers many other topics, a high-ranking Russian Foreign Ministry official said.
"By the way, in this dialogue we are discussing not only issues related to the Ukrainian settlement but also major economic initiatives and joint cultural and humanitarian projects that have the potential of becoming bridges between our countries in the future," Alexander Gusarov, director of the ministry’s North Atlantic department, said in an interview with the International Affairs magazine.
In light of this, the diesel deal can be seen as "a concrete result and the embodiment of the consistent and painstaking work of the presidents [of Russia and the United States] and their teams, who continue to work on a wide range of issues on the current international and bilateral agenda," he added.

title: Russia and Ukraine exchange 540 captives after latest UAE mediation
body: Russia and Ukraine agreed to release 540 captives following a new round of UAE-led mediation, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced on Friday. Each side agreed to exchange 270 captives, the ministry said. This brings the total number of captives exchanged between the two countries through the Emirates' efforts to 8,537. The ministry thanked both countries for co-operating with the UAE as a trusted international mediator and for appreciating its commitment to supporting work to resolve the crisis. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy shared several photos of the released detainees and wrote: "National Guard members, including Azov warriors, border guards, warriors of the Territorial Defense Forces, the Navy, the Land Forces, the Airborne Assault Forces, and the State Special Transport Service, as well as nine civilians, are returning home. Most of them had been in captivity since 2022." He added: "We remember one and all and continue searching for everyone. I thank everyone who works to make these exchanges possible." This is the 27th detainee exchange between Russia and Ukraine through UAE-led talks. The ministry said the Emirates would continue to support initiatives for a peaceful resolution to the war and to address the humanitarian impact on refugees and prisoners. The two countries last exchanged captives in August, when 206 were released.

title: Allient Defense Receives Best in Show Award at AUSA 2026
body:
