title: Israel vows major West Bank operation after attack kills 2 troops
body: Tel Aviv — Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Friday that he had ordered a major military operation in the occupied West Bank and told troops to cordon off a large city in the territory after a shooting attack by two Palestinian men that killed two soldiers.The Israeli military said forces killed the Palestinian gunmen after they opened fire at a junction near the West Bank city of Hebron. The military later confirmed that two soldiers, Staff Sergeant Ron Yonatan Roytman and Sergeant Yuval Shai Svilem, were killed in the attack, while three others were lightly injured.   Netanyahu said he had ordered the evacuation of residents from the neighborhood in Hebron where the gunmen lived ahead of a house-to-house sweep for weapons. "Our first step will be to demolish this site and completely transform it," Netanyahu said. He added that he ordered the IDF to cordon off Hebron, a city with more than 200,000 inhabitants. Netanyahu said a broader military operation would follow. "The IDF will enter the neighborhoods from which the terrorists emerged, evacuate the residents, go house-to-house, and dismantle the terror infrastructure. We are prepared for an extensive operation in Judea and Samaria," he said, using Israel's name for the West Bank.Israel's military said a large amount of weapons and ammunition was discovered in the attackers' vehicle, alleging that they were planning a major attack on civilians. The shooters used an M16 rifle and a handgun in their attack, the IDF said.The escalation in the West Bank comes just before Israel holds elections on Tuesday, in which Netanyahu has made national security a central issue of his campaign for another term.Netanyahu said the Palestinian shooting attack was an attempt to influence Israel elections, and referenced a warning he made a few weeks ago about Israel's enemies preparing attacks to affect the vote.Netanayhu called the gunmen involved in the shooting near Hebron "Hamas terrorists." Hamas called the attack heroic and a legitimate response to "ongoing crimes and brutal attacks against our people, land, and holy sites," but the group stopped short of claiming responsibility.  Hamas, long designated a terrorist group by Israel and the U.S., called for any Palestinians in the West Bank with guns to use them to attack Israeli soldiers and civilians living in the occupied territory.Following the shooting, the IDF said it had launched "offensive counterterrorism operations" in the Hebron area, and that soldiers were operating inside the residences of the shooters in Friday's attack and other suspects.The IDF said it had arrested around 70 wanted Palestinians during operations in the West Bank over the past week. Netanyahu's Likud party said the prime minister had convened his top security chiefs Friday, and that the party was canceling all campaign events for the rest of the day. The attack follows a recent surge in Israeli settler attacks on Palestinians. It also comes after Brad Lander, a New York Democratic candidate for Congress, was briefly detained by Israeli forces this week while helping Palestinian farmers during the annual olive harvest.

title: Kongsberg demonstrates containerised ‘NSM in a box’
body: Kongsberg has successfully demonstrated a containerised Naval Strike Missile (NSM) transportation and launch system designed for rapid deployment to land sites, truck-mounted applications, or as a modular fit for maritime platforms. The prototype installation, packaging four NSM missile canisters into a standard 20 ft ISO shipping container, was tested on an undisclosed military range facility in Norway at the start of October. The company-funded demonstration is intended to reduce time to market and serve as a risk reduction for potential customers seeking a ‘mission module’ solution. In service or on order for 15 customers in both ship-based and coastal defence applications, NSM was originally developed by Kongsberg to meet the Royal Norwegian Navy’s requirements for a highly discriminative, low-observable surface-to-surface guided weapon able to penetrate shipboard defences and operate effectively in both blue water and littoral environments. Capable of ranges in excess of 250 km, NSM is a highly autonomous weapon combining GPS-aided midcourse guidance with an advanced dual-band imaging infrared seeker embedding automatic target recognition functionality. According to Ståle Mortensson, vice-president business development and strategy in the Emerging Business unit of Kongsberg’s Missiles & Aerostructures business, the company’s decision to self-fund the prototyping and test of a mission module is reflects market interest in a containerised solution. “The ability to distribute and redeploy modules is a natural trend that is being followed by many customers,” he told Naval News . “For us, this is a market development initiative under which we are making an early investment to reduce non-recurring engineering, and help potential customers understand how they could install and use such a capability. So it is about shortening the time to market, and reducing risk.” Ståle Mortensson, vice-president business development and strategy Up to four NSM missile canisters can fit into the standard 20 ft ISO shipping container. Kongsberg picture. The prototype container installation built up by Kongsberg builds on the company’s prior work to package a four-pack NSM launcher, and associated Missile Firing Unit, into a truck-mounted coastal defence system. It has also been informed by the company’s involvement in the US Navy/Marine Expeditionary Ship Interdiction System programme, and ongoing work to integrate NSM into the Royal Danish Navy’s Standard Flex container system. The 20 ft container installation accommodates four encanistered NSM missiles on an elevating structure. The container roof opens just prior to launch, allowing the launcher unit inside to raise, fire, then retract. A live launch using a NSM Ballistic Test Vehicle was conducted at a firing range on 1 October. This was followed by a restrained firing to demonstrate blast management. “We were able to package the full four-pack, the elevating mechanism and the blast management inside the container,” said Mortensson. “We also found room for a generator and an electronics compartment. Only the mission planning needs to be external.” Kongsberg sees three main applications for container-based NSM installations; a mobile truck-mounted capability; for rapid deployment/redeployment to ground sites; and as a modular fit for both crewed and uncrewed vessels. The prototype installation was tested on an undisclosed military range facility in Norway at the start of October. Kongsberg picture. According to Mortensson, the performance observed from the prototype demonstration has left Kongsberg in a much better position to discuss the integration of an NSM mission module with platform OEMs. “On a ship, for example, it is very important to understand issues around footprint, installation and handling,” he said. “We are now better able to inform customers about ship design and topside impacts like securing points, blast management and fly-out angles.” The post Kongsberg demonstrates containerised ‘NSM in a box’ appeared first on Naval News .

title: 2026 Tanyigbe Yam Festival celebrates act of kindness, 100th birthday of community matriarch
body: The 2026 Tanyigbe Annual Yam Festival of the Chiefs and people of Tanyigbe Traditional Area in the Ho Municipality of the Volta Region has ended on a memorable note, with a family paying tribute to a man who carried an injured schoolmate home more than 56 years ago and the community celebrating the 100th birthday of Madam Flora Afua Abro. The festival, which began with traditional rites to seek blessings for the community, its farmlands and rivers, featured several days of celebrations across the four towns of Tanyigbe before the observance day for the departed. The opening rites included the ceremonial introduction of harvested yam tubers into the community by the Chief Lands Priest, known as Anyinuor, after which other community members followed suit. On Saturday, September 26, indigenes gathered at their respective ancestral stool houses to offer traditional tributes to their ancestors and seek blessings for the new year. The festival also featured sports activities and free health screenings for locals. The residents receive free health screening One of the festival’s notable highlights was a special homage paid by the Ziadzi-Tawiah House of Tanyigbe Anyigbe to the Tatsyi-Gamese Family of the Vovoe Clan in Tanyigbe Etoe. The gesture was inspired by a long-forgotten act of compassion recalled by the family following the death and burial of their elder, MacMicky Kudzo Hiadzi, also known as Fo Atawia-Kodzo, in July. According to Hiadzi-Tawiah Dan, a member of the family based in Richmond, California, preparations for his late brother’s life history brought to light an incident from May 1970 involving a football match between pupils associated with Agasco Middle School and Tanyigbe Kpodzi LA Middle School. During the match, Fo Atawia-Kodzo sustained a severe leg injury. Despite the rivalry between the schools, his schoolmate, Efo Vincent Gamese-Korsi, carried him on his back all the way to his home in Anyigbe. The injury reportedly left Hiadzi with a permanent leg deformity. Moved by the act of kindness, Mr Hiadzi-Tawiah Dan and Dziko-Kwame Akumah, a fellow member of the diaspora and friend of the late Hiadzi, proposed that Efo Gamese-Korsi be honoured for his selfless intervention. Tanyigbe Local Volleyball Team played with the Tanyigbe SHS team The family subsequently travelled to Tanyigbe Etoe with gifts and traditional attire to pay homage to the elderly man, whom they described as a “One-Man Ambulance” for his extraordinary gesture. The presentation, made in the presence of elders of the Vovoe Clan, reportedly left Mr Gamese-Korsi visibly surprised and touched. He thanked the family, prayed for God’s abundant blessings upon them and asked that their expenses be replenished. He also encouraged residents of Tanyigbe to shun selfishness and emulate acts of kindness. The festival concluded with celebrations marking the centenary of Madam Flora Afua Abro, who was born on August 13, 1926. The Hiadzi-Tewiah House and the Vovoe Elders at the Ceremony. The celebrations, held from October 2 to 4, brought together her Akumah family, children, members of the Adeblevi, Kodivi and Vleevi clans, the Global Evangelical Church and traditional rulers. The occasion attracted relatives and well-wishers from Akoefe, Tokokoe, Takla, Hordzo, Lume, Ho Bankoe and Ga Mashie, among other communities. Fo Gamese Korsi receiving the Gifts from Ms Tawiah-Maa. Madam Abro, also known as Kordzonor and the mother of 11 children, expressed gratitude to everyone who contributed to the celebration and wished them equally long and fulfilling lives. The two occasions added a strong sense of family history, compassion and intergenerational connection to this year’s Tanyigbe Yam Festival.

title: $242m Petroleum Dispute: Court Grants UBA Interim Order Against Vitol, Four Shipping Firms
body: Wale Igbintade The Lagos State High Court has granted interim preservative orders of Mareva injunction in favour of United Bank for Africa (UBA) Plc against Vitol SA, a Switzerland-based energy trading company, and four other shipping companies over a petroleum products diversion dispute involving $242 million. UBA alleged that Vitol wrongfully released cargoes of petroleum products consigned to the bank’s order under the relevant bills of lading. Addressing the court, Bode Olanipekun, SAN, lead counsel to UBA, urged the judge to grant the interim preservative orders against Vitol and the other shipping companies. In her ruling, Justice K. A. Jose granted three prayers in UBA’s application, including requests to restrain the dissipation of assets and dealings in funds up to the disputed amount by Vitol SA. “Prayers 1–3 are granted as prayed against the 2nd Respondent only,” the judge ruled. The application was brought pursuant to Order 43, Rule 1 of the High Court of Lagos State (Civil Procedure) Rules 2019 and the Lagos State High Court Practice Direction No. 2 of 2019. In the substantive proceedings, UBA intends to contend that Vitol SA and the owners of the vessels are liable for alleged conversion, misrepresentation and negligence arising from the non-delivery of the petroleum products. The bank also cited 34 financial institutions and public agencies, including commercial banks, merchant banks, microfinance banks, the Nigerian Ports Authority and the Nigeria Customs Service, in connection with the application. In an affidavit supporting the application, UBA’s Group Head of Recoveries and Remedial Management, Anthony Chilaka, stated that the bank had issued a letter of credit in favour of Vitol SA to facilitate a petroleum products transaction. According to the affidavit, the cargo was transported to Nigeria, where the masters of the vessels issued several bills of lading. UBA further alleged that Vitol subsequently endorsed the bills of lading in favour of the bank and handed over the original copies to it. The bank maintained that the endorsement entitled it to take possession of the cargo upon completion of the voyage. However, Chilaka stated that UBA had not received the gasoil despite the completion of the voyage. “The applicant has not been given possession of the gasoil despite completion of the voyage,” the affidavit stated. UBA alleged that the cargo was instead diverted for the benefit of another party, arguing that the failure to deliver the petroleum products amounted to conversion and negligence. The bank further contended that the respondents had obligations arising from the transaction and the endorsement of the shipping documents but failed to fulfil them. It also alleged that cargoes associated with the transactions were diverted to other parties after the completion of their voyages rather than being delivered to UBA.

title: Man Utd defeat to Como ‘unacceptable’, says Carrick
body: Manchester United manager Michael Carrick admitted on Friday his side have “lost their way” after a 4-1 thrashing by Champions League debutants Como made it seven games without a win. After a successful interim spell in charge in the second half of last season, Carrick was appointed on a permanent basis just five months ago, but his position is at risk ahead of Sunday’s visit of Bournemouth to Old Trafford. United are off to their worst start in the Premier League era, were dumped out of the League Cup by Brighton and have lost two of their opening three Champions League games. “Recently we haven’t had a good time. I totally accept that. We had five months of relative success in a spell where I was happy with a lot of things we were doing as a team,” Carrick said in an impassioned address at the start of his press conference on Friday. “We haven’t done well enough lately. We’ve had a spell we’re really not happy with. Como was a bad night. It hurt me. It was really unacceptable. “The supporters have to make the effort and spend the money to come and watch us. To have the feeling we all had after the game was a tough moment.” Carrick added: “My job is to put a team on the pitch that represents the supporters and that they can be proud of the identity we show. We have gone away from that recently in certain games which I am fully aware of and definintely doing something about.” AFP The post Man Utd defeat to Como ‘unacceptable’, says Carrick appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Transcorp Power Posts Resilient Q3 2026 Performance
body: Transcorp Power Plc, a power subsidiary of Transnational Corporation Plc (Transcorp Group), has reported a profit before tax of ₦83.1 billion for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, with its profit before tax margin improving to 31.2 per cent from 29.6 per cent in the corresponding period of 2025. The company’s unaudited financial results showed that revenue declined by 13.7 per cent to ₦266.1 billion from ₦308.5 billion in the corresponding period of 2025, while profit before tax fell to ₦83.1 billion from ₦91.18 billion. Despite the decline in revenue, Transcorp Power improved its profit before tax margin to 31.2 per cent, reflecting its ability to sustain profitability amid operational challenges in Nigeria’s electricity supply industry. The company attributed the revenue decline to structural challenges affecting the sector, including the vandalisation of critical transmission infrastructure, which constrained power evacuation, gas supply limitations, and delays in the delivery of essential turbine parts and components due to global supply chain disruptions arising from the Middle East crisis. Transcorp Power said it maintained operational readiness and plant availability despite the challenges, while continuing to focus on efficient power generation and operational excellence. Its financial position also strengthened during the period, with total assets increasing by 11.7 per cent to ₦629.5 billion, while shareholders’ funds rose by 8.9 per cent to ₦199.8 billion. Retained earnings grew by 11.5 per cent to ₦147.7 billion. Cash and cash equivalents increased by 365 per cent to ₦10.3 billion, supported by improved collections, partial settlement of legacy market debts, and the reversal of expected credit loss provisions, which the company said reflected improving liquidity across the electricity market. Commenting on the results, the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Transcorp Power Plc, Peter Ikenga, said the performance demonstrated the resilience of the business despite external challenges, including transmission constraints, vandalisation of critical infrastructure and gas supply limitations. He said the company had continued to work with stakeholders to address broader industry challenges while improving its profit margin, strengthening its balance sheet and increasing cash reserves. Ikenga added that Transcorp Power remained focused on operational excellence, efficient generation and long-term value creation for shareholders. The Chief Finance Officer of Transcorp Power Plc, Dr Evans Okpogoro, said the nine-month results reflected financial discipline and resilience despite external sector challenges that affected revenue. He said the improvement in profit margin, growth in cash reserves and increase in shareholders’ funds demonstrated the company’s financial strength, prudent capital management and capacity to deliver sustainable value despite operational challenges largely beyond its control. Looking ahead, Transcorp Power said it would continue to pursue growth opportunities, strengthen operational reliability and fuel security, and collaborate with stakeholders across the power value chain to support Nigeria’s growing energy needs.

title: Netanyahu bloc falls to 48 seats as opposition reaches 54, days before election - poll
body: The gap between Israel's coalition and opposition blocs has widened to six seats ahead of Tuesday's Knesset election, despite the two largest parties being separated by just two seats, according to a Maariv poll by Lazar Research published Friday.The coalition bloc receives just 48 seats this week, following the failure of Ofer Winter's People of Israel party to cross the electoral threshold. The party receives 3% of the vote, below the required 3.25%. Meanwhile, the opposition's change bloc has strengthened to 54 seats. Recent polling averages have shown the two political blocs nearly tied, highlighting the fluctuations in the election race.The poll also shows that United Torah Judaism and Otzma Yehudit each lost one seat, polling 7 mandates, while Likud (19), Shas (8), and the Religious Zionist Party (7) each gained one. Overall, the coalition bloc has weakened by three seats compared with the previous week's poll.Within the opposition bloc, the most significant change is the two-seat jump by Naftali Bennett's B'Yachad party, which rises to 15 seats. The Democrats also gained one seat this week, reaching 10. In contrast, Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party (21) and Yisrael Beytenu (8) remain unchanged. Other election surveys published on Wednesday also placed Eisenkot's party ahead of Likud.The poll also shows that the Reservists or the New Economic Party narrowly crosses the electoral threshold, winning four seats.This distribution of seats between the blocs depends on the Reservists-Economic Party crossing the electoral threshold. Given its narrow margin above the threshold in the current poll, if the party fails to qualify, the distribution is expected to shift to 50 seats for the coalition, 56 for the Zionist opposition, and another 14 for the Arab parties.In addition to People of Israel (3%), the Haredi Public party (0.9%), Noam LeYisrael (0.5%), and Tzomet Beit Yisrael (0.5%) also fail to cross the electoral threshold.Voter turnout intentions continue to riseThe Maariv poll also found that the proportion of Israelis who are certain they will vote in Tuesday's Knesset election continues to rise, reaching 81%. The figure suggests a potential increase in voter turnout compared with the 2022 election, when turnout stood at 71%.As in the October 8 poll, the percentage of respondents certain they will vote is higher among opposition party supporters (87%) than among those intending to vote for coalition parties (83%).Of particular note is the significant increase in the proportion of Arab party supporters who say they are certain to vote, rising from 74% on October 8 to 81% in the current poll, matching the national average.These figures could result in the Arab party bloc winning significantly more seats in the upcoming election than it holds in the current Knesset. Arab voter turnout has emerged as a significant issue in the election campaign, amid concerns over crime and political distrust in Arab communities.Eisenkot maintains lead over NetanyahuThe Maariv poll also found that Gadi Eisenkot continues to lead Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a head-to-head matchup for prime minister, with 49% support compared with Netanyahu's 41%.Naftali Bennett, who was tied with Netanyahu at 43% in the previous poll, now leads him by 45% to 43%.Against Avigdor Liberman, Netanyahu continues to lead, although the gap has narrowed slightly, with Netanyahu receiving 44% compared with Liberman's 39%.Majority of Israelis prefer unity government over new electionAs in the previous poll, most Israelis (60%) would prefer a unity government to be formed if the Knesset election produces no clear result.Of those surveyed, 33% want such a government to be headed by a leader from the change bloc, while 19% want Netanyahu to lead a unity government. Another 8% have no preference regarding who leads it, provided that a unity government is established.Only 23% would prefer another election in the event of a deadlock, down from 27% in the previous poll. Another 17% said they did not know. A previous Maariv poll published on October 16 also found majority support for a unity government, with 27% preferring another election.A breakdown of the findings by political bloc shows a decline in the proportion of coalition voters who would prefer another election, from 32% to 25%.Opposition voters, meanwhile, remain consistent in their preferences, with a majority (55%) favoring a unity government headed by a leader from their own bloc.The poll was conducted between October 19 and 22 among a representative sample of Israel's population aged 18 and older, including Jewish and Arab respondents. The initial sample consisted of 1,000 participants, while the final sample included 1,048. Data were collected from the general population using Panel4All's online respondent panel. A total of 580 people were contacted, 188 responded (30%), and 78 completed the survey (41%). The researchers also conducted supplementary telephone polling among the Arab population. A total of 687 telephone calls were made, 308 people responded (45%), and 100 completed the survey (32%). The poll's maximum margin of sampling error was 3%.

title: Quantum Systems Demonstrates Integrated Multi-Domain Operations at Forward Edge 2026
body:
Quantum Systems has completed its two-week Multi-Domain Exercise “Forward Edge 26”, demonstrating how unmanned systems can operate together across air, land and sea and across continents – orchestrated via the MOSAIC UXS software suite.
Quantum Systems has concluded its Multi-Domain Exercise “Forward Edge 2026” at a military training field in central Germany, demonstrating the coordinated multi-domain operations of unmanned systems across air, land, and sea. Together with selected technology partners, the company brought aerial reconnaissance, ground robotics, maritime systems and counter-drone capabilities into four operational scenarios, connected through its MOSAIC UXS software suite.
The exercise culminated in the demonstration of four scenarios:
The exercise focused on orchestrating a multitude of unmanned systems by Quantum Systems and partner companies, through the MOSAIC UXS software suite and successfully demonstrated the viability of unmanned multi-domain operations.
Sven Kruck, Co-CEO of Quantum Systems, said: “Today Quantum Systems and its partners demonstrated the future of warfare: Silent, precise, lethal and orchestrated through software and AI. “Forward Edge 26″ was a glimpse into the future. And the future is unmanned.”
For armed forces and defence and security customers, the exercise showed how reconnaissance, protection and mission execution can work together rather than remain in separate capabilities.
Martin Karkour, CRO of Quantum Systems, said: “Traditional military exercises often focus on traditional military hardware. At Forward Edge 26, we demonstrated a different approach: An entirely unmanned exercise, software orchestrated through MOSAIC UXS. Unmanned multi-domain operations are real and they are possible today.”
Technology and industry partners included Daimler Truck, Frontline Robotics, Ground A, Planet, Wolf Radar, Reactive Dynamics, Tencore, Volkswagen, XTEND, and Quantum Systems’ German-Ukrainian joint ventures, Quantum Frontline Industries (QFI) and Quantum Tencore Industries (QTI). Their participation demonstrated how systems from different manufacturers can be connected within one operational architecture in MOSAIC UXS.
With the completion of the exercise, Quantum Systems has demonstrated the next step in its development: bringing together hardware, software, AI and partner technologies to deliver coordinated multi-domain operations. The results will inform further system development, integration and operational validation.

title: France deploys 70,000 police, shuts Paris museums ahead of protests
body:
Some 70,000 law enforcement officers will be deployed across France on Saturday while the Louvre and several other major Paris museums will be closed as authorities seek to prevent renewed violence during planned protests.
Protests last week devolved into mayhem, with people setting fires, storming public buildings, smashing shop windows, looting and clashing with police. It was France's most violent unrest in years.
Demonstrators plan to take to the streets again Saturday to denounce the high cost of living. Students, members of the CGT labor union and activists from the “ yellow vest ” movement, whose demonstrations against social injustice shook France in 2018 and 2019, are all set to join.
French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said some 70,000 police officers and gendarmes would be deployed, along with helicopters, armored vehicles and water cannons. In addition, elite police units will help secure public buildings like city halls in a “highly mobile” security operation, he said.
“There have been numerous calls from radical far-left groups on social media to commit acts of violence and vandalism. There have also been renewed calls for looting, with those messages clearly being spread by rioters," Nuñez said at a news conference.
“We will be absolutely uncompromising" with those involved in violence, he added, warning that police will have a “very firm approach to making arrests, and there will be legal consequences.”
In a statement to The Associated Press, the Culture Ministry said the Louvre, the Orsay and Picasso museums as well as the Grand Palais would be closed. The ministry called on all institutions under its authority to adopt any necessary measures to ensure “visitor safety, staff protection and the preservation of artworks,” according to the statement.
After two days when admission was by invitation only, Art Basel Paris opened to the public Friday — but only for the day, with the threat of unrest prompting organizers to cancel the weekend program. One of the world’s most prestigious contemporary art fairs, Art Basel includes exhibitions by 211 international galleries at Paris’ Grand Palais.
"This decision has not been taken lightly, and the safety of everyone involved in the fair remains our utmost priority," organizers said in a statement Thursday.
Saloni Doshi, an art collector who traveled to Paris from India for the fair, grew worried last Saturday as she saw the fires and panicked people, and she received phone calls from friends asking whether Paris was safe. She agreed with the organizers' rationale to close.
Antoine Donzeaud and Elisa Rigoulet, the owners of the gallery exo exo, felt the same.
“We understand this decision, which we consider reasonable and consistent with the urgency of the social demands currently unfolding in France,” they said in a text message.
A demonstration Saturday in the city of Orléans, about 110 kilometers (70 miles) south of Paris, will also be closely watched.
About 50 organizations have called for a protest against the far right on the sidelines of the two-day congress of Marine Le Pen’s nationalist, anti-immigration party ahead of next spring’s presidential election. Organizers include labor unions, left-wing political parties, student organizations and anti-racism groups.
Hugues Moutouh, the prefect of the Loiret region, said that 20,000 to 30,000 demonstrators from across the country were expected.
Le Pen, whom opinion polls place as the front-runner in next year’s election, accused left-wing organizations and political parties of trying to “disrupt a political party’s democratic congress,” on news broadcaster Franceinfo.
Still, she said she had “no concerns” about security because the government had “recognized the need for measures allowing the congress to proceed safely.”

title: Iran foreign exchange reserves to last beyond Trump's term
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 23 (MNA) – entral Bank Governor Abdolnaser Hemmati says "Iran’s foreign exchange reserves are "in a good shape and would carry on til the end of Donald Trump’s adminstration."
Hemmati made the remarks while in New York speaking to Bloomberg News on the sidelines of the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank.
He said Iran has sufficient foreign exchange resources to withstand economic pressure.
Asked by a Bloomberg reporter about the amount of Iran’s foreign exchange reserves, Hemmati replied, “Do you want to report the amount of these reserves to Trump and the Federal Reserve? I will not disclose the figure to you.”
The Central Bank governor then stressed the adequacy of the country’s foreign exchange resources, saying, “Foreign exchange reserves are in very good condition and will be sufficient for us even after Trump’s adminstration.”
The Bloomberg reporter also asked whether Iran’s foreign exchange reserves would be sufficient to withstand economic pressure over the next two years. Hemmati replied, “Yes, our reserves are absolutely sufficient.”

title: Ukraine wants partners’ Patriot interceptors now. Europe can hand them over only with US approval, Ukraine’s president says
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Ukraine's defense minister raised the urgent need for Patriot interceptors with Sweden on 22 October, the Defense Ministry reported . The same day, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned of more Russian ballistic strikes and blamed US supply cuts. Patriots are Ukraine's main defense against Russian ballistic missiles, and their deliveries keep shrinking. Figures Zelenskyy released in August showed Patriot interceptor deliveries falling from 675 in 2023 to 364 in 2025, with 264 projected for 2026. Europe holds enough PAC-2 and PAC-3 interceptors for Ukraine's minimum winter needs, Zelenskyy told journalists on 16 October, but he did not yet know how many Europe would hand over, Ukrainska Pravda reported . Partners' stocks now, Ukraine's missiles later Russia fired 21 ballistic missiles at Kyiv overnight on 22 October, Zelenskyy said . Defense Minister Yevhenii Khmara told his Swedish counterpart, Pål Jonson, that Ukraine must counter ballistic threats as fast as possible, in particular with Patriot interceptors. Explore further 1,000 Patriot missiles arrive too late for this winter, so Ukraine asked the Ramstein arms coalition to open its warehouses The ministry's readout says Ukraine has Patriot missiles under contract. It also says Kyiv asks partners to transfer interceptors from their stocks in exchange for future deliveries allocated to Ukraine. Khmara made the same request at the Ukraine Defense Contact Group meeting on 8 September. He said then that Ukraine was contracting about 1,000 Patriot missiles with partners' help and an EU loan, but they would arrive only in the coming years, LB reported . He asked allies for missiles from their stocks now, in exchange for future upgraded missiles under Ukraine's contracts. "Only when the American side approves it" Zelenskyy spoke to journalists before meeting Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo, Ukrinform reported . He said the Americans had reduced supplies and Russia would step up ballistic attacks. "Europeans can provide the missiles only when the American side approves it," Zelenskyy said. He said the US had sent most of its interceptors to the Middle East. On 19 October, Zelenskyy told US senators that US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth was not signing off on Patriot deliveries allies had already paid for. Axios obtained the call transcript from Ukrainian officials. A US government official told the Kyiv Independent that Ukrainian officials' claims that Hegseth was holding up the missiles were " not true ." Washington says nothing has changed. " We have our own needs, too ," Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on 20 October, but there is " nothing being deliberately denied to Ukraine ." Hegseth told reporters in Eau Claire, Wisconsin, that the US had not changed its posture toward Ukraine, " but certainly with things like interceptors, we want to make sure our guys have the most possible as well ." title: U.S. claims of Canadian political interference have ‘no merit,’ Carney says
body:
Prime Minister Mark Carney says there is “no merit” to American claims that Canadians might be interfering in U.S. politics ahead of November’s midterm elections.
Officials in the Trump administration, including U.S. Ambassador to Canada Pete Hoekstra , have claimed Canadian politicians are interfering in the democratic process south of the border.
Hoekstra has said the administration is watching Canadian politicians closely ahead of the midterms and warned them to butt out of American politics.
Carney has consistently rebutted accusations of electoral interference and told reporters in Turkey today that he’s “disappointed” the U.S. envoy is spreading those claims.
Canadian diplomats were told this week not to meet with or attend events with candidates in the U.S. midterm elections amid a period of “heightened sensitivity.”
The prime minister says Canada has deep diplomatic ties to the United States but is careful to avoid even the perception of interference in electoral processes.

title: I once wanted to be a DJ – UK’s Prince William
body: Prince William has made a rare royal appearance on a BBC chat show, with the heir to the throne confessing he would have liked to join the police or be a DJ. The Prince of Wales appeared on an episode set to air Friday evening, to promote his Earthshot Prize, which goes to environmental causes. The show’s host, comedian Graham Norton, is known for his A-list guests and mildly ribbing celebrities. Wearing a blue suit, shirt and tie, William was roaring with laughter in images released ahead of the show on his and his wife’s Instagram. He sat on the show’s sofa next to actresses Cate Blanchett and Hannah Waddingham and conservationist Robert Irwin, all involved in the prize. Hello! magazine wrote that William is the first working royal to appear on a British talk show although Sarah Ferguson, the former wife of William’s uncle, the former prince Andrew, was interviewed by Norton when she still had a royal title. The Graham Norton Show is now in its 33rd series and is the broadcaster’s most watched chat show. Recent guests include Madonna. The BBC reported there were “cheers and gasps from the audience” when William appeared as a surprise guest. He will present the Earthshot Prize in Mumbai on November 17. Launched in 2020, the prize supports initiatives that help tackle environmental crises such as climate change. As with previous competitions, this year’s winners will receive one million pounds ($1.3 million) each “to accelerate the impact of their innovative solutions”, organisers said. William was asked whether he ever fantasised about another job rather than becoming king, telling Norton: “I did want to be a policeman when I was younger. I thought I could make a good one,” adding that he also went through “a phase of wanting to be a DJ — I wasn’t very good.” William spoke of his family’s love for “The Celebrity Traitors”, a devious reality show currently topping ratings. He also said he was a “big fan” of director Christopher Nolan’s “Dark Knight” trilogy about Batman, which he called “psychologically dark and deep”. The prince has kept tight-lipped about the return to Britain of his estranged brother Prince Harry, who said in an interview this week with GQ magazine that he wanted things to “work out” with his father, King Charles III, and William, his elder brother. AFP The post I once wanted to be a DJ – UK’s Prince William appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Brands, Creators Explore New Partnership Opportunities at YouTube PluggedIN 2026
body: Landmark Event Centre in Victoria Island, Lagos, became a bustling hub for content creators and brands as YouTube PluggedIN held its second edition. The event, a brainchild of Adetutu Laditan, the founder of Woof Studios Africa, provided the right ambience for brands to connect with creators as they pitch their projects to them. In partnership with Insight Redefini, the event, themed “Beyond the Placement: Rethinking How Brands Work with Creators,” examined how brands, agencies and creators can move beyond conventional advertising placements to develop content that combines business objectives with authentic audience engagement. Speaking at the event, Babatunde Olaifa, Group CEO of Insight Redefini, emphasised that the growth of the creator economy depends on meaningful collaboration among brands and creators. He noted that no single stakeholder could build the ecosystem alone, highlighting the importance of combining their respective strengths to transform creative ideas into valuable content. Building on a 2025 pilot, this year’s edition expanded the conversation to more brands, with a focus on small-group discussions and one-to-one engagements designed to connect brands with creators and move promising ideas towards campaign briefs, partnerships and funded content. Adetutu Laditan, Founder and Creative Director of Woof Studios Africa, highlighted the growing ambitions of Nigerian creators and the need to address the business and production complexities involved in turning creative ideas into content that can be funded, produced and distributed to wider audiences. Discussions throughout the event centred on three priorities: involving creators earlier in the creative process, ensuring brand-funded content remains relevant and authentic to audiences, and translating conversations into tangible partnerships, content opportunities and measurable outcomes. A key highlight was a brand panel moderated by Esosa Osagiede, Group Creative Director at Insight Redefini, which explored what brands look for when selecting creators for partnerships. Panellists, including brand managers from established Nigerian brands, identified brand fit and genuine audience influence as critical considerations. They stressed that follower counts and views alone do not necessarily reflect a creator’s ability to connect with audiences or influence their perceptions and behaviour. One of the panellists, Media and Consumer Experience Manager of Mondelez International, Bolaji Popoola, noted that a shared understanding of objectives, audiences and creative direction is essential to building effective partnerships. Prominent Nigerian creators, including Kiekie, Taoma, Aproko Doctor and Ify’s Kitchen, also shared perspectives on collaborating with brands through content that reflects their creative identities while meeting commercial objectives. In an interview, Babatunde Shobanjo, Chief Operating Officer of Insight Redefini, described the initiative as a positive development for the media and marketing communications industry, pointing to the value of creating platforms where brands and creators can explore new ways of working together. The emphasis on collaboration reflects Insight Redefini’s integrated approach to marketing communications. Earlier in 2026, agencies within its ecosystem, working with global partners, won a Gold Lion at the Cannes Lions International Festival of Creativity in the Creator Collaboration category for Vaseline’s The Real Nigerian Prince campaign. The event comes amid growing interest in digital video and creator-led content as platforms for brands to connect with audiences. YouTube previously reported that watch time in Nigeria grew by more than 50 per cent year on year in 2025, with the platform reaching more than 30 million adults in the country each month.

title: Israel’s election is being cast as a historic showdown - but four trends tell a different story
body: Night after night, or at least on the nights he anchors Channel 12’s nightly news, Danny Kushmaro introduces the election segment by calling them the most fateful elections in Israel’s history.And he is not alone. “Israel’s most important elections” or “Israel’s most fateful elections” has become a refrain of this campaign.It brings to mind a verse from Ecclesiastes (7:10): “Don’t say, ‘How was it that the former days were better than these?’ You would be asking an unwise question.”Kohelet cautions against romanticizing the good old days. Here’s a related lesson for Tuesday’s election: don’t assume that the current one is more fateful or important than all those that came before. That would be an unwise assumption.Besides, we seem to say that about almost every election.What about the December 1973 election, two months after the Yom Kippur War? That wasn’t critical? The 1977 election, which forever changed this country’s political landscape and brought Menachem Begin to power, wasn’t fateful? How about the 1996 election, just months after Yitzhak Rabin’s assassination? Or Ariel Sharon’s defeat of Ehud Barak in 2001, as the peace process with the Palestinians unraveled and the Second Intifada gathered force?Every election feels like the most fateful and important one. Ever.But perspective is needed.How 'fateful' elections turns political battles into existential warsAnd why does that matter? Because calling this the most important and fateful election ever turns the political competition, the battle between the pro-Netanyahu and anti-Netanyahu blocs, into nothing less than an existential matter. Defeat becomes harder to regard as a setback that can be corrected next time. Instead, it begins to sound like something the country cannot survive.And that can make accepting the outcome harder.Therein lies the problem.Since Naftali Bennett formed his government in 2021, Israel has struggled with more than the question of who should govern. It has struggled with whether the losing side will give the other side a chance to do so.Before Bennett’s government was even sworn in, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu branded its formation “the greatest election fraud.” He meant broken campaign promises, not stolen ballots. But the message cast a government formed legitimately through the parliamentary process as fraudulent and, therefore, illegitimate.From the minute Bennett’s government took office, the opposition worked tirelessly to bring it down. The main arena was the Knesset, where the coalition’s slim majority made every vote consequential.As a result, the opposition sometimes voted against legislation it supported, believing it would weaken the government. In recordings published in May 2022, Likud MK Miri Regev defended voting against measures benefiting soldiers and vulnerable groups because the overriding objective was to topple the coalition.The government spent much of its short life fighting for survival.Then Netanyahu won the 2022 election and formed his hard-right government. Suddenly, the shoe was on the other foot.Yair Lapid conceded the election and arranged an orderly handover. But as opposition to the judicial overhaul brought masses into the streets, the language of illegitimacy crept in again.For instance, at a massive demonstration in Tel Aviv in April 2023, former Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency) director Yuval Diskin said that while the government had been elected legally, it was morally illegitimate because of its “appalling composition and reprehensible actions.”By August, the Kaplan protest leadership was also calling the government illegitimate, amid questions about whether Netanyahu would obey the High Court. Once again, the distinction between fighting a government’s policies and denying its legitimacy was becoming blurred.Will Israel's next government have room to govern?That leaves a question hanging over Tuesday’s vote: will whichever government emerges be given room to govern, both in the Knesset and in the streets?Calling this election “the most fateful ever” hardly prepares the ground for that.If voters are told that the future of the country, and indeed the Jewish people, hangs in the balance, accepting defeat becomes that much harder.Are these elections consequential? Of course. So were many of those that came before. But at this critical juncture, the country also needs to accept and live with the results. Israel desperately needs a government given the space to govern.Accepting the outcome does not mean supporting the next government, abandoning opposition, or refraining from protest. Nor does winning an election give a government a blank check.But opposing a government’s policies is different from treating its very existence as illegitimate. There is a difference between working to replace a government and, from the outset, seeking to make governing impossible.That distinction must hold for whichever side wins.Magnifying the stakes may bring voters to the polls. But it may also do something this country can ill afford: make it harder afterward for the losing side to accept the results and let the winners govern.That is one takeaway from this campaign. Here are three more.Election's fiercest battles taking place within blocsDespite the characterization of these elections as the most fateful ever, the campaign has been relatively subdued: no televised debates between the leading candidates, no massive outdoor rallies. Much of the action has consisted of social media clips, interviews, and leaks to the press.And some of the fiercest fighting has taken place inside the blocs: Netanyahu vs Ofer Winter, Gadi Eisenkot vs Avigdor Liberman.In the anti-Netanyahu bloc, three candidates who regard themselves as worthy of the premiership have periodically sniped at one another: Eisenkot, Bennett, and Liberman. They share an interest in replacing Netanyahu, but each wants to be the one to do it.The sharper fighting, however, has been on the Right, where Netanyahu and Religious Zionist Party head Bezalel Smotrich have spent considerable energy trying to persuade Winter and his People of Israel party to withdraw.The stated concern is the electoral threshold. If Winter fails to cross the 3.25% bar, votes coming predominantly from the Right will not translate into seats.The cautionary tale is April 2019, when Bennett and Ayelet Shaked’s New Right narrowly missed the threshold. Had it crossed, Netanyahu could have formed a coalition, and the country would have been spared the dizzying spiral of repeat elections.But Winter also presents Netanyahu with an uncomfortable challenge from within his own political camp.The anti-Netanyahu parties say this government failed: failed to prevent October 7 and failed to achieve its declared objectives afterward, with Hamas, Hezbollah, and the Iranian regime still standing. Netanyahu can dismiss those charges as the familiar carping of his opponents.That is harder when Winter delivers a similar message from the Right.Winter’s emphasis on new faces – his list includes no one who has previously served in the Knesset – reflects his contention that the political leadership associated with October 7 needs to be replaced. His indictment extends across the Knesset, but it also challenges Netanyahu’s claim to be the leader best equipped to keep the country safe.The competition is therefore about more than whether Winter will waste right-wing votes. It is also about whether he will persuade right-wing voters that their own leadership has failed.The rival across the political divide challenges your policies. The rival on your own side challenges your claim to speak for your own camp.Polls are shaping Israel’s election, not just measuring itPolls are supposed to measure public opinion. Good polls reflect what the public thinks.In this campaign, however, polls don’t merely reflect opinion. They help shape it. And Israel’s electoral threshold gives them particular power to do so.Israelis famously don’t want to be freiers – suckers. They don’t want to vote for a party that falls below the 3.25% threshold and wins no representation, because they will feel, and are repeatedly told, that they wasted their vote.So voters wait to see whether polls show Winter’s party, or Yoaz Hendel and Yaron Zelekha’s party, crossing the threshold before deciding whether to support them. If the party looks likely to pass, they may vote for it. If not, they look elsewhere.The result is a circular process: voters consult the polls to decide whether a party is viable, while its viability depends on whether they will vote for it.A poll showing a small party below the threshold can frighten away the very voters who might otherwise put it over. One showing it above the threshold can give hesitant supporters the confidence to vote for it.At that point, the polls are doing more than reflecting opinion. They are shaping it.Their influence also extends to the choices available on the ballot. Benny Gantz’s withdrawal this week followed polls consistently showing his party below the threshold. The fledgling party led by Gilad Erdan and Yuli Edelstein withdrew before the lists were finalized, against a similar polling backdrop.Polls are critical in elections. They become a problem when they start to decide those elections.The airwaves and newspapers have been filled with candidate interviews. Netanyahu, Eisenkot, Lapid, Winter – everybody is getting airtime.And everybody is being asked a version of the same question: whom will you refuse to sit with in a coalition?It is a natural and legitimate question. Voters are entitled to know which government their vote might help bring into being.But insisting on unequivocal answers encourages candidates to make commitments before they know the parliamentary arithmetic they will have to work with.If candidate X promises never to sit with party Y or candidate Z, and then does precisely that, the recording of his promise will be played on an endless loop. The candidate will be branded a liar.Bennett’s signed pledge before the 2021 election not to allow Lapid to become prime minister, even through a rotation, and not to form a government dependent on Mansour Abbas is the obvious example. He subsequently formed precisely such a government.Did he break a campaign pledge? Obviously. But his defense was that the election results left a choice between breaking that promise and sending the country into yet another election. So here’s a formula for understanding politics: politicians don’t break promises; they encounter changed circumstances.That line might invite a knowing smirk, but it makes a serious point: coalition government requires compromise, and the election results determine which compromises will be necessary.If everyone adheres to every coalition veto issued during this campaign, the country may end up with plenty of promises intact and no government for a very long time. Politicians should leave room for compromise before the election, rather than making absolute promises they may have to abandon afterward for the good of the country.Changing course does not necessarily mean a lack of backbone. Sometimes it is what separates a functioning government from yet another round of inconclusive elections.

title: 7 Killed in Greek Orthodox Church Funeral Shooting in Jordan’s Karak
body: Two gunmen opened fire at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, killing at least 7 and wounding ~10. Security forces are pursuing the unidentified attackers. No motive confirmed. The source told the official Al-Mamlaka broadcaster that “at least seven people died in the shooting at Hammoud Church in Karak, while about 10 others were wounded, some of them critically” when two unidentified gunmen opened fire inside the church, according to authorities. An eyewitness told Al-Mamlaka that a vehicle arrived carrying the gunmen, who fired continuously for five minutes before fleeing the scene. Between 150 and 200 people were inside and around the church at the time, the witness said, adding that most of the victims were aged between 50 and 70. Security forces are investigating, Minister of Government Communications Mohammed Al-Momani said. Karak is home to a significant Christian community in the Muslim-majority kingdom. title: FACTBOX: Bank of Russia holds key rate at 14%
body:
MOSCOW, October 23. /TASS/. The Bank of Russia has decided to maintain its key rate at 14% per annum, stating that current price pressures remain elevated, according to the regulator's press release.
TASS has compiled the key details of the decision.
- The Bank of Russia's Board of Directors has decided to maintain the key rate at 14% per annum.
- The economy as a whole is growing at a moderate pace in the second half of 2026.
- Current price pressures remain elevated, and inflation expectations remain high.
- According to the Bank of Russia's assessment, underlying price growth is not slowing and remains within the 5-6% range on an annualized basis, primarily due to the impact of temporary capacity constraints in certain industries.
- This requires restrained growth in aggregate demand to resume a decline in underlying inflation, the Central Bank emphasized.
- The Bank of Russia noted that it will make further decisions on the key rate depending on inflation dynamics and inflation expectations, as well as an assessment of risks from domestic and external conditions.
- In Q3 2026, seasonally adjusted price growth averaged 8% on an annualized basis, up from 4.8% in Q2 2026.
- The corresponding core inflation rate increased to 6.2%, up from 4.5% in the previous quarter.
- Price dynamics continued to be influenced by volatile items, primarily motor fuel, the regulator noted.
- Annual inflation stood at 6.8% as of October 19 and is projected to settle within the 7.1-7.6% range by year-end.
- High inflation expectations are hindering a slowdown in inflation.
- Despite a slight decline in household and business expectations in October, overall, they have remained near their highest levels in two years in recent months, the Central Bank emphasized.
- The expectations of financial market participants and analysts have increased.
- According to high-frequency data, the economy is growing at a moderate pace in the second half of 2026.
- Business sentiment improved slightly in October following the low levels of previous months.
- Consumer demand growth is slowing but remains elevated, the Central Bank pointed out.
- Investment activity continues to recover compared to levels at the beginning of the year.
- Tensions in the labor market are gradually easing.
- According to surveys, the supply of workers at enterprises continues to improve, but the situation remains uneven across industries, the Central Bank noted.
- Wage growth is slowing and gradually converging with productivity growth.
- However, the gap in their dynamics remains significant, the regulator emphasized.
- At the same time, companies plan more moderate wage indexations in 2027 compared to 2026.
- Unemployment remains near historical lows.
- Lending activity was elevated on average in Q3 2026, driven primarily by the corporate segment.
- The retail loan portfolio grew moderately, the regulator noted.
- Households' propensity to save has declined somewhat but remains high.
- The Bank of Russia is proceeding from the announced fiscal policy parameters.
- Over the medium term, this will contribute to a slowdown in inflation.
- If fiscal policy parameters change, monetary policy may need to be adjusted, the regulator pointed out.
The ruble slowed its gains on the Moscow Exchange following the Bank of Russia's decision to maintain the key rate at 14% per annum, trading data showed.
Prior to the announcement, the yuan was trading at 12.037 rubles, down 12.8 kopecks, according to data as of 1:25 p.m. Moscow time.
By 1:30 p.m. Moscow time, the yuan paired its losses to 11.45 kopecks, trading at 12.05 rubles.
The MOEX Index turned lower following the central bank's decision to hold the key rate at 14% per annum, trading data showed.
As of 1:25 p.m. Moscow time, ahead of the rate announcement, the MOEX Index was up 0.22% at 2,434.74 points.
The RTS Index stood at 945.44 points, up 0.22%.
By 1:30 p.m. Moscow time, the MOEX Index reversed its gains to trade down 0.45% at 2,418.68 points.
The RTS Index also slid 0.45% to 939.21 points.

title: Man who teased governor on Facebook gets bail after one month in detention
body:
A Federal High Court in Jalingo, Taraba State, has granted bail to Fonya Sule, who was detained for about one month over a Facebook post concerning Governor Agbu Kefas and the All Progressives Congress (APC) deputy governorship candidate, Zainab Ibrahim.
Mr Sule was detained at the Jalingo Correctional Centre following a complaint by the Taraba State Government over the post, which allegedly defamed the governor and Ms Ibrahim, popularly known as Aunty Zee.
The state government, through the Office of the Attorney-General, filed the complaint on 30 September before the Upper Area Court in Jalingo.
Court documents seen by PREMIUM TIMES indicate that Mr Sule published the post on his Facebook page on 12 August.
The post read: “Aunty Zee be Very careful ooh, if not u will soon carry belle, that your boss na one time BuGu.”
Ms Ibrahim is the APC deputy governorship candidate in Taraba State for the 2027 election.
The state government alleged that the publication was intended to damage the reputations of the governor and Ms Ibrahim, describing it as criminal defamation and injurious falsehood.
The complaint, filed in suit number CM/138/28, was brought under Section 122(A) of the Taraba State Administration of Criminal Justice Law, 2021.
It was signed by the Director of Public Prosecutions, A. D. Mustapha, and four other state counsel. The prosecution cited Sections 392 and 393 of the Penal Code Law of Taraba State, 1997.
Mr Sule’s lawyer, Pius Danba, approached the Federal High Court in Jalingo to seek his client’s release on bail, arguing that the alleged offence was bailable and that the prosecution had yet to prove its case.
The court granted the bail application, according to Mr Danba, who spoke to journalists at the Jalingo Correctional Centre.
The lawyer said his client was presumed innocent until proven guilty by a competent court.
Mr Sule was arrested after the publication and remanded at the correctional centre pending the determination of the case.
There was no immediate information on the bail conditions or the next date for the proceedings.

title: Akatsico, UNCG deepen partnership for academic development
body: The Akatsi College of Education (Akatsico) and the University of North Carolina Greensboro (UNCG) in the United States have deepened their institutional partnership, with both institutions exploring opportunities in research, academic exchanges, professional development and international collaboration. The engagement, held at the Akatsico Conference Room, brought together the College Management, Heads of Departments and Heads of Units to discuss practical steps towards translating the partnership into sustainable and measurable academic activities. Dr Felix Kwame Kumedzro, Principal of Akatsico, said the engagement marked an important step towards transforming the emerging relationship between the two institutions into a sustainable partnership based on mutual benefit. He said the collaboration would focus on joint research and publications, faculty and staff development, faculty and student exchanges, as well as joint conferences, seminars and workshops. Dr Kumedzro said the College’s Governing Council had already approved the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with UNCG, expressing the expectation that the engagement would help both institutions develop a clear roadmap for implementing the partnership. He said Management was committed to moving beyond discussions to practical and measurable activities that aligned with the College’s vision of innovation, quality teacher education, research and internationalisation. Dr Morgan Chitiyo, Dean of the School of Education at UNCG, said the partnership would create opportunities for students and faculty of both institutions to broaden their global perspectives while strengthening research and professional development. He said the collaboration would also open opportunities for Akatsico staff and graduates to pursue graduate and doctoral programmes at UNCG in disciplines including Education, Business, Arts and Sciences. Dr Chitiyo said UNCG had limited funding, grants and scholarships available to support visiting students and faculty members undertaking programme upgrades or research, with successful PhD candidates potentially having opportunities to work as Research or Teaching Assistants. As part of the partnership, the first cohort of students from UNCG’s Department of Specialised Education Services is expected to visit Akatsico in November 2027 for a study programme. Senior representatives from UNCG are also expected to accompany the students to Ghana, providing an opportunity for academic interaction and knowledge exchange between students and faculty of the two institutions. Akatsico students are, in turn, expected to have opportunities to visit UNCG under the reciprocal exchange arrangement. The two institutions also agreed to explore the development of a dedicated e-learning platform to facilitate online collaboration in research, teaching and learning. The engagement further highlighted opportunities for joint research projects, academic publications and applications for research grants as key areas for strengthening the partnership. A hybrid conference scheduled for October 17, 2026, is also expected to provide an opportunity for educators, alumni and researchers from both institutions to participate in academic discussions. The College identified hosting partner students and faculty, securing research grants, producing joint publications and achieving qualitative impact on teacher education as some of the key indicators for measuring the success of the partnership. Dr Kumedzro reaffirmed Akatsico’s commitment to sustaining and nurturing the relationship, saying the partnership aligned with Theme Four of the College’s five-year Strategic Plan, which focuses on national and international partnerships for development. Akatsi College of Education, established in 1963, is a public College of Education in the Volta Region offering Bachelor of Education programmes in various disciplines. The College continues to pursue initiatives aimed at strengthening teaching, learning, research, professional development and institutional partnerships.

title: Netanyahu closes West Bank after thwarted potential ‘major attack’
body:
Two Palestinian gunmen were killed after the shooting, the IDF said.
Five people were injured in a shooting at an Israeli military checkpoint in the West Bank, sparking Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to close off the entire area in what he described as a thwarted potential "major attack."
Two Palestinian gunmen were killed by Israeli security forces after the shooting in Hebron, according to the Israel Defense Forces.
The shooting left five people injured, including two who were in critical condition, according to Israel’s Magen David Adom emergency medical service.
Speaking at the scene, IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir said the attackers’ vehicle contained large quantities of ammunition and weapons, leading him to believe they may have been planning a larger attack.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the closure of the entire West Bank in response, according to a statement. The IDF also launched what it described as a counterterrorism operation in Hebron and surrounding villages.
Hamas stopped short of claiming responsibility for the shooting but praised the attack and called on its supporters to carry out further attacks against Israeli soldiers and settlers.

title: Romania blames Russia for attacking cargo ship in Black Sea
body:
AFP reported this, according to Ukrinform.
In a Facebook post, Dan said the Comoros-flagged cargo ship Khoryv was "struck by a drone and sank near Romanian territorial waters."
Later, speaking to journalists, the Romanian President said the attack was part of an escalation by Russia amid its war against Ukraine. Romanian Prime Minister Luca Niculescu called the attack “unacceptable” and a flagrant violation of international law.

title: Court rejects key evidence in Dasuki’s N33.2bn trial
body:
The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) High Court in Maitama, Abuja, on Friday rejected key exhibits the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) presented to prove its N33.2billion fraud charges against former National Security Adviser (NSA) Sambo Dasuki and his co-defendant.
The rejected exhibits were seven extra-judicial statements attributed to Mr Dasuki’s co-defendant, Aminu Baba-Kusa. The EFCC took the statements when Mr Baba-Kusa was in its custody in 2015.
Trial judge Charles Agbaza rejected the seven extra-judicial statements in a ruling it delivered after nearly eight months of a trial-within-trial that focussed on the admissibility of the statements.
Mr Agbaza ruled that the statements “failed to comply with Sections 15(4) and 17(2) of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act.”
It is unclear yet how crucial the rejected statements are to the prosecution’s case.
The judge ruled that they could not be used in the case because the EFCC failed to provide “credible evidence that the seven statements complied with the provisions of the ACJA.”
Mr Baba-Kusa is a businessman and retired Group Executive Director (GED), Business Development of the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC).
Mr Dasuki and Mr Baba-Kusa are facing a joint trial for alleged diversion of N33.2 billion in arms and security funds entrusted to the NSA office.
The EFCC is prosecuting them alongside Mr Baba-Kusa’s companies, Acacia Holdings Limited and Reliance Referral Hospital Limited, which allegedly received part of the suspicious funds from the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) under Mr Dasuki’s supervision.
The trial has lasted over a decade, suffering spells of setbacks and adjournments that stalled its progress.
EFCC had to re-arraign the defendants in March last year after the case was reassigned to the current trial judge, Mr Agbaza, kicking off afresh after about 10 years of a complicated run.
They denied the charges again, as they previously did before the former judge.
The main trial paused again on 14 January, when the EFCC tried to tender Mr Baba-Kusa’s statements as evidence through its first prosecution witness presented so far in the main trial.
The judge ordered the trial-within-trial to test Mr Baba-Kusa’s claim, and the sub-trial commenced on 24 February.
Mr Baba-Kusa’s lawyer objected to the admissibility of the statements on the grounds that they were obtained under duress, prompting the judge to order a trial-within-trial to ascertain the voluntariness of the statements.
The defence argued that a statement made by someone while being held in the underground cell of the EFCC could not be said to have been freely made.
He also said there was no compliance with Section 15(4) and 17 (2) of the ACJA 2015.
The EFCC called three witnesses, all its investigators, during the trial-within-trial who testified about the circumstances surrounding how Mr Baba-Kusa’s statements were taken.
Salihu Kadir said Mr Baba-Kusa voluntarily wrote his extrajudicial statements without any form of coercion.
Mr Kadir said that there was a CCTV camera recording, but he urged the court to note that it was done about 10 years ago and was not mandatory under the law.
On 24 February, Halima Kazeem, an assistant commandant 1 at the EFCC, said he was treated well in custody in 2015.
Similarly, Michael Adariku, an assistant commander 2 at the EFCC, refuted the suggestion of detaining him in an underground cell during investigations in 2015.
When Mr Baba-Kusa, who testified in June as the sole defence witness in the trial-within-trial, confirmed that he wrote the statement and that cautionary words were administered to him before writing them.
However, on Friday, the judge rejected the statements because there was no audio-visual recording.
He ruled that the “aim of audio-visual recording is for the court to see the circumstances” that took place when the statements were taken, “whether voluntarily,” and not coerced by the prosecution.
EFCC’s lawyer Oluwaleke Atolagbe requested a copy of the ruling to study to decide the prosecution’s next steps, which could be an appeal or restrate
Thereafter, the judge adjourned the case until 13 November.
In the substantive trial, the EFCC has called one prosecution witness, Mr Adarikun, as the first prosecution witness.
Mr Adarikun narrated how N2.2 billion intended for election security was allegedly diverted from the NSA office under the leadership of Mr Dasuki.
So far, he has testified about transfers from the Office of the National Security Adviser’s account, with the approval of Mr Dasuki, to Mr Babba-Kusa, who allegedly used the proceeds to buy properties and foreign currencies in euros and dollars.
The decade-old trial suffered multiple adjournments in its early years, largely due to the State Security Services (SSS) refusing to release Mr Dasuki on bail in defiance of multiple court orders.
Mr Dasuki served as NSA between 2012 and 2015, in the heat of Boko Haram attacks in Nigeria’s North-east, under the administration of then-President Goodluck Jonathan.
The N33.2 billion fraud trial is one of the several cases the EFCC filed in the aftermath of the scandal of alleged diversion of funds meant for procurement of arms to firm up the Nigerian military’s offensive against Boko Haram terrorists between 2014 and 2015.
An audit panel, established by President Muhammadu Buhari following his 2015 election victory, found that approximately $2 billion for arms procurement was unaccounted for. These funds were managed by the NSA, led by Mr Dasuki.
Mr Dasuki is also standing trial alongside former Sokoto State Governor Attahiru Bafarawa, his son Sagir Bafarawa, former Minister of State for Finance Bashir Yuguda, and Dalhatu Investment Limited for N4.6 billion arms procurement fraud.
The charges accused them of diverting N4.6 billion from the NSA office’s account. The money was said to be meant for the procurement of arms to firm up the offensive against Boko Haram terrorists between 2014 and 2015.

title: Ukrainian media identifies Russian officers responsible for blockade, starvation of occupied Oleshky
body:
An investigation by Ukrainian media outlet Slidstvo.info published on Oct. 23 has uncovered the identities of Russian officers involved in the blockade of the city of Oleshky in Kherson Oblast.
The Russian-occupied city, located just across the Dnipro River from Kherson , has been effectively blockaded by Russian forces in the area, who prevent humanitarian aid from entering. Civilians attempting to flee via the only roads in and out of the city are frequently targeted by drones.
Building on a previous investigation published in late September that identified the commanders of the Russian 126th Coast Guard Brigade of the Black Sea Fleet and the 331st Guards Airborne Regiment as operating in the area, Slidstvo.info established the presence of the 217th Guards Airborne Regiment and its commander, Georgy Yanchev.
According to the Oct. 23 investigation , the 217th Regiment previously took part in the Battle of Kyiv at the outset of Russia's full-scale invasion and later fought in Chasiv Yar, one of the main hotspots of fighting in Donetsk Oblast.
Yanchev, who has served in the Russian military since 1993 and holds the rank of colonel, has three children who live in the central Russian city of Samara.
Oleshky has been under Russian occupation since the early days of the full-scale invasion. Residents face severe shortages of food, water, and electricity, while mined roads, constant drone attacks, and interrogations by Russian troops at checkpoints make safe evacuation virtually impossible.
As the humanitarian crisis in the city has grown increasingly severe this autumn, international pressure to provide assistance to the remaining residents trapped inside has mounted.
On Oct. 16, Pope Leo XIV expressed concern over the worsening situation in Oleshky during a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
The pope called for a local ceasefire to allow humanitarian aid deliveries and the safe evacuation of civilians from the front-line city, where around 2,000 residents remain trapped amid severe shortages of food and medicine.
Ukraine and Russia are nearing an agreement on the final details of civilian evacuation from Oleshky and nearby settlements, Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said on Oct. 18.
In the meantime, Ukrainian soldiers fighting on the western bank of the Dnipro have made repeated deliveries of food aid to the area by drone.

title: Malaria: Nigeria’s prevalence drops to 15.2%, FG targets 50% reduction by 2030
body: By Chioma Obinna The Federal Government has reported a decline in malaria parasite prevalence among children aged six to 59 months from 22 per cent in 2021 to 15.2 per cent in 2025, while setting a target to halve malaria prevalence and malaria-attributable deaths by 2030. The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, disclosed this on Thursday at the launch of the 2025 Nigeria Malaria Indicator Survey (NMIS) Report and the National Malaria Strategic Plan 2026–2030 in Abuja. Pate, who was represented by the ministry’s Permanent Secretary, Daju Kachollom, said the 6.8 percentage-point decline reflected progress in the country’s malaria control efforts but warned that the gains must be sustained. He said the Federal Government was targeting a 50 per cent reduction in malaria prevalence and malaria-attributable deaths from their respective 2025 levels by 2030. The minister, however, cautioned against interpreting the decline as evidence that malaria had been brought under control nationwide, stressing the need for stronger prevention, surveillance and funding. He cited Kebbi State as an example of significant improvement, with malaria prevalence reportedly dropping from 49 per cent in 2021 to 18 per cent in 2025. Pate said the findings underscored the importance of using reliable data to identify high-burden communities and direct interventions where they would have the greatest impact. Bed-net use remains a concern The minister also highlighted the need to improve the consistent use of insecticide-treated nets, a major tool for preventing malaria transmission. According to the survey findings, 72.3 per cent of children and 80.6 per cent of pregnant women in households that owned insecticide-treated nets slept under one. He said the figures demonstrated the need to strengthen public awareness and ensure that households translated access to preventive tools into consistent use. New strategy targets high-burden areas Pate said the National Malaria Strategic Plan 2026–2030 was aligned with the Nigeria Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative and would be implemented through the Sector-Wide Approach, guided by the principle of “One Plan, One Budget, One Report, One Conversation.” He explained that the plan’s sub-national tailoring approach would enable authorities to direct resources and interventions according to the malaria burden and epidemiological circumstances of individual states and communities. The minister urged state governments to take ownership of their respective survey findings, align malaria control plans and budgets with identified needs, and ensure timely release of funds. He also called on development partners to align their financial and technical support with national priorities. NPC calls for data-driven interventions The Director-General of the National Population Commission, Dr Abuh Muhammed, said the survey demonstrated the value of collaboration between the National Malaria Elimination Programme and the commission. He said the partnership combined technical expertise in malaria control with the commission’s survey infrastructure and field operations, providing evidence to guide national planning. Muhammed reaffirmed the commission’s commitment to supporting evidence-based policymaking and urged government officials and development partners to use the findings to direct resources to areas with the greatest need. Pate commended the National Malaria Elimination Programme, the National Population Commission and other partners involved in producing the survey. He reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to strengthening domestic financing, improving surveillance and sustaining coordinated action to reduce malaria cases and deaths. The 2030 target will require sustained investment in prevention, early diagnosis, effective treatment and routine health services, alongside targeted interventions in communities where malaria transmission remains high.
