title: First Lady Melania Trump Secures Ceasefire Between Russia and Ukraine, Localized to Oleshky
body: Office of the First Lady Briefings & Statements Search Select Category All News Briefings & Statements All Presidential Actions Executive Orders Nominations & Appointments Presidential Memoranda Proclamations Fact Sheets Releases Remarks Research All Briefings & Statements Presidential Actions All Executive Orders Nominations & Appointments Presidential Memoranda Proclamations Fact Sheets Releases Remarks Research First Lady Melania Trump successfully secured a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, localized to the city of Oleshky. Both nations agreed to temporarily stop all military action in Oleshky to allow for humanitarian aid to enter and to prepare a civilian evacuation through a designated safe passageway. The localized ceasefire will begin on October 29, 2026. “The situation in Oleshky is dire. Oleshky is a front-line war city on the brink of disaster. Oleshky’s remaining population is comprised primarily of elderly residents who urgently need medical attention, medicine, food, and clean water,” said First Lady Melania Trump. “The people of Oleshky have limited electricity, live amid mined roads, and endure regular military attacks. It was abundantly clear that without my intervention, the possibility to bring humanitarian aid into the city and to evacuate the elderly would be impossible.” First Lady Melania Trump and her representative worked directly with Russian and Ukrainian leadership to define the terms of the localized ceasefire. The First Lady initiated discussions with both nations and aligned the parties on the agreement’s objectives, technical procedures, timing, processes, and terms, in her formal role as Exclusive Intermediary. “Non-military, civilian leaders from both countries will work together to visit Oleshky residents in their homes and determine the level of assistance they require. Residents who wish to evacuate will receive coordinated support and transportation to their preferred destination. I anticipate some will want to go to Russia, and some to Ukraine,” said First Lady Melania Trump. The First Lady continued, “I have also secured an impartial American media organization to accompany and document Russian and Ukrainian teams on the ground throughout the process. This will play a significant role in ensuring that the wishes of each family are faithfully respected.” The exigent circumstances of Oleshky came to First Lady Melania Trump’s attention during a private discussion at her Fostering the Future Together event in New York City during the 81st United Nations General Assembly. “My representative and I immediately leveraged the communication channel we established with Russia and Ukraine through the previous six reunifications of 34 children. Both nations promptly assigned teams to coordinate the complex mechanics involved, including demining. All parties have worked around the clock since that moment,” explained First Lady Melania Trump. All media inquiries for the Office of the First Lady should be directed to OFLPress@who.eop.gov . About Oleshky Oleshky is located in southern Ukraine, directly across from the Dnipro River in Kherson. Before the war, roughly 24,000 people lived in Oleshky. Today, an estimated 1700-2000 residents remain, primarily older people who have been unable to leave, along with approximately 50 children. There has not been a formal demographic count in Oleshky since 2022. Since the war began, the city has remained on the front line, with much of its population displaced or evacuated. Following the destruction of the Kakhovka Dam, approximately 90 percent of the city’s territory was flooded. title: Ogogo’s daughters announce Nollywood plans, pledge to sustain father’s legacy
body: By Adegboyega Adeleye The daughters of late Nollywood actor Taiwo Hassan, popularly known as Ogogo, say they plan to pursue careers in the film industry and continue their father’s legacy. Taiwo Halima Olamide, known as Lima Ogogo, and her sister, Shakirat Taiwo, popularly called Kira Ogogo, announced their plans in an appreciation video shared on social media on Wednesday, October 21. The sisters also thanked Nigerians and members of the entertainment industry for supporting their family following their father’s death. “You guys loved our daddy so much. This is an appreciation video to tell you people thank you,” they said. Lima, speaking on behalf of the family, added: “On behalf of my family and I, we want to say thank you very much to everybody who stood by us.” The sisters acknowledged support from several public figures, including Honourable Tayo Ayinde, the First Lady, the Ogun State governor, Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, and the Olu of Ilaro. They also thanked those who sent messages of condolence during the family’s period of mourning. They said their entry into Nollywood would be a lasting commitment, rather than a one-off tribute to their father. “We are going to start seeing Ogogo through my sister Kira Ogogo. We are coming to the industry, and we’re here to stay,” Lima said. The sisters urged fans who enjoyed Ogogo’s films to support their upcoming projects by watching and sharing their content, particularly on Kira Ogogo’s YouTube channel, KiraOgogoTV. Ogogo, a prominent figure in Yoruba cinema, died on August 23, 2026, aged 66. He was buried the following day in Ilaro, Ogun State, according to Islamic rites. His death drew tributes from Nollywood colleagues and admirers. The post Ogogo’s daughters announce Nollywood plans, pledge to sustain father’s legacy appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Bayelsa Assembly approves state police, takes first reading of two bills
body: By Emem Idio, Yenagoa The Bayelsa State House of Assembly has approved the proposed establishment of State Police Services, joining other state legislatures in endorsing the constitutional amendment aimed at decentralising policing in Nigeria. The approval followed the passage of the Sixth Alteration Bill by the National Assembly and its subsequent transmission to the 36 state Houses of Assembly for consideration, as required by the constitutional amendment process. Speaking shortly after the approval, on Wednesday, the Speaker of the House, Rt. Hon. Michael Ogbere, thanked members for their consideration and endorsement of the proposed State Police Services. In a related development, the House has taken the first readings of two bills: the Ijaw Cultural Heritage Bill and the Retirement Age for Magistrates and Chairmen of Customary Courts Bill, 2026. The bills are expected to proceed through the legislative process for further consideration by the lawmakers. title: 14 countries offering visa on arrival to Nigerians in 2026
body: Nigerian passport holders can travel to several countries where they can obtain a visa upon arrival, eliminating the need to secure a conventional visa from an embassy before departure. The destinations span Africa, Asia, the Middle East and the Pacific, offering options for Nigerians planning holidays, business trips and other short visits. A visa on arrival (VoA) allows eligible travellers to obtain a visa at an authorised airport, seaport or border crossing. However, the facility does not automatically guarantee entry, as immigration officials may require supporting documents and evidence that visitors meet the country’s entry conditions. According to VisaChecker’s September 2026 data, 14 destinations offer visa-on-arrival access to Nigerian passport holders. Passport Index also identifies several destinations under this category, although the figures reported by different databases vary. Here are 14 countries Nigerians can consider when planning international trips. African countries offering visa on arrival to Nigerians 1. Burundi Burundi, an East African country known for its mountainous landscapes and Lake Tanganyika, offers Nigerian passport holders a visa-on-arrival option. Passport Index lists the facility as allowing stays of up to 30 days. Travellers should confirm whether advance authorisation or additional documentation is required before departure. 2. Comoros Comoros, an island nation in the Indian Ocean off the eastern coast of Africa, is another destination Nigerians can access through a visa-on-arrival arrangement. Passport Index lists a permitted stay of up to 45 days for eligible Nigerian visitors. Travellers should verify the applicable fees and entry procedures before travelling. 3. Djibouti Djibouti, located in the Horn of Africa, offers Nigerian passport holders visa-on-arrival and electronic visa options, according to Passport Index. The database lists a maximum stay of up to 90 days under the visa-on-arrival category. Travellers should confirm which application route applies to their circumstances and intended port of entry. 4. Madagascar Madagascar, an island country off the southeastern coast of Africa, is known for its distinctive wildlife, rainforests and beaches. Nigerian passport holders are listed as eligible for visa-on-arrival access, with Passport Index indicating a stay of up to 90 days. An electronic visa is also listed as an option. Travellers should check the latest requirements before choosing between the available routes. 5. Mauritius Mauritius is a popular Indian Ocean destination known for its beaches, lagoons and resorts. Passport Index lists visa-on-arrival access for Nigerian citizens for stays of up to 14 days. Because the permitted period is relatively short, travellers intending to stay longer should establish the appropriate immigration route before booking. 6. Mozambique Mozambique, located in southeastern Africa, offers Nigerian passport holders a visa-on-arrival option. Passport Index lists a maximum stay of up to 30 days. Visitors should confirm the conditions attached to the facility and ensure they have the necessary travel documents before departure. Asian and Middle Eastern countries offering visa on arrival 7. Cambodia Cambodia, in Southeast Asia, is known for its historical temples, including the Angkor Wat complex, as well as its cultural attractions. Passport Index lists both an electronic visa and visa-on-arrival options for Nigerian passport holders, with the latter allowing stays of up to 30 days. Travellers should confirm the approved entry points, applicable fees and documentation requirements before travelling. 8. Iran Iran is listed among destinations offering Nigerian passport holders a visa-on-arrival option. However, travellers should exercise particular care when checking current entry rules, eligible entry points and any prior approval requirements. They should also review relevant travel advisories before making arrangements. 9. Lebanon Lebanon, on the eastern coast of the Mediterranean Sea, is another destination listed as offering visa-on-arrival access to Nigerian passport holders. Passport Index lists a stay of up to 30 days. Additional requirements may apply, and travellers should confirm their eligibility directly with Lebanese authorities or the relevant diplomatic mission before departure. 10. Maldives The Maldives offers a 30-day tourist visa on arrival to visitors of all nationalities, subject to immigration requirements. According to the Maldives Immigration Service, tourists do not need pre-approval for this visa. However, visitors must have a machine-readable passport with at least one month of validity, confirmed return or onward tickets, a prepaid booking at a registered tourist facility and sufficient funds, or an approved sponsorship arrangement. Travellers must also complete the required Traveller Declaration electronically within 96 hours before arrival. Meeting the requirements does not guarantee admission, which remains subject to immigration clearance. 11. Timor-Leste Timor-Leste, a Southeast Asian country occupying the eastern part of Timor island, offers visa-on-arrival access to eligible visitors. The country’s tourism information states that tourists arriving at Presidente Nicolau Lobato International Airport in Dili can generally obtain a 30-day visa on arrival for US$30. Travellers should have a passport valid for at least six months, a return or onward ticket, proof of accommodation and sufficient funds. An online arrival declaration is also required. Different procedures may apply to those entering through land borders. Pacific and island destinations offering visa on arrival 12. Palau Palau, an island country in the western Pacific Ocean, offers a 30-day tourist visa on arrival, according to published entry guidance. Visitors may be required to show proof of onward or return travel. They must also complete the country’s entry form within 72 hours before arrival and sign the Palau Pledge, a commitment to protect the country’s natural environment and respect local traditions. Nigerians should confirm the latest requirements with Palau’s Bureau of Immigration before travelling. 13. Samoa Samoa, an island country in the South Pacific, allows visitors to apply for a visitor permit on arrival. Its Ministry of the Prime Minister and Cabinet states that visitors can apply for a permit valid for up to 90 days using the arrival card. Travellers must have a passport valid for at least six months beyond their intended stay, a confirmed return or onward ticket, any necessary visa for their next destination, sufficient funds and a confirmed residential contact address. Employment is not permitted under the visitor permit. 14. Tuvalu Tuvalu, a small island nation in the Pacific Ocean, is also listed by Passport Index as offering visa-on-arrival access to Nigerian passport holders, with a stay of up to 30 days. Travellers should confirm the latest entry conditions, available entry points and any documentation requirements with the relevant authorities before booking flights. What Nigerians should know before travelling Although a visa on arrival can make international travel more convenient, it does not mean a traveller can board a flight without preparation. Nigerian passport holders should take the following steps before travelling: 1. Confirm eligibility. Check the destination’s official immigration website or contact its embassy to establish whether Nigerian ordinary passport holders qualify for a visa on arrival. 2. Check passport validity. Many countries require passports to remain valid for at least six months, although the rules differ by destination. 3. Prepare supporting documents. These may include confirmed return tickets, accommodation bookings, evidence of sufficient funds and details of the purpose of the visit. 4. Check entry points. Some countries issue visas on arrival only at designated international airports or seaports. Arriving through an unapproved border crossing could require a different visa arrangement. 5. Confirm fees and payment methods. Visa fees and accepted payment methods vary. Travellers should establish the exact amount and whether cash is required before departure. 6. Check for additional authorisation. Some destinations require an electronic declaration, registration or advance authorisation even when a visa is issued on arrival. 7. Confirm requirements with the airline. Airlines may check a passenger’s eligibility and travel documents before boarding. Travellers should verify the applicable rules before purchasing non-refundable tickets. Visa policies can change, and immigration officers retain the authority to refuse entry when a traveller does not meet the applicable conditions. Nigerians should therefore verify the latest requirements directly with the destination country’s immigration authorities before making final travel arrangements. body: Without IDF soldiers stopping two Hamas terrorists on Friday morning, a major attack would likely have been made targeting civilians, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said. "Our forces are operating with reinforcements to thwart terrorism and are carrying out extensive waves of arrests," Netanyahu also said. It starts by insisting that every life is sacred, that everyone is created in God's image. For now: Shabbat Shalom, to everyone who believes in the hard work of making peace & justice a reality, for everyone.— Brad Lander (@bradlander) October 23, 2026Lander reiterated his opposition to Israel's presence in the West Bank, while stressing that violence would not bring about peace."I've spoken out loudly this week against Israel's occupation of the West Bank, which imposes violence on a daily basis, and I will continue to do so," he wrote. "But violence is not the path to ending it — or to achieving safety, freedom, and peace for both Palestinians and Israelis."Lander also criticized Netanyahu's response to the attack, accusing him of threatening collective punishment against Palestinians."And neither is collective punishment or ethnic cleansing of an entire neighborhood, or punishing millions of people for the criminal act of two, which Netanyahu has promised to enact in response," Lander wrote.Reflecting on his experiences in the West Bank over the past week, Lander said he would share more about his visit in the coming days, adding that he was preparing to return home."There is a path to ending this excruciating cycle of violence. It starts by insisting that every life is sacred, that everyone is created in God's image," he wrote."For now: Shabbat Shalom, to everyone who believes in the hard work of making peace & justice a reality, for everyone," Lander concluded.Jerusalem Post Staff contributed to this report.

title: Quebec coroner’s report questions suicide conclusion in death of 18-year-old
body:
Warning: This story includes the topic of suicide. Please read at your own discretion.
For Emmanuel Diafouka’s parents, the fight for answers has never stopped.
On Jan. 30, 2025, their 18-year-old son was found dead from a gunshot wound to the head in a park in Dollard-des-Ormeaux.
Police concluded his death was a suicide and the family says investigators closed the case in less than a week.
But his family never accepted that explanation.
Now, a coroner’s report says that while Diafouka died of a close-range gunshot injury to the head and that DNA and other evidence pointed him handling the weapon, there was insufficient evidence to conclude that he intended to kill himself.
“I will not say that we are happy – it’s not the word I can use – but it’s like they gave us some hope regarding the next step,” said Jean-François Diafouka, the boy’s father.
The coroner’s report also identifies the weapon as a shortened .22 calibre semi-automatic rifle, which is a prohibited firearm.
His parents want to know where the gun came from and whether someone else was involved in their son’s death.
“For me it’s clear that there’s other people involved in the death of my son,” said Jean-François. “Since the beginning, that’s my point.”
The family, which has involved the Center for Research-Action on Race Relations (CRARR) in their quest to get answers, say they also believe race is part of the story. They question whether enough was done to get to the bottom of their son’s death.
“It shows the need for the police department, any police department, to be more rigorous and sensitive when dealing with the death of a youth under very mysterious circumstances,” said Fo Niemi, CRARR’s executive director.
Global News reached out to the Montreal police for comment but have yet to hear back.
A complaint filed last year with the Police Ethics Commissioner over Montreal police’s handling of the case is still awaiting a decision.
The family continues to demand that police reopen the investigation into Emmanuel’s death.
If you or someone you know is in crisis and needs help, resources are available. In case of an emergency, please call 911 for immediate help.
For immediate mental health support, call 988. For a directory of support services in your area, visit the Canadian Association for Suicide Prevention at suicideprevention.ca.
Learn more about preventing suicide with these warning signs and tips on how to help .

title: Counterfeit Products: Ex-NBA Secretary Seeks Life Sentence, N20m Fine
body: Wale Igbintade A former Secretary of the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), Adebisi Iyaniwura, has petitioned the Senate to consider life imprisonment for aggravated counterfeiting offences, a minimum fine of N20 million and a mandatory 10-year jail term as part of proposed measures to curb the circulation of fake and adulterated products in Nigeria. In a petition dated October 21, 2026, and received at the Federal Secretariat in Abuja, Iyaniwura urged the Senate Committees on Industry, Trade and Investment and Health to initiate amendments to existing laws governing the production, importation, distribution and sale of counterfeit and unwholesome products. He also addressed the petition to the Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, seeking coordinated legislative and executive action against what he described as a serious threat to public health, consumer safety and national security. The legal practitioner expressed concern over the continued circulation of counterfeit goods in Nigerian markets, warning that unscrupulous manufacturers, importers, distributors and traders were exposing consumers to products capable of causing serious illness, injury and death. Describing the practice as a “satanic act”, Iyaniwura accused some business operators of placing profits above human lives. “Nigerians are daily being killed by the satanic acts of unscrupulous business people in their desperation to make profits at the cost of Nigerians’ blood,” he wrote. He argued that counterfeiting should not be treated merely as commercial fraud, given its potential consequences for public health, consumer safety and legitimate businesses. Among the products identified in the petition are food items, pharmaceuticals and automobile spare parts. According to him, consumers who unknowingly purchase counterfeit products risk suffering financial losses, serious health complications and, in some circumstances, death. He warned that fake food products and medicines could expose consumers to harmful substances or products that fail to meet established safety and quality standards. He also raised concerns about substandard automobile components, which could compromise vehicle safety and contribute to fatal road accidents. To address the problem, Iyaniwura called for amendments to existing legislation to introduce stiffer penalties capable of deterring individuals and businesses involved in the manufacture, importation, storage, distribution and sale of counterfeit products. Under his proposal, offenders would face a minimum fine of N20 million and a mandatory 10-year prison sentence, while life imprisonment would be considered for aggravated offences warranting the most severe punishment under the proposed framework. He maintained that tougher sanctions would send a clear message that the deliberate manufacture and distribution of potentially dangerous products for financial gain should attract serious criminal consequences. Beyond imprisonment and fines, the former NBA secretary called for the forfeiture of premises, properties and other assets linked to counterfeiting operations. He proposed that such assets be forfeited in accordance with applicable proceeds-of-crime legislation, arguing that the measure would help authorities deprive offenders of the financial benefits of the illegal trade and disrupt the networks sustaining it. Another major proposal is the introduction of provisions requiring counterfeit-related cases to be concluded within 90 days. He argued that prolonged prosecutions could undermine enforcement efforts and allow alleged offenders to continue operating while cases remain pending. He therefore urged lawmakers to consider measures to expedite the determination of cases involving the production, importation, storage and distribution of counterfeit goods. The proposed 90-day timeline would, however, require careful consideration of court procedures, evidential requirements and the capacity of the justice system to ensure timely adjudication without compromising fair hearing and due process. In addition to tougher penalties and expedited trials, Iyaniwura proposed mandatory QR-code traceability for consumable products nationwide, beginning with pharmaceuticals. Under the proposed system, QR codes would enable consumers and regulatory authorities to verify product information and trace goods through the supply chain. He argued that the technology could help identify suspicious products, establish their origins, track distribution channels and support investigations into suspected counterfeiting. The petitioner maintained that combating counterfeiting required a comprehensive approach combining tougher criminal sanctions, asset forfeiture, faster prosecution and improved product-tracking systems. He also highlighted the implications for legitimate businesses, which face unfair competition when counterfeit products are sold alongside genuine goods. The petition was received at the Federal Secretariat in Abuja on October 21, 2026. No formal response from the relevant Senate committees or the Attorney General of the Federation was included in the information provided.

title: New tax laws: Commercial drivers still face multiple highway taxes — NURTW
body: …Tax Ombud pledges fairness, transparency in tax administration By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief Commercial drivers across Nigeria are still being subjected to multiple highway taxes despite the Federal Government’s tax reforms aimed at eliminating the practice, the National Union of Road Transport Workers (NURTW) has said. The union lamented that a driver travelling from Calabar to Kano could spend as much as ₦300,000 on the road on various taxes and levies imposed by different collectors. The NURTW made the allegation at a stakeholders’ engagement forum on tax administration in Abuja on Friday, calling on the three tiers of government to urgently end the practice, which it said was imposing a heavy burden on transport operators and undermining the economy. Speaking on behalf of the union’s National President, Alh. Musiliu Akinsanya, popularly known as MC Oluomo, Suleiman Danzaki, the Senior Special Adviser on Intergovernmental and International Affairs, said commercial drivers were yet to experience any significant change in the multiple taxation of their operations nationwide. “A driver travelling from Calabar to Kano will spend as much as ₦300,000 on the road before he can get to his destination because of the various people on the road collecting various types of taxes,” Danzaki said. He expressed concern that, apart from overburdening transport operators, the practice could also be depriving governments of revenue, as some collectors allegedly issued receipts printed privately rather than official government receipts. Danzaki urged the federal, state and local governments to take immediate and coordinated action to eliminate multiple taxation, warning that the burden on commercial drivers had wider implications for the cost of transportation, the movement of goods and the nation’s economy. However, the Tax Ombud, Dr. John Nwabueze, assured taxpayers that his office was working to promote fairness, transparency and accountability in the country’s tax administration. Nwabueze spoke at the forum, themed “Promoting Fairness in Tax and Revenue Administration in Nigeria,” which was organised to gather complaints and identify challenges confronting taxpayers, with a view to improving compliance and ensuring a more efficient tax system. He said the tax reforms, which commenced in January 2026, were designed to simplify compliance, strengthen revenue mobilisation, support eligible small businesses and promote transparency and accountability. However, he stressed that the success of the reforms would depend not only on the quality of the laws but also on their fair and consistent implementation. “Fairness is not a favour to taxpayers; it is the foundation of public trust and sustainable revenue mobilisation,” he said. According to him, taxpayers are more likely to comply voluntarily when they are treated fairly, understand their obligations and have access to impartial channels for resolving disputes. Conversely, he warned that arbitrary assessments, overlapping levies and inconsistent enforcement could undermine public confidence in the tax system. Nwabueze said the establishment of the Office of the Tax Ombud under the Joint Revenue Board of Nigeria (Establishment) Act, 2025, marked a significant milestone in protecting taxpayers’ rights and strengthening accountability in tax administration. He said the office was mandated to promote lawful, reasonable, transparent and fair administrative processes while encouraging constructive dialogue and accountability among taxpayers and revenue authorities. Since its establishment, he added, the office had made progress in developing a digital complaints management framework, building stakeholder partnerships, introducing taxpayer education initiatives and establishing a dedicated call centre. “Our priority now is to expand access, strengthen operational capacity and ensure that taxpayers know where to turn when they experience administrative difficulties,” he said. The Tax Ombud identified five pillars of fairness required to balance the government’s revenue needs with the rights and dignity of taxpayers. They are equity and proportionality; procedural justice; professionalism, courtesy and respect in tax administration; transparency and accountability; and the protection of vulnerable taxpayers. He urged tax authorities to translate the principles into practical improvements in taxpayers’ everyday experiences by applying the law consistently, communicating obligations clearly and treating taxpayers with dignity. The engagement came amid concerns over the effectiveness of tax reforms in addressing longstanding complaints about multiple levies, overlapping demands and the conduct of revenue collectors across the country. The post New tax laws: Commercial drivers still face multiple highway taxes — NURTW appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Andre Onana involved in car crash
body: Manchester United goalkeeper, on loan with Turkish side Trabzonspor, Andre Onana was involved in a car crash on Thursday evening. According to the report, Onana was “reportedly rushed to hospital after being caught up in a high-speed car crash for medical checks before being discharged.” Medical tests concluded that the goalkeeper had “no problems” following the incident, as confirmed by Trabzonspor. A spokesperson for the club is reported to have told local media: “Andre Onana was involved in a road traffic accident earlier this evening. “There are no problems with him, and we wish him a speedy recovery.” The reports indicate that Onana’s car was crashed into by another vehicle while travelling at what is described to have been “high speed.” The impact from this initial crash is then said to have caused Onana to collide with the vehicle in front of him. Andre Onana is yet to make a formal statement following the crash, but further updates are expected soon.

title: Badasky: Let’s Make Wedding Gowns More African
body: Oghenevwede Ohwovoriole in Abuja A Kaduna based fashion designer and CEO, Badasky Fashion House, Grace Barnabas Pati, known as “Badasky,” has called for the need for African brides to be more African in their wedding gowns. She made the call in a chart with Thisday in an interview on the fashion industry in Kaduna and Nigeria as a whole. Grace pati said, she has been an advocate of African brides wearing African fabrics during wedding ceremonies because it will help to promote our culture and tradition. “I’m an advocate of let African brides or let people embrace their root in terms of my wedding collection I have this collection I call the root collection these collections are made with African prints African fabrics fused with a touch of Western designs. “When we talk about wedding dresses the first thing that comes to our mind is just the white dress but for me I find it boring so I feel we have so much rich fabrics rich cultural heritage that we can showcase, and let it reflect in our dresses so, I’ve been pushing for Africans to start wearing African wedding dresses so I can’t wait to see the day that most brides will walk down the aisle in their African wedding dresses instead of just the regular white dresses so I believe maybe if I keep on going in the next five to ten years one day this will come to reality.” Speaking on her brand she, said “Our brand is focused on wedding dresses and mostly female dresses for special occasions or people that just want something different and unique from the common designs you see out there. “My personal styling aesthetic at Badaski is a blend of African cultural heritage and modern Western designs. I love using African fabrics like Ankara, Adire, Ashoke anything traditional but that doesn’t mean I don’t use other fabrics so I tend to fuse them to give them that contemporary touch.” “When working with clients, I listen to their preferences and understand their personalities then create styles that suit their individual taste while adding my own creative touch. I like when a client looks unique. When I have a bride, I don’t want her to, I want when you see this bride you should be able to tell that this is a Badasky bride but there are instances where the bride will be like I want this particular design from another designer. “Yes, we can go with her design but I will try to structure the design in a way that it will still look unique that you can be able to tell the difference between my design and the other designer so it always have that Badasky touch.” she emphasised On the Nigerian designer she admires, she said, “I love Tubor “Sandrah Tubobereni” and the reason why I love Tubor is each piece of hers tells a story especially her bridal collections like you can see there is a connection between the bride and the dress. There are stories behind the dress just like my own designs, so I can relate with Tubor and I love how she does her presentations and the detailing of her dresses. I try my best to do my own detailings in my own way and I also try as much as to pay attention to details and my bride’s personality.” Speaking on trending designs she said, “Personally I’m someone that don’t like to focus much on trends because trends come and go. I believe as a designer you shouldn’t be someone that just moves with the trend. You should try to always make things that are timeless. “There are timeless designs that whether after some years people will still wear this design and they will love it. It will not look outdated so honestly I’m not a designer that works with trend though once in a while you might pick something and just spice up your work but I don’t depend heavily on trends. I try to work with designs that I think they are going to be timeless and will be appreciated.” “In my work I envision each of my piece my bridal piece or my collections as a work of art and with art there is no time there is no trend. Art is timeless. There are some artwork that have been even before our parents were born and now they are like in museums and people see them and still appreciate them. “That is how I want my work to be seen and sometimes trends can make you lose your own personal touch. I believe every business has the way they are structured or their own personal touch.” She also spoke on challenges faced by designers in the industry saying, “one of the major challenges we face if you ask most fashion designers is electricity. We face serious problem with electricity because our work is heavily dependent on it; you need electricity for your machines, ironing, and lots of things in the fashion space. “Another challenge we face sometimes could be logistic problems, sometimes you might finish your own parts, do your own good job but I think the logistic system here is still growing so sometimes it can be challenging. “You could send a dress to a client and then the logistic company says it will get to your client between this period and then the clothes doesn’t get delivered between that period. The client gets upset and starts asking for refunds. Sometimes because of the exchange rate for our international clients and then maybe you want to send via the international courier services the prices might be so high. “Sometimes the price of shipping a heavy wedding dress might be too high and discourages the bride from wanting to place an another order. “Another challenge in the fashion industry is that a lot of times some fashion designers tend to copy when you come up with some unique styles and then someone out of the blue just copies it meaning we don’t have respect for someone’s intellectual property here. “Though I know there are some designers that have made it clear when you copy their designs they’re going to sue you but I’m just saying it’s not a common thing. “it’s a challenge especially when you really work hard to bring that design to life. There should be stricter measures to protect intellectual property in the industry.” She urged government to guarantee constant power to grow the economy and ensure strict regulations on logistics companies. “Almost every businesses in Nigeria including the fashion industry needs constant power supply; the first thing the government should do for us is to make sure we have constant power supply. I believe if the issue of electricity is solved a lot of our lives problems are solved over 80% because with electricity you can meet up with timing, and work will go smooth without stress.” “There should be a strict regulation around logistics to make sure that all these people are effective and when people disappoint or people do not do what they say they do they should be held accountable for their actions.” Speaking on the fashion industry in Kaduna she said, “Fashion in Kaduna is still growing trying to pick up we all know when you speak of fashion everybody turns to Lagos, Port Harcourt, and Abuja Abuja but here in Kaduna we still have fashion shows that do take place once in a while and then apart from that there are designers too that are really really doing a great job so the fashion industry in Kaduna is not yet there but it’s on its way.” “And sometimes your environment shapes your designs because if I’m here in Kaduna there are some kind of designs that will be appreciated more here than Lagos and there are some designs that Lagos people will love so much and then Kaduna people will not like.” Speaking on what she hopes to achieve in the next five to ten years she said, “in the next five to ten years I really want to make impact in the fashion industry, and also in the next five to ten years I would like Badasky not only be known as a dress brand but also a brand for bags and shoes.” “Apart from that I also want to make impact in the fashion academy sector you know I run a fashion house; I have a fashion academy where I train people and because it’s in a confined space so the number of student you get is limited so I created a platform it’s called soweeafrica, an online fashion academy platform that makes learning easy and accessible. “Because there are a lot of people that want to learn how to sew but they cannot travel and come over because of the high cost of transportation and accommodation, with soweeafrica you can just sit down at the comfort of your home and then you go through your classes. “Since it’s an online program it has been discounted so people don’t have to break the bank to be able to learn how to sew.”

title: Re: University of Ghana orders students with CGPA below 1.00 to withdraw
body: Reference is made to the MyJoyOnline news publication of 23 October 2026 on the above. According to the report, the University of Ghana has once again ordered undergraduate students who obtained a Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) below 1.00 at the end of the 2025/2026 academic year to withdraw from the University. The story, culled from a publication on the University’s Facebook page, does not explain how this decision serves the best interests of the University, Ghana or the affected students. The University’s Academic Affairs Directorate merely states that the directive is in accordance with Section 9.26 of the University Regulations for Junior Members (2017). Assuming it is important to identify and punish those responsible for breaching this regulation, why does the University believe that only the students must bear the consequences? Failing an examination is only a small part of the academic process. To establish the causes of examination failure and determine where responsibility lies, we must also interrogate the quality of lecturers, the effectiveness of teaching methods, the accessibility of learning materials and the ratio of students to lecturers. We should also know whether the affected students have been interviewed by the University to understand the challenges that may have contributed to their poor grades. What if a student was dealing with trauma resulting from bereavement? What if a student lacked the resources to obtain adequate food and maintain the physical and mental well-being necessary to cope with the demands of academic life? Even if we were to conclude that the students themselves were solely responsible for failing their continuous assessments and examinations, that would still not justify denying a Ghanaian the opportunity to pursue an education, especially when they can afford it. This is because the 1992 Constitution of Ghana recognises the right to educational opportunities. This right is not conditional upon a student’s ability to maintain a CGPA above 1.00. Article 25(1) of the 1992 Constitution provides: “All persons shall have the right to equal educational opportunities and facilities and with a view to achieving the full realisation of that right— (a) basic education shall be free, compulsory and available to all; (b) secondary education in its different forms, including technical and vocational education, shall be made generally available and accessible to all by every appropriate means, and in particular, by the progressive introduction of free education; (c) higher education shall be made equally accessible to all, on the basis of capacity, by every appropriate means, and in particular, by the progressive introduction of free education; A few points are worth noting from the above. The Constitution recognises the right of all persons to equal educational opportunities and facilities. Basic education must be free, compulsory and available to all. Until secondary and higher education are made free, as envisaged by the Constitution, every Ghanaian who is interested in pursuing such education and can afford to pay for it should have the opportunity to do so. Using a CGPA requirement above 1.00 to deny people educational opportunities is a denial of their right to education and, in my view, runs contrary to the spirit of the Constitution. We should be clear that this decision is not about telling students to resit their examination papers or repeat their year of study. They have been dismissed from the University. This practice is not only an infringement on the Constitution of Ghana, but it also makes a mockery of the University’s full-fee-paying policy. This policy allows the University to admit students who are less academically qualified than others with better grades because the former can pay full fees without government subvention. The apparent irony is that some students admitted under such arrangements subsequently succeed academically when given the opportunity. Today in Ghana, we have medical doctors who were admitted to study biological science with an aggregate of six in their Senior Secondary School Certificate results and those who came on the full fee-paying route with terrible grades but are also successful medical doctors. If the University can recognise that students with comparatively weak entry grades may succeed when given a chance, why should it be so quick to abandon students who struggle after admission? Should the institution not first examine the factors responsible for their difficulties and explore reasonable opportunities for improvement? This recurring practice does not merely raise questions about the University’s commitment to the future of the students entrusted to its care; it also raises questions about its approach to academic preparation and student development. How does denying students who have performed poorly in examinations the opportunity to receive further academic training solve the problem, when the very purpose of education is to develop knowledge, skills and competence? A university does not exist merely to train students who are already academically accomplished. It should also provide opportunities for learning, growth and transformation. It is a place where people are equipped to become something more than they were when they arrived. As Ghana’s premier university, the University of Ghana is one of the institutions upon which the nation depends to prepare young people for leadership and responsible citizenship. Not all of us can become biological scientists or engineers, but each of us can make a meaningful contribution to society in our own way. It is the responsibility of the University, particularly one of the standing of the University of Ghana, to help students discover and develop their potential, especially when they have placed their confidence in the institution by seeking its training. Education is recognised as a human right because, beyond academic performance, people need the educational process itself: the academic environment, extracurricular activities, discipline, social interaction and opportunities for personal development. These experiences can help students discover their abilities and find their place in society. How many of the University administrators who took this decision, which could affect hundreds of other people’s children, would deny their own children the opportunity to continue their education because they had failed to attain a CGPA of 1.00? I call on the management of the University to reverse this decision immediately and remove this provision from the University Regulations for Junior Members. Alternatively, the management should resign, since it has failed to understand and carry out its mandate in the spirit of the 1992 Constitution of Ghana regarding education. Benjamin Akyena Brantuo Former JCR President Commonwealth Hall, University of Ghana kwakuakyenabrantuo@gmail.com

title: France to deploy 70,000 police ahead of new protests
body: France will deploy some 70,000 police nationwide as it braces for new protests this weekend after some of the worst urban violence in years erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations a week ago, the government said Friday. President Emmanuel Macron, who according to aides is postponing a visit later this month to Nigeria and Senegal amid the crisis, held a meeting of his defence council of top ministers and officials and was to meet security forces. He was also set to host for the first time representatives of high school pupils, whose protests over conditions at their schools sparked the movement that has broadened into a nationwide show of anger against the government at the rising cost of living. Some 70,000 security personnel will be deployed on Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said at a press conference in Paris, warning that calls for violence and looting were circulating on social media. The protests have come at a critical moment for France six months ahead of elections to replace Macron, with a new poll underlining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen is the frontrunner and showing her position has been strengthened by the latest events. Adding to tensions, Le Pen is at the weekend due to host her National Rally (RN) party congress in Orleans, with thousands of supporters expected but local authorities fearing clashes as opponents head to the city. Nunez was expected to visit the city Friday to “inspect the security arrangements” at the request of the prime minister’s office, it said. At Macron’s meeting with students, “we will present our demands to him — which remain the same: the state of school infrastructure and an overhaul of the Parcoursup (university admissions) system,” Nathanael Combary, president of Renouveau Lyceen (High School Renewal) told AFP. Macron’s government has sought to draw a line between the legitimate demands of protesters and the looting, burning and ransacking that erupted on the sidelines of protests last Saturday. In a judicial response of unprecedented firmness, courts have already sent 217 people, half of them first-time offenders, to prison over the events on Saturday, Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said. On Thursday, Macron called for “the utmost severity” against “acts of delinquency”, accusing “ultra-left” groups of having sought to “bring down the republic” last weekend. – ‘Police have a responsibility’ – On Saturday, a second round of demonstrations is expected across France. Lyon’s city centre in the southeast will be off-limits to demonstrators this weekend, while in Paris protesters will only be allowed to march a limited route between Bastille and Nation squares. Authorities in Marseille had also banned protests but announced Friday that a union-organised demonstration would be allowed on an “exceptional basis” — the only one authorised in the southern Bouches-du-Rhone department. They also reversed a decision to suspend all public transport in the city on Saturday. But in the capital, leading museums including the Louvre will be closed on Saturday while the Art Basel art fair is being cut short. Some 20 percent more members of the security forces will be deployed this weekend after heavy criticism of the anticipation and intelligence gathering of police last week. “In a country governed by the rule of law, the police have a responsibility both to ensure that protests can take place peacefully and safely and to protect the public from violent disorder,” said Eva Cosse, senior Europe researcher at Human Rights Watch, expressing alarm over reports of children being severely injured by crowd-control weapons. The violence has tarnished the image of France ahead of elections that could be a turning point in its modern history, with the government’s debt pile also troubling investors. A new poll by Harris Interactive for M6/RTL made after the violence showed Le Pen soaring ahead on 33-35 percent in the first round of voting for the presidential elections. It predicted that hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon was on course to face her in the run-off where Le Pen would emerge as an easy winner on some 70 percent of the vote. The post France to deploy 70,000 police ahead of new protests appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Mob attacks bus driver after two die in accident
body:
A motorcycle rider and his passenger were killed on Friday morning when a vehicle rammed into the motorcycle at Bukuru Low-Cost Junction in Jos South Local Government Area of Plateau State .
A mob subsequently attacked the driver of the vehicle, but his condition remained unclear as of the time of filing this report.
Two eyewitnesses, Sharon Ibas and Tuwan Timothy, independently corroborated accounts of the crash, including the collision between a Toyota Hiace bus, a Peugeot Boxer J5, and the motorcycle.
Mr Ibas said the accident occurred at about 9 a.m. as he travelled to Abuja in a Blue Whales Toyota Hiace bus.
He said their driver stopped near the junction, where youths and vigilante personnel were controlling traffic during a funeral procession.
According to him, the Peugeot Boxer J5, approaching from behind, failed to stop and rammed the bus’s rear.
Mr Ibas said the Peugeot driver subsequently hit the motorcycle, killing both rider and passenger at the scene.
“While our vehicle was approaching Bukuru, there was a procession of people carrying a corpse. Youths and vigilante members were stopping vehicles to control traffic. Our driver stopped, but the driver of the Peugeot Boxer refused to stop and hit our vehicle from behind,” he said.
Mr Ibas said youths at the scene descended on the Peugeot driver and beat him severely.
He added that security personnel later arrived and rescued the driver, although he could not confirm whether the man survived the assault.
“The driver was lynched by angry youths. I am not sure if he survived the beating. Security officials arrived and rescued him,” he said.
He said the mob also destroyed the Peugeot vehicle.
Mr Timothy, the second eyewitness, also confirmed Mr Ibas’s account of the incident, providing additional corroboration of the reported sequence of events.
When contacted, the spokesperson for the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) in Plateau State, Yakubu Longsan, said he had contacted the command’s Bukuru unit, whose officials told him the accident had not been reported to them.
Mr Longsan advised members of the public to report road crashes to the FRSC and contact the corps for updates on rescue operations and emergency response.
The incident comes days after a road crash along Bukuru Express Road in Jos South killed a father and his son and injured seven others.
The FRSC attributed the crash to overspeeding and reckless driving.

title: Showjumping leaps forward with Global Champions Tour at Giza Pyramids
body: A perfect breeze swept through the arena as Italian rider Emanuele Gaudiano jumped the first fence of the Global Champions Tour (GCT) stop in Cairo atop his horse Chabrello PS on Thursday afternoon. It marked a historical moment as the tour kicked off its inaugural event in Egypt, with the Pyramids of Giza providing the perfect backdrop for the one-of-a-kind show. Taking place this weekend, the GCT in Cairo features 50 of the best riders in the world, competing for a €1.75 million prize purse. It is the penultimate stop on the tour before next week’s Finals in Rabat and drew a sellout crowd on opening night on Thursday. The GCT was founded in 2006 by Dutch Olympic champion Jan Tops. What started as a six-event showjumping tour has evolved into a global championship spanning 17 destinations across 15 countries in 2026. From Miami to Mexico City, Shanghai to Cairo, the tour has taken riders to all corners of the globe. But they all agree that competing in front of the Pyramids is an unrivalled experience. None more so than Egyptian rider Sameh El Dahan, who got back to representing Egypt earlier this year after five years flying the British flag. This GCT event serves as the perfect homecoming for the 41-year-old, who received massive roars from the Cairo crowd when he went clear in round one of the team competition on Thursday. “When I first heard that the event is coming here, take away the Pyramids on the side for a minute, but just that there is a five-star event that will be in Egypt with this calibre, I was very excited as soon as I heard the news,” El Dahan told The National . Hosting an event at the Pyramids of Giza requires a huge amount of planning and lots of red tape to clear, so El Dahan was understandably sceptical but extremely hopeful it would happen. “Lots of the riders asked me 'what do you think the show will be like?' I said, if they are able to make it, they'll make an amazing show. And then add the backdrop, where in the world would you be jumping underneath thousands of years of history like this? “So for me as an Egyptian coming back, I've competed all over the world, different continents, championships, this, that, the other. But I haven't competed on home ground for 16, 17 years. The buzz just coming to the show, like everybody's ringing me, asking me for tickets, 'we want to see you', people I haven't heard from for years. It's been great, honestly. “I hope people don't mind me saying that, it's socially exhausting, but I love it. I really, really love it, and I love the buzz that the people have, and they're proud to have us here, and I'm proud to perform in front of them.” Saudi rider Abdulrahman Al Rajhi, fresh off taking team gold and individual silver at the Asian Games in Japan, could not stop smiling as he sat for an interview with the Pyramids lit up behind him as nightfall descended on the Egyptian capital. View this post on Instagram “Whenever we talk about Egypt, the Pyramids is something special. And I've always dreamt to come and visit it and experience such a historical place,” said the Saudi Olympian. “And guess what? We're here at one of the most historical places in the world, at the most prestigious sport in the world, and one of the biggest shows and events, and with the most important riders from all over the world. And to be part of it and to be part of this amazing event definitely is such an amazing experience.” Qatari rider Sheikh Ali bin Khalid Al Thani described staging a GCT at the Pyramids as “a win for the sport” while Tops, the founder and president of the GCT said the tour’s arrival in Cairo is “an important milestone” on the 20-year anniversary of its launch. New heights “When we launched the Tour in 2006, our ambition was to take show jumping to new heights,” said Tops. “Twenty years later, seeing the world's best riders competing against the backdrop of the Pyramids of Giza is an incredibly proud moment and a reflection of how far we have come. “From six events to a championship reaching audiences around the world, we have continued to push boundaries and create new opportunities for riders, teams and fans. “Our ambition has always been focused on the future. Cairo marks another important milestone in our journey, and as we look ahead to the next 20 years, our focus is firmly on further innovation, expanding the global reach of the sport and inspiring a new generation of fans around the world.” The action continues on Friday afternoon with a CSI5* 1.45m show followed by CSI5* 1.55m in the evening, before the €1,000,000 Grand Prix of Cairo closes out proceedings on Saturday.

title: Video: This week in Finland, 23 October 2026
body:
An increasing number of people in Finland are turning to food aid, the government shelved plans for a tourist tax, and Helsinki secured a major athletics event.

title: What is known about Austria declaring four Russian diplomats personae non gratae
body:
MOSCOW, October 23. /TASS/. Austria has declared four Russian diplomats personae non gratae, Profil magazine reported.
Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Dmitry Lyubinsky told TASS that Moscow would inevitably retaliate against these steps.
The Austrian authorities, having decided to expel four Russian diplomats, are thoughtlessly pursuing the West’s anti-Russian policy, and there will be a response to this move, the Russian Embassy said in a statement.
TASS has summarized the key information available so far.
Austria has declared four Russian diplomats personae non gratae, Profil magazine reported. According to the publication, they must leave the country immediately.
Three diplomatic staff members of the embassy and a member of the Russian delegation to the Vienna negotiations on military security and arms control have been declared personae non gratae, the Russian Embassy in Austria said.
Russia will inevitably retaliate against the expulsion of four Russian diplomats from Austria, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Dmitry Lyubinsky told TASS.
The Austrian authorities, having decided to expel four Russian diplomats, are thoughtlessly pursuing the West’s anti-Russian policy, the Russian Embassy said in a statement. The embassy noted that such actions would inevitably prompt an appropriate response.
In May, the Austrian Foreign Ministry declared three staff members of the Russian Embassy and Russia’s Permanent Mission to the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe personae non gratae.
The Russian Embassy in Austria noted that "no evidence, let alone proof, has been presented of the alleged violations of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations."
On September 8, Hungarian Foreign Minister Anita Orban announced the expulsion of 10 staff members of the Russian Embassy in Budapest. In response, a group of staff members of the Hungarian Embassy in Moscow and the Hungarian Consulates General in St. Petersburg and Kazan were ordered to depart Russian territory.
On September 2, the German government decided to close Russia’s Consulate General in Bonn as of September 18. Staff members of Russia’s Consulate General in Bonn and the Russian House in Berlin, as well as their family members, were required to depart Germany.
On May 29, Romania decided to close the Russian Consulate General in Constanta, and the consul general was declared persona non grata. On June 25, Russia responded in kind, deciding to close Romania’s Consulate General in St. Petersburg and declare its head persona non grata.
On July 27, Romania announced the expulsion of a Russian diplomat. At the time, the head of the Russian diplomatic mission was handed a verbal note stating that one of the Russian diplomats had to leave the country within five days.
On August 27, Russia responded by declaring a staff member of the Romanian Embassy in Moscow persona non grata.

title: One dead, three injured as two-storey building collapses in Lagos
body: ​By Olasunkanmi Akoni Tragedy struck in the early hours on Friday when one yet-to-be-identified construction worker was reportedly confirmed dead and three others critically injured following the midnight collapse of an uncomplicated two-storey building project in Lagos State. ​The unfortunate incident occurred along Akinola Street, near Fadeyi Bus Stop, off the busy Ikorodu Road axis. ​According to local sources, the victims were part of a crew that chose to sleep overnight at the site to prepare for an early start on the next day’s construction work. Reports said disaster struck in the middle of the night when the entire structure suddenly caved in, trapping the workers beneath the rubble. ​Emergency responders, led by the Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA) alongside auxiliary safety teams, arrived at the scene shortly after the incident to commence search and rescue operations. First responders managed to pull three survivors from the debris with varying degrees of injury, while one body was recovered from the ruins. ​Meanwhile, the survivors have been rushed to a nearby hospital for medical treatment, while emergency crews continue to clear the site to ensure no additional victims remain trapped. ​Details surrounding the cause of the collapse remain sketchy as of press time. LASEMA Permanent Secretary, Dr. Femi Oke-Osanyintolu, who confirmed the incident said the cause of collapse cannot be ascertained presently. . “Emergency responders are making frantic efforts to ascertain the number of people (onsite workers) trapped beneath the collapsed structure. “Coordinated search and rescue ongoing with the agency’s excavator. “Meanwhile, ad at 3:33am, three adult ales rescued alive, while one ault male recovered dead. Operations ongoing,” Oke-Osanyintolu stated. The post One dead, three injured as two-storey building collapses in Lagos appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Chernihiv attack injures 25, city administration says
body:
The number of people injured in a Russian attack on Chernihiv on Friday has risen to 25, head of the Chernihiv City Military Administration Dmytro Bryzhynsky said.

"According to preliminary information, 16 people sought medical assistance from ambulance crews at the scene, while another eight people were transported to hospital," Bryzhynsky said on Telegram.

Earlier, Bryzhynsky reported a strike on a Nova Poshta terminal in the northern part of the city. The facility was damaged, and people were believed to be trapped under the rubble, he said. One person was reported killed and 16 injured.

title: Ex-agitator questions coastal highway re-routing
body: By Chancel Bomadi Sunday BOMADI — A Niger Delta ex-agitator and former Delta State House of Assembly candidate, Chief Kingsley Muturu, has called on the Federal Government to provide clear explanations for the proposed re-routing of the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway to link with the existing East-West Road. Muturu, who contested under the All Progressives Congress (APC), said the proposed adjustment by the Minister of Works, David Umahi, had raised concerns in the Niger Delta, stressing the need for transparency regarding the reasons for the decision and its technical justification. Speaking with journalists over the weekend, the former agitator and peace ambassador said the government should explain the proposed changes, particularly in view of the survey plans and engineering designs already developed for the project. He argued that the region deserved clear information about the original highway alignment, the proposed adjustments and how the project would connect with the existing East-West Road. Muturu questioned whether the Niger Delta’s difficult terrain should pose an obstacle to the construction of major transport infrastructure, noting that the region had long supported petroleum exploration and transportation activities. “The Federal Government has demonstrated its capacity to construct major bridges and transport infrastructure across lagoons, rivers and other challenging waterways beyond the Niger Delta, which generates the nation’s wealth,” he said. “Why should the same terrain, which can be assessed and engineered for petroleum operations, automatically become an insurmountable obstacle to road construction?” He called for transparency and responsible leadership in decisions concerning the highway, warning against using the region’s geographical challenges as a reason to limit infrastructure development. Muturu noted that the oil industry had developed the technical capacity to explore, drill, install pipelines and transport crude oil across difficult terrain. He urged political leaders, traditional rulers and community stakeholders in the Niger Delta to demand fair treatment and equitable infrastructure development. The former lawmaker, however, acknowledged that oil exploration and road construction involved different engineering processes, technical requirements and environmental considerations. “Our point is straightforward: if the terrain can be studied and suitable engineering solutions devised for oil exploration and transportation, then the feasibility of roads, bridges and other essential infrastructure should likewise be evaluated through thorough technical investigations,” he said. “The Niger Delta deserves engineering solutions, not assumptions that its geography renders development impractical.” He maintained that a project of national significance such as the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway should be guided by credible technical evidence, transparent decision-making and meaningful engagement with communities that could be affected by changes to its alignment. Muturu urged President Bola Tinubu and the Federal Ministry of Works to ensure that decisions on the project were based on sound engineering principles, economic considerations, environmental protection and fairness to affected communities. The post Ex-agitator questions coastal highway re-routing appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Bear attacks killed 28 people in Russia in 2026
body:
KRASNOYARSK, October 23. /TASS/. The death toll from bear attacks in Russia has risen to 28, according to TASS calculations based on regional reports and public data.
Siberia and the Far East face a difficult situation as bears increasingly enter populated areas. Forest populations have grown significantly, while this year's poor taiga food harvest has left the animals hungry, driving them toward settlements.
On October 23, a watchman was killed by a bear at an industrial facility near the village of Boguchany in the Krasnoyarsk Region, bringing the national toll to 28, including eight in that region.

title: Musk restricts Starlink service to punish Kiev — magazine
body:
LONDON, October 23. /TASS/. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk may have restricted Starlink satellite communications for the Ukrainian armed forces to punish Kiev for striking Russian oil refineries, UK’s The Economist reported, citing sources.
The magazine noted that the decision to restrict access to Starlink "appears to have come from a small circle around President [Donald Trump], Mr. [Elon] Musk and [special presidential envoy] Steve Witkoff." The article specified that in this way, "Musk wanted to punish Ukraine for striking Russian refineries."
Meanwhile, a source told The Economist that Musk had contacted the White House only after the restrictions had already been imposed.
Last week, the Kiev authorities said that SpaceX had imposed restrictions on the operation of Starlink terminals for the Ukrainian armed forces at speeds exceeding 160 kilometers per hour, disrupting several military operations. Musk stated that Starlink is not used for offensive military operations, but rather for defense and civilian purposes only. Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government, and any restrictions on speed or use are set by the US Army and, ultimately, by the president. The Wall Street Journal reported that it was the SpaceX CEO who ordered the restriction of Ukraine’s access to Starshield.
On the evening of October 22, US President Donald Trump announced that Ukraine’s access to the Starshield military satellite communications system had been restored.
Earlier on October 23, it was reported that Sergey Sternenko, a former adviser to Ukraine’s defense minister, wrote on his Telegram channel that some Ukrainian army operations had been disrupted again due to incomplete restrictions on satellite communication system use. He described the situation with Starlink and Starshield as "ambiguous."

title: ‎Kaduna APC presidential rally: Confront Tinubu on worsening security in our zone, Wakili tells Northwest govs
body: ‎ ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎As President Bola Tinubu prepares to visit Kaduna State on Saturday for his campaign tour, a chieftain of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) and senatorial candidate for Kaduna North, Dr Abdullahi Ahmad Wakili, has urged the seven governors of the Northwest to abandon political silence and confront the President directly over the region’s worsening security crisis. ‎ ‎Wakili said the visit must not end in “political speeches, campaign promises and party celebrations” while residents of the Northwest continue to face kidnapping, banditry and violent attacks. ‎ ‎According to him: “The Northwest is bleeding, our communities are living in fear, and too many families continue to suffer the consequences of insecurity. ‎ ‎ “For residents of affected communities, the issue is not political slogans or campaign activities; it is the fundamental right to live, work, travel and sleep without the constant fear of kidnapping, banditry and violent attacks.” ‎ ‎He specifically called on Governors Uba Sani of Kaduna, Abba Kabir Yusuf of Kano, Dikko Umaru Radda of Katsina, Nasir Idris of Kebbi, Umar Namadi of Jigawa, Ahmad Aliyu of Sokoto and Dauda Lawal of Zamfara to rise above partisan differences and speak with one voice. ‎ ‎“You are the elected leaders of the people of the Northwest. You cannot claim to represent our interests while failing to communicate the urgency of the security crisis to the highest authority in the country,” Wakili said. ‎ ‎He stressed that the governors’ access to the President should be used to secure tangible protection for citizens rather than merely strengthen political relationships. ‎ ‎“My message to the seven governors is direct: do not waste this opportunity. Do not allow the President to leave Kaduna without hearing the truth about the suffering of our people,” he added. ‎ ‎Wakili urged the governors to tell President Tinubu that the region could no longer endure “endless insecurity” while communities demanded protection and families struggled to recover from violent attacks. ‎ ‎“Tell him that the people are tired of promises that do not translate into lasting security. Tell him that the time for decisive action is now,” he said. ‎ ‎According to him, the Federal Government must move beyond assurances and deploy a clear, coordinated and measurable response, including improved intelligence gathering, adequately equipped security personnel, stronger protection for vulnerable communities and effective measures to rescue abducted persons and prosecute perpetrators. ‎ ‎“We need more than assurances. We need a clear, coordinated and measurable security response,” Wakili said. “The Federal Government must work closely with the state governments and security agencies to develop practical solutions that produce visible improvements on the ground.” ‎ ‎He insisted that his appeal was not hostility towards the President or opposition for its own sake, but a demand for responsible leadership. ‎ ‎“The security and welfare of citizens must take precedence over political interests, party loyalty and campaign calculations,” he said. ‎ ‎Wakili warned that if the governors failed to use the President’s visit to press for concrete security action, they would have to explain to their people why such an opportunity was allowed to pass. ‎ ‎“History will remember not only the promises our leaders made, but also what they did when their people needed them most,” he said. ‎ ‎He said farmers must be able to return to their farms, traders must conduct their businesses safely and children must attend school without fear of abduction. ‎ ‎“Our security is not a campaign issue to be discussed and forgotten after the rallies. It is a matter of life and death,” Wakili declared. ‎ ‎“The governors must speak. The President must listen. And the people must see decisive action.
