title: Peace in Ukraine achievable if US respects Russia’s interests — Russian diplomat
body:
MOSCOW, October 23. /TASS/. It is quite possible to achieve a model of a sustainable settlement in Ukraine if the United States shows due respect for Russia’s interests, according to a high-ranking Russian Foreign Ministry official.
"We believe that if the American team shows due respect for our interests and redlines, which the American negotiators are well aware of, we will ultimately be able to come very close to a model of a long-term and sustainable political settlement. Naturally, this settlement must be based on the objectives of the special military operation, as articulated by the Russian president, on the territorial realities on the ground, and on the Russian constitution," Alexander Gusarov, director of the ministry’s North Atlantic department, said in an interview with International Affairs magazine.
He noted, however, that the domestic political and party landscape in the United States may have a significant impact on the congressional legislative agenda regarding Russia. "It should be noted that even now, when the administration has a majority in both houses of Congress, at least until the elections, it has not prevented the advancement in Congress of what we view as a rather harmful sanctions bill against Russia and Iran, known as the Lindsey Graham Act (Graham is designated in Russia as a terrorist and extremist - TASS). So, obviously, there are forces that are interested in this kind of inertial, or rather confrontational, development of relations between Russia and the United States. In our view, this does not serve first and foremost the interests of the Americans themselves," Gusarov emphasized.

title: Darkuman–Kaneshie road works move to 24-hour schedule
body: Construction works on the Darkuman Junction–Kaneshie First Light road corridor in Accra are being carried out around the clock as the Ministry of Roads seeks to accelerate rehabilitation and minimise delays in completing the project. The decision to adopt a 24-hour schedule is expected to increase the pace of work on the busy route, where damaged road surfaces and inadequate drainage have created difficulties for motorists and other road users. The project involves road repairs, civil engineering works and the installation of underground storm drains. Awerco Construction Limited is among the contractors undertaking the works, which extend from Atico Junction through Kaneshie First Light to Hansonic Junction. The rehabilitation is expected to improve movement along a corridor linking communities such as Darkuman, Kaneshie and Dansoman, while addressing drainage problems that have contributed to the deterioration of sections of the road. Work began on August 21, 2026, following the engagement of contractors by the Ministry to repair damaged stretches and improve the drainage system. Construction activities, particularly excavation and drain installation, have resulted in localised traffic adjustments along parts of the route. Motorists may therefore encounter changes in traffic flow as work progresses. When completed, the project is expected to improve the flow of stormwater, restore worn-out road surfaces and enhance safety for commuters. The extended works are also intended to improve connectivity along the corridor and make daily journeys easier for residents and motorists.

title: Apprentices BAE and Babcock cannot take offered elsewhere
body: Strong apprenticeship applicants who cannot be offered a place by BAE Systems or Babcock will be put in front of smaller firms in the same communities under a scheme launched at Barrow-in-Furness, with pilots covering the North West and Devonport, according to The 5% Club. The Apprenticeship Talent Bridge was opened by Pat McFadden, the Work and Pensions Secretary, at an event bringing together defence employers, local businesses and government. Babcock supports the South West pilot covering Devonport and BAE Systems supports the North West pilot covering Barrow-in-Furness and the Preston area. Apprentices will be matched to smaller companies from April 2027, with sign-up opening this month. The charity said major defence employers attract large numbers of applicants for their apprenticeship programmes but cannot offer a place to every strong candidate, while other employers in the same communities struggle to attract the people and skills they need. Research published by Make UK in March found half of manufacturers identify skills shortages as their biggest barrier to growth. Mark Cameron, chief executive of The 5% Club, said: “Talent shouldn’t be lost because opportunity can’t be seen. Major employers have more talented apprenticeship applicants than they can employ, while other businesses are struggling to find the people they need. “The Apprenticeship Talent Bridge connects the two. It is a simple idea, but one that could keep more talent in the sector, open up opportunities young people may never have known existed, and help employers access the skills they need to grow.” Tania Gandamihardja, group human resources director at BAE Systems, set out the scale of the company’s intake and the competition for places: “Over the last decade, we’ve recruited more than 9,000 apprentices across the UK and know first-hand the value that apprenticeships bring to individuals, businesses and the wider industrial base. They’re one of the best routes into a skilled and rewarding career, but that also makes them highly sought-after. “By connecting applicants with fantastic opportunities elsewhere in the sector and with our supply chain SMEs, we can help more young people take that first step, while also supporting businesses across the North West to access the talent and skills they need to grow.” Debbie Joce, skills director at Babcock, said: “Apprenticeships are vital to the future workforce and the long-term success of the defence industry. At Babcock, we recognise the role we play in creating these opportunities, not just within our own organisation but across the communities where we live and work. “The Apprenticeship Talent Bridge is a great way of industry working together with government to open doors and create opportunities across the wider employer and supply chain community. By helping more people access high-value, skilled careers, we can make the most of the talent coming through and help ensure that talented people aren’t lost.” Luke Pollard, the Minister for Defence Readiness and Industry, said: “Every young person who shows the talent and drive to succeed in defence deserves a route into the industry. Initiatives like this make that happen, with industry working together to build skills, create jobs, and strengthen our defence industrial base for the long term.” McFadden said: “This partnership will open doors for young people to exciting careers in the defence industry and help businesses boost their talent pipeline. More opportunities for our young people seeking a career in defence will help to boost our engineering and manufacturing skills base and ensure they benefit as we deliver record increases in defence spending.” The two pilot areas are the obvious places to start, because Barrow builds the submarines and Devonport refits them, and both have supply chains full of firms competing for the same machinists, electrical technicians and welders as the yard down the road. A candidate good enough to reach the final stages at BAE Systems is more than good enough for a tier two supplier, and until now that candidate simply disappeared. Participation is voluntary and applicant data is shared only with consent, with employers keeping their own selection processes. The initiative is funded by Ufi VocTech Trust and the ERA Foundation with in-kind investment from the charity, and draws on insight from Airbus Defence and Space. It builds on a commitment in the Defence Industrial Strategy to develop a clearing-style approach for defence apprenticeship and graduate applicants. The Defence Youth Participation and Employment Pledge set a wider no wrong door approach, an ambition to increase opportunities for under twenty fives by a quarter to more than forty thousand a year by the end of this Parliament, and support for at least fourteen thousand people annually through apprenticeships across defence and its supply chain by 2035. The post Apprentices BAE and Babcock cannot take offered elsewhere first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Belarus Still Hosts Russian Drone Relays, Ukraine’s Border Service Says
body:
Ukraine’s State Border Guard Service (DPSU) said Belarus has continued to allow Russian drones to use relay stations on its territory on Friday, Oct. 23.
DPSU spokesperson Andrii Demchenko, speaking in a televised interview, added that the border agency has not recorded Russian troops being moved into Belarus or Belarusian forces being pulled toward the Ukrainian border.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Demchenko said the threat from Belarus remains, but that border guards have no preliminary information pointing to preparations for an attack near the border, as reported by state media Ukrinform .
He said Russia is not sending additional infantry groups or units to Belarus.
According to Demchenko, Belarus is instead supporting Russia through relays that help guide Russian aerial weapons launched at Ukraine via Belarusian territory. He said he believes Belarusian leader Alexander Lukashenko wants to avoid committing Belarusian units to the war because they would suffer losses.
On June 19, President Volodymyr Zelensky gave Lukashenko a week to dismantle relays near the border, and said on June 24 that they had stopped working two days prior. Zelensky said it was unclear whether the equipment had been dismantled.
In September, Demchenko said border guards had detected the relays being activated again , amplifying signals for Russia’s Shahed and Gerbera drones heading toward western Ukraine’s Rivne, Volyn and Lviv regions.
He linked the relays to the Sept. 13 drone attack near the Yahodyn crossing with Poland. Russian independent outlet Meduza said that drones struck a gas station near the crossing and a passenger train on the Kyiv-Warsaw line.
Belarusian opposition leader Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya said on Sept. 23, on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, that she considers a new Russian attack from Belarusian territory a real possibility.
“If Russia at some point again wants to attack Ukraine in any way from the northern border, then Lukashenko will be very happy to provide territory, logistics, and Belarusian infrastructure to help [Russian leader Vladimir] Putin achieve his goals and intentions,” she said.
The Associated Press reported in July that Lukashenko has repeatedly said he has no plans to send troops into the war unless Belarus is attacked.
Anastasiia Bzova is journalist covering politics, culture and current affairs. She focuses on delivering accurate, accessible reporting that helps readers understand the issues shaping their opinions.

title: Ghana Hydrological Authority identifies three outstanding issues affecting operations
body: The Ghana Hydrological Authority (GHA) has identified three major outstanding issues affecting its effective operations: the passage of regulations to support implementation of the law establishing the Authority, approval of its conditions of service, and operationalisation of the statutory fund provided for under the law. The concerns come as the government pledges to address staffing shortages, poor staff retention and funding constraints at the Authority, amid fears that the loss of experienced technical personnel could undermine critical flood forecasting and coastal protection efforts. Minister for Works, Housing and Water Resources Ahmed Ibrahim says the government will work to resolve the outstanding issues and facilitate the recruitment of additional personnel to strengthen the Authority’s operations. The commitment follows a working visit to the Authority, during which management outlined key challenges affecting its ability to deliver on its mandate. Mr Ibrahim expressed concern about the growing attrition of experienced personnel, warning that the departure of technical staff could lead to the loss of institutional knowledge accumulated over the years. According to the Minister, the Authority has an approved staff establishment of about 230 positions but currently has only 89 employees. He said the government would work with the Ministry of Finance to secure financial clearance for recruitment, including young engineers graduating from the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST). “We are going to work seriously on them. The regulation will be worked on, the fund will be established together with the board and the Minister for Finance,” he said. Mr Ibrahim added that the government would pursue approval of the Authority’s conditions of service to help retain experienced workers and make the institution more attractive to prospective recruits. He urged existing staff not to leave, assuring them that the government was committed to addressing their concerns. The Minister identified three major outstanding issues requiring attention: the passage of regulations to support implementation of the law establishing the Authority, approval of its conditions of service, and operationalisation of the statutory fund provided for under the law.

title: Russian sabotage and reconnaissance groups step up activity in Sumy and Chernihiv regions – SBGS
body:
Andrii Demchenko, Spokesperson for the State Border Guard Service of Ukraine, said this in a television interview, according to Ukrinform.
“If we compare it with a period when there was virtually no activity by enemy sabotage and reconnaissance groups, several cases have now already been recorded both in the Sumy and Chernihiv regions. The task of such groups is to gather intelligence on how our defenses are organized and find out where our positions are located. If they succeed, they also try to attack Ukrainian positions with their own forces,” Demchenko said.
In addition, the Spokesperson said that attempts to mine the area are frequently detected during counter-sabotage operations.
“In other words, when withdrawing, the enemy tries to make sure that our soldiers are blown up by the devices that the enemy plants during their operations,” he added.
Demchenko emphasized that the Defense Forces use drones to detect such groups in a timely manner. Border guards also receive advance intelligence about possible attempts by sabotage and reconnaissance groups to infiltrate along certain sections of the border and conduct counter-sabotage operations.
Demchenko noted that in the Kharkiv region, the enemy is attempting to expand its area of control.
“The enemy is trying to destroy the positions held by Ukrainian defenders, hoping that infantry groups will subsequently be able to advance more easily. But once again, the enemy is suffering heavy losses,” the spokesperson said.
As reported by Ukrinform, Russian troops are currently most frequently captured in the Kharkiv region during enemy attempts to expand their area of control.

title: Netflix can’t fire its way out of this downward spiral
body:
Netflix co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters assured investors this week that they have nothing to be concerned about. Sure, the company was going to lay off 1,000 employees, downsizing its product, tech, and legal departments, and was ousting its chief content officer, film chairman, and film vice president. But it had also hired a new COO — “one of the most effective at-scale operators in the entertainment industry,” Sarandos said — to turn things around.
Though executive shake-ups aren’t uncommon, having so many of them back to back would send a concerning message even in the best of circumstances. With Netflix, however, the situation looks undeniably grim given the streamer’s recent troubles with missed ad revenue targets, sluggish growth, and a failed attempt at acquiring Warner Bros. Losing WB to David Ellison’s Paramount was a huge blow — that merger would have given Netflix an easy way to expand its catalog, grow its user base, and build a more established presence in movie theaters. The company now has to navigate those challenges on its own while also figuring out why its current content slate hasn’t resulted in record profits.
While Netflix has put out some well-received fare like East of Eden, Adolescence, and The Diplomat, the company is well known for canceling series before they’ve even had a chance to build an audience. People frequently complain that they rarely see advertisements for Netflix’s new projects, but when they do, it tends to be for weird misfires like The New Stanford Prison Experiment and Wonka’s The Golden Ticket. In each of the recent executive firings, you can see Netflix trying to signal to investors and the public that it has a clear understanding of what hasn’t been working with its output from the past few years. There’s no denying that Netflix’s recent lineup has been lackluster, but these issues feel like they’re endemic to the company itself rather than something that can be blamed solely on a trio of executives.
Sarandos insisted to investors that Netflix’s “content around the world is largely working,” but he admitted that the company needs “better execution” in the US, where business is “just not growing as fast as it could or as fast as we’d like.”
Netflix’s push into more markets around the globe was largely led by Bela Bajaria, who led TV and content at Netflix over the past decade. Bajaria ushered the streamer into a new era of being a hub for unscripted programming, sports, and internationally produced projects. Bajaria is part of the reason that a Netflix subscription gives you access to WWE and Lupin as well as Bridgerton.
On paper, Bajaria did exactly what she was hired to do. She expanded and diversified Netflix’s library of content, hoping to attract more people to the platform. Bajaria was instrumental in the production and rollout of international series like Money Heist and Squid Game — the latter of which became a global phenomenon and boosted subscriptions while also winning the streamer a few Emmys. Netflix’s current approach to acquiring and distributing international programming has been so successful that Sarandos said the company has no plans to change its strategy. But it seems that success was not enough to protect Bajaria’s job.
In a statement about incoming COO Peter Rice’s hiring and Bajaria’s dismissal, Sarandos thanked her for her “dedication, innovation, creativity and leadership” and said he was grateful for “everything she’s done to help Netflix entertain the world.” But that gratefulness didn’t exactly gel with recent reports that Bajaria is being used as a scapegoat and was axed with little notice.
Film chairman Dan Lin — who joined Netflix in 2024 and reported directly to Bajaria — exited Netflix in a somewhat similar fashion to his former boss. After years of courting filmmakers with massive production deals, Netflix hired Lin to help it rein in its spending. Lin had a strong track record of producing financial hits for other studios, like Warner Bros.’ The Lego Movie and Disney’s live-action Aladdin. Lin also appointed Doug Belgrad as VP and tasked him with overseeing Netflix’s lineup of original content. By all accounts, Lin did exactly what Netflix courted him for, and his mind for austerity was aligned with the company’s larger goals. But as The Hollywood Reporter notes, Lin’s brusque personality could sometimes lead to friction with some of the high-profile talent Netflix is in business with, like Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew auteur Greta Gerwig and AI startup InterPositive founder Ben Affleck.
While much of Netflix’s recent programming is the product of Bajaria, Lin, and Belgrad’s leadership, they were not the only people responsible for turning the streamer into what it is today. In recent years, Netflix has also gotten into podcasts and gaming — initiatives that have often felt like desperate attempts at clawing back attention from rivals like YouTube, TikTok, and any one of the free ad-supported television platforms on the market. The fact that there are so many other different services that Netflix’s subscribers might prefer to spend more time on is one of the biggest challenges. And many of these competitors have become more attractive to customers as Netflix has continuously raised its prices.
Aside from introducing ad-supported tiers, forcing subscribers to pay more has been Netflix’s primary method for revenue growth. Netflix isn’t unique in that regard — all of the major streamers are doing it — but it has undoubtedly soured some people on the platform at a time when its offerings haven’t always felt like they justified their price. Even when Netflix has stumbled its way onto unexpected gems like KPop Demon Hunters, the company doesn’t always seem to have the strongest game plan to capitalize on their success. Rice’s hiring does suggest that Netflix knows it has to do things differently, and his past may provide some insight into the streamer’s future plans.
Before coming to Netflix, Rice served as 21st Century Fox’s president until the studio was acquired by Disney. Rice became Walt Disney Television’s chairman in 2019 and oversaw production for a number of the company’s networks, including ABC and FX. And after being fired by Bob Chapek in 2022, Rice pivoted into producing projects like Jason Reitman’s Saturday Night, 28 Years Later, and the upcoming Elden Ring movie. Rice’s roots in traditional studio film development points to Netflix getting even more serious about screening its films in theaters. The streamer already has plans to give The Magician’s Nephew and the KPop Demon Hunters sequel sizable theatrical runs, and it is currently trying to secure Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi’s La bola negra an Academy Award at the upcoming Oscars.
Having a larger presence in movie theaters won’t solve all of Netflix’s problems, but it could help shift the way that people perceive the platform and its catalog. And in Sarandos’ assertion that Rice has a deep understanding of talent relationships, you can hear that the co-CEO is banking on his new COO to convince filmmakers that Netflix is where they need to bring their latest ideas. Rice’s hiring makes for a compelling narrative about Netflix finding its way forward by relying on the instincts of an industry veteran known for effortlessly jumping between the film and TV worlds. But that narrative doesn’t feel quite as convincing when you look back at the way Netflix’s partnerships with directors like David Fincher, Shawn Levy, and Noah Baumbach resulted in some pretty terrible projects.
In order for Netflix to really turn the ship around, it has to realize that content is only one piece of the puzzle. Splashy new movies and series won’t mean much if people don’t feel that the service is financially accessible, but Netflix’s vague allusions to “improving” monetization suggest that the service is only going to get more expensive. Right now, Netflix needs to be focused on demonstrating that it has a clear plan for how it can move into the future. The company can start by acknowledging the larger issues with its business model instead of simply throwing executives under the bus.

title: People are vibe coding their way to better TVs
body:
Vibe coding has reached TVs. Social media is awash with posts from people using LLMs and open-source tools to remove ads and tracking, trim bloat so the OS runs faster, and even completely change the look and organization of their homescreens. While a lot of it is fun — one user turned their TV homescreen into a Pokémon town — I think there’s a level of frustration behind it, too. And TV companies should take notice.
[Media: https://twitter.com/gathint/status/2111379569030939102]
Several vibe-coded TV-debloating projects exploded in popularity over the weekend. Cleanyourtv (known as tv-vibehack until the 19th), tv-detox, and dumbtv all claim to accomplish similar things — remove sponsored ads, debloat the TV so it runs faster, and block unwanted data collection that tracks what you’re watching — without hacking, or rooting, the TV. By default, they all also replace the TV’s built-in app launcher with simpler ones. Many users are going a step further and vibe-coding their own replacement launchers, like the Pokémon one below.
[Media: https://twitter.com/robbietilton/status/2111936458923851923?s=20]
Most of the projects we’ve seen so far focus on TVs that run on Android and Google TV operating systems (such as TCL, Hisense, Sony, and older Amazon Fire products), using existing developer modes and the Android Debug Bridge (ADB) to tweak settings and apply (and remove) packages. According to the GitHub pages, they can also work with some Fire TV products that use a custom fork of Android (although likely not on the new Vega-based Fire TV Sticks). Because they use built-in developer tools, they don’t require root access or firmware hacking, and they’re reversible. Even projects that totally change the look of the interface just use Android’s ability to install custom launchers — in many cases with an assist from Claude Code or a similar tool to create the new launcher, too.
As Verge friend Chris Person notes in his Aftermath post, none of this requires AI. These projects take advantage of capabilities that already exist in Android, and in some cases reinvent the wheel. Android debloating programs that use ADB have been around for years, and so have replacement launchers that make Google TV OS look like Apple TV. AI just made the process easier and faster.
There’s nothing similar available for Samsung’s Tizen OS or LG’s webOS, apart from rooting the TV, which is a whole different level of hacking and device control. While there’s a webOS vibe hack for LG TVs that’s based on cleanyourtv, it doesn’t really do the same thing, essentially streaming the Apple TV-like launcher from an always-on device on the same network. They also won’t work for Roku or Vizio’s SmartCast.
These projects, or any OS vibe coding someone might attempt, won’t necessarily stop all data collection. A good basic rule is that if the TV is connected to the internet, it’s collected at least some data. Dumbtv blocks certain manufacturer and ad partner addresses your TV sends data to, but since it’s usually encrypted during transit, knowing what exactly gets sent is impossible. The data blocking is similar to what you can do with Pi-hole to block malicious DNS requests on your network.
TVs have increasingly become a means for companies to gather viewing data and serve up ads. By using automatic content recognition (ACR) and digital fingerprinting, manufacturers are able to know what content you’re watching, send that information to their ad partners, and then display targeted ads on the TV.
ACR isn’t just used for ads, though. It allows companies to measure audience metrics, and it can feed show recommendations based on what you’ve watched. It’s important to note that users need to agree to ACR tracking, and there are ways to opt out of it after the fact in a TV’s menus (although those options are not always easy to find). There are also options in most menus — again, usually buried — for turning off targeted ads.
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/tv-detox-homepage.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/dumbtv-homepage.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
But even after doing that, there’s always concern that companies still collect some amount of your data and use it in ways you might not be comfortable with. Whether or not it’s true does little to assuage those fears. The weekend of vibe coding, on the other hand, is a way for people to try and take control of their TVs to get the user experience they want.
There are also dangers to vibe-coding your TV. One person who tried to vibe-hack a Samsung TV with Claude bricked it. The only way to fully avoid ACR, ads, or any type of data collection is to never connect it to the internet. A firmware download to a USB stick can apply critical updates instead of Wi-Fi or Ethernet. If you still want to stream content, a streaming device that doesn’t use ACR, like an Apple TV 4K (grab a last-generation model before the expensive new one replaces it), is an option. But any streaming requires sharing some amount of your data with someone to function properly.
The biggest takeaway from the vibe-coding weekend is that the current state of TV OSes has people fed up. Most people aren’t going to stop watching TV anytime soon, but the experience needs to improve. The ads, the data collection, and the cluttered layouts are too aggravating. AI now allows anyone to code their own solution, and it’s only going to get easier. If TV manufacturers don’t take note and make changes, there’s a chance that users will make the changes for them.

title: Ghana Armed Forces to hold live-fire demonstration at Bundase on October 30
body: The Ghana Armed Forces (GAF) will conduct its 2026 Land Combat Fire Power Demonstration at the Battle Training Camp in Bundase on Friday, October 30, involving live firing of heavy weapons, battle drills and other tactical manoeuvres. In a press release issued on Friday, October 23, the GAF said the annual exercise was organised for students of the Ghana Armed Forces Command and Staff College. The demonstration is expected to bring together government officials, Defence Attachés, military personnel and other invited guests. The Armed Forces has cautioned residents of Bundase and surrounding communities against panicking when they hear gunfire and explosions during rehearsals and the main exercise. It explained that the sounds would result from the planned military activities and urged residents to remain calm as the demonstration takes place. The GAF also assured the public that all necessary safety measures had been put in place ahead of the exercise. It appealed to residents and the general public to cooperate with the military to ensure the successful conduct of the demonstration.

title: PSG v Lyon French Ligue 1 game postponed due to Paris protests
body: PSG’s home Ligue 1 game against Lyon scheduled for this Sunday has been postponed until Monday, the French league announced, following a request by police amid a wave of violent protests in the French capital. “The LFP takes note of the police decree prohibiting the staging of the game between Paris Saint-Germain and Olympique Lyonnais on Sunday at 8:45 pm (1945 GMT)… and has decided to reschedule the match for Monday at 8:30 pm,” the French league said in a statement. French authorities are braced for another weekend of protests in Paris and across the country after some of the worst urban violence in years erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations a week ago. The post PSG v Lyon French Ligue 1 game postponed due to Paris protests appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: 22-year-old arrested for allegedly vandalising NNPC depot cable
body: The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Gombe State Command, has arrested a 22-year-old man, Abdulrahman Ali, for allegedly vandalising an armoured cable supplying electricity to the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) depot in Gombe. The suspect, who reportedly confessed to his involvement in the crime, pleaded for leniency, blaming his circumstances for his actions. The state commandant, Mohammed Inuwa Usman, disclosed this on Friday while briefing journalists on recent breakthroughs recorded by the command in its fight against vandalism and other criminal activities. According to the command, Ali, of Tudun Wada Pantami, Gombe, and another suspect who is still at large allegedly conspired to vandalise the cable along Bauchi Road at about 3am on October 16, 2026. Edo Community Leader Defrauded of N5.4m in Fake Appointment Scam 11 killed as trailer rams into vehicles in Gombe They allegedly sold the stolen cable for N100,000 and used the proceeds for personal purposes. The command said Ali was arrested in Gombe while attempting to flee the state following intelligence gathered by its Department of Intelligence and Investigation. During questioning, the suspect reportedly admitted his involvement in the offence and appealed to the authorities for mercy, citing the circumstances that led him into the crime. In a related development, the NSCDC said its anti-vandal unit, working with the Lubo Community Security Committee, recovered 968.4 metres of vandalised aluminium power transmission cables along the Lubo-Zambuk axis of Yamaltu-Deba Local Government Area. The cables were abandoned by suspected vandals who fled when they were intercepted at about 12:12am on October 12. The command said efforts were ongoing to apprehend the fleeing suspects. The commandant also disclosed the arrest of a 21-year-old man, Idris Mohammed, over the alleged killing of Usman Jibrin Isah in Kwami Gari, Kwami Local Government Area. He said the incident occurred on September 12 following a minor misunderstanding between the suspect and the deceased at a park. According to him, the deceased allegedly struck Mohammed with a stick during an exchange of words, prompting the suspect to stab him with a pair of scissors, resulting in his death. The suspect was apprehended by NSCDC personnel. Usman said investigations into the cases were ongoing and that the suspects would be charged before a competent court upon their conclusion. He reaffirmed the corps’ commitment to protecting critical national assets and infrastructure and safeguarding lives and property across the state.

title: Obuasi SHTS abuse allegations: Parliamentary committee demands thorough investigation
body: The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Gender, Children and Social Welfare has called for a thorough, impartial and timely investigation into allegations of sexual abuse involving students of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS). The Committee said the investigation must establish the facts, examine how previous complaints were handled and ensure that anyone found culpable faces the appropriate disciplinary or criminal consequences. The allegations were brought to public attention through Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow , an investigative documentary by journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni. In a statement issued on Friday, October 23, the Committee condemned all forms of child abuse and urged the Ghana Education Service (GES) and the Criminal Investigations Department of the Ghana Police Service to ensure a comprehensive investigation. It acknowledged the suspension of the school’s headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai, pending investigations, and the referral of the matter to the police, stressing that these steps must lead to accountability and restore public confidence. The Committee also commended the Ministers for Education and Gender, Children and Social Protection, Haruna Iddrisu and Agnes Naa Momo Lartey, respectively, for meeting with Manasseh Azure Awuni to obtain first-hand information to guide their ministries’ responses and support for affected students. It emphasised that the investigation must respect due process, noting that every accused person is presumed innocent until proven guilty by a competent court. However, it warned that no political affiliation, position or institutional interest should shield anyone from lawful scrutiny. The Committee called for confidential counselling, appropriate medical care and other necessary support for affected students. It also urged authorities to protect students, families, witnesses and whistle-blowers from intimidation, retaliation and stigmatisation. It appealed to the media and the public to protect the identities and privacy of affected children and avoid circulating material that could expose them to further harm. The Committee further commended the National Democratic Congress (NDC) for directing Abdulai to step aside from the Juaben Constituency chairmanship contest pending the police investigation. It noted his subsequent resignation as constituency secretary and withdrawal from the contest. Beyond the case, the Committee called for a comprehensive review of school safeguarding and complaints-handling systems, including safe and confidential reporting channels, prompt referrals and independent investigations. It said weaknesses that allow complaints to be ignored, suppressed or mishandled must be identified and corrected. Commending Manasseh Azure Awuni and his team for bringing the allegations to public attention, the Committee reaffirmed its commitment to protecting children and ensuring that schools remain safe environments for learning. It stressed that the truth must be established, due process upheld and anyone found responsible made to face the full consequences of the law.

title: Ukrainian hryvnia drops to all-time low of 45.20/$1
body:
The National Bank of Ukraine (NBU) set the official hryvnia exchange rate against the U.S. dollar for October 26 at UAH 45.2021 per $1, weakening by 15 kopiikas over the day and reaching a new all-time low.

The previous record low was recorded on October 14, 2026, at UAH 45.0802 per $1.

At the same time, the official hryvnia exchange rate against the euro weakened by 14 kopiikas over the day, to UAH 50.5766 per EUR 1.

Overall, since the beginning of 2026, the official hryvnia exchange rate against the U.S. dollar has weakened by 6.7%, compared with 0.8% for the whole of last year.

On the interbank market on October 23 (as of 3:00 p.m.), the hryvnia traded against the U.S. dollar at UAH 45.38/$1 bid and UAH 45.42/$1 ask.

As reported, on October 23 the reference hryvnia exchange rate against the U.S. dollar updated its historical low, reaching UAH 45.1604 per $1.

title: 6th iNTTA Expo ends with focus on 24-hour economy and youth-led entrepreneurship
body: The final day of the iNTTA Expo in Cape Coast is focusing on how Ghana’s proposed 24-hour economy can drive tourism development, create opportunities for young entrepreneurs and attract investment into the sector. The Friday, October 23 programme, held under the theme “24-Hour Economy as a Vehicle to Tourism Development”, is bringing together policymakers, business leaders, tourism stakeholders and young innovators to explore ways to sustain economic activity beyond conventional business hours. The day’s activities began with a recap of key discussions and commitments from the first two days, before turning attention to the role of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in supporting tourism growth under a round-the-clock economy. The Ghana National Chamber of Commerce and Industry’s Central Region representative, Benedictor Anita Mensah, is scheduled to lead discussions on how SMEs can contribute to the expansion of tourism-related businesses. Youth-led entrepreneurship is another major focus, with a panel examining how artificial intelligence (AI) can help young people transform side hustles into scalable businesses. The session is expected to explore the opportunities technology offers young entrepreneurs seeking to expand their operations and participate in Ghana’s growing tourism and creative economies. A cultural performance by the Central Regional Centre for National Culture is also scheduled before the policy keynote address by Augustus Obuadum Tanoh, Presidential Adviser to Ghana’s 24-Hour Economy Authority. Mr Tanoh is expected to address the role of the policy in tourism development, while a subsequent fireside chat will examine how extended business hours, investment, youth entrepreneurship, local supply chains, safe digital experiences and partnerships across Africa can support Ghana’s economic transformation. The programme also features an Innovation Zone for Youth Creative Changemakers, providing a platform for selected young innovators to present business ideas and initiatives in tourism, trade, technology, agribusiness and the creative economy to investors and industry leaders. The conference is expected to conclude its formal sessions with a closing plenary at which delegates, investors and government representatives will outline commitments, partnerships and next steps emerging from the three-day event. Beyond the conference sessions, delegates are scheduled to participate in site visits to explore investment opportunities in Cape Coast, particularly in tourism infrastructure, cultural heritage development and coastal hospitality projects. The activities will culminate in an evening beach networking gala at Lush on the Coast, bringing together registered delegates, sponsors, government officials and diplomatic guests. The three-day iNTTA Expo has provided a platform for stakeholders to discuss investment opportunities across tourism, hospitality, energy infrastructure, digital finance, agribusiness and health tourism, with the final day placing particular emphasis on youth-led innovation and the potential of the 24-hour economy to expand Ghana’s tourism industry.

title: GPHA Board inspects Tema Port dredging, breakwater rehabilitation works
body: The Board of Directors of the Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority (GPHA), led by its Chairman, John Asiedu Nketiah, has inspected ongoing infrastructure works at the Port of Tema to assess their progress and impact on port operations. The inspection covered recently completed dredging works and the rehabilitation of the port’s breakwaters, projects expected to improve operational efficiency and strengthen the port’s capacity to accommodate larger vessels. Under the dredging project, selected berths have been deepened from 11 metres to 14 metres, allowing bigger vessels to berth at the port. The Board received a briefing on the scope and progress of the projects from GPHA’s General Manager of Engineering, Ing. Komla Ofori. Speaking to the media after the inspection, Mr Asiedu Nketiah expressed satisfaction with the completed dredging works and the progress of the breakwater rehabilitation, particularly the advanced technology being deployed. He said the breakwater project remained on schedule and was expected to be completed and handed over within a month. The Director-General of GPHA, Major General Paul Seidu Tanye-Kulono, said he was optimistic that completing the projects would boost the Authority’s operational and commercial prospects by enabling larger vessels to berth safely at the Port of Tema. The breakwater rehabilitation works are being undertaken by GYTD Group Limited.

title: Russian forces strike Ukrainian army deployment sites by FAB bombs in Zaporozhye area, DPR
body:
MOSCOW, October 23. /TASS/. Russian combat aircraft struck the Ukrainian army’s deployment sites by FAB high-explosive glide bombs in the Zaporozhye area and the Donetsk People’s Republic (DPR), Russia’s Defense Ministry reported, releasing the relevant footage.
"The Defense Ministry of Russia has uploaded footage of aircraft crews of the Russian Aerospace Forces delivering strikes on installations behind enemy lines, hitting a temporary deployment site of units of the Ukrainian army’s 225th separate assault regiment in the settlement of Volnyanka in the Zaporozhye Region by five FAB-500 aerial bombs with the unified glide/adjustment module, and also a temporary deployment site of the 100th separate mechanized brigade of the Ukrainian army in the settlement of Krinitsy in the DPR by five FAB-500 aerial bombs with the unified glide/adjustment module," the ministry said in a statement.
Russia’s Defense Ministry regularly reports on the delivery of strikes on the Ukrainian army’s temporary deployment sites and UAV control posts in various sectors of the engagement lines by FAB-250, FAB-500, FAB-1000, FAB-1500 and FAB-3000 high-explosive precision-guided bombs.
Russian forces also struck two Ukrainian locomotives near Kharkov by Geran drones, the ministry reported.
"Unmanned Systems Forces of the Defense Ministry of Russia continue delivering strikes by attack unmanned aerial vehicles on installations behind enemy lines. Specifically, a strike delivered by Geran drones the other day hit two locomotives near the city of Kharkov. Live-recording images showed that the targets had been successfully hit," the ministry said.

title: 2026 Luv FM-Republic Bank Habitat Fair launched to offer homeownership solutions in Kumasi
body: The 2026 edition of the Republic Bank Luv FM Habitat Fair has been launched in the Ashanti regional capital, Kumasi, with a target of making homeownership accessible to the average Ghanaian. The annual event is aimed at bringing key stakeholders in the housing and construction industry together in one place to make homeownership more accessible. The five-day event is scheduled to take place from November 25 to 29, 2026, at the Kumasi City Mall. But this will be preceded by a mini-clinic on Friday, October 30, at the Poku Trading Arcade in Adum. The event is offering prospective homeowners and property developers an opportunity to access housing-related services, building materials, financing and interior decoration solutions under one roof. The housing deficit in Ghana is seemingly compounding with recent population growth. The Luv FM/Republic Bank Habitat Fair is in its eighth year and continues to attract relevant institutions to help address challenges making home ownership more affordable and accessible. The annual fair is designed to bring stakeholders across the building and construction value chain together, enabling prospective homeowners to access reliable services, appropriate resources and building solutions at competitive prices. By bringing these services together at the Kumasi City Mall, the organisers aim to make it easier for patrons to explore available options, obtain relevant information and identify solutions that suit their housing needs and budgets. Relationship Manager at Luv FM and Nhyira FM, Maxwell Frimpong Manso, says the fair has become an established initiative in Kumasi, providing practical solutions to challenges associated with building and owning homes. He identified the Lands Commission, the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG), Asantehene’s Land Secretariat and other stakeholders as key participants whose involvement helps prospective homeowners access the necessary guidance and services. “Habitat Fair has come to stay here in Kumasi as an important initiative in addressing the housing deficit and the growing demand for housing in the Ashanti region. The fair would cover more than the construction of houses, with interior decoration products and services also available to patrons,” he said. Head of Mortgage Banking at Republic Bank, Dan Adjetey Mohenu, indicated the bank’s partnership with Luv FM for the fair reflects its commitment to supporting individuals at different stages of home building. He explained that the bank’s financing solutions are not limited to people seeking to purchase completed houses but also extend to individuals who are gradually developing their own properties. According to him, prospective homeowners could explore financing options for various stages of construction, including foundation works, as well as funding for interior decoration. “The bank was prepared to support eligible customers with the financial resources needed to advance their housing projects, subject to the bank’s assessment criteria and requirements. Applicants would be required to demonstrate their financing needs and provide the necessary supporting information for the bank to assess their applications,” he said. The partnership is expected to give prospective homeowners access to both housing-related services and financial solutions, helping them navigate the often-challenging process of building or acquiring a home. The 2026 Luv FM-Republic Bank Habitat Fair is expected to provide a platform for prospective homeowners to engage directly with professionals and institutions involved in land acquisition, construction, financing and home improvement.

title: FG Designates Redeemer’s Health Village As TETFund Centre, Guarantees Scholarships For Robotic Surgery Academy
body: In a breakthrough for Nigeria’s healthcare sector, the Federal Government has adopted the newly inaugurated Redeemer’s Health Village (RHV) Robotic Surgery Academy as the nation’s 29th TETFund Centre of Excellence, guaranteeing full scholarship coverage for all enrolled trainees. Speaking at the official inauguration on Thursday, Minister of Education Dr. Tunji Alausa declared that the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) will fully fund the tuition fees of qualified medical professionals undergoing specialist training at the academy through its local scholarship scheme. ﻿ The strategic partnership — established alongside RoboMed Global, the National Postgraduate Medical College of Nigeria (NPMCN), and Redeemer’s University — establishes Nigeria’s pioneer institute for advanced robotic and telesurgical operations. ₦250bn Healthcare Injection Highlighting the government’s drive to curb brain drain and eliminate foreign medical tourism, Alausa disclosed that the Federal Government has injected over ₦250 billion into medical education across the last two years. “The same number of medical students admitted while I was in medical school is the same number we have maintained over the years, without sufficient consideration of our population growth,” the minister stated, confirming plans to expand annual medical programme enrolments to 20,000 within two years. By designating RHV as a Special Centre of Excellence, TETFund sponsorship will ensure that financial barriers do not stop top clinical talent from acquiring cutting-edge surgical skills locally. $4m Infrastructure The newly launched academy hits the ground running with $4 million worth of dual robotic surgical systems, designed to power both clinical service delivery and high-level training. According to RHV Chief Executive Officer Adedamola Dada, the academy aims to produce 400 certified specialists within two years across three main specialties: Urology, General Surgery, and Gynaecology. The academy’s scope extends beyond doctors to train an entire technical ecosystem, including operating theatre personnel, biomedical engineers, and hospital administrators. RHV also recently achieved full accreditation as an academic medical school. Co-founder of RoboMed Global, Dr. Obi Ekwenna, emphasised that the academy relies on a total-ecosystem training model inspired by aviation safety standards prioritizing communication, simulation, and strict team coordination. “The essence of the academy is to train the entire ecosystem, not just surgeons alone,” Ekwenna noted, explaining that candidate evaluation will blend advanced simulation, supervised clinical practice, and structured patient care. Institutional Backing, Local Accreditation The National Postgraduate Medical College of Nigeria (NPMCN) will oversee the academic standards and award official postgraduate fellowship diplomas upon completion, while Redeemer’s University will lead specialised training for nursing teams and biomedical maintenance engineers. Vice-Chancellor of Redeemer’s University, Prof. Shadrach Akindele, and NPMCN President Prof. Anthony Ikefuna both hailed the project as a decisive milestone. Following RHV’s landmark execution of Nigeria’s first robotic and telesurgical procedures in September, the academy is positioned to establish West Africa as a regional hub for technology-driven patient care. Redeemer’s Health Village is a faith-based tertiary medical facility established by the Redeemed Christian Church of God (RCCG). The post FG Designates Redeemer’s Health Village As TETFund Centre, Guarantees Scholarships For Robotic Surgery Academy appeared first on Channels Television .

Brick, the company behind the $59 gadget that blocks you from using apps on your phone, has launched a new device that’s designed to help you cut back on doomscrolling in bed. The $129 Brick Night introduces a location-based element: instead of requiring you to tap your phone against the device, like the OG Brick , this version uses Bluetooth to automatically kick in when you enter your bedroom (or any other room you put it in).
The Brick Night uses two CR2477 batteries, and you can set a location zone of up to 25 feet x 25 feet. Both this and the Brick allow you to select specific apps to block instead of rendering your entire phone inaccessible, but the pitch with the Night version is that the blocking happens automatically in the background when you enter the room, and so won’t interrupt or add new steps to your usual bedtime routine.
Brick’s night version also supports multiple users, and each can independently configure their own settings, modes, blocked app selection, time windows, and spaces. Still, the Brick Night is more than twice the price, and because it doesn’t include NFC capabilities, it can’t be used for both location-based and tap-based blocking — which would allow it to replace the original Brick.

title: Ukraine must develop new logistics routes through Romania and Moldova — MP
body:
MP Oksana Savchuk said this in a comment to Ukrinform at the Rebuilding Ukraine Forum in Bucharest.
Savchuk said developing logistics routes via the Danube and Romania’s transport infrastructure is strategically important for Ukraine, particularly for moving goods and supporting the economy.
“In terms of ports, this is issue number one for Ukraine, because cooperation through the Danube and through Constanța Airport is extremely important for logistics and cargo transport,” the MP said.
She stressed the need to secure European Union financing to restore and create new logistics routes between Ukraine, Romania and Moldova. Given the limited capacity of the Black Sea corridor, Ukraine must consider alternative transport options, including routes through the Baltic region.
“At this forum, I will be presenting the importance of securing EU‑level financing to restore new logistics routes between Ukraine, Romania and Moldova,” Savchuk said.
Another focus of her work at the forum is presenting investment opportunities in Ivano‑Frankivsk region and its communities. She arrived in Bucharest together with representatives of local governments from Ivano‑Frankivsk, Kalush and the Zelena community, which borders Romania directly.
Savchuk said communication has resumed on the prospect of opening a new border crossing on the Ukrainian–Romanian border within the Zelena community. Such a step could strengthen cross‑border ties and create additional opportunities for passenger movement and cargo transport.
“Recently, communication has resumed regarding the possibility of opening a future border crossing between Ivano‑Frankivsk region and the Romanian side. This can be done only on the territory of the Zelena community,” the MP said.
She also named rail‑infrastructure development as a priority. Savchuk said Ukraine must build additional rail lines and adjust logistics routes to expand transport capacity toward Romania and other European countries.
Among the expected outcomes of the forum, Savchuk said, are developing cooperation concepts between Ukrainian communities and identifying partner cities in Romania. This should support regional investment projects and deepen economic ties between the two countries.
As reported, Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha and EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Kaja Kallas coordinated efforts in a phone call to maintain stable operations of Ukraine’s food corridor in the Black Sea.
According to the Institute for the Study of War (ISW), Moscow seeks to disrupt not only maritime but also land‑based exports from Ukraine.

title: Abu Dhabi Considered for Ukraine-Russia-US Talks in November
body:
Abu Dhabi is being considered as the venue for renewed talks between Ukraine, Russia and the United States, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Thursday, Oct. 22 .
Moscow has suggested holding the meeting around mid-November, while Kyiv wants talks by early November. The three sides have not jointly confirmed a date or venue.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Peskov told reporters that the UAE capital was under discussion but declined to elaborate on preparations for documents or proposals ahead of the meeting.
Russian presidential aide Yuri Ushakov had indicated a possible meeting around mid-November , describing it as talks between negotiating teams or experts. He said Russia had not yet decided who would attend.
President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Wednesday, Oct. 21, that Ukraine supported a US proposal to meet as soon as possible, preferably no later than early November.
“We have received feedback that Russia supports a trilateral meeting at the level of our negotiating teams,” Zelensky told reporters, according to Reuters .
He said Ukraine was ready to participate. Kyiv Post previously reported that Washington had relayed Moscow’s willingness to resume the negotiations following US envoy Steve Witkoff’s visit to Russia.
The diplomatic contacts began with talks in Oslo on Oct. 20 involving Witkoff, Zelensky and European leaders. They discussed security guarantees, territorial questions, sanctions and Ukraine’s postwar economy.
Witkoff then met Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg on Oct. 21 to discuss proposals emerging from those consultations.
Representatives of Ukraine, Russia and the US held three rounds of negotiations earlier this year : two in Abu Dhabi in January and February, followed by talks in Geneva in February. Those meetings did not produce an agreement to end the war.
Ushakov said Moscow wanted the next round to focus on security arrangements for Russia and Ukraine after the war.
Kyiv has backed renewed negotiations while also calling for a ceasefire, an end to attacks on energy infrastructure and humanitarian measures. No shared agenda for the proposed Abu Dhabi meeting has been announced.
Ukraine is also seeking enforceable guarantees against another Russian attack. As Kyiv Post reported, Zelensky has outlined US commitments modeled on NATO’s Article 5 and backed by Congress, alongside NATO membership and a European-led Coalition of the Willing.
He has described those arrangements as complementary, rather than competing alternatives. No final agreement on the guarantees has been announced.
The proposed November meeting would bring negotiating teams back together; it would not itself constitute a leaders’ summit or confirmation that the parties are ready to sign a settlement.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Sinai Monastery Deal Nears Breakthrough with Egypt
body: Negotiations over the future of Saint Catherine’s Monastery in Sinai are nearing a decisive stage, with Archbishop Symeon reportedly preparing to accept a proposed agreement with Egypt following consultations with senior Greek Orthodox Church officials. According to Greek news outlet Proto Thema, Archbishop Symeon informed Egyptian officials by telephone that he intends to accept the compromise, which has been under discussion for several months. The agreement aims to resolve the dispute over the monastery’s property status and safeguard its future. Archbishop May Confirm Acceptance in Writing Archbishop Symeon’s illness currently prevents him from travelling to Egypt to sign the agreement in person. Instead, he is expected to send a signed letter formally confirming his acceptance, with an in-person signing to follow when his health permits. Once the letter reaches Egyptian officials, the Greek government is expected to be informed so that the next steps can be coordinated through diplomatic channels. Greek Church Supports the Compromise The Holy Synod of the Hierarchy of the Church of Greece, known as the DIS, has played a key role in advancing the negotiations. During discussions, senior Church officials examined the proposed agreement and its implications for the monastery and the interests of Hellenism. George Kallantzis, secretary-general of Greece’s Ministry of Education and Religious Affairs, also participated. Greek Foreign Minister George Gerapetritis has reportedly discussed the matter with his Egyptian counterpart in recent days, highlighting the diplomatic importance of reaching a settlement. Supreme Court Decision Adds Urgency The negotiations are taking place ahead of a decision expected from Greece’s Supreme Court, the Areios Pagos, on October 24. According to Proto Thema, once Archbishop Symeon formally confirms his acceptance, the Greek government is expected to request a suspension of the decision through diplomatic channels. The move would give the parties an opportunity to advance the agreement and bring the dispute closer to resolution. Protecting a Historic Orthodox Institution Located at the foot of Mount Sinai in Egypt, Saint Catherine’s Monastery is one of the world’s oldest continuously operating Christian monasteries and a major centre of Orthodox Christian heritage. The dispute has focused on the monastery’s property status and its long-term future, raising concerns in Greece about the protection of its religious, historical and cultural significance. The proposed agreement seeks to secure the monastery against future legal challenges and establish a framework for its continued operation. With Archbishop Symeon preparing to communicate his acceptance and Greek and Egyptian officials engaged in diplomatic discussions, the negotiations have entered a crucial phase. The next steps will determine how the agreement is formalised and how the pending court proceedings are addressed. title: South Ossetia’s new government takes shape, with Russian officials in top posts
body: South Ossetia has appointed a new prime minister after parliament unanimously backed 44-year-old Soslan Margiev, a former chairman of the Moscow Region Court. Addressing MPs, Margiev said the region needed reforms. His priorities include making high-quality healthcare more accessible, improving South Ossetia’s investment appeal, developing its tourism potential and expanding social benefits. “We have every opportunity to deliver these changes through our strategic partnership with the Russian Federation. We need to build an effective system of public administration that will help us develop our economy and social sector and, ultimately, improve living standards in our country,” the new prime minister said. Clarify Margiev’s previous judicial roleMake the Russian partnership wording more neutral South Ossetia election: as expected, former Moscow official Marat Kambolov becomes new president Russian State Duma MP Kazbek Taisaev, who observed the election: “Russia will continue to provide South Ossetia with comprehensive support” Soslan Margiev Soslan Margiev was born in Tskhinval and studied law in North Ossetia before working in various Russian courts. He has now made the unlikely career move to become South Ossetia’s prime minister. Some people in South Ossetia see him as a protégé of influential businessman Anatoly Margiev, head of the Ossetian diaspora in Sochi, and suspect the two men are related. However, the new president, Marat Kambolov, who personally selected Margiev for the post, justified his choice by arguing that a legal professional would find it easier to restore law and order in South Ossetia. “When I arrived here, I was certain that the head of government would definitely come from Moscow. He didn’t necessarily have to be an administrator. But after working here, meeting people and speaking with many of you, we made the only right decision. He is a lawyer in the fullest sense of the word. We are building a state governed by the rule of law,” Kambolov said. Unlike Kambolov himself, Margiev at least comes from South Ossetia. So he is not entirely an outsider. Moscow's new man in Tskhinvali: what Kambolov's appointment means – views from Tbilisi Three interpretations of Kambolov’s appointment in Tskhinvali: a new stage of annexation, a Kremlin–Tbilisi agreement, or simply an anti-corruption effort Kambolov previously signed decrees appointing several ministers and a first deputy prime minister before parliament had officially confirmed the prime minister in office, thereby breaching the procedure for forming a government. Ekaterina Tolstikova Last week, he appointed local officials to head the interior ministry, emergency situations ministry, defence ministry and other departments. However, he named another Moscow-based official, Ekaterina Tolstikova , as first deputy prime minister. She is a former colleague of Kambolov, with whom she worked in Russia’s federal government. The cabinet is still incomplete. The posts of economy, agriculture, justice, and education and science ministers remain vacant. Kambolov has also made appointments at the State Security Committee (KGB). He dismissed an appointee of the former president and replaced him with Yevgeny Romanov , whom he also brought in from Russia. EU does not recognise “presidential election” in Georgia’s Russian-occupied Tskhinvali region EU condemns appointment of Russian official as “president of South Ossetia” and calls on Russia to stop actions undermining Georgia’s territorial integrity Thus, the top three positions in South Ossetia’s government — president, prime minister and deputy prime minister — are held by Russian officials who had no previous experience in politics as such. Two of them have never had any connection with South Ossetia. However, judging by social media and opinion polls, the people of South Ossetia do not seem to find this unacceptable, provided the “imported” government does its job and delivers on its many ambitious promises. Only time will tell. The terminology, place names and views expressed in this article are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the editorial position of this website. title: Police warn officers, public against bail payments
body: The Nigeria Police Force has warned that officers who demand money for bail will face disciplinary action, while members of the public who pay for bail risks arrest and prosecution. SP Awu Fidelis, the Head of the Complaints Response Unit (CRU), Force Headquarters, Abuja, gave the warning during a sensitisation rally in Lagos on Friday. The rally was organised by the CRU in partnership with the Eagle Crime Awareness and Prevention Initiative (ECAPI). Fidelis said the Inspector-General of Police, Mr Olatunji Disu, had repeatedly emphasised that bail was free and that no money should be demanded or paid for the release of arrested persons. He urged residents to report officers who demanded money for bail, stressing that both the giver and receiver would be arrested and prosecuted. According to Fidelis, the partnership between the police and ECAPI is an important initiative towards rebuilding public trust, strengthening accountability and improving police-public relations. He said complaints against police personnel were investigated and appropriate disciplinary measures taken against officers found culpable. “The increasing number of people reporting misconduct through the CRU’s offices and communication channels indicated the growing public confidence in the complaint-handling process, ” he said. He said members of the public could report police misconduct through the CRU’s telephone lines, 08057000001 and 08057000002, for calls, 08057000003 for WhatsApp complaints, as well as its social media platforms. Also speaking, the Officer-in-Charge of the CRU, Lagos State Command, DSP Idris Mogaji said the unit had recorded successes in addressing complaints against police officers through prompt investigations and disciplinary measures. “We keep the complainants informed about the progress and outcomes of investigations, including disciplinary decisions taken against officers found culpable,”he said. He said the Commissioner of Police in the state, Mr Fatai Tijani, had convened a meeting with officers to address concerns, including personnel using unregistered vehicles, particularly buses, “The command has taken steps to ensure compliance with the directive and had acted on a recent incident involving some police officers,” he said. He urged residents to report unprofessional conduct through 09111111151, 09111111150, the command’s social media platforms or written petitions to the CP, reaffirming the command’s commitment to accountability. The founder of ECAPI, Amb. Samuel Eniola said the organisation would extend its campaign on police accountability and crime prevention to communities, markets, motor parks and police formations across Lagos State. Eniola said the campaign aimed to educate residents, particularly youths, on the functions of the CRU and how to report police misconduct. He said the exercise would cover local government areas, communities, police stations, barracks, area commands, transport unions and other associations across the state. According to him, .the campaign will also target police personnel to help improve their understanding of the CRU and its role in receiving and addressing complaints against officers. Eniola said the ECAPI had begun engaging local governments and had received encouraging responses, adding that the outreach would continue across the state. He identified the youths as key target, noting that sustained sensitisation was necessary to educate them on criminal behaviour and its consequences. The ECAPI founder said community-based engagements would help reach young people who might not regularly access to information through television, radio or newspapers. He added that the initiative’s mandate extended beyond advocacy against police brutality. It also include crime prevention, responsible behaviour and cooperation with law enforcement agencies to build a safer society and strengthen police-public relations. In his remarks, Tijani, represented by the Deputy Commissioner of Police in charge of Administration, Mr Anthony Placid, expressed the command’s support for the partnership. He commended the leaderships of the CRU and the ECAPI, describing the collaboration between the police and advocacy organisations as timely and important for strengthening public trust. Tijani said such cooperation could improve information sharing, promote accountability and enhance security at the community level. title: Seven killed as gunmen open fire near Christian church in Jordan — TV
body:
BEIRUT, October 23. /TASS/. At least seven people were killed in a terrorist attack on a funeral procession near a Christian church in the Jordanian city of Al-Karak, a source in the kingdom’s security service told Al Mamlaka television channel.
"Gunmen opened fire from a vehicle at people gathered near the church. Seven people were killed and around 10 were injured, some of them in critical condition," the source told the television channel.
Two masked gunmen were shooting at the crowd for several minutes and then fled the scene, the television channel cited witnesses. They did not get inside the church where more than 150 people has gathered.
Security forces have blocked all entry roads to Al-Karak and are combing city quarters.

title: Yle price comparison: Finland's food prices lower than Sweden, Estonia
body:
A Lidl grocery basket was cheaper in Helsinki than in Tallinn or Stockholm.
The same product, the same retail chain and possibly even the same manufacturer.
But the price can vary considerably depending on whether you buy the item in Helsinki, Athens or Stockholm.
Yle compared the price of the same basket of groceries in Lidl stores in Finland, Sweden, Estonia, Poland, Germany, Spain and Greece.
Lidl was chosen for the comparison because it is the only grocery chain with stores both in Finland and in other European countries. Thirty staples were included in the shopping basket.
Finland has long been known as an expensive country in comparisons, but the old perceptions are becoming outdated. Tallinn, for example, once a go-to for cheap shopping, has closed the price gap and is now more expensive than Helsinki.
Food in Finland still costs more than the European average, but the gap has narrowed in recent years. In this comparison, the grocery basket cost roughly the same in Helsinki, Stockholm and Tallinn.
Differences in the grocery basket prices are explained by taxation, wage levels and transport costs, as well as competition between shops and consumer habits.
But the biggest factor behind the differences is food inflation in recent years. Prices have risen in Finland too, but elsewhere inflation has galloped ahead faster. In Estonia, for example, food prices climbed faster than anywhere else in the eurozone in 2022, by more than 19 percent.
Finland's food prices were lower last year than in Estonia and in the other Nordic countries, according to Eurostat.
Price differences between Finland and Estonia are explained by wages and taxes, among other things.
Retail workers in Finland earn more than their Estonian counterparts, which pushes up costs.
In Estonia, meanwhile, the value-added tax on food is 24 percent, compared with 13.5 percent in Finland. This raises prices in Estonia relative to Finland and partly explains why a grocery basket in Tallinn has crept up to Helsinki's level, both in Yle's comparison and in Eurostat's figures.
Finns' preference for domestic products shows up especially in meat. Lidl in Finland sells plenty of Finnish meat because consumers want it.
"Estonian consumers favor imported products more than Finns do. That means meat can be brought in from Poland, for example, where production costs are lower," said Bate Ismail , an economist at the Finnish Food and Drink Industries' Federation.
Vegetables in Finland are up to a fifth more expensive than the EU average. Transport costs are among the factors behind this. When it comes to domestic production, heating and lighting greenhouses drive up costs.
The flip side is coffee, which is cheaper in Finland. Cheap coffee is an important way for shops to lure customers, as are cheese and sweets.
The same phenomenon shows up in olive oil, which is cheaper in southern countries than in the north. In Greece and Spain, olive oil is a so-called loss leader.
In Finland, Lidl keeps a particularly close eye on S Group pricing. If shoppers pay more for comparable products in rival Finnish stores, Lidl has no need to cut its prices to the level of other countries.
