title: Rassvet satellite constellation to comprise hundreds of spacecraft — Bureau 1440
body:
MOSCOW, October 23. /TASS/. Russia’s Rassvet low-Earth orbit satellite constellation will comprise several hundred spacecraft that will provide next-generation satellite communications, Dmitry Agafonov, Deputy CEO for Business Development and Products at Bureau 1440, said in an interview with the Vesti TV program.
"We’re talking about several hundred spacecraft in low Earth orbit that are interconnected via laser communication terminals to ensure precisely this seamless transmission of information from any point on the planet to the final recipient. We’re talking about user devices. These are subscriber terminals. We’ve already introduced a line of digital subscriber terminals as part of our digital solutions," he said.
According to Agafonov, Rassvet will employ a polar constellation, which will ensure the broadest possible coverage across Russia. The constellation will support solutions in various fields: from geological exploration to emergency rescue services.
In addition, Bureau 1440 terminals will be installed on high-speed trains and long-distance trains. By 2027, the terminals will be installed on more than 500 trains, Agafonov added.
In 2026, Bureau 1440 successfully launched the first two batches of spacecraft for the Rassvet low-Earth orbit constellation. The spacecraft are equipped with 5G NTN-based communication, an upgraded power supply system, next-generation inter-satellite laser communication terminals, and a plasma propulsion system.

title: $242m Petroleum Products Diversion Claim: UBA secures court order against Vitol, four others
body:
A Lagos State High Court, last Thursday, granted interim preservative orders of Mareva Injunction against Vitol SA – a Switzerland based Energy Trading company, and four other shipping companies in favour of United Bank for Africa Plc.
The bank accused Vitol of wrongful release of cargoes of petroleum products which were consigned to the order of United Bank for Africa Plc in the Bills of Lading.
Addressing the Court, Bode Olanipekun, SAN, lead counsel for United Bank for Africa, urged the Court to grant the interim preservative orders against Vitol and the other shippers.
In a ruling on the application, the presiding judge, Hon Justice K A Jose granted three prayers in UBA’s application, including requests to restrain the dissipation of assets and dealings with funds up to the disputed amount by Vitol S.A.
“Prayers 1–3 are granted as prayed against the 2nd Respondent only,” the judge ruled.
The application was brought pursuant to Order 43 Rule 1 of the High Court of Lagos State (Civil Procedure) Rules 2019 and the Lagos State High Court Practice Direction No. 2 of 2019.
UBA is seeking to contend in the substantive proceedings that Vitol SA and the owners of the vessels, are liable for alleged conversion, misrepresentation and negligence arising from the non-delivery of the petroleum products.
UBA also cited 34 financial institutions and public agencies, including commercial banks, merchant banks, microfinance banks, the Nigerian Ports Authority and the Nigeria Customs Service, in connection with the application.
In an affidavit supporting the application, UBA’s Group Head of Recoveries and Remedial Management, Anthony Chilaka, stated that the bank issued a letter of credit for the benefit of Vitol SA to facilitate a petroleum products transactions.
UBA alleged that the cargo was transported to Nigeria and that the vessels’ masters issued several bills of lading.
The bank further alleged that Vitol subsequently endorsed the bills of lading “to the order of” UBA and handed over the original copies to it.
UBA maintained that the endorsement entitled it to take possession of the cargo upon completion of the voyage.
However, Chilaka stated that the bank had not received the gasoil despite the completion of the voyage.
“The applicant has not been given possession of the gasoil despite completion of the voyage,” the affidavit stated.
UBA alleged that the cargo was instead, applied to the use of another party, contending that the respondents’ failure to deliver it amounted to conversion and negligence.
The bank argued that the respondents had obligations arising from the transaction and the endorsement of the shipping documents, which it claimed were not fulfilled.
The bank alleged that the cargoes associated with those transactions were also diverted to the use of other parties after their voyages, rather than delivered to UBA.

title: Jide Kosoko laments debt as N300m cinema film fails to make profit
body: By Adegboyega Adeleye Veteran Nollywood actor and filmmaker Jide Kosoko says he is in debt after his film, Eleko: Oba Esugbayi , failed to recoup its production cost of more than N300 million at the cinemas. Kosoko made the disclosure in a recent interview with African A-List, saying the film was financed by investors who expected returns, not money given to him as a gift. “My film ‘Eleko: Oba Esugbayi’ that recently came out and we took to the cinemas, cost us over N300 million. Do I have 300 million? You should know that some people gave it to me and it was not that they dashed me; they invested in it and we took the film to the cinemas,” he said. The filmmaker said the movie did not generate enough revenue to recover the investment. The small amount it earned was shared among those involved in the project. “Different things happened and we did not earn our money back. The little that was earned was split. As I am, if you hear someone with debt dancing around their neck, it is me,” Kosoko said. In another account of the interview, Kosoko was quoted as clarifying that the debt remark was not necessarily a reference to unpaid wages. He said the people who worked on the production had been paid, but the film did not deliver the financial returns he and the investors had hoped for. He also acknowledged the substantial investments made by cinema operators when asked about the film’s cinema earnings and their distribution. “I won’t deceive anyone, but truly, those who own the cinemas have huge investments,” he said. Kosoko’s comments echo concerns raised by actor and filmmaker Ramsey Nouah, who has said that releasing a film in cinemas does not always make financial sense. Nouah said only a small fraction of cinema releases recover their production costs and turn a profit, adding that producers can still fail to recoup their investment after spending heavily on advertising and promotion. The post Jide Kosoko laments debt as N300m cinema film fails to make profit appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: NDC mourns Efiewura actor Kwame Dzokoto, celebrates his political contributions to the party
body: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Western Region has expressed profound sorrow over the death of celebrated television personality and party communicator Seth Kwame Dzokoto, popularly known as Efiewura and SKD. In a statement, the party described his death as a major loss to the NDC, Ghana’s media and entertainment industry, and the wider public, citing his distinctive presentation style, humour and ability to connect with audiences. Mr Dzokoto began his political communication career as Deputy Constituency Communications Officer for Tarkwa-Nsuaem before becoming the NDC’s parliamentary candidate for the constituency in the 2016 general elections. He also served on the Western Regional Communications Committee between 2018 and 2022, contributing to the party’s communication and advocacy activities. The party recalled that in 2023, when he faced serious health challenges, former President John Dramani Mahama facilitated arrangements to support his medical treatment abroad. According to the statement, his surgery was successful, and he returned to public and political engagement after recovering. The NDC said it was particularly saddened by reports that Mr Dzokoto died while participating in a radio discussion on the forthcoming constituency election, describing the circumstances as a reflection of his commitment to political discourse and party work. “His exceptional ability to connect with people, entertain audiences and communicate political ideas made him a cherished personality among his colleagues, supporters and the general public,” the statement said. The party said his death had left a painful void in its Western Regional Communications Bureau, adding that his contributions to broadcasting and political communication would continue to inspire future generations. It extended its condolences to his wife, children, extended family, friends, media colleagues and members of the NDC fraternity. The statement was signed by the Western Regional Communications Officer, Richard Ernest Kirk-Mensah, on behalf of the party’s regional leadership and members.

title: Police Rescue 11 Ghanaian Fraud Victims in Ogun
body: James Sowole in Abeokuta and Becky Uba Umenyili Operatives of the Ogun State Police Command have rescued 11 Ghanaian nationals allegedly held hostage in the Sagamu area of the state, who were lured to Nigeria with promises of Canadian and Spanish visas. The victims, comprising seven males and four females, were allegedly deceived by a fellow Ghanaian national, who promised to facilitate their overseas travel, and extorted huge amounts of money from them before bringing them to Nigeria and holding them in captivity. Following a tip-off, the Anti-Kidnapping Unit of the Command launched an attack at the identified hideout and safely rescued all 11 victims. Recent investigations indicate that the victims are receiving appropriate care and support, while detectives intensify efforts to track down and apprehend all persons connected with the alleged criminal network. Meanwhile, the state Commissioner of Police, Mr. Bode Ojajuni, emphasized the Command’s resolve to protect lives and combat trans-national crime, as he lamented the heinous crime, stating categorically that there is “no haven for criminals who exploit the hopes of others.” The police boss enjoined the public to verify all overseas travel and visa-processing arrangements before making commitments, while also assuring them that the Command would make efforts to bring the culprits to justice.

title: Bagbin assures Ghanaians of passage of anti-LGBTQ+ bill after review
body: Speaker of Parliament Alban Bagbin has assured Ghanaians that the Proper Human Sexual Rights and Ghanaian Family Values Bill will be passed into law after Parliament undertakes a second consideration of the legislation to correct errors identified in the version initially approved. He said the bill, popularly known as the anti-LGBTQ+ bill, would be reconsidered during Parliament’s next sitting, stressing that the legislation should be treated as a matter of national consensus. Speaking at the ongoing IPR Ghana 2026 National PR Conference and Excellence Awards in Koforidua, Mr Bagbin explained that the initial passage took place in his absence and was rushed, prompting him to call for a review of the process. “When the law was rushed through at the last minute at my back, I came out and said no way, this bill must go through as a consensus bill. We don’t want partisanship in it. It is for everybody. It means a lot to Ghanaians,” he said. The Speaker said Parliament had identified errors, particularly in some last-minute amendments, which would be addressed during the second consideration before the legislative process proceeds. “We have identified a few mistakes, most of the last-minute amendments, and therefore the next meeting will come back for a second consideration, and we’ll pass it,” he said. Mr Bagbin further insisted that the legislation would become law under his watch, adding: “When we are no longer there, you can do what you want to do. But so far as we continue to exist, that law will be the law of the land. You can do whatever you want after I’m gone.” He also commended the Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, for his contribution to the parliamentary debate on the bill, saying his role had made Ghana proud.

title: Botchorishvili Hosts Central Asian Foreign Ministers in Batumi
body: Georgian Dream Foreign Minister Maka Botchorishvili hosted a meeting of counterparts from five Central Asian countries in the coastal city of Batumi, discussing bilateral partnerships and Middle Corridor cooperation amid Tbilisi’s intensifying engagement with the region. The visiting officials included Turkmenistan’s Foreign Minister Rashid Meredov, Kazakhstan’s Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tleuberdi, Kyrgyz Foreign Minister Zheenbek Kulubaev, Tajikistan’s Foreign Minister Sirojiddin Muhriddin, and Uzbek Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov. As part of the event, Botchorishvili held a series of bilateral meetings with her counterparts, discussing further deepening “bilateral and multilateral relations” and the importance of “developing the Middle Corridor,” a trade route linking Asia and Europe while bypassing Russia, the Georgian Foreign Ministry reported. In a briefing following the October 23 meeting, Botchorishvili spoke about “a historical friendship, shared economic interests, a common goal of strengthening the ties between Europe and Asia, and the particular importance of the development of the Middle Corridor.” “Today’s meeting also showed that Georgia is a very important country for Central Asia to have access to international markets,” she added. The evening before, on October 22, Georgian Dream Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze also hosted the visiting Foreign Ministers at an official dinner, where he reiterated that “deepening relations with Central Asian countries and further developing cooperation across various sectors is a priority for the Government of Georgia,” according to the official press release. The Batumi meeting is a continuation of Tbilisi’s increased engagement with Central Asian countries as Tbilisi seeks to promote its role in the Middle Corridor, including through a series of recent high-level visits and signing strategic partnership documents with Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan. Georgian Dream government officials, led by Kobakhidze, have traveled in recent months to Kyrgyzstan , Tajikistan , and Kazakhstan , while in July two Central Asian leaders, Uzbekistan’s President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Turkmenistan’s President Serdar Berdimuhamedov, visited Georgia. The increased engagement between Georgia and Central Asian countries also comes amid strained relations between Tbilisi and its traditional Western partners, including the United States and the European Union. title: Higher sales lift Guinness Nigeria’s nine-month profit 53% to ₦40.7 billion
body:
Guinness Nigeria reported a 53.1 per cent boost in bottom line for the nine months to September, relative to the same period of last year, according to the latest unaudited report of the alcoholic beverage manufacturer.
Profit after tax stood at ₦40.7 billion, up from ₦26.6 billion a year ago, as third-quarter profit accounted for 37.8 per cent or ₦15.4 billion of the earnings posted in the period, contributing more than one third of revenue.
Nigeria remains the company’s primary market as it was responsible for more than 98 per cent or ₦397 billion of sales, while exports contributed ₦6.3 billion.
Revenue climbed to N403.3 billion from ₦335.1 billion, while gross profit was up by 20.4 per cent.
Guinness Nigeria is majority-owned by Singapore-based Tolaram Group, the lead developer and major equity investor in Nigeria’s deepest sea port, the Lekki Deep Sea Port, which acquired a controlling stake of 58 per cent in the company from Diageo in 2024.
Diageo, the British multinational owner of Guinness’ global operations, said after divesting its stake that it is sticking to the brand’s ownership in Nigeria even though it has been licensed to Tolaram on a long-term basis.
Operating profit rose 23.4 per cent to ₦65 billion. Finance costs fell 71.9 per cent to ₦4.3 billion after the company sharply cut back finance expense on loans and borrowings, easing the pressure on pre-tax profit, in turn boosting earnings.
Total assets advanced to ₦271.5 billion from ₦245.2 billion, lifted by a jump in inventories and property, plant & equipment.
In April, Guinness Nigeria resumed dividend payments after a four-year pause, triggered by loss-making, and announced an interim dividend per share of N₦2.00 for the first quarter of the year.
In a corporate announcement on Wednesday, the company declared an interim dividend of ₦7.00 per share for the third quarter of the year, equivalent to a potential payout of ₦15.3 billion.
Shareholders, “whose names appear in the Register of Members as at the close of business on Friday, 30 October 2026,” are eligible for the cash distribution, the company said. Payment is scheduled for 13 November, it added.

title: Ukraine to switch to winter time on October 25
body:
Kyiv and the rest of Ukraine will switch to winter time at 0400 on Sunday, October 25, the Kyiv City State Administration said.

The administration warned that the clock change can challenge the body's adjustment mechanisms and negatively affect the well-being of people with chronic illnesses, sleep disorders or cardiovascular problems, as well as older people and children.

To ease the transition, doctors recommend gradually shifting sleep schedules by going to bed and waking up 15-20 minutes later in the days before the clock change. They also advise spending at least 20-30 minutes outdoors in daylight each day, as daylight helps regulate melatonin levels and walking can reduce stress.

The administration also recommends maintaining regular meal times, eating a substantial breakfast soon after waking up, and avoiding smartphones and news feeds for an hour before bedtime to improve sleep quality.

People are also advised to reduce physical and emotional strain during the firs…

title: Virginia man arrested after Quantico Iwo Jima statue defaced with sledgehammer
body: A Virginia man was arrested on Wednesday after allegedly using a sledgehammer to decapitate the statue depicting Marine Corps Cpl. Harlon Block from Quantico’s Iwo Jima sculpture. At roughly 10:13 p.m., officers with the Prince William County Police Department responded to calls about property destruction near Marine Corps Base Quantico in Virginia. Miguel Alonso Maldonado Soriano, 27, was arrested at the scene and has been charged with felony destruction of property, trespass with intent to damage property, and felony injury to a monument, per the police department. The alleged destruction via a sledgehammer has caused hundreds of thousands of dollars in damage to the historic military monument, police said. Per the Washington Post , a second Marine from the statue is missing the bayonet from the rifle slung over his back, while a third figure’s helmet and face had been “chipped and gouged.” The memorial was created in honor of Associated Press photographer Joe Rosenthal’s iconic photograph of U.S. Marines raising the flag over Mount Suribachi, Iwo Jima, on Feb. 23, 1945. Austrian-born American sculptor Felix de Weldon, serving with the U.S. Navy at the time, was so moved by the image that he immediately constructed a scale model of the flag raising. It would take him another nine and a half years to complete the full-sized model now standing in Arlington, Virginia. The smaller monument, allegedly defaced by Maldonado Soriano, stands near the National Museum of the Marine Corps. Maldonado Soriano is being held without bond pending a court appearance.

title: Mahama urges UK to prioritise Africa’s debt challenges during G20 presidency
body: President John Dramani Mahama has called on the United Kingdom to use its 2027 presidency of the G20 to help address Africa’s growing debt challenges and push for reforms to the global financial system. He said the high cost of debt repayment was limiting African countries’ ability to invest in critical sectors such as education, healthcare, road infrastructure and job creation. Speaking at a meeting with the cross-party UK Parliamentary Group in London on Friday, October 23, President Mahama called for stronger international cooperation to help African countries manage their debt obligations and secure more affordable financing. He urged the UK to make Africa’s debt challenges a priority during its leadership of the G20, a forum of major economies that discusses global financial and economic issues. President Mahama’s appeal comes amid concerns over the pressure debt servicing places on public finances across the continent, reducing the resources available for development priorities. He called for reforms that would make the global financial system more responsive to the needs of developing economies and improve their access to financing for sustainable development.

title: Authorities investigating whether first Kenya and Nigeria Ebola cases crossed paths
body:
Kenya Red Cross personnel during a simulation of the evacuation of remains of an Ebola victim in the Kenyan capital Nairobi on October 22. Kenyan authorities detected a ninth case of Ebola in the country, the health ministry said Tuesday. Tony Karumba/AFP via Getty Images hide caption
JOHANNESBURG – The first Ebola patient confirmed in Nigeria may have crossed paths with the first Kenyan Ebola patient at a Ugandan airport, health officials said Thursday.
Nigeria announced its first case of Ebola in more than a decade on Tuesday. Nigerian health authorities said the patient is the Ugandan-born wife of a diplomat based in Abuja who had vacationed in Uganda in September and returned to Nigeria earlier this month.
She is being treated and 44 people she had close contact with have been quarantined, Dr. Wessam Mankoula, head of emergency preparedness and response at the Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, told a press briefing on Thursday.
Authorities are now investigating what the source of her exposure was.
Nigeria, Africa's most populous country, is the fourth on the continent to record an Ebola case during the current outbreak, but it's the first in West Africa and the furthest away from the epicenter in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
Congo's current Ebola outbreak began in May in the country's east. It has become the fastest spreading on record. At least 4,600 people have died and about 9,700 have been infected in Congo.
Neighboring Uganda initially recorded about 20 cases but was declared Ebola-free in August.
The first case in Kenya was recorded in early October and since then eight other cases have been confirmed in the east African nation.
The first Kenyan patient, who has since died, travelled from Congo to Kenya, via Uganda.
Officials are now investigating whether that person crossed paths with the Nigeria case at the Entebbe International Airport in Uganda – as they were there on the same day.
Dr. Mankoula said the center was probing whether there had been "some sort of interaction between the two cases at the airport."
Ebola is spread through direct contact with an infected person's bodily fluids or contaminated items. It causes severe fever and can be deadly. However, generally people are not considered infectious until they start showing symptoms.

title: Putin discusses measures to protect youths from external threats with Security Council
body:
NOVO-OGARYOVO, October 23. /TASS/. Russian President Vladimir Putin focused on countering attempts from abroad to influence the country’s youths at a meeting on Friday with permanent Security Council members.
"Much work is being done with the youth environment and our youths in our country. And it is finding specific, versatile content," the head of state told participants in the meeting via video link. "However, there are threats as attempts are being made from abroad to influence the country’s youths," he added.
The meeting was attended by Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin, speaker of Russia’s Federation Council, or upper house of parliament, Valentina Matviyenko, State Duma Speaker Vyacheslav Volodin, Security Council Deputy Chairman Dmitry Medvedev, Security Council Secretary Sergey Shoigu, Presidential Administration Head Anton Vaino, and Federal Security Service Director Alexander Bortnikov.

title: Casualties feared as multi-storey building collapses in Nairobi
body: A multi-storey building collapsed mid-construction in the Kenyan capital on Friday, the Red Cross said, with reports from local media of casualties and looting at the site. Videos spreading online showed a dramatic crash and huge clouds of dust as the building came down in a busy business and residential district. “At around 1340 hours, a multi-storey building under construction collapsed on 9th Street in Eastleigh, Nairobi,” the Red Cross posted on X, adding that it had dispatched a team. Local media reported looting and possible casualties trapped beneath the rubble, with images showing large crowds gathered at the site. There were conflicting reports on the size of the building, which may have been as high as 18 storeys. Eastleigh is a densely packed residential and market area, known as a hub for the Somali community. Nairobi is undergoing an extremely rapid construction boom, with high-rise buildings appearing all over the city as Kenya’s population expands. AFP The post Casualties feared as multi-storey building collapses in Nairobi appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Netanyahu announces largest operation in West Bank since 1967
body:
TEL AVIV, October 23. /TASS/. Israel is preparing to launch a large-scale military operation in the West Bank, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has announced. He described it as the largest operation of its kind since the 1967 Six-Day War, during which Israel took control of the West Bank, then under Jordanian rule.
"Defense Minister Israel Katz and I oversaw the planning of a very large-scale IDF operation in Judea and Samaria [Israel’s designation for the West Bank - TASS]. Nothing on this scale has been seen since the Six-Day War. The IDF is ready to carry it out. We will decide on the timing, but it will take place soon," Netanyahu said, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office.
He made this statement after an attack by armed Palestinian radicals near the city of Hebron earlier on Friday, as a result of which five Israelis were wounded. The shooters were eliminated on the spot. After the incident, the Israeli military surrounded Hebron and began combing the area in search of possible accomplices. Netanyahu then announced his intention to isolate the West Bank.
Now the prime minister has unveiled plans to tighten military policy towards the West Bank. According to him, whereas before the army confined itself to destroying buildings in refugee camps, now this practice will be extended to Palestinian cities, starting with Hebron.
"We will take measures that have not been taken before: we intend to apply the successful offensive model that we used in refugee camps, which are, in fact, strongholds of terror, to this area in Hebron, where the terrorists came from. We will evacuate residents, search house by house, seize weapons and destroy all terrorist infrastructure. At the same time, we will impose a blockade of the cities of Hebron and Halhul. We will consider extending this model to other cities," he pointed out.

title: Memoirs of East Turkestan Republic’s First Leader Published in France
body: A French edition of Turkiston Qayg‘usi ( The Sorrow of Turkestan ), written by Alihan Tora Saghuni, an Uzbek religious leader who headed the East Turkestan Republic established in 1944 in what is now China’s Xinjiang region, has been published in France under the title Amer Turkestan ( Bitter Turkestan ). The 448-page volume, published by Bleu Autour on October 23, brings the memoirs of a leading figure in the region’s independence movement to French readers. The book examines the political upheavals of the 20th century through Saghuni’s experiences of persecution by Soviet and Chinese authorities and his involvement in the East Turkestan independence movement. Combining history and memoir, the work reflects the author’s personal experiences and political views. The French edition also includes writings in which Saghuni recounts his leadership of the East Turkestan Republic between 1944 and 1946. The translation was prepared by French historian and Orientalist Stéphane A. Dudoignon, a senior researcher at France’s National Center for Scientific Research (CNRS). From 2024 to 2026, he worked on the book with Saghuni’s son, Qutlughkhan. The edition includes scholarly commentary to help readers understand the historical events and political context of the narrative. Alihan Tora Saghuni was born in 1885 in Tokmok, in present-day Kyrgyzstan, to a family of Uzbek origin. His pen name is associated with the ancient city of Balasagun, one of the centers of the medieval Karakhanid state. After receiving a religious education, he became involved in the social and political life of Turkestan and later moved to China’s Xinjiang region. In November 1944, amid an uprising against Chinese authorities, the East Turkestan Republic was proclaimed in the city of Ghulja, also known as Yining. Saghuni became head of its provisional government. The republic existed amid a complex struggle involving local nationalist movements, Chinese authorities, and the Soviet Union, which exercised considerable influence over events in the region. The name East Turkestan remains politically sensitive in China, where authorities associate it with separatist movements seeking independence for Xinjiang. Beijing rejects the term as a designation for the region, which has been under Chinese Communist rule since 1949. In a 2019 government white paper , Beijing declared that “there has never been any state known as ‘East Turkistan,'” despite the establishment of short-lived republics of that name in 1933 and 1944. In 1946, Saghuni was forcibly taken to the Soviet Union. He spent the remainder of his life in Tashkent, where he worked on historical and religious writings. He died in 1976. The Sorrow of Turkestan became one of his best-known works on the region’s history and fate. Dudoignon presented the book at the Rendez-Vous de l’Histoire festival near Blois, France, on October 9. According to Uzbekistan’s UzA news agency, an English translation is planned as the next step. The work has previously appeared in other languages, including Turkish. According to Dudoignon’s research institute , the French edition is the first translation of Saghuni’s writings into a Western European language.

title: 270 Ukrainians return home in prisoner exchange
body:
As reported by Ukrinform, President Volodymyr Zelensky announced this on Facebook .
“270 of our people are home. A very important result. National Guard members, including Azov warriors, border guards, warriors of the Territorial Defense Forces, the Navy, the Land Forces, the Airborne Assault Forces, and the State Special Transport Service, as well as nine civilians, are returning home. Most of them had been in captivity since 2022,” Zelensky said.
According to him, most of those released are soldiers who defended Ukraine in Mariupol. Defenders from the Donetsk, Luhansk, Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia, Kherson, Kyiv, Mykolaiv and Chernihiv fronts are also returning home. Many were illegally convicted in Russia. Among those returning are five people who had been considered killed in the Russian terrorist attack at the Olenivka detention facility in July 2022.
“We remember one and all and continue searching for everyone. I thank everyone who works to make these exchanges possible. And, of course, I am grateful to our warriors who are replenishing Ukraine’s prisoner exchange fund on the front so that we can bring our people home. Glory to Ukraine!” Zelensky emphasized.
As reported, on August 24, 10 Ukrainian servicemen returned to Ukraine from Russian captivity via Belarus as part of a special stage of the exchange. On August 19, 103 Ukrainian servicemen were released from Russian captivity. In August, Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said that a total of 9,716 Ukrainians had returned home from Russian captivity since February 24, 2022.

title: New South Darfur mobilization committee pledges support for Sudan Army
body: The Higher Committee for Mobilization and Popular Resistance in South Darfur State has formally assumed its duties, pledging to strengthen support for the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF)and the “Battle for Dignity,” which it describes as a campaign to defeat the rebellion and protect civilians. The handover ceremony was attended by government and military leaders, as well as prominent community figures from the state. Speaking to Radio Tamazuj, South Darfur State Governor Bashir Mursal said the committee was committed to uniting public and official efforts and mobilizing all available resources and capabilities in support of the armed forces. “The committee will stand behind the military in the decisive battle to rid the country of rebel militias,” he stated. “We will continue fighting without retreat, even if it means sacrificing millions of martyrs to uphold their cause.” Meanwhile, Lieutenant Colonel Yassir Adam Mohammed, head of the Higher Mobilization Committee, reaffirmed their commitment to advancing the “Battle for Dignity,” saying it would continue the struggle from where others had left off. “The committee has outlined its work plan for the coming phase, focusing on organizing public mobilization, establishing communication channels with different sectors and local communities, directing logistical and community support towards frontline positions, and strengthening security and military coordination to consolidate stability and reassure residents,” he said. The committee called on the people of South Darfur to thwart attempts by those spreading rumors and discord, and to rally behind the armed forces and other regular security forces. “The determination of the Sudanese people and their armed forces would remain the strongest guarantee of protecting national sovereignty and the country’s unity,” the committee said. The post New South Darfur mobilization committee pledges support for Sudan Army appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: 443 Drones Downed: Russian Airfield, Chemical Plant and Tax Data Center Targeted in Overnight Attacks
body:
Ukrainian Drones targeted infrastructure facilities across several Russian regions overnight on Oct. 22-23, with fires reported near the Baltimor military airfield in Voronezh.
Russian officials reported damage to residential buildings and industrial infrastructure, while authorities in Gorodets introduced restrictions following the reported damage to the data center.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
A fire broke out near the Baltimor military airfield in Voronezh following the overnight attack, according to an analysis by the Russian outlet Astra .
An OSINT analyst examined footage provided by eyewitnesses and determined that the fire had occurred in the vicinity of the airfield, with flames and smoke visible.
Voronezh Region Governor Alexander Gusev said dry grass had caught fire due to falling debris.
“Air defense forces on duty detected and destroyed several jet-powered aerial targets in the sky over Voronezh. According to preliminary data, there are no casualties. The fall of debris from the intercepted targets ignited dry grass in the suburbs; the fire has since been extinguished,” he wrote on his Telegram channel.
He added that outbuildings in a garden cooperative (SNT) and several passenger cars sustained damage.
Gusev had earlier warned of a potential missile threat in the region. In the early hours of Oct. 23, he also reported that drone debris had damaged the facade of an apartment building and a passenger car in Voronezh.
Meanwhile, the Ukrainian Telegram channel Exilenova+ reported that, according to preliminary information, the former Voronezh Military Aviation Engineering University and an adjacent military aircraft parking area had been
The university specialized in training military aviation engineers, technicians, and aircraft maintenance specialists. In 2012, it was incorporated into the Zhukovsky and Gagarin Air Force Academy.
“The extent of the damage and potential losses of aviation equipment are currently unknown. We are awaiting confirmation of the results,” the report stated.
According to open-source data, the 47th Guards Bomber Aviation Regiment is stationed at the Baltimor airfield. Since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine on Feb. 24, 2022, the Russian Aerospace Forces have regularly used the airfield to launch airstrikes against Ukrainian territory.
A fire near the Baltimor airfield was previously reported on Sept. 2. Before that, the airfield had been targeted in an attack on May 27.
Monitoring channels reported that the Azot plant in the city of Berezniki, Perm Krai, had been struck. The facility is owned by Uralchem, a company belonging to billionaire Dmitry Mazepin.
Both Astra and Exilenova+ confirmed the reported strike through its own analysis. According to the outlet’s OSINT assessment, smoke was rising from the plant’s premises.
The facility is located nearly 2,000 kilometers (1,243 miles) from the Ukrainian border.
Perm Krai Governor Dmitry Makhonin said on Telegram that air defense forces and mobile fire groups had repelled a drone attack on Friday.
“Twenty drones were shot down in the skies over Perm Krai. Emergency services are working at the sites where the debris fell... An industrial facility sustained minor damage. There are no casualties. Emergency services are on-site,” he wrote.
Makhonin did not identify the industrial facility that had been damaged. He added that the response to the attack had also resulted in minor damage to the windows of two apartments in residential buildings in Berezniki and Solikamsk.
The Azot plant manufactures various chemical products, including nitric acid, ammonium nitrate, and potassium nitrate, which are used, among other things, in the production of gunpowder and explosives .
It is also the only plant in Russia that produces sodium nitrate and crystalline sodium nitrite. Azot was previously targeted in an attack on Sept. 11.
In the city of Gorodets in Nizhny Novgorod region, Ukrainian channels and Astra’s OSINT analysis reported damage to a data center belonging to Russia’s Federal Tax Service.
The facility serves as a backup data center for the tax authority and has been operating since 2015. It was officially opened on Dec. 7, 2015, in a ceremony attended by then-Prime Minister Dmitry Medvedev, Finance Minister Anton Siluanov, and Mikhail Mishustin, who headed the Federal Tax Service at the time and is now Russia’s prime minister.
United Russia, the country’s ruling party, said at the time that the Gorodets facility was part of a three-center system designated as Data Center No. 1. The system also includes the Federal Data Center in Dubna, Moscow region, and Data Center No. 2 in the settlement of Yerzovka in the Volgograd region.
The facilities were designed to back one another up in the event of a failure, helping ensure the “continuity of service provision.”
“Data Center No. 2 provides partial replication of the most critical services in the event of an emergency,” United Russia added.
The centers can store not only tax information but also data from the Unified State Register of Legal Entities (EGRUL), population records – including civil registry (ZAGS) data – cadastral records, and other information.
Municipal authorities in Gorodets and the surrounding district introduced several restrictions following the attack, according to the news outlet NN.ru.
Schools and colleges switched to remote learning, public events were canceled, and traffic across the dam of the Gorky Reservoir was suspended.
Regional Governor Gleb Nikitin acknowledged damage following a drone attack, including damage to “one piece of infrastructure.” He also said three people had been injured “as a result of falling debris.”
Following the reported attack on the Gorodets data center, Mikhail Klimarev, executive director of the Internet Protection Society, suggested on the radio station Echo of Moscow that the consequences could “collapse the entire tax system” and create serious problems for many Russians, who might have to prove their ownership of apartments and land plots.
On the morning of Oct. 23, Russia’s Defense Ministry reported that air defenses had shot down 443 drones over the country. Nizhny Novgorod region and Perm Krai were among the regions listed as having been targeted.
The Ukrainian side has not yet commented on any involvement in the reported attacks.
Julia is a Deputy Head of News and correspondent for Kyiv Post who has previously worked as a parliamentary editor, journalist, and news editor. She has specialized in covering the work of the Ukrainian parliament, government, and law enforcement agencies.

title: Ebola Patient In Nigeria Is Swiss, Had Not Visited DRC, Says Swiss Foreign Ministry
body: The Ebola patient in Nigeria is a Swiss woman and the wife of a staff member at Switzerland’s embassy in Abuja, Bern said Friday. The couple had recently travelled together to Uganda, but neither of them had visited the Democratic Republic of Congo, the epicentre of the current outbreak, the Swiss foreign ministry said. On Tuesday, Nigeria announced its first recorded Ebola case, saying it was a woman who arrived in Abuja on a flight from Uganda. A total of 44 contacts have been identified. On Wednesday, the authorities confirmed that the patient had the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, which is driving the outbreak in the DRC and for which there are currently no specific vaccines or treatments. Switzerland’s foreign ministry said Friday she was “the wife of a Swiss member of staff” at Bern’s embassy in the Nigerian capital Abuja. “The Swiss woman, who is symptomatic, has been hospitalised for about a week at a private clinic in Abuja,” it said in a statement. “The infection may have occurred during a trip to Uganda approximately two weeks ago,” the Swiss authorities added. “Her husband is in isolation; he has shown no symptoms. He accompanied his wife on the trip, during which she is believed to have contracted the Ebola virus,” it said. “Neither individual travelled” to the DRC, it added. The ministry said that the 25 other embassy staff members — eight Swiss nationals and 17 local employees — “are also doing well”. Following consultations with the Nigerian health ministry and the World Health Organization (WHO), they do not need to go into isolation, the statement said. Bern is considering the “potential repatriation of the patient” to Switzerland, it added. Following the DRC, Uganda and Kenya, Nigeria has become the fourth African country to be affected by the Bundibugyo outbreak. After flaring up in the northeastern DRC in May, the deadly viral haemorrhagic fever spread into neighbouring Uganda, where 20 confirmed cases, including two deaths, were recorded before the outbreak there was officially over in August. To date, the epidemic has surpassed 9,700 confirmed cases, including 4,690 deaths, according to WHO figures as of October 20. AFP The post Ebola Patient In Nigeria Is Swiss, Had Not Visited DRC, Says Swiss Foreign Ministry appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Hundreds of taxi drivers stage protest in Helsinki
body:
Taxi drivers say fares have been falling for years, while rising operating costs leave them struggling to earn enough to make a living.
More than 100 taxi drivers working through ride-hailing platforms Uber and Bolt gathered at Helsinki’s Olympic Stadium on Thursday to protest against rising operating costs and low fares.
The drivers say high fuel prices combined with cheap rides are making it increasingly difficult to earn a living.
"When the price of diesel has been as high as 2.50 euros per liter and some rides are offered at very low prices, the compensation drivers receive may not even cover the cost of the trip," said Mahmoud Kappa , one of the protest organisers.
The protestors called on Uber and Bolt to raise fares by at least 15 percent and reduce their commissions to a maximum of 15 percent of each fare.
They also called for greater pricing transparency, fairer fares for airport journeys and during peak hours, and the freedom to accept or reject rides without facing consequences.
Suleman Rafaqat , who has lived in Finland for two years, said the current pricing system made it difficult for drivers to make a living.
"Sometimes, working days can stretch from morning until night, and earnings can be close to zero," Rafqat said.
Yle contacted Uber and Bolt representatives for comment, but neither had responded to interview requests by Thursday afternoon.

title: Greece’s New Frigate Kimon Opens to Public in Thessaloniki
body: Greece’s newest warship, the frigate Kimon , arrived at the port of Thessaloniki on Friday, October 23, ahead of public visits marking Ochi Day, the national anniversary commemorated on October 28. The French-built Belharra-class frigate will welcome visitors from Saturday, October 24, until Tuesday, October 27, giving the public an opportunity to see one of the centrepieces of Greece’s ongoing naval modernisation programme. Ochi Day commemorates Greece’s rejection of an Italian ultimatum on October 28, 1940, a defining moment that led to the country’s entry into the Second World War. Visiting Hours for the Frigate Kimon The frigate will be open to the public at the port of Thessaloniki during the following hours: Saturday, October 24: 10 am to 6 pm Sunday, October 25: 10 am to 5 pm Monday, October 26: Noon to 5 pm Tuesday, October 27: Noon to 5 pm Dedicated visits for school groups are scheduled from 10 am to noon on Monday and Tuesday. Access will be provided through the facilities of the Thessaloniki Port Authority. Inside Greece’s New Belharra-Class Frigate Measuring 121.6 metres in length and displacing approximately 4,600 tonnes, the Kimon is the first of four French-built Belharra-class frigates acquired by the Hellenic Navy. The warship is equipped with advanced systems designed to strengthen Greece’s air defence, anti-surface warfare and anti-submarine capabilities. Its weapons include Aster 30 surface-to-air missiles, Exocet anti-ship missiles and MU90 anti-submarine torpedoes. The frigates form part of a wider effort to upgrade Greece’s naval capabilities amid evolving security challenges in the Eastern Mediterranean and the Aegean Sea. The original contract for the first three frigates was valued at approximately €3.05 billion, including weapons systems and technical support. The arrival of the Kimon in Thessaloniki for the Ochi Day commemorations offers the public a closer look at a new generation of Greek naval power as the country prepares to mark one of the most significant dates in its modern history. title: Kazakh Women Share Stories of Sexual Violence Under #IAmJaneDoe Hashtag
body: Women in Kazakhstan have joined the international #IAmJaneDoe social media campaign, sharing accounts of sexual violence they experienced as children and teenagers. The posts include allegations of abuse by relatives, acquaintances, and strangers. Many participants say they remained silent because they feared being judged and did not trust law enforcement authorities. Denis Dzhivaga, director of the Kazakhstan International Bureau for Human Rights and Rule of Law, told The Times of Central Asia why speaking out publicly sometimes becomes the only way for survivors to draw attention to their experiences, despite tougher legislation. How #IAmJaneDoe Began The international #IAmJaneDoe campaign emerged amid a case involving a former student at Cornell University in the United States. In September 2026, a woman identified in court documents by the pseudonym Jane Doe filed a civil lawsuit against seven former members of the Chi Phi fraternity, the university, and other defendants. According to the plaintiff, she was subjected to a gang sexual assault in October 2024. The initial investigation ended without criminal charges being filed. After the lawsuit was brought, prosecutors reopened the investigation, and New York Governor Kathy Hochul appointed state Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor. No criminal charges have been filed, and the seven men deny wrongdoing. Women in different countries began posting under #IAmJaneDoe in an effort to frustrate attempts to reveal the plaintiff’s identity. Through these posts, they express solidarity with the plaintiff and share their own experiences of violence. In Kazakhstan, the campaign has brought attention to the silence surrounding sexual abuse within families. In their accounts, women describe incidents dating back many years, including alleged crimes committed by fathers, stepfathers, and brothers. Dzhivaga believes that the decision to share such experiences publicly is often linked to a lack of effective support. “From families that try to cover up cases of abuse to police officers who still prefer not to interfere in family matters, everything pushes women to at least tell their stories publicly. Quite often, women simply have no other options,” he said. However, speaking out does not guarantee sympathy. According to the human rights advocate, women who share their experiences face blame and condemnation, including from other women. What Has Changed Under the ‘Saltanat Law’? In June 2024, amendments informally known as the “Saltanat Law” came into force in Kazakhstan. They were adopted following the murder of Saltanat Nukenova, a case that sparked widespread public outrage. Former Minister of National Economy Kuandyk Bishimbayev was sentenced to 24 years in prison for her murder. The amendments reinstated criminal penalties for battery and intentional infliction of minor bodily harm, strengthened protections for women and children, and expanded measures aimed at preventing violence. However, Dzhivaga argues that the legislative changes have not yet produced comparable improvements in how government agencies respond. “When everyone was celebrating the adoption of the law, I said that passing a law is only half the battle. What matters is how it is enforced. The law has to work, but in many respects, the response has remained the same. Essentially, the system has not changed yet,” the human rights advocate explained. One continuing obstacle is the concept of uyat , or shame, deeply rooted in Kazakh society and associated with violating accepted social norms and damaging a family’s reputation. In cases of sexual violence, fear of public disgrace can pressure survivors into silence, especially when the alleged perpetrator is a close relative. “Raping, killing, and torturing someone is not considered uyat, but speaking out about it is. And the police often continue to take a wait-and-see approach,” Dzhivaga said. He believes police should respond more actively to public accounts of violence and assess whether they warrant legal action. Kazakhstan’s Interior Ministry told Tengri Life on October 14 that social media posts can provide grounds for a criminal investigation if they contain sufficient evidence of a possible offense. The ministry said such accounts are assessed according to the details provided and whether the people involved can be identified. Human Rights Concerns and the Government’s Response On October 6, the United Nations Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women reviewed the situation of women in Kazakhstan. Experts acknowledged legislative changes but drew attention to persistent obstacles preventing survivors from obtaining protection. One issue is the absence of a separate criminal offense specifically covering domestic violence. Kazakh authorities said they intend to address this gap in the law. Human Rights Watch also called for better enforcement of protection orders and timely assistance for women who seek help from the police. Kazakhstan’s representatives told the UN committee that reported cases of domestic violence had declined by 24% in the first half of 2026. According to the figures they presented, the number of killings declined by 20%. These statistics reflect officially recorded cases and do not, on their own, indicate the extent of violence that remains unreported to law enforcement authorities. Dzhivaga acknowledges that the government has become more open to discussing the problem but points to a shortage of temporary accommodation for survivors and rehabilitation programs. “There are very few centers and shelters where victims of violence can turn for help and find at least temporary accommodation. A shortage of shelters and rehabilitation services has been documented across Kazakhstan,” he said. In Dzhivaga’s view, overcoming the social stigma faced by survivors is just as important as improving legislation. The accounts shared under #IAmJaneDoe illustrate how many stories of violence can remain untold for years, even after new legal protections have been introduced.

title: AG recommends prosecution of NDC’s Ashie Moore for alleged theft of a Singaporean businessman’s property
body: The Office of the Attorney-General has recommended that the Greater Accra Regional Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Emmanuel Nii Ashie-Moore, be charged with stealing, following allegations that he removed a Singaporean businessman’s luggage and personal belongings while the businessman was in police custody. A document cited by Myjoyonline in connection with the case indicates that the Attorney-General’s Office considers the evidence gathered sufficient to support a charge against Mr Ashie-Moore under Section 124 of the Criminal Offences Act, 1960 (Act 29). The document refers to an investigation docket containing witness statements, CCTV footage from Fiesta Residences and a cybercrime analysis report. It identifies Mr Ashie-Moore as the first suspect and says the evidence suggests that he removed the complainant’s belongings from the hotel while the businessman was in police custody. “Upon careful review of the entire docket, including the statements of the complainant, the 1st suspect, investigating officers, the CCTV footage from Fiesta Residences, and its accompanying cybercrime analysis report, it is my considered view that there is sufficient evidence to support a charge of stealing against the 1st suspect, Emmanuel Nii Ashie-Moore,” the document states. According to the document, the CCTV footage corroborates the alleged removal of the luggage by Mr Ashie-Moore and other unidentified persons. It also raises questions about how Mr Ashie-Moore came to possess the complainant’s medication and how the businessman’s passport was deposited at the High Court Registry. The document says these circumstances suggest that Mr Ashie-Moore had control over the complainant’s property and support an inference that the belongings were dishonestly appropriated without lawful justification. It consequently advises investigators to charge him with stealing, obtain a statement from him and forward it to the Attorney-General’s Office for prosecution. “Your Special Investigation Unit (SIU) duplicate case docket with R.O. No.204/2025 is hereby retained for prosecution,” the document adds. The recommendation does not, in itself, amount to a criminal conviction. Background to the US$800,000 ECG contract allegations The case is linked to allegations by Singaporean businessman Toh You Kang, who accused Mr Ashie-Moore of taking US$800,000 in connection with purported contracts with the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) for the supply of electric cables. In a human rights action filed at the High Court in 2025, Mr Kang alleged that he paid the money after Mr Ashie-Moore represented that he could help secure contracts with ECG. Mr Kang also accused the NDC regional chairman of violating his rights, including through his alleged detention and the seizure of his personal belongings. The claims formed part of a wider legal dispute between the two men. Mr Ashie-Moore, through his lawyer, Gideon Tettey Tetteh, denied receiving the US$800,000 and rejected the allegations against him. His legal team instead accused Mr Kang of defrauding Mr Ashie-Moore and his business partners. The allegations remain subject to the relevant legal processes.

title: China’s first aircraft carrier forms ‘evolving pattern’ of voyages in disputed Asian seas
body: NEW TAIPEI CITY, Taiwan— China’s first aircraft carrier, heavily watched around East Asia as an emblem of Beijing’s growing naval power , had made at least six faraway deployments since its completion 14 years ago. It made another in October. So frequent are the Chinese aircraft carrier CNS Liaoning’s publicly visible voyages that military analysts presume that the People’s Liberation Army Navy has fixed a routine that will let the relatively aged carrier help train and equip the fleet’s two more modern ones. Still, the carrier group’s passages not far from Taiwan , Japan and the Philippines – places that have political or maritime sovereignty disputes with China – have raised alerts . “The current voyage by the Liaoning appears to be part of an established evolving pattern of far-seas training deployments,” said Carl Thayer, an Asia specialist and emeritus professor at the University of New South Wales in Australia. “The Liaoning demonstrates China’s naval military capability and political influence through its constant presence in China’s near and far seas,” he said. The aircraft carrier led a naval task group to the western Pacific Ocean on Oct. 14 for training, the Chinese People’s Liberation Army Navy said via China’s official Xinhua News Agency. Citing the navy, Xinhua called the expedition a “drill” and part of an annual routine training plan aimed at “testing and improving combat readiness.” China’s state-controlled Global Times news outlet called the Liaoning’s October voyage its second in the distant seas and hailed the carrier’s long-term progress as going from a “coastal pathfinder” to a “far-sea blade.” The vessel, categorized as a “short take-off but arrested recovery” aircraft carrier, measures about 305 meters (1,000 feet) long and with flight deck width up to 75 meters. As of Oct. 23, the carrier group had done exercises near the southernmost Japanese outlying islands and was headed for the South China Sea near the Philippines, according to local media reports in East Asia. The reports said it went with two large destroyers and a guided-missile destroyer. The deployments are meant to show China’s two more-modern carriers, the CNS Fujian and the CNS Shandong, how to adopt new technology, experts said. The nine-year-old Shandong carrier would learn about “new and emerging” technology as the older Liaoning tests flight operations, sensors and modern aircraft, said Collin Koh, a senior fellow at Nanyang Technological University in Singapore. “The Shandong aircraft carrier is basically an improved version of the Liaoning,” Koh said. He said the current deployment was probably “meant maybe to validate certain technologies.” Being the oldest of China’s three carriers, the Liaoning would “not be the frontline reaction force if there were a contingency”, said Alexander Huang, chairman of the Council of Strategic and Wargaming Studies in Taipei. China’s maritime rivals have taken notice. The Taiwan Ministry of National Defense said in mid-October it was monitoring the possibility of large-scale Chinese military exercises nearby as an outcome of the Liaoning’s movements. China claims self-ruled Taiwan as part of its territory and has not ruled out the use of force to take it. The PLA has stepped up military activity in waters near the island since 2022. In the South China Sea, Beijing has already shored up its sovereignty claims over the past two decades by building artificial islands, often for military use. Brunei, Malaysia, the Philippines and Vietnam dispute parts of the sea with China. In Tokyo, which disputes a group of uninhabited islets with Beijing, the defense ministry said it had seen fighter aircraft taking off and landing from the Liaoning carrier 250 kilometers (155 miles) south of Japan’s Ishigaki Island. The Chinese carrier group launched and recovered aircraft in Japan’s maritime exclusive economic zone during its deployment, said Colin Karotam, senior resident fellow with the Defence Strategy Program at the Australian Strategic Policy Institute. That activity is “uncommon,” Karotam said, though it may have taken place before. The Chinese carrier group’s activities also began shortly before the Keen Sword 27 U.S.–Japan military exercises launched on Oct. 19. The exercises on Ishigaki are biennial and include the Philippines among other nations. China sees the United States, a treaty ally of both Japan and the Philippines, as a military rival in Asia. Xinhua said the Liaoning’s movements in October comply with international law and “are not directed at any specific country or target.”

title: Six arrested after Dubai resident loses years of savings in online shopping scam
body: Dubai Police arrested six suspects in connection with a bank fraud scheme that used a fake online shopping website to gather card details and steal money from victims' accounts. Police said the investigation and arrests followed complaints from victims who noticed sudden deductions from their bank accounts despite not making or authorising the transactions. One victim, identified by her initials SN, said she woke up to text messages about a large sum withdrawn from her account, wiping out savings she had accumulated over several years. Shocked by the unexpected transactions, the woman, who works for a private company, contacted Dubai Police for help. “I wasn’t even using my phone or making any purchases. I was fast asleep while someone unknown was draining money from my account,” she said. The complaints prompted the General Department of Criminal Investigation at Dubai Police to launch an investigation that led to the arrest of a six-member fraud gang known as the "unexpected deduction" gang. The investigation revealed that the suspects had set up a fake online shopping website to obtain victims’ bank card details. They later used this information to make unauthorised purchases and transfer money into digital wallets to receive the stolen funds. Police said the gang also opened bank accounts and digital wallets to move stolen funds. According to the investigation, the gang sold some compromised bank card details to other people for money, allowing further fraudulent transactions. Digital wallets and bank accounts Dubai Police formed a specialised team to investigate the complaints. Through surveillance and investigative efforts, officers identified all six gang members, found where they were living and carried out a co-ordinated raid. During the operation, police recovered bank cards belonging to victims that the gang allegedly intended to sell to other fraudsters, as well as chequebooks believed to have been used to assist their illegal activities. The investigation also found that the suspects had exploited digital wallets provided by a telecoms company to receive proceeds from the alleged fraud. Dubai Police urged residents to be careful when shopping online and to verify website authenticity before entering personal or banking information. The force warned the public against sharing bank card details or other sensitive financial information with untrusted people or organisations. Residents who discover unfamiliar deductions or suspect fraudulent activity should report it promptly through the Dubai Police contact centre on 901, the Police Eye service, or the eCrime service available through the Dubai Police smart application and official website.

title: Behind the scenes at COP17: where thousands of delegates are staying in Armenia
body: How Armenia housed COP17 delegates The sports and concert complex hosts the so-called Green Zone at COP17. Anyone can take part in discussions here, including civil society representatives, scientists and environmental activists. The venue also hosts debates, exhibitions and cultural events. В Ереване начала работу 17-я Конференция сторон Конвенции ООН о биологическом разнообразии (COP17). Делегации со всего мира, в их числе ученые, представители международных организаций, гражданского общества, частного сектора и медиа будут участвовать в мероприятиях в столице Армении до 30 октября. В рамках конференции с 19 октября проходят комплексные дискуссии и переговоры с участием международных партнеров по вопросам сохранения биоразнообразия. Из правительства сообщают, что на COP17 в страну прибыли порядка 15 тысяч зарубежных гостей. Организация столь масштабной международной конференции предполагает не только тщательную подготовку и выполнение намеченной программы, но и координацию вопросов, связанных с безопасностью, транспортом, обслуживанием участников. И, конечно, особым вызовом для небольшой страны было размещение тысяч гостей в комфортабельных условиях. Из министерства окружающей среды сообщили JAMnews, что предложили прибывающим как гостиничные, так и иные места проживания в Ереване и близлежащих поселениях. Armenia sets new tourism record as visitor numbers hit all-time high Restaurant boom in Armenia: business responds to rising demand Armenia temporarily waives visas for citizens of 113 countries A guesthouse whose first guests were European experts This year, Sofia Gabrielyan converted her parents’ house in Nork-Marash, an upscale administrative district of Yerevan, into a five-bedroom guesthouse. Its first guests were two groups of experts from European countries who had come to attend COP17. “They booked our guesthouse back in August, while renovations were still in full swing. I was confident we would finish everything on time and welcome COP17 guests. First, we registered on the system, and our guesthouse passed the required checks. Soon afterwards, conference participants chose it as their accommodation,” Sofia says. Sofia Gabrielyan’s guesthouse She considers it symbolic and significant that her guesthouse opened during the conference and welcomed European experts as its first guests. She believes she has done everything possible to convey the spirit of Armenian culture and create the right atmosphere. “I hope to continue welcoming international visitors in the future. I bought some beautiful carpets with traditional patterns, hand-embroidered curtains and tablecloths. I carefully planned the breakfast menu. I decided to serve linden honey and local fruit, and selected herbs from the mountains for tea.” In the evenings, she plans to play works by renowned Armenian composers, including Khachaturian, Babajanian, Forsh and Akhverdyan, for guests in a specially equipped small gazebo. She has also prepared a short guide in English suggesting things to do in Yerevan and the surrounding area in the evenings and at weekends. “We exchanged emails with our guests. On one of their days off, we offered to take them on a tour in a seven-seater car. We thought we could show them the pagan temple at Garni and the medieval Geghard monastery complex. They were delighted. They probably weren’t expecting such an offer. We want to show them not only our country, but also how hospitable Armenia and its people are,” the guesthouse owner says. As for prices, she offered her first guests a 30% discount. Phenomenon of guesthouses in Armenia: competition not in favor of luxury hotels Guesthouses are significantly cheaper, offer personalized service, and provide foreigners with the opportunity to interact with locals and experience the local cuisine. Yerevan’s major hotels are also hosting conference delegates Best Western Plus Congress Hotel confirmed that it has been hosting COP17 participants since 14 October, with bookings opening three months earlier. Most guests come from Europe and the Middle East. “We have welcomed high-ranking guests from participating countries. Some have come for a few days, while others will stay for two weeks. We are delighted to host conference guests, just as we traditionally welcome all our visitors. “Most of the bookings for this period come from COP17 participants. We are also hosting a group of media representatives. They know the conference venues and entertainment programmes very well. They probably researched the available information thoroughly before their visit. “We met guests at the airport and prepared Armenian wine and sweets for them in their rooms. However, we serve a classic breakfast menu,” the hotel said. How COP17 delegates found accommodation A dedicated team worked to ensure that COP17 participants found suitable accommodation. The organisers reserved hotel rooms at agreed rates for large delegations. They specifically designed this group booking option for delegations of 25 or more participants. Other delegates chose and booked their own accommodation through online platforms for hotels and guesthouses. Although Yerevan hosts the main conference events, the organisers also considered hotels and guesthouses in other regions as alternative options. However, the full picture of how the organisers distributed guests across different accommodation options will only emerge from official figures after the conference ends. COP17 has undoubtedly marked an important moment for Armenia’s engagement with the international environmental agenda. At the same time, the conference has put the country’s infrastructure, tourism industry and service sector to the test. Discussion in the Green Zone Welcoming thousands of international visitors requires coordinated work across multiple organisations. It also gives Armenia an opportunity to strengthen its reputation as a country capable of hosting major international events. “Based on the first few days of COP17 and our experience hosting the European Political Community summit , which took place in Yerevan this May, we can say that Armenia is positioning itself as a country capable of hosting high-level international events to a high standard,” Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said. Another session of the conference in the Blue Zone at the Meridian Expo Centre All delegates have found accommodation and are satisfied with it Ani Hakobyan, spokesperson for the environment minister, told JAMnews: “All COP17 participants have accommodation. Guests are staying in hotels, guesthouses and flats available for short-term rent. We also offered delegations accommodation options in settlements near Yerevan.” According to Hakobyan, the ministry has received no statements, letters or complaints from participants who were unable to find accommodation. She noted that such problems sometimes arise at COP conferences, but no incidents of this kind have occurred in this case. The accommodation team listed available options on official online platforms. Alternatives included hotels, guesthouses and rental properties not only near Yerevan but also in Gyumri, Vanadzor, Dilijan, Tsaghkadzor and Jermuk. There is no precise information yet on whether conference participants took up these offers. Hakobyan also said that international visitors are covering their own accommodation costs.
