title: Zelensky wants no peace, as he is not taking concrete steps toward it — former spokeswoman
body:
MOSCOW, October 23. /TASS/. Ukraine’s Vladimir Zelensky is not seeking to conclude a peace agreement with Russia, as evidenced by his failure to take any concrete steps in that direction, Yulia Mendel, Zelensky’s former spokeswoman, stated.
In particular, she noted on her Telegram channel that if he were genuinely guided by the country’s interests rather than his own, he would have have repealed the 2022 decree prohibiting negotiations with Russian President Vladimir Putin, initiated the necessary legislative changes to hold presidential elections, and resigned, transferring his powers to the parliament speaker.
"If Zelensky truly wanted elections or a viable path toward a settlement, he would take these concrete legal steps rather than endlessly performing the role of the aggrieved wartime leader on international media," she emphasized.

title: Appeal Court Rejects EFCC’s Supreme Court Bid against Aisha Achimugu
body: . Dismisses application for leave to appeal as lacking merit Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt The Court of Appeal sitting in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, yesterday, dealt another significant blow to the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) in its protracted legal battle with prominent businesswoman, Aisha Achimugu, dismissing the commission’s application for leave to challenge an earlier appellate judgment at the Supreme Court. The ruling, delivered yesterday, October 22, 2026, represents another important judicial victory for Achimugu, whose prolonged confrontation with the anti-graft agency has involved investigations, asset seizures, the freezing of corporate and personal bank accounts, and several court proceedings. In dismissing the EFCC application, the appellate court held that the commission had failed to establish sufficient grounds to justify granting the permission sought. Excerpt of the ruling shows that the court declared that the commission’s motion for leave to appeal its earlier judgment to the Supreme Court “lacks merit and accordingly dismissed.” Consequently, the decision leaves undisturbed, for now, the substantive judgment delivered by the same appellate court on July 22, 2026, which discharged an interim order freezing her bank accounts linked to Achimugu and corporate entities associated with her. Besides, it constitutes a fresh procedural setback for the EFCC in its efforts to sustain the restrictions earlier imposed on the businesswoman’s financial operations. The latest development is particularly significant because the earlier Court of Appeal judgment had raised fundamental questions about the manner in which investigating agencies deploy interim freezing orders and the limits of their statutory powers in relation to private individuals and corporate organisations. In that judgment, a three-member panel comprising Justices Muhammad Ibrahim Sirajo, Ishaq Mohammed Sani and Eleojo Enenche unanimously vacated the freezing order initially granted by the Federal High Court in Port Harcourt on April 10, 2025. The court held that allowing an interim ex parte freezing order to remain in force for more than 15 months amounted to an abuse of court process and a subversion of the rule of law. The appellate court reasoned that such orders were intended as temporary measures to preserve disputed funds pending the hearing and determination of substantive applications, rather than indefinite instruments for restricting access to bank accounts. The judgment followed a legal dispute arising from an application by the EFCC before Justice Turaki Adamu of the Federal High Court, Port Harcourt, seeking to freeze the accounts linked to Achimugu and companies associated with her. The application was granted on April 10, 2025, with affected banks directed to prevent outward transactions on the accounts. However, Achimugu subsequently challenged the order, arguing that the continued restrictions constituted an abuse of judicial process. But the dispute took another dimension when the businesswoman raised concerns over the movement of N1.8 billion from a SunTrust Bank account to a Central Bank of Nigeria/EFCC recovery account while the freezing order remained in force. In a ruling delivered on August 27, 2025, Justice Adamu held that the transfer was unlawful and directed its reversal. Dissatisfied with that decision, the EFCC approached the Court of Appeal, questioning, among other issues, the jurisdiction of the trial court to deliver its ruling during the judicial vacation, an alleged denial of fair hearing, and the evaluation of evidence relating to the bank accounts. In its July 22 judgment, the Court of Appeal rejected the commission’s arguments concerning jurisdiction and fair hearing, holding that the delivery of a reserved ruling during judicial vacation did not invalidate the proceedings. The appellate court, however, agreed with the EFCC on the separate issue involving the N1.8 billion transfer, finding that the evidence before the lower court did not sufficiently establish that the money originated from an account covered by the April 10 freezing order. Consequently, it set aside the order directing the reversal of the N1.8 billion, while expressly clarifying that its decision did not validate the legality of the EFCC directive transferring the funds. Notwithstanding that limited finding in favour of the commission, the appellate court discharged the freezing order in its entirety, ruling that the prolonged restriction could no longer be justified as an interim measure. The court’s conclusion was unequivocal: the ex parte order restricting the accounts of Achimugu and the affected corporate entities was discharged and vacated. Hence, yesterday’s refusal to grant the EFCC leave to challenge that judgment at the Supreme Court has now reinforced the Achimugu’s position in the particular dispute over her accounts. Although the refusal of leave does not, by itself, constitute a fresh determination of the underlying financial allegations, it means the commission has failed in the application placed before the Court of Appeal to secure permission for a further challenge. It is believed that for Achimugu, the decision is an important development in a legal battle she has consistently maintained was characterised by excessive enforcement measures and disregard for her constitutional rights The Founder of Oceangate Engineering Oil and Gas Limited and Group Managing Director of Felak Concept Group has repeatedly denied wrongdoing and questioned the commission’s handling of investigations into her business activities. In a public statement in July, she accused the EFCC of subjecting her to intimidation, reputational damage and prolonged disruption of her legitimate business interests. She maintained that investigations and enforcement measures against her had adversely affected substantial investments, business relationships and the operations of companies built over several years. The businesswoman also raised concerns about what she considered a sustained trial by media, insisting that allegations against any individual must be established through proper judicial processes rather than public accusations. The EFCC, on its part, has maintained that its investigations and asset-recovery proceedings fall within its statutory mandate to combat financial crimes and recover proceeds of unlawful activities. The wider dispute has also produced other court decisions, including separate forfeiture proceedings relating to assets linked to Achimugu. On July 16, 2026, an FCT High Court ordered the final forfeiture of assets valued at approximately N8.9 billion, including jewellery, vehicles and cash, following an application by the commission. More recently, on October 12, a Federal High Court in Abuja dismissed a separate N10 billion fundamental rights action brought by Achimugu over the search of her residence and seizure of personal belongings. Those proceedings are distinct from the Port Harcourt bank-account dispute and eere not overturned by yesterday’s ruling. Nevertheless, the latest decision brings renewed attention to the balance between the powers of anti-corruption agencies and the constitutional protections available to citizens and businesses. While the EFCC possesses extensive statutory authority to investigate financial transactions and seek judicial orders for the preservation of suspected proceeds of unlawful activities, the exercise of those powers remains subject to judicial supervision and procedural safeguards. The significance of the July judgment, which yesterday’s decision leaves undisturbed, lies principally in the court’s insistence that an interim order cannot be permitted to operate indefinitely merely because an investigation remains ongoing. That position is especially relevant in a commercial environment where access to banking facilities is essential to the survival of businesses, the discharge of contractual obligations and the preservation of legitimate investments. For Achimugu, the judgment offers a measure of relief in one of the most consequential aspects of her confrontation with the EFCC, even as other legal disputes between the parties remain separate questions for the courts. For the anti-graft agency, the decision underscores the importance of ensuring that investigative measures, however necessary, remain consistent with the requirements of due process and the limits imposed by law. Ultimately, yesterday’s ruling does not determine Achimugu’s innocence or guilt in relation to allegations under investigation. What it establishes is that the EFCC’s latest application to take the earlier appellate judgment to the Supreme Court has failed. And in a dispute that has stretched across several courts and generated considerable public attention, that is a significant legal development for Achimugu.

title: DILG says Bato has 1 week to surrender, offers P50-M reward for arrest
body: MANILA, Philippines – The Department for the Interior and Local Government (DILG) and the Philippine National Police (PNP) set a deadline of one week for International Criminal Court (ICC) suspect Senator Bato dela Rosa to surrender. “Senator Bato mistook my gesture of negotiation as a sign of weakness. Now the gloves have to come off. It is time to bring justice to his victims,” DILG Secretary Juanito Victor “Jonvic” Remulla said in a press conference on Friday, October 23. In the same briefing, Remulla also announced that his department is offering a P50-million reward for those who can help capture Dela Rosa. The interior chief also described Dela Rosa as “armed and dangerous. “We have given him all the courtesy that could be afforded a senator of the Republic of the Philippines, and he has shown nothing but cowardice by going into and remaining in hiding,” Remulla added. The ICC Pre-Trial Chamber I, in November last year, issued a warrant against Dela Rosa due to his role in former president Rodrigo Duterte’s drug war. He was Duterte’s first PNP chief who implemented the anti-drug campaign which human rights organizations said took the lives of nearly 30,000 people. The ICC named him a co-perpetrator in the case . It added that those involved “controlled a structure of power” which enabled them to “direct and control the actions” of those who carried out drug war killings. In November, the warrant was still sealed. It was only made public on May 11 , after Dela Rosa, following months of absence in the upper house, showed up at the Senate to back Alan Peter Cayetano’s election as Senate president. For three days, Dela Rosa hid inside the Senate building until a shooting chaos — allegedly triggered by his mistah Senate sergeant-at-arms Mao Aplasca — ensued on the night of May 13. Hours later, Dela Rosa escaped from the Senate at around 2:30 am with his ally Senator Robin Padilla. Padilla is now facing an obstruction of justice complaint due to the incident, while Aplasca has been dismissed by the Office of the Ombudsman. On Friday, Remulla said there’s already a task force, headed by PNP deputy chief Police Lieutenant General Wilson Joseph Lopez, directed to locate and arrest the senator. The DILG said they are validating reports of Dela Rosa’s sightings in Western Mindanao, Eastern Visayas, Bicol, Metro Manila, and Southern Luzon. “The PNP is always ready for that whether peaceful or armed confrontation… whether with search warrant or arrest warrant. We have the necessary force, personnel, and training for that,” said Nartatez. The Department of Justice announced on May 21 that the PNP and National Bureau of Investigation had been ordered to arrest the senator – but this happened weeks after Dela Rosa’s escape. – Rappler.com Must Read Ronald ‘Bato’ dela Rosa, Rodrigo Duterte’s most loyal soldier

title: Benue government, JED clash over alleged attack on electricity worker
body:
The Benue State Government and Jos Electricity Distribution Plc (JED) have exchanged accusations following an alleged attack on the electricity company’s staff and the invasion of its office in Makurdi.
The government, in a statement issued on Thursday by the Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Solomon Iorpev, rejected JED’s allegation that about 50 persons who invaded its office on Wednesday were Benue youths allegedly acting on the government’s instructions.
JED had said the incident followed a dispute over the connection of the Government House to a refurbished 2MVA 33/11kV transformer supplying the Government House and the State House of Assembly.
The company alleged that the group assaulted staff, abducted 10 personnel, seized four vehicles and took technical equipment. It said the affected personnel and properties were released at about 5:45 p.m. after the transformer was reconnected.
However, the state government described the allegations as unfounded and demanded that the company withdraw its insinuation that it sanctioned violence.
In its response, the government argued that JED’s use of the word “allegedly” showed that it had not established a link between the state and the incident.
It also accused the company of making claims without providing names, identities or other credible evidence to support them.
The government called on security agencies to conduct an impartial and transparent investigation into the allegations of abduction, assault and injuries.
It also rejected JED’s account of a separate incident on 3 September, when the company said its staff were held at the Government House after detecting a metre bypass on the premises.
JED had alleged that its staff were forced to reconnect the bypassed metre before being released.
The company said the matter remained unresolved despite several communications with state government officials.
The government described JED’s reference to the September incident as misleading and challenged the company to publish records of the correspondence it claimed to have had with state officials.
On the dispute over the transformer and metering, the government said such matters should be handled through the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) and, where necessary, the courts.
It also insisted that regulatory requirements and safety standards governing electricity operations must apply equally to JED and its customers, including public institutions.
The government further accused JED of making reckless statements before investigations into the incident had been concluded.
It described the company’s allegations as suspicious but did not provide evidence to support its claim that the statement was an attempt to tarnish the government’s image.
The government demanded the immediate withdrawal of the allegation that it sanctioned violence, a retraction of claims that it engaged in money-bypassing or illegal connections, and a formal apology to the government and the people of Benue State.
It warned that it could pursue legal action if the company continued to disseminate what it described as false information.
JED, in its earlier statement, said the incident had been reported to relevant security agencies and that it would cooperate with investigations to establish what happened and prevent a recurrence.
The company also said technical interventions, including transformer energisation and the handling of metering irregularities, must comply with applicable regulations and safety standards.
Although both parties expressed support for constructive engagement and adherence to regulatory requirements, their statements presented conflicting accounts of the incidents and the alleged involvement of state officials.
As of Thursday, neither statement provided the outcome of a security investigation into the alleged attack or independently established who organised the group that entered JED’s Makurdi office.

title: Ballots cast on election day in B.C. will be counted by hand, Elections BC says
body:
It’s the last full day of campaigning in British Columbia’s election ahead of final voting day Saturday, when most ballots will be counted by hand.
Elections BC has confirmed that votes cast on election day will be tallied manually, in a departure from 2024, when electronic tabulators were used to count paper ballots for the first time in a general election.
That was hailed as a success in Elections BC’s report on the polls, but the agency says in a statement that it’s going back to a manual count due to “short time frames and complex operational logistics of a snap election.”
It says paper ballots cast at advance polling stations and at district electoral offices will be counted with electronic tabulators, and it expects those results to be reported first.
Elections BC also says the election-night count will not include absentee or mail-in ballots, which will be tallied at the final count scheduled for Nov. 6 to Nov. 10.
The B.C. Conservatives held a rally in Surrey on Thursday night, with mayor-elect Doug McCallum endorsing Lorne Doerkson as the province’s next premier.
Also present at the rally were former B.C. premier Christy Clark, and former Surrey mayors Linda Hepner and Dianne Watts
NDP Leader David Eby is wrapping up his campaign in Surrey on Friday, underscoring the city’s importance as an election battleground, with 10 ridings up for grabs.
Advance voting numbers released Thursday were down more than 11 per cent compared to 2024, bucking a two-decade upward trend.
There were more than 891,000 advance votes cast from Friday to Wednesday, representing about 24 per cent of all registered voters.
That compares to more than one million advance votes cast in 2024, when numbers spiked 49 per cent over the previous election.
Elections BC’s report on the 2024 election says electronic tabulation allowed the first preliminary results to be reported within five minutes of polls closing, and 59 per cent of preliminary results to reported within half an hour.
In past elections first results typically started to be reported around 45 minutes after polls closed,” it said.

title: One killed, 16 injured in Russian attack on Chernihiv – regional administration
body:
One person was killed and 16 injured in a Russian attack on Chernihiv on Friday, head of the Chernihiv City Military Administration Dmytro Bryzhynsky said on Facebook.

"One person was killed and another 16 injured in the enemy attack," he wrote.

Earlier, Bryzhynsky reported a strike on a Nova Poshta terminal in the northern part of the city. The facility was damaged and, according to preliminary information, people were trapped under the rubble. At the time of his earlier report, one person had been killed and four injured.

title: Russia’s Medvedev solid on track to semis of 2026 ATP Almaty Open tournament
body:
ALMATY, October 23. /TASS/. Russia’s top-ranked tennis player Daniil Medvedev has reached the semifinals of the 2026 Almaty Open tennis tournament after defeating France’s Terence Atmane on Friday.
The Russian top seed, who is playing under neutral status at the tournament, defeated his unseeded French opponent in straight sets, 6:4, 6:4.
"It is not easy to play against Terence," the official ATP website quoted Medvedev as saying after his match against Atmane.
"Big serve, big shots. I had to stay in the match and found some good passing shots and good winners," the Russian tennis player added.
Medvedev is now set to take on the winner of the quarterfinal match between his compatriot Karen Khachanov (the No. 5 seed) and Kazakhstan’s Alexander Bublik (the No. 3 seed) in the semifinals.
Medvedev, 30, spent sixteen weeks as the world’s No. 1 player in 2022. He is currently ranked No. 6 in the ATP Rankings. He previously won the 2021 US Open and holds 24 ATP titles. He won five of those 24 titles in 2023. Also, in 2021, he won the Davis Cup as well as the ATP Cup while representing the Russian national team.
The 2026 Almaty Open is an ATP 250 tournament held on indoor hard courts from October 19 to 25, with $1.075 million in prize money on offer. Russia’s Daniil Medvedev is the tournament’s reigning champion.
On February 28, 2022, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) issued recommendations to international sports federations to bar athletes from Russia and Belarus from taking part in international tournaments, citing Moscow's special military operation in Ukraine as the reason.
Following the IOC's recommendations in late February 2022, the majority of global sports federations excluded athletes from Russia and Belarus from international sports tournaments.
The International Tennis Federation (ITF) ruled on March 1, 2022, to suspend the membership of the Russian and Belarusian national tennis federations while also scrapping all previously scheduled tennis tournaments in the two countries.
On March 14, 2022, the ITF also reaffirmed its ban on the Russian and Belarusian national tennis teams competing in the 2022 Davis Cup and the 2022 Billie Jean King Cup.

title: Kindergarten shelters reserved exclusively for education participants – Cabinet
body:
The Cabinet of Ministers has regulated the use of civil protection shelters at kindergartens and general secondary education institutions by people other than participants in the educational process.
Under Resolution No. 1288 of October 15, the government amended the procedure for establishing and maintaining the civil protection shelter fund.
In particular, in accordance with the law on preschool education, shelters at preschool institutions are to be used exclusively to protect participants in the educational process.
School shelters are also available exclusively to participants in the educational process while in-person classes are being held, the resolution says.
At the same time, school shelters may be used to accommodate both participants in the educational process and other members of the public only by decision of local executive authorities or local self-government bodies, and in accordance with procedures established by the institution's owner or operator.
If a decision is made to use a school shelter for both students and other members of the public, the operator must ensure that teachers, a psychologist if available, and police or security personnel if available remain with the children throughout the shelter period. It must also separate the areas occupied by students and other people where possible, minimize or eliminate overlapping routes to and from the shelter, provide separate functioning toilets, and make available a separate room or designated area for children with special educational needs to help regulate their emotional state and provide psychological support, as well as psychological, pedagogical and developmental services. The operator must also ensure the safety of all participants in the educational process.

title: Nigeria Wins Bid To Host ITTF Championship In 2028
body: Nigeria has won the right to host the 2028 International Table Tennis Federation (ITTF) Africa Championships. At the African Table Tennis Federation annual general meeting in Morocco, Nigeria secured the 2028 hosting rights with 23 votes, defeating Tunisia, which received 15. The National Sports Commission described the development as another major milestone for Nigerian sports. It said that the hosting rights are a strong vote of confidence in Nigeria’s growing capacity to host major international sporting competitions. “Winning the hosting rights for the 2028 ITTF Table Tennis Championships and the 2027 Africa Para Table Tennis Championships is another major milestone for Nigerian sports,” Director General of the NSC, Bukola Olopade, said on X. “Under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu Renewed Hope mandate, our vision is to reposition Nigeria as a leading sports destination. Through RHINSE, we are deliberately shifting from simply consuming sports to producing sports by hosting major competitions, creating economic opportunities and contributing to national development. “Together with Chairman Mallam Shehu Dikko, we remain committed to building a sports economy that attracts global attention, investment and partnerships.” Olopade assured that Nigeria will deliver a world-class championship that sets a benchmark for future competitions in Africa. “Nigeria is ready to welcome the world,” he added. “The future of Nigerian sports is about creating a sporting economic culture and destination the world comes to.” The selection of host for the continental tournament was fiercely contested by Nigeria and Tunisia. After the votes, Nigeria was supported by the delegates with 23 of the 38 certified voters cast their vote for the West Africa nation ahead of Tunisia who garnered 15 votes to concede the hosting right to Nigeria. Other hosts decided at the AGM include Libya (Cup), Algeria (Championships), Botswana (Youth) and Nigeria (Para) for 2027, while the hosts for the 2028 event include Nigeria (Championships), Rwanda (Youth) and Egypt (Para). The host of the Cup in 2028 is yet to be decided. The President, Nigeria Table Tennis Federation (NTTF), Adesoji Tayo, said the confidence reposed in Nigeria by the delegates was overwhelming, while promising to deliver a world-class tournament in the city of Lagos. “We want to thank all the delegates for putting their trust in Nigeria to host a befitting tournament in 2028 as well as the African Para Championships in 2027,” he said. “As an experienced organiser of major table tennis tournaments in the world, we are poised to deliver a seamless event that continues to attract more people to Nigeria. The city of Lagos will again witness the best of table tennis, and we assure all our visitors that Nigeria will be the place to be in 2028.” The post Nigeria Wins Bid To Host ITTF Championship In 2028 appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Niger revives support for Christian pilgrimage after 10-year suspension
body:
The Niger State Government has begun preparing for the 2026 Christian pilgrimage, more than a decade after it suspended government sponsorship of pilgrimages because of economic challenges.
The preparations were disclosed in a report by Northern News published on Friday, which said the Niger State Pilgrims’ Welfare Board had begun coordinating arrangements for the exercise under Governor Mohammed Umaru Bago.
The board held a strategic meeting involving its members and staff of the Christian Department at its headquarters in Minna to coordinate preparations and improve pilgrims’ welfare.
The meeting was convened by the board’s Executive Secretary, Muhammad Aliyu, who was represented by the Director of Administration, Ado Bello.
Mr Bello said the engagement was intended to strengthen collaboration between board members and staff in organising the pilgrimage in line with the state government’s New Niger Agenda.
He said the Christian and Muslim departments shared responsibility for serving pilgrims, emphasising early planning, accountability, and coordination ahead of the 2026 exercise.
The Christian Department’s Director of Administration, Paul Lawrence, said preparations would include mobilising intending pilgrims across the state’s 25 local government areas and conducting screening in collaboration with relevant agencies.
He said the department also planned to provide orientation and spiritual programmes, improve accommodation and feeding arrangements, and strengthen engagement with the Christian Association of Nigeria and church leaders.
Mr Lawrence said the department would work with the Nigerian Christian Pilgrims Commission to ensure compliance with national guidelines, timely processing of travel documents and coordinated airlifting arrangements.
He added that security agencies and medical screening teams would vet intending pilgrims and ensure they met the required health standards.
“Measures to prevent abscondment and promote discipline throughout the exercise have been put in place,” he said, while appealing to the board’s management to sustain operational and financial support.
The head of the Christian board members, Deborah Salawu, welcomed the preparations and pledged the members’ support for the exercise.
On 17 May 2016, the administration of former Governor Abubakar Sani Bello suspended state sponsorship of both Muslim and Christian pilgrims travelling to Mecca and Jerusalem, citing Nigeria’s economic challenges and the state’s dwindling revenue.
In a statement issued in Minna by his then Chief Press Secretary, Jibrin Ndace, Mr Bello said the government had put the sponsorship of pilgrims to the holy sites on hold with immediate effect.
“Government is committed to supporting our people in fulfilling their religious obligations, but the dwindling economic fortunes of the state, in the face of other equally people-oriented demands, sponsorship of pilgrims to Hajj and Jerusalem is hereby suspended,” the statement said.
The former governor, however, said the state would continue to sponsor officials whose participation was necessary to facilitate pilgrimage arrangements.
The suspension of government sponsorship did not stop individual Muslims from performing Hajj.
Muslim residents continued to register through the Niger State Pilgrims’ Welfare Board and travel to Saudi Arabia using personal funds.
The Bago administration later resumed direct funding for selected Muslim pilgrims. For the 2025 Hajj, the state government reportedly spent ₦3.02 billion to cover the fares and related costs of 357 sponsored pilgrims.
The preparations for the 2026 Christian pilgrimage therefore represent a renewed effort to support Christian pilgrims, following the earlier suspension that affected both religious groups.
However, the report did not state how many Christians the government intends to sponsor in 2026, the budget for the exercise, or whether the state will cover all pilgrimage expenses.

title: Uzbekistan Cotton Harvest Reaches 4.63 Million Tons as Water Losses Persist
body: Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Agriculture says the country had harvested 4.63 million metric tons of raw cotton as of October 22, exceeding its target by 3%. About 76% of the cotton harvested so far was harvested mechanically, reflecting the industry’s shift away from manual labor. A new study, however, highlights another challenge: extensive water losses in the country’s irrigation system. According to the Ministry of Agriculture, nearly 3,000 harvesting machines collected 3.52 million metric tons of cotton. Mechanized harvesting accounted for 98.5% of the crop in the Jizzakh region, 94.2% in the Syrdarya region, and 81.2% in the Tashkent region. In other regions, the figure was as low as 61%. Although the national target has been exceeded, the first picking is continuing on more than 49,000 hectares. Machines have reduced the need for seasonal workers in an industry that depended on large-scale manual labor for decades. Nevertheless, approximately 1.1 million metric tons of cotton was still picked by hand. At an international seminar on October 19–20, the government-linked Center for Economic Research and Reforms presented a study reporting that cotton yields had increased by 71% and grain yields by 48% between 2017 and 2025, while water withdrawals had declined by 22%. Water-saving technologies now cover 2.6 million hectares of agricultural land, according to the study. The same study, however, estimates that approximately 37% of irrigation water is lost during transportation through canals, while nearly half of irrigated farmland is affected by soil salinization. A 2021 World Bank report estimated that agriculture accounts for nearly 90% of the country’s freshwater withdrawals, with cotton the largest user of irrigation water. These losses are particularly significant for Uzbekistan, whose agricultural sector depends on water from the Amu Darya and Syr Darya rivers. Decades of river water diversion for irrigation have been among the main causes of the Aral Sea’s decline. The study also assesses the climate impact of agricultural production, finding that agriculture accounts for 17.5% of the country’s greenhouse gas emissions. Methane, primarily associated with livestock farming, makes up nearly two-thirds of the sector’s emissions. Proposed measures include reducing water losses, restoring pastures, and improving fertilizer efficiency. The pressure on Uzbekistan’s water resources is also expected to increase. In July, the OECD warned that shrinking glaciers, rising temperatures, and growing demand threaten to reduce the country’s water availability in the coming decades.

title: Advocates flag contributions, not costs, of newcomers in Alberta referendum aftermath
body:
A union representative for a beef processing plant south of Calgary is warning of worsening labour shortages if immigration policy proposals that narrowly passed in Alberta’s referendum are enacted.
“These are tough and high turnover jobs with few candidates lining up to fill them,” said Faduma Ahmed, with the United Food and Commercial Workers Local 401 at Cargill’s abattoir in High River, Alta.
With 98 per cent of polls reporting in Monday’s referendum, a slim majority of votes were cast in favour of limiting access to or charging a fee for provincially funded services based on immigration status. Premier Danielle Smith’s government had argued that the cost to provide health care and education to temporary Alberta residents amounts to $1 billion a year and that a surge in newcomers has strained affordability and services.
But critics have warned that the referendum’s outcome could make Alberta less attractive to newcomers at a time when jobs desperately need to be filled.
At the Cargill plant, temporary foreign workers, refugees, permanent residents and citizens from all over the globe work side by side and all pay taxes, said Ahmed. It’s back-breaking work, with staffers often having to hoist whole carcasses.
“When we sit down to eat, we rarely think about the intense and the gruelling labour it takes to get the food onto our tables, right on our plate,” she said, adding that workers have come to her concerned about their ability to pay for health care and school for their children.
“They are foundational to keeping our economy moving, and they are navigating the exact same punishing affordability crisis as every other Albertan.”
Ahmed said the union will draw a “hard line” if the proposals become law.
“We will fight to ensure immigrant workers receive the same services they do today, up to and including making the employers pay at the bargaining table to fund the differences.”
Another sector that relies heavily on immigration is health care for seniors.
“Often we’ll find they’ll work in roles that maybe some Canadians may not be interested in,” said Leah Lechelt, executive director of the Christian Health Association of Alberta, which represents non-profits that employ 22,000 staff across the province.
She said some college programs for health-care aides have closed or reduced their enrolment simply because there haven’t been enough applications domestically.
The workforce hails from around the world, and are mostly health-care aides, but also cleaning and food-service staff, Lechelt said. They deal with vulnerable patients, so regulations largely limit those jobs to permanent residents and citizens.
“It’s really a very attractive role for somebody who is fairly new to Canada and sometimes is working on some English language proficiency skills.”
The association has established an apprenticeship program that enables those in entry-level jobs, like housekeeping, to train on-site to become health-care aides and pursue a better-paying career path.
“And then we can backfill those positions with other newcomers, maybe starting out in their journey in Canada.”
One of the referendum proposals asked whether Albertans would support the province taking more control of immigration from the federal government.
It was an idea the Business Council of Alberta has long advocated, said president Adam Legge.
“There’s a bit of a better on-the-ground intel perspective compared to a centralized decision in Ottawa,” he said.
“Oftentimes there are some skills and geographic mismatches between what Ottawa approves on an immigration basis and what is needed.”
For instance, he said there’s a huge demand for workers in the skilled trades, like heavy-duty mechanics, welders and electricians.
He said he heard from members generally that they don’t want to see anything deter people from choosing to live in Alberta.
Research by University of Calgary economist Trevor Tombe commissioned by the Calgary Chamber of Commerce found immigrants paid an estimated $4.1 billion in Alberta personal income taxes in 2026.
It also found immigrants younger than 40 had a net fiscal contribution of almost $1 billion, after the cost of provincial family programs, workers’ compensation and social assistance are accounted for.

title: Kyrgyzstan Opens Snow Leopard Research and Rehabilitation Center
body: A research and rehabilitation center for snow leopards, named Ak Ilbirs, opened on October 23 in Kyrgyzstan. The facility, located in the village of Ananyevo on the shores of Issyk-Kul, will study snow leopard behavior and support efforts to increase the animals’ numbers. The opening coincided with International Snow Leopard Day. Russia’s Republic of Tatarstan helped establish the center; its leader, Rustam Minnikhanov, attended the ceremony alongside Kyrgyz Prime Minister Adylbek Kasymaliyev. Snow leopards inhabit mountainous regions across 12 Asian countries, including Kyrgyzstan. The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) classifies the species as vulnerable, with their numbers threatened by poaching and dwindling prey, as well as conflicts with local herders. Their elusive behavior and remote habitats also make it particularly difficult to estimate their numbers. Kyrgyzstan plays a prominent role in international snow leopard conservation efforts. In 2023, the snow leopard was recognized as a national symbol of Kyrgyzstan. The following year, at Bishkek’s initiative, the United Nations General Assembly designated October 23 as International Snow Leopard Day. In April 2025, Kyrgyzstan established the Ak Ilbirs ecological corridor in the Issyk-Kul region, covering more than 792,000 hectares. It connects Khan-Tengri Nature Park, the Sarychat-Ertash Nature Reserve, and the Naryn Nature Reserve. Such corridors allow snow leopards to move between mountain habitats, reducing the risk that isolated populations will lose genetic diversity. Kyrgyzstan is also exploring opportunities to develop tourism in areas inhabited by snow leopards. Indian company SUJAN Luxury Hospitality has proposed both wildlife watching and scientific expeditions involving local residents. The proposal, still under discussion, also includes training rangers and developing tourism infrastructure. In 2025, Kyrgyzstan’s nature reserves and national parks received more than 271,000 tourists , an increase of 24% from the previous year. Revenue from visits more than doubled to $431,000. However, snow leopards tend to avoid human activity, meaning that tourism development in their habitats will require careful management of routes and visitor numbers.

title: IDF soldier indicted for firing on Palestinian vehicle, seriously wounding 18-year-old woman
body: An IDF soldier was indicted on Friday morning on suspicion of his involvement in the shooting at a Palestinian vehicle carrying a couple in the West Bank, seriously wounding an 18-year-old woman.Following the lifting of a gag order, it was cleared for publication on Friday morning that Pinchas (Hasi) Shem Tov Ran, 37, from Itamar, who serves as a security coordinator in the Gidonim Ridge area, is the security official arrested on suspicion of involvement in a shooting incident in the village of Aqraba in the West Bank.The Jerusalem District Attorney's Office filed an indictment against him on charges of aggravated assault with intent to cause serious injury and obstruction of justice.The indictment was filed with the Jerusalem District Court by attorney Shai Etzion of the Jerusalem District Attorney's Office. The prosecution also requested that Ran remain in custody until the conclusion of legal proceedings against him.According to the indictment, the incident occurred on September 18, after Ran entered the village of Aqraba, which lies outside his area of responsibility, driving an off-road vehicle and accompanied by a career soldier.Prosecutors allege that military officials had warned Ran several times not to operate outside the boundaries of his assigned area and to adhere to established procedures, particularly the rules of engagement.While in the village, Ran stopped several passersby and checked their identity cards, allegedly without legal authority to do so. He later noticed a vehicle carrying a couple and called on the driver to stop.Prosecutors allege Ran fired at fleeing vehicleAccording to the indictment, the driver feared that he would be subjected to violence after realizing that the individuals were not soldiers and that one of the occupants of the off-road vehicle was masked. He therefore ignored the calls to stop and accelerated.In response, prosecutors allege, Ran drew his weapon and fired at least three shots toward the fleeing vehicle, intending to strike the vehicle and its occupants.Two of the bullets struck the vehicle and the woman sitting in the passenger seat. One bullet penetrated her lung and lodged near her heart. The young woman was evacuated to a hospital in serious condition, underwent surgery to remove the bullets from her body, and required hospitalization for several days.The indictment further alleges that Ran returned to the scene after the shooting and searched for spent bullet casings in an effort to obstruct the legal proceedings. Later, when security officials asked whether he had heard about the incident, he denied knowing about it or having been present at the scene.According to Ran's account, as presented by the Honenu legal aid organization representing him, the shooting occurred after a vehicle without license plates sped toward him and an officer accompanying him in what they perceived as an attempted ramming attack.Ran maintains that the two men feared for their lives and were forced to jump aside. He then fired into the air in an attempt to make the vehicle stop, but it fled into the village.The investigation was conducted jointly by the Israel Police's Judea and Samaria District Central Unit and the Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency).On October 11, two members of the security forces were arrested on suspicion of involvement in the incident, in an operation that also involved Border Police officers and investigators from the Military Police Criminal Investigation Division.During searches, authorities seized the suspects' firearms and a vehicle believed to have been used in the incident. The authorities' statement did not specify what happened to the second suspect.Honenu lauds Ran for military service achievementsThe Honenu organization, whose attorney Nati Rom represents Ran, provided details about the defendant's military service and family background.Ran served in the regular military as a combat soldier in the Paratroopers Brigade's 101st Battalion and has served for years as a reservist in Battalion 697 of Brigade 551, the Fire Arrows Formation.Since the outbreak of the Iron Swords War, he has completed more than 600 days of reserve duty and participated in combat operations in the Gaza Strip and southern Lebanon.According to the organization, he continued volunteering for operational missions even during periods when other members of his team were taking breaks from combat. Among other assignments, he assisted forces from the Golani Brigade and the Border Police's undercover unit in the West Bank.Last month, during Rosh Hashanah, Ran was selected as an outstanding community security coordinator by the commander of the Samaria Brigade. He also received a certificate of appreciation for his service alongside the Border Police's undercover unit in the West Bank.His younger brother, Or Yosef (Orush) Ran, was killed on October 7, 2023, during the battle for Kibbutz Kfar Aza, after fighting terrorists and helping evacuate residents.The family has six sons, all of whom served as combat soldiers. Even after his brother was killed, Pinchas continued serving in the reserves and participating in operational missions.IDF officers, commanders write letters of support for RanSince his arrest, letters of support and recommendation from officers and commanders who served alongside Ran over the years have been submitted to the court.Among those who wrote letters was Maj. Dr. Limon Adam, deputy commander of Battalion 697 and former commander of its support company, who described serving alongside Ran during combat operations in the Gaza Strip and Lebanon."Pinchas exemplifies professionalism, seriousness, personal responsibility, and humanity," he wrote.He added that Ran had fought alongside him throughout the periods of combat and revealed that even when Ran learned of his brother's death in Kfar Aza, he "refused to leave his comrades in the unit."Lt.-Col. (res.) Tzach Eckstein, former commander of Battalion 697, noted in his letter that Ran continued volunteering for repeated rounds of combat in Lebanon and Gaza, even beyond what was required of him, and asked the court to take his military service into account.Maj. (res.) Rotem Shaked Aharon, operations officer of the support company, who has known and commanded Ran for 16 years, emphasized his commitment to the mission and his operational experience.According to Aharon, Ran consistently demonstrated personal responsibility, dedication, and fighting spirit over the years.First Sergeant (res.) Amit Barak, the battalion's mobility officer, also described Ran's willingness to volunteer for operational missions, including alongside the Golani Reconnaissance Unit in Lebanon and Border Police undercover forces in the West Bank.He concluded his letter with the words: "I wish everyone could have Pinchas by their side during a combat incident or any other complex situation. He always acted calmly, responsibly, and with sound judgment."The Israel Police and Shin Bet emphasized that they view incidents of extreme violence with particular severity, especially when they involve unlawful activity and the exceeding of legal authority. They made clear that they would continue working to ensure that those involved are held accountable under the law.

title: Zelenskyy: 270 return to Ukraine from Russian captivity, including 9 civilians
body:
Ukraine has brought back 270 people from Russian captivity, including National Guard servicemen, among them Azov fighters, border guards and members of other components of the Defense Forces, as well as nine civilians, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said.
"270 of our people are home. A very important result. Returning home are National Guard servicemen, including Azov fighters, border guards, territorial defense servicemen, members of the Ukrainian Navy, Ground Forces, Air Assault Forces and the State Special Transport Service, as well as nine civilians. Most of them had been in captivity since 2022," Zelenskyy wrote on Telegram on Friday.
The president said most of those released were servicemen who had defended Ukraine in Mariupol. Also returning home were servicemen from the Donetsk, Luhansk, Kharkiv, Zaporizhia, Kherson, Kyiv, Mykolaiv and Chernihiv sectors.
"Many were illegally sentenced in Russia. Among those returning are five people who had been considered killed in the Russian terrorist attack in Olenivka in July 2022," Zelenskyy said.
As reported, on Wednesday, August 19, 103 Ukrainian servicemen returned from Russian captivity, including 31 who were seriously wounded. Those released included members of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, the State Border Guard Service and the National Guard. They included defenders who had taken part in the defense of Mariupol and fought in the Donetsk, Luhansk, Kharkiv, Zaporizhia, Kherson, Dnipro and Sumy sectors. The youngest serviceman released was born in 2000, while the oldest was 59.
On August 24, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reported the return from Russian captivity of 10 Ukrainian servicemen who had previously been considered missing.

title: Belarus continues to help Russia use signal repeaters during attacks on Ukraine – military spox
body:
Andrii Demchenko, Spokesperson for the State Border Guard Service of Ukraine, said this in a television interview, according to Ukrinform.
“The threat [from Belarus – ed.] certainly remains, but it cannot be said that we have any advance information or, in fact, are detecting preparations for such actions directly near our border. Fortunately, this is not the case. In other words, the enemy – Russia – is not redeploying additional forces to Belarus, if we are talking about infantry groups or units. Belarus itself is also not deploying additional forces directly to our border,” the Spokesperson said.
At the same time, Belarus continues to support Russia by providing territory for signal repeaters to operate.
“So, for the most part, Belarus continues to support Russia through these same repeaters, with the aerial assets launched by Russia at Ukrainian territory receiving signals from Belarusian territory. Lukashenko probably understands the consequences if he sends his units into the war against our country – his units would suffer losses, and therefore he is trying to avoid such steps. Instead, he is ready to help Russia kill Ukrainians in other ways,” Demchenko said.
As reported by Ukrinform, State Border Guard Service spokesperson Andrii Demchenko said that Belarus is closely coordinating with Russia on activating signal repeaters when drones are launched.

title: The money starts as bags of cash in a Moscow market and ends up clean in China, leaked files show
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Russia's state-backed payment firm A7 took in at least 283 tons of cash rubles, worth more than $14 billion, between November 2024 and July 2025, and turned much of it into payments to China that hide where the money came from, the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists (ICIJ) and Russian investigative outlet Proekt reported on 21 October, citing leaked internal records. Cut off from Western banks over its war against Ukraine, Russia now moves money the way drug gangs launder theirs: cash goes in, and clean-looking wire transfers come out abroad. The overlap is literal. Last year, UK investigators found that a network laundering British drug gangs' cash had bought a Kyrgyz bank that was handling payments for Promsvyazbank, Russia's state defense bank. That same bank co-owns A7, which " is also likely to facilitate cash-based money laundering ," anti-money-laundering expert George Voloshin told ICIJ. On 1 October, the US Treasury named A7 a " significant transnational criminal organization ." Most of the market cash pays Chinese suppliers, and China supplies about 90% of the high-priority Western-restricted items Russia imports for its weapons. Drone makers working for the Russian army are among A7's clients, Proekt found in April. From market stalls to a defense bank vault Much of the cash came from Moscow's giant Sadovod market, where broker teams known as "departments" collect bags of rubles from traders, the records show. Vans take the numbered bags to an A7 office, where about 50 cashiers count the money before it is trucked to Promsvyazbank. The bank vaults it and credits A7. At its peak, A7 handled at least 58 tons of cash a month. Russia's central bank has flagged the problem itself. Money of unknown origin comes " primarily " from Moscow's wholesale and retail markets and from illegal crypto exchanges, a senior Central Bank official said in September, as quoted by ICIJ. Sadovod market in Moscow, where broker teams later collected cash for the A7 payment firm, Russia, 19 September 2023. Photo: Nikita Andreev/Wikimedia Commons Clean money for Chinese factories A7 then orders shell companies outside Russia to pay its clients' suppliers, mostly Chinese exporters. The money moves through Kyrgyzstan, largely via the state-owned Trading Company of the Kyrgyz Republic, and the wire transfers carry no trace of cash or of Russia. The records list accounts at ICBC, Bank of China, Agricultural Bank of China, and China Construction Bank. One $287,000 transfer went through Standard Chartered's Hong Kong branch with "Sadovod" recorded as the client. Chinese banks began refusing Russia-linked payments in December 2023 under the threat of US secondary sanctions. Stripping the funds of their origin makes them easier for Chinese banks to accept, illicit-finance expert Zachary Tvarozna told ICIJ. " The only company that sees everything is A7 itself ," Voloshin said. A7, Promsvyazbank, the Chinese banks, and Kyrgyzstan's economy ministry did not answer ICIJ's questions. A7 has publicly rejected the US accusations, saying it runs " a modern, multi-tiered compliance system ." Explore further US Treasury cracks down on Russia-China-Kyrgyzstan payment network, expands sanctions Sanctioned, but still moving A7 launched in late 2024, co-owned by Promsvyazbank and led by Moldovan oligarch Ilan Shor, a " sanctioned and convicted criminal fraudster ," according to the US Treasury. Ukraine sanctioned its network in February, and the UK followed in May. A7 claimed to have moved more than 7.5 trillion rubles, about 13% of Russia's 2025 foreign trade transactions, and its network also helped Iran sell oil and buy weapons, the Treasury said. Sanctions did hit A7's crypto side. Daily volume of its ruble token A7A5 fell 96% from its peak by June 2026, blockchain analytics firm Elliptic found . The cash channel is harder to touch: Western banks can see where A7's money lands, but not where it starts.
