title: Retro gaming is being overrun with AI
body:
Retro video games are everywhere lately — especially in places where they aren’t supposed to be. Halo in a web browser, Wind Waker on the iPhone, Super Smash Bros. in mixed reality. Over the past month or so, these kinds of unexpected projects have gone viral with incredible frequency thanks to new AI tools, as hobbyists take apart games and then rebuild them for new platforms. But while AI has supercharged the pace of these ports, it’s also tearing apart tight-knit communities dedicated to preserving games.
Decomps and recomps — shorthand for decompile and recompile — are a form of reverse engineering that involves breaking a game down to its building blocks and then rebuilding it so it can run on hardware it was never intended for. When done manually, it’s a slow, painstaking process. A group spent years decompiling the original Animal Crossing on the GameCube, for instance. But AI coding tools have cut that timeline down significantly, and the sheer number of ports has grown dramatically in recent months.
This summer, Chris Sotraidis, an AI consultant who works on game ports as a hobby, saw a port of Command & Conquer: Generals Zero Hour — which EA made open source last year — for the iPhone and iPad. The “technical challenges” inspired him to try making a handful of similar ports, including a mobile port of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time using an existing community-built decomp of the game. Within just a few weeks, he was working on a dozen projects. He says that kind of productivity wouldn’t happen without the use of AI.
[Media: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yL_HKL2HLhE]
Some of those ports “would have been possible with minimal AI assistance if I’d had significantly more time,” Sotraidis says. “But I’m honest enough to say that the pace and volume would not have been possible for me without it. It would have been extremely slow by comparison. The tools allow you to move much faster if you know what you want.”
That speed has drawn many people to try out these AI tools, either for fun, the technical challenge, or for preservation reasons. It’s also a reason why there’s been what seems like a deluge of new projects popping up on platforms like Reddit, X, and GitHub. But these ports can be problematic from a preservationist perspective. One of the reasons why decomp projects exist in the first place is that users can pull a game apart and understand how it works, but that kind of understanding and knowledge is lost when AI does the work. Sure, you can put Spider-Man in a Batman game, but you probably won’t discover how certain programming decisions came to be, which can hurt the ability to restore games faithfully.
The rapid pace of AI-driven decomps has overwhelmed the DIY scene. Last week, a community-focused website that tracks decomp projects and provides various resources abruptly shut down due to AI’s impact. “It is now clear that, with the right guidance, human input, and code reviews, AI can expedite the decompilation process in a significant way,” the site’s owner, writing under the pseudonym Encounter, said when announcing the shutdown. “What is also now clear is that the community aspect of decompilation has been broken. Our projects have always been open source to encourage contributions and to benefit the community as a whole. Bad actors have been abusing this in increasingly troublesome ways.”
Those ways include taking existing decompilation projects and “finishing” them with AI, as well as racing to quickly port decomps that the user never actually contributed to in the first place. In essence, one of the big problems is people who are using AI to rush through the process while building on the work of others. This is especially an issue given the community-centric nature of the existing decomp scene. “The bottom line is that these kinds of hostile forks put little to no effort into meaningfully contributing to existing projects, tearing apart our community fabric,” Encounter wrote.
[Media: https://twitter.com/udiWertheimer/status/2106946965657223353]
Given the ongoing challenges with video game preservation, in which it’s estimated that more than 90 percent of classic games are “critically endangered,” the rise of AI in the decomp scene can be seen as something of a double-edged sword. On the one hand, it has created a surge of interest, turning words like decomp and recomp from niche terminology to headline material, while allowing non-programmers the opportunity to experiment and test ideas. On the other hand, the speed and lack of attention to detail in many of these projects run counter to the aims of most preservationists, who try to not only keep games alive for modern audiences but also understand the way they were built. AI is a quick fix that could have long-term drawbacks.
This has created a divide, with those on the preservation side feeling disillusioned by the prevalence of slop, and those on the AI side excited by the possibilities, particularly as the tools continue to evolve. As Sotraidis explains, “I think a lot of what gets dismissed as slop today can improve as the tools get better and people learn to use them well. That doesn’t make the current criticisms invalid. Better tools aren’t automatically going to make people give proper credit or treat each other well. But I do think thoughtful creators and builders will be able to make even more amazing things, faster.”
For those vehemently against the use of AI in ports and decomps of classic games, they might be fighting a losing battle. AI tools seem to be infiltrating every aspect of game development, not just in the realm of hobbyist retro fans. Fortnite developer Epic Games recently launched a vibe-coded version of its PC games store, and it has reportedly shifted to “AI-accelerated development” for an upcoming collaboration with Disney. On X, Epic’s CEO Tim Sweeney wrote that he believes AI tools will lead to “a new golden age of gaming.”
Meanwhile, at least one major name has embraced the decomp scene. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma set up an internal division called Xbox Labs to explore the space and “turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience.” She noted, “While it is hard to predict the future of gaming, it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life, and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators.” (Currently, the only thing the division has teased is an experimental dashboard.)
Xbox embracing decomps is particularly notable at a time when old games are serious business. Some of the biggest releases this year are remakes of Halo: Combat Evolved and Ocarina of Time, while Resident Evil has been rejuvenated in part due to a stream of strong remakes. The question for the future is whether audiences would rather play a lavish remake of Halo or a vibe-coded port that they can take anywhere.

title: Sheikh Theyab holds talks with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi
body: Sheikh Theyab bin Mohamed , deputy chairman of the Presidential Court for Development and Fallen Heroes’ Affairs, held talks on Friday with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi. Sheikh Theyab and Mr Modi explored ways to expand deep-rooted bilateral ties within the framework of the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in place between the nations. The high-level meeting was held on the sidelines of the two-day NDTV World Summit. The two reflected on central themes of the conference, including shifts in the global economy, the role of artificial intelligence and technology in driving development and the importance of building international partnerships to address pressing challenges. The discussions demonstrate the strength of relations between the long-standing allies, which date back to the formation of the Emirates. ذياب بن محمد بن زايد يلتقي ناريندرا مودي، رئيس وزراء جمهورية الهند، على هامش قمة "NDTV" العالمية 2026، حيث ناقش الطرفان أهمية تعزيز الشراكات الدولية لمواكبة المتغيرات العالمية وتحويل التحديات إلى فرص للنمو والازدهار. pic.twitter.com/YlommOsrCo — مكتب أبوظبي الإعلامي (@ADMediaOffice) October 23, 2026 Flourishing friendship On Monday, Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed , Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, met Dr Subrahmanyam Jaishankar , India's Minister of External Affairs, in Mumbai as part of a working visit to the country. Sheikh Abdullah said the UAE-India partnership was continuing to gain momentum, helping to reinforce the countries as vital drivers of global economic growth. The UAE is home to about four million Indian citizens, the largest expatriate community in the country. In May, Mr Modi made an official visit to the Emirates, during which he met President Sheikh Mohamed. Sheikh Mohamed made a working visit to New Delhi in January, where he and Mr Modi pledged to deepen co-operation in sectors including artificial intelligence, the economy and food security, during discussions at the Prime Minister's residence. Mr Modi made a two-day visit to the UAE in 2024, where he addressed a crowd of 40,000 Indians at Zayed Sports City Stadium. He also spoke at the World Governments Summit in Dubai, before inaugurating the first Hindu temple in Abu Dhabi.

title: Ukraine Returns 270 in New POW Exchange
body:
Ukraine has brought home 270 people in a prisoner exchange with Russia, including military personnel and nine civilians, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Friday, Oct. 23.
Most of those released had been held in Russian captivity since 2022. Among them were five Ukrainian prisoners of war who survived the July 2022 Russian attack on the Olenivka prison.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“270 of our people are home. A very important result,” Zelensky wrote on Telegram .
Those released include members of Ukraine’s National Guard, including fighters from the Azov unit, as well as border guards, Territorial Defense members, and personnel from the Navy, Ground Forces, Air Assault Forces, and State Special Transport Service.
According to Zelensky, most of those returning are soldiers who defended the besieged southern port city of Mariupol. Others served in the Donetsk, Luhansk, Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia, Kherson, Kyiv, Mykolaiv, and Chernihiv sectors.
Many of the released Ukrainians had been illegally convicted in Russia, Zelensky said.
Among those returning are five people who were previously believed to have died during Russia’s July 2022 attack on the Olenivka prison, where Ukrainian prisoners of war were held.
According to open-source data, more than 53 Ukrainian defenders were killed and over 130 wounded in the mass killing of Ukrainian prisoners of war at Penal Colony No. 120 in Russian-occupied Olenivka (Donetsk region) on the night of July 29, 2022. Most of the victims were members of the Azov Regiment who had defended the Azovstal steel plant in Mariupol.
“We remember every single person and continue the search for everyone,” Zelensky wrote, thanking those involved in securing the exchanges.
He also thanked Ukrainian troops on the front lines for capturing Russian personnel, which he said helps Ukraine bring its own people home through prisoner exchanges.
Meanwhile, the Ukrainian state project I Want to Find (Khochu Nayti), which provides information about Russian military personnel captured, missing, or killed in Ukraine, reported on Telegram that 270 Russian soldiers had returned to Russia in the exchange.
More than half of those released – 150 people, or 56 percent – had been located by their relatives through the project. It helped their families confirm their captivity, enabling them to secure official prisoner-of-war status for the soldiers in Russia.
According to the project, 40 percent of those exchanged had spent less than a year in captivity, while another 43 percent had been held for one to two years. Only 17 percent had been in captivity for more than two years.
“For comparison: in the August exchange, more than half of the military personnel whom Russia brought back from captivity had spent less than a year there,” the report stated.
Half of those returned were between 35 and 44 years old, while young men aged 19 to 24 accounted for the next-largest group, at 21 percent. The exchange also included 11 prisoners of war aged over 55.
Ahead of the elections, Russian authorities announced they were prepared to include residents of the Russian-occupied parts of Donetsk and Luhansk regions who had been recruited into the Russian Armed Forces on prisoner-exchange lists. Before that announcement, Russia had refused for years to facilitate the return of these prisoners of war.
“As soon as the elections were over, officials predictably tried to ‘forget’ their promises. However, the prisoners of war themselves and their families continued to push for them to be honored,” the project said.
POWs from the so-called “LDNR” (Donetsk and Luhansk People’s Republics) recorded video appeals and repeatedly asked Russia to include them in exchange lists during interviews.
Many had been in captivity since the beginning of the full-scale war. During that time, they had witnessed numerous exchanges in which Moscow brought home service members who had spent only a few months in captivity, the project noted.
Following public pressure, Russian authorities included dozens of Russian Armed Forces personnel from the so-called “LDNR” in Friday’s exchange. Among them were Dmitry Ryabtsev and Sergey Kharitonov, who had been held in captivity for more than four years.
The most recent known return took place on Aug. 24, when Ukraine brought home 10 servicemen via Belarus as a special stage of an exchange previously agreed between the two sides. All 10 had fought in the Donetsk sector and had been listed as missing – two since 2024 and eight since 2025.
Earlier, on Aug. 19, Ukraine and Russia exchanged 103 prisoners each . Those released to Ukraine included members of the Armed Forces, Border Guard Service, and National Guard who had fought in Mariupol and other sectors.
In April, Kyrylo Budanov, head of Ukraine’s Presidential Office, announced preparations for another exchange shortly after Ukraine brought home 182 people in its 72nd prisoner swap.
The group included 175 military personnel and seven civilians, many of whom had been held in captivity since 2022. Among them were defenders of Mariupol and the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant.
At the time, Budanov said a larger group could not be returned immediately because of what he described as bureaucratic delays on the Russian side.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Russian diplomat backs Trump’s mandate to pursue independent policy on Ukraine
body:
MOSCOW, October 23. /TASS/. US President Donald Trump has sufficient authority to pursue an independent policy course on Ukraine, regardless of the internal political situation in his country, Alexander Gusarov, the director of the Russian Foreign Ministry’s North Atlantic Department, said in an interview with the International Affairs Journal.
"We would not confuse the internal political situation in the United States and the president’s push to resolve the Ukraine conflict," the senior Russian diplomat said, commenting on Trump’s ambition to end the Ukraine conflict ahead of next month’s Congressional mid-term election. "The US president has enough foreign policy powers to pursue an independent policy course on that issue," he said.
Moscow has no doubt that Trump is genuinely seeking mutually acceptable parameters for a long-term and sustainable political and diplomatic settlement of the conflict in Ukraine, Gusarov maintained. "And we appreciate the consistent efforts being made by himself and our teams toward this goal," the diplomat continued. "As [Russian] Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov has repeatedly stressed, what we value in the Trump administration is that it has been willing and capable of looking into the root causes of the Ukraine crisis since its tenure in office," he concluded.

title: Wolves enter Finnish villages after Google clears 1300 acres for AI data centers
body:
This is thankfully a less common but still very serious side effect of an AI data center being built nearby.
When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .
Google ’s Finland country manager has apologized for unauthorized forest clearings near Muhos, which have turned 816 acres of forest into an expanse of mud. The American search and AI giant has also been told to cease work where it has cleared roughly 500 acres of forest, 55 miles southeast of the village of Otanmäki. Now The Guardian reports that wolves, who used to live in the forests, are roaming into villages neighboring these man-made muddy wastelands.
Local anger continues to simmer over the damage done to Finnish forests, as Google seems to have ridden roughshod over regulations in the hurry to build new AI data centers in Finland . However, the report suggests that it isn’t just environmentalists who have a beef with Google. Some families say wolves and other wild animals have entered the countryside villages. This would be a serious human safety concern.
“We had wolves coming into the village because all the wild animals moved out of the forest,” explained Anni Ranta, 53, whose family has lived in Otanmäki for generations. Ranta also fears the U.S.-owned data centers will make Finland an even juicier target for Russian aggression.
Finland is far from the first place targeted by AI data center developers to complain about environmental effects . This latest report also cites locals grumbling about construction/factory noise, streams turning brown, and rare birds being pushed out, among other unwanted side effects. We’ve seen similar concerns voiced across the U.S. and in other countries.
Google’s flouting of environmental policy has been unprecedented and clear, a representative of the Finnish Association for Nature Conservation (SLL) indicated to The Guardian. The Finnish Licensing and Supervision Authority (LVV) seems to agree, as it issued an order for Google to stop development near Muhos and Otanmäki. Nevertheless, a Google spokesperson was upbeat. “We will fully comply with LVV’s requests in this matter,” they said. “We look forward to maintaining an active, open dialogue with all authorities to strengthen our partnership with Finland and local organizations.” Google must be hoping the touted business benefits of the data centers will sway the government and/or regulators.
We last reported on these in-development data centers in Finland earlier this month, after the Finnish government (LVV) gave notice to Google to stop its construction activities in Muhos and Kajaani (near Otanmäki).

title: Key rate decisions to depend on inflation — Central Bank
body:
MOSCOW, October 23. /TASS/. The Bank of Russia will make further decisions on the key rate depending on inflation dynamics and expectations, the Central Bank said after the Board meeting.
"The Bank of Russia will make further key rate decisions based on the dynamics of inflation and inflation expectations as well as the analysis of risks posed by domestic and external conditions. The baseline scenario assumes that the key rate will average 12.5-13.5% per annum in 2027," the regulator said.
"Given the monetary policy stance, annual inflation will return to 4.0% in 2027 and stay on target further on," the Central Bank added.

title: Ebola: Nigerian govt urges 15 states to speed up preparedness
body:
The federal government has urged 15 states to speed up preparedness as Nigeria steps up measures to contain the country’s first confirmed imported case of Ebola disease.
The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, made the call on Thursday while briefing the National Economic Council (NEC) on Nigeria’s response to the Ebola case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).
Mr Pate said 21 states had already updated their Ebola response plans, while the remaining 15 states are expected to expedite the establishment of appropriate preparedness and response mechanisms, Voice of Nigeria reports.
The minister identified coordination and governance, detection at points of entry, laboratory testing capacity, logistics for essential medical supplies and personal protective equipment, and effective communication as key components of the national response.
The development comes as the federal government continues to strengthen preparedness following confirmation of an imported Ebola case in Abuja.
At the NEC meeting, Mr Pate said Nigeria is working to operationalise a robust national response system involving federal and state authorities.
The minister said the government had already informed all state governments about the situation, while most states had response plans developed with guidance from the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC).
He said the government is working to ensure that the remaining states strengthened their preparedness.
Mr Pate said the government is coordinating with the World Health Organisation (WHO), Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) and other technical partners.
He also said Nigeria is strengthening its surveillance at points of entry and working to ensure that existing screening capacity, including thermal imaging equipment, was functional.
Speaking later on Thursday at a ministerial press briefing in Abuja, Mr Pate said there are no restrictions on large gatherings for now.
He said there is currently no indication to alter the course of planned large gatherings.
“At this moment there is no indication that requires us to alter the course of large gatherings that have been planned,” he said.
He, however, said the government could review the decision if the situation changed.
“But if the situation changes, we would make a determination, we would consult broadly with the right experts and make that determination,” he said.
Mr Pate said such decisions would be based on scientific evidence and public health considerations.
The minister also disclosed that the confirmed Ebola patient was recovering, with laboratory results showing improvement.
He said he had spoken with the clinicians treating the patient and that there was a possibility she would recover.
“Thankfully, that individual is being taken care of and in fact is recovering. Today I spoke to the clinicians and I understand that lab results are showing great improvement and there is a possibility that she will recover from this,” Mr Pate said.
At the ministerial briefing, Mr Pate urged Nigerians to remain vigilant but said there is no need for panic.
He advised people to follow basic public health measures, including regular hand washing and avoiding unnecessary contact with bodily fluids.
He also urged people experiencing symptoms such as fever, headache and muscle aches, particularly those with a relevant travel history, to isolate themselves and promptly notify public health authorities.
Hospitals have also been directed to prepare isolation beds and strengthen infection prevention and control measures, while private health facilities have been urged to promptly notify public health authorities of suspected cases.

title: One person killed, four injured in strike on Nova Poshta terminal in Chernihiv
body:
One person has been killed and four others injured following an enemy strike on a Nova Poshta terminal in the northern part of Chernihiv, reported Dmytro Bryzhynsky, head of Chernihiv City Military Administration.

"As a result of the attack, one person was killed, and two others sustained injuries, they are being transported to a hospital. Two more victims are receiving emergency medical care," Bryzhynsky wrote on Facebook.

According to him, the target of the attack was a Nova Poshta terminal. The head of the administration later clarified that the facility sustained damage in the strike and that, according to preliminary information, people were trapped under the rubble.

title: Emergency Nurseries Rescue DR Congo’s Ebola Orphans
body: A caregiver wore a protective gown and gloves as she bottle-fed a baby — one of hundreds of children orphaned by the Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ebola outbreak. With the disease still spreading five months into the epidemic, the nursery in the remote east is one of 12 receiving the children of those killed by the highly contagious haemorrhagic fever. “Many children have lost both their father and mother because of Ebola,” Marie Bakikula, a caregiver at a UNICEF-supported nursery in Mongbwalu, told AFP. The mining town in Ituri province near the Uganda border is considered the epicentre of the outbreak. Children account for about one-third of deaths and more than one-quarter of infections in the current crisis — more than 2,000 cases, according to UNICEF. A short distance from the nursery, workers in white protective suits loaded a child-sized coffin into the back of a pickup truck. Others survive but lose their families. Ebola orphans arriving at the emergency nurseries have seen their parents die and burial teams in protective suits come to remove the bodies. Others were separated from their families after their parents, infected with the virus, were transferred to Ebola treatment centres. “They all believe that by coming here they will never see their parents again,” said Monique Ndjangosi, a psychologist at the Mongbwalu nursery. Disinfected Toys A man walks with his adopted child, whose family was affected by the Ebola outbreak in Mongbwalu, north eastern Democratic Republic of Congo on October 10, 2026.(Photo by MARIE RUWET / AFP) Nearby, a young girl and three boys played among stuffed toys recently disinfected with chlorine. Their mothers had tested positive for the virus. The children will remain under observation for 21 days, the disease’s incubation period, in case they develop symptoms. “One of them showed symptoms seven days after arriving and was admitted to the Ebola treatment centre,” said Bakikula, who volunteered to work at the facility after surviving Ebola herself. The only contact many children maintain with their infected parents comes through photographs and videos taken by healthcare workers. “We cannot take them inside the treatment centre to visit their parents. It’s too risky,” Ndjangosi said. Unidentified Children Marie-Therese Tsesi, a 63-year-old nurse, folds clothing at her home with one of her adopted five children orphaned by the Ebola outbreak in Mongbwalu, north eastern Democratic Republic of Congo October 11, 2026.(Photo by MARIE RUWET / AFP) In some cases, child protection teams succeed in locating relatives, even distant family members, who can care for orphaned children. In others, this proves impossible. “We still have children we have not been able to identify because they are too young and their parents arrived in a coma,” said Celine Lusinde, head of provincial child protection services. Her office has registered 8,200 newly orphaned children since the outbreak began. Marie-Therese Tsesi, a 63-year-old nurse, has taken in five Ebola orphans at her modest mud-brick home near Mongbwalu hospital. “Their father was the only parent they had left. He died of Ebola,” she said. “They were sleeping outside and showing signs of malnutrition.” Thousands Killed Kenya Red Cross personnel doff their Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) during a simulation of the evacuation of remains of an Ebola victim in the Kenyan capital Nairobi on October 22, 2026(Photo by TONY KARUMBA / AFP) The current Ebola epidemic, the DRC’s 17th, quickly became the deadliest ever recorded in the central African country and remains uncontrolled despite months of efforts. Cases have also been detected in Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria. The disease, which spreads through contact with bodily fluids and causes severe haemorrhagic fever, has infected 9,704 people and killed 4,687 in the DRC, according to the latest health authority figures, giving it a fatality rate of nearly 50 percent. A clinical trial is under way, but there is currently no approved vaccine or specific treatment for the Bundibugyo strain behind the outbreak. Health authorities continue to face shortages of resources, while insecurity caused by armed groups in Ituri province, the area hardest hit by the epidemic, restricts access to some communities. Many deaths occurring outside health facilities are believed to go unreported. AFP The post Emergency Nurseries Rescue DR Congo’s Ebola Orphans appeared first on Channels Television .

title: UK Telegraph staff face cuts after Axel Springer takeover
body: Staff at Telegraph Media Group received notice on Friday of a round of job cuts just months after the German company Axel Springer took control. The British newspaper publisher was bought out earlier this year on the promise of fresh investment, but after examining the business the newspaper is to start a consultation period. Staff at risk received an email by midday, Telegraph editor Chris Evans and chief executive Carolin Hulshoff Pol said in an email to staff on Friday, which was seen by Bloomberg News. “These are difficult choices that we believe are necessary for the future of the business,” Ms Hulshoff Pol wrote in the memo. It didn’t say how many cuts were being made. The cuts signal a shift for the newspaper group under Axel Springer, which acquired TMG for £575 million ($766 million) in June. In April, it completed the purchase of the publisher of The Daily Telegraph by acquiring a call option held by RedBird IMI in a deal notified to the UK government. RedBird IMI had acquired the Telegraph titles as well as The Spectator magazine in 2023, but a retrospective change in British law forced the consortium to find a new buyer. The deal united two of Europe’s most influential media brands on the right of politics. The buy-out was led by Axel Springer’s billionaire chief executive, Mathias Doepfner. At the time, the German media group, which also owns Business Insider and Politico , pledged to back an investment programme “to grow and expand the business to enable it to become the leading centre-right media outlet in the English-speaking world”. Axel Springer subsequently parachuted in its own top managers to the UK group. Ms Hulshoff Pol, formerly head of the German title Bild , became chief executive, while long-time executive Patrick Wehrmann was appointed as finance chief. Mr Evans will remain in his position. Under the changes, the publication plans to merge the comment and analysis teams, and combine features and lifestyle workers, Mr Evans told staff at a meeting on Friday at which the cuts were announced. “We will look to develop new revenue streams, and we will look to expand into overseas markets,” he said.

title: Commanding the Depths: HAVELSAN’s Technological Approach to Underwater Operations
body: Technological advancements do not alter the fundamental principle underlying the command and control philosophy: “The ability to make the right decision in the shortest possible time.” With the increasing volume and diversity of big data, shrinking decision making timelines and growing cognitive workload on personnel, it has become essential to provide users with new capabilities to perform their duties more effectively and efficiently, and to support their decision making processes. Against this backdrop, HAVELSAN continues to integrate technology into every phase of the command and control cycle for underwater platforms and systems. Sponsored by This article opens a three-part HAVELSAN series on command and control for Naval News. We begin underwater, examining submarine combat systems and the integration of sensors, data and weapons. The next two articles will explore command and control for surface naval operations and autonomous systems. The rapid acceleration of technological development is shaping the Future Operating Environment (FOE), while emerging operational concepts such as Multi-Domain Operations (MDO) and Cross-Domain Command (CDC) are generating new operational requirements. These requirements, in turn, are driving fundamental changes in command and control information systems. Today, “business as usual” is no longer an option. Having embraced the operational concepts driving this transformation and the fundamental changes they entail, HAVELSAN continues to lead the development of information systems supporting command and control at the operational and tactical levels, both for manned submarines and for unmanned underwater platforms and systems. Command and Control of Submarines Combat Management Systems (CMS), whose primary function is to enable submarines to fire torpedoes and guided missiles, continue to evolve through integration with increasingly long-range sensors—particularly sonar—and weapons. They provide target tracking, target motion analysis solutions, weapon engagement and control, and a tactical picture of the surrounding surface and subsurface environment, enabling the detection of more targets at greater ranges. Drawing on nearly two decades of experience in CMS for conventional submarines, HAVELSAN closely follows these developments and continues to contribute to the enhancing of various CMS types, including those developed by HAVELSAN and other manufacturers, such as the integration of the encapsulated ATMACA missile and the AKYA torpedo. In addition, HAVELSAN has intensified its efforts on the ADVENT MÜREN CMS to equip submarines with a range of capabilities reflecting technological advances, foremost among them Network Enabled Capability (NEC). ADVENT MÜREN CMS provides network-centric capabilities to the submarines (Credit: HAVELSAN) On the other hand, however advanced a CMS may be, its definition and scope limit its ability to support many activities throughout a submarine’s mission cycle. Adopting an innovative approach to tactical-level submarine command and control, HAVELSAN integrates the submarine’s command center—the Control Room, which operates 24/7—into the common information architecture of the command-and-control cycle, starting from the port phase. Thus, the Control Room serves as a multi-purpose “Tactical Operations Center” where data required for the submarine’s mission cycle is displayed, evaluated, interpreted, and decision support is provided. This innovative approach, which addresses submarine command and control through “Combat System Integration,” is based on the premise that the entire submarine constitutes a single “Combat System” and aims to ensure holistic command and control of the submarine, starting from its operations in port phase. HAVELSAN’s “Submarine Combat System Integration” goes beyond merely installing monitors or consoles for individual systems within the Control Room. Instead, it creates a physical, functional, and ergonomic environment that maximizes the utility of the data these systems generate, accommodates the growing volume and diversity of information in the Control Room, and enhances the submarine’s operational effectiveness. Combat System Integration in submarines, where space constraints are critical, stands as the culmination of expertise and capabilities in this field. Aiming to meet the full range of command and control requirements for submarine operations, this approach can be applied to both new-construction submarines and comprehensive mid-life modernization programs. HAVELSAN’s holistic command and control approach also underpins the “Compact Mission System” developed for mini, or midget/light submarines, which have substantially smaller crews and more limited physical space than conventional submarines. Command and Control of Unmanned Underwater Vehicles ÇAKA S-KUSV Kamikaze Drone on HAVELSAN stand at IDEF 2023 The use of Unmanned Underwater Vehicles (UUVs) is expanding rapidly, not only in civilian applications such as acoustic and hydrographic data collection and the security of critical underwater infrastructure, but also in military use including mine laying, mine countermeasures, anti-surface warfare and anti-submarine warfare. The use of Unmanned Underwater Vehicles (UUVs) within the framework of concepts such as “Swarm Operations” and “Manned-Unmanned Teaming” introduces new dimensions to their command and control. Beyond the constraints of physical space, the absence of personnel on board UUVs makes a holistic approach to the combat system a necessity rather than an option. Autonomous UUVs must possess artificial intelligence capabilities to generate alternative solutions in response to operational changes and on-platform situations, identify anomalies and relationships between processes, and support decision-making. Recognising the distinctive advantages of UUVs, HAVELSAN has initiated the development of “Compact Mission Systems” that, as with mini submarines, encompass holistic tactical-level command and control of the platform. Compact Mission Systems adopt an integrated command and control approach that treats the entire UUV—including machinery control, steering, navigation and communications systems—as the combat system. Construction of the ÇAKA Hybrid Unmanned Maritime Vehicle and development of the AVISTA ROV are continuing in accordance with this approach. Illustration of HAVELSAN’s AVİSTA ROV (Credit: HAVELSAN) Operational-Level Command and Control of Underwater Platforms In the Future Operating Environment, the rapid increase in the number and diversity of missions of UUVs, alongside submarines, will necessitate a fundamental transformation, particularly in operational level command and control. Critical operation processes at this level include “Waterspace Management (WSM)”, covering the positioning of platforms at the right place and time and the allocation of operating areas for effective weapon employment; “Prevention of Mutual Interference (PMI)” to ensure underwater navigational safety; coordination between platforms within “Support Operations”; and “Communications Management” to transmit mission orders to platforms and manage the data received from them. HAVELSAN has focused on command and control systems capable of mission planning, locationing, and control of large numbers of UUVs, including Extra-Large Autonomous Unmanned Underwater Vehicles (XLUUVs), alongside submarines, and of coordinating their activities with manned platforms, taking into account the underwater environment’s unique physical and stealth constraints and limited communications opportunities. The operational-level command and control system developed by HAVELSAN—designed to enable one or more “Unmanned Underwater Vehicle (UUV) Operations Centers” to manage the centralized and holistic command and control of UUVs—will also evaluate the data and information transmitted by the UUVs. By processing this data, it will also facilitate transmission to relevant units to establish a “Common Operational Picture (COP).” These centers are positioned not merely as platform control points, but as decision, command, and control nodes that serve as the underwater component of the Cross Domain Command (CDC). Protection of Critical Underwater Infrastructure Critical Underwater Infrastructure (CUI) includes underwater energy transmission lines, natural gas and oil pipelines, communications and fibre-optic cables, port and naval base infrastructure, and offshore energy installations. These assets are vital to states’ economic continuity and national security. In the Future Operating Environment (FOE), protecting them requires an integrated approach combining physical security measures, such as barriers and metal nets, with acoustic sensors, unmanned systems and network-centric command and control architectures. Recent attacks targeting CUIs, associated with “Seabed Warfare”, have clearly demonstrated the vulnerability of these assets and the need for continuous surveillance and protection. In CUI Protection, UUVs act as force multipliers in patrol, reconnaissance, surveillance, detection, and identification missions. Protection is also supported by defensive measures that employ weapons at various levels, such as fire-control systems jointly developed by HAVELSAN and ROKETSAN that enable mobile shore-launched AKYA torpedoes. MATRA DEEP combines next-generation software with underwater sensors to deliver reliable detection performance under challenging underwater conditions. (Credit: HAVELSAN) HAVELSAN continues to develop MATRA DEEP, a “Critical Underwater Infrastructure Protection System” requiring an integrated command and control architecture that synchronises acoustic detection, manned and unmanned underwater systems, and network-centric command and control capabilities, while integrating them with the surface, land and air security and defence systems protecting the critical facility. To deliver holistic security, this solution also draws on products and capabilities from HAVELSAN’s land/joint and air portfolios. HAVELSAN Operation Intelligence and Operation Autonomy: Big Data and Decision-Support-Enabled Command and Control The volume of data generated and transmitted by command and control systems at both operational and tactical levels continues to grow day by day. This big data spans a broad spectrum, from the critical infrastructure condition on the seabed to satellite imagery in space. It is not only the volume of data that is increasing; its variety and velocity are also rising. The scale of data generated by sensors, operations centers, and platforms, as well as data exchanged with other platforms, open sources, and command-and-control centers at different levels, underscores the critical need for AI-enabled decision-support systems, especially under time constraints. HAVELSAN has identified the need for an architecture supporting command and control of underwater platforms and systems in the Multi-Domain Operations (MDO) and Cross-Domain Command (CDC) that encompasses all business processes, reduces personnel’s physical and cognitive workload, and transforms available data—often underutilised because of the limits of human perception and comprehension—into actionable decision support. On this basis, HAVELSAN has defined two core capabilities employing optimisation, big data and artificial intelligence. These capabilities are founded on the use of data generated by command and control systems and received through mission networks within a common information structure, the provision of data-driven support throughout every phase of the command and control cycle, and the execution of appropriate activities through automated or autonomous methods under human supervision: Operation Intelligence: The ability to detect relationships, patterns, and anomalies of the data processed by Information Systems with a holistic view of business processes on board and to determine the impact of the obtained results on the “overall operation.” Operation Autonomy: The ability to use operation intelligence for decision support in manned systems and management of the “operation” in unmanned platforms within the assigned mission, commander’s intent and established constraints. HAVELSAN’s data distribution systems are actively used on Turkish submarines. (Credit: HAVELSAN) Operation Intelligence and Operation Autonomy are conceived not as a single closed system replacing existing systems, but as a system-of-systems capability that acquires data from independent constituent systems on an ontology-based foundation. HAVELSAN’s extensive experience gained through development of the SUBSTAR Submarine Data Distribution System provides a significant advantage in this field. Operation Intelligence and Operation Autonomy can be employed flexibly as individual capabilities across operational or higher level command and control systems, the ADVENT MÜREN Combat Management System, Compact Mission Systems for mini subs and UUVs, and other systems such as navigation, communications, and periscopes. Their primary application, however, is to provide holistic decision support covering the entire operation by using data obtained from these systems. Conclusion HAVELSAN is pioneering adaptable, holistic underwater command-and-control systems at the operational and tactical levels that not only display data and information to provide situational awareness but also interpret it to support commanders’ and operators’ decisions, reduce personnel’s physical and cognitive workload, and maximize the use of legacy systems. These systems are designed to adapt to missions and future operational requirements, while the core capabilities developed, such as “Operation Intelligence” and “Operation Autonomy” are employed in other command and control systems. With its vision and experience in holistic command and control, HAVELSAN stands ready to serve as a Combat System Integrator for newly built submarines, foremost among them the National Submarine (MİLDEN), submarines undergoing mid-life modernization, unmanned underwater vehicles, and shore-based underwater systems. – End – The post Commanding the Depths: HAVELSAN’s Technological Approach to Underwater Operations appeared first on Naval News .

title: “I forgive you” – Koku Anyidoho tells Asiedu Nketiah
body: Former Deputy General Secretary of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Samuel Koku Anyidoho, says he has forgiven National Chairman Johnson Asiedu Nketiah, reflecting on their troubled political relationship as a 21-year era at the party’s headquarters draws to a close. In a post on X on Thursday, October 22, Mr Anyidoho recounted how Mr Asiedu Nketiah was elected General Secretary in 2005, replacing the late Dr Nii Armah Josiah Aryeh, and went on to become the party’s longest-serving General Secretary before rising to the chairmanship. Mr Anyidoho, who served as his deputy, recalled that their relationship deteriorated after he challenged his boss for the General Secretary position, despite what he said was an assurance that Mr Asiedu Nketiah would not seek another term. “He knows, and most people know, I contested because he had assured me that he would not contest again. As it is, the rest is history,” he wrote. He also alleged that Mr Asiedu Nketiah unilaterally announced his suspension after the contest, a decision he insists was invalid. Mr Anyidoho maintained that he remains a bona fide member of the NDC. Despite their differences, he said he had chosen to move on and focus on the positive aspects of life rather than dwell on past grievances. “I honestly had no issues whatsoever working with him as his Deputy,” he stated, adding that he was taken aback by the fallout following his decision to contest him. Mr Anyidoho further alleged that he was deliberately provoked in an attempt to make him resign from the party, but said he refused to take the bait. “Ultimately, you wanted me to get angry and say I have resigned from the NDC, but because I was your Deputy and know your modus operandi, I did not fall for your bait,” he wrote. He said a chance meeting with Mr Asiedu Nketiah at Kumasi airport about two months ago offered a reminder that their differences did not erase their shared history. The two exchanged greetings, shook hands, joked and later chatted briefly on the same flight to Accra. “I believe that there is more that unites us than divides us,” he said. Mr Anyidoho also acknowledged Mr Asiedu Nketiah’s contribution to the NDC and Ghanaian politics, while alluding to his reported ambition to become the party’s presidential candidate. “He has certainly written some history politically within the NDC and Ghana. I thank God He did not create me with a petty mind nor petty heart so I say to Johnson Kwadwo Asiedu-Nketiah, Ayekoo,” he wrote. Concluding his message on a note of reconciliation, Mr Anyidoho said he had moved on and wished the NDC National Chairman well as he navigates the next phase of his political career. “I have moved on in life and wish you well as you also move on in life. Shalom,” he added.

title: Ukraine receives 50,000 rounds of ammunition for F-16 cannons from Denmark
body:
Denmark has delivered 50,000 rounds of 20 mm ammunition for the autocannons on Ukraine's F-16 fighter jets, Ukraine's Defense Ministry said on Oct. 23.
First delivered to Ukraine in 2024, the U.S.-made jets have become a key part of the country's defenses against Russian attacks on its rear areas, particularly jet-powered drones.
"Ukrainian pilots are already using them to intercept jet-powered attack drones," the ministry said on social media .
"We are grateful to Denmark for its quick and efficient response to our request for additional ammunition."
In addition to mounting points for various air-to-air and air-to-ground missiles, F-16 fighter jets are equipped with 20 mm M61 Vulcan rotary cannons designed for close-range engagements.
While missiles are often used to shoot down Russian cruise missiles during mass attacks, the cheaper autocannon ammunition is frequently used against Russian jet-powered drones, which are too fast for most Ukrainian interceptor drones to intercept.
On Sept. 30, Bloomberg reported that Kyiv was seeking to procure additional 20 mm rounds for its F-16s, with sources saying an average of 150 rounds was required per interception.
President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Oct. 5 that Ukraine was "scouring munitions for F-16s virtually all over the world." Zelensky also praised the jets as one of the most effective means of countering jet-powered drones.
Denmark, the Netherlands, Belgium, and Norway have collectively supplied Ukraine with around 50 F-16 fighter jets.
Intensive use in defending Ukrainian airspace means the jets require frequent maintenance, which can currently be carried out only by Kyiv's partners.

title: Fiscal policy to contribute to inflation deceleration — Central Bank
body:
MOSCOW, October 23. /TASS/. Announced parameters of the fiscal policy will facilitate inflation slowdown in the midterm, the Bank of Russia said after its Board meeting.
"The Bank of Russia takes into account the announced parameters of fiscal policy. On the medium-term horizon, fiscal policy will help slow down inflation. Changes in the fiscal policy parameters may require an adjustment in the monetary policy pursued," the regulator said.
The Bank of Russia made a decision earlier today to keep the key rate at 14% per annum.

title: Volvo Cars Faces Loss, To Cut 2,500 Jobs Worldwide
body: Shares in Swedish carmaker Volvo Cars plunged Friday after it said US tariffs and strong competition from local brands in China pushed it into a third-quarter loss. The company also said it would cut about 2,500 jobs worldwide. Volvo Cars, controlled by Chinese group Geely, reported revenue of 66.9 billion kronor ($6.7 billion) for the third quarter, down nearly 23 percent from the same period last year. It swung to a net loss of 5.7 billion kronor for the quarter from a net profit of 4.5 billion kronor a year earlier. Around 1000 GMT, Volvo Cars shares were down over 25 percent on the Stockholm stock exchange. “We continue to operate in a very tough environment with strong external challenges: de-globalisation, hypercompetition and climate change,” chief executive Hakan Samuelsson said in a statement. In response, the company announced a new five-billion-kronor savings plan it said would lead to about 2,000 job cuts in Sweden and 500 more globally, “through natural attrition and by targeted exit packages to employees”. The company currently employs some 39,300 people worldwide, including 19,500 in Sweden, it said in an email to AFP. The company, which had bet heavily on electric vehicles, said the removal of consumer incentives for EVs in the United States under President Donald Trump had also hit its margins. In 2024, Volvo Cars dropped a plan to transition to exclusively EV sales by the end of the decade. “We are convinced that we have the right long-term strategy addressing these challenges,” Samuelsson said. “However, in the short term, with severely challenged volumes, we need to reinforce our turnaround plan with additional decisive actions, lowering our break-even point and improving cash flows to make us more resilient.” ‘Intense Competition’ Struggling along with other European auto companies in the face of a difficult global landscape, Volvo Cars last year announced an 18-billion-kronor cost-cutting plan. In May 2025, the group said it would cut 3,000 jobs and two years earlier, 1,300 positions in Sweden were eliminated. Calling the third quarter “very disappointing”, Samuelsson said the company was struggling in particular in the US and Chinese markets. In China, the market for “legacy premium brands is in severe decline due to intense competition from new Chinese alternatives, basically eliminating profitability for legacy premium brands,” the chief executive said. The situation led to a nearly 50 percent drop in revenue in China compared to a year earlier. Meanwhile in the United States, the carmaker was also affected by “continued negative effects from tariffs”. Hampus Engellau, an analyst at Handelsbanken, told AFP that in addition to tough markets, Volvo Cars was also suffering from problems of “its own making”. In particular, Engellau pointed to its failure to increase the “production and sales of its new electric vehicle,” the EX60. The vehicle has been a success in Europe, with more than 50,000 orders, but Volvo Cars is struggling to ramp up production as quickly as planned. Volvo Cars said in September that Samuelsson would resign when his contract ends, with Skoda Auto CEO Klaus Zellmer set to replace him “no later” than October next year. title: Britain is not interested in normalizing relations with Russia — MFA
body:
MOSCOW, October 23. /TASS/. Britain is the leader of the Western world in prolonging the Ukrainian conflict; London is not interested in normalizing relations with Russia, the director of the North Atlantic Department of the Russian Foreign Ministry, Alexander Gusarov, said in an interview with the International Affairs Journal.
"The facts are stubborn, and they speak directly to the opposite, that it is London today that is one of the leaders of the Western collective advocating the escalation and prolongation of the Ukrainian conflict," Gusarov said. "All this convinces us that London at this stage is not interested in normalizing relations. This does not mean that we are forgetting important memorable pages of our history, including the history of the military alliance of our countries in countering fascism and Nazism. We remember the Arctic convoys, but for us the national security of our country is absolutely imperative, and we will never allow any threats to come from Britain or any other country."
Gusarov sees no reason to believe that with the formation of a new government in London there will be at least some progress for the better in bilateral relations.
"This would require London’s decisive break with the foreign policy guidelines that they, London, have been nurturing over the past years," he noted. "In the meantime, there is only one goal, this is inflicting a strategic defeat on Russia, and by someone else, in this case, by Ukrainian hands. London has been working towards this goal for a long time, generating anti-Russian provocations, replicating anti-Russian sanctions, expelling our diplomats, encouraging this, the implementation of the same similar goals of their European allies. At the same time, as we see, the degradation of the socio-economic situation in Britain itself, as well as the consequences of this disastrous line for the level of tension throughout Europe, is not taken into account."
"In this regard, we are forced to be extremely skeptical about the narratives that are periodically voiced by representatives of the British establishment, and, in particular, the Foreign Office, regarding the alleged absence of hostile plans towards Russia," Gusarov said.

title: One Dead, Three Rescued As Building Collapses In Lagos
body: One person has been confirmed dead and three others injured after a building collapsed in the Fadeyi area of Lagos State. The incident occurred on Akinola Street, off Ikorodu Road, on Friday morning. An emergency response team carries out a search-and-rescue operation with an excavator at the scene of a building collapse in Lagos State on October 23, 2026. The Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA) said that while the cause of the collapse has yet to be ascertained, emergency responders are making frantic efforts to ascertain the number of people (on-site workers) trapped beneath the collapsed structure. An emergency response team carries out a search-and-rescue operation with an excavator at the scene of a building collapse in Lagos State on October 23, 2026. LASEMA said emergency responders have begun a coordinated search of the incident scene to ensure the prompt rescue of victims trapped under the collapsed building. title: State Police Has Received Approval Of 24 Houses of Assembly, Met Constitutional Threshold — Gbajabiamila
body: The Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, has met the threshold of two-thirds of the 36 state Houses of Assembly as required by law, the Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill said on Friday. Chairman of the group and Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, disclosed in a statement that the bill has been approved by 24 Houses of Assembly. “The Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill notes with satisfaction that the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, providing for a dual policing system, has been approved by 24 State Houses of Assembly, meeting the constitutional threshold of two-thirds of the 36 states,” it said. “The Working Group commends the State Houses of Assembly for their decisive action on this reform of national importance and appreciates the National Assembly for passing the amendment in both chambers.” Members of the Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill: (L-R) Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun; Gbajabiamila; Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi; and Inspector General of Police, Olatunji Disu, addressing journalists on August 3, 2026. (Photo by Lanre Lasisi/Channels TV) It said that in line with Section 9 of the Constitution, the amendment can now be returned to the National Assembly for transmission to President Bola Tinubu for assent. The approval is expected to give constitutional backing to the policing framework that the working group’s draft National Policing Bill, 2026 is designed to implement. The group stated that while its efforts remain on track, the draft bills are currently undergoing legislative drafting review and validation at the Federal Ministry of Justice and are expected to be returned on or before Friday, October 30, 2026. “Thereafter, the Group will give them final consideration before presenting them to Mr President,” it added. “The Working Group urges all stakeholders to support a smooth transition to a dual policing system that makes Nigerians safer.” The Presidential Working Group on October 19 said it had completed the drafting stage of its assignment and formally submitted the draft National Policing Bill (2026), together with 29 consequential amendment bills, to the Federal Ministry of Justice for legislative drafting review and validation. The justice ministry’s review is aimed at ensuring that the bills conform to legislative drafting standards and conventions and that they do not conflict with existing laws. “The Ministry of Justice is expected to return the validated draft bills to the Working Group on or before Friday, 30th October 2026. The Working Group will then give the validated bills final consideration before presenting them to Mr President, thereby concluding its mandate,” Gbajabiamila had said in a statement. The proposed policing bill seeks to establish the constitutional and legislative framework for a dual policing structure, comprising a Federal Police Service and State Police Services, to improve security at the grassroots. title: AMD looks to AAD 2028 after record R10 billion defence export year
body:
Following a record year in which South African defence exports broke through the R10 billion mark, the South African Aerospace, Maritime and Defence Industries Association (AMD) held its annual general meeting (AGM), held jointly with its associated South African Aerospace Maritime and Defence Export Council (SAAMDEC) at Denel’s Irene Campus just south of Pretoria.
AMD used the opportunity to reflect on the past financial year. While recognising the challenges members faced, it pointed to a number of positives that characterised the preceding year. Export growth, the improved relationship between industry and government that manifested in July’s Defence Industry Lekgotla, and the successful completion of the Africa Aerospace and Defence (AAD) 2026 exhibition were all cited as key examples of progress made, while also looking to the future as it gears up to be the lead partner for AAD 2028.
Reflecting on this, SAAMDEC Chairperson Michelle Nxumalo said, “one of the most notable achievements of the past year was South Africa surpassing the R10 billion mark in defence exports. The R10 billion milestone is therefore much more than a number, it demonstrates our capability to develop and deliver sophisticated internationally competitive defence solutions.”
But she cautioned, “a milestone is not a destination. We must translate a strong year into sustained growth.”
In presenting SAAMDEC’s annual Chairperson’s report, she noted that the organisation (alongside AMD) has used the past year to further engagements with relevant stakeholders and partners to advance and support export growth. Pointing to the organisation’s first-ever engagement with the Export Credit Insurance Corporation of South Africa (ECIC), Nxumalo said this represents a key milestone, as defence exports often require “substantial financing, guarantees, as well as long-term risk support.”
She also pointed to the improved cooperation with various government departments and the inclusion of defence industry representatives in the various presidential state visits and international business forums.
Next, Sandile Ndlovu, AMD CEO, briefly summarised both AMD and SAAMDEC’s annual reports, noting that AMD has seen strong growth in terms of both the quality and quantity of members in recent years. Noting that while some used to ask why they had to join AMD, today “we receive membership applications on a daily basis now,” he said.
He also noted that AMD’s decision to broaden its engagements with government beyond the Department of Defence has already proved fruitful. People right across government, he said, “now finally understand the value of our industry.”
Pointing to concrete examples, Ndlovu said, “the head of our foreign intelligence services was in Qatar over the past three days. He called and said, ‘Sandile, there are immense opportunities here for your industry, and I’ve taken up some leads and as soon as I get back in the country you and I must talk,’” he said, noting that something like this would have been unheard of only a few years ago.
Additionally, Ndlovu informed members that while the defence industry is principally concentrated in three provinces, only Gauteng had previously designated the defence industry as an industry worthy of special focus up until now.
“We can now report that the Western Cape, KwaZulu-Natal, and the Eastern Cape provinces have now also identified that our sector is a sector that requires special attention,” he said.
Regionally, Ndlovu noted that the Southern African Development Community (SADC) has decided to include the aerospace and defence industry permanently in its annual Industrialisation Week, with SADC officials encouraging greater collaboration in the sector across the region.
AMD’s Honorary Treasurer, Thivash Moodley, reported that the organisation’s financial position remains strong. In the 2025/26 financial year, he noted that AMD increased its revenue by some 34%, substantially thanks to a very successful AAD 2024.
Since then, he noted, AMD took the decision to invest heavily in itself through organising and attending events in support of the industry, other industries and the South African National Defence Force.
Moodley said the organisation remained financially secure as it looks ahead to AAD 2028, encouraging all AMD member to actively participate as they seek maximise the opportunities proffered by the key biennual event.

title: How close can pure functional programming get to C?
body:
In Why Lean is Faster Than Rust , the author shares an impressive result: a DEFLATE compression library written in Lean 4 , a functional programming language and proof assistant, outperforming an equivalent Rust package that crates.io says has been downloaded over a billion times. From the article:
lean-zip beats every single compression level miniz_oxide provides, i.e. we're capable of providing the same compression at higher throughput. At its fastest setting we're 15% quicker and the output is 8.8% smaller.
However, the article also notes that while they managed to surpass Rust's miniz_oxide , they were no match for the end boss of DEFLATE performance: libdeflate , written in C.
lean-zip is certainly not the best here: libdeflate unsurprisingly blows it out of the water (unsurprisingly because this is a very carefully tuned implementation using architecture-specific SIMD, that we can't touch in Lean).
Enter Roc , a functional programming language (but not a theorem prover) with an explicit focus on runtime performance.
Roc's tagline is "Fast, Friendly, Functional," and Fast comes first because both running fast and compiling fast have always been central goals. Roc is not a mature language (it's still weeks away from its first numbered release, 0.1.0), and its nascent package ecosystem has had almost no optimization work done on it. Still, between its language design, longstanding optimizations , and brand-new compiler implementation , I figured Roc already had enough of a foundation in place to take on the champ: libdeflate.
So I spent a bunch of time grinding through performance optimizations on roc-deflate , a package Niclas Ahden wrote (and uses in paid production work ) for DEFLATE compression. I didn't expect to beat libdeflate's performance across the board, but I wanted to see how close it could get on the non-streaming APIs (as roc-deflate hasn't implemented streaming yet), using the classic Silesia corpus for benchmarking and verifying that it produced identical outputs.
Here's where the benchmarks stand today, running on the 2021 M1 MacBook Pro where I did all the optimization work, as well as on an AMD Ryzen 9 3900X Ubuntu machine for an x64 comparison.
roc-deflate ran these 144 benchmarks slower on average than libdeflate, in the median case 8.9% slower on the Ryzen 3900X, and 2.6% on the M1 MacBook Pro.
So while we didn't outperform the champ on average, a median slowdown percentage in the single digits compared to such a carefully-tuned SIMD-powered C library is wild. It's frankly not a result I knew was achievable going in, since Roc is a functional language with automatic memory management racing against code that doesn't have to do bounds checks. (Bounds checks have a cost, but then again, the last time a skipped bounds check in C compression code led to a major Remote Code Execution vulnerability was yesterday .)
The graph shows more detail than just the median gap. On the worst-case inputs, roc-deflate was 18% slower than libdeflate, but on the best-case inputs, roc-deflate was slightly over 18% faster! That's not because Roc has some magical optimization that C can't access; it's just that the two implementations are different, and although on average roc-deflate is slower, for certain inputs it happens to be faster. So while it's possible to get a speedup by switching from libdeflate to roc-deflate, you shouldn't expect it on average.
To be clear, C's performance ceiling is higher than Roc's. For any input where roc-deflate currently outperforms libdeflate, C code can close that gap. The reverse is not true; Roc code is memory-safe, does automatic reference counting, checks bounds, and supports no Rust-style unsafe to opt out of any of that. These properties give Roc code stronger safety guarantees than code written in C, Zig, Rust, and other languages that allow full access to the hardwareâand the price it pays for those guarantees is a lower performance ceiling.
Obviously we can't extrapolate from this one result about how close Roc can get to C in the general case, but now something has been demonstrated that nobody knew was achievable before. As far as I know, this is the most optimization effort that has been put into any Roc package to date, so how close others can get to this result is a complete unknown right now. So while I'm thrilled by this result, I'm fully aware that we won't know how well it generalizes until we've optimized a wider sample of real-world Roc code bases!
An obvious question is "Why settle for any amount slower?" If you could get C levels of performance, why not use libdeflate itself and close that remaining gap?
A pure-Roc implementation has several advantages over a pure-C one:
If any of these guarantees don't hold in practice, it can only be due to a defect in Roc's compiler, the platform the application is running on, or the underlying hardware. So when you see in roc-deflate's docs that the entire package is 100% pure functions, you can be confident you are getting all of the above properties from everything the package has to offer. The type system enforces it!
The reason we've been working so hard on all this might become clearer if you look at the proposition in reverse: would you give up guaranteed memory safety, guaranteed lack of side effects, guaranteed deterministic behavior across all targets, and the security benefits of having no exploitable build scripts in packages...for an average speedup percentage in the single digits?
That answer can legitimately vary by use caseâRoc's own compiler, for example, wants the maximum performance the hardware can deliver âbut I bet a lot of people reading this can see why we're so excited to have achieved this result.
Most of the optimizations that improved roc-deflate's numbers came from general optimization techniques that are widely beneficial across languages. (I always recommend Casey Muratori's Performance-Aware Programming Series , which I paid for and learned a lot from.) Some of the optimization techniques were Roc-specific, though, and I wanted to mention them here as a reference for others. Even if you're not writing Roc code, this can also give you an idea of how Roc achieves its performance .
One of Roc's most effective optimizations is opportunistic mutation (which Koka calls "Functional but In-Place" ). You can learn how it works in Roc's docs on opportunistic mutation , but from a performance optimization perspective, it's critically important to avoid unnecessary sharing so that values remain unique and therefore eligible for in-place mutation.
You can't opt out of bounds checks (e.g. getting a value out of a dynamically-sized collection) in Roc like you can in C, Zig, and Rust, but Roc's compiler can optimize them away if it knows they'd be guaranteed to pass. Bounds checks are most costly inside loops, so you can get a lot of mileage out of adding something like if collection.len() <= highest_index_used { return 0 } before the loop starts. This adds an additional check that looks redundant, but it can allow the optimizer to safely delete costlier checks inside the loop, once it can tell that failures would not be reachable after that early return.
Roc's compile-time evaluation can be used to assemble lookup tables at compile time as long as nothing depends on runtime inputs. Even better, since their lengths are known at compile time, you can do things like Ok(entry) = lookup_table.get(5) to do an exhaustive pattern match that Roc's compiler will know is valid thanks to compile-time evaluation. This avoids runtime bounds checks that non-constant tables might have to pay for.
In Roc, a + b desugars to a.plus(b) . For an integer like U64 , U64.plus includes an overflow check, whereas plus_wrap does not. Although plus is the safer default, overflow checks have a runtime cost , as CPUs can do wrapping integer arithmetic in one instruction. When Roc's compiler can prove that overflow won't occur, both plus and plus_wrap will optimize to the same instructions, but when it can't, you may get a speedup by choosing plus_wrap .
I'm sure there are still opportunities to improve roc-deflate's performanceâespecially on x64 CPUsâas well as the optimization pipeline in Roc's compiler.
At this point I feel reasonably confident that all the low-hanging fruit has been picked, but if anyone wants to try it out for themselves, here's the script I ran to set up and run the benchmark suite on Linux . (Note that Claude Opus 5.5 generated this script, and I haven't vetted it for security; run it outside a sandbox at your own risk!) It pins both Roc compiler revisions and roc-deflate versions, so you'll want to adjust those commits if you're trying out potential improvements.
For my part, I'll be focusing on the upcoming Roc 0.1.0 release from now until it's out. It's been eight years in the making, so I'll be very happy for us to finally have a numbered release! If you'd like to learn more about Roc, check out roc-lang.org or come say hi on Roc Zulip !

title: Koretsky instructs executive bodies to form cybersecurity teams
body:
Prime Minister of Ukraine Serhiy Koretsky has instructed the heads of all executive bodies to urgently form cybersecurity teams, purchase software, and commission it into operation.
