title: Forms Capital wins CIMG Marketing-Oriented Finance House of the Year, 2025
body: Forms Capital Limited has been adjudged Marketing-Oriented Finance House of the Year, 2025 at the Chartered Institute of Marketing, Ghana (CIMG) 37th Annual National Marketing Performance Awards, in recognition of the company’s excellence in strategic marketing and its commitment to creating value for customers and delivering strong business results. The award was presented at the ceremony on Saturday, 17 October 2026, at the Labadi Beach Hotel in Accra. The recognition highlights Forms Capital’s strategic approach to marketing, including the use of market insights, effective marketing programmes and customer-focused initiatives to support business growth and strengthen its position in Ghana’s financial services industry. For Forms Capital, the recognition represents an important milestone in its commitment to making financial services more accessible, relevant and impactful for individuals, businesses and communities. Commenting on the achievement, Ishmael Abbey, Head of Business Development at Forms Capital Limited, said: “ We are honoured to receive this recognition from the Chartered Institute of Marketing, Ghana. It affirms our belief that marketing goes beyond promoting products and services; it is about understanding people’s needs, creating meaningful value and building lasting relationships with customers”. “At Forms Capital, we continue to pursue innovative and customer-focused approaches that connect our financial solutions to the aspirations of individuals, entrepreneurs and businesses. This award is an encouragement to keep challenging ourselves, deepening customer trust and contributing to the growth of the communities we serve. We are grateful to our customers, partners and dedicated team members whose continued support and commitment make achievements like this possible”, he added. Advancing Customer-Centred Financial Services Forms Capital Limited continues to strengthen its approach to financial services through customer-focused solutions, strategic partnerships and initiatives designed to respond to evolving financial needs. Its marketing philosophy centres on connecting customers with relevant financial opportunities while building trust, improving engagement and supporting sustainable business growth. As the company advances its growth ambitions and prepares for its next phase of development in Ghana’s financial services sector, the CIMG award provides further motivation to deepen its commitment to innovation, customer experience and responsible business growth. The company recognises that sustainable success is built on a combination of strong strategy, customer understanding, effective execution and the collective efforts of its people. This achievement therefore belongs to the entire Forms Capital team, alongside the customers and partners who continue to be part of its journey.

title: European Parliament calls for EU naval operation in Black Sea
body:
The European Parliament has called on the European Union to consider deploying a naval operation in the Black Sea following deadly attacks on civilian merchant vessels off the coasts of Bulgaria and Romania and repeated violations of Romanian airspace.
In a resolution adopted on Thursday, October 22, lawmakers condemned Russia's attacks on civilian shipping and warned of escalating security threats in the western Black Sea. The resolution received 432 votes in favor, 52 against and 88 abstentions.
The resolution states that the attacks form part of a pattern of escalation in Russia's war against Ukraine, with consequences for maritime security across the region.
MEPs called on the EU and its member states to consider deploying a naval operation in the Black Sea, citing freedom of navigation and maritime security as essential to protecting NATO's eastern flank, the Black Sea region and the Danube delta.
They also urged NATO to consider a dedicated Black Sea initiative, building on discussions about a proposed 'Black Sea Sentry' framework. The resolution further emphasizes closer security cooperation between Bulgaria, Romania and Türkiye.
The resolution does not specify the potential operation’s size, composition, mandate or deployment timeline. It also does not outline how such a mission would be coordinated with NATO or how it would be funded.
The calls come as attacks on commercial shipping and airspace violations raise concerns about the security of maritime routes and infrastructure in the region.
The European Parliament also called on EU countries, working with NATO, to help Bulgaria and Romania improve the early detection and tracking of hostile drones threatening Black Sea shipping.
MEPs urged the EU to accelerate the implementation of its Black Sea maritime security hub initiative, which is intended to strengthen maritime safety, protect critical maritime infrastructure and safeguard the marine environment.
The resolution also calls for unused funding under the EU's Security Action for Europe (SAFE) instrument to be directed toward helping Bulgaria and Romania address these security challenges.
Beyond immediate threats to shipping, lawmakers called for stronger protection of submarine telecommunications cables, electricity transmission links and data cable projects in the region.
The proposed measures include enhanced maritime surveillance, closer regional cooperation and rapid-response mechanisms to improve the resilience of critical undersea infrastructure.
MEPs also stressed that the EU's next long-term budget should address a broad range of security and defense requirements, including those affecting the Black Sea region.

title: Ukraine Says More Than 20,400 Central Asians Signed Russian Army Contracts
body: More than 20,400 Central Asian citizens have signed contracts with Russia’s armed forces since its full-scale invasion of Ukraine began, according to the Ukrainian government’s “I Want to Live” project. The new figures come as families in Kazakhstan secure the return of young men who say they went to Russia for civilian work and were forced into military service. The project’s October figures identify 8,207 Uzbek citizens and 5,308 Tajiks, together accounting for about two-thirds of the regional total. Kazakhstan accounts for 3,819. A further 2,219 are from Kyrgyzstan, and 884 from Turkmenistan. The count covers identified contract signers as of October 1, rather than the number currently fighting, and excludes ethnic Central Asians with Russian citizenship. The figures have not been independently verified. “I Want to Live” is a Ukrainian state project that helps Russian servicemen surrender. For some Kazakh families, the immediate struggle has been to get their sons out of the Russian army. Twenty-year-old Ainabek Keldibek went to Russia expecting to work as a security guard. As TCA reported , he and other young Kazakh men later appeared in appeals for help, with some wearing Russian uniforms in or near the combat zone. On October 7, relatives went to Kazakhstan’s Foreign Ministry in Astana to demand help bringing the men home. Lawyer Meirman Shekeyev, who accompanied them, said he knew of at least 21 cases. Families said their relatives had accepted civilian jobs before being pressured to sign military contracts. Keldibek has now returned to Kazakhstan . His sister told RFE/RL ’s Kazakh service that he arrived in Shymkent on the evening of October 21. She said others were still waiting to return. Kazakhstan’s Foreign Ministry had earlier asked Moscow to help repatriate the men and opened a hotline for their families. Their accounts fit a pattern documented by the International Federation for Human Rights . Its April study found that migrants in Russia had been offered military contracts as an alternative to detention or deportation. Others were recruited abroad with promises of civilian work, only to find themselves sent to the front. “Many of these men knew in some capacity what they were signing up for. But some were also deceived or coerced,” FIDH President Alexis Deswaef said. The war has also drawn Central Asians to Ukraine’s defense. TCA’s earlier reporting on both sides described volunteers who regarded Ukraine as home and saw Russia’s invasion as a threat to their families. Kazakh national Zhasulan Duysembin joined Ukraine’s armed forces in 2021 after settling there. In a 2022 interview , he told Ukrainska Pravda : “I had two children in Ukraine, and for the first time I started to think that they might be in danger.” Uzbekistan’s Migration Agency has warned citizens that offers of work or help with immigration papers can lead to recruitment into armed conflicts. It has also reminded them that joining foreign armed forces can bring criminal liability at home. For other families, there has been no homecoming. Kiril Nysanbaev went to Russia for work after completing his military service in Kazakhstan. His twin sister, Kamilla, told RFE/RL that he called from a detention center in Chelyabinsk and said officers had beaten him and forced him to sign a military contract. He was later killed in Ukraine’s Donetsk region. His family learned of his death months afterwards. Kamilla said the family buried him in Russia after Kazakh police warned that bringing his body home would trigger an investigation against them. “I warn them to avoid going to Russia,” Kamilla said.

title: Military reinforcements move to Mideast. And, millions of Americans vote early
body:
Good morning. You're reading the Up First newsletter. Subscribe here to get it delivered to your inbox, and listen to the Up First podcast for all the news you need to start your day.
Heavier fighting in Iran could resume in the coming weeks as military reinforcements arrive and some U.S. personnel leave the region. This shift comes as a person briefed on the U.S. and Israel's war planning told NPR that the countries were preparing plans for a possible attack on Iran after the U.S. midterms. Iran said it is prepared .
Traffic in Tehran on Wednesday moves past an installation depicting butterflies forming the Iranian national flag. Atta Kenare/AFP via Getty Images hide caption
Although Election Day is more than a week away , almost 21 million Americans have already voted, either by mail or early in-person voting, according to the University of Florida's Election Lab.
Trump must sit for a deposition in his $10 billion defamation case against the BBC, a federal magistrate judge ruled. Trump is required to comply with court rules or face sanctions, the judge said yesterday. The case centers on a Panorama broadcast from late October 2024, which allegedly edited the president's Jan. 6 speech to make it appear he incited a violent siege of Congress. Trump has described the broadcast as false, misleading and defamatory under Florida law.
Trump promised to lower grocery prices in his second term. While some individual items have gotten cheaper since he returned to office, overall grocery prices have risen, driven by factors such as increased labor costs, tariffs and higher energy prices due to the conflict with Iran. Specific issues facing a single crop, animal species or geographic region can cause the price of one item to rise well above inflation, while lowering the price of another. NPR analyzed five everyday food items — ground beef, eggs, coffee, butter and chocolate chip cookies — to better understand the math behind grocery store prices.
Petter Mattei portrays stars in the Metropolitan Opera production of Lincoln in the Bardo , adapted from George Saunders' surreal novel about the president grieving the loss of his son in the midst of the Civil War. Karen Almond/Metropolitan Opera hide caption
Check out what NPR is watching, reading and listening to this weekend:
🍿 Movies: A new film version of Jane Austen's Sense and Sensibility focuses on the Dashwood family's two oldest sisters, Elinor and Marianne, who face financial insecurity due to laws that disadvantage widows and daughters.
📺 TV: Actor Sharon Horgan stars as Alex, a 50-year-old divorcée who finds herself at multiple personal and professional crossroads in HBO's new show Youth .
📚 Books: Barbara Trapido's Brother of the More Famous Jack follows Katherine Browne, who is determined to escape her stiflingly conventional upbringing and create a life with fewer constraints.
🎵 Music: NPR's New Music Friday host Stephen Thompson breaks down the best albums released today, including Anderson .Paak and Cordae's Heavy Is the Crown and Fenne Lily's Win Win . Listen to a playlist of the best songs from the new albums .
🎭 Theater: Missy Mazzoli's music brings George Saunders' Booker Prize-winning novel, Lincoln in the Bardo , to life in a stage adaptation at the Metropolitan Opera House in New York. Mazzoli is the first woman composer to have a world premiere on the Met stage.
Karl Bushby, pictured here in Turkey in 2025, started his Goliath Expedition 28 years ago. Karl Bushby hide caption

title: Saudi Arabia flight cancellations: Which airlines are suspending services and until when?
body: Flight cancellations across Saudi Arabia continue as airlines extend suspensions amid ongoing regional tensions and attacks by Yemen's Houthis . Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport has partially reopened following its closure earlier this month, but international services remain heavily disrupted. Etihad Airways has extended cancellations on routes to Riyadh and Dammam into November, while flydubai has suspended several Saudi services until October 29. The disruption has also spread beyond the capital, with an attack on Dammam's King Fahd International Airport on Wednesday adding to concerns over aviation safety in the kingdom. Here is how major airlines have adjusted their operations and when flights are expected to resume. Etihad Air ways Etihad Airways has cancelled flights between Abu Dhabi and Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah until November 5 owing to the regional disruption. All services to and from Riyadh and Dammam are affected, along with four Jeddah services – EY601, EY602, EY603 and EY604. Emirates Emirates has suspended all of its flights to Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah until October 25. Flydubai The airline has cancelled flights to Riyadh, Dammam and Abha up to and including October 29. Air Arabia Air Arabia has cancelled services between Sharjah and several Saudi destinations including Riyadh, Abha, Dammam and Taif. No resumption date has been announced. Qatar Airways The airline has temporarily suspended flights to and from Riyadh and Dammam up to and including October 24. Meanwhile, its services to Jeddah have been reduced from seven daily flights to four. Gulf Air Gulf Air has said flights after Sunday, October 18 are currently proceeding as scheduled, following its previously announced Riyadh cancellations. Oman Air Oman Air has announced that all flights to and from Riyadh are suspended until October 31. SalamAir The Omani low-cost airline has cancelled flights to and from Riyadh and Dammam until October 31, citing regional security developments. Air France The French airline has extended its suspension of flights to and from Riyadh up to October 24. British Airways British Airways is scheduled to return with a limited service to Riyadh on November 3, operating one flight daily, according to previously announced plans. The airline discontinued flights to Jeddah in April as part of wider changes to its Middle East operations. Air India and Air India Express Air India and Air India Express have suspended flights to and from Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam until October 24. Akasa Air The Indian low-cost airline has suspended flights to and from Riyadh until October 24 and Jeddah until October 21. Cathay Pacific The Hong Kong airline has extended its suspension of flights to Riyadh up to January 31, 2027. Pakistan International Airlines The airline announced a temporary suspension of flights to Riyadh on October 9, without setting out a resumption date. The Pakistan Airports Authority said at the time that its other Saudi services were continuing as usual. Delta Air Lines The US airline has postponed the launch of flights between Atlanta and Riyadh until March 2027. Services had been scheduled to begin on October 23. IndiGo The Indian airline has cancelled flights to and from Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah up to October 24. Lufthansa The German airline has suspended flights to Riyadh until November 18, extending its previously announced October 16 deadline. The Lufthansa Group’s advisory also lists Dammam services as suspended through November 30. Eurowings, part of the group, is scheduled to resume flights to Jeddah on November 12. Malaysia Airlines Malaysia Airlines has announced that flights to and from Jeddah and Madinah will resume on October 18 after a safety review. KLM The Dutch airline has extended cancellations of all flights to Riyadh and Dammam up to October 31. Philippine Airlines The Philippine flag carrier has suspended Riyadh flights PR654 and PR655 until November 29, citing the security situation at King Khalid International Airport. Scoot The Singapore Airlines-owned low-cost carrier has cancelled flights between Singapore and Jeddah until December 2.

title: European Commission declines to comment on potential EU negotiation group for talks with Putin
body:
The European Commission has declined to comment on reports regarding a potential high-level European Union negotiation group for talks on establishing peace in Ukraine, noting that the EU is already involved in such discussions.
On Friday in Brussels, European Commission spokesperson Arianna Podesta addressed media reports suggesting that Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, Finnish President Alexander Stubb, and Czech President Petr Pavel could be potential candidates for such negotiations.
She said that the European Union was present at the talks held in Oslo earlier this week. It is expected that these discussions will continue in a multilateral format at the level of high-ranking officials; naturally, the European Union will also be represented.
Christian Wigand, a spokesperson for external relations, added that negotiations are taking place in various formats, in different locations, and at different levels, involving heads of state and government, ministers, senior diplomats, and EU representatives. He emphasized that the European Union is participating in this process.
Podesta also stressed that the EU has always worked to ensure that Ukraine remains in a strong position and has consistently sought to achieve a just and lasting peace for Ukraine. According to her, the EU does this whenever the opportunity arises. At present, multilateral talks at the level of senior officials are expected to take place, she said, declining to provide any additional comments.

title: Russia has kept the Red Cross away from Ukrainian POWs since 2024. Now about 1,500 captives it never confirmed as prisoners face prosecution
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); About 1,500 Ukrainians held in Russia and occupied Ukraine are facing criminal prosecution even though the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) has never confirmed them as prisoners, Petro Yatsenko, representative of Ukraine's Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War, said on 19 October at an event on missing persons at UN headquarters in New York. The event was organized by the permanent missions of Ukraine and Poland to the UN. Without ICRC confirmation, there is no official record that a person is alive or held, which leaves captives without proper protection, the headquarters said. Amnesty International calls this enforced disappearance, a practice that puts people outside the protection of the law. The ICRC itself has been shut out. Under the Geneva Conventions it is supposed to visit prisoners of war, but on 18 September it told Reuters that Russia has given it no access to Ukrainian POWs since 2024. UN investigators have gathered evidence of systematic torture in the detention centers where they are held. Russia denies torturing or mistreating POWs. Families lose track of captives as Russia moves them between prisons Kateryna Nazarii, who coordinates families of the 24th Mechanized Brigade, is the wife of a Ukrainian serviceman held by Russia. The ICRC has not been able to confirm his status as a prisoner of war. Russia does not let the ICRC or other humanitarian organizations into the prisons where Ukrainians are held, and does not hand over complete lists of prisoners, Nazarii said at the event. When families do find out where a relative is held, she said, that person is moved to another prison, and contact is lost again. Many of those whose captivity Russia has not confirmed are civilians. Among them, Yatsenko said, are about 200 young people born after 2000 and nearly 400 people over 60. None of them has been confirmed through the ICRC, according to the headquarters. Secrecy and torture in Russian captivity Most Ukrainian POWs are cut off from the outside world. In a March 2025 report, Amnesty International found that 24 of the 43 families of confirmed POWs it interviewed had received no word at all from their relative. Counting prisoners allowed only one brief call or text at the start of captivity, 72% of those 43 were held incommunicado. The UN monitoring mission found that only 21 of 174 former POWs it interviewed had been able to correspond with their families, Amnesty noted. Silence is what makes the abuse possible, Amnesty argues. The UN monitoring mission found that 97% of former POWs it interviewed had been tortured or ill-treated, the report notes, and methods include beatings, electric shocks, burns, and sexual violence. A UN commission of inquiry concluded in 2024 that the torture amounted to a "coordinated state policy," the report adds. A Ukrainian defender who returned from Russian captivity shows the effects of his detention. June 2023. Photo: libkos/Instagram When the Red Cross did get in, it saw what Russia chose to show. An OSCE expert mission reported in September 2025 that, according to former prisoners, Russian staff presented only prisoners in relatively good physical condition during ICRC visits and kept the sick and tortured out of sight. The experts also found that Russia blocked visits to some facilities and gave incomplete prisoner lists. The unconfirmed are not a small group. A quarter of the 3,767 POWs who returned to Ukraine by November 2024 had never been confirmed by Russia as captives, the Coordination Headquarters said, as cited by Amnesty. Hundreds or possibly thousands more may still be held without Russia notifying the ICRC, Amnesty concluded. Those who come back describe the conditions. Anatolii Zemlianyi, a soldier of the 2nd Assault Brigade released in the May 2025 exchange, told Frontliner that he spent eight months in a hospital in occupied Donetsk with a grenade wound in his leg and got no proper treatment. In captivity, he said, prisoners drank water from puddles. A Ukrainian service member who returned from captivity compares his current appearance with a photo taken before his detention. June 2023. Photo: libkos/Instagram Russia continues to hold Ukrainian civilians unlawfully Nobody knows how many Ukrainian civilians Russia holds. "It is not known," the UN human rights office said in a September 2025 report , which cites Ukraine's Prosecutor General's Office as having identified 15,250 civilians detained by Russia between February 2022 and August 2025. Exchanges bring very few of them back: of 5,941 people released from Russian captivity between February 2022 and 14 August 2025, 352 were civilians, Ukraine's human rights commissioner Dmytro Lubinets told The Week. Under the Fourth Geneva Convention, an occupying power may intern civilians only for imperative reasons of security, and only under a regular procedure with periodic review, the same UN report notes. Russia instead treats detained civilians as criminals, Oleksandr Kononenko, a representative of Ukraine's human rights commissioner, told relatives of civilian hostages in 2023. "This convention clearly states that civilian hostages should not be detained. They should be released. What is Russia doing? It 'makes all these people criminals' and accuses them of terrorism, opposition to a special military operation, and assistance to the Ukrainian Armed Forces, which is completely absurd from the point of view of an independent state and those people who are patriots of their state," Kononenko said. Kyiv believes Russia detains civilians partly to trade them. Regular civilian swaps risk signaling to Russia that by detaining more Ukrainians it could get more Russians released, so it may seize more people to replenish its "exchange fund," Lubinets said. Ukraine therefore demands that civilians be released unconditionally. Amnesty sees a second motive. It concluded that Russia has long used arbitrary arrest, torture, and enforced disappearance to intimidate civilians in areas it controls. One of newest is teacher who stayed in her occupied village to care for her 83-year-old mother “We remember everyone who is in captivity” – Ukraine brings home 160 defenders held since 2022 After four years in Russian captivity, 205 Ukrainian defenders are home in the first stage of a 1000-for-1000 exchange

title: A shared sense of purpose: 5 career lessons from a Pru Life UK leader
body: Editor’s note: This content is sponsored by Pru Life UK and was handled by BrandRap, the sales and marketing arm of Rappler. No member of the news and editorial team participated in the publishing of this piece. “My career did not follow a straight line.” This sounds like inspiring advice from the get-go – and even more so when you discover that this came from Haidee Plopenio, Head of Business Continuity Management at Pru Life UK. This year, she marks her 29th year with the top insurance company, which is celebrating its 30th year anniversary. Photography by Lem Atienza; makeup by Dorothy Mamalio; hair by Marjorie Caballos As the head of Business Continuity Management, Plopenio says her role shouldn’t be seen as intimidating as it sounds. “My title may sound formal, but my work is really about people, preparation, and collaboration. I work with different teams to help ensure that Pru Life UK can continue serving our customers, employees, and stakeholders, even during disruptions,” she said in an interview with Rappler. Before she landed her current role, Plopenio juggled many hats in different disciplines: technology (which taught her structure), business analysis (understanding needs), project management (collaboration and delivery risk), risk management (foresight), and eventually business continuity and resilience, which tied all these things together. In our exclusive chat, Plopenio walks us through her journey with Pru Life UK, where we pick up career advice that can fuel anyone – even from unrelated fields. She mentioned that over time, she was given opportunities to grow across different functions, and each role helped her prepare for the work she does today. Put power in preparation In Plopenio’s job, delayed gratification is in motion. “What I find most fulfilling is knowing that the work we do, although often behind the scenes, helps protect what matters most: Our customers, employees, and the trust that they place in Pru Life UK,” Plopenio said. “In business continuity, you may not always see the impact immediately, but when something happens, preparedness becomes very real.” But preparedness goes beyond her job description. For her, protection – which is central to Pru Life UK’s service for its customers – is synonymous with preparedness. “Protection means being ready and being present when people need you most. Protection is not only about products or processes. Earlier in my career, I may have thought of protection mainly in terms of insurance [or] insurance coverage,” she explained. Screenshot “But over time, especially through my work in business continuity and resilience, I have come to see protection more broadly. It means helping families prepare for uncertainty. It means ensuring customers can continue to rely on us during difficult moments.” Foster a collaborative mindset In dealing with company curveballs, Plopenio stressed the importance of bringing all hands on deck. “I also value the collaborative culture in Pru Life UK. In crisis management and business continuity, I have seen teams from different departments come together quickly during challenging situations,” she recalled. “That shared sense of purpose and teamwork is one of the reasons I have stayed.” Promote accessibility “I believe Pru Life UK has helped address a very Filipino need – the desire to protect and provide for one’s family. So many Filipino families worry about illness, loss of income, education, emergencies, and even natural calamities. So these are realities we also consider in business continuity because disruptions can affect people’s ability to access important services,” she said. “The company has also helped make insurance more understandable and accessible through its people. We have financial advisors who guide customers based on their needs, life stage, and goals.” Find ways to reframe perspective Let’s face it: Although more Filipinos are now aware of insurance and its significance, not a lot would treat it as an immediate necessity. Oftentimes, it gets put aside as a “next time” expense, rather than something integral to one’s everyday life. “The more we connect insurance to real-life concerns, family, health, education, emergencies, and peace of mind, the more people see it not as an expense but as an act of care.” Value your people – and make sure it shows Now that Pru Life UK has crossed its 30th year, Plopenio wishes that in the next 30 years, the company remains a trusted partner for Filipino families. “I hope the company continues to innovate, strengthen resilience, and make protection more accessible to more Filipinos. I also hope it continues to invest in its people because my own journey shows how much an organization can shape and grow its people when it provides trust, opportunity, and purpose.” In fact, in our conversation, “people” is the word that showed up the most. “My journey with Pru Life UK has taught me that protection is not just about policies or plans; it is about people. It is about preparing today so that families, customers, employees, and communities can face tomorrow with more confidence.” “The first and foremost consideration in everything we do is our care for our people,” she said, highlighting the need to empower people to grow. And with how Plopenio is warmly surrounded by different Pru Life UK employees who cheered her on – from the start until the end of our shoot and interview – I know this isn’t just lip service. You really get what you give. – Rappler.com

title: Only 15% of Nigerian Schools Budget for WASH Maintenance, Says LAPO
body: Folalumi Alaran in Abuja President of the Lift Above Poverty Organisation (LAPO), Faith Negbe Osazuwa-Ojo, has said only 15 per cent of Nigerian schools have budgeted funds for the maintenance of water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) facilities, raising concerns over the health, dignity and learning conditions of millions of schoolchildren. Osazuwa-Ojo disclosed this at the organisation’s 33rd Annual Development Forum in Abuja on Thursday, warning that inadequate access to safe water, decent toilets and handwashing facilities continued to undermine children’s welfare and educational development. The LAPO president, who spoke at the forum themed ‘Safe Water, Healthy Learning: Advancing WASH in Nigerian Schools,’ said findings from the 2021 Water, Sanitation and Hygiene National Outcome Routine Mapping (WASHNORM) report showed that only 37 per cent of schools had access to basic water supply services. She added that only 35 per cent had access to basic sanitation services, while 30 per cent provided basic hygiene services, including handwashing facilities, soap and water. The LAPO president described the figures as more than statistics, saying they reflected the daily struggles of Nigerian children forced to learn in environments where basic necessities were lacking. “These are far more than statistics. They represent the daily reality and struggles of millions of Nigerian children,” she said. She painted a picture of pupils arriving at school eager to learn but finding no clean drinking water, decent toilets or facilities to wash their hands, warning that such conditions could encourage the spread of preventable diseases, reduce school attendance and disrupt learning. Osazuwa-Ojo said every child deserved to learn in a safe, healthy and dignified environment, stressing that access to water, sanitation and hygiene should be treated as a fundamental requirement for quality education. She called for stronger partnerships, increased investment and sustained action to ensure that Nigerian schools became safe places where children could learn and thrive. The LAPO president reaffirmed the organisation’s commitment to improving lives, noting that the future of Nigeria depended partly on the choices made today to protect and support its children. Earlier, the Chairperson of the forum, Dr Oyefemi Obazee, called on government, education authorities and development partners to prioritise investments in school WASH facilities, backed by adequate funding, effective implementation and sustained accountability. Obazee said Nigeria’s development challenges required collaboration among government, civil society, academia, the private sector and development partners to develop practical and sustainable solutions. She noted that despite efforts by the Nigerian government and its development partners to improve access to water, sanitation and hygiene through the National WASH Policy, many schools still lacked basic facilities, exposing pupils to conditions that compromised their health, dignity and academic performance. “At LAPO, we believe that quality education cannot thrive where basic human needs are unmet,” she said, adding that every child deserved an environment that protected their health and enabled them to realise their full potential. Addressing stakeholders, Obazee urged school proprietors, administrators and teachers to regard WASH as an essential component of quality education and to promote hygiene practices while ensuring that facilities were properly maintained. She also called on development partners and the private sector to invest in innovative and sustainable solutions for underserved schools, while urging parents, traditional rulers, religious leaders and community stakeholders to support schools and promote good hygiene practices. Obazee challenged students to become ambassadors of change by practising good hygiene, caring for their environment and encouraging their peers to do the same. The concerns raised at the forum were reinforced by former Minister of Aviation and Co-Chairman, Chief Osita Chidoka, who was represented by Deputy Corps Marshal Victor Nwokolo (rtd). He argued that Nigeria had focused too heavily on building infrastructure without ensuring that it continued to function. Citing the example of a 10-year-old pupil, Hajara, at Sabon Layi Primary and Junior Secondary School in Potiskum, Yobe State, Chidoka said the school had a borehole, but the facility stopped working, forcing the child to carry water from home until it was converted to a solar-powered system. He said the case illustrated the difference between providing infrastructure and delivering reliable public services. According to him, government should measure success by the number of facilities that remain functional rather than by the number of projects completed. Chidoka proposed that every public school should have a clearly designated institution responsible for its water and sanitation services, a funded maintenance arrangement and a publicly accessible record showing whether facilities were operational. He also called for dedicated maintenance budgets, regular inspections and stronger community participation in monitoring school facilities. The communiqué issued at the end of the forum identified inadequate funding, poor maintenance, weak institutional accountability and limited community participation as major obstacles to sustainable WASH services in schools. It recommended gender-sensitive sanitation facilities, adequate menstrual hygiene support for adolescent girls, accessible infrastructure for children with disabilities and stronger coordination among federal, state and local governments.

title: Finance Ministry rejects claim it withheld ABFA data from PIAC
body: The Ministry of Finance has rejected claim that it withheld information on the utilisation of the Annual Budget Funding Amount (ABFA) from the Public Interest and Accountability Committee (PIAC). In a statement issued on Friday, October 23, 2026, the Ministry said it had provided PIAC with petroleum receipts and distribution data and explained the arrangements governing the use of ABFA resources, including funds ring-fenced for the Accra–Kumasi Expressway. The clarification follows a PIAC statement dated October 21 concerning the exclusion of ABFA utilisation data from its 2026 Semi-Annual Report. “The exclusion of ABFA utilisation data from PIAC’s report should therefore not be presented as evidence that the Ministry withheld information,” the Ministry stated. According to the Ministry, officials participated in PIAC’s virtual validation workshop and held in-person meetings with the Committee to explain petroleum revenue receipts, distribution and the arrangements for ABFA utilisation. On the Accra–Kumasi Expressway, the Ministry cited paragraph 572 of the 2026 Mid-Year Fiscal Policy Review, which states that all funds allocated to the project, including the total ABFA realised in 2026, have been ring-fenced. The funds will be used for construction when the contract is awarded. The Ministry said the decision follows PIAC’s recommendation to stop spreading petroleum revenues thinly across numerous projects with limited economic impact. It explained that concentrating the resources on the expressway is intended to deliver a major infrastructure investment with clear national benefits and value for money. The Ministry also rejected suggestions that District Assemblies had been deprived of their share of ABFA resources. It said the five per cent share due to the District Assemblies Common Fund is being paid from the Consolidated Fund, an arrangement it had explained to PIAC. “Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies have therefore not been shortchanged by the decision to ring-fence ABFA resources for the expressway,” the statement said. The Ministry reaffirmed its commitment to providing PIAC with the information required to discharge its mandate and to accounting publicly for petroleum revenues. It added that relevant details would continue to be published in the Annual Report on Petroleum Funds, Petroleum Reconciliation Reports, Budget Statements and other fiscal reports.
