title: Hundreds of flights cancelled as Typhoon Champi shuts Taiwan
body: Hundreds of flights in the East Asia region were cancelled on Friday as powerful Typhoon Champi roared close to Taiwan’s north-east coast. Schools and offices in Taiwan were shut as Champi neared the island. While it is uncertain if it will make landfall, the storm was forecast to bring 90cm (35in) of rain and strong winds to the north-east until Saturday. One person died after being swept away by waves, authorities said. The storm also injured 171 people and forced 1,000 others to evacuate. Champi is the latest in a string of intense typhoons as a Super El Niño heats up the Pacific Ocean and fuels storms. At its peak earlier this week, it was the planet’s strongest storm of the year so far. On Friday afternoon, Champi was packing wind gusts of 191km/h (119mph) . After passing Taiwan’s north-eastern tip and the Okinawa islands in southern Japan, Champi is expected to hover over the waters off China’s eastern coast, before curving farther to the north-east to Japan’s main island. Weather agencies in Taiwan, Hong Kong and Japan forecast that the eye of the storm is expected to pass without making landfall in Taiwan. However, a forecaster in Taiwan’s Central Weather Administration told Reuters that they could not rule this out completely – especially if the storm “stalls, loops or wobbles from side to side” as it approaches. Rainfall is expected to peak on Saturday morning and continue to batter Taiwan until Saturday evening, the Central Weather Administration said. Taiwanese authorities have urged people to stay away from coasts and mountains. Work and classes were suspended in nearly all of Taiwan’s 22 counties and cities on Friday – what’s colloquially known as a “typhoon holiday” – as Champi approached the island. Taiwan’s $5tn (£3.7tn) stock exchange was also closed on Friday because of the severe weather. Only Kinmen county, an archipelago located to the west of Taiwan’s main island, continued work and classes as usual. In Japan, power cuts were reported in nearly 8,400 households in the southern Okinawa prefecture, according to the local power company. More than 160 flights have been cancelled across four Japanese airlines. Champi has also stirred up heavy rains and winds in Batanes, a Philippine island chain below southern Taiwan. Photos posted on the local government’s Facebook page showed waves crashing into seaside villages and roads closed to traffic. There were no immediate reports of casualties. Typhoon Champi became the strongest storm of the year earlier this week, when it attained a maximum sustained wind speed of 185mph (298km/h) as it moved over the Philippine Sea – the equivalent of a Category 5 hurricane. While initially categorised as a “super typhoon”, Champi weakened on Wednesday as it continued barrelling through the sea. This is shaping up to be one of the most active typhoon seasons the region has seen in years. Champi is Japan’s 30th typhoon of the year – making this the first time since 2013 that the country has seen so many storms. The recent frequency of storms is due to an unusually strong El Niño – a naturally occurring phenomenon that hits the Pacific Ocean every few years and can trigger extreme weather events, from droughts to typhoons.

title: Cyprus police open investigation into financial affairs of Roman Abramovich
body: Police in Cyprus have opened an investigation into the financial affairs of Roman Abramovich, following revelations by BBC Panorama that accountancy firm Deloitte helped in falsifying documents to hide his wealth and evade tax. Serious questions about the integrity of some of Abramovich’s professional advisers were raised earlier this month in a joint report from the BBC and the Bureau of Investigative Journalism (TBIJ). A Cypriot Ministry of Justice official told MPs this week that the report’s findings would be looked at as part of a new investigation by the police’s Financial Intelligence Unit. Lawyers for Abramovich have said that he denies evading tax or concealing his fortune. Deloitte Cyprus said it acts “in compliance with applicable laws”. The police investigation was announced at a parliamentary committee meeting in the Cypriot capital, Nicosia, held to discuss the combating and prevention of money laundering. The Ministry of Justice official told MPs the police would try to determine whether any criminal acts had been committed. Last week, the report from the BBC and TBIJ detailed how accounts signed off by Deloitte in Cyprus in 2006 meant assets such as superyachts, mansions and private jets worth $672m (£508m) vanished from Abramovich’s company accounts. Deloitte, which is the world’s largest accountancy firm, also appears to have advised on a scheme to evade a huge tax bill on the oligarch’s wealth, through the falsification of documents. The evidence was contained in leaked files, including thousands of documents about Abramovich’s finances and the operations of a network of offshore companies, administered from Cyprus between 1995 and 2022. The BBC and media partners including TBIJ, the Guardian, Paper Trail Media, the Organised Crime and Corruption Reporting Project, and Cyprus Investigative Reporting Network, have been reporting on the leaked files since 2023 as part of the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists’ Cyprus Confidential investigation. A representative from the Cypriot police, Andreas Anastasiades, confirmed to MPs that its Financial Crime Unit had already begun to gather evidence, and said the investigation was expected to last several months. When asked by the BBC if the investigation would look into Deloitte’s work, Andreas Anastasiades said: “We will look at any company or person who may be involved.” He added: “We will see if there has been fraud or if some documents have been manipulated.” Lawyers for Abramovich say that Panorama has provided no evidence that the billionaire knew about, authorised or directed the falsification of any document. They also say it was legitimate for his companies to rely on advice from professionals. Deloitte Cyprus says it is unable to comment because the documents are more than 20 years old and no longer accessible. The BBC and TBIJ have previously reported on a tax scheme that allowed Abramovich to dodge millions in tax on the running costs of his yachts. Following that report, two former company directors have been indicted and are due to stand trial in Cyprus next month over €25m in unpaid VAT. Mr Abramovich’s lawyers previously told the BBC that he had “always obtained independent expert professional tax and legal advice” and “acted in accordance” with it.

title: Pellet found in deceased person's estate was Soviet-era enriched uranium, police say
body:
Authorities received a call about someone finding the radioactive material in 2024.
Radioactive materials discovered in a dead person's estate in Asikkala, southern Finland in 2024 turned out to be an enriched uranium pellet, according to local police.
The small piece of enriched uranium measured 5x10mm in size, but according to authorities it did not pose any immediate danger to people or the environment.
After it was discovered , the pellet was sent for further examination in Germany, at the European Commission's Joint Research Centre (JRC) Directorate for Nuclear Safety and Security.
They found that it was an unused, low-enriched pellet used to fuel commercial nuclear reactors. Its origins pointed to the Soviet Union from around the end of the 1980s to the beginning of the 90s.
Police in the province of Häme received a call from the emergency response centre in October 2024, reporting that an individual in Asikkala said they had found suspected radioactive material.
After arriving, police decided to open a preliminary probe into the matter, treating the case as a suspected nuclear energy offence.
Detective Inspector Jari Kiiskinen said police do not know how the pellet ended up with the deceased person.
Based on the way the pellet was packaged, police quickly began to suspect the pellet was radioactive. A radiation detection device was also found at the scene.
Police have since closed the preliminary investigation, as the suspect in the case is deceased.
Kiiskinen said he did not know whether similar radioactive material discoveries have been made before in Finland. He noted that this incident was of minor significance.

title: Run AI prompts in any app from your menubar
body:
A couple of months ago I noticed something disrupting my workflow: typing the same prompts over and over again. Fix the grammar. Rewrite this product copy. Create 3 variants. Different input every time, but the prompt itself? Same, dozens of times a day.
And every time, the same ritual: open Claude, paste the text, rewrite the prompt, wait, copy the result back. Super inefficient.
Chat is great for figuring out what you want. Tweaking. Exploring. But once a prompt works, you’re not iterating anymore, you’ve got a program to run. And programs deserve a runner.
That’s Snippetbar. Your best prompts, saved in your menubar, running on whatever you’ve just copied in a single click or keyboard shortcut.

title: Terekhov: Experiment to attract labor migrants during war not necessary
body:
Mayor of Kharkiv, head of the Association of Frontline Cities and Communities Ihor Terekhov considers it inappropriate to introduce an experimental project during the war to improve and digitize the process of confirming the qualifications of foreigners and stateless persons who plan to immigrate to Ukraine for employment.
"The Ministry [Economics and Environment] has published a draft of new rules for vetting foreign specialists who are planned to be recruited to work in Ukraine. It has invited public discussion. The application has been accepted. My only suggestion is not to start this experiment during wartime," Terekhov wrote on his Telegram channel.
He criticized the policy aimed at debureaucratization of procedures for foreigners, which, in his opinion, does not take into account the consequences of such actions for able-bodied Ukrainians.
"For foreigners, they promise less bureaucracy and more understandable procedures. In the table where the consequences of the decision for people are assessed, there is a place for future immigrants. For Ukrainian workers, there is none. A very unique personnel policy: the benefits for foreign workers were listed, but the consequences for Ukrainians were not even separately assessed," Terekhov wrote.
He believes that the government should instead pay more attention to the employment of immigrants and those left without work due to the destruction of enterprises.
"While the ministry is improving the procedures for people on the other side of the border, Ukrainians are looking for work after the destruction of enterprises. The displaced people are trying to earn money by renting housing. Someone is ready to retrain, but needs help. There are people who have experience and a profession, but after being forced to move, they cannot find a job. This is who the state needs to work with. A Ukrainian worker should not be a note that the ministry adds after a public discussion," Terekhov emphasized.
In his opinion, it is necessary to pay more attention to working conditions and the level of wages.
Terekhov emphasized that the employment of servicemen after returning from the front should become a state priority already during their service.
"Our defenders must return to civilian life with the opportunity to work and support their families. After an injury, a person may need a second profession or a specially equipped workplace. It is necessary to prepare for this now. The employment future of our military personnel must be a state priority already during their service," Terekhov wrote.
"Therefore, I repeat, my position is clear: the experiment of attracting labor migrants during the war must be stopped. I expect the same persistence from the Ministry of Economy in the search for opportunities for Ukrainians. In particular, for those whom we want to return home. Ukrainians should not be the last in line for the attention of their own state," Terekhov summed up.
As reported, on October 22, the Ministry of Economy and Environment published for public discussion a draft resolution on the introduction of an experimental project to improve and digitize the process of confirming the qualifications of foreigners and stateless persons planning to immigrate to Ukraine for employment.
According to the project, the State Employment Center will annually by December 31 form a list of professions and requirements for the qualifications of specialists and workers, the need for which can be met through immigration. Foreigners whose profession is included in this list will be able to submit an application, documents on education, experience and employment contract or an official offer of employment in electronic form through the Obriy system or the mobile application of the Diia portal.
It is assumed that the experimental project will operate during the period of martial law and three months after its termination or cancellation, but no more than two years.

title: US Reportedly Plans to ‘Offer’ Ukraine EU Membership for Dropping NATO Bid
body:
A US peace proposal would ‘offer’ Ukraine European Union membership and an investment package in exchange for abandoning its bid to join NATO, The Economist reported on Thursday, Oct. 22 .
The reported outline also includes a demilitarized zone in Donbas, the eastern Ukrainian region comprising Donetsk and Luhansk.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Russia could receive commercial agreements with American companies, sanctions relief and restored political ties with Washington. The package also envisages resuming Russian gas supplies to Europe, including reviving Nord Stream, according to the report.
Ukrainian officials are familiar with the general framework but have not received full details of the latest US proposals, The Economist reported. Neither Kyiv nor Washington has announced that Ukraine has accepted the terms.
One Ukrainian official told the magazine that Kyiv fears US representatives could pursue lucrative deals with Moscow before the war ends, allowing Russia to gain economic and diplomatic benefits while fighting continues.
The reported outline follows talks in Oslo on Oct. 20 between President Volodymyr Zelensky, US envoy Steve Witkoff and European leaders. The discussions covered Ukraine’s security, territorial questions, sanctions and postwar economic prospects.
US officials described work on two tracks : Ukraine’s sovereignty, security guarantees, European integration and reconstruction; and a separate framework addressing Russia and future security arrangements.
Witkoff subsequently met Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg on Oct. 21.
After that meeting, Zelensky said Washington had relayed that Moscow was open to resuming trilateral negotiations with Ukraine and the US. He said the teams could meet by early November, although no date had been set.
The Kremlin then indicated that Putin was ready in principle to resume talks around mid-November.
Kyiv is pressing for security commitments it considers enforceable. Zelensky has said Ukraine is negotiating US guarantees modeled on NATO’s Article 5 and backed by a vote in Congress.
He described NATO membership, bilateral US guarantees and a European-led Coalition of the Willing as complementary parts of Ukraine’s security framework. No final agreement on those guarantees has been announced.
The reported offer does not establish an agreed accession date or mean Ukraine would automatically join the EU.
Under the EU’s accession rules , membership requires negotiations, the European Parliament’s consent, unanimous approval by the Council and ratification of an accession treaty by all member states and the candidate country.
A previous US-backed peace framework reportedly proposed that Ukraine could join the EU as soon as January 2027. Kyiv Post reported in December 2025 that the proposal would involve territorial concessions and require Brussels to consider changes to its enlargement process. That was a proposed timetable, not an agreed accession date.
Renewed Russian energy supplies would also require European decisions. The EU adopted a legally binding phaseout of Russian gas imports in January, with remaining long-term LNG supplies due to end from January 2027 and pipeline supplies from autumn 2027.
As Kyiv Post previously reported, Germany’s government opposes reopening Nord Stream , which also faces US and EU sanctions.
The reported package therefore includes benefits Washington cannot deliver alone. Ukraine’s accession and any lasting return of Russian gas to the EU market would require agreement in Europe, alongside a settlement accepted by Kyiv and Moscow.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Rain eases in Batanes as Typhoon Rosal starts moving away
body: MANILA, Philippines – Typhoon Rosal (Champi) is now less likely to bring significant rainfall to Batanes, the weather bureau said on Friday afternoon, October 23. But scattered rain and thunderstorms can still hit Batanes, Cagayan, Isabela, Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, La Union, the Cordillera Administrative Region, Palawan, Masbate, the Visayas, the Zamboanga Peninsula, Misamis Occidental, Camiguin, Surigao del Norte, Dinagat Islands, Basilan, and Tawi-Tawi in the next 24 hours, due to Rosal’s outer rainbands and the trough or extension of the typhoon. Rosal was already 385 kilometers north northeast of Itbayat, Batanes, as of 4 pm on Friday. It is moving north northwest at 20 kilometers per hour (km/h), and is expected to leave the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) on Saturday morning, October 24. So far, the typhoon has maximum sustained winds of 155 km/h and gustiness of up to 190 km/h. At its peak, Rosal was a super typhoon with maximum sustained winds of 215 km/h. The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) has yet to lift tropical cyclone wind signals for portions of Northern Luzon. These areas are still under wind signals as of 5 pm on Friday: Signal No. 2 Gale-force winds (62 to 88 km/h), minor to moderate threat to life and property Batanes Signal No. 1 Strong winds (39 to 61 km/h), minimal to minor threat to life and property northern part of Cagayan (Santa Ana, Gonzaga, Lal-lo, Santa Teresita, Camalaniugan, Aparri, Buguey, Gattaran, Baggao, Santa Praxedes, Claveria, Sanchez-Mira, Pamplona, Ballesteros, Abulug, Allacapan, Lasam) including Babuyan Islands northern part of Ilocos Norte (Pagudpud, Adams, Bangui, Vintar, Burgos, Bacarra, Pasuquin, Carasi, Dumalneg) northern part of Apayao (Calanasan, Luna, Santa Marcela, Flora, Pudtol) Rosal’s periphery or outer bands will also bring strong to gale-force gusts to these areas: Friday, October 23 most of Luzon and Visayas, Zamboanga Peninsula, Misamis Occidental, Basilan, Tawi-Tawi, Davao Occidental, Davao Oriental Saturday, October 24 Batanes, Babuyan Islands, Ilocos Norte, Aurora, northern Quezon, Polillo Islands, Bicol, Romblon, Capiz, Iloilo, Negros Occidental Sunday, October 25 Batanes, Babuyan Islands Conditions have begun to improve in seaboards affected by the typhoon, but travel remains dangerous, especially in the country’s northernmost provinces. Up to very rough or high seas (travel is risky for all vessels) Northern seaboard of Batanes – waves up to 7 meters high Remaining seaboards of Batanes – waves up to 6 meters high Seaboards of Babuyan Islands – waves up to 5.5 meters high Seaboard of Ilocos Norte; northern seaboard of mainland Cagayan – waves up to 5 meters high Seaboards of Isabela and northern Ilocos Sur; remaining seaboard of mainland Cagayan – waves up to 4.5 meters high Up to rough seas (small vessels should not venture out to sea) Seaboards of northern La Union and northern Aurora; remaining seaboard of Ilocos Sur; northern and eastern seaboards of Catanduanes; northeastern seaboards of Northern Samar and Eastern Samar; western seaboard of Pangasinan – waves up to 4 meters high Eastern seaboards of Albay and Sorsogon; northern seaboards of Camarine Norte, Camarines Sur, and Northern Samar; northern and eastern seaboards of Polillo Islands; eastern seaboard of Eastern Samar – waves up to 3.5 meters high Seaboard of Zambales; eastern seaboards of Dinagat Islands and Siargao-Bucas Grande Islands; northern seaboard of Kalayaan Islands – waves up to 3 meters high Up to moderate to rough seas (small vessels should take precautionary measures or avoid sailing, if possible) Seaboard of Surigao del Sur; western seaboards of Bataan and Lubang Islands; remaining seaboards of La Union and Pangasinan – waves up to 2.5 meters high Western seaboards of Batangas, Cavite, Occidental Mindoro, and Palawan including Calamian Islands; eastern seaboard of Davao Oriental; remaining seaboards of Lubang and Kalayaan Islands – waves up to 2 meters high ALSO ON RAPPLER Part 1: New candidates in the running to be Marcos’ 2nd SC justice | Part 2: Old-timer bets in the running to be Marcos’ 2nd SC justice Red flags in 2027 agri budget: Coordinates at sea, ‘overpriced’ infra projects Wesley So tops 2026 US Chess Championship, bags P3.55 million After Rosal’s exit from PAR, it may weaken into a severe tropical storm by Sunday morning, October 25. Rosal, which entered PAR on Tuesday, October 20, is the Philippines’ 18th tropical cyclone for 2026, and the first for October. PAGASA earlier estimated the country may have one or two tropical cyclones during the month. The Philippines is currently in a transition period to the northeast monsoon or amihan, following the end of the southwest monsoon or habagat , which was announced last October 5. The northeast monsoon typically brings surges of cold temperatures, but the upcoming amihan period could be warmer as the existing strong El Niño in the tropical Pacific Ocean is predicted to become very strong in the fourth quarter of 2026. – Rappler.com

title: Palau launches updated National Nutrition Guidelines during World Food Day celebration
body: By: L.N. Reklai KOROR, Palau (Oct. 16, 2026) — Palau launched its updated National Nutrition Guidelines on Oct. 16 during the country’s World Food Day celebration at the Bureau of Agriculture in Ngchesar, promoting healthier eating habits and helping communities prevent noncommunicable diseases. Students visiting different booths during the World Food Day learning about proper nutrition, Oct. 16, 2026. The launch supports the goals of World Food Day, observed annually to raise awareness about hunger, malnutrition and poverty, while promoting sustainable and resilient food systems that can provide safe, diverse and nutritious food for everyone. This year’s theme, “Innovate today. Nourish tomorrow,” highlights the importance of combining innovation, including data and technology, with traditional knowledge to improve food security and nutrition while protecting the planet. Palau Community College CRE Extension program teachers and students showcasing healthy agricultural products at World Food Day, Oct. 16. Verna Kyota, diabetes coordinator under the Ministry of Health and Human Services’ Bureau of Public Health, said the updated guidelines are intended to help people make healthier food choices and reduce their risk of noncommunicable diseases. “It’s a guideline for community people, those who want to lead healthy lives and prevent non-communicable diseases,” Kyota said. The guidelines are designed for the general population and can also be used in community health programs. Kyota said one example is the use of the guidelines by recipients of Non-Communicable Disease grants to guide their programs and promote healthier lifestyles. Nutrition guidance designed for Palau The National Nutrition Guidelines follow the principles of a healthy food group guide but are tailored to Palau’s food supply and local eating habits. Instead of the familiar food pyramid, the guidelines use a taro leaf to illustrate healthy food portions, reflecting a familiar local plant while providing practical guidance on balanced eating. The guidelines also emphasize understanding food labels so consumers can make more informed decisions when purchasing packaged foods. Key areas include reading nutrition facts, checking serving sizes and understanding the number of servings in a package or container. By providing practical information about balanced diets and food choices, the guidelines aim to help individuals and communities improve their health through everyday decisions. Guidelines for children are in development The government is also developing age-specific nutrition guidance to support children’s health. Kyota said a separate set of nutrition guidelines for school-age children, from ages 5 to 18, is being finalized, with a launch expected by the end of this year. Work is also underway on nutrition guidelines for children from birth to age 4, which officials hope to launch next year. For the school-age guidelines, the initial focus will be on public schools. Kyota said the program will include training school cooks to apply the nutrition recommendations when preparing meals for students. “Then after that, we hope to push it to private schools,” Kyota added. The planned school-based effort would extend nutrition education beyond individual households and help schools reinforce healthy eating habits among children. World Food Day: Building healthier and more sustainable food systems World Food Day promotes awareness and action on hunger, malnutrition and food insecurity, while encouraging communities to help build food systems that are sustainable and resilient. People can support these goals by buying food from local farmers and cooperatives, reducing food waste through meal planning and proper food storage, sharing information about balanced diets and sustainable agriculture, and supporting food banks and other organizations assisting people facing food insecurity. Palau’s updated National Nutrition Guidelines contribute to these efforts by providing locally relevant information to help people understand nutrition, make healthier food choices and prevent diet-related diseases. The post Palau launches updated National Nutrition Guidelines during World Food Day celebration appeared first on Island Times News .

title: Analysis: Ukraine’s Starshield access is still crippled, and no one is taking the blame
body:
Elon Musk, the CEO of Tesla, SpaceX, and X, attends a press briefing held by U.S. President Donald Trump in Washington, D.C., U.S., on Sept. 29, 2026. (Finn Gomez / Getty Images)
Eleven days after Ukraine's Starshield terminals started mysteriously malfunctioning, there is still nobody in Washington who wants to take responsibility, while Trump administration officials continue pointing fingers firmly at SpaceX CEO Elon Musk.
The Wall Street Journal reported on Oct. 23 that U.S. President Donald Trump had ordered Musk on Oct. 21 to lift the restrictions on Ukraine's Starshield terminals, claiming Trump was "frustrated the system's speeds remained capped at around 100 miles an hour", another indication that the SpaceX CEO has far more control over the military version of the Starlink satellite internet service than previously believed.
In remarks to reporters, Trump refused to confirm or deny ordering Musk to restore Ukraine's service, but claimed Musk had made the change. "Whether I called or whether somebody else called, doesn’t make any difference," Trump said.
"The bottom line, he put it back," he said.
Ukraine's Starshield terminals were still experiencing severe problems on Oct. 23, multiple Ukrainian officials told the Kyiv Independent, raising questions as to whether the U.S. government is actually in control of a piece of vital national security infrastructure, or whether, as multiple American government officials have claimed, control ultimately rests with Musk and SpaceX.
"Overall, there's no change anywhere ," a senior Ukrainian official told the Kyiv Independent, when asked about whether Trump's intervention with Musk had solved the problems with Starshield.
"Starshield still doesn't work," a Ukrainian intelligence official confirmed to the Kyiv Independent. According to multiple military sources, the unpredictable "speed limit" that caps a terminal's speed at 160 kph — and in many cases, at much slower speeds — is still in place, severely hampering Ukrainian drone operations.
Ukraine uses Starshield terminals to control interceptor drones that counter Russia's jet-powered Geran drones, which Moscow has been using as part of a renewed terror-bombing campaign aimed at Ukrainian civilians and civilian infrastructure.
They are also used to control middle-range strike and logistics drones that are crucial for day-to-day operations on the front line. Despite popular misconceptions, they play no part in Ukraine's deep-strike campaign against Russian oil refineries.
"As of this morning, instances of connectivity loss at speeds of 161 km/h are still being observed. There is currently no confirmation that these restrictions have been lifted," a source in the Ukrainian Defense Ministry told the Kyiv Independent on Oct. 23.
In an interview with Fox News on Oct. 21, President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed he had been communicating with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio to try to fix the issues. "Regarding Starlink and Starshield: they are still restricted, but the secretary of state told me that he will work with his team to unblock this issue," Zelensky said.
Despite Ukrainian and U.S. officials apparently engaging in discussions to resolve the disruption to Ukrainian communications, nobody publicly has taken credit — or blame — for making or implementing the decision, which is not only politically "toxic " but also could have severe negative commercial implications for SpaceX, the operator of Starshield and Starlink.
Reporting in The Telegraph and the Wall Street Journal placed blame squarely on Musk's shoulders. Citing four sources familiar with the events, the Telegraph was the first to report that Musk was ultimately responsible, claiming Musk suggested restricting Ukrainian Starshield terminals to Trump, who "agreed" with the SpaceX CEO's suggestion.
Citing "U.S. officials and people familiar with the matter," the Wall Street Journal also reported that Musk ordered the slowdown, potentially after discussing it with Trump. But after the disruption became public, the White House refused a coordinated messaging strategy — leading to various figures in Washington pointing fingers at each other, as the political toxicity and potential legal consequences of helping Russia kill Ukrainian civilians by hobbling Ukrainian defenses became clear.
Musk himself attempted to shift responsibility to the Pentagon and the Trump administration for the slowdown, in a carefully crafted reply to former Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov in which he didn't explicitly rule out his involvement in the affair. "Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government," Musk said. "Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS."
Reuters reported that the order to restrict Starshield originated inside the White House and was relayed to Defense Department leaders, citing two U.S. officials and a Western official briefed on the matter.
Ukraine's embassy in Washington had attempted to get answers from both the Department of Defense and SpaceX, one Ukrainian government official told the Kyiv Independent, including high-level corporate contacts at SpaceX they had previously enjoyed a good relationship with, but were greeted with a wall of silence.
A number of sources familiar with the events previously told the Kyiv Independent they believed SpaceX and Musk were ultimately responsible for the restricting of Ukraine's Starshield, something which one source referred to as a "commercial decision."
Asked by journalists outside the White House on Oct. 19 who was responsible, Trump claimed ignorance: "I don't know who it was, but I'd like to find out," he said, appearing unconcerned about the unexplained malfunction in a critical piece of American national security infrastructure.
Other senior figures in the administration also denied responsibility and attempted to point the finger toward SpaceX, and ultimately, Musk.
Asked by journalists whether the administration was responsible for the problems with Starshield, U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth claimed the administration had not "pulled anything back." and indicated any change had come from SpaceX. "There are terms of service that ultimately need to be complied with, and that's where Starlink has the option to make those decisions," Hegseth said. "But nothing's changed from our view. We haven't made any directives or anything like that.
In a response to journalists, Rubio appeared to claim that SpaceX had the ability to modify Starshield's operation independently of the Pentagon, contradicting Musk’s claim that Starshield limits are controlled by the U.S. government.
"The president has nothing to do with the decisions that are made by Starlink and Starshield and by Mr. Musk. That's a private company," Rubio said in comments to journalists during his recent trip to India. "We don't control what a private company… how they decide their product can be used," he said.
Earlier in the week, Rubio inaccurately claimed that Ukraine had never had access to Starshield. "Starshield is a defense product, a military product," Rubio said. "It's not, at this moment, available to Ukraine, and that's under conversation," he said. "I know Ukraine wants access to Starshield. They do not have Starshield now," Rubio continued.
Despite Rubio's claims, Ukraine has operated Starshield since 2024, as contemporary reporting made clear. Ukraine was initially given access to 500 Starshield terminals under a pilot program, Bloomberg reported in 2024. By the end of 2024, two separate Pentagon contracts with SpaceX were providing 3,000 terminals of the militarized version of SpaceX's Starlink satellite internet system.
American ambassador to NATO Matt Whitaker also attempted to shift the blame toward SpaceX and away from the administration. "They are a private company," Whitaker said in an interview with Fox News on Oct. 21. "Obviously they have terms of use that are applied to all of their customers, including the Ukrainians. I think it is more of a dispute along those lines than anybody in this administration trying to change how Starshield or Starlink is used," he said .
Rushton is a British journalist and security and foreign policy analyst based in Kyiv. He has covered Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine since February 2022, writing about every aspect of the conflict. His work has appeared in Yahoo News, New Lines Magazine, and The Telegraph, amongst others.

title: Bank of Russia has decided to keep its key rate at 14%
body:
MOSCOW, October 23. /TASS/. The Bank of Russia has decided to keep its key rate at 14%, as current price pressure remains elevated, according to a press release from the regulator.
"On 23 October 2026, the Bank of Russia Board of Directors decided to keep the key rate at 14.00% per annum. The economy as a whole is growing at a moderate pace in 2026 H2. Current price pressures remain elevated. Inflation expectations stay high. According to the Bank of Russia’s estimates, underlying price growth has not yet decreased and remains in the range of 5-6% in annualized terms, primarily due to the impact of a temporary reduction in production capacities in certain sectors. This requires aggregate demand to grow moderately for underlying inflation to resume its decline," the regulator said.
The Bank of Russia notes that it will make further decisions on the key rate depending on the dynamics of inflation and inflation expectations, as well as the analysis of risks posed by domestic and external conditions. According to the Central Bank, the current seasonally adjusted price growth averaged 8.0% in annualized terms compared to 4.8% in 2026 Q2. The similar indicator of core inflation rose to 6.2% from 4.5% in 2026 Q2. Price dynamics were still affected by volatile components, primarily motor fuel. As of 19 October 2026, annual inflation stood at 6.8% and is expected to come in at 7.1-7.6% as of the end of 2026
"High inflation expectations impede a slowdown in inflation. Despite a slight decrease in the expectations of households and businesses in October, they have generally remained near two-year highs in recent months. Expectations of financial market participants and analysts have increased," the regulator added.
The Bank of Russia noted that according to high-frequency data, the economy is growing at a moderate pace in 2026 H2.
"Business sentiment improved somewhat in October compared to low levels of the previous months. Growth in consumer demand is slowing but remains elevated. Investment activity continues to recover compared to the levels of early 2026," the regulator said.

title: Ukraine says Starlink still restricted after Trump says limits lifted
body: Ukraine is still recording issues with the Starlink network, sources within the defence ministry say, after Donald Trump said limits on the satellite uplink had been reversed by Elon Musk. The sources told the BBC that instances of drones experiencing connection loss at speeds of 161km/h (100mph) were being recorded, hampering military operations. The US president had denied instructing the tech billionaire to restrict connectivity to Starlink’s military-grade counterpart, Starshield, before saying on Thursday that Musk had “put it back”. Musk previously said he was not behind the slowdown, which affected Ukraine’s ability to use attack drones and co-ordinate defensive operations. The Ukrainian defence ministry sources said the military was constantly monitoring the performance of both the Starlink and Starshield networks. They added that there was “currently no confirmation that these restrictions have been lifted”. Last week, Kyiv said uplink speeds to the low Earth orbit satellites had been restricted, affecting the speed at which drones could travel. Any drone travelling faster than 100mph lost its connection, officials said. Shortly after, Musk said that Starshield, which Ukraine uses for some of its operation, was controlled by the US military and suggested that the Pentagon could be behind the issues. The White House has since repeatedly denied deliberately placing limits on the network in Ukraine. Trump refused to say whether he had called Musk to ask him to liftrestrictions to the service when asked about reports to that end on Thursday, but said: “Bottom line, he put it back.” Ukraine uses both the civilian service Starlink and the more secure Starshield, depending on what communications are needed. The networks use 10,000 satellites to provide connectivity, particularly in remote areas and on the battlefield. Starshield allows Ukrainian drone operators to see targets in real time, as well as operate interceptor drones. Russia is not authorised to use Starlink, so when Ukraine sends long-range missiles deep into Russia to hit oil refineries, the network does not work. Ukrainian reports of a slowdown to the service came during a tense diplomatic row between Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky about Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil infrastructure. Faced with midterm elections next month, Trump has waived some sanctions on Russia and agreed a deal to import Russian diesel for the US market – a move criticised by Ukraine and its European allies. Trump said the strikes on Russian oil refineries, which Kyiv says are crucial to stemming the main revenue source for Moscow’s war effort, have pushed global prices higher. While the attacks have had an impact on global fuel prices, rises seen this year have primarily been due to the Iran war. Zelensky said the US had also threatened to withdraw intelligence sharing if the strikes did not stop, something Trump later denied. The row prompted a war of words between the two world leaders, with Trump suggesting it was time for Ukraine to get a new president and Zelensky implying Trump was not a real leader. Earlier on Thursday – before Trump’s comments – Zelensky had said the speed of the system had still not been restored fully. “I am waiting to hear from US Secretary of State [Marco] Rubio. He promised to get back to me with information within 48 hours or so.” The Wall Street Journal reported that Trump had told Musk that he was frustrated the Starlink system’s speeds were still capped, and that the system was working closer to normal following that conversation.

title: Sudanese organization warns WFP aid cuts will heighten hunger risk
body: The General Coordination of Displaced Persons and Refugee Camps in Sudan has warned that funding-driven cuts to World Food Programme (WFP) assistance in the country will exacerbate the risk of hunger and leave vulnerable communities increasingly exposed to food insecurity. Adam Rijal, the official spokesperson for the organization, told Radio Tamazuj that reductions in humanitarian assistance threatened the lives of hundreds of thousands of people who rely on aid for their basic food needs. “The decision comes at a time when civilians are grappling with the consequences of war, displacement and deteriorating livelihoods, amid rising risks of hunger and malnutrition,” he said, warning that cuts to assistance amounted to a humanitarian threat. The WFP’s decision comes amid mounting pressure on food security driven by conflict, displacement, drought and climate-related disruptions that have affected agricultural production. Rijal cautioned against attributing these conditions to the El Niño phenomenon without first establishing the relevant timeframe for its possible occurrence and consulting experts in the field. He said reducing assistance under such circumstances would mean more than simply cutting food rations. Adding that it could deprive displaced families of essential meals and force them to adopt harmful coping strategies, including withdrawing children from school, selling their remaining possessions, or reducing the number and size of daily meals. “The most vulnerable groups bear the heaviest burden, particularly women, children, older people and persons with disabilities,” Rijal stated. Rijal called on donor countries and international organizations to urgently close the funding gap to ensure the continuity of food assistance and its delivery to those in need. He also urged an expansion of the humanitarian response and stronger nutrition and food security programmes, prioritizing the areas worst affected by the crisis. In addition, Rijal called for efforts to end the war, beginning with a humanitarian truce that would ensure the uninterrupted flow of aid and food to affected communities. The post Sudanese organization warns WFP aid cuts will heighten hunger risk appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Court rejects Machar’s request to play videos
body: The special court hearing the trial of former First Vice President Dr. Riek Machar and seven co-accused on Friday dismissed Machar’s application to play video footage during the proceedings, ruling that the request is premature. Machar, a 74-year-old opposition leader, had sought permission to play videos featuring senior government officials to support his arguments in the ongoing trial. Presiding Judge Dr. James Alala Deng dismissed the application during the 123rd session of the trial, saying the proceedings had not yet reached the stage at which the proposed video evidence could be considered. “The court dismissed the application as premature as proceedings had not yet reached the stage at which the proposed video evidence could be considered,” Deng said. Deng said Machar should first focus on understanding and responding to the specific offences he is accused of committing. He maintained that evidence would be considered at the appropriate stage of the proceedings, in accordance with established procedures. Deng reiterated that the court had not yet framed the charges, making the application premature. “The evidence would be considered at the appropriate stage of the proceedings and that the accused would have an opportunity to respond in accordance with the applicable procedures,” he said. Deng urged Machar to concentrate on the charges against him and refrain from commenting on previous court decisions or matters unrelated to the issues currently before the court. He warned against turning the proceedings into a political rally, emphasising that all accused persons should be treated equally before the court and are expected to comply with its rules. Investigations into threats Deng said an investigation into threats against Machar, his defence team and his co-accused had been completed. He said the matter would be referred to the relevant authorities, including the attorney general and the police. Lead prosecutor Ajo Ony’Ohisa Igele opposed the application, arguing that it is premature and that the fifth accused should focus on responding to the charges against him rather than introducing video footage at this stage of the proceedings. Defence’s response Defence counsel Dr. Geri Raymond Legge challenged the prosecution’s position, arguing that the court should consider the application. He denied allegations that the defence had turned the proceedings into a political rally and maintained that the videos are intended to bring the matter to the attention of the wider public. The court adjourned the proceedings to October 26, 2026, when the examination of the fifth accused is expected to continue. The post Court rejects Machar’s request to play videos appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Kremlin says trilateral negotiations planned for November in Abu Dhabi
body:
Trilateral negotiations regarding a peaceful settlement are planned to take place in Abu Dhabi during the first half of November, stated Dmitry Peskov, spokesperson for Vladimir Putin.
"Nothing can be ruled out a priori, but these negotiations—the ones in Abu Dhabi, scheduled for the first half of November—will take place in a trilateral format," Peskov told reporters on Friday, according to Russian media.
He was responding to a question about whether the talks could expand to a quadrilateral format, given the plans to discuss the architecture of European security.
According to the spokesperson, Putin had previously outlined the subject of the negotiations: security issues for Russia and Ukraine following a transition toward a peaceful settlement.
"This is a crucial component of the transition to a peaceful settlement. Without it, a comprehensive solution is impossible," Peskov said.
"It is difficult to say how or in what format future discussions will take place. Clearly, it would be impossible to discuss the architecture of European security without other participants, but the initial discussion will indeed take place in a trilateral format," he emphasized.
In late September, The Atlantic, citing a member of the Ukrainian negotiating team, reported that a meeting between representatives of Ukraine, the United States, and Russia could be organized in Abu Dhabi (UAE) in October. According to the source, the negotiators intended to discuss a limited truce. "It would commit each side to refrain from striking the other’s energy infrastructure, specifically power plants, oil refineries, and similar facilities," the report says.
Furthermore, it was expected that a separate agreement, brokered by the Egyptian government, would stipulate that Russia and Ukraine would not strike each other’s cargo vessels in the Black Sea, particularly those transporting grain to markets in the Middle East and Africa.

title: One Dead, Three Missing From Ship in ‘Distress’ in Black Sea
body:
Romania launched a rescue operation on Friday after a ship sent a distress signal, the latest in a spate of incidents in the Black Sea, where suspected Russian drones have hit several vessels off Romania and Bulgaria.
No cause was given straight away for the emergency but Romanian fighter jets shot down two Russian drones over the Black Sea last weekend and NATO said this week it was deploying additional planes and radar systems because of the attacks on shipping.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The Khoryv cargo ship sent a distress signal around 10:00 am (0700 GMT), when it was 13 nautical miles across from the Romanian port of Constanta. Romanian authorities say its crew was comprised of 10 Ukrainian and three Azerbaijani nationals.
“Rescue vessels have managed to recover nine people alive, and one body from the water,” the Romanian Naval Authority said in a press release, adding that three crew were missing.
The Khoryv cargo ship is Comoros-registered, according to the specialised site VesselFinder.com.
The naval authority said it was “in distress outside Romanian territorial waters”.
“Due to adverse weather conditions and poor visibility, an aerial rescue operation by helicopter is not possible,” said the authority.
Drones have struck merchant vessels in the Black Sea off Romania and Bulgaria in the last three weeks in the latest spillover from Russia’s war on Ukraine.
Seven crew went missing on October 15 off Romania’s coast as the Wine Trader, a chemical tanker, caught fire after a drone attack, according to President Nicusor Dan, who called for the “unacceptable” attacks to stop.
Romania has asked NATO for more equipment.
On Thursday, following a meeting Romania’s Supreme Council for National Defence, the presidency said that “threats to freedom of navigation and critical infrastructure have increased significantly”.
The NATO country bordering Ukraine is looking into “accelerated development of maritime surveillance capabilities, mine countermeasures and effective countermeasures against drones that intrude unauthorised into national airspace and territorial waters”.
NATO said Tuesday it was deploying additional planes, drones and radar systems to the Black Sea because of the attacks on ships.

title: Michael Carrick does not have support of all Man United players but manager alone can't be held responsible
body: AFC Bournemouth visit Old Trafford on Sunday buoyed by a European win against seven-time continental champions AC Milan. Bournemouth, who were a third-tier club with average crowds of 5,500 the last time Milan won the Champions League in 2007, drew 4-4 at Old Trafford last season and won 3-0 in two visits before that. They will meet a United team reeling from a dreadful start to the season, the low point of which was Wednesday’s 4-1 Champions League hammering by Milan’s tiny neighbours, Como. Michael Carrick’s United side have not won in seven games and while the manager is set to be in charge against Bournemouth, his position is perilous. Carrick has long needed wins but they have not come. In the Premier League, United are 13th after seven matches and while Bournemouth are on a high, they too have won only one league game. The addition of European football isn’t helping the domestic form of either side and two United players have blown up the dressing room with their post-match comments after the last two European defeats, in Madrid and now Como . Lisandro Martinez , who wants a new contract but has made no headway towards getting one, was critical of the club’s technical director Jason Wilcox among others after the defeat to Atletico Madrid, while captain Bruno Fernandes was critical of his boss Carrick and his staff after being substituted in Como. The Portuguese, who had done no interviews since August, offered to speak to the media and said: “It’s the decision of the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball. But sometimes when you give the ball too much to these teams, they get confidence.” Asked if Carrick got his tactics wrong, Fernandes added: “That’s on the manager and staff to see it, not me.” This is an affront to the name of Manchester United. — Andy Mitten (@AndyMitten) October 21, 2026 Criticism 'for the dressing room' Fernandes was correct in what he said. Whether he should have said it publicly is another issue. United looked passive, not just against Como but in too many games this season. United played to Como’s style and strengths and the team have struggled to press all season. Como’s model of extreme possession with penetration by playing through opponents diagonally was a recipe for disaster for United. Martinez struck a chord with fans, while Fernandes, despite being the club’s best player and captain, saw his actions questioned. “You do not criticise your manager in public if you are the captain because no good can come from that,” one former Premier League captain told The National . “This is stuff for the dressing room. As captain, if you smell things are changing on the pitch then you change things. If what the manager wants you to do isn’t working, you can feel it as a player. So you adjust. It’s what leaders do.” Fernandes normally chooses his words carefully since he is aware of the global impact of them. But these criticism were meant to make headlines. As a result, it doesn’t look like all United players are with the manager Carrick right now. Onus on players as well Yet in a rain-lashed Como on Wednesday night, Carrick was right to say that those players should be playing for Manchester United, not him. When the unity goes, players get defensive and lash out. They blame anyone but themselves. United fans will get behind their team on Sunday. The Stretford End want their players to maintain the standards expected at Manchester United and will make that clear. This isn’t the weight of history crashing on the shoulders of current players once again. Yet, it is another reminder of how things were once great and now they are not. It’s not the fault of those who wear the red shirt in 2026 that they are not as good as legends of yore who were some of the best in the English league and beyond. It's just a reminder that certain standards are expected and the players fell short of the expected levels in Wednesday’s atrocious defeat in Italy. "I 100% take responsibility for the overall team and the performance. That's where it stops. It stops with me." Michael Carrick reacts to Manchester United's "unacceptable" display against Como. 🎙️ @LiamMacdevitt 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/agXYEERLGq — Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) October 21, 2026 United's leaders want it to work for Carrick and there is little appetite for yet another managerial change. But it’s whether the club have the faith that Carrick can turn fortunes around. This run cannot continue and the club are privately weighing up other managerial options, just as they did before Carrick got the job permanently after the excellent work he did in guiding his team into the Champions League. Sadly, this is the time of year that United managers lose their jobs. Erik ten Hag was dismissed in October 2024, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer in November 2021, Jose Mourinho in December 2018. Sir Alex Ferguson took control of United 40 years ago in November 1986. Carrick has remained calm amid the chaos, but he is struggling to get a tune from the very same players who couldn’t stop winning under him last season. To make matters worse, United’s injuries are extensive, there is no recognised centre forward and the fixture list is unrelenting. Manchester United’s problems go well beyond the first team manager. The club operate under the cloud of a vast and continuing debt placed on it when the Glazer family took over in a controversial and highly leveraged takeover in 2005. Fans have consistently protested this, even when the team are winning. But the problems always come into sharper focus when United are on a losing streak, like they are on now.

title: Five Israelis wounded and two suspected Palestinian attackers killed in West Bank shooting
body: Five Israelis have been wounded and two suspected Palestinian attackers killed by Israeli security forces following a shooting in the occupied West Bank, Israeli officials say. Footage verified by the BBC shows an intense gun battle between soldiers and the gunmen, at a military checkpoint at the entrance to the city of Hebron. In response, Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he had ordered the military to prepare for a full lockdown of the West Bank, beginning later on Friday. The attack comes at a time of high tensions, with extremist Jewish settlers targeting Palestinians during the annual olive harvest, and Israel’s general election taking place in four days time. The two injured Israelis are in critical condition, according to Israel’s ambulance service. The Israeli military said it had found a large quantity of ammunition in the attackers’ vehicle. The military said they believe the gunmen had intended to carry out a much larger attack on the nearby Route 35, but ran into the checkpoint – so instead decided to open fire there. Unverified CCTV footage shows two gunmen exit a car armed with what appears to be a handgun and an assault rifle and start firing on soldiers at the checkpoint, before coming under return fire. The Israeli military said it had begun raids on the homes of the attackers, while far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich said he had ordered the demolition of several Palestinian buildings adjacent to the site of the attack. It is common practice for Israeli forces to demolish the homes of Palestinians who are suspected of carrying out attacks on Israelis. Netanyahu, who has built his election campaign on promising security for Israelis, said that his Likud party would cancel campaign events for the morning. The West Bank was already expected to be placed under lockdown for the election on Monday and Tuesday, according to Israeli media. At least 96 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli forces or settlers in the West Bank since the start of the year, according to the UN. Four Israelis, both security forces and civilians, have been killed by Palestinians there over the same period, the UN says.

title: INEC: Results with discrepancies won’t be uploaded on IREV
body: Dr. Lawrence Bayode, Director, ICT at the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), has promised Nigerians that results with discrepancies will not be uploaded to the INEC Result Viewing Portal. Speaking in Abuja when an organisation, RiseNetworks, launched the AI4Election Hackathon initiative, Bayode said any result that does not tally with results on the BVAS would not be uploaded on IREV. He said the commission would deploy AI technology that uses intelligence documents processing to digitise polling unit results sheet as well as perform consistency check. He said the commission was exploring practical application of AI in areas such as voters information services, electoral data management operational efficiency and detection of misinformation. Nigerians need explanations on N10bn Ebola response fund, Atiku tells FG Family: Fasoranti to be buried December 17 The electoral official said what the system does is to perform a consistency check between the entered figure on the BVAS and the scanned results (EC8) before transmission is allowed. Bayode said it was important to ensure that the results on the IREV were the ones that emanated from the polling units. “It will help to improve accuracy, reduce human error and strengthen transparency. This initiative demonstrates that for INEC, AI is not merely a subject for discussion. We are moving from conversation to practical application while maintaining human oversight, accountability, appropriate safeguards,” he said. Bayode noted that AI has a major role to play in the election, arguing that what needs to be done is to look at how it would be used without compromising the integrity, transparency and credibility. He said the commission recognizes that Artificial Intelligence represents significant opportunities to improve electoral administration. He revealed that the commission had taken deliberate steps towards responsible AI adoption, including the establishment of an Artificial Intelligence division within the ICT department. “AI elections hackathon presents an opportunity to let the creativity of young Nigerians in addressing real electoral challenges, welcome innovations that can improve voters innovation, expand accessibility for persons with disability, bridge language barriers, strengthen information integrity and make electoral information more accessible to citizens.” “On September 25, 2025, the commission adopted the policy on election technology appreciation and deployment. This policy provide a framework to streamline the development, appreciation and deployment of election technology by the commission. In this policy, the commission captured the use of AI in elections. “Recently, when the commission decided to employ the use of AI, it went further to go beyond this policy that was put in place in 2025 to develop a framework that will guide the responsible deployment of AI that is still work in progress,” he said. On her part, Chief Executive of Rise Networks, Dr. Toyosi Akerele-Ogunisi, said major stakeholders such as the INEC, META, Google, Microsoft, amongst others joined forces to launch the #AI4Elections Hackathon ahead of Nigeria’s 2027 Elections. She said the initiative was designed to invite eligible Nigerians to apply for the #AI4Elections Hackathon, a national, multidisciplinary and nonpartisan programme designed to bring together Nigeria’s technology ecosystem, electoral experts, researchers, universities, developers, innovators and civil society to develop and reward responsible AI projects that can support electoral processes in 2027 and beyond. “The programme which will connect innovators, researchers, civil society and electoral stakeholders is structured around three interconnected pillars: the #AI4Elections Hackathon, where participants design, develop and demonstrate solutions to electoral challenges; #AI4Elections Development Hub, which will support the further testing, refinement and development of promising solutions; and the #AI4Elections Community of Practice, which will connect participants, researchers, mentors, institutions and other stakeholders for continued learning, collaboration and knowledge-sharing beyond the Hackathon,” she said. She said the programme was a response to the growing influence of artificial intelligence on information production, digital communications and civic participation, as well as emerging challenges including synthetic media, misinformation, privacy risks, cybersecurity threats and the manipulation of information environments.

title: Russian Central Bank Holds Key Interest Rate Steady
body:
Russia’s Central Bank decided to hold its key interest rate at 14% during its latest meeting on Friday, weighing inflation risks against the need to lower currently high borrowing costs for businesses and consumers as the Kremlin prioritizes spending on the war against Ukraine.
The Central Bank reported that annual inflation hit 6.8% earlier in the week. Policymakers slightly increased their full-year inflation forecast, now at 7.1% to 7.6%, but they still expect price growth to fall toward the 4% target next year.
Inflation expectations remain high, the Central Bank said, though officials have argued that some of the more recent price increases are rooted in one-time factors, like Ukraine’s strikes on Russian oil refineries raising the cost of gasoline and diesel.
“Underlying price growth has not yet decreased… primarily due to the impact of a temporary reduction in production capacities in certain sectors,” it said in a press release, while also alluding to inflation risks associated with the war in Iran and its impacts on global energy markets.
Policymakers also hiked the projected key rate range for next year by two percentage points, now at 12.5 to 13.5%.
The rate hold, which analysts widely expected, comes as spending on the war in Ukraine continues to strain the Russian government’s finances, while Ukrainian drone and missile attacks on energy infrastructure and commercial sites in recent months have raised the cost of some goods and services.
Despite its more bearish outlook on inflation, the Central Bank raised its forecast for economic growth this year, with GDP now expected to come in at 0.5% to 1% by the end of 2026, according to Friday’s press release.
Sofia Donets, chief economist at T-Investments, said policymakers appeared to leave room for another rate cut this year, “ especially since the signal in the press release remained neutral with no explicit guidance on the future direction.”
Inflation is a growing concern across the globe as the war in Iran drives up the price of oil, which rose above $116 per barrel for the first time since May on Friday. For Russia, Ukrainian attacks against oil refineries have compounded the problem since it can sometimes take up to several months to repair the complex facilities.
“The speed at which [production] capacity is restored is itself an element of uncertainty,” Central Bank Governor Elvira Nabiullina said at a press conference later on Friday.
“Another factor of uncertainty is the full range of secondary effects — namely, how this will feed into prices across a broad spectrum of goods and impact inflation expectations,” she said.
A long period of high borrowing costs has weighed down economic growth in Russia, leaving business leaders pressing for a lower key interest rate to stimulate investment. But the Central Bank has so far prioritized keeping price growth subdued.
“There were individual opinions in favor of raising the rate, but only one option was discussed in detail: keeping the rate unchanged,” Nabiullina said of the key rate decision on Friday.
The Central Bank ’s next rate meeting takes place on Dec. 18.

title: Russia’s tax service runs on two key data centers. Drones went after one of them overnight, along with a chemical plant that supplies explosives makers
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Drones attacked a Russian tax-service data center overnight on 23 October, Ukrainian monitoring channel Exilenova+ reported . A chemical plant in the Urals was also attacked, and a fire broke out near a Russian bomber base by late morning. Russian officials admitted injuries and damage but blamed falling debris. Ukraine has not commented. Ukraine's long-range drones have widened their target list from Russian refineries to the servers and chemicals that keep Russia's state and war industry running. The tax service's data center in Gorodets The target in Gorodets, Nizhny Novgorod Oblast, is one of the Federal Tax Service's two key data centers, which work as a geographically distributed pair. It stores and processes state registers, including tax databases, Exilenova+ said. The extent of the damage is unconfirmed. The site lies about 785 km from Ukraine's northern border in a straight line. The moment of impact at Russia’s Federal Tax Service data center in Gorodets last night. pic.twitter.com/PftC6keRpY — Exilenova+ (@Exilenova_plus) October 23, 2026 Eyewitness footage shows a blast and fire in the area of the data center, which serves both the tax service and the Finance Ministry, Russian Telegram channel Astra found . The center opened in 2015. Mikhail Mishustin, then head of the tax service and now Russia's prime minister, attended the launch. Nizhny Novgorod Governor Gleb Nikitin claimed air defenses repelled 19 drones. Falling debris injured three people in the Gorodets district and damaged several homes, an educational facility, and an infrastructure facility, he said, and local schools switched to remote learning. A Pantsir air defense missile hit a house, Exilenova+ claimed , though officials recorded it as a drone hit. Ukrainian strikes inside Russia on Gorodets, Berezniki, and Voronezh, with distances from Ukraine, 23 October 2026. Map: Euromaidan Press/Datawrapper This month, drones already hit three Yandex data centers and a VK data center near St. Petersburg . A chemical plant behind Russia's gunpowder In Berezniki, Perm Krai, smoke rose over Uralchem's Azot plant as air defenses fired, Astra reported . The regional security ministry announced a drone attack at about 06:00, and authorities closed the airspace within 50 km of the city. Ukraine's long-range Liutyi drones visited Berezniki, Exilenova+ wrote. Our old friends, the Liutyi drones, paid Berezniki a visit today. Haven’t seen them in a while. pic.twitter.com/NXuhIJ3xpm — Exilenova+ (@Exilenova_plus) October 23, 2026 The attack on Azot was continuing in the morning, the channel wrote , adding that the plant covers about 140 hectares with some 90 production buildings. It makes ammonia, nitric acid, ammonium and potassium nitrate, and urea. Russian defense plants use its nitric acid to make explosives and gunpowder, including the Perm gunpowder plant, Astra said. Berezniki lies 1,500–1,600 km from Ukraine's border and the war zone. Smoke rises over Uralchem's Azot chemical plant in Berezniki, Perm Krai, after a drone attack, Russia, 23 October 2026. Photo: Exilenova+/Telegram Drones attacked Azot before, on 11 September. Earlier this year, Ukraine's Security Service hit Lukoil's refinery in the same region. Explore further Phones down, water off, a factory roof broken open: Russian-occupied Luhansk counts the damage after another night of drones Fire near a Su-34 base in Voronezh Late in the morning, Voronezh Governor Aleksandr Gusev declared a missile alert, and explosions followed in the city. Gusev later claimed air defenses downed several "jet-powered aerial targets." Debris set dry grass on fire in a suburb and damaged outbuildings and several cars, he said, adding that no one was hurt. Missile alert in several regions of the Russian Federation. Explosions have been heard in Voronezh. We are assessing the situation. pic.twitter.com/GY0NRZTo4x — Exilenova+ (@Exilenova_plus) October 23, 2026 Eyewitness footage shows fire and smoke near Baltimor military airfield, Astra found . The strike preliminarily hit the grounds of a former military aviation engineering university and a nearby parking area for military aircraft, Exilenova+ said . Fire and smoke near Baltimor military airfield in Voronezh after a Ukrainian attack, Russia, 23 October 2026. Photo: Astra/Telegram Baltimor hosts the 47th Guards Bomber Aviation Regiment, whose Su-34s Russia uses to strike Ukraine, Militarnyi reported , saying Ukraine attacked the airfield with missiles. Voronezh lies about 185 km from Ukraine's border. Smoke rose over the base after an attack on 27 May , and a fire broke out near it on 2 September . Moscow counts drones, Kyiv stays silent Russia's Defense Ministry claimed it downed 443 drones overnight over 20 Russian regions, including Nizhny Novgorod Oblast and Perm Krai, as well as Russian-occupied Crimea and two seas. Ukraine's General Staff has not reported on the strikes. A night earlier, drones reportedly hit a sanctioned weapons plant near Moscow. Russia's air defenses now have to cover state servers and Ural chemical plants as well as the airfields its bombers fly from. title: United Continues Starlink Rollout with Installations Underway on Boeing 737 MAX 8 Fleet on Guam
body: United’s Guam-based Boeing 737 MAX 8 fleet among the first of the airline’s MAX 8 aircraft to receive fast, free Starlink Wi-Fi, with installation already complete on two aircraft Airline completes transition of its Guam-based Boeing 737-800 fleet to newer 737 MAX 8 aircraft ahead of schedule Latest investment builds on United’s commitment to Guam, including a refreshed check-in lobby at Antonio B. Won Pat International Airport CHICAGO and HAGÅTÑA, Guam, October 13, 2026 – United Airlines® is continuing to rollout fast, free Starlink Wi-Fi for MileagePlus® members, with installations now underway on the airline’s Boeing 737 MAX 8 fleet. United has completed installation on two of its Guam-based MAX 8 aircraft, among the first of the airline’s MAX 8 fleet to receive Starlink. United Chief Customer Officer David Kinzelman traveled to Guam to announce the milestone today at a press conference at Antonio B. Won Pat International Airport. The addition of Starlink comes as United confirms it has completed the transition of its Guam-based fleet to newer Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft ahead of schedule, delivering a more modern onboard experience for customers traveling throughout Guam, Micronesia and the broader Pacific region. “Guam is where two of our biggest customer investments come together,” said David Kinzelman, United’s Chief Customer Officer. “We said we would replace the entire Guam fleet with MAX 8 aircraft by the end of this year, and we’ve finished early. Now those same aircraft are among the first MAX 8s in our fleet to get Starlink. Starlink is a game changer for our customers, delivering the fast, reliable connectivity they expect, and we’re proud that our Guam-based aircraft are among the first of our MAX 8s to receive it.” Bringing Starlink to Guam Starlink uses low-Earth orbit satellites to deliver fast and reliable internet connectivity, including over oceans and in remote regions that have traditionally been difficult to reach with conventional inflight Wi-Fi. The technology is particularly impactful across United’s Pacific network, where many flights operate over long stretches of open ocean and connect remote communities. United customers using Starlink can stay connected with family and friends, access information and services online, work remotely and enjoy entertainment throughout their journey, with a faster, more responsive internet experience in flight than traditional broadband services available in many parts of Micronesia. United has been rapidly expanding Starlink and expects to complete installations throughout its fleet before the end of 2027. Since launching Starlink Wi-Fi last spring, United has flown more than 36.6 million passengers on Starlink-equipped aircraft across more than 527,000 flights, powering 14.4 million devices — and Wi-Fi customer satisfaction scores on those airplanes nearly doubled during that time. Starlink is now available on about 46% of United’s daily flights. Starlink is free for MileagePlus members in every class of service and allows customers to connect multiple devices at the same time. Customers will receive a notification before their flight if it’s equipped with Starlink. Visit united.com/starlink for additional information. United Completes Guam MAX 8 Transition Ahead of Schedule United has also completed the replacement of its Guam-based Boeing 737-800 fleet with ten newer Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft, ahead of its previously announced schedule. The MAX 8 aircraft feature United’s signature interior with seatback entertainment at every seat, larger overhead bins, more extra-legroom seating, USB charging and wireless Bluetooth connectivity. The airline first unveiled its Guam-based MAX 8 fleet in March this year, with the aircraft progressively introduced on routes throughout the region. The MAX 8 aircraft now operate all United’s narrowbody flying from Guam, including service throughout Micronesia and to destinations across Asia. United’s Guam-based narrowbody fleet serves 15 destinations from Guam, including the airline’s unique Island Hopper service. United also operates extensive service between Guam and Japan and flights throughout the region. United’s Boeing 737 MAX 8s have 164 seats, including 14 United First® seats, and feature 13-inch high-definition screens in United First and 10-inch HD screens in United Economy®. The aircraft are also specially configured to support the needs of communities across Micronesia; the front rows of Economy can be converted when necessary to accommodate a medical stretcher for patients requiring medevac transportation. Investing in Guam The introduction of Starlink is the latest in a series of significant investments United has made in Guam over the past 12 months. In addition to introducing the new MAX 8 fleet, United has refreshed its check-in lobby at Antonio B. Won Pat International Airport, including new next-generation kiosks and a redesigned layout intended to create a more streamlined experience and reduce congestion for customers. Together, the investments are designed to provide a more consistent, modern experience for customers from the moment they arrive at the airport through their time onboard. United is one of the largest private employers in the region, with more than 1,000 employees throughout Guam and Micronesia, many of whom have worked for the airline for more than 30 years. As Guam’s hometown airline, United also supports numerous nonprofit organizations across the region through annual donations and hundreds of volunteer hours from local employees.
