title: Palau Develops Long-Term Plan to Maintain Palau-Japan Friendship Bridge
body: By: Laurel Marewibuel KOROR, Palau (Oct. 22, 2026) — “Reporting is very important. Recording and reporting,” said Tkakl Mekreos, chief of Road and Bridge Maintenance, as Palau develops a long-term system to maintain the Japan-Palau Friendship Bridge and other critical public infrastructure. As the bridge approaches its 25th anniversary in January 2027, Palau is working with Japan to strengthen inspections, train local staff and establish a long-term maintenance plan for roads, bridges and heavy equipment. The Japan-Palau Friendship Bridge, also known as the Koror-Babeldaob Bridge, connects Koror with Babeldaob, where the national government and much of the country’s infrastructure are located. Completed in 2000 with more than 3.2 billion yen in Japanese assistance, the bridge is a vital link for transportation and essential services. “This bridge is very important,” Mekreos said. “It carries water lines, electricity, and also communication lines.” The current bridge replaced the original Koror-Babeldaob Bridge, which collapsed in 1996. Mekreos said engineers learned from the first bridge’s failure, which was attributed to concrete failure and insufficient maintenance and inspection. “Learning from the first bridge, the engineers decided to use the extradosed bridge in a composite material,” he said. That experience is helping shape Palau’s efforts to prevent similar infrastructure problems through regular inspections, better recordkeeping and planned maintenance. Long-term plan with Japan In 2025, Palau began a technical cooperation project with the Japan International Cooperation Agency, or JICA, called “Establishment of Asset Management System of Roads, Bridges and Heavy Machineries in SIDS.” The project will continue through 2030. The initiative aims to help Palau develop a systematic way to assess the condition of public infrastructure, identify maintenance needs and plan repairs before problems become more serious. Palau is working with JICA, KEI, SPI and PCCK on the project, which also involves the Koror State Government, the Palau Public Utilities Corporation, Nauru and the Marshall Islands. A regional seminar held in June brought participants together to discuss common challenges and share practical solutions. “We have the chance to get to know each other and share our challenges, our best practices,” Mekreos said. The project includes maintenance workshops, pilot inspections and the development of systems for managing information about roads, bridges and heavy machinery. It also seeks to strengthen local technical skills and adapt Japanese infrastructure management practices to the needs of small island developing states. Mekreos said the project’s first phase identified gaps in technical knowledge and expertise. The next phase will focus on developing the management system and training local personnel to carry out inspections and maintenance work. Detailed bridge inspection planned Although the bridge receives a general inspection every year, Mekreos said a detailed inspection has not been conducted since 2002. A new detailed inspection is planned between 2026 and 2028. It will use concrete-penetrating X-ray technology to help assess the condition and structural integrity of the bridge. “Just by looking at the outside of the bridge, the bridge looks pretty good,” Mekreos said. “But pretty soon we will be using concrete penetrating X-rays to do a detailed inspection and assess the integrity of the concrete.” The inspection is intended to provide a clearer picture of the bridge’s condition beyond what can be seen from the outside. The findings can help officials determine what maintenance is needed and support decisions about how to protect the structure over the long term. Better records, climate planning The project will also establish standard operating procedures and maintenance plans, along with a geographic information system map covering roads, bridges and heavy machinery. Mekreos said Palau is working with Polaris on the mapping effort. Having reliable records of public infrastructure will help government officials identify problems, set priorities and make better-informed decisions about maintenance spending. “We will better inform our leaders,” he said. The initiative will also help Palau consider climate risks when planning infrastructure maintenance and future improvements. “With these new initiatives, we can start to incorporate climate solutions and designs to maintain our infrastructure based on climate advice,” Mekreos said. For Palau, the effort represents a practical extension of its long-standing partnership with Japan. Beyond maintaining a bridge that connects two major parts of the country, the goal is to build local expertise and establish a system that can protect public infrastructure for decades to come. Mekreos said strengthening local staff’s ability to inspect infrastructure, maintain accurate records and report findings is central to the project’s success. “Recording and reporting” will be essential to helping Palau understand the condition of its infrastructure and make timely decisions about its future. The post Palau Develops Long-Term Plan to Maintain Palau-Japan Friendship Bridge appeared first on Island Times News .

title: Russia changes world balance, making US, Europe move to dialogue — legislator
body:
MOSCOW, October 23. /TASS/. Russia managed to change the political situation in the world, proving the pointlessness of sanctions, so the United States, and now European countries, are moving from confrontation to dialogue, the first deputy chairman of the State Duma’s Committee on CIS Affairs, Eurasian Integration and Relations with Compatriots, Viktor Vodolatsky, has told TASS, commenting on the results of the negotiations on Ukraine in Oslo and St. Petersburg.
The Croatian portal Advance previously published an opinion that the resumption of direct economic cooperation between Russia and Slovakia indicates that dialogue with Moscow is ceasing to be a "political taboo" in the European Union. In addition, preparations are underway for the Russia-US-Germany forum, which could take place in 2027.
"Russia has changed the political line-up and balance of power in the world. Today we observe that those sanctions [which were initiated by the West], they do not produce any results. Naturally, first of all, the United States understood this and is beginning a more open dialogue with Russia on the resumption of political and, most importantly, economic ties. Forces are beginning to appear in Europe that say that it is necessary to conduct a dialogue with Russia. Various political forces, including state leaders, are increasingly saying this," Vodolatsky said.
Russian Presidential aide Yury Ushakov previously stated that President Vladimir Putin, during a meeting with the American leader’s special envoy Steve Witkoff, informed that Moscow is ready to resume trilateral negotiations on the 10th of November on the main topic, which concerns building a security system for Russia and Ukraine after the end of the conflict. Currently, Abu Dhabi is considered as the main platform for trilateral negotiations.

title: World must cut emissions 18% in four years to find a way back below 1.5°C – UN 2026 Emissions Gap Report
body: Countries must slash greenhouse gas emissions by almost a fifth (18%) by 2030 and 45% by 2035, compared with 2025 levels. Only then can they stop global heating from running far past 1.5 degrees Celsius (°C) and bring it back down by the end of the century, the United Nations said on Wednesday. In its annual Emissions Gap Report , the UN Environment Programme (UNEP) said decades of weak action had made crossing 1.5°C “imminent and unavoidable”. If deep cuts start now, warming could peak at about 1.7–1.8°C around the middle of the century, with roughly an even chance of falling back to 1.5°C by 2100. “Overshoot is not surrender,” UN Secretary-General António Guterres said in a message on the report. “We can still keep it as small and as short as possible.” Under the 2015 Paris Agreement, almost every country promised to keep global warming “well below” 2°C and to try to stop it at 1.5°C. The figure measures the rise in Earth’s average temperature over many years, compared with the late 1800s, before factories and cars. UNEP now says that even if every country cut its emissions as hard as possible starting today, warming would still pass 1.5°C, because so much heat-trapping gas has already built up in the air. Scientists call this an overshoot: going above the limit for a while, likely for several decades, and then pulling temperatures back down. And on the policies governments actually have in place, the world is not heading for a small overshoot at all, but for about 2.8°C by 2100. Figure 1. Where warming is heading by 2100 under different paths. This is what climate change is. Burning coal, oil and gas, and clearing forests, releases carbon dioxide and other gases that trap the sun’s heat like a blanket. The thicker the blanket, the hotter the planet gets. Above 1.5°C, the report warns, heatwaves, floods and droughts become more frequent and severe, bringing more heat deaths and economic losses. Every extra fraction of a degree also raises the risk of changes that cannot be undone, such as melting ice sheets, carbon escaping from thawing frozen ground, disrupted ocean currents and the loss of coral reefs. Coming back down will take more than cutting pollution. About 320 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide, roughly eight years of today’s fossil fuel emissions, would have to be pulled back out of the air this century, and UNEP calls that uncertain. The effects are already visible. The EU’s Copernicus Climate Change Service said August 2026 tied July 2023 as the hottest month ever recorded, with an average global air temperature of 16.96°C, 1.65°C above pre-industrial levels. The world’s oceans were also the warmest ever measured for an August. The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) warned on Wednesday that the El Niño now building in the Pacific “could be unprecedented in strength”, and the UN says about 50 million people could face greater hunger as a result. The WMO also found that 2025 was one of Africa’s warmest years on record. Researchers at the University of Chicago’s Climate Impact Lab estimate that the extra heat from this El Niño alone could cause about 451,000 additional deaths worldwide between June 2026 and February 2027. Nigeria faces about 31,400 extra deaths between September and February, more than any other country. Looking further ahead, the lab projects that Sahel countries such as Niger and Burkina Faso could see 60 or more heat deaths for every 100,000 people each year by 2050, a higher rate than malaria causes in Africa today. Rising temperatures are also moving malaria itself. A study in Nature , promoted by the University of Chicago and co-written by Climate Impact Lab researchers, found that some very hot West African and Sahel countries are becoming too hot for malaria-carrying mosquitoes, while risk is climbing in the cooler highlands of East Africa and in southern Africa. By 2100 it could rise by about 20% in areas such as the Rift Valley. Table 1. The warming we are already living with What The numbers Source Hottest month on record (joint) August 2026: 16.96°C, 1.65°C above pre-industrial; ties July 2023 Copernicus, 10 Sept 2026 Ocean heat Warmest August sea surface ever measured: 21.07°C Copernicus, 10 Sept 2026 El Niño “Could be unprecedented in strength”; about 50 million could face more hunger WMO/OCHA briefing, 21 Oct 2026 Extra heat deaths from El Niño About 451,000 worldwide (June 2026–Feb 2027); Nigeria about 31,400 (Sept–Feb) UChicago Climate Impact Lab, Sept 2026 Heat deaths by 2050 60+ per 100,000 people a year in Sahel countries such as Niger and Burkina Faso Climate Impact Lab, Mar 2026 Africa 2025 was one of the continent’s warmest years on record WMO State of the Climate in Africa 2025 The outlook is bleaker than a year ago. UNEP’s 2025 report, Off target , said warming could still be held close to 1.5°C if emissions fell 26% by 2030 and 46% by 2035 from 2019 levels. This year’s edition, The point of return , says that chance “has been lost”. Even if every country kept its climate plan, emissions would fall only 5–8% by 2030, and warming would reach 2.6°C by 2100. Last year the same calculation gave 2.3–2.5°C. UNEP blamed the change mainly on the United States leaving the Paris Agreement and on revised estimates of past emissions. Global emissions reached 58.4 billion tonnes in 2025, roughly level with 2024, and every five years of pollution at today’s rate pushes peak warming up by about 0.1°C. Table 2. One year on: what changed between the 2025 and 2026 reports 2025 report: Off target 2026 report: The point of return Global emissions 57.7 billion tonnes in 2024, up 2.3% 58.4 billion tonnes in 2025, roughly flat 1.5°C goal Still within reach with a limited overshoot Chance with no or limited overshoot “has been lost”; peak 1.7–1.8°C Cuts needed 26% by 2030 and 46% by 2035 (vs 2019) 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035, 69% by 2040 (vs 2025) Warming if all pledges kept 2.3–2.5°C 2.6°C Warming on current policies Up to 2.8°C 2.8°C Countries with new climate plans 60 (63% of emissions) 124 (about 76% of emissions) Figure 2. Global emissions since 1990 and where different paths take them. “Every additional fraction of a degree and additional year of warming above 1.5°C increases climate impacts and risks,” said Inger Andersen, UNEP’s executive director. “So, we must pull out all the stops to minimize peak warming and return to 1.5°C by the end of the century.” Countries are moving, but slowly. By 1 September, 124 governments covering about 76% of global emissions had handed in new climate plans, up from 60 a year earlier. Every G20 member except Argentina, Saudi Arabia and the United States has now set targets for 2035, but only Mexico strengthened its target for 2030, and only six G20 members (China, India, Indonesia, Russia, South Africa and Türkiye) are on course to meet their 2030 goals. The Paris Agreement’s main tool for closing the gap is the global stocktake, a check-up every five years on whether countries are doing enough together. The first, completed at the COP28 summit in Dubai in 2023, set goals such as tripling renewable energy and moving away from fossil fuels. The second runs until 2028, and the report urges governments to use it to set clear goals for 2035 and 2040. Figure 3. The emissions gap: cuts needed versus cuts promised. The report spells out where the cuts must come from. Electricity from coal must fall by at least 75% by 2035 and 95% by 2040. The energy the world draws from coal, oil and gas must drop by 55%, 15% and 5% respectively by 2035. Methane, a powerful heat-trapping gas from oil and gas sites, coal mines, livestock and rubbish dumps, must fall at least 25% by 2035, and road transport emissions by 20%. Figure 4. What has to be cut, and by how much. There is progress to build on. In 2025 renewables generated more of the world’s electricity than coal for the first time, and solar power has been built seven times faster than forecast a decade ago. Before the Paris Agreement, the world was on course for almost 4°C of warming. For Africa, the gap between cause and harm is stark. The world’s least developed countries, many of them African, produce just 3% of global emissions, about 1.5 tonnes a person against a world average of 6.4 tonnes and 17.6 tonnes for each American. Figure 5. Greenhouse gas emissions per person, 2025.

title: European leaders view Meloni, Stubb, and Pavel as potential negotiators with Putin – media
body:
European leaders are considering forming a group of negotiators to represent the continent’s interests in talks with the Russian Federation aimed at ending the war in Ukraine. Potential candidates include Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, Finnish President Alexander Stubb, and Czech President Petr Pavel, The Telegraph reports, citing diplomatic sources.
According to the publication, the potential candidates have already been approached with such proposals. Other individuals mentioned as possible members of the negotiating group include Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre.
The ezine says that Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, Finnish President Alexander Stubb, and Czech President Petr Pavel have been named as possible candidates for this role, as have Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre. In recent weeks, there has been a growing sense in Europe of the need to identify representatives for potential peace talks, driven by concerns that Donald Trump may no longer represent the continent’s best interests.
According to The Telegraph, European diplomats favor forming a group of leaders to engage with the Russian Federation, a move intended to avoid potential disagreements between nations over the selection of a single representative.
Finnish President Alexander Stubb is among those being considered for the group; he maintains contacts with U.S. President Donald Trump and has been involved in European efforts to support Ukraine. Czech President Petr Pavel, former chair of the NATO Military Committee, also believes it is necessary to designate representatives who will be mandated to conduct negotiations on behalf of Europe.

title: Europe has no place at negotiating table, Trump could represent it — Crimean lawmaker
body:
SIMFEROPOL, October 23. /TASS/. European leaders have undermined their credibility as partners in dialogue, making their presence at the negotiating table with Russia inappropriate, while US President Donald Trump could convey their views, State Duma member representing the Republic of Crimea Mikhail Sheremet told TASS.
Politico previously reported that European Union countries were concerned about their status in the Ukraine negotiations and were trying to find someone who could represent the bloc’s interests. According to The Telegraph, candidates for the role include Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, Finnish President Alexander Stubb, Czech President Petr Pavel, Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store and Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen.
"The frenzied, revanchist and Russophobic policies of the leaders of several European countries have led them into a political and economic dead end, leaving them entirely incapable of engaging in constructive dialogue with their key neighbor and economic donor, peace-loving Russia," Sheremet said. "That is why I am convinced that, under the difficult circumstances now emerging, Europe’s interests at the upcoming talks could be represented by its strategic ally, US President Donald Trump, who commands authority and enjoys the trust of the European Union."
The US president and European Union politicians have repeatedly exchanged harsh remarks. Sheremet believes that disagreements between the White House and several European capitals are not as deep as they appear publicly. "I am convinced that America remains Europe’s key partner and most important ally," he emphasized.
The lawmaker also noted that, as Europe is repeatedly rocked by unrest, "one cannot help but recall the times of European prosperity under the leadership of level-headed, civilized politicians such as Silvio Berlusconi, Angela Merkel and Viktor Orban," who were capable of redirecting Europe’s confrontational agenda toward a constructive and peaceful course.
"Today, public support for the leaders of major countries such as Germany and France does not exceed 15%, and they are afraid to meet their own citizens in public, raising serious questions about their legitimacy," Sheremet said.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov previously said that Abu Dhabi in the United Arab Emirates was currently being considered the main venue for trilateral talks between Russia, the United States and Ukraine.

title: The urban Filipino is tired, cash-strapped, and sick of the ‘resilience’ excuse
body: MANILA, Philippines – For years, every calamity and crisis has been followed by a familiar consolation. Filipinos are resilient. Whatever happens, they find a way, pick themselves up, and keep going. “ Bagyo ka lang; Pinoy kami. ” (You’re just a storm; we’re Filipinos.) But many Filipinos are now rejecting that romanticized view. Nearly half (48%) of urban Filipinos surveyed by research firm Organic Intelligence said they rejected the romanticized narrative of “Filipino resilience,” according to its Pinoy, Kaya Pa Ba? study released in October. The sentiment was strongest among younger respondents aged 18 to 24, of whom 64% rejected the narrative. In Mindanao, the figure reached 59%, compared with 38% in Metro Manila. That said, at what point does enshrining the resilience of Filipinos for enduring hardship become an excuse for allowing that hardship to continue? Play Video “We are not rejecting resilience per se. What we are rejecting is the necessity of it amid all of these crises. Why is that the default coping?” said Jason Ligot, Organic Intelligence group account director for development communication and communication design, in a press briefing on Friday, October 23. “We should be holding government and institutions to account. And then second, why is the onus always on me?” he added. Curiously, resilience was higher among groups facing greater hardship. Mindanao respondents scored 86 out of 100 on the Resilience Index, compared with 80 in Luzon outside Metro Manila. Those aged 45 to 54 scored 87, against 77 among younger adults. Researchers said lower-income respondents also tended to score higher. So how do these high scores square with the growing rejection of the resilience narrative? Ligot suggested that those facing the greatest hardships may be drawing more heavily on their psychological reserves because they have little choice. Although 69% of Filipinos maintained an optimistic financial outlook, 44% lacked enough savings to survive three months without work. Another 45% said inflation had drained them to the point of losing their drive to get ahead. The Philippines may have officially reached upper-middle-income status in July, but that does not mean ordinary families have the financial security to weather another crisis. At the Zero Poverty PH 2030 forum on October 16, World Bank economist Sharon Faye Piza warned that many households remain vulnerable to economic shocks that could push them back into poverty , calling for better-paying jobs and stronger social protection. Must Read World Bank: 4Ps a ‘far more effective’ program for reducing poverty Loaning to live The study also found that Filipinos are also borrowing just to get by. The survey found that 46% had taken out a loan in the preceding one to two months, with 42% of all respondents borrowing for essentials, including food and transportation. Official banking data similarly show a broader expansion in consumer credit. Outstanding consumer loans reached P2.84 trillion in August , up 17% from a year earlier, according to the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP). Credit card receivables alone climbed 23.8%. Play Video More worryingly, there are signs of growing repayment difficulties. Non-performing consumer loans grew nearly 20% from a year earlier, and the share of bad debt climbed to 5.67% of all consumer loans, according to BSP data . So what can be done? Of course, there are big problems to fix. The study calls for holding the government accountable, addressing the economic pressures on households, and building more free public spaces where Filipinos can relax for free. But these changes will take time. But businesses can act more immediately to help struggling consumers and earn their loyalty along the way. Asked what would make them feel a brand was genuinely on their side, 27% of respondents chose a price freeze , the most popular response. Smaller or tingi sizes followed at 16%, free shipping at 14%, and promotional bundles at 12%. “It has to be tangible,” said Sheila Mangila, Organic Intelligence group account director for marketing intelligence. “It’s about material conditions that will really help them survive the everyday.” – Rappler.com The study surveyed 800 Filipinos in urban areas aged 18 to 65 through an online panel in May 2026. Its findings may not fully capture perspectives of rural or digitally disconnected Filipinos. Must Read New urban poor commissioner has lavish lifestyle. Palace still defends her.

title: Nigerians need explanations on N10bn Ebola response fund, Atiku tells FG
body: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has asked the Federal Government to tell Nigerians where the N10 billion that it earmarked for Ebola response is. On 9 June, the Presidency announced that President Bola Tinubu had ordered the immediate release of ₦10 billion for Ebola emergency preparedness. Following the discovery of an index case in Abuja, concerns have been raised about the money. The Presidential Candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) had earlier demanded explanations about the money, warning Nigerians not to politicise the Ebola issue. INEC: Results with discrepancies won’t be uploaded on IREV Uproar in Rivers over forced virginity test on female students Responding Dele Alake, spokesman of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, said the money had not been touched. He also accused Atiku of denigrating the office of the President by constantly referring to the Commander-in-Chief as Bola, his first name. Alake also said rather than commend the Federal agencies for tracking and isolating the index Ebola patient and taking steps to preventing the disease from spreading, the opposition “had been trivialising the issue”. In a statement issued on his behalf by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku insisted that the N10 billion must be accounted for. “Ebola destroys lives through disease. Bola’s policies have made food and medical care unaffordable and buried businesses that Nigerians spent years building. Yet the APC wants a debate about how two words sound. Atiku Abubakar asked for the money trail and an account of the emergency response. The party in power came back with a pronunciation lesson. What an extraordinary way to tell a frightened country it has no answers. “Now, with a case confirmed in Abuja, the APC says the money remains “untouched”. It presents that claim as a defence. It is an indictment of the Bola administration. “Was the money released or was it not? If it was released, where is it held, who controls it, and why has it not been used for the preparedness President Tinubu announced? If it was never released, why was an order for its immediate release announced in June? Publish the release documents, the account records and the Task Force’s expenditure reports. Insulting Atiku Abubakar will not account for one naira. “The APC says an infected person cannot transmit Ebola before symptoms appear. That is true. It does not answer what happened after symptoms appeared. According to the World Health Organization’s account, the patient developed symptoms on 7th October, sought care at a private facility on 11th October, and received laboratory confirmation on 20th October. When was Ebola first suspected? When were public health authorities alerted? When was testing ordered? When did contact tracing begin? “The APC claims surveillance “tipped off” the government. Then publish the timeline. Name the agency that raised the alert, give the date and explain the action taken. 44 identified contacts are people whose health must be protected. They are not a trophy for an APC press release. “Health workers treating the patient and tracing contacts deserve protection, equipment and every resource needed to act quickly. Questioning the government’s preparedness is no insult to them. Demanding applause for President Tinubu while refusing to explain an untouched emergency fund is an insult to Nigerians. “The APC also objects to our warning that a health emergency must never be used to interfere with campaigning or voting. President Tinubu’s government can address that concern directly: publish any proposed restrictions, their medical justification and the advice of the health authorities. Public health guidance must protect people. It must never become a political tool. “President Tinubu ordered ₦10 billion released in June. His party now says it is untouched. That contradiction came from the Presidency and the APC. They should resolve it with records. Show Nigerians where the money is. Explain the response timeline. Protect health workers. Trace every contact. President Tinubu and the APC owe the country answers not ‘Bola-Ebola’ tales.”

title: Austria expels 4 Russian diplomats, Moscow vows response
body:
Austria is expelling four Russian diplomats for security reasons, the Austrian Foreign Ministry said on Oct. 23, as reported by the DPA news agency.
Three members of the Russian Embassy, as well as a Russian delegate at the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) responsible for military security and arms control, "carried out activities incompatible with their diplomatic status," the ministry said.
Vienna hosts major international institutions like the OSCE or U.N. agencies, making it a popular target of Russian spies.
With the latest step, Austria has expelled 18 Russian diplomats since 2020. Other European countries have taken similar measures due to growing concerns about Russian espionage amid the full-scale war in Ukraine.
Russia's Foreign Ministry warned that an "inevitable" response will follow, according to the Russian state news agency TASS.
Austria previously expelled three staff members of the Russian Embassy in May over suspected signals intelligence activities in the EU country's capital.
Although neutral, Austria has joined international and EU sanctions against Russia while providing financial and humanitarian aid to Kyiv.

title: Storied Mirage F1CZ 213 unveiled at the South African Air Force Museum
body:
The South African Air Force Museum at Air Force Base Ysterplaat in Cape Town hosted a special aviation heritage event on 17 October to unveil newly restored Dassault Mirage F1CZ tail number 213, which recorded the first air-to-air kill against a MiG-21 over Angola.
Hosted by the Aeronautical Society of South Africa, Western Cape Chapter, the programme commenced with an aviation talk by author Lionel Reid, who shared insights from his book, The MiG Diaries. The programme was followed by the unveiling of 213, marking a significant milestone in preserving South African military aviation heritage, reported Corporal Pumela Kondile for the South African Air Force (SAAF).
The ceremony was opened by Lieutenant Colonel James du Toit, Officer-in-Charge of the South African Air Force Museum at Air Force Base Ysterplaat, who welcomed guests on behalf of the Officer Commanding Air Force Base Ysterplaat, Colonel EMT Wilson. Distinguished guests included Lieutenant General (Retired) Carlo Gagiano and representatives of the Aeronautical Society of South Africa, Western Cape Chapter, including Professor Johan van der Spuy, Dr René Heise, Colonel (Retired) Dr Alan Nelson and Dr Adam Venter, together with members of the base.
In his opening address, du Toit highlighted the importance of preserving the heritage of the South African Air Force and recognising the people whose dedication and service shaped its history.
“Aircraft such as Mirage 213 are more than machines. They represent the people who flew them, maintained them and served alongside them. Preserving that history and the culture of our Air Force ensures that what previous generations built is not simply remembered but passed on to those who follow us. We preserve the past not to remain in it, but to give the next generation something to be proud of and to build upon.”
The talk by Reid provided an engaging start to the programme, offering guests insights into military aviation history through The MiG Diaries and reinforcing the importance of recording and sharing personal experiences with future generations.
As recorded in the MiG Diaries, Mirage F1CZ 213 was one of two SAAF Mirage F1s involved (along with tail number 203) in the first recorded air-to-air engagement between South African Air Force Mirage F1s and Cuban-flown Angolan MiG-21s over Angola in 1981, culminating in a SAAF aerial victory.
On 6 November 1981, Major Johan Rankin and Lieutenant Johan du Plessis were scrambled from Air Force Base Ondangwa after radar detected unidentified aircraft roughly 140 nautical miles northwest of the base. They were airborne within about two minutes.
After flying low level, the pair climbed rapidly to about 25 000 feet. Du Plessis spotted two MiG-21s flying in a fighting-wing formation, passing 3–5 nautical miles to port. The MiGs were flying toward the sun, which prevented a reliable infrared lock for the Matra R550 Magic missiles the Mirage F1s were carrying. Rankin therefore closed from behind the MiG wingman and fired his 30 mm cannons from about 550 metres, causing visible damage and fuel leakage. When the MiGs turned away, Rankin pursued the wingman again; after that pilot reversed his turn — allowing Rankin to close rapidly — he fired another cannon burst. The MiG (C-41) exploded and broke apart behind the cockpit. Rankin broke away to avoid debris, and both Mirages returned to Ondangwa. The fight occurred near Cahama in southeastern Angola.
Cuban pilot Danasio Valdes survived ejecting from his stricken MiG-21 while the other badly damaged MiG — flown by Ezequiel Cancela — managed to return and land at Lubango. The incident is widely regarded as the SAAF’s first confirmed air-to-air kill since the Korean War and the Mirage F1’s first air-to-air kill anywhere in the world.
After Reid’s talk, the focus then shifted to the unveiling of the Mirage F1CZ. Martin Strumpfer, who led the restoration effort, outlined the process and the technical expertise required to restore the iconic aircraft. His presentation highlighted the dedication and attention to detail involved in preserving this significant piece of South African aviation heritage, Kondile reported.
“The event brought together historical accounts and aircraft restoration, demonstrating the importance of preserving both the stories and physical reminders of the past. It also highlighted the value of collaboration between the South African Air Force Museum, the Aeronautical Society of South Africa, aviation historians, authors and restoration specialists in safeguarding the country’s aviation legacy,” Kondile concluded.
A more detailed account of the MiG-21 kill can be found by Lionel Reid here .

title: Public frustration with elected leaders could fuel military coups in Africa – Yemi Osinbajo
body: Former Nigerian Vice President Yemi Osinbajo has warned that growing public tolerance for military coups in Africa reflects frustration with elected leaders who abuse power, weaken constitutional institutions and undermine democratic principles. Speaking at the third Good Governance Africa Annual Lecture, held under the theme Democracy Under Pressure: Rebuilding Trust, Accountability and Institutional Integrity in Africa’s New Political Era , Mr Osinbajo said the trend should prompt a serious examination of the failures of elected governments. Citing an Afrobarometer report indicating that 53% of Africans would accept military intervention if elected leaders abused their power, he cautioned against interpreting such sentiments as support for military dictatorship. “A coup is an attack, of course, on constitutional government, but the conditions in which coups occur also demand honest reflection,” he said. “They often follow profound failures in security, accountability, and public confidence.” Mr Osinbajo added that some elected leaders had themselves weakened constitutional rule by manipulating political rules or restricting opportunities for genuine political change. His remarks come amid concerns about political instability, public discontent and the resurgence of military takeovers in parts of Africa. Good Governance Africa said the lecture was organised against a backdrop of rising protests, political dissatisfaction and violence across the continent. GGA seeks answers to growing democratic discontent Tina Asante-Apeatu, Executive Director of Good Governance Africa’s West Africa Regional Office, said the organisation convened the forum to examine whether growing dissatisfaction with democracy represented a rejection of democratic governance itself or concerns about how it was being practised. “Research is showing more and more people are complaining,” she said. “People are complaining of democracy, protest, violence here and there, not only in Ghana but in Africa.” She said the organisation wanted to create a platform for citizens to express their views and help identify the factors driving the growing discontent. “So we thought, listen, let’s bring the conversation back on board. Let the citizens know, or let’s hear from the citizens,” she said. “Is it really that they are fed up with democracy as we know it, or is it that misinformation and disinformation is playing a part here?” Ms Asante-Apeatu said the forum was intended to stimulate public discussion and bring citizens and experts together to better understand the challenges confronting democratic governance. “So we decided to bring this conversation up to trigger the conversation from ordinary people. I mean, hearing from the experts so we know what is actually happening,” she added. Discussions at the lecture also focused on the abuse of authority and the need to strengthen accountability, with panelists drawn from governance institutions, the legal profession, security services, civil society and research institutions. One panelist described the prevailing circumstances as a major security threat, highlighting the links between democratic governance, political stability and public confidence in state institutions. Participants also highlighted the need for more participatory democracy, arguing that citizen involvement should extend beyond elections and occasional public consultations to give people a meaningful role in governance and decision-making. The concerns raised at the lecture point to a challenge facing African democracies: rebuilding public trust in elected institutions while protecting constitutional rule against both authoritarian leadership and military intervention.

title: Over 83% of Ukrainian manufacturers face labor shortages — poll
body:
MOSCOW, October 23. /TASS/. Labor shortages have become the primary challenge for Ukrainian enterprises, with over 83% of companies reporting the issue, the NV news outlet reported, citing data from the GRC.UA recruitment agency.
According to GRC.UA’s analytical report, titled "Labor Market Barometer," "83.3% of production managers cited labor shortages among the main problems reported by the surveyed companies." Meanwhile, the outflow of people abroad was cited by 66.7%, and a general shortage of workers across various categories stood at 50%.
Amid the severe workforce deficit, the report notes that 100% of the surveyed employers now hire individuals aged 50 and older for various positions. Furthermore, 66.7% of respondents recruit women for "traditionally male occupations" and employ people with disabilities.
The survey data was collected in September-October, polling 6,160 respondents across various regions of Ukraine.

title: Recall of House approved-GAB may lead to reenacted budget – senators
body: MANILA, Philippines – Recalling the House-approved version of the 7.2-trillion proposed 2027 national budget, as pushed by some lawmakers, may result in a reenacted budget, senators said on Friday, October 23. Senate finance committee chairperson JV Ejercito warned of potential delays in the passage of the 2027 General Appropriations Bill (GAB) after the Makabayan bloc proposed recalling House Bill No. 10858 to correct provisions they believe could be declared unconstitutional. “There are proposals to recall the HGAB. In my opinion, there is a great chance the proposed 2027 national budget may not be approved if that would happen,” Ejercito said in a chance interview. “The Senate is running on a very tight schedule due to the impeachment, regular plenary sessions, and budget hearings. Right now, we are targeting to pass our version of the budget bill by second week of November,” he added The Supreme Court (SC) declared the 2024 and 2025 General Appropriations Acts (GAA), or national budget laws, unconstitutional. Citing the court’s rulings, the Makabayan bloc called on the House to “clean its own mess,” pointing to provisions in the proposed 2027 budget involving the release of unprogrammed appropriations, cuts to foreign-assisted projects to accommodate congressional insertions, and prohibited lump-sum allocations. ACT Teachers Representative Antonio Tinio told ANC’s Headstart : “If this were not corrected, [it] would risk many portions of the budget for 2027 as well. We don’t want yet another budget that will be declared unconstitutional.” Senator Panfilo “Ping” Lacson , chairperson of the Senate committee on accounts, echoed Ejercito’s position, saying recalling the budget was “not the solution.” “They can submit their proposals to the House or to the Senate finance committee for consideration. After all, the Senate version of the budget bill will be subject to the bicam so they should attest and address their concerns there,” Lacson said. “Recalling the budget to the House is not the solution because that would result to a worse scenario — a reenacted budget,” he added. Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian also said there was no need to recall the proposed budget, adding that the Senate could address the questioned provisions in the consolidated version of the budget bill. “Looking at the Supreme Court decision on the 2026 budget, there are only a few provisions that will be affected. I don’t see the need to make major correction in the 2027 budget,” Gatchalian said. Under the 1987 Constitution, if Congress fails to pass the GAB for the incoming fiscal year, the GAA for the preceding fiscal year is deemed reenacted and remains in effect until a new appropriations law is passed. – Rappler.com

title: Sudanese army claims gains against RSF in Blue Nile
body: The Sudan Armed Forces’ (SAF) Fourth Infantry Division has announced that it has recaptured the areas of Bakori and Akleli in the Blue Nile region following military operations that it said inflicted casualties and destroyed equipment belonging to the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and their allied forces. In a military communiqué, the division’s command and operations room said troops from the Al-Naba Al-Yaqin force, operating along the Geissan axis, had retaken the two areas and driven out opposing forces. Al-Waleed Ajabna, head of the division’s command and operations room, said in an audio recording that the RSF and the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North (SPLM-N) had been driven out of the two areas, which he said had been secured. In a statement issued through its media office, the division said the operation involved both the Martyr Adrob and the Al-Naba Al-Yaqin forces. It added that military operations will continue to pursue withdrawing enemy forces and to secure the areas recaptured by the army. On August 28, the RSF announced that it had taken control of the Bakori military base, alongside a claim that it had captured the Surkum base in coordination with its ally, the SPLM-N. The reported recapture of Bakori therefore comes approximately 55 days after the RSF announced its takeover. Bakori is located in Geissan locality and hosts the headquarters of the Sudanese army’s 13th Infantry Brigade. Akleli also holds military significance within the area of operations in the Blue Nile region. Radio Tamazuj could not independently verify when the RSF and its allies took control of Akleli. As of publication, the Tasis Alliance had not commented on the army’s announcement that it had recaptured the two areas. Radio Tamazuj was also unable to reach the RSF leadership for comment. The post Sudanese army claims gains against RSF in Blue Nile appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: 11 killed as trailer rams into vehicles in Gombe
body: The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) has confirmed the death of 11 people in a multiple-vehicle crash involving a trailer, two cars and five motorcycles in Kumo, Akko Local Government Area of Gombe State. The accident occurred at Tashan Magarya Junction along the Gombe–Billiri road, leaving several other people injured, according to an FRSC incident report. The report attributed the crash to brake failure, which allegedly caused the driver of a DAF trailer travelling from Gombe towards Yola to lose control and ram into two Volkswagen Golf cars and five motorcycles. The collision involved eight vehicles, including the trailer, and resulted in multiple casualties. Lagos: One dead, several feared trapped as building collapses Namadi hails company for upholding journalistic ethics The FRSC said its personnel received a distress call at 5:32 p.m. on Thursday and arrived at the scene two minutes later to commence rescue operations. The victims were evacuated to the Federal Medical Centre (FMC), Kumo, for medical attention. The report also stated that 11 people received first aid. Those injured reportedly sustained various degrees of injuries, including compound fractures, lacerations and bruises. Following the rescue operation, the vehicles involved in the crash were handed over to the Motor Traffic Division of the police in Kumo for further investigation and necessary action. The identities of the deceased and the current conditions of the injured victims were not immediately made available as of the time of filing this report.

title: Lebanese and British troops conclude three-week joint exercise with mock helicopter assault
body: Lebanese and British troops have concluded a three-week joint exercise in Lebanon aimed at enhancing co-operation between the two militaries. Operation Pegasus Cedar 2026 was held at a pivotal time for the Lebanese Armed Forces, which have been given the formidable challenge of disarming Iran-backed Hezbollah and extending state control across the country. The task has been made more difficult by Israel’s occupation of parts of southern Lebanon and its bombardment of the country. British army commander Lt Col Alex Phillips said the exercise was an opportunity for the two militaries to learn from each other. The National was granted access to the drills, which took place at Hammana Barracks, east of Beirut. “It's incredibly important to build our relationship of mutual support and to develop our professionalism as militaries in the region,” he told reporters. Soldiers from Lebanon's elite Air Assault Regiment and the UK's 4th Battalion, The Royal Regiment of Scotland, trained together over three weeks of drills. Six other countries, including the US , Qatar and Jordan , were also involved. It culminated in a mock assault, with LAF helicopters swooping through the valley before placing British and Lebanese soldiers on the roof of a building to launch attacks. Observers included LAF Chief of Staff Maj Gen Hassan Audi, the army's second most senior officer. بحضور قائد الجيش بالنيابة اللواء الركن حسان عوده، أُقيم حفل اختتام تمرين PEGASUS CEDAR 2026 الذي امتدّ لثلاثة أسابيع، نفّذه فريق بريطاني من الفوج الملكي الاسكتلندي والفوج المجوقل في الجيش اللبناني، بمشاركة عناصر من جيشَي الولايات المتحدة وإيطاليا وحضور عناصر من جيوش فرنسا وقبرص… pic.twitter.com/IFxHsXtPqZ — الجيش اللبناني (@LebarmyOfficial) October 22, 2026 The British contingent is normally based at Dhekelia Garrison in Cyprus. The exercise built on a joint drill held in September 2023, which was described as the largest exercise involving UK and Lebanese troops. The latest exercise was the first joint drill between the countries to take place since Israel launched its war on Gaza, after the Hamas-led attacks on October 7, 2023. Lebanon has repeatedly been dragged into the wider regional war, with Hezbollah and Israel exchanging fire. Israeli troops occupy a large part of southern Lebanon, where residents have been ordered to flee and villages have been demolished. A US-backed peace process called for the Lebanese military to reassert control and disarm Hezbollah, in exchange for the withdrawal of Israeli troops. But that process has largely ground to a halt. Hezbollah , which was not party to the agreement signed in June, has rejected it. The LAF, while highly respected in Lebanon, is poorly funded and equipped and relies largely on foreign support.

title: Logeist Group supports Ashanti GJA initiative to honour veteran journalist Kofi Badu
body: Logeist Group Limited is supporting the Ashanti Regional Branch of the Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) in its initiative to honour veteran journalist Kofi Badu at the 2026 Ashanti Media Excellence Awards. The recognition is intended to celebrate Mr Badu’s contribution to journalism and his service to the media profession. He currently serves as Chief of Staff at the Manhyia Palace, having built a career in journalism. The Ashanti GJA is using the awards platform to recognise outstanding journalistic work and celebrate individuals whose professional contributions have helped shape the media landscape. The 2026 edition of the awards is scheduled for Saturday, October 24, at the Longford Royal Event Centre, Odeneho Kwadaso, Kumasi, at 6:00 p.m. It will be held under the theme, “Celebrating Excellence, Championing Credibility: Journalism in the Age of AI,” which highlights the importance of professional standards, credibility, and ethical reporting amid the growing influence of artificial intelligence in news production and distribution. The Association is also proposing to institute an annual Kofi Badu Honorary Award for Veteran Journalists to recognise experienced media practitioners whose careers reflect professional dedication, ethical journalism, mentorship and service to society. The proposed award is expected to provide a platform for celebrating veteran journalists and preserving their contributions to the development of the profession for future generations. “For Ashanti GJA, Mr Badu represents a valuable link between generations of journalists. His career offers lessons in professional growth, institutional leadership, innovation and the enduring importance of journalism in national development,” said Kofi Adu Domfeh, Chairman, GJA Ashanti. The support from Logeist Group Limited underscores the role of corporate partnerships in advancing initiatives that promote professional excellence and recognise contributions to public service. The Ashanti GJA continues to position the Media Excellence Awards as a platform for encouraging quality journalism, strengthening professional standards and inspiring the next generation of media practitioners.

title: Trump slams LeBron James over apparent national anthem stretches
body:
The president accused the NBA star of disrespecting the U.S.
President Donald Trump attacked Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James on Thursday over a video appearing to show the NBA star stretching during the national anthem ahead of his Sixers debut against the New York Knicks on Tuesday.
"While listening to our National Anthem, LeBron James disrespects our Country!" Trump wrote in a social media post alongside a video of James that included overlaid text claiming that James was "working on his golf swing."
"I said right from the beginning that he's no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE. LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for!" Trump added.
In the video, LeBron can be seen performing arm stretches before moving on to mimic a basketball shooting motion.
Trump has a long history of attacking James going back to his first administration, when the president disparaged the four-time NBA champion's intelligence over an interview he did with CNN.
More recently, Trump speculated in July that James was a "racist" after he signed with the Sixers.
"I think LeBron is, maybe he's a racist, but maybe he doesn't like Trump, I don't know," Trump said in response to a question about if James or Michael Jordan was a better player. "I only like people who like me, so I would say Michael Jordan all the way."
James has yet to comment on Trump's latest remarks. Representatives for James did not immediately respond to ABC News' request for comment on Thursday.
The NBA star has publicly criticized Trump in the past. After Trump rescinded a White House invitation to the Golden State Warriors in 2017, James told reporters: "He doesn't understand how many kids, no matter the race, look up to the president of the United States for guidance, for leadership, for words of encouragement. He doesn't understand that, and that's what makes me more sick than anything."
James later told reporters, "This is a beautiful country and we're never going to let one person dictate how beautiful and how powerful we are."
James scored 14 points for the 76ers in their 106-100 victory over the Knicks, the defending NBA champions, in the opener Tuesday at Madison Square Garden.
The four-time NBA champion will make his home debut for Philadelphia against his former team, the Cleveland Cavaliers, on Thursday night.
