title: Press review: Russia open to Ukraine talks as Iran tensions rise amid US-Israeli threat
body:
MOSCOW, October 23. /TASS/. Russia signals its readiness for peace talks with Ukraine and the US as Europe risks being sidelined; Iran warns of retaliation amid reports of a possible US-Israeli attack after the midterms; and Hungary puts the Paks II nuclear project on hold, leaving Rosatom uncertain about its future. These stories topped Friday’s newspaper headlines across Russia.
The goal of negotiations with the United States and Ukraine will be to achieve a lasting peace settlement and guarantee Russia’s security, President Vladimir Putin said. He stressed that the discussions should also address Europe’s security architecture as a whole. Moscow places great value on Washington’s mediation efforts, while the Kremlin previously said a meeting could take place in mid-November. Nevertheless, the final say will rest with the parties directly involved in the conflict, as Russia and Ukraine will ultimately have to reach an agreement themselves, the Russian Foreign Ministry told Izvestia.
"The president has repeatedly said that, ultimately, it will be the Ukrainian and Russian sides that reach an agreement. The United States, in this case, is offering its good offices. It is therefore creating the conditions for an agreement and, accordingly, the necessary environment for the parties to reach a deal," Rodion Miroshnik, ambassador-at-large at the Russian Foreign Ministry, told Izvestia.
Possible trilateral talks between Russia, Ukraine, and the United States in Abu Dhabi in November are unlikely to bring the conflict closer to an end, according to Bogdan Bezpalko, political scientist and member of the Russian Presidential Council for Interethnic Relations. He said he saw no signs that Kiev was prepared to negotiate. If the meeting takes place, it could conclude without substantial progress, producing only agreements on specific humanitarian issues. The expert also noted that the talks might not take place at all, as Ukraine has not altered its position.
Meanwhile, Kiev’s European partners are continuing their efforts to become part of the negotiating process. According to Politico, EU countries are concerned about their role in a potential settlement of the conflict and are trying to choose a single representative to speak for the bloc in the discussions.
Europe is struggling to find a candidate with sufficient political influence who has not been undermined by staunch support for Ukraine or harsh criticism of Russia, political scientist Malek Dudakov believes. Europe fears a resumption of direct dialogue between Russia and the United States that would leave European representatives on the sidelines.
"Although Zelensky is rapidly losing support among Western public opinion, European leaders continue to offer their unconditional backing to Ukraine’s incumbent president," Fernand Kartheiser, a member of the European Parliament from Luxembourg, told Izvestia.
Iran is prepared for a new round of armed conflict with the United States and Israel, and if hostilities resume, enemy casualties will be "dozens of times higher" than in previous months, Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of the Islamic Republic’s Supreme National Security Council, told online publication Drop Site. According to him, the Americans still have valuable assets in the region, particularly data centers and undersea internet cables. He also did not rule out fresh strikes against the energy infrastructure of Persian Gulf countries. His remarks came amid reports in Western media of a US-Israeli military operation being planned for after the November 3 congressional midterm elections, Vedomosti writes.
Ilya Vaskin, junior research fellow at the Center for Middle Eastern, Caucasian and Central Asian Studies at the National Research University Higher School of Economics, believes Tehran has sufficient military defensive capabilities to repel another potential US-Israeli attack. Therefore, he said, it is highly unlikely that enemy aggression would force Tehran to negotiate on Washington’s terms. At most, the parties would continue their backchannel dialogue, about which little is known, the Iran specialist said.
"I would not rule out the possibility that the adversaries will refrain from launching another round of violence. We have too little information, and the potential costs of the conflict far outweigh the benefits. The current regional status quo may persist, with the leaders of both countries continuing to exchange bellicose statements," he told Vedomosti.
A joint US-Israeli military operation against Iran is entirely possible amid a stalemate in negotiations caused by irreconcilable differences between the parties’ positions, research fellow at the Center for Middle East Studies at the Russian Academy of Sciences’ Primakov National Research Institute of World Economy and International Relations (IMEMO) Alexey Yurk said.
"It is difficult to say whether such a strategy could break the negotiating deadlock. It might only lead Washington and Tehran to harden their positions. But both sides understand that there are currently no other options for breaking the impasse," the expert said.
Yurk did not rule out that reports in Western media about a planned US-Israeli strike on Iran could be deliberate information leaks intended to undermine Trump and the Republicans in the midterm elections, given the negative attitudes toward the war among undecided American voters. However, the political scientist believes this does not in itself mean that such plans are not being discussed at the White House and the Pentagon.
Hungarian authorities have not responded to Rosatom’s requests for negotiations over the Paks II nuclear power plant project, the Russian state corporation’s CEO Alexey Likhachev told Izvestia. He stressed that Rosatom intends to build the plant as quickly as possible and avoid legal proceedings. However, the Hungarian authorities have effectively suspended progress on the project to conduct an audit and determine its future.
"We have officially informed the Hungarian government, repeatedly informing it of our readiness and our requests for negotiations, but so far we have received no response," Likhachev stressed.
As a result, uncertainty still surrounds the future of the project. "In the absence of any concrete signals from the Hungarian government, there is currently a nonzero probability of both the project moving forward with even greater momentum and its complete suspension," Likhachev said. "Our objective, of course, is not to end up in court and establish grounds there for holding our partners financially liable. Our objective is to build the plant as quickly as possible," he added.
Foreign media previously reported that Hungary’s new government was allegedly considering replacing Rosatom as the project’s contractor. However, Hungarian company Paks II Zrt, which commissioned the Paks II plant, denied reports of Rosatom’s possible replacement, according to Portfolio.
The company stressed that a comprehensive review of Paks II was still underway and that a final decision on the investment project had yet to be made. Paks II Zrt also stated that there was "no room for speculation" regarding such a complex project.
It would be extremely difficult for an outside contractor to take over the Paks II project because of the time required to review documentation and renegotiate contracts, leading analyst at the National Energy Security Fund and an expert at the Financial University under the Russian Government Igor Yushkov told Izvestia.
Moreover, Rosatom is the only corporation in the global nuclear industry capable of providing a full range of services, from design to decommissioning. Therefore, if Rosatom is replaced, Budapest will have to bring in a team of separate contractors, Yushkov explained.
Although the Hungarian economy is not currently experiencing a critical energy shortage, the new nuclear power plant project is strategically important for the country, Artyom Ilyinsky, junior research fellow at the Department of European Political Studies at the Russian Academy of Sciences’ Primakov National Research Institute of World Economy and International Relations (IMEMO), told Izvestia. According to him, the plant could provide a reliable safety net for the country’s energy system, particularly given Budapest’s plans to phase out Russian gas supplies by 2027.
Vladimir Zelensky said in an interview with British businessman Steven Bartlett that he "will not give up Donbass" and once again accused US President Donald Trump of being sympathetic to Russia, seemingly playing into the hands of Democrats who support Ukraine ahead of the congressional elections. Meanwhile, the Ukrainian Armed Forces are once again attacking Russian targets in the frontline area using the Starlink/Starshield satellite communications system, which some are proposing to extend across the whole of Russia, Nezavisimaya Gazeta writes.
Amid preparations for peace negotiations, Moscow and Kiev continue active combat operations. Ukraine continues to demonstrate an unwillingness to compromise on ending the conflict.
Over the past 24 hours alone, Ukrainian forces launched an attack involving more than 1,200 unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), of which 630 drones were directed at the Moscow region.
According to Politico, the European Union is also seeking additional sources of assistance for Kiev. The EU is preparing to urge Canada and the United Kingdom to increase their support for Ukraine as part of efforts to cover a 70 bln euro funding gap expected to emerge next year. Kiev has yet to obtain the money.
According to Politico, US Democrats are also considering opening an investigation into SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, who allegedly restricted Starlink operations in Ukraine in recent days, US media reported, citing Ukrainian military personnel. However, Democrats would only be able to put pressure on Musk if they regain control of Congress in the November elections.
Earlier, US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth denied claims by Ukrainian officials and media outlets that Starlink satellite communications services had been restricted for Ukraine. He said Washington’s policy toward Kiev had not changed. "In other words, despite statements about wanting to end the conflict in Ukraine, the United States is in fact supporting Kiev’s plans," retired Lieutenant General Yury Netkachev, a military expert, told Nezavisimaya Gazeta, commenting on Hegseth’s statement.
A number of Russian experts and participants in the special military operation say that Starlink/Starshield satellite communications are functioning in Ukraine again. According to Dmitry Rogozin, commander of the Bars-Sarmat Special-Purpose Unmanned Systems Center, reports of problems with Starlink/Starshield on the Ukrainian front are "a disinformation ploy by Kiev aimed at discrediting the Ukrainian Armed Forces’ American partners in the eyes of NATO’s European allies." Rogozin maintains that Ukrainian forces continue to actively use Starlink/Starshield across the entire front and in rear areas near the front line.
The European Union (EU) should rethink its decision to completely phase out imports of Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG) from January 1, 2027, in light of current economic realities, Novatek CEO and co-owner Leonid Mikhelson said on October 22 at the 19th Verona Eurasian Economic Forum. He warned that the situation on the global gas market would worsen if the EU’s decision remained in force, Vedomosti writes. Russian LNG cannot be excluded from the global economy, so the volumes currently supplied to Europe will be diverted to other markets, Mikhelson stressed.
The Novatek chief pointed out that growing global gas demand cannot be met without Russian resources. According to Novatek’s forecast, global gas consumption will rise from the current 4.3 trillion cubic meters per year to 5.5 trillion cubic meters by 2050. Meeting this demand will require producing 120-135 trillion cubic meters over the next 25 years, compared with a total of just 87 trillion cubic meters extracted over the previous 25 years, Mikhelson noted.
Novatek’s Yamal LNG plant is currently the only supplier of Russian gas to the EU, Igor Yushkov, an expert at the Financial University under the Russian Government, told Vedomosti. Once the complete ban on supplies to the EU takes effect, the company could redirect exports to countries in South, East, and Southeast Asia, as well as Turkey, the analyst said.
After ending imports of Russian LNG, Europe will have to compete for available gas supplies from the United States and Qatar, Yushkov noted. This could indeed push up gas prices on the global market, the expert said. Sergey Suverov, an investment strategist at Aricapital Management Company, and Sergey Kaufman, an analyst at Finam Financial Group, shared his assessment.
Suverov forecasts that the average gas price in Europe will rise to $650 per 1,000 cubic meters in 2027. Kaufman believes prices could reach $800 per 1,000 cubic meters. According to Vedomosti’s calculations based on World Bank data, the average gas price in Europe was approximately $600 per 1,000 cubic meters in January-September 2026. In 2025, gas in Europe cost around $427 per 1,000 cubic meters.

title: No, the iPhone Duo isn’t a small phone
body:
When we published our review of the iPhone Duo, I got a lot of hopeful questions from my fellow Mini fans who took note of the cover screen’s Mini-ish 5.4-inch size. “Is this… a small phone that turns into a tablet?” they asked. And I’m sorry to be the bearer of bad news, but no. The Duo is not the small phone we’ve been looking for.
I wish it was. I like a small phone. I own an iPhone 13 Mini that I refuse to surrender, even though it barely lasts a full day.
But the Duo is thick and heavy. You will feel its weight every time you read an email, scroll Instagram, or put it in your pocket. It is a dense phone, and after a week with the Duo, my 13 Mini feels almost comically light. Like, can this be a real phone? Surely not.
[Image: Thanks to its wider format, the Duo gives you a bigger keyboard compared to the Mini. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/DSC04352_processed.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
The Duo’s front panel is also quite a bit wider than the 13 Mini — 84.1mm compared to 64.2mm — which makes it much harder to reach your thumb all the way across like you can with the Mini. The Duo tries to compensate for this by putting controls on the right side, which helps a bit. As reported by Wired, Apple is also planning to add its reachability feature to the Duo later this year to help out in those moments. But inevitably there’s something I need to tap that’s out of one-handed reach on the Duo, and the illusion of using a small phone is gone. On the other hand, you get a much larger onscreen keyboard with the Duo; the Mini’s feels cramped by comparison.
It comes down to this: Liking a small phone isn’t the same thing as liking a small screen. Sure, all things being equal, a big screen is nicer for a lot of stuff. But I’ll put up with a tiny screen to enjoy the benefits of a phone so small I can forget it’s in my pocket. It’s a tradeoff. The iPhone Duo offers a different set of tradeoffs. Put up with the small screen on the outside, and you’ll be rewarded with a really big screen whenever you need it. And that small screen is attached to a big, heavy phone.
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/DSC04358_processed.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/DSC04357_processed.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
This sounds like I hated using the Duo, but I didn’t. I just had to calibrate my expectations. I think you’ll be disappointed by the Duo if you expect a small phone that expands into an iPad Mini. But if you go in expecting a small-screen experience you can tolerate in order to get a much bigger screen whenever you want, you’ll have the right idea about the Duo.
Photography by Allison Johnson / The Verge

title: 6 Israeli soldiers wounded in Palestinian op. in West Bank
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 23 (MNA) – In the latest martyrdom-seeking operation by Palestinians in the occupied West Bank, local media report that six Israeli soldier were injured.
Following the wounding of six Israeli soldiers in an anti-Zionist operation in Hebron (Al-Khalil), Netanyahu ordered the city to be placed under siege and security measures to be tightened across the West Bank.
According to Al Jazeera, Israeli media reported that Benjamin Netanyahu, the Prime Minister of the Zionist regime, ordered the cancellation of all Likud party election-related activities scheduled for today, following a shooting incident early this morning at the northern entrance to the city of Hebron, in the southern occupied West Bank.
Reports indicate that two Palestinians were killed and six Israeli soldiers were wounded in the shooting. Israel Army Radio stated that the two gunmen were residents of Hebron. According to the Hebrew-language outlet Walla, preliminary investigations suggest that two young Palestinians caught the Israeli forces off guard, opening fire as the soldiers approached them.
The Israeli military announced that the Chief of the General Staff has ordered the reinforcement of troops in the central region and has authorized the establishment of a complete security cordon around the city of Hebron and its surrounding villages.
The Zionist regime's military further stated: "Our forces are currently besieging Hebron and launching an extensive offensive operation in the area."
Netanyahu also announced that he has instructed security forces to place Hebron under siege and to completely seal off the West Bank. He claimed that Israeli forces had prevented a larger-scale attack in the West Bank, and asserted that they would pursue Hamas operatives—and those backing them—anywhere and at any time.

title: ODA Press Tour Showcases Japan-Supported Development Projects Across Palau
body: By Laurel Marewibuel KOROR, Palau — Journalists and community participants joined the Embassy of Japan’s Official Development Assistance (ODA) Press Tour on Oct. 21, 2026, visiting several development initiatives across the country focused on health, judicial infrastructure, and public works maintenance. Media visited the wheelchair lifts at the Judiciary that provide access to persons with disabilities. Photo credit: Laurel Marewibuel The tour opened in Ngaraard State at a community table-top garden managed by the local government. The garden operates under Peace Winds Japan’s project, “Establishing a Sustainable Health Screening System and Supporting Dietary Improvements for the Prevention of Non-Communicable Diseases in the Republic of Palau.” Building on earlier health screening initiatives from 2022 to 2025, the one-year project aims to institutionalize preventive care, expand health screenings, and promote nutrition education through cooking classes, peer support groups, and gardening outreach. Participants then visited the Judiciary Building in Melekeok State, following the completion of a USD $154,000 renovation project finished in August 2026. Funded via a January 2025 grant agreement between the Embassy of Japan and the Bureau of Public Works, the upgrades added wheelchair lifts at the main entrance and enclosed parking areas to improve accessibility for elderly visitors and individuals with physical disabilities. The renovation marks the 105th project completed in Palau under Japan’s Grant Assistance for Grassroots Projects (GGP) program, which has supported non-profit and municipal community projects since 1999. The itinerary concluded at the Japan-Palau Friendship Bridge, where Tkakl Mekreos, chief of Road and Bridge Maintenance, provided an overview of a Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) technical cooperation program titled “Establishment of Asset Management System of Roads, Bridges and Heavy Machineries in SIDS.” The program focuses on data-driven planning, regular inspections, technical training, and regional maintenance coordination across Micronesia. Connecting Koror and Babeldaob, the bridge serves as a major conduit for traffic, utility lines, and communication systems, and will reach its 25th anniversary in January 2027. The tour ended with a luncheon hosted by Japanese Ambassador to Palau Kenichi Kasahara, attended by representative members of Peace Winds Japan and JICA Overseas Cooperation Volunteers (JOCV). The volunteer program, active in Palau since 1997, currently has 26 volunteers serving across education, healthcare, infrastructure, and environmental sectors. title: Navantia, Multiverse Computing join hands on AI for naval defense
body:
Navantia and Multiverse Computing have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to establish a framework for strategic collaboration on the development, validation and deployment of artificial intelligence and quantum-inspired solutions applied to naval defense.
The agreement was signed by Enrique Lizaso , co-founder and chief executive officer (CEO) of Multiverse Computing, and Gonzalo Mateo-Guerrero , Chief Operating Officer (COO) of Navantia.
The companies will explore new lines of work in efficient AI for embedded systems and for surface and submarine platforms; signal processing and situational awareness; mission planning and logistics optimisation; and Command, Control, Communications and Intelligence (C4I) systems. They will also assess joint proposals for European defense and innovation programs.
Multiverse Computing will make its CompactifAI technology available to the collaboration in order to optimise AI models and facilitate their adaptation to environments constrained by computing capacity, power or connectivity.
On the other hand, Navantia will contribute its product knowledge, naval architecture, systems integration, operational requirements and life-cycle expertise. This complementarity will make it possible to move from experimentation towards AI capabilities embedded in naval products and solutions, according to the partners.
For Navantia, the agreement represents a step forward in incorporating artificial intelligence into its portfolio of products and services and in consolidating in-house industrial capability. The collaboration seeks to accelerate product evolution, strengthen technological sovereignty and broaden participation in national and European initiatives.
For Multiverse Computing, the agreement strengthens its presence in the defense sector, one of the areas where the efficiency of artificial intelligence models has the most direct impact. The company, headquartered in San Sebastián, develops quantum-inspired technology aimed at reducing the size and the inference cost of AI models.
“The agreement will make it possible to apply artificial intelligence to Navantia’s products and accelerate their evolution towards more efficient and more advanced naval solutions,” said Mateo-Guerrero.
“In artificial intelligence applied to defence, the difficult step is not the demonstration but the integration: moving from a model that works in the laboratory to a capability that a naval system can sustain throughout its entire life cycle. That is the ground we want to work on with Navantia,” commented Lizaso.
To remind, Navantia recently signed a contract to repair and modernize two Mandume-class patrol vessels for the Angolan Navy.

title: Zelensky Yacht Fake: How Russia’s Doppelgänger Network Works
body:
A Kremlin-linked disinformation network collected remarks by then-US Sen. JD Vance as evidence that a fabricated story about yacht purchases linked to President Volodymyr Zelensky had reached American political debate, The Insider reported on Wednesday, Oct. 21.
The investigation cited hacked correspondence between Russia’s Presidential Administration and the Social Design Agency, one of the organizations behind the operation known as Doppelgänger.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The yacht allegations appeared in Russian newspaper Komsomolskaya Pravda and on DC Weekly, an English-language website publishing fabricated news.
In December 2023, Vance asked on Steve Bannon’s podcast: “So that one of Zelensky’s ministers can buy a bigger yacht?”
The Insider said operatives collected his remarks, other reactions and attempts to debunk the story in internal files prepared for the Presidential Administration. Those records document what the campaign claimed as a success; they do not establish that Vance knowingly repeated Russian disinformation.
Doppelgänger combines invented stories with websites designed to resemble legitimate news outlets and social media accounts that amplify the material.
As Kyiv Post previously reported , French investigators identified fake websites and accounts circulating pro-Russian content and attacking Ukraine and its leaders in 2023.
The deception borrows the appearance of familiar publications to make fabricated reports seem credible. Coordinated accounts then help those reports reach audiences beyond the websites themselves.
EU DisinfoLab, which named the operation , has documented impersonations of outlets including Le Monde, The Guardian and Der Spiegel, as well as government institutions. Its research identifies weakening support for Ukraine and exploiting divisions in countries supporting Kyiv as central objectives.
The Insider’s investigation describes a broader workforce producing multilingual material and using artificial intelligence to identify politically sensitive subjects. It also reports efforts to attract attention from prominent figures, including Elon Musk and Vance.
The investigation builds on earlier disclosures by US authorities.
In September 2024, the US Justice Department announced the seizure of 32 internet domains used in Russian government-directed influence campaigns known as Doppelgänger.
The department alleged that Russian organizations, including the Social Design Agency, operated under the direction of the Presidential Administration and its first deputy chief of staff, Sergei Kiriyenko.
Their objectives included reducing international support for Ukraine, promoting Russian interests and influencing US and other foreign elections.
Investigators described the use of fabricated identities, paid advertisements and AI-generated material to drive readers toward deceptive websites.
Paid advertising also helped the operation reach audiences on mainstream platforms.
Research reported by AFP estimated that Meta received approximately $338,000 for at least 8,000 sponsored posts linked to the campaign between August 2023 and November 2024.
The researchers, from Check First, Reset Tech and AI Forensics, said their findings captured only part of the activity. Responding to AFP, Meta pointed to its earlier investigations and said it had blocked tens of thousands of posts associated with the network.
The Insider’s files also covered the Stars of David painted on buildings in Paris in autumn 2023 and a fabricated video threatening visitors to the Paris Olympics.
The French Foreign Ministry publicly attributed the amplification of the graffiti photographs to the Russian-linked RRN/Doppelgänger network in November 2023.
French investigators identified 1,095 automated accounts on X that published 2,589 posts. At the time, the ministry distinguished that finding from the separate investigation into who commissioned the graffiti.
The Insider said the network’s internal reporting recorded both the spread of its fabrications and the responses they generated, including debunks.
For its Kremlin overseers, a false story reaching an American politician’s remarks could become evidence of influence—even after the original allegation had been exposed.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Global Hamas fundraising network shut down after 'Gaza aid diverted'
body: A global network that fund raised for Hamas by allegedly diverting financial donations intended as humanitarian aid for Gaza has been closed down by a series of arrests. The fund-raising operation for the militant group was controlled by Saleem Alzaq, 45, a senior Hamas propaganda official, according to prosecutors. US authorities claim that Mr Alzaq's network raised $2 million for Hamas, of which $1.5 million was received after the 2023 October 7 attack on Israel . Arrests have included founders of two charities based in France, who are alleged to have worked with Mr Alzaq. One of the charities, Association Baraka, was set up by Faouzi Barika, a 35-year-old Algerian, just days after October 7 to allegedly act as the vehicle to raise funds for Hamas. The charity has been closed down following the swoop by France's security service, the General Directorate for Internal Security (DGSI). Two weeks after the US notices, the charity website was still operating an apparent link to an international payment system. PayPal told The National it was not processing payments for either the individual or the organisation. Days later the website closed. Mr Alzaq, Mr Barika and Association Baraka have been placed under sanctions by the US under the Specially Designated Global Terrorist (SDGT) designation. Code words Mr Alzaq has been charged for his alleged role in the social media fund-raising under the guise of aid for Gaza. If convicted, he faces a 20-year prison sentence in the US, although he is currently in Gaza. The indictment filed against Mr Alzaq in a New York court states that he and his “co-conspirators have solicited donations from around the world” which were “purportedly to provide humanitarian aid to the people of Gaza”. Mr Alzaq's activities allowed Hamas to “exploit the sympathy and generosity of the international public at the expense of the Palestinian people”, it adds. In a conversation with an undercover US law enforcement officer, Mr Alzaq is alleged to have used coded language for his activities. Hamas was referred to as “the Green”, and he boasted that he could deliver monthly donations to “them” using terms such as “buy bread” or “give it to the bakeries”. US arrests Three men have been arrested in the US for allegedly donating funds to Hamas through the financing network. Abdel Adhami, 35, and Omar Adhami, 33, from Louisiana, and Raed Yousef, 56, from Florida, were arrested for allegedly donating a total of $155,000. The Adhamis and Mr Yousef face a number of charges, including providing material support to a foreign terrorist organisation. They face 20 years in prison if convicted. Mr Alzaq's alleged fund-raising activity fits into a pattern in which Hamas has benefited from organisations purporting to be charities, the US authorities say. French network Included in the French round of arrests and accused of being part of Mr Alzaq's financing network is Amel Oualid, 39. She was also arrested by the DGSI. The Algerian citizen and her charity, Ensemble C Mieux, have also been sanctioned under an SDGT designation for allegedly raising money for Hamas. Mr Barika and Ms Oualid are also accused of sending hundreds of thousands of dollars in cryptocurrency to Mr Alzaq. The “investigations and arrests spanned multiple jurisdictions in the United States and across international borders”, said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A Eisenberg. “Money is the lifeblood of terrorist organisations, and the arrests disrupted a global financing network that was supplying Hamas with the funds needed to continue its campaign of destroying innocent lives,” he added. The US Department of Justice describes Mr Alzaq as being a battalion deputy in the Al Qassam Brigades , Hamas’s armed wing. He serves in the photography department of its media office, a Hamas propaganda operation. In this role, he has photographed Hamas events, including those led by senior leaders such as the late Ismail Haniyeh and Yahya Sinwar .

title: OpenAI lowers valuation target, raises up to $30 billion
body:
OpenAI is closing in on a new funding round of up to $30 billion but has lowered its valuation target to get there. The company originally pitched investors on a $1.4 trillion valuation, according to internal documents obtained by the Financial Times . That number has since dropped to $1.25 trillion, CNBC also reports . The FT says demand was weaker than in previous rounds, with some backers experiencing "indigestion" after heavy investments in earlier fundraises.
UAE investors and investment firm Coatue are leading the $30 billion round. The funding is being positioned as a bridge ahead of a potential IPO. OpenAI is also negotiating a commercial deal to secure additional compute capacity through the UAE, according to CNBC.
OpenAI confidentially filed an IPO prospectus with the SEC in June. CFO Sarah Friar told employees in August that OpenAI would be a publicly traded company by 2027. CEO Sam Altman said in September that the timing was unfavorable for going public . He had already communicated that internally back in June. Competitor Anthropic is also preparing an IPO and is targeting a valuation between $1.5 and $2 trillion. Ad Ad

title: Sheikh Khaled tours cultural spots in Athens during official visit
body: Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed, Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi, toured two of Greece's leading cultural attractions on Friday as part of his official visit to the country. Sheikh Khaled viewed the extensive collection of artwork at the National Gallery of Greece and also visited the National Archaeological Museum in Athens. He was briefed on the creative works at the gallery that reflect the rich history and heritage of Greece and the evolution of its art scene. Officially known as the National Gallery – Alexandros Soutsos Museum, it was founded in 1900 and is home to more than 20,000 exhibits, including paintings, sculptures and prints from the post-Byzantine period to the modern era. Picturing the past Among the artworks adorning the walls of the National Gallery is Street Market, a painting by Greek artist Panayiotis Tetsis that captures the bustle of everyday life in the capital. Measuring more than 12 metres wide and nearly 2.5 metres high, the oil-on-canvas triptych depicts a crowded open-air market, with shoppers and vendors filling the scene. The painting was inspired by a weekly market on Xenokratous Street in central Athens, where the artist maintained his studio. The archaeological museum, the largest of its kind in Greece, was established towards the end of the 19th century and contains a treasure trove of antiquities. خالد بن محمد بن زايد، ولي عهد أبوظبي، يزور المعرض الوطني اليوناني في أثينا، وسموّه يطّلع على أعمال توثّق تطوّر الفن اليوناني، وتعكس دور الفنون في التعبير عن هوية الشعوب وتاريخها وتعزيز التواصل والتفاهم بين الثقافات. pic.twitter.com/J3BPV1BWPu — مكتب أبوظبي الإعلامي (@ADMediaOffice) October 23, 2026 Landmark visit Sheikh Khaled had on Thursday held talks with Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis as major deals were agreed on between the countries. Discussions between at the Prime Minister's Office centred on efforts to bolster collaboration across sectors including energy, infrastructure, health care, advanced technology and health care. Sheikh Khaled emphasised the UAE's desire to strengthen long-standing relations with Greece to support the aspirations of both nations. It was also announced during the visit that the UAE is to invest a further €15 billion ($16.8 billion) in Greece as part of a joint initiative between the countries.

title: Ghana wins LA 2028 Olympic boxing qualifier hosting rights
body: Ghana has secured hosting rights for the 2028 Olympic Boxing African Qualification Tournament, scheduled for August 2027.This follows a successful bid application by the Ghana Boxing Federation (GBF). Paulo Ferreira, the World Boxing Director of Events, formally informed the Ghana Boxing Federation of the decision on Tuesday, October 21, 2026, of the decision. Subsequent to this, a ‘‘Host City Agreement’’ will be formalized between the International Olympic Committee and Ghana. The Host City Agreement is a binding legal contract between the IOC and a selected city that hosts its tournament. For the most part, the agreement clearly spells out all local operating expenses, including public security, police escorts, medical services, and specialized infrastructure upgrades and whose responsibility it is. In the past, the IOC (and in the case of football, FIFA) has retained all major commercial revenues—including broadcast rights, ticket sales, and official sponsorships—while host cities receive no direct share of those earnings. For Ghana’s part, the government, through the Ministry for Sports and Recreation and the Accra Metropolitan Assembly, will assume all associated costs, including intra-and inter-city transportation, accommodation arrangements, existing boxing infrastructure requirements, etc. However, the operational support and expertise will come from the Ghana Boxing Federation. A tentative date of August 13–22, 2027, has been set for the tournament.

title: Taiwan NCHU’s Veterinarian visit Palau to strengthen Bilateral Cooperation and Youth Global Engagement
body: Date: October 18, 2026 Taiwan and Palau enjoy longstanding diplomatic ties and a close partnership, with continued cooperation in healthcare, education, and human resource development. Following a well-received veterinary outreach mission in 2025, the “StrayLOHAS” University Social Responsibility (USR) Project of National Chung Hsing University (NCHU) was once again invited to Palau in October 2026. Through veterinary services and training for local volunteers, the initiative further strengthens people-to-people exchanges and demonstrates Taiwan’s commitment to contributing its professional expertise to international cooperation. Ambassador Andy Kang-I Chen of the Embassy of the Republic of China (Taiwan) in the Republic of Palau attended the team’s training session and thanked Koror State for hosting the mission. He noted that this mission is more than a professional exchange. Stray dogs are a real challenge for Palau’s tourism, as a number of visitors have been bitten, and addressing the issue benefits residents, visitors, and the animals themselves. By helping Palau tackle this challenge and improve animal welfare, the cooperation reflects the partnership between Taiwan and Palau. The Embassy also welcomes further opportunities for young Taiwanese professionals to contribute their expertise, respond to the needs of partner communities, and showcase Taiwan’s values and capabilities on the international stage. USR StrayLOHAS Project integrates veterinary education with community engagement, cultivating veterinary professionals with practical clinical skills while addressing stray animal population management, shelter animal healthcare, and animal welfare. In recent years, the project has expanded its outreach beyond Taiwan, sharing its experience in veterinary medicine and professional training through international exchanges and hands-on collaboration. These efforts highlight Taiwan’s contributions to advancing animal health and welfare through education and professional partnerships. Building on last year’s collaboration, USR StrayLOHAS Project dispatched a seven-member professional team to Palau to conduct a three-day veterinary outreach mission at the Koror State Animal Shelter. The mission received an enthusiastic response from the local community, with 25 surgical procedures scheduled over three working days, including spay and neuter surgeries and other soft tissue procedures. Free veterinary consultations were also arranged for local animals. Recognizing the limited veterinary workforce and medical resources available in Palau, the team brought essential veterinary supplies from Taiwan to support clinical services and help alleviate the workload of the local government veterinarian responsible for animal healthcare and shelter operations. Beyond providing veterinary services, this year’s mission places particular emphasis on local capacity building. USR StrayLOHAS Project team organized practical training sessions for local animal care volunteers, covering basic veterinary assistance skills, including needle handling and radiographic imaging procedures. The team also provided free educational materials to promote environmental hygiene and awareness of zoonotic disease prevention. Through knowledge sharing and community education, the initiative seeks to strengthen local animal care capabilities and ensure that the benefits of bilateral cooperation extend beyond the mission itself. The continued engagement of USR StrayLOHAS Project team reflects Taiwan’s commitment to addressing the needs of its diplomatic allies through professional expertise and educational cooperation. By encouraging young professionals to apply their knowledge and skills in international settings, the initiative highlights the role of Taiwan’s higher education institutions in fostering global engagement and meaningful contributions to partner communities. Such exchanges further strengthen the friendship between the peoples of Taiwan and Palau and reinforce the longstanding partnership between the two countries. title: Israel orders closure of West Bank after soldiers kill 2 men behind an alleged attack
body:
Israeli soldiers and emergency personnel gather near ambulances following a shooting attack near Yehuda Junction, near Hebron, in the occupied West Bank, Friday, Oct. 23, 2026. Mahmoud Illean/AP hide caption
HEBRON, West Bank — Israeli soldiers shot and killed two men who the military said had launched an attack near the city of Hebron in the occupied West Bank on Friday morning. At least five people were injured, including some critically.
The army said it prevented a "terror attack against Israeli civilians" and that the gunmen carried an M16 rifle and a handgun. It did not elaborate on the target of the alleged attack. There was also no word on the identities of the two dead and those injured.
A few hours later, Israel ordered the army to prepare for a full closure of the West Bank. The office of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said it instructed security forces to immediately cordon off the city of Hebron and prepare to fully close all of the West Bank, starting Friday.
The deadly shooting comes as Israeli voters will decide next Tuesday whether to grant Netanyahu yet another term as prime minister — or usher in a new era of Israeli politics. The election comes three years after the Hamas-led attacks on Israel that triggered the war in Gaza.
Israel's government has warned of potential attacks by the country's "enemies" in the lead-up to the election.
Following the shooting, Netanyahu held an emergency meeting of his Security Cabinet and officials from top military and security agencies. He blamed Hamas, saying the militant group was "planning a major attack aimed at murdering innocent civilians."
"Our brave soldiers thwarted this attack with courage and determination," he said, without elaborating on what the planned attack entailed.
"I commend them for their actions and wish our wounded a speedy recovery," he added but did not say if the wounded were soldiers or civilians.
Earlier Friday Israel's far-right national security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, known for extremist views, said that the attack shows that Israel needs to restrict the Palestinians' freedom of movement in the West Bank.
"The lives of the residents of Judea and Samaria, of the settlers, the lives of the soldiers, the lives of the police officers, the lives of our fighters are a million times more important than freedom of movement," he said, using an Israeli reference to the West Bank.
Ahead of the anniversary of the Oct. 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack that triggered the war, Netanyahu said the Palestinian militant group could attack Israel in a bid to influence the outcome of the elections. He did not provide evidence to back up the claim.
Emergency responders said five people were injured, some critically, and were being evacuated to hospitals in Israel. A statement from the responders said gunfire was still ongoing as they arrived at the scene of the attack near the Yehuda Junction in the morning.
Two men in their 20s had gunshot wounds to their lower limbs, one was unconscious and seriously injured, the responders said.
"We arrived at a difficult scene while shooting was still taking place in the area," said Tzuriel Edri with the response team.
An investigation was underway, authorities said.
Also Friday, the army said soldiers and Israeli security and intelligence agencies conducted dozens of operations in the West Bank and apprehended dozens of people, including those affiliated with Hamas and Islamic Jihad militant groups. It also said it had located weapons, including M16 rifles and submachine guns.
Closures of the West Bank, such as the one ordered Friday, are growing more common in the territory. It's the fourth time in the past month that Israel has imposed restrictions across the area, shutting gates and checkpoints connecting Palestinian villages to major roads.
Meanwhile, Israeli roads in the territory remain open to Israeli drivers, including settlers, who can still travel through the area but may face delays.

title: US stresses there is no military solution to Sudan war in Geneva talks
body: There is no military solution to the civil war in Sudan, where the fighting is fuelling further instability in the region, a senior US official said. Massad Boulos , President Donald Trump's senior adviser for Arab and African affairs, said Washington officials this week joined representatives of 27 countries in Geneva for the sixth Consultative Meeting on Sudan. "Every day that this war continues comes at a devastating cost to Sudanese civilians and risks spreading further instability to the region," Mr Boulos said in a post on X on Thursday. The impact of the conflict on the wider region was underscored this week when a drone strike killed four people in Chad, near Sudan's western border. At least 14 were injured, an official from Chad's Wadi-Fira province said on Thursday. Sudan’s civil war , which began in April 2023 between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), has repeatedly spilled over into Chad. International efforts aimed at ending the conflict have so far been unsuccessful. Mr Boulos voiced strong support for the efforts of the Quintet – which comprises the African Union, Arab League, UN, EU and Intergovernmental Authority on Development – to enable an inclusive and credible Sudanese-led political process to take place. He added that those efforts complemented US engagement with the Quad, which also includes the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Egypt, to press for a humanitarian truce that could pave the way for a permanent ceasefire. During the Geneva meeting, participants called on all parties to the conflict to engage in good faith to pursue de-escalation, protect civilians and commit to a humanitarian truce. The UAE, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Qatar, Turkey, the UK, Chad, China, France, Germany, Russia, Switzerland and South Sudan were among the nations represented. Mr Boulos thanked Switzerland and the UN for hosting the meeting and said participants had collectively raised their voices in support of ending the conflict. In Geneva, the U.S. joined 27 partner countries and international organizations at the 6th Consultative Meeting on Sudan. Our message was clear: Sudan's war must end, and there is no military solution to the conflict. Every day that this war continues comes at a devastating cost… pic.twitter.com/HfVLnWbAEn — U.S. Senior Advisor for Arab and African Affairs (@US_SrAdvisorAF) October 22, 2026 African civil society groups this month called on Sudan to allow international inspectors into the country to investigate accusations that SAF used chemical weapons in the war. In a resolution adopted at the end of a three-day forum in Senegal's capital Dakar, the groups urged the African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights to demand that Sudan allow the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons to send technical teams into the country. Both the SAF and the RSF have been accused by the UN of war crimes and rights breaches. The conflict has created one of the world’s largest humanitarian crises. More than 14 million people have been displaced and nearly 20 million face hunger, the UN World Food Programme has said.

title: Opinion: I Spent 15 Years in Government. Here Is What the State Can Learn Next
body: Zhandos Sabit spent more than 15 years in Kazakhstan’s public service, including the Ministry of National Economy, a regional akimat, and the Prosecutor General’s Office. He now works in the private sector. In March 2014, I went to a meeting in Astana on the development of the machine-building industry. It was held at the then Ministry of Industry and New Technologies. Officials from central and local bodies came, along with the National Chamber of Entrepreneurs and several business owners. I was there as a representative of a state body. When the entrepreneurs began to talk about problems in the industry that we had never heard of, and about how to solve them, I was surprised. They were asking how to increase local content. We were asking whether a proposal complied with current legislation. It turned out that we civil servants knew the resolutions and laws of the sector, and not much beyond that. We sat at one table and spoke about different things. I have seen the same in other sectors since. My former colleagues may take offense, but I will say what I think: many civil servants, myself included in those years, were lawyers and bureaucrats first. That is how the system trains us. Faced with a problem, the first question is whether an idea contradicts the law, and only rarely whether the idea works. Nobody can be blamed for this, because the rules are what an official is held responsible for. It does mean that civil servants should lean on people who know a sector from the inside and take their suggestions seriously. I saw another side of this when I worked in a regional akimat. We prepared a road map for developing the communications sector in the region and agreed it with the central body. Wherever an item needed a decision from the center or money from the republican budget, the central body either struck it out or rewrote it as “study the issue”, with “provide information” as the expected result. I understand why: the center answers for the budget and for every precedent it sets. But how long can an issue be studied? Colleagues in the region put it bluntly: go and fight for the money from the republican budget yourselves. An idea can sit for years between two levels of government, and nobody has done anything wrong. Kazakhstan’s “Listening State” concept raises a question: what happens to what the state hears? I spent more than 15 years in public service, and my proposal comes from that work. Kazakhstan already has channels for individual appeals, and eOtinish is one of them. They are there to answer a person. My proposal is the next step: a platform for solving problems that keep coming back. Its unit would be a problem together with a proposed solution, not a letter. Appeals, petitions, input from business associations, and regional statistics are kept in separate places today, and an AI-assisted system could read them together. If dozens of complaints about delayed services come from different regions, they may trace back to one outdated procedure. Instead of dozens of replies, the responsible ministry would receive one question: why does this procedure exist, and can it change? People would still make every decision. Entrepreneurs, researchers, civic activists, and local communities could bring their own proposals to the same platform. I would like working groups of qualified specialists from each sector to examine them. The people who know the sector would shape the ideas, and the ministries would check them against the law and the budget. Young and old, scientists and critics should all be able to take part. What happens after that is crucial, and the road map shows why. A proposal that needs a decision from the center or money from the republican budget should get a clear answer within a fixed time: either it goes ahead, perhaps as a pilot, or it is declined, with reasons. “Study the issue” should not be an acceptable outcome. I would place responsibility for monitoring deadlines with a designated body in the Presidential Administration or the Prime Minister’s Office. Once a working group endorses a proposal, the responsible ministry should have 60 days to approve it, possibly as a pilot, or decline it with written reasons. Overdue responses would be escalated to the coordinating body, with each proposal’s status and deadline published. When a proposal looks promising, one region could test it for a year under a special regime, so that the decision rests on results. Once a year, the results would be published, together with a list of what changed because of citizens’ proposals, and the best of them would go into a nationwide plan. I am not saying that we lack strategies and programs. We have plenty, and the country has gained from them. Many were prepared together with foreign experts, who bring valuable experience. But an expert in Europe cannot know what is happening in a remote village, and the real capacities of our regions are best known to the people living there. Local specialists should take a larger part in drafting. There is also the matter of continuity. The “Ak Bulak” program for 2011–2020 was folded into the Regional Development Program to 2020 in 2014 . There may have been good reasons. Still, it sometimes looks as if a new program takes over before the old one has been fully assessed, and the goals that were not met quietly drop out of view. A public record of what each program achieved would help the next one, and would give credit to the people who carried out the first. The law and the budget set limits on what can be done, and a citizen should be able to see how each decision was reached. title: Russia to Unveil ‘Anti-Drone Dome’ at Africa Summit
body:
Russia will unveil a new air defense system dubbed the “Anti-Drone Dome” at the Russia-Africa summit between Oct. 28 and 29 in Moscow, seeking to sell its military technology abroad as Ukrainian drone strikes continue to hit targets across Russia.
State arms exporter Rosoboronexport announced the planned presentation on Friday, according to Interfax Russia .
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The system combines radar detection, electronic jamming, weapons and physical barriers to protect civilians, military personnel, bridges, buildings, energy infrastructure and industrial facilities. A separate version is designed to shield moving convoys and cargo.
“All the tools and solutions used in it have proven their effectiveness in real conditions,” Rosoboronexport CEO Alexander Mikheyev said.
The company said the system relies entirely on Russian-made equipment and can be tailored to individual customers and facilities, though the effectiveness of similar systems, such as the Arena-M anti-drone system deployed on Russian tanks in the summer of 2026, has been questioned on the front lines .
The sales pitch also comes as Russia struggles to prevent Ukrainian drones from reaching targets deep inside its territory. Repeated attacks have struck oil refineries, warehouses and data centers, putting pressure on Russian air defenses.
In September, Ukrainian attacks damaged several major refineries, forcing some to suspend or reduce production. By mid-September, half of Russia’s six largest diesel-producing refineries had significantly cut or halted output .
Ukrainian drones have also reached targets hundreds of kilometers inside Russia, including facilities near Moscow.
In May, Russian President Vladimir Putin replaced the head of Russia’s Aerospace Forces amid a reported surge in Ukrainian drone attacks.
The force’s new chief, Alexander Chaiko, later reportedly survived a suicide bombing at an upscale Moscow restaurant in August.
The planned presentation also comes as Moscow seeks to strengthen military and political ties with African governments and promote Russian-made weapons.
The Anti-Drone Dome will give Rosoboronexport a new product to pitch to potential customers, although the company has yet to publish detailed performance data or demonstrate the system publicly.
For now, Rosoboronexport’s claims of effectiveness in real-world conditions remain unverified independently.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: MRT-3 privatization eyed by mid-2027 under P103.6-billion deal
body: MANILA, Philippines – The Metro Rail Transit Line 3 (MRT-3) may be privatized by mid-2027, with the Department of Transportation (DOTr) set to bid out the train line under a P103.6-billion public-private partnership project this year. The decision to privatize the train line comes after President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s order to prioritize the modernization of MRT-3. DOTr Secretary Giovanni “Banoy” Lopez said the government would retain control over fares of MRT-3 under the proposed arrangement. “Through public-private partnership, we bring in the expertise and investment this line needs. Ang kailangan natin dito ‘yung may matagal nang experience sa pagpapatakbo ng riles para sa kapakinabangan ng mga komyuter. At lilinawin ko po, mananatili pa rin sa DOTr ang pagtatakda ng pamasahe ,” Lopez said in a statement released on Friday, October 23. (What we need here is an entity with extensive experience in operating railways for the benefit of commuters. And let me make this clear, the DOTr will still be responsible for setting fares.) Under the arrangement, a private company will be responsible for operating, maintaining, and upgrading the railway under a concession agreement. The project includes replacing trains and upgrading the signaling system to improve the line’s capacity, reliability, and efficiency. Payments to the private operator, or concessionaire, will be linked to its delivery of services and compliance with performance standards covering train availability, reliability, cleanliness, and maintenance. The agreement is intended to hold the operator accountable for the quality of service it provides to commuters. The DOTr said about 100 local and international companies have already expressed interest in the MRT-3 project. – Rappler.com

title: Hacking attempts rise after flaws found in program affecting 70 percent of websites
body:
The homepage of the PHP.net website is seen on Thursday in Singapore. Cybersecurity flaws were recently identified in the popular PHP programming language, which is used on a vast number of websites across the world, including those of major companies and national governments. The PHP Foundation released two patches designed to fix the vulnerabilities. Yong Teck Lim/Getty Images hide caption
A few months ago AI caused global alarm after autonomous agents were found to have cheated on evaluations and then tried to cover it up, in what became known as the "Hugging Face hack."
This week, AI and hacking are back in the spotlight with AI technology credited to have helped prevent a global cybersecurity crisis.
Cybersecurity firm Wiz Research, using OpenAI technology, announced on Wednesday it had discovered security flaws in a computer programming language that helps run some 70% of the world's websites.
OpenAI called the bug "one of the most impactful vulnerabilities in recent memory." Wiz Research warned that its "successful exploitation could allow attackers to take control of affected servers, steal sensitive data, and deface the websites running on them."
Corporations and governments from the U.K. to Japan are now rushing to prevent hackers from capitalizing on the flaws.
The flaws were discovered in a major programming language called PHP, short for Hypertext Preprocessor. Wiz Research calls PHP "the backbone of the web," saying the technology has underpinned much of the internet since the 1990s.
"These findings rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history," the firm said, adding that before publicly disclosing the flaw, teams had worked on building a solution that's now available to websites to protect themselves.
As countries scrambled to prevent cyberattacks, numerous websites and pages were taken offline in the past few days. The U.S. National Security Agency warned organizations using PHP to "maintain heightened awareness" over the coming weeks. The U.K.'s National Cyber Security Center called on organizations to "take immediate action" to update their websites to the latest fixed or patched version.
Dozens of British and Finnish government services were taken offline this week. In France, many local government sites were also briefly taken down. China's Industry Ministry urged entities to review security gaps.
In Japan, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi put out "an urgent request for everyone to take action," adding, "If it is difficult to apply the fix patch promptly, temporarily suspending websites and similar measures can be considered an effective way to reduce risk."
Matthew Prince, the head of the cybersecurity firm Cloudflare, said his organization saw tens of thousands of attempts to exploit the flaw in the first 45 minutes of its discovery. That's now in the millions, Prince said on Thursday.
Wiz Research said the flaws in PHP had been present for decades.
"But demonstrating their exploitability required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve," the organization said. The AI models have "substantially reduced that barrier, turning a longstanding flaw into an exploit. "

title: ‘Stop Fanning Embers of Discord among Traditional Institutions in Yorubaland’
body: Sunday Okobi The Isese Religious Association in Oyo, Oyo State, has cautioned members of the public, including bloggers, against unguarded utterances and retroactive actions that could create unnecessary tension and unhealthy developments among traditional institutions in Yorubaland. The Chairman of the Isese Worshippers Committee and the Asiwaju Awo of Oyo, Chief Onifade Olanipekun, gave the warning at a press briefing held at the ancient Palace in Oyo town. Chief Olanipekun said: “Our kings and traditional institutions represent important aspects of our history, identity, customs, and collective heritage. They deserve responsible public engagement, constructive dialogue, and respect, even when opinions differ. “The unity of Yoruba land is a shared responsibility. We must not allow unverified allegations, inflammatory publications, or the actions of a few individuals to create unnecessary divisions among our people and institutions.” He stated that the Isese Religion Association Oyo Alaafin, on behalf of the Isese community and Sàngó worshippers in Oyo, has categorically rejected allegations circulating on social media suggesting that the Isese community and Sàngó worshippers in Oyo have failed to support His Imperial Majesty, the Alaafin of Oyo, Oba Abimbola Akeem Owoade I. According to him, “The association considers this allegation misleading and a misrepresentation of the relationship between the Isese community and the revered traditional institution of the Alaafin of Oyo. We therefore, wish to reassure His Imperial Majesty, the people of Oyo, and the public of our continued commitment to the dignity, honour, and preservation of the paramount ruler’s throne, as well as the cultural heritage and traditional values of Oyo Kingdom. “The Isese community and Sàngó worshippers in Oyo wish to state unequivocally that our support for the Alaafin’s throne did not begin today. Our commitment to this traditional institution has been evident since the installation of His Imperial Majesty as the Alaafin of Oyo and remains firmly rooted in our reverence for our ancestors, our spiritual heritage, and the enduring tradition of our forefathers. “In our religious and cultural understanding, the Alaafin’s throne holds profound historical and spiritual significance. Our reverence for the throne is inseparable from our responsibility to preserve the history, customs, traditions, and identity of Oyo Kingdom for present and future generations.” While pointing out that the association emphasizes that support for the Alaafin’s throne should not be measured solely by social media comments, online confrontations, or public exchanges of insults, Chief Olanipekun noted that genuine commitment to a traditional institution is demonstrated through responsible conduct, constructive engagement, cultural preservation, peaceful advocacy, and practical efforts to safeguard the values it represents. He added: “While we recognise that individuals have the right to express their views responsibly, we strongly reject any attempt to use the name of Isese religion as a justification for insulting traditional rulers, provoking division, or undermining the cultural institutions of Yorubaland. “We, therefore, urge members of the public to distinguish between individuals’ conduct and the established position of the Isese community in Oyo. The actions or statements of individuals on social media should not automatically be attributed to the entire Isese community or interpreted as the official position of our association. “We also appeal to anyone identifying as an Onísẹ̀ṣe, regardless of their state or place of residence, to exercise restraint and demonstrate respect when expressing opinions about the Alaafin, other traditional rulers, and the cultural institutions of Yorubaland.”

title: Cable saboteurs to face up to fourteen years in jail
body: Those who intentionally damage critical undersea energy and telecoms infrastructure would face prison sentences of up to fourteen years and unlimited fines under proposals published today, which also place new security and resilience duties on subsea telecoms providers and give ministers power to intervene where national security is at risk, according to the government. A White Paper published by the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology sets out proposals to update 140-year-old legislation, and marks the start of a twelve-week public consultation. Ian Murray, the Telecoms Minister, said: “Undersea cables are the hidden backbone of modern Britain, carrying the data we rely on every day to message friends and family, do our banking, and run our businesses. “The threats we face have changed dramatically, with suspicious Russian activity around critical undersea infrastructure, yet some of the laws protecting these vital connections date back more than a century. “We intend to modernise those laws with tougher penalties, stronger requirements on industry and new powers to protect our national security, making sure the UK’s critical infrastructure is fit for the threats of today and tomorrow.” Dan Jarvis, the Security Minister, said: “Undersea cables carry the energy and data our country relies on every day. Protecting them is vital to our national security. “We’re toughening the law to stay ahead of those who seek to do us harm. Those who deliberately or recklessly damage our undersea infrastructure will face tougher penalties, including longer prison sentences and unlimited fines. “These measures are part of the work underway across government to protect our critical infrastructure and keep our country safe.” Michael Shanks, the Energy Minister, said: “Undersea pipelines and cables are critical to keeping energy flowing to homes and businesses across the UK. “This legislation will further strengthen deterrence and help ensure we can prevent, detect, and respond to threats against our energy supply.” The fibre-optic cables running along the seabed carry around ninety-nine per cent of Britain’s international data. Undersea pipelines provide seventy-four per cent of the country’s gas supply, and undersea electricity cables carry supply from Europe and from the growing offshore wind sector. The proposals cover four areas, the first of which would modernise criminal law on harmful conduct against telecoms and energy undersea infrastructure through new offences, stronger penalties and new enforcement measures; introduce statutory security and resilience duties for subsea telecoms cable infrastructure providers; create a national security direction power allowing the Secretary of State to direct providers of subsea cable infrastructure and repair capabilities where necessary and proportionate; and establish a regulatory regime covering sensing technologies installed on subsea fibre optic cables. Fibre optic sensing can detect activity at sea, and the government says it could pose national security risks if sensitive data fell into the wrong hands. The government states that Britain already has a highly resilient subsea cable network, and that where cable faults occur they are due to accidents involving anchors or trawler nets dragged across the cables, environmental hazards or technical failures. It adds that suspicious activity around critical undersea infrastructure is increasingly being observed, and that in April the British armed forces exposed a covert Russian submarine operation around critical undersea infrastructure in and around British waters. The Royal Navy has tracked the Russian vessel Yantar in waters around Britain, which this publication covered when the United Kingdom tracked the Russian spy ship amid cable concerns . The Defence Committee reported yesterday that failure to deter Russia in the High North, particularly from underwater threats, puts subsea data cables and energy pipelines in and around British waters at particular risk during peacetime. Its report records that Russia’s Main Directorate for Deep-Sea Research holds assets designed specifically to degrade or destroy critical infrastructure and technological networks, including undersea energy pipelines and data cables. The post Cable saboteurs to face up to fourteen years in jail first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Nikos Karvelas Takes Fresh Legal Action Against Anna Vissi Over New Album
body: Greek composer Nikos Karvelas has reportedly taken further legal action against Anna Vissi, seeking to prevent the popular singer from releasing her upcoming album. Dispute Continues The latest notice follows a series of public developments involving the two prominent figures in Greek music. title: Russia Vows Retaliation After Austria Expels Its Diplomats
body:
Russia’s Foreign Ministry has vowed to issue an “inevitable” response to Austria expelling four of its diplomats, the state-run TASS news agency reported Friday.
Austria’s foreign ministry said earlier that it declared the Vienna-based Russian diplomats personae non gratae over “activities incompatible with their diplomatic status,” a term usually used for spying.
“A response will follow inevitably,” Russia’s Deputy Foreign Minister Dmitry Lyubinsky told TASS without providing further details.
Three of the expelled diplomats worked at Russia’s Embassy in Vienna and one at the Russian delegation to the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) on military security and arms control, the Austrian ministry said.
The move brings the total number of Russian diplomats expelled in Austria over the past six years to 18. While Austria is a neutral country, politically its governments have sided with Ukraine since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022.
In May, Austria expelled three Russian diplomats, citing an “antenna forest” on the roofs of Russian diplomatic buildings that could be used for spying.
Moscow routinely issues tit-for-tat expulsions of diplomats from the host country’s embassy in Moscow.
Vienna is a major diplomatic center, hosting the OSCE and UN organizations such as the International Atomic Energy Agency.

title: Russian strikes hit Kharkiv, Zlatopil and Nova Vodolaha, sparking fires and causing damage
body:
This was reported on Telegram by Mayor Ihor Terekhov, according to Ukrinform.
Strikes were recorded in the Slobidskyi district, where a farm building caught fire . In the Osnovyanskyi district, the enemy struck a high-rise residential building and civilian infrastructure.
Later, it was reported that a private home in the same district had been hit, and a fire broke out at the site. According to Oleh Syniehubov, head of the Kharkiv Regional Military Administration, the roof of a four-story building is also on fire.
On the morning of October 23, the Russians launched an attack —according to preliminary data, with two missiles—on the city of Zlatopil.
“As a result of the Russian attack, several residential buildings and a civilian enterprise were severely damaged,” said Mayor Mykola Baksheev.
In addition, the enemy attacked the village of Nova Vodolaha.
“Today, the enemy struck the village of Nova Vodolaha again. Preliminary reports indicate it was a ‘Banderole’ missile. The strike hit non-residential buildings,” said community leader Oleksandr Yesin.
According to preliminary reports, there were no casualties as a result of these attacks.
In the Bezlyudivka community of Kharkiv Oblast, a large-scale fire broke out in a warehouse building as a result of a Russian strike; a fire train was deployed to extinguish the blaze, according to the State Emergency Service.
“A strike on a private enterprise’s building in the Bezlyudivka community caused damage and sparked a large-scale fire,” the statement said.
The State Emergency Service (SES) noted that, despite the threat of renewed shelling, SES units, firefighters from the local fire department, a fire train, as well as employees and equipment from a Kharkiv municipal utility company have been mobilized to address the aftermath of the enemy attack.
According to preliminary reports, there were no casualties.
As previously reported, Russian invaders launched strikes on Kharkiv and 12 settlements in the region over the past day, resulting in two deaths and 46 injuries, including a child.

title: National currencies account for nearly 100% of Russia-China settlements
body:
HONG KONG, October 23. /TASS/. The share of the ruble and yuan in settlements between Russia and China has reached nearly 100%, while bilateral trade continues to grow steadily, Russian Deputy Finance Minister Ivan Chebeskov, who headed the Russian delegation at the APEC Finance Ministers’ Meeting held in Hong Kong, said in an interview with TASS.
"We meet regularly with our Chinese partners and discuss all issues on our agenda. I would like to point out that the share of national currencies in our settlements with China has already reached almost 100%. Therefore, increasing the use of national currencies in settlements is no longer a pressing issue on our agenda. The mechanisms are working, the partnership is developing, and trade is taking place," the deputy minister said. "We understand that maintaining bilateral trade and the volumes of trade between our countries requires a stable financial infrastructure connecting the two countries’ banking systems. This financial infrastructure has been established and is functioning," he noted.
Chebeskov also pointed out that "all payment mechanisms have already been established, and the ability to use them is also ensured at the legislative level. This has been our key objective since sanctions were first introduced. Everything businesses need is already operational," he added.
The deputy minister recalled that a new law regulating cryptocurrencies had recently entered into force in Russia. "Some further adjustments to the regulation of Russian stablecoins may be necessary. Otherwise, our regulatory framework is generally in place and functioning. Therefore, the introduction of any new mechanisms is not under discussion," Chebeskov said.
"We are, of course, ready to participate in existing international systems. In some cases, we are holding negotiations, while in others, certain restrictions remain. However, there are no infrastructure-related or legislative restrictions on our country’s part," the deputy minister stressed.
Around 500 participants, including delegations from 21 APEC economies, among them Russia, attended the bloc’s Finance Ministers’ Meeting in Hong Kong on October 20-21. This year’s meeting focused on fiscal policies to support households, financing digital infrastructure, ensuring equal access to financial opportunities, and promoting dialogue among young finance professionals within APEC.

title: US forces deployed 600–700 km away from Strait of Hormuz
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 23 (MNA) – Commander of the IRGC Navy says that US forces are no longer present in the Persian Gulf and have moved 600 to 700 kilometers away from the Strait of Hormuz.
“Today, the Americans are not present in the Persian Gulf. They have moved 600 to 700 kilometers away from the Strait of Hormuz, and their vessels are no longer seen in the area,” Ozamayi said.
“The United States no longer has a place in the Strait of Hormuz,” he added.
Ozamayi’s remarks came hours after US President Donald Trump accused Iran of trying to drive up oil prices ahead of the US midterm elections by spreading what he called “fake news” about mine explosions and attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz.
Trump claimed that the volume of oil transiting the strait had now exceeded pre-war levels, arguing that Iran was resorting to various measures to push oil prices higher.
Meanwhile, Brent crude prices rose above $113 per barrel on Friday, reaching their highest level in five months.

title: Poland Reports Detaining Another Suspect, ‘Georgian National’, Over Russian Artist’s Killing
body: Polish authorities reported detaining a second suspect, a 22-year-old Georgian national, on suspicions of “aiding and abetting” the murder of Robert Kuzovkov, also known as Semyon Skrepetsky, a Russian artist critical of President Vladimir Putin and Chechen leader Ramzan Kadyrov. “The court has ordered his pre-trial detention for a period of three months” as the investigation proceeds, ​Tomasz Siemoniak, Polish minister and coordinator of special services, wrote on X on October 22. The suspect was identified as Makhmud A. in Polish media reports that cited Siemoniak. The arrest comes months after Polish authorities reported in June that they detained another suspect, who was “using a Georgian passport.” Kuzovkov was shot dead by an “unidentified gunman” early on June 15 in Biała Podlaska, a small Polish town near the Belarusian border, where he had been granted asylum in 2021. He was known for his caricatures of Vladimir Putin, Chechen leader Ramzan Kadyrov, and Belarusian President Aleksandr Lukashenka, among others. Before these arrests, Polish authorities initially detained two Belarusian citizens in connection with the murder, but later said they were released as no links could be established to the crime.
