title: Anchor Varsity Marks 10 Years of Growth, Holds Combined Convocation
body: Funmi Ogundare Anchor University, Lagos, is set to hold its combined 6th and 7th convocation ceremonies alongside activities marking its 10th anniversary from November 16 to 22, with the Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Samuel Bandele, describing the milestone as an opportunity to reflect on the institution’s growth and achievements. Bandele, who will be rounding off his tenure early next year, said the celebrations would be particularly significant as they would be his last convocation ceremonies with the university. He said the institution had recorded considerable progress since its establishment, gaining greater visibility locally and internationally, while its students continued to make breakthroughs in their professional careers. Speaking ahead of the anniversary and convocation ceremonies, Bandele said the occasion offered the university an opportunity to reflect on its journey and acknowledge what he described as God’s faithfulness. “There are a lot of activities lined up to commemorate the two events. This occasion gives us a rare opportunity to reflect on where we were coming from and where we are today by the grace of God. “Looking back, we can confidently say the Lord has been good to us as an institution. The school has grown in leaps and bounds, becoming more visible than ever before. We are making waves within and outside Nigeria,” he stated. The VC added that the university had made holistic progress as a faith-based institution, noting that increasing parental confidence in the school reflected its growing acceptance. Bandele also reaffirmed his commitment to the institution, declaring that he would continue to give his best until his last day on campus. He, however, allayed concerns among some parents over the university’s capacity to accommodate more students, given its current space constraints. According to him, the new governing council has commenced the process of relocating the institution to its permanent site, while contingency arrangements are being made to accommodate all students in the interim. The week-long celebration will begin on November 16 with an opening assembly dedicated to praise, worship, prayers and special ministration. The second day will feature community service, while activities on the third day will include an entrepreneurship and innovation exhibition and a novelty football match on campus. The fourth day will feature an alumni summit, with activities including reunions, networking, testimonies, drama, spoken-word performances, a music concert and other entertainment. The fifth day will be dedicated to the decennial and convocation lecture and a book launch. The anniversary programme will climax with the convocation ceremonies on November 21, at the university campus.

title: Austria Expels Four Russian Diplomats: Foreign Ministry
body:
Austria has ordered the expulsion of four Russian diplomats, accusing them of engaging in “activities incompatible” with their status, the foreign ministry said Friday.
“Based on findings by the Austrian security authorities, the Austrian foreign ministry has taken measures against four Russian diplomats in Vienna,” said a ministry statement.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Three diplomats at the Russian Embassy “engaged in activities incompatible with their diplomatic status”, the ministry said.
Another from Russia’s delegation to the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) “also engaged in activities incompatible with his status... (and) has likewise been declared persona non grata and ordered to leave Austrian territory,” it added.
Several European countries have expelled Russian diplomats since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, which has drawn heavy sanctions from Western governments.
Hungary expelled 10 members of the Russian diplomatic mission in September under new Prime Minister Peter Magyar to protect the country’s “security and sovereignty”.
Austria has also expelled diplomats several times since 2022, though not in the same large numbers as other countries.
Austria has in recent years lost favour in the NATO military alliance. The neutral European Union country is regularly described as a hotspot for Russian spies owing to its relatively lax espionage laws.

title: NUEE Strike: Edo Appeals to Parties to Sustain Constructive Engagement, Reaffirms Commitment to Electricity Workers’ Welfare
body: Felix Omoh-Asun in Benin City Against the backdrop of the current strike by the National Union of Electricity Employees (NUEE), which has put Edo State in total darkness for four days now, the state government has appealed to all parties to sustain constructive engagement, exercise restraint, and prioritise a peaceful resolution that minimises disruption to residents, businesses, healthcare facilities, and other essential services across the state. The state government also reaffirmed its commitment to the welfare of electricity workers, protection of consumers’ interests, and development of a stable, efficient and sustainable electricity market. A statement by the state Commissioner for Power, Paul Usenbo, on Thursday, said the state government was aware of the industrial dispute involving members of NUEE and the management of Benin Electricity Distribution Company (BEDC), which culminated in a conciliation meeting convened by the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment in Abuja on Wednesday, October 21, 2026. The commissioner noted that the meeting addressed critical issues affecting electricity workers, including consequential adjustments, personal protective equipment, staff promotions, staff welfare, salary harmonisation and overtime payments. According to Usenbo, resolutions reached included the immediate restoration of overtime payments and a three-week timeline for BEDC management to address the remaining issues in consultation with the unions. “The ministry particularly notes that the industrial action is to be suspended in the affected states, with the exception of Edo State, pending the resolution of issues peculiar to the state. This underscores the need for sustained engagement and a practical resolution of outstanding concerns affecting electricity workers in Edo State,” the statement said. He stated further that towards this regard, the Commissioner for Labour and Employment, who is presently in Abuja, is actively engaged in efforts to address the labour-related issues and facilitate constructive dialogue towards an amicable resolution. “The Edo State Ministry of Power will continue to work with the relevant authorities, labour unions, and electricity sector stakeholders to promote industrial harmony and protect the public interest. “The ministry recognises that electricity workers are indispensable to the effective operation of the power sector. Their welfare, safety, and professional development must remain important considerations in building a functional and sustainable electricity market,” he added. He maintained that under the leadership of Governor Monday Okpebholo, the Edo State Government remains committed to practical solutions that advance electricity sector reform, encourage investment, protect consumers, and improve electricity service delivery throughout the state. “The ministry assures the good people of Edo State that it will continue to engage the appropriate authorities and stakeholders towards resolving the outstanding issues in the interest of workers, electricity consumers, and the overall development of the state’s power sector,” Usenbo said.

title: Russia’s Doppelgänger operation used fake Ukrainian channels to spread disinformation. Hacked files show who ran it
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Sergei Kiriyenko, first deputy chief of staff of the Russian Presidential Administration, set the goals for the Ukraine strand of the operation, launched in early 2023 under the codename "Uganda." Alexander Kharichev, now head of the Kremlin's Directorate for Monitoring and Analysis of Social Processes, oversaw it, according to hacked correspondence published by The Insider on 21 October. Doppelgänger disguises Russian narratives as local news through cloned media sites, fake accounts, paid ads, and fabricated videos. The FBI named Kiriyenko among its orchestrators in 2024, and its contractor, the Social Design Agency (SDA), run by Ilya Gambashidze, is still expanding , now targeting AI chatbots. The new files go inside the Ukraine campaign and show the operation reporting even exposed fakes to the Kremlin as achievements. Telegram channels posing as Ukrainian An internal briefing on narratives says the project ran its Telegram channels on the principles of agent work and psychological operations, the Russian version of the investigation shows. Early on, the team decided to disguise all its outlets as Ukrainian and to run its campaigns without direct Russian propaganda. Every channel carried Ukrainian news to look unconnected to Russia. Dropping pro-Ukrainian themes, the briefing warned, would eventually expose the client and wreck the whole plan. Explore further Russia-linked bot networks kept their weekly rhythm after drone strikes on three Yandex data centers—disinformation monitor LetsData Four goals and a can of stew Kiriyenko set four goals: discredit Ukraine's military and political leadership, split its elites, demoralize its army, and disorganize its population. The SDA prepared the project's pitch and carried out the work. Political strategist Alexander Asafov proposed fakes of his own: in May 2023, that soldiers were bribing commanders to avoid the front, and in January 2024, that Ukraine was pulling air defenses back to Kyiv to protect the authorities. After an Il-76 military transport crashed in Belgorod Oblast on 24 January 2024, Moscow claimed it had been carrying Ukrainian prisoners of war. Kharichev's subordinate Yevgeny Kazakov, chairing a meeting in his place, proposed sending a fake to the widows of Ukrainian soldiers: "They died for an expensive Il-76—the Russians have few of those." The idea was dropped. The same meeting produced another fake, and three days later the team launched it: that recruitment centers had sent widows a can of stewed meat with a little flag as compensation. The same producers also oversaw letters falsely attributed to Deputy Defense Minister Nataliia Kalmykova, the Russian version says. Debunks filed as results The SDA collected coverage of its work in a folder for the Kremlin. It filed the "Zelensky's yacht" story, which JD Vance, then a US senator and now US Vice President, echoed, together with its debunk. The report also included a TikTok campaign about former Defense Minister Oleksii Reznikov's family that the BBC had already exposed. The Insider concludes that the team has had more failures than successes. The US sanctioned Gambashidze and the SDA in March 2024, and the UK followed in October. title: Passenger car production in Russia jumps 27% to 660,000 in January-September — minister
body:
ST. PETERSBURG, October 23. /TASS/. Passenger car production in Russia grew by more than 27% year-on-year in the first nine months of 2026, reaching nearly 660,000 units, Industry and Trade Minister Anton Alikhanov told reporters on the sidelines of the Russian Industrialist forum and exhibition.
In total, Russian automakers rolled out over 764,000 vehicles across all segments during the nine-month period, up 22.4% year-on-year.
"We are seeing positive dynamics in domestic automotive production. According to manufacturers, over 764,000 vehicles across all segments rolled off our assembly lines in the first nine months, which is 22.4% higher than in the same period last year. Of those, nearly 660,000 were passenger cars, with growth in this segment exceeding 27%," he said.
Earlier the Industry and Trade Ministry reported that nearly 1.077 million new vehicles were sold in Russia between January and September 2026, a 6.2% increase year-on-year. Meanwhile, the market for domestically produced vehicles exceeded 687,000 units over the nine months, up 23.4% compared to January-September 2025.
TASS is the official media partner of the Russian Industrialist forum.

title: Election Security: NPTF Flags Off Training of 10,000 Police Officers Across Nigeria
body: Linus Aleke in Abuja The Nigeria Police Trust Fund (NPTF) has flagged off the training of 10,000 police officers drawn from police formations across the federation on election security ahead of the 2027 general election. Speaking at the flag-off ceremony of the 2026 Election Security Training at the Nigeria Police Resource Centre in Jabi, Abuja, the Executive Secretary of the NPTF, Mohammed Sheidu, said the programme demonstrated the Fund’s commitment to strengthening the operational capacity and preparedness of the Nigeria Police Force ahead of the forthcoming elections. He said the initiative was designed to ensure that officers deployed for election duties were adequately prepared to discharge their responsibilities professionally and effectively. Sheidu noted that electoral credibility depended not only on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), but also on security agencies’ ability to provide a safe and peaceful environment for citizens to exercise their democratic rights. He identified proper training, adequate equipment and operational mobility as three critical requirements for effective election security, adding that the programme would strengthen officers’ practical skills in election security management, crowd control, conflict prevention, de-escalation, respect for fundamental human rights and the lawful handling of election-related incidents. He urged the participating officers to remain disciplined and impartial, stressing that their responsibility was to uphold the law, maintain public order and protect all citizens equally, irrespective of political affiliation. Declaring the training open, the Inspector-General of Police (IGP), Olatunji Disu, said the officers were being equipped to make sound decisions under pressure and in accordance with the law. He acknowledged the likelihood of tension, provocation and misinformation during elections, emphasising that discipline and restraint must guide police conduct. Disu also stressed the importance of inter-agency collaboration, noting that no single agency could independently secure an election of such magnitude. He highlighted the need for support from the Armed Forces and intelligence agencies to address security threats and provide timely warnings. The Chairman of INEC, Professor Joash Ojo Amupitan (SAN), represented by National Commissioner, Rear Admiral Jamila Abubakar-Sadiq (rtd.), said security was paramount to the successful conduct of elections. He noted that elections were an exercise in public trust, which could not thrive in an environment characterised by fear, physical threats, administrative chaos and security vulnerabilities. title: Buttigieg endorses independent over Democratic nominee in Montana Senate race
body:
Both parties are paying increased attention to Montana in recent weeks.
Pete Buttigieg, the former Transportation Secretary and popular Democratic Party surrogate who has confirmed considering a 2028 presidential bid, is endorsing independent Montana U.S. Senate candidate Seth Bodnar, according to an announcement shared first with ABC News.
"The best leaders I've served with, in uniform and in government, care more about getting the job done than about who gets the credit, and Seth is one of them. Seth and I don't agree on everything, but he has spent his adult life serving this country and the next generation ... and he'll bring that same character to the Senate on behalf of all Montanans," Buttigieg wrote in a statement shared first with ABC News.
It's a notable step by a major Democrat to endorse an independent, but some Democrats feel Bodnar, a former University of Montana president and Green Beret, stands a better chance against Republican Kurt Alme than Democratic candidate Alani Bankhead.
Montana is among a few states this year along with Nebraska, South Dakota, and Idaho where many Democrats are backing independents for Senate .
However, Air Force veteran Bankhead, who won the primary in June has rebuffed pressure to withdraw from the race to clear a path for Bodnar. Bankhead has alleged that people within the Democratic Party tried to get her to drop her bid, a claim the party denies, according to ABC affiliate KWYB .
The matchup has created an additional challenge for those who want to wrest the seat from Republican control, given that the vote among Democrats or those disaffected with Republicans may get split among Bodnar and Bankhead.
"Montana deserves a senator who will fight corruption in Washington, defend reproductive freedom, and work across the aisle to lower costs and actually get things done. Seth Bodnar will be that Senator," Buttigieg, who is a veteran like Bodnar and Bankhead, wrote. He did not mention Bankhead in his statement.
Bodnar, in his own statement, said he was honored to have Buttigieg's support "and proud that people across the political spectrum are joining this campaign."
"Montanans have always voted for the person, not the party, and they want a senator who will put their families, jobs, and public lands ahead of partisan games in Washington. I'll answer to Montana, and I'll work with anyone who's willing to do the same," he said.
The seat is opening up as Republican Sen. Steve Daines is retiring, with Alme, a former U.S. Attorney for Montana, aiming to succeed him. Both parties are paying increased attention to congressional races in Montana , with President Donald Trump having joined Alme and other Republicans for a rally there last week and Vice President JD Vance set to rally in Montana next week.
"I'm ready to step up again to make our lives more affordable, make our communities safer, and protect our Montana way of life," Alme said at the rally last week. "And unlike my liberal opponents, I have the experience to get it done."
Buttigieg, who rose to prominence during his 2020 presidential run, has spent the past two years traveling around the country to stump for Democratic candidates and has endorsed in races up and down the ballot.
While he has confirmed he would consider running for president in 2028, he said he is more focused on the midterms and electing Democrats in 2026.

title: First Shipment of Russian Diesel Departs for the United States Under Trump Deal
body:
The Kremlin confirmed Friday that the first shipment of diesel to the United States left port the day before as part of an energy deal made between President Donald Trump and Russia’s Vladimir Putin.
“The first tanker is on its way to buyers,” spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters. “From here on out, shipments will continue on a regular schedule.”
Reuters, citing shipping data, confirmed the tanker was loaded with 40,000 tons of ultra-low sulphur diesel in the Baltic port of Primorsk. It is expected to arrive in the United States on Nov. 7.
Trump announced the diesel deal on Oct. 9, saying that Russia would “immediately” supply 300,000 metric tons of diesel to the U.S. and global markets, followed by another 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons thereafter.
The following day, Russia partially lifted its diesel export ban — first introduced in the summer due to domestic shortages.
Most experts agree that the agreement will have little effect on global energy markets in the near future. The 300,000 tons scheduled to hit the U.S. market this month cover only three-quarters of the country’s daily consumption, according to calculations by The Guardian.
Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said Wednesday that subsequent shipments “will satisfy all the U.S. requirements within our capacity.” Deliveries to other international buyers, he added, will depend on how quickly Russian refineries can restore output following Ukrainian drone strikes.
“If, according to the schedule, we can reach full volume only by the end of the year, then other countries will receive the volumes they previously received,” Novak said.
Turkey’s energy minister said this weekend that Ankara had negotiated to secure a share of the Russian diesel under the Trump agreement.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and European allies have criticized the U.S.-Russian agreement, arguing that it will bolster the Russian economy and strain transatlantic relations.
By most accounts, the diesel deal is designed to boost support for Republicans going into the midterm elections in early November. Polls show that surging energy costs in the United States, largely triggered by the war in Iran, are driving voter frustration and hurting the chances of Trump allies being elected to office.

title: Tom Hunter and Willie Haughey back Fife weapons plant
body: Two of Scotland’s best known business figures have backed the proposal to turn the former Mossmorran chemical plant into a weapons components factory, with Sir Tom Hunter saying Europe cannot depend on America for its protection and that Donald Trump has a point about NATO burden sharing, according to comments made on the Go Radio Business Show . Hunter, who became Scotland’s first home-grown billionaire after selling Sports Division and now runs the Hunter Foundation, co-presents the programme with Lord Willie Haughey, the Labour peer who built City Facilities Management in Glasgow. Haughey raised the Mossmorran proposal on Sunday’s edition and put it to Hunter that Scotland needs to take a more pragmatic view. Hunter said: “I mean, the fact is, you know, we live in a world where we need defence. We didn’t think we were going to need it, but once again, we cannot depend on America to protect us. And I actually think Donald Trump’s got a point about NATO. We haven’t been paying our way. So we need to get a European wide defence industry to keep us safe. We can’t depend on the Americans.” Haughey’s reply to that was “got a point for once” , before he turned to the politics of building armaments in Scotland. He said: “What people have to know is that the first rule of government is to keep your citizens safe and secure. And whether we like it or not, we are living in a more dangerous place at the moment than we have been maybe for decades.” The proposal they were discussing comes from TBG International Limited, a Hampshire-based defence contractor, which submitted a pre-application screening request to Fife Council last month for an energetics manufacturing facility on the site of the former Fife Ethylene Plant near Cowdenbeath. Energetics covers explosives, propellants and pyrotechnics, the chemical heart of almost every munition, and the plans set out process buildings, earth-covered storage magazines and the earthworks that go with them, alongside the reuse of existing offices and warehouses. Fife Council has told the company that a full environmental impact assessment will be required, because an integrated chemical installation producing explosives falls under Schedule 1 of the assessment regulations. ExxonMobil stopped production at Mossmorran in February after concluding the plant was no longer financially viable, putting more than 400 jobs at risk, and expects decommissioning to run until 2028. Haughey also made a wider claim about European industry, telling listeners that around half of the car manufacturers are approaching governments for help to remodel and re-equip their factories to make armaments, because Chinese producers have taken the volume out of the car market. Fewer cars to build means fewer jobs, he argued, at the same moment that Europe cannot say where the next conflict will come from. “See the people who are complaining about not wanting to build armaments factories, they’ll be the first people to complain if they don’t feel as if they’re being protected.” Finding work for the Mossmorran workforce has been a live question since the closure was announced, and Douglas Alexander, the Scottish Secretary, said in November last year that Babcock had signalled a willingness to explore whether it could in time employ some of the plant’s skilled workers. The site sits a short drive from Rosyth, where Babcock is building the Type 31 frigates. Scotland’s place in the defence spending increase has been contested all year, with the Scottish Affairs Committee warning that skills shortages could stop the country benefiting and this publication reporting that Scotland risks missing out on the defence spending boost . The Scottish Government confirmed this month that it will match funding for two Defence Technical Excellence Colleges , one on each coast, having been offered the money in the spring. Wes Streeting told the Commons yesterday that he wants the colleges backed with £50 million in England to expand to Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, and offered to work with the Scottish Government on the defence of the United Kingdom regardless of constitutional differences. The post Tom Hunter and Willie Haughey back Fife weapons plant first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Denmark Delivers Over 50,000 Cannon Rounds for Ukraine’s F-16s
body:
Denmark has delivered more than 50,000 rounds of 20 mm ammunition for Ukraine’s F-16 fighter jets, Ukraine’s Defense Ministry announced on Thursday, Oct. 22 .
The ammunition has arrived and is being used to intercept Russian jet-powered Shahed-type attack drones, the ministry said.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Denmark redirected part of a planned ammunition sale after an urgent request from Kyiv, securing the agreement of the partner country that was due to receive the rounds.
Copenhagen, which has also donated F-16s to Ukraine, had already supplied much of its 20 mm ammunition stockpile to Kyiv or sold it to partners as it transitions to F-35 fighters, according to the ministry.
The delivery follows earlier ammunition shipments from Belgium and Spain , which President Volodymyr Zelensky announced on Sept. 29.
Speaking to journalists on Saturday, Oct. 17, Zelensky said Ukraine was increasing supplies of 20 mm ammunition for its F-16s under agreements with international partners.
He said aircraft accounted for 55–60% of the jet-powered Shahed drones Ukraine had shot down. The figure referred to aircraft interceptions overall, rather than kills specifically attributed to F-16 cannons.
Zelensky also said cheaper missiles were beginning to enter service, with further counter-drone capabilities expected from partners and Ukrainian manufacturers.
“Several new solutions will soon be available to us in Ukraine from our partners, and we also have domestically produced systems that are already in operation,” he said.
He did not specify which of those systems would be fitted to F-16s.
The F-16 carries an internal M61A1 Vulcan, a six-barrel, 20 mm rotary cannon.
According to manufacturer General Dynamics Ordnance and Tactical Systems , the F-16 gun system carries 511 rounds and fires at a rate of 6,000 rounds per minute.
Its linkless, closed-loop feed system stores both unfired ammunition and spent casings in a rotating drum rather than ejecting the casings from the aircraft.
The Danish delivery adds ammunition for a weapon Ukrainian pilots are already using against jet-powered drones, alongside efforts to secure additional missiles and other interception systems.
Ukraine’s Defense Ministry thanked Denmark for responding promptly to its request.
Ukraine is also developing additional counter-drone weapons: Zelensky previously announced that Kyiv had identified prototypes designed to intercept jet-powered Shaheds , alongside negotiations with partners over further F-16 support.

title: Russia Pounds Kyiv’s Energy Infrastructure: How Are Residents Preparing for Winter?
body:
Massive Russian attacks on energy infrastructure have already disrupted electricity and water supplies in the capital. Power outage schedules are not always followed, public transport is experiencing disruptions, and it remains unclear when the heating season will begin or how long it will last.
Yet despite Russian attacks and the resulting problems, offices and businesses continue to work in Kyiv, and traffic jams continue to clog the roads. Kyiv residents are in no hurry to leave the city.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
We asked them several questions. The most important was: what will they do if the situation deteriorates?
“Of course, it’s not easy, but I’m glad that somehow things are a little easier this year than they were in 2022–2023. But what else can we do? Last year, the problems were mainly on the Left Bank, while the Right Bank managed more or less to cope. I hope both banks will manage this year,” Artem, a student, says.
Artem, the student (Photo by Sergii Kostezh/Kyiv Post)
Artem, the student (Photo by Sergii Kostezh/Kyiv Post)
“It’s quite unpleasant. I live right here in the city center, so my electricity isn’t cut off that often. But when it comes to heating, yes, it’s cold. During previous winters, the temperature in my apartment dropped to 7 or 8 degrees Celsius. That’s really unpleasant. I honestly don’t understand what I’m paying for,” says Roman, a food delivery worker.
Roman, a food delivery worker (Photo by Sergii Kostezh/Kyiv Post)
Roman, a food delivery worker (Photo by Sergii Kostezh/Kyiv Post)
“To be honest, the cold doesn’t bother me that much. I’ve probably got used to it because I’m from Pokrovsk. I’ve been used to it for a long time,” says Oleksandr, a displaced person from Donbas whose hometown was destroyed by Russian forces through massive bombing and artillery attacks.
Oleksandr, a displaced person from Donbas (Photo by Sergii Kostezh/Kyiv Post)
Oleksandr, a displaced person from Donbas (Photo by Sergii Kostezh/Kyiv Post)
“Last winter was also very unpleasant. I had no heating in my apartment until February. So far, everything is fine this year. Power cuts, power cuts – so what? Nothing unusual. I expect it to be cold, and we need to be prepared for that. I’m ready because my family lives outside the city, and we have the opportunity to prepare,” says Nelia, a pensioner.
Nelia, a pensioner(Photo by Sergii Kostezh/Kyiv Post)
Nelia, a pensioner(Photo by Sergii Kostezh/Kyiv Post)
“We have our own house, and we’ve ordered a large portable power station. Yes, it’s quite expensive, but what can you do? We also have boilers. They’re large, wood-burning solid-fuel boilers. That’s how we get through the winter, and I think we’ll get through this one without any problems, too,” says Oleksandr, a worker.
Oleksandr, a worker(Photo by Sergii Kostezh/Kyiv Post)
Oleksandr, a worker(Photo by Sergii Kostezh/Kyiv Post)
“I think it’ll be like last year. I don’t think the heating season will begin at all. For example, I had no heating throughout the entire year,” says Artem, a software developer.
Artem, a software developer(Photo by Sergii Kostezh/Kyiv Post)
Artem, a software developer(Photo by Sergii Kostezh/Kyiv Post)
Our next question to residents was who should be held responsible for preparing the capital for winter?
Whilst the war is clearly Russia’s doing, that does not eliminate the need for Kyiv to prepare for massive attacks, establish backup networks, develop alternative energy sources and provide additional protection for municipal infrastructure.
In Kyiv, the issue has taken on a political dimension, with the local authorities blaming the central government for the lack of preparedness and the central government pointing the finger at the city authorities.
“I actually think things will be much worse this year. That’s the trend, and I haven’t seen any preparations in Kyiv for what lies ahead, either by the local authorities or the central government. They’re doing nothing. What has Kyiv done? Nothing. They just moved money from one pocket to another, and in the end, accomplished nothing,” says Roman.
“First and foremost, the local authorities are responsible. Local officials need to be held accountable, starting at the lowest level. I don’t think the head of the administration is entirely to blame. There are subordinates who are supposed to perform their duties. Where are they, and what have they done? They should be held accountable,” says Nelia.
“I think responsibility is shared. The Kyiv City State Administration and, in particular, the Kyiv City Council had greater control over how allocated funds were spent, while the central government failed to ensure that all the necessary funding was provided,” says the student, Artem.
“I can’t say that only the central government is responsible. The city authorities must also be held accountable. Moreover, I think we should have been preparing for this throughout these years of war, using the summer to get ready. The fact that we aren’t prepared now is a systemic problem, in my opinion,” says Olha, a lawyer.
Olha, a lawyer (Photo by Sergii Kostezh/Kyiv Post)
Olha, a lawyer (Photo by Sergii Kostezh/Kyiv Post)
Finally, what will people do if things get really bad? What do they expect from the heating season? Will it even begin?
“I’m not leaving. I have nowhere to go! Where else could I go?” says Oleksandr, reacting emotionally.
“One option might be to go to the Kyiv region, to a village. But there’s a problem: not everyone can do that. People who live in Kyiv are tied to the city. Most can’t easily leave because they have studies or jobs,” says Artem.
“First of all, I don’t really have anywhere to go. I’ve made it through four winters, and I’ll make it through this one, too. So I think I’ll stay in Kyiv,” Nelia says.
“If I didn’t leave in 2022, I certainly won’t leave in 2026. That’s final,” says Olha.

title: Dialogue between Russia and Montenegro frozen, Russia’s ambassador tells TASS
body:
MOSCOW, October 23. /TASS/. The dialogue between Moscow and Podgorica is frozen, Russia’s ambassador to Montenegro Alexander Lukashik said in an interview with TASS.
"The pro-Western orientation of Montenegro’s foreign policy, its membership in NATO and the uncontested desire to keep up with the EU bureaucracy have led to an almost complete freezing of the Russian-Montenegrin dialogue," he said.
At the same time, as the ambassador clarified, "occasional contacts with Montenegrin representatives are maintained to resolve some urgent practical issues, including through law enforcement agencies.".

title: Digital 2027 report: Global use of GenAI tools rises, web browser activity declines
body: MANILA, Philippines – Media intelligence company Meltwater and creative agency We Are Social released the Digital 2027 report this October, providing data on worldwide digital trends. The more than 900-page report seeks to provide worldwide statistics on the various aspects of digital daily life, from the adoption of artificial intelligence tools like generative AI, to the use of web browsers and mobile phones. It is aided by a series of individual deep dives by author Simon Kemp into specific aspects of the main report. Some Philippine statistics In the local country headlines report , the Philippines is said to have a total population of 118 million people, a figure that increased by 936,000 from last year. The report also showed 149 million cellular phone connections in the country, or 126% compared to the total population of the Philippines. The figure likely infers people having more than one phone on hand. Meanwhile, 95.9 million individuals — or 81.3% of the population — were using the internet, while the report mentioned there were 94.7 million social media user identities in the country, which represent a decline of about 1.1 million user identities. The report also mentioned 94.4% of internet users in the Philippines aged 16 and up used AI tools each month. However, only 5.5% of internet users in the country aged 16 and up paid for subscriptions to an AI tool each month. Within the Philippine context, 71.17% of active AI users aged 16 and up use AI tools to find information, 37.6% of active AI users aged 16 and up use AI tools to seek advice on problems, 32.8% of active AI users aged 16 and up used AI tools for personalized recommendations. Further, 27.5% of Philippine internet users aged 16 and up believe AI benefits society overall. GenAI tools, social media, and mobile According to the report, 38.9% of the global population of 8.32 billion people — or around 3.24 billion — currently use generative AI tools each month. This shows a growth of about 1.2 billion new users, though the report emphasizes a caveat of potential duplication —that a user may have more than one account for a generative AI service to decouple personal and work uses. Meanwhile, social media user identities now number 5.81 billion or 69.9% of the world’s population, though a similar caveat applies here as some duplication due to decoupling personal and work social media identities may occur. Citing two separate reports from GSMA Intelligence and Ericsson, there are now 5.86 billion unique mobile phone users worldwide as of the report’s release this month. Further information from Ericsson showed the 7.68 billion smartphones in use today account for nearly 90% of all active mobile phone handsets, and nearly 86% of total cellular mobile connections, with the caveat that some folks may have more than one smartphone. Web browser use declines The report said that across the world’s top 10,000 web domains, the total monthly web traffic declined by more than 10% since the launch of ChatGPT in 2022. Combined traffic across the top 10,000 web domains fell by almost 50 billion visits per month between Q4 2022 and Q2 2026. Further, there has been an 11.2% decline in the total time spent visiting the top 10,000 global domains over a two-year period, This fall is equivalent to more than 6.6 billion hours per month in that time frame. Aside from the potential effects of AI use, the report suggests people are more readily using native mobile apps rather than using their browsers to get what they want from the internet. That said, web users did load an average of just under 3 trillion pages per month across the world’s top 10,000 domains in the second quarter of 2026. The figure is up more than 2% compared to the same time period in 2024. The full Digital 2027 report can be downloaded from this site . Meanwhile, Simon Kemp’s reports on some of the pertinent statistics are available here . – Rappler.com

title: Netanyahu orders West Bank lockdown after Hebron checkpoint shooting
body: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the “full closure” of the occupied West Bank after five people were injured in a shooting at a military checkpoint near the city of Hebron. “I have instructed the [military] and the security forces to immediately impose a cordon around the city of Hebron and to prepare for a full closure of the entire [ West Bank ], effective today,” Mr Netanyahu’s office said in a statement. Israel’s military said it killed two suspects armed with a rifle and a handgun. Two of those injured were reported to be in a critical condition. Palestinian media reports named the pair as family members Mohammad Jaaba and Firas Jaaba, both 27 and from Hebron. The military said the men had planned to carry out a “large-scale” attack on Israelis. There are a number of illegal Israeli settlements in Hebron. Settler and military violence against Palestinians has swept across the West Bank during the olive harvest season, while Israel is preparing to hold elections that could unseat Mr Netanyahu’s ultranationalist coalition government, which has been in power for four years. Mr Netanyahu later said Israeli forces would demolish parts of Hebron in response to the attack, referencing earlier operations in which Israel levelled entire refugee camps in the north of the occupied West Bank and displaced their populations. “We will implement the successful, offensive model we employed in the refugee camps, this time within the cities. The [Israeli army] will enter the neighbourhoods from which the terrorists emerged, evacuate the residents, go house-to-house and dismantle the terror infrastructure. We are prepared for an extensive operation in [the occupied West Bank].” “A few weeks ago, we warned of attempts by our enemies to strike at us − at our citizens and our soldiers − in the lead-up to the elections. That is what they attempted to do here,” he added. “Concurrently, we are imposing a closure on the cities of Hebron and Halhul … the Defence Minister and I have overseen the planning of a very extensive [army] operation in [the occupied West Bank] on a scale not seen since the Six-Day War. The [military] is prepared to carry it out; we will determine the timing, but it is coming.” Shortly after Mr Netanyahu’s words, Defence Minister Israel Katz elaborated on the operation, in a post on X. “The Jenin refugee camp model arrives in Hebron,” he wrote, referencing the now-destroyed camp in the north of the occupied West Bank. “Every [tribal] clan neighbourhood in Hebron from which the terrorists emerged today will be evacuated of its residents, and the terror infrastructure in the neighbourhood will be addressed and dismantled,” he added. “This is the only language that jihadist terrorism understands. Just like in Gaza, just like in Lebanon.” Hamas praised the attack but did not claim responsibility. After the attack, Israel's far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, who lives in the illegal Hebron settlement of Kiryat Arba, called for the Palestinian Authority to be dismantled. It is supposed to control parts of the West Bank. “We have to act before it’s too late. The Palestinian Authority must be dismantled and demilitarised, and its terror infrastructure wiped out completely,” he said. Israel’s military chief of staff Lt Gen Eyal Zamir described the attack as “serious” and said a “large quantity of ammunition was found in the vehicle in which the terrorists arrived at the scene ... which was intended to be used to carry out a larger-scale attack”.

title: Greece Challenges Turkish-Libyan Memorandum at UN
body: Greece has formally challenged the legal validity of the Turkish-Libyan maritime memorandum at the United Nations, warning that its ratification by Libya’s parliament does not change its status under international law. In a letter to UN Secretary-General António Guterres, Greece’s Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Aglaia Balta, reiterated Athens’ position that the 2019 agreement between Turkey and Libya is invalid and cannot produce legal effects against third states. The diplomatic intervention comes after Libya’s House of Representatives ratified the memorandum, prompting Greece to intensify its efforts to challenge the agreement internationally. Athens is seeking to prevent Turkey and Libya from using the ratification to strengthen their claims over maritime zones in the Eastern Mediterranean. Greece Challenges Memorandum at United Nations According to diplomatic sources cited by Greek media, Balta’s letter stresses that the Turkish-Libyan memorandum contradicts the principles of international law, particularly the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). Greece maintains that the agreement cannot establish legally binding maritime boundaries affecting the rights of other countries. Athens argues that Turkey and Libya do not have opposite or adjacent coastlines that would provide a valid legal basis for the maritime delimitation outlined in the memorandum. The Greek government has repeatedly described the agreement as illegal, invalid and without legal standing, arguing that it disregards the maritime rights of Greek islands in the region. Balta also raised the issue at the UN Security Council, highlighting Greece’s concerns over the potential consequences for stability and security in the Eastern Mediterranean. Although Greece holds the Security Council presidency for October, Balta made her intervention in her national capacity. ‘Geography Does Not Change’ Greece has reiterated that the ratification of the memorandum by Libya’s parliament does not alter its legal status. The Greek position is that international maritime boundaries must be determined in accordance with international law, rather than through unilateral political decisions. Athens has also stressed that the law of the sea cannot be rewritten to accommodate the interests of individual states. The dispute centres on the 2019 maritime memorandum signed by Turkey and the internationally recognised Government of National Accord in Libya. The agreement established a claimed maritime boundary between the two countries across an area where Greece argues that its islands, particularly Crete, have maritime entitlements that cannot be ignored. Greece and other regional actors have challenged the agreement, arguing that it disregards the geographical position and maritime rights of Greek islands. Greece Pursues Talks With Libya and Egypt Alongside its diplomatic challenge at the United Nations, Greece is pursuing negotiations with regional partners to strengthen its position on maritime boundaries. Athens says it has approached Libyan authorities in good faith and remains willing to begin substantive discussions on delimiting maritime zones in accordance with international law. Greece is also moving forward with Egypt on expanding the geographical scope of their existing Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) agreement. On Thursday, Greek Foreign Minister George Gerapetritis and Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty agreed to begin consultations on extending the 2020 Greece-Egypt EEZ delimitation agreement. The two ministers reaffirmed that discussions would be based on international law and UNCLOS. Signed in August 2020, the existing agreement established a partial maritime boundary between Greece and Egypt between the 26th and 28th meridians. The agreement recognises the maritime influence of Greek islands, including Crete, Karpathos and Rhodes, in the delimitation of the continental shelf and EEZ. Any expansion of the agreement would form part of Greece’s broader effort to establish maritime boundaries through bilateral negotiations and internationally recognised legal principles. For Athens, the parallel diplomatic efforts with Libya and Egypt are intended to reinforce its position that maritime claims in the Eastern Mediterranean must respect international law and the rights of states in the region. Source: Greek media reports and statements attributed to Greek diplomatic sources. title: New Zealand defense chief resigns over ‘inappropriate relationship’
body: WELLINGTON, New Zealand — The Chief of the New Zealand Defence Force, Air Marshal Tony Davies, has informed Defense Minister Paul Goldsmith that he is resigning his role. Arrangements are underway to transition responsibilities to the Vice Chief of Defence Force, Rear Adm. Mat Williams, who will serve as Acting Chief of Defence Force. Air Marshal Davies said: “The resignation is for personal reasons, and results from errors of judgement made by me in the past, for which I am taking responsibility. The errors of judgement were contrary to the values of the Defence Force. “These matters revolved around an inappropriate relationship I had when in a position of unit command, and I regret not disclosing this when I had the opportunity to do so.” Appointed as the Chief of Air Force from 2016 before becoming the Vice Chief of Defence Force in 2018, Air Marshal Davies, born 1966, was promoted to his current rank on appointment to Chief of Defence Force on June 6, 2024. The Chief of Army, Maj. Gen. Rose King, will act as Chief of Defence Force until Sunday before Williams takes on the role.

title: PICRC Strengthens Palau’s Capacity to Respond to Crown-of-Thorns Starfish Threats Through Australia Partnership
body: The Palau International Coral Reef Center (PICRC) recently coordinated a two-week Crown-of-Thorns Starfish (COTS) Control Training to strengthen Palau’s capacity to monitor and respond to COTS threats and protect its coral reefs. The training was led by visiting experts from the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority (GBRMPA) in Australia, including PICRC’s Board Member Dr. David Williamson, and was supported by the Koror State Government, The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and the Environment (MAFE), the Australian Embassy and Australian Government, the University of Queensland, and the Great Barrier Reef Foundation. The collaboration focused on strengthening COTS response capacity, protecting priority reefs, and building practical skills among Palau’s science, management, and tourism sectors. There were approximately 20 participants from PICRC, the Palau Pacific Resort, Paddling Palau, Airai Rangers, Koror State Government Division of Conservation and Law Enforcement (KSG-DCLE), and the Bureau of Fisheries under MAFE. As the local coordinator, PICRC supported the training through Chief Researcher Ikelau Otto, who coordinated the project. Additional PICRC staff also participated in the training and fieldwork alongside the participating organizations. Over the two weeks, participants conducted reef surveys and COTS control activities at Ngederrak Reef and Lighthouse Reefs. The team completed 21 dives and removed 2,205 COTS across 20.95 hectares. The training began with presentations by the GBRMPA on the broader impacts COTS can have on coral reefs. Participants were introduced to COTS control equipment, including vinegar guns, and received hands-on instruction on how to assemble, use, dismantle, and clean the equipment. The training also covered the Manta tow survey method, which uses a snorkeler to rapidly survey reef areas to identify heavy COTS density or hotspots to focus control efforts. Dr. Williamson noted that COTS are native to Palau and are part of the natural reef ecosystem, but high densities can threaten coral reefs. He also highlighted the importance of early monitoring and intervention during outbreaks. The training concluded with a closing ceremony on September 18 at PICRC. On behalf of PICRC’s CEO, Chief Researcher Ikelau Otto shared her remarks, recognizing the partners, trainers, and participants for their contributions and emphasized the importance of strengthening local skills and preparedness His Excellency Toby Sharpe, Australia’s Ambassador to Palau, highlighted the growing challenges facing coral reefs and the importance of continued partnerships in protecting Palau’s marine environment. Koror State Governor Eyos Rudimch expressed appreciation for the training, participating organizations, and equipment provided. MAFE Minister Steven Victor recognized the Australia-Palau collaboration and the involvement of public and private sector organizations in addressing the COTS threat. During the closing of the training, the COTS control vinegar injecting guns were transferred to PICRC, MAFE and Koror State. These equipment will be used to support continued response efforts. PICRC also brought the training to the wider community through its Berius el Chais radio program hosted by Mr. Nolan Rebluud and Mr. Asap Bukurrou. On September 15, Dr. Williamson joined the program to discuss COTS, reef protection, and the Australia-Palau partnership. Through PICRC’s coordination and continued collaboration with local and international partners, particularly Australia, the training strengthened Palau’s local capacity and provided practical knowledge and equipment to support ongoing COTS monitoring and control. The partnership provides a foundation for continued collaboration to protect Palau’s priority reefs and strengthen the long-term resilience of its coral reef ecosystems. title: The Economist source in Kiev claims US has presented new plan for Ukraine
body:
LONDON, October 23. /TASS/. The United States has allegedly proposed new terms for a peace agreement to resolve the Ukraine conflict, including Kiev’s renunciation of NATO membership, the establishment of a demilitarized zone in Donbass and the restart of operations of the Nord Stream gas pipeline, the British magazine The Economist reports, citing sources among Ukrainian officials.
According to the publication, under Washington’s latest proposal, sanctions against Russia are also expected to be eased, Moscow could be allowed to conclude business deals with the United States and resume gas supplies to Europe. Ukraine, in turn, is being offered an "investment package" and European Union membership in exchange for dropping its bid to join NATO, The Economist writes.
Earlier, Russian presidential press secretary Dmitry Peskov said that Vladimir Putin had not sent any documents outlining plans for a settlement in Ukraine through US envoy Steve Witkoff.
Russian presidential aide Yury Ushakov said that during his meeting with Witkoff, Putin had informed him that Moscow was ready to resume trilateral talks with the United States and Ukraine in the first ten days of November on the main issue of establishing a security system for Russia and Ukraine after the conflict ends.

title: Uproar in Rivers over forced virginity test on female students
body: There is tension at Government Comprehensive High School (SNR), Taabaa, Khana Local Government Area of Rivers State, over allegations that a monarch subjected female students to forced virginity tests. The management of the school has kicked against such an act, saying it contravened the dignity of the girl child. The management staff of the school has also petitioned the Rivers State Ministry of Education, accusing the paramount ruler of Taabaa community, HRH Mene M.S.K Nule, of allegedly forcing virginity testing on female students, invasion of the school premises and taking over of the school farm. The petition dated October 12, 2026, also seeks immediate investigation by appropriate authorities into the incident, which has been reportedly happening in the last seven years. Zamfara community fights back No child left behind: Nigeria’s critical role in ending polio Th traditional ruler has denied allegation, but admitted conducting roll calls to identify students who are still virgin and sensitizing them to maintain their virginity until they complete their studies. Nule disclosed that he started the virginity roll calls in 2020 when he got reports that some teachers of the school were molesting female students. He said he regularly visits the school with his team and asks students who are virgins to stand up, adding that only one female student stood up when he first conducted the exercise. He said: “I always speak to them on the need to focus on their education and not indulge in early sexual activities. I always carry out these activities annually and by 2025, we got four students who stood up as virgins and I rewarded them, the students, not their parents, with N20,000 each. He said though he has been warning students and teachers, by way of subtle threats, that he would come after teachers molesting students, a situation that made many teachers left the school out of fear. He denied taking the students to a health centre for virginity testing, adding that his efforts were helping the students and school to progress. Raising concerns about the dignity of girl-child amidst, the Youths and Environmental Advocacy Centre (YEAC-Nigeria), condemned the acts, describing the allegations, if proven, to be grave violations of the rights and dignity of the girl-child, the Child Rights Act and Rivers State Child Rights Law which prohibit dehumanizing treatment for children. The rights group in a statement on Tuesday in Port Harcourt, Rivers State capital, called for immediate investigation into the matter. He called on the authorities to immediately set up an independent fact-finding committee to investigate the allegations. The Rivers State Government says it has commenced investigation into the report to establish the facts, and will take all appropriate actions, including referral to the relevant authorities, against any person or body found to have been involved. The Permanent Secretary at the Rivers State Minister of Education, Dr. Mina Tele Ikuru, condemned the reports of alleged forced virginity testing on female students in the school and any other schools in the state. He urged schools authorities in the state to uphold the highest standards of child protection and to ensure that no student is subjected to degrading, coercive or invasive practices under the guise of cultural tradition, scholarship programmes, disciplinary measures or community development initiatives. When contacted, the Rivers Police Command spokesperson, ASP Agabe Blessing Kaborlo, requested that a message be sent to her, promising to make inquiries and respond. However, she had not done so as of the time of filling this report.

title: Abu Dhabi private schools to hire 2,000 Emirati teachers in next five years under education push
body: Abu Dhabi on Friday unveiled plans to hire 2,000 Emirati teachers at private schools over the next five years under a major push to champion local talent in the education sector. The Emiratisation Policy for Private Education will seek to provide training and qualifications for a new generation of Emirati educators to encourage them to play a leading role in developing the next generation of learners. It is being supported by the Ministry of Human Resources, the Emirati Talent Competitiveness Council - also known as Nafis - and private education operators, Gems Education, Taleem, Sabis, International Community Schools, and Liwa Education. Private schools in the capital will be asked to meet new recruitment targets specific for teaching roles in an expansion of the government's Emiratisation strategy. Adek said the plans would complement existing Emiratisation goals, while establishing a dedicated approach to boosting Emirati representation in the classroom. Private schools are already subject to Emiratisation employment targets, with the new scheme aiming to sharpen focus on hiring citizens in teaching positions rather than in administration roles within schools. It will initially focus on Social Studies, Arabic, and Islamic Studies roles, with recruitment and integration taking place progressively over the coming five years. Teacher training plan As part of the strategy, Adek is working with Emirates College of Advanced Education to launch a teaching programme to develop a long-term pipeline of qualified Emirati teachers. The programme will provide specialised training, practical classroom preparation and employment opportunities within the private education sector. It is open to Emirati jobseekers and those seeking to transition into education careers, subject to approved eligibility requirements. It will offer two dedicated pathways for teachers and teaching assistants, creating flexible entry routes for Emirati talent at different qualification levels to pursue careers. Through the Nafis programme - which was introduced in September 2021 to ensure 10 per cent of all skilled jobs in private companies are taken up by citizens by the end of 2026 - participants will be eligible to receive a monthly financial incentive of up to AED4,000 throughout the training period. Making the grade The policy will provide schools with access to a pool of national talent and will offer funded qualification pathways, practical school-based training and structured routes into employment. Private schools are already making significant progress on a mission to integrate Emirati employees within their teaching workforce. Adek signed an agreement with Aldar Education in May to create more than 300 opportunities for Emirati teachers within its schools. The education authority has now entered into further strategic partnerships with Sabis, Taaleem, GEMS Education, International Community Schools and Liwa Education, Taaleem has committed to recruiting more than 200 Emirati educators, Sabis more than 150, Gems Education more than 120. International Community Schools and Liwa Education have pledged to create teaching positions for at least 77 and 61 Emiratis respectively. Emiratisation plans take shape Employers in the UAE with at least 50 members of staff - including schools - are required to raise their Emirati workforce by 1 per cent every six months under the Emiratisation scheme. They must hit a 10 per cent target by the end of this year, with companies who fail to hit targets or flout rules facing significant fines. The initiative has proved crucial in encouraging large numbers of citizens – who have typically preferred to take up jobs in the public sector – to join the private sector. Government figures released in July showed more than 190,000 Emiratis were employed by 32,000 private sector companies. In April, Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed , Vice President, Deputy Prime Minister and Chairman of the Presidential Court, on announced the extension of the landmark Emiratisation strategy Sheikh Mansour unveiled a series of updates to the programme, include the expansion of the children's allowance for Emiratis, removing the previous cap on the number of eligible children. A salary support programme for children of Emirati women in the private sector and the wives of citizens working for private companies will also be introduced.

title: GPL 2026/27: Hearts of Oak target league summit against Basake Holy Stars
body: Hearts of Oak will aim to move to the top of the Ghana Premier League table when they host Basake Holy Stars at the University of Ghana Sports Stadium on Friday, October 23. The Phobians sit second with 14 points, level with the league leaders but behind on goal difference, and head into the encounter on the back of consecutive victories. Hearts have scored eight goals and conceded just twice in seven matches, while remaining unbeaten at home in the league this season, with two wins and a draw from three games. However, Basake Holy Stars will provide a stern test, having climbed to fifth with 12 points after winning four of their opening seven matches. The Ayinase-based side have won three of their last five league games but face the challenge of improving an away record that has seen them lose all three matches on the road this season. Hearts will also be seeking their first home victory over Basake Holy Stars, having recorded one draw and one defeat in their previous two home meetings with the visitors. With both sides enjoying encouraging spells of form, Friday’s encounter presents an opportunity for Hearts to strengthen their title ambitions, while Holy Stars will hope to continue their impressive start to the campaign.

title: Family: Fasoranti to be buried December 17
body: The family of the late leader of Afenifere, Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, has announced that the elder statesman will be buried on December 17, 2026. The burial arrangements were contained in a programme of activities signed by his son, Dr. Taiwo Fasoranti, who is also the Secretary to the Ondo State Government. The family described the late Fasoranti as its beloved patriarch, a foremost nationalist and leader of Afenifere, who died at the age of 100. According to the programme, a Christian wake-keeping service will be held on Wednesday, December 16, 2026, at his residence within the Omolere Nursery and Primary School Compound at 4:00 p.m. Nollywood actor Francis Duru dies at 57 2027: Tinubu prioritises your safety, Tompolo tells Benue people The funeral service and interment will take place on Thursday, December 17, 2026, at St. David’s Cathedral, Ijomu, Akure, at 10:00 a.m. The interment will follow immediately after the funeral service at the church cemetery, while a reception for guests will be held at his residence immediately after the interment. The family also announced that an outing and thanksgiving service would take place on Sunday, December 20, 2026, at St. David’s Cathedral, Ijomu, Akure, by 10:00 a.m. They called on the public to support them with prayers and attendance as they honour the memory of the late elder statesman, whom they described as a distinguished elder and patriot.

body:

title: Phones down, water off, a factory roof broken open: Russian-occupied Luhansk counts the damage after another night of drones

It was the third night in four that drones went after communications in occupied eastern Ukraine. A pro-Russian local channel also showed a damaged factory, and the occupation authorities have stayed silent. Ukraine's drones have spent months hitting what keeps Russia's occupation running, from fuel depots to supply lines and now communications. Blasts before dawn, then outages Explosions hit Luhansk before dawn, and the strikes probably targeted communications facilities, Exilenova+ said . Another Ukrainian monitoring channel, Supernova+, wrote that the city's TV tower came under attack. Exilenova+ posted night footage of the strikes. The moment of arrival in Luhansk. Strikes on local communications facilities in occupied Luhansk. pic.twitter.com/4Jz7aK7tKs — Exilenova+ (@Exilenova_plus) October 23, 2026 By morning, water stopped flowing in parts of Luhansk and nearby villages, including Metalist and Tsvitni Pisky. A notice posted by local Telegram channel Luhansk Online cited unstable voltage at water facilities. The city's water utility later switched to backup phone numbers after its dispatch lines failed. Third night in four Overnight on 20 October, drones struck Ugletelecom, the occupation's telecom operator in Donetsk. A night later, they hit the seized Ukrtelecom building in Luhansk, which houses the occupation's mobile operator Lugacom. That strike disrupted the internet so badly that service centers across occupied Luhansk Oblast stopped accepting documents. Explore further Ukraine drone forces expand kill zone into occupied regions, commander says: Russia’s trains, comms towers, and depots struck Silence from the occupation The occupation authorities have not commented. Leonid Pasechnik, the Russian-installed head of occupied Luhansk Oblast, posted nothing about the attack. On 21 October, he claimed Kyiv was carrying out "terrorist strikes" on civilians. Russia's Defense Ministry claimed it downed 443 drones overnight over Russian regions, Crimea, and two seas, without mentioning Luhansk. The same night, Russia launched 176 drones at Ukraine, some from occupied Donetsk and from Hvardiiske in occupied Crimea, Krym.Realii reported , citing Ukraine's Air Force . Ukraine's General Staff has not reported on the attack yet. After the previous strike on Luhansk, it said Ukrainian forces hit command posts of Russian units in the Luhansk area. A pipeline-valve plant hit, too Ogonyok Luhanska also posted daylight photos of the Marshal plant after what it called a "night arrival." They show a damaged workshop roof, and the channel wrote it had information that the drone hit inside the plant. The Luhansk Pipeline Valve Plant Marshal, registered in Ukraine in 1994, makes taps and valves at 13 Montazhna Street, according to Ukrainian state registry data published by VB.ua. The Marshal pipeline-valve plant in occupied Luhansk with a damaged workshop roof, 23 October 2026. Photo: Ogonyok Luhanska/Telegram Earlier that morning, Luhansk Online reported restricted traffic on Montazhna Street between Brestska and Sukhodilska streets. Ukraine has hit industrial sites in occupied Luhansk Oblast before. For example, in March, drones struck a plant in Alchevsk that made artillery shell casings. title: From drought to deluge: ‘Super’ El Niño’s expanding reach
body: PORT MORESBY, 22 OCTBER 2026 (UN NEWS CENTRE) —Across Papua New Guinea, water sources are drying up, crops are failing and food prices are rising months before the worst agricultural impacts are expected. Behind those warning signs is an El Niño whose Pacific Ocean temperatures have already surpassed the equivalent measurements during the historic 1997 and 2015 events – part of an unfolding climate pattern being dubbed a “Super El Niño” by some climate watchers. The 2026-2027 El Niño is forecast to become one of the strongest on record, threatening to intensify drought, floods and other weather extremes across countries already grappling with food insecurity, displacement and economic pressures. Children on the frontlines, again El Niño can shift rainfall patterns thousands of kilometres from the tropical Pacific, leaving some regions facing drought and water shortages while others contend with heavier rains, flooding and heightened disease risks. More than 347 million children in nearly 100 countries and territories could be exposed to unusually dry or wet conditions between October and December because of El Niño, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) warns in a new analysis. “For children, El Niño is far more than a weather pattern. It can mean increased displacement, malnutrition, water shortages and disease outbreaks,” said UNICEF Executive Director Catherine Russell. “Children are also at risk of schools closing, while families could experience added financial hardship.” Already, 1.1 billion children – nearly half of the world’s children – are already exposed to at least three overlapping climate-related hazards such as drought, extreme heat or floods. In Papua New Guinea, impact is already here Some of those consequences are already visible in Papua New Guinea, a mountainous Pacific island nation where remote terrain and difficult logistics have complicated responses to previous droughts. El Niño conditions have been present since mid-2026 and are forecast to peak between October and December. In September, the Niño 3.4 index – a measure of sea surface temperatures in the tropical Pacific used to track El Niño – surpassed those recorded during every previous El Niño event, including 1997 and 2015. The Government, which declared the event in June, has established a dedicated task force and approved a US$112 million supplementary budget. Yet, needs are mounting. Some 1.2 million people are estimated to require direct food relief, with water shortages, crop losses, dwindling food reserves and higher prices already reported. Schools are being disrupted and concerns are growing over health, nutrition and bushfires. The largest impacts on agriculture and food security are expected from November. One ocean, very different extremes What dries out one part of the world can bring deluges to another. Across the Greater Horn of Africa, wetter-than-normal conditions could raise the risk of river and flash flooding, increase the spread of waterborne diseases and disrupt schooling. In the wider region – including Yemen, Sudan and Afghanistan – children living amid conflict and displacement face particularly acute risks because El Niño can magnify existing hunger, malnutrition and difficulties accessing essential services. A race to act early For governments, the forecasts offer something disasters often do not: time. Asia and the Pacific is expected to bear a particularly large share of the exposure, with some 190 million children – more than half of the global total identified by UNICEF – living in areas forecast to experience unusually wet or dry conditions between October and December. The World Food Programme (WFP) is urging countries across the region to strengthen social protection systems that can rapidly expand when droughts, floods or economic shocks threaten household food security. “A flood, drought, or sudden economic shock can wipe out a family’s progress in a matter of days,” said Samir Wanmali, WFP Regional Director for Asia and the Pacific. “Social protection systems that are inclusive, nutrition-sensitive and ready to expand during a crisis can prevent a temporary shock from becoming a lasting setback.” Lessons from a not-so-distant past The urgency is sharpened by lessons from earlier El Niño episodes. In analysis published in May, the UN Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP) pointed to the 2015-16 event as a warning of how climate extremes can cascade through economies and societies. More than 70percent of Southeast Asia’s land area experienced drought during that episode, exposing more than 200 million people to severe drought at its peak. The pressures this time are unfolding against tighter government finances, elevated debt and persistent economic uncertainty and supply chain worries, potentially reducing the ability of governments and households to absorb another shock. Warmer world raises the stakes Meanwhile, climate change is raising the baseline risk. Higher temperatures accelerate the loss of moisture from soil and vegetation, potentially intensifying drought when rainfall falls short. For governments, that means preparing for extremes in both directions – from failing rains, water shortages and crop losses to intense rainfall, flooding and landslides. The challenge is to turn forecasts into decisions before harvests fail, reservoirs run low or floods force families from their homes. That will be the focus of a regional El Niño exchange beginning on next week in Bangkok, bringing governments, meteorological experts, UN agencies and frontline practitioners together to compare emerging impacts and lessons from previous crises. The post From drought to deluge: ‘Super’ El Niño’s expanding reach appeared first on Island Times News .

title: 135th IPRM Meeting Held in Ergneti
body: The 135th meeting of the Incident Prevention and Response Mechanism (IPRM) took place on October 22 in the village of Ergneti, near the occupation line in Georgia’s Russia-occupied Tskhinvali region. The Incident Prevention and Response Mechanism (IPRM) was established in 2009 within the framework of the Geneva International Discussions that followed the 2008 Russo-Georgian war. It serves as a forum for the regular discussion of security-related incidents and developments on the ground. IPRM meetings have been held regularly in Ergneti, near the Tskhinvali occupation line, with the participation of representatives from Tbilisi and the Tskhinvali de facto authorities. In contrast, meetings in Gali, in occupied Abkhazia, have been suspended multiple times, from 2012 to 2016, and again since 2018. The meetings are co-facilitated by the OSCE and the European Union Monitoring Mission in Georgia (EUMM). The meeting, which brought together the representatives of Georgia’s central government and de facto authorities of Tskhinvali/South Ossetia, was co-facilitated by Bettina Patricia Boughani, Head of the EU Monitoring Mission in Georgia (EUMM), and Christoph Späti, Special Representative of the OSCE Chairperson-in-Office for the South Caucasus. The next IPRM meeting is set to take place on December 15. SSSG Statement Georgia’s State Security Service said that “all incidents detected in the occupied region and territories adjacent to the occupation line from the previous meeting up to the present date were discussed in detail.” During the meeting, the SSSG representatives “strictly raised the issue of bringing to justice and ensuring the enforcement of law against the representative(s) of the Russian occupation force responsible for the murder of Georgian citizen Tamaz Ginturi .” 23/10/2026 – Two Georgian Citizens Illegally Detained in 2024 Near Tskhinvali Occupation Line Released to Tbilisi The Georgian side once again condemned the practice of so-called borderization and “strictly demanded the immediate release of all individuals held in illegal detention.” According to the SSSG, the meeting also addressed ongoing violations of fundamental human rights in the occupied Tskhinvali region, as well as the illegal restrictions on freedom of movement and the regime at the so-called crossing points. EUMM, OSCE Statement The EUMM and OSCE co-facilitators “welcomed the continued commitment of all participants to the IPRM format and reiterated its importance as a practical platform for addressing security developments and matters impacting conflict-affected communities on both sides of the administrative boundary line (ABL),” the release said . During the meeting, the sides discussed “security developments, focusing on human security and the freedom of movement for conflict-affected populations on both sides of the ABL,” with detention cases remaining “an important part of the discussions.” The co-facilitators reiterated their concern over the “continued practice of detentions,” while welcoming the recent release of detainees. They called for “continued efforts to resolve all existing cases” and encouraged the timely exchange of information, noting that all cases had been discussed “in detail.” “Co-facilitators welcomed the changes to the crossing regime introduced at the beginning of September,” the release said. “But they called on participants to work towards the full reopening of the crossing points. They underlined the importance of freedom of movement for the daily lives, livelihoods and well-being of women, men and children living in the vicinity of the ABL.” 21/08/2026 – Tskhinvali to Expand Operation of Akhalgori, Java Crossing Points The sides also highlighted the role of the EU Monitoring Mission’s hotline “for the timely exchange of information on a wide range of security and humanitarian issues, including detentions and facilitating crossings on humanitarian grounds.” Tskhinvali’s Statement The issue of Georgian police presence near the village of Chorchana/Tsnelisi was also discussed, as at the previous IPRM meeting, according to Igor Kochiev, a representative of the occupied Tskhinvali. “Despite the fact that South Ossetia offers various options for solving this problem, the Georgian side demonstrates the lack of political will and responsibility necessary for the dismantling of the post and its withdrawal from the territory of the republic,” Kochiev told journalists. On security along the boundary between South Ossetia and the rest of Georgia, Kochiev described the situation as “relatively calm, stable and predictable.” He said no crossings of the so-called “state border” or detentions had been recorded during the period, adding that neither the EU Monitoring Mission nor Georgian law enforcement agencies had reported any violations, describing situation as “relatively calm and stable.” Kochiev also claimed that a drone had entered the airspace of the occupied Tskhinvali region but said it was flying too high to identify its type. The representatives of the occupied region again raised the issue of Tamaz Gagloev , an Akhalgori resident detained by Tbilisi on espionage allegations. Kochiev said Tbilisi had provided no clear information on the outcome of court hearings. He also questioned Georgian officials’ assurances that Gagloev was in satisfactory health and expressed hope that representatives of the International Committee of the Red Cross would be able to visit him soon.
