title: Spanish Navy and Navantia design an IAMD frigate aiming to extend F110 class
body: The Spanish Navy and Navantia are developing the new F110 IAMD frigate. This evolution of the Bonifaz class features advanced integrated air and missile defense capabilities to enhance fleet combat power and counter emerging aerial threats. Navantia press release The Spanish Navy and Navantia are working together on the definition of a new frigate, an evolution of the current F110, with enhanced air and missile defence capabilities, with the aim of extending the existing F110 ‘Bonifaz’ class. The work is based on requirements established by the Spanish Navy for the development of a future capability under its Armada 2050 document and builds on the F110 programme, currently under construction. The future configuration, under the name F110 IAMD (Integrated Air and Missile Defence), will evolve the platform to substantially enhance its air and missile defence capabilities while retaining the versatility, anti-submarine and anti-surface warfare capabilities, and digital architecture that characterise this new generation of frigates. The objective is to provide a platform capable of simultaneously and jointly respond to a wide range of air threats, ballistic missiles and cruise missiles, while also performing area air defence, high-value asset escort and air defence coordination missions within a naval task group. Its increased speed and endurance will also facilitate its integration into extended deployments and highly demanding combined operations. F-110 Flight II / IAMD scale model on Navantia booth at DALO Industry Days 2026. New capabilities for the Spanish Navy Integrated air and missile defence: enhanced capability to detect, classify, track and simultaneously engage multiple threats at greater ranges. Greater combat power: expanded vertical launch capacity, designed to accommodate different types of missiles and adapt the weapons load to the requirements of each mission. Advanced command and control: evolution to the SCOMBA New Generation (NG) combat management system, hosted in the cloud and capable of integrating sensors, weapons, autonomous systems (UxVs), onboard systems and data links, enabling a shared tactical picture within the naval combat cloud and supporting the coordination of a naval force’s air defence. Allied interoperability: designed for full integration into NATO and European Union task groups, with the ability to exchange information and operate within joint, multi-domain networks. Response to emerging threats: an open, scalable and cyber-secure architecture designed to incorporate new sensors, effectors and solutions to counter next-generation missiles and uncrewed systems. Multi-mission capability: retention of anti-submarine warfare, anti-surface warfare, electronic warfare and asymmetric threat capabilities, together with a multi-mission space for mission modules, a second helicopter and uncrewed vehicles. Greater availability and efficiency: use of the Digital Twin, condition-based maintenance and the integrated platform management system to anticipate potential issues, optimise through-life support and support crew training. The future frigates will complement the capabilities of the five F110 frigates currently under construction and will represent an evolution of the F110 family aimed at strengthening the fleet’s air and missile defence capabilities. Their final configuration will be developed in close collaboration between the Spanish Navy, the Ministry of Defence and Navantia, in accordance with operational requirements and the corresponding procurement process. Sovereign capability and industrial development The development of these new frigates will provide continuity to a highly complex naval design and shipbuilding capability while strengthening Spain’s strategic autonomy. The programme will mobilise engineering, systems integration and through-life support capabilities, with the involvement of Navantia’s industrial partners, comprising more than 500 companies across Spain, as well as technology centres and academic institutions. The future frigates will further develop the F110 family, which was conceived from the outset to evolve and adapt to changing missions and threats. They will enable the Spanish Navy to incorporate next-generation capabilities to protect the Naval Force, strengthen deterrence and contribute to collective defence, as well as to European and Allied missions. -End- Check out our recent coverage of the F110 IAMD with Navantia during the reveal of the new design at DALO Industry Days 2026: And here is our exclusive tour aboard the first-in-class frigate Bonifaz (F111) recorded in May 2026: The post Spanish Navy and Navantia design an IAMD frigate aiming to extend F110 class appeared first on Naval News .

title: Iran sitting volleyball crowned in Asian games in Japan
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 23 (MNA) – Iran’s men’s sitting volleyball team secured their fifth consecutive title at the Asian Para Games after sweeping past Kazakhstan in straight sets on Friday.
The Iranian team delivered a commanding performance at the Okazaki Central Park General Gymnasium, defeating Kazakhstan 3-0 in the final with set scores of 25-17, 25-15 and 25-17 to extend their dominance in the continental competition, Tehran Times reported.
On their way to the final, the Iranian players overcame Thailand, Kazakhstan and China, advancing through the competition with a series of victories. Their success against these opponents paved the way for another appearance in the final, where they completed their campaign with a convincing win over Kazakhstan.
Sitting volleyball is one of the flagship team sports at the Asian Para Games, bringing together some of the continent’s top athletes with physical impairments. Iran’s latest triumph adds another chapter to the country’s distinguished record in the discipline and reinforces their reputation as a major force in Asian para-volleyball.
With their fifth consecutive title secured, Iran’s players once again celebrated a memorable achievement, keeping the gold medal firmly in their hands and extending a remarkable streak of success at the Asian Para Games.

title: Russia preparing false-flag operations to destabilize Europe – HUR
body:
According to Ukrinform, the press service of the Ukrainian Defense Ministry's Main Intelligence Directorate (HUR) reported this on Telegram .
"Russia is stepping up its destabilization strategy against the European Union with the aim of reducing or cutting off external support for Ukraine by discrediting our country's Security and Defense Forces and intimidating European governments and societies. According to assessments by Ukraine's military intelligence, this could involve carrying out provocative acts of sabotage in Central and Eastern Europe, including the Baltic states," the statement said.
According to the HUR, Russia is considering various scenarios, including false-flag operations followed by accusations against Ukraine through Russian propaganda channels and international platforms accessible to the Kremlin.
According to military intelligence, potential targets for Russian provocations could include critical infrastructure facilities, areas bordering Russia, the Kaliningrad exclave, the Suwalki Gap, regions of EU member states with Russian-speaking populations, and facilities controlled by the Kremlin, including the network of Russian Orthodox Church sites.
In early October 2026, Ukraine's military intelligence said Russian intelligence services had been ordered to step up their activities across the EU and NATO. Ukraine warned its partners about the associated threats.

title: First tanker with Russian diesel under Trump deal heads to US, Reuters reports
body:
A Malta-flagged tanker carrying 40,000 metric tons of Russian diesel is en route to New York, expected to arrive early next month, Reuters reported on Oct. 23, citing LSEG data.
The tanker Agioi Fanendes is delivering the first cargo as part of a deal announced by U.S. President Donald Trump on Oct. 9 to purchase Russian diesel, a step he claims will help push down fuel prices.
The ship loaded its cargo in the Russian Baltic port of Primorsk on Oct. 22 and is set to arrive in the U.S. on Nov. 7, according to Reuters .
Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak announced on Oct. 21 that the first tanker carrying 40,000 metric tons of diesel would soon depart for the U.S. , with additional shipments to follow.
According to Trump, Russia would "immediately supply over 300,000" metric tons of diesel fuel to U.S. and global markets, 500,000 metric tons in November, and 1 million metric tons "immediately thereafter."
Soon after the announcement, Moscow partially lifted restrictions on its diesel exports, permitting the sale of 500,000 metric tons.
The deal has been broadly lambasted by Kyiv, its European allies, and U.S. lawmakers, who argue it will provide little relief to U.S. consumers while helping to fund Moscow's war machine in Ukraine.
The agreement was followed by a sharp deterioration in Ukraine-U.S. ties, with Kyiv facing restrictions on Starlink operations and allegedly deliberate delays in shipments of Patriot interceptors.
Trump has also sharpened his rhetoric toward President Volodymyr Zelensky, claiming the Ukrainian leader is not interested in ending the war and should be replaced.

title: Oil hits $115 as Houthis launch another wave of attacks on Saudi Arabia
body: Oil prices rose on Friday, with Brent hitting $115 a barrel, as Yemen’s Houthi rebels launched another wave of attacks on Saudi Arabia, stoking concerns about further disruption to supplies from the Middle East. Brent , the benchmark for two thirds of the world's oil, was trading 1.65 per cent higher at $115 a barrel at 5.26pm UAE time. West Texas Intermediate, the gauge that tracks US crude, climbed 1.89 per cent to $101.30 a barrel. Brent, which on Thursday settled at its highest level since May 4, is ⁠set to close higher for a third successive week, while WTI ​is ⁠on track to finish ‌lower. “Oil prices remain supported by geopolitical risks with Brent futures and WTI ... both holding on to large overnight gains,” said Edward Bell, head of research at MUFG, and Soojin Kim, research analyst at the group. “Houthi militants claimed an attack on the oil loading port at Yanbu in Saudi Arabia, along with attacks on Aramco facilities and the Dammam airport in the past several days. Production and export flows through the Strait of Hormuz are still holding at close to pre-conflict levels, though at elevated shipping rates.” Saudi Arabia has faced regular attacks from the Iran-backed Houthis, with the group last month making rapid advances along Yemen's Red Sea coast near the Bab Al Mandeb strait, a key waterway for global crude supplies. The Houthis have claimed attacks on the Saudi Defence Ministry headquarters in Riyadh, King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, an Aramco site in Yanbu and Abha International Airport over the past 48 hours. Developments in Libya, an Opec member, are also affecting oil prices. Production was curtailed in the country after the closure of an oil pipeline valve connecting Al Zawiya refinery with the Hamada and Tahara oilfields. People entered the crude receiving station near the refinery and closed the valve, Libya’s National Oil Corporation said in a statement published on Facebook. The pipeline belongs to the Arabian Gulf Oil Company, an NOC subsidiary. Libya’s crude has been valuable to global markets as supply disruptions continue owing to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Many European countries import crude from Libya, with the country’s production estimated at about 1.4 million barrels per day.

title: ‘Serious questions to answer’: Labour slams Luxon over Israel’s Pacific Islands Forum move
body: WELLINGTON, 22 OCTOBER 2026 (RNZ PACIFIC)—New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon has “serious questions to answer” over Israel becoming a partner of the region’s main political decision-making institution, Labour’s foreign affairs spokesperson says. Israel has joined the Pacific Islands Forum (PIF) as a development partner, the Israeli Foreign Ministry announced in a statement on Wednesday. A number of Pacific governments have been forging closer ties with Israel’s government at the same time that its standing in the international community has dropped to a new low. The Israeli government has been widely accused of violating international law with its devastating military attack on Gaza and attacks on four other Middle Eastern countries over the past two years. Luxon stated earlier this month that his Israel counterpart Benjamin Netanyahu would be arrested if he came to New Zealand, after the International Criminal Court’s recent decision to issue arrest warrants for Netanyahu and others in his cabinet. He said Israel’s entry to the PIF ecosystem was ultimately a decision for the Forum, but noted its partnership status would be “lower tier”. The New Zealand leader attended the meeting in Palau last month when PIF leaders decided to recognise Israel as a new partner. ACT leader David Seymour extended “a warm Pacific welcome” to Israel after it was accepted as a partner state. “Another democratic country in the Pacific Islands Forum is a good thing – possibly a bit geographically challenged. But then we’ve had Britain try and join the Trans-Pacific Partnership, so it seems geography is no barrier these days.” However, Labour’s foreign affairs spokesperson Vanushi Walters said if her party were in government, it would have opposed Israel’s inclusion in the PIF. “Christopher Luxon has said that he would arrest Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu if he came to New Zealand,” she said. “He has serious questions to answer on how this situation has come about and what steps New Zealand took to object.” New Zealand has issued a travel ban targeting some Israeli leaders. But in terms of who from Israel would be attending the PIF summit in New Zealand next year, Luxon said it was more on an official level, rather than leader level. Tel Aviv has stepped up its diplomatic focus on the Pacific over the last few years, gaining support from a number of Pacific countries in the process. With its new PIF status, Israel will be obliged to engage actively with the region on development priorities in the areas such as water management, desalination, agriculture and climate change adaptation. “Israel will participate in the Forum’s Sectoral Partnership Stream, enabling focused cooperation in areas of mutual interest,” the Israeli Foreign Ministry said. It also referred to a more wide-ranging agreement between Israel and the PIF that would set out key goals, and a mechanism to measure their progress. The PIF Secretariat itself has not issued a formal statement. In recent times, three Pacific countries have announced they would open embassies in Jerusalem: Papua New Guinea, Fiji and Naoero and other Pacific nations are considering following suit. They are among just a handful of countries that recognise Jerusalem as the capital of Israel, as it remains a disputed territory between Israelis and Palestinians. Samoan government released a statement highlighting Prime Minister La’aulialemalietoa (La’auli) Leuatea Schmidt’s reflections from his past visit. La’auli wants to open the embassy as soon as possible and they are looking forward to it. “The Prime Minister spoke about some of his greatest memories in Israel and one is when he was walking through the old city and seeing an abundance of fruits used to make juice which he said was amazing,” the Samoan government said in a statement on Tuesday. Sione Tekiteki, a former PIF advisor and now law lecturer at Auckland University of Technology (AUT), told RNZ’s Midday Report that Israel was seeking to use the Pacific as a means of legitimising itself – using the affection it has won in the region. “They are obviously tied. The strategic aspect here is gaining formal recognition through the Forum, which elevates it’s status beyond bilateral relationships,” he said. They are among just a handful of countries that recognise Jerusalem as the capital of Israel, as it remains a disputed territory between Israelis and Palestinians. Samoa’s government released a statement highlighting Prime Minister La’aulialemalietoa Leuatea Schmidt’s reflections from his past visit to Jerusalem. “He wants to open the Embassy as soon as possible and they are looking forward to it,” the statement read. “The Prime Minister spoke about some of his greatest memories in Israel and one is when he was walking through the old city and seeing an abundance of fruits used to make juice which he said was amazing.” In June, Fiji hammered out an agreement for Israel to open an embassy in Suva, which would service nine Pacific countries. Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar, who is subject to multiple complaints at the International Criminal Court (ICC) in relation to Gaza, landed in Fiji last June, and was welcomed by Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka – who himself was deployed in the Golan Heights in his military days. Rabuka, while sharing a kava bowl with Sa’ar, told him “We will always be with you.” Most recently, Naoero opened a Jerusalem embassy within days of withdrawing from the ICC. Its government boasted about its record of voting in tow with Israel at the United Nations. Most recently, Naoero opened a Jerusalem embassy within days of withdrawing from the ICC, a move applauded by the Trump administration. The Naoero government press office has not responded to questions on whether this decision had to do with active ICC charges laid against Israeli leaders. Tekiteki said in the decision to grant membership – made in Palau at last month’s PIF leaders summit – partners were considered in their totality, “as opposed to having specific conversations around specific countries”. The nature of Israel’s diplomacy in the region has been described by Israel officials as a “sharing of expertise”, rather than a traditional aid relationship. Israeli firms have established themselves in several Pacific countries, and Pacific nationals are provided opportunities to travel to Israel to study and work. Deputy Foreign Minister Sharren Haskel told RNZ Pacific last year that they do not measure their friendship with the region by the amount spend on aid – which is relatively minor. “Israel is not a major economical power that has a lot of money to spend, especially during times of war,” she said, adding that Israel had no plans to increase support in monetary terms. “It’s not about the amount of money that we can invest but the quality and the things and how it affects the people.” Haskel visited Papua New Guinea and Fiji a year ago. Her country agreed to provide for cybersecurity services in Fiji, with representatives from defence contractor Elbit, also part of her visiting delegation. On the same trip, Haskel suggested that Fiji could deploy army personnel to the Gaza strip, where it is currently carrying out a devastating long-term military campaign against Palestinians. This came before a formal request by the United States to Fiji in December for troops to join a UN-authorized International Stabilisation Force in Gaza – which Fiji has given no formal response to. As for PIF itself, Tekiteki says New Zealand, as next year’s hosts, will have to make some hard decisions around Israel’s participation. “Israel is a sectoral partner… it is still unclear whether, moving forward, sectoral partners would be invited into the PIF leaders meeting, or whether those dialogues would be held at ministerial leave,” he said…. title: APC accuses Atiku of politicising ebola response, says N10bn untouched
body: The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council has accused former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar of politicising Nigeria’s Ebola response, insisting that approved emergency funds remain untouched. The council’s spokesperson, Mr Dele Alake, said this in a statement issued on Thursday in Abuja. Daily Trust reports that President Bola Tinubu approved N10 billion for the Ebola emergency in June. But in his response, Alake said relevant agencies deployed other available resources. INEC: Results with discrepancies won’t be uploaded on IREV Abdulaziz Abdulaziz: Why Tinubu deserves a second term “On accountability, the Atiku camp should note that the N10 billion the President approved for the Ebola emergency in June remains untouched,” he said. He said the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) and other agencies strengthened surveillance at entry points. According to him, the surveillance network alerted the government to the index case and facilitated contact tracing for 44 contacts. The council commended the agencies for their contributions to monitoring the Ebola threat and supporting the public health response. It also criticised Atiku’s reference linking President Tinubu’s name to Ebola, saying it risked turning a serious health concern into political ridicule. “We believe linking and rhyming President Bola Tinubu’s name to Ebola only risks turning a serious health concern into a vehicle to ridicule the President,” Alake said. The council also defended the handling of the infected Nigerian’s detection, citing the virus’s incubation period and the timing of symptoms. “For anyone infected with the virus, the incubation period ranges from two to 21 days, with symptoms typically appearing eight to 10 days after exposure. “An infected person cannot spread or transmit Ebola to others until they actively develop symptoms,” he said. Alake urged opposition politicians to support health authorities rather than criticise the government’s response to the public health threat. “A responsible opposition will applaud the Task Force for being responsive. But the Atiku camp always goes for cheap shots at the government,” he said. The council also rejected Atiku’s allegation that a ministerial briefing was intended to discourage Nigerians from attending campaign rallies or voting. Alake described the allegation as speculative, adding that the briefing instead urged Nigerians to comply with protocols announced by the task force. He called on Atiku and his supporters to avoid politicising public health concerns, urging Nigerians to shun rumours and follow health authorities’ guidance. “We advise Atiku Abubakar and his hirelings to avoid politicising public health issues,” he said. The council said protecting Nigerians from the deadly disease should remain the priority. (NAN)

title: Lagos: One dead, several feared trapped as building collapses
body: One person has been confirmed dead, while three adult males have been rescued following the collapse of a two-storey building under construction in the Fadeyi area of Lagos State. Several other persons are feared trapped beneath the rubble as emergency responders continue search and rescue operations at the scene. The Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA) confirmed the incident in a statement issued by its Permanent Secretary, Dr Olufemi Oke-Osanyintolu, on Friday. Oke-Osanyintolu said the building collapsed in the early hours of Friday, adding that rescue teams were working to establish whether more people remained trapped beneath the debris. Edo Community Leader Defrauded of N5.4m in Fake Appointment Scam INEC: Results with discrepancies won’t be uploaded on IREV According to him, LASEMA received a distress call about the incident at 12:10 a.m., prompting the immediate activation of its Cobra Response Team from the agency’s Onipanu Base. He said the response team arrived at the scene two minutes later, at 12:12 a.m., and discovered that the two-storey structure, which was still under construction, had collapsed. The team subsequently commenced search and rescue operations after preliminary observations indicated that construction workers might have been trapped beneath the wreckage. Oke-Osanyintolu said emergency responders immediately began efforts to locate and evacuate victims while implementing safety measures to protect both the trapped persons and personnel involved in the rescue operation. He disclosed that groaning sounds were heard beneath the rubble during the operation, raising hopes that additional victims could still be alive. To intensify the search, the agency deployed an excavator to assist responders in removing debris and accessing areas where victims were suspected to be trapped. The LASEMA Permanent Secretary said three adult males had been rescued from the collapsed building, while one person was confirmed dead. He added that the rescued victims received immediate pre-hospital medical attention from LASEMA paramedics and personnel of the Lagos State Ambulance Service (LASAMBUS) before being transported to hospital for further treatment. Oke-Osanyintolu listed the agencies involved in the emergency response as the LASEMA Response Team, Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, LASAMBUS and officers of the Nigeria Police Force from Alagbon Division. He said the search and rescue operation remained ongoing as emergency personnel continued efforts to determine whether other construction workers were still trapped beneath the debris. Oke-Osanyintolu said the circumstances surrounding the incident would be investigated by the relevant regulatory agencies.

title: Moscow to Present New ‘Anti-Drone Dome’ at Upcoming Russia-Africa Summit
body:
Russia’s state exporter Rosoboronexport will reveal a planned air defense system called the “Anti-Drone Dome” at next week’s Russia-Africa summit in Moscow, the Interfax news agency reported Friday.
The multilayered system combines radar detection, electronic jamming, weapons and physical barriers, Rosoboronexport said in a statement.
The “Anti-Drone Dome” is designed to protect civilians and military personnel, as well as bridges, buildings and energy and industrial facilities. Rosoboronexport said a separate system offers protection for mobile convoys and cargo.
“All the tools and solutions used in it have proven their effectiveness in real conditions,” Rosoboronexport CEO Alexander Mikheyev said.
The system relies entirely on Russian-manufactured equipment and is “adaptable to a specific partner and specific facility,” the state arms exporter said.
Moscow hosts the Russia-Africa summit next Wednesday and Thursday.
The upcoming presentation for Moscow’s African partners comes as Russia itself continues to struggle against Ukrainian drone attacks that have repeatedly overwhelmed air defense systems, targeting oil refineries, warehouses and data centers.
Earlier this spring, President Vladimir Putin replaced the head of Russia’s Aerospace Forces following a series of destructive Ukrainian drone strikes. Its new chief, Alexander Chaiko, narrowly survived a suicide bomb attack at an upscale Moscow restaurant in August.

title: FACT CHECK: No Palace announcement abolishing Grades 11 and 12
body: Claim: The Office of the President announced the official removal of Grades 11 and 12 from the country’s education system. Rating: FALSE Why we fact-checked this: A Facebook user posted a supposed statement from the Office of the President, purportedly signed by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. It read: “Inanunsyo na ng DepEd [Department of Education] ang pinal na desisyon na tuluyan nang alisin ang Grade 11 at 12 sa ating sistema. Wala na ang Senior High School, kaya magbabago na ang nakasanayang antas ng pagtatapos ng mga mag-aaral.” (The DepEd has announced its final decision to completely remove Grades 11 and 12 from our system. Senior High School is being phased out, which means the established level at which students complete their education will change.) The statement continued, “Ang hakbang na ito ay bahagi ng pagbabago ng DepEd upang ituon ang pokus sa ibang antas ng edukasyon.” (This step is part of the DepEd’s transformation to shift its focus toward other levels of education.) The post’s author said in the caption, “Good news nga ito. Kung ito ay nalagdaan na, laking ginhawa sa mga magulang at sa mga bata. Sayang naman kasi ang dalawang taon para sa K-12 na ‘yan; ‘di naman nagagamit talaga.” (This is indeed good news. If it has already been signed, it will be a huge relief for both parents and children. After all, those two years for K-12 are just a waste — they don’t really get put to any actual use.) The post garnered 1,100 reactions, 352 comments, and 572 shares as of writing. The facts: There is no official announcement abolishing Grades 11 and 12. The K to 12 program remains in effect as it is mandated by law under the Enhanced Basic Education Act of 2013 . The misleading post sourced the fake announcement from a TikTok video posted by “Department of the Philippines,” an account posing as a government social media page. The Department of Education (DepEd) has already debunked the fake post. In an October 21 statement, the agency said, “Fake news ang kumakalat na post sa social media tungkol sa umano’y pagtanggal ng Grade 11 & 12.” (The post circulating on social media regarding the alleged removal of Grades 11 and 12 is fake news.) It further reminded the public not to follow pages falsely claiming to be affiliated with the government and to consult only DepEd’s official channels for verified information. The Presidential Communications Office also denied the statement’s authenticity, according to multiple media reports . Removing K to 12: There have been countless debates and multiple attempts to remove or revise the K to 12 curriculum. In June 2025, Senator Jinggoy Estrada filed Senate Bill No. 3001 or the proposed Rationalized Basic Education Act, which sought to remove senior high school in the current learning system and revert back to the four-year secondary curriculum. In July 2026, Senator Alan Peter Cayetano also voiced opposition to continuing K to 12 and proposed to scale back to K to 10. Back in April, DepEd Secretary Sonny Angara, one of the primary authors of the law, expressed continued support for the K to 12 system amid calls for its abolition. He said that instead of removing it entirely, the department is focusing on “decongesting” the curriculum, such as prioritizing core subjects and addressing concerns over heavy workload. Other fact checks: Rappler has previously debunked false claims about removing the K to 12 curriculum: FACT CHECK: No DepEd announcement abolishing Grades 11 and 12 FACT CHECK: K to 12 program not abolished FACT CHECK: No law passed abolishing K-12 program FACT CHECK: Arroyo did not say the K to 12 program will be abolished – Eirene Manatlao/Rappler.com Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

title: Asian football chief backs Gianni Infantino's Fifa presidency bid
body: Asian football's governing body has said it will support Gianni Infantino's bid for reelection as Fifa ⁠president, having earlier opposed his proposed plans to sell commercial rights to world tournaments. Earlier in July, the Asian Football Confederation had in a statement said that “AFC stands in solidarity with Uefa and Concacaf in expressing serious concerns over Fifa’s proposal to introduce private investment into [its] flagship competitions”. Infantino later apologised for mistakes “in relation to the communication and consultation process” for the World Cup sale plans. On Friday, AFC president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa said the regional body is backing Infantino. “I think that we reaffirm our ​full commitment, ⁠of course, to supporting you and ‌your leadership as you seek a new mandate as a Fifa president,” Sheikh Salman said in comments directed ​at the Swiss-Italian, who was present at the AFC's extraordinary congress in ⁠Tokyo. Later, in an AFC statement, Sheikh Salman added: “Our greatest strength lies in our unity, and we have all seen the historic heights Asian football can achieve when we stand together. The Asian game’s remarkable journey and historic achievements are deeply rooted in the strong partnership, trust, and shared vision that we share as one united family. “As we look towards a brighter and more competitive future, our solidarity remains our greatest strength. We are ready to move forward, united in support of Fifa president Gianni Infantino.” Infantino is up for reelection in March as he seeks a fourth term until 2031. Potential candidates must submit their nominations by November 18. Several key AFC members had publicly declared their support for Infantino. Infantino ‌also gave Sheikh Salman his backing in his address to delegates. “You've been doing a fantastic job in AFC in ⁠the last 13 years, my dear Salman,” he said. “You will do fantastically as well for ⁠the next how many years you want. And always, always with my full support, with the partnership of Fifa, because we have seen what we have been doing in the last years.” While Africa has also backed Infantino's reelection, ​he continues to face opposition from European football's governing body . Uefa has sent a letter to Fifa seeking answers about his presidency, including questions over the World Cup rights sale project and the Fifa Peace Prize. Football's world governing body had revealed plans to sell a 20 per cent stake in a subsidiary company set up to run Fifa's competitions, attracting widespread criticism. Japan Football Association president Tsuneyasu Miyamoto said on Friday that the association was aiming to align with the AFC but ⁠that they had not made a decision.

title: Spanish Navy and Navantia develop F110 IAMD frigate with expanded air and missile defence
body: The work follows requirements set by the navy under its Armada 2050 document, Navantia said on 23 October. The navy, Spain’s Ministry of Defence and the shipbuilder will determine the final configuration through the requirements and procurement process. The design is intended to engage aircraft, ballistic missiles and cruise missiles simultaneously. Its missions would include area air defence, escort of high-value assets and coordination of a naval task group’s air defence. Expanded vertical launch capacity would allow different missile types to be carried, with the weapons load tailored to each mission. Navantia did not disclose launcher numbers, missile selections or how many additional frigates were under consideration. The variant would also have greater speed and endurance for extended deployments and demanding combined operations. It would retain the F110’s anti-submarine and anti-surface warfare capabilities. The frigate would use the cloud-hosted SCOMBA New Generation combat management system to connect sensors, weapons, autonomous vehicles, onboard systems and data links. A shared tactical picture within the naval combat cloud would help coordinate air defence across the force. The architecture is designed to accommodate new sensors, weapons and countermeasures against emerging missiles and uncrewed systems. The ship would also be built to exchange information and operate within NATO, European Union and joint multi-domain networks. Electronic warfare and protection against asymmetric threats would remain part of the ship’s capabilities. A multi-mission space would support mission modules, a second helicopter and uncrewed vehicles. Digital-twin technology, condition-based maintenance and an integrated platform management system would help identify problems, plan support and train crews. Navantia said those tools were intended to improve availability and through-life efficiency. The proposed programme would sustain Spanish naval engineering, shipbuilding and systems integration work. Navantia said its development would involve a domestic industrial network of more than 500 companies, alongside technology centres and academic institutions.

title: Osun Engages Security Agencies on New Transport Law
body: Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo The Osun State Government has engaged security agencies and other relevant stakeholders on the implementation of the state’s Integrated Transport, Traffic and Park Management Law, 2026, ahead of its enforcement. The engagement, held yesterday, was aimed at promoting effective traffic management, curbing illegal revenue collection and ensuring orderliness in the state’s transportation sector. Speaking at the event, the Chairman of the state House of Assembly Committee on Public Works and Transport, representing Irewole/Isokan state constituency, Hon. Abiola Waheed Ibrahim Inaolaji, said the meeting was designed to familiarise participating institutions with the provisions of the law, clarify their responsibilities and strengthen inter-agency collaboration. According to the lawmaker, the law was designed to protect residents and the state’s transport infrastructure. Inaolaji emphasised that enforcement must be carried out within the confines of the law, warning against harassment of motorists, unauthorised revenue collection and abuse of power by enforcement officers. He said the success of the law would depend largely on public confidence, cooperation among relevant agencies and strict adherence to its provisions. According to him, the legislation is intended to protect residents, improve the state’s transportation system and eliminate thuggery and violence associated with motor park activities. Also speaking, the Osun State Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Zungura, described the law as a significant development in the regulation of the state’s transportation sector. Zungura, who noted that the law was signed on October 15, 2026, said it addressed critical aspects of road management, including traffic lights, vehicle impoundment and towing. He expressed optimism that its implementation would improve traffic control and address some of the challenges associated with the existing transportation management system. Zungura said: “The programme is a laudable one that every security agency in the state will appreciate, not only because it involves road management, but it’s also a cooperation of all security agencies to make sure that the road management has been done properly.” He added that the legislation could reduce crises previously experienced at local government motor parks, saying: “In the past, we used to have issues in the local government garages, but this law will minimise, if not eradicate, the crises that normally emanate from the garages.” The police commissioner urged officers responsible for enforcing the law to comply with its provisions, while clarifying that the provision of adequate parking spaces was the responsibility of the relevant transport management authorities. On motorists who cover or deface their vehicle number plates, Zungura said the Inspector-General of Police (IG) had directed commissioners of police across the country to ensure that offenders are arrested and prosecuted. “That’s a very general phenomenon that cuts across all the states. And because of that, the Inspector-General of Police has given a marching order to all Commissioners of Police that any such person or vehicle that is seen covering or defacing the number plate should be arrested and prosecuted,” he said. Also, the FRSC Sector Commander in Osogbo, Sunday Tayo, called on the state government to provide standardised and well-organised motor parks to support effective enforcement of the law. Tayo said the absence of standard motor parks in Osun State could pose challenges to implementation, stressing that appropriate facilities would improve coordination among security agencies and park management officials. “The law is a welcome one. It’s going to help the working apparatus of federal safety,” he said. He urged the government to learn from organised motor parks in Oyo State, citing Iwo Road and Challenge in Ibadan as examples of facilities that could accommodate security agencies and park management officials. According to him, standard motor parks equipped with surveillance cameras and other necessary facilities would improve monitoring and strengthen enforcement. Similarly, Hon. Solanke Hamzak of the Osun State Internal Revenue Service described the law as necessary for the state’s development, urging security personnel and other enforcement officers to discharge their duties in accordance with its provisions. He warned against illegal activities at motor parks, stressing the need for transparency and accountability in the collection of authorised revenues. The engagement forms part of the state government’s preparations for the implementation of the new law, which is expected to strengthen coordination among relevant agencies and improve the administration of transport and motor park activities. Stakeholders at the meeting emphasised the need for cooperation, accountability and lawful enforcement to ensure that the implementation of the legislation promotes road safety, protects commuters and transport operators, and supports an orderly transportation system across Osun State. The sensitisation programme brought together security agencies, transport operators, park managers and other stakeholders to discuss the provisions of the law and their responsibilities ahead of its implementation. The Corps Commander of Osun State Amotekun Corps, High Chief Dr Hon. Adekunle Isaac Omoyele, promised that the state security outfit would support the Osun State Park Management in maintaining law and order in the park. He said Amotekun was established to complement the efforts of other security agencies, and the state security has been cooperating with other security agencies.

The Berezniki branch of Uralchem is reportedly the legal successor to the Berezniki Chemical Plant. It produces ammonia, nitric acid, ammonium nitrate, potassium nitrate, urea, nitrite-nitrate salts and other chemical products.

title: Royal Navy warship duo completes workout in South China Sea
body:
Two Royal Navy warships have completed a major ten-day workout in the South China Sea with allies.
Royal Navy patrol ships HMS Spey and HMS Tamar led the UK’s participation in Bersama Lima 2026, a multinational military exercise involving the five members of the Five Power Defence Arrangements (FPDA): the UK, Australia, Malaysia, New Zealand and Singapore.
Bersama Lima 2026 demonstrated the five nations’ continued commitment to regional security under the FPDA, a defense arrangement established more than 50 years ago.
The exercise tested the participating forces’ ability to operate together across land, sea and air domains through a series of increasingly complex scenarios, culminating in a two-day war game.
Before the operational phase, personnel spent a week familiarizing themselves with each other’s vessels, equipment, procedures and communications to improve interoperability during at-sea operations.
The maritime phase involved corvettes, frigates, patrol ships and a submarine. Activities included maritime security operations, boarding and searching suspect vessels, shore-based target engagement directed by soldiers aboard ships, anti-submarine warfare and air defense exercises supported by aircraft.
HMS Tamar hosted a Royal New Zealand Navy Deployable Boarding Team, which conducted simulated inspections of vessels suspected of illegal fishing and narcotics smuggling. The training also prepared the team and the ship for upcoming maritime patrol duties.
Commander Tom Lindsey , commanding officer of HMS Tamar, said the exercise provided an opportunity to test his crew’s warfighting skills alongside FPDA partners. He highlighted the participation of fifth-generation fighter aircraft, international boarding teams and Singapore’s newest submarine, as well as the forces’ ability to assemble a task group and operate together across different scenarios.
HMS Spey and HMS Tamar are Portsmouth-based River-class offshore patrol vessels, each crewed by approximately 60 sailors. They have maintained a continuous Royal Navy presence in the Indo-Pacific for more than five years under Operation Highmast.
Following the exercise, HMS Spey headed to Southeast Asia for several weeks of patrols and diplomatic engagement. HMS Tamar was scheduled to travel toward Australia and New Zealand through Pacific island chains, conducting maritime security patrols and countering illegal fishing.

title: She Was a Leading Arctic Ornithologist. Now She’s Imprisoned for $25 in Donations.
body:
Sofya Rozenfeld dedicated her life to following Arctic birds across the tundra, counting flocks from a small seaplane and advocating for the species she studied.
When her colleagues urged her to leave Russia as she faced criminal investigation for donating to Alexei Navalny’s Anti-Corruption Foundation (FBK), she struggled to imagine a life away from that work.
“For Sofya, leaving her geese would have been like abandoning her children,” Alexandra Panyutina, who studied with Rozenfeld at Moscow State University and later worked alongside her, told the independent media project Veter.
Even as she awaited sentencing, Rozenfeld continued her fieldwork, securing court permission for a 10-day expedition to the Russian Arctic.
“The first piece of advice [from her colleagues] was to leave Russia,” her friend Artur Ryabitsev said . “But she was against it: ‘No, I live here; I work here; everything I have is here. What would I do outside Russia?’”
On Oct. 7, a Moscow court sentenced the ornithologist to 3.5 years in a penal colony for making two donations totaling 2,000 rubles ($25) to the FBK.
Rozenfeld, 50, is now the third woman in Russia to be imprisoned for donating to the late Kremlin critic’s organization, which was banned as “extremist” in 2021. The Nobel Peace Prize-winning rights organization Memorial has designated her a political prisoner.
The sentence has stunned friends and colleagues, who describe a scientist devoted to studying and protecting Arctic waterfowl.
By spring 2026, authorities had opened more than 200 criminal cases over donations to the FBK, the exiled news outlet Mediazona reported. The average donation amounted to just 400 rubles ($5).
For Rozenfeld, a researcher at the Russian Academy of Sciences’ Institute of Ecology and Evolution, the case threatened to sever a passion for the Arctic that stretched back to her time as a student.
After her family emigrated to Israel in the late 1980s, she returned to Moscow at 15, finished school and enrolled in Moscow State University’s biology faculty. She holds dual Russian-Israeli citizenship.
Panyutina recalled witnessing Rozenfeld’s determination early on.
“Imagine a second-year student organizing her own expedition to Wrangel Island to study snow geese,” she told Veter. “You could say that was the start of her fieldwork. And it continued right up until she was handcuffed.”
Rozenfeld chose to focus her research on the Arctic, particularly geese, swans and related waterfowl that breed in the Far North before migrating thousands of kilometers south.
To track those journeys, one must determine where the birds nest, where they stop during migration and where they spend their winters. But the real challenge lies in determining how many birds there actually are.
Previously, such counts often relied on rough estimates that varied wildly among researchers. Colleagues describe Rozenfeld as one of the few specialists capable of producing more reliable population counts across vast, remote territories.
“She could say: This is how many birds of a particular species we have, this is where they live, and this is where they go for the winter,” Mikhail Kalyakin, director of Moscow State University’s Zoological Museum, told Veter. “To do that, she had to fly over the tundra.”
Working with colleagues, Rozenfeld developed a survey method in which the team would take detailed photos of birds while flying an ultralight seaplane built by a fellow researcher at low altitudes and speeds. These photos would then be used to count populations.
She also got involved with conservation policy, serving on a commission assessing birds for Russia’s Red Data Book of threatened species and helping inform decisions about their protection.
“She fought for their conservation, for their survival, so that we could learn more about them and protect them,” Panyutina said. “She felt responsible for them.”
That sense of responsibility helped keep Rozenfeld from leaving Russia after investigators raided her Moscow apartment and interrogated her in December 2025.
“The first advice she received was to leave Russia,” her friend Artur Ryabitsev told Veter. “But she was against it: ‘No, I live here, I work here, everything I have is here. What would I do outside Russia?’”
Relatives said she could not imagine how she would continue her profession from another country.
She continued her work as the criminal case progressed, including on the court-approved expedition to the Yamalo-Nenets autonomous district shortly before her final hearing.
According to her colleagues, Rozenfeld feared going to prison but remained hopeful that she would receive a lighter punishment.
In court, she explained that she had signed up for recurring donations to FBK “out of a desire to fight corruption.”
“Don’t we have law enforcement agencies for that?” the judge interrupted .
“I believe that any public help is needed here,” she replied. “Because I have seen the horrific forms this evil can take in my own work related to scientific research and environmental protection. It seemed to me that any help in combating corruption would be a good thing.”
While the verdict shocked her friends and family, Panyutina recalled that Rozenfeld herself appeared composed and focused in court — “like someone in an extraordinarily difficult situation trying with all her strength to keep composure and maintain dignity.”
As soon as the sentence was announced, uniformed officers approached Rozenfeld to take her into custody.
“They handcuffed Sofya and pushed her into the cage,” Ryabitsev recalled. “The judge finished reading the verdict, and then they took her away.”
Her relatives have since set up a support website and appealed to the Israeli authorities for assistance. Israel’s Foreign Ministry told Newsru.co.il that it was in contact with her family, but did not say whether a consular official had visited her.
Rozenfeld is one of a growing number of Russian academics, scientists and engineers who have been prosecuted for donating to FBK.
Andrei Dymov, an associate professor at the Higher School of Economics and senior researcher at the Steklov Mathematical Institute, are among those who have been prosecuted. Physicist Yevgeny Onishchenko, a former researcher at the Lebedev Physical Institute, received 18 months of compulsory labor for a 5,000 ruble ($60) donation.
“I think, until the very last second, none of us could really take in the possibility that she would actually go to prison,” Panyutina said. “Including Sofya herself.”

title: Nollywood actor Francis Duru dies at 57
body: Veteran Nollywood actor, Francis Duru, has passed away. He died at the age of 57 following a brief illness. His family announced this in a statement published on the actor’s Instagram page in the early hours of Friday. “We, the family of Francis Duru, regret to announce his passing following a brief illness. APC accuses Atiku of politicising ebola response, says N10bn untouched Lagos: One dead, several feared trapped as building collapses “We appreciate your prayers, love, and understanding. May his soul rest in peace. Amen,” the statement read. The announcement was also confirmed by the National President of the Actors Guild of Nigeria (AGN), Abubakar Yakubu, in a post on the guild’s Instagram page. Reacting to the development, Yakubu paid tribute to the late actor, describing his death as the loss of another great talent in the Nigerian film industry. “Another great thespian is gone. Rest in peace, Francis Duru,” he wrote. Duru was a veteran figure in Nollywood whose acting career spanned several productions in the Nigerian film industry. He was known for his performances in movies that contributed to his recognition among audiences. He gained prominence through his role in the 1995 film Rattlesnake, one of the productions associated with his career in Nollywood. Over the years, Duru featured in several Nigerian films, establishing himself as one of the actors who contributed to the development and growth of the country’s movie industry.

title: Putin Says Renewed Peace Talks Must Focus on Security for Russia, Ukraine and Europe Overall
body:
Russia n President Vladimir Putin said Thursday that future talks on ending the war against Ukraine should focus on security guarantees for both countries and an overall framework for security throughout Europe.
Putin, interviewed on Russia n state television a day after meeting U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff, confirmed that Russia was ready to resume U.S.-mediated talks with Ukraine next month.
He restated longstanding Kremlin policy that Russia never wanted to launch its full-scale invasion, but had run into hostile reactions from Ukraine on key issues of concern to Moscow.
Talks on a variety of matters could lead to a positive outcome, Putin said, but Russia remained intent on resolving the conflict once and for all rather than agreeing to a short-lived ceasefire.
"The goal of these talks will be to ensure the security of Ukraine and Russia after reaching peace agreements, in their final form, not as a result of a temporary ceasefire for some short period of time. We are ready to resume these contacts to achieve this goal," Putin said.
The Russia n president said Witkoff also stressed that discussions had to extend to "the architecture of European security as a whole. And I agree with that too. Well, let's see how things develop in the coming days."
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who met Witkoff in Norway on Tuesday, said Ukraine was ready for talks likely to take place by early next month. Ukraine, he said, supported "any proposals for a ceasefire, an end to the war, an energy ceasefire as well as humanitarian initiatives."
The United States has led efforts to negotiate an end to the war in Ukraine, but talks have stalled since Trump ordered attacks against Iran in February.
Many of the disagreements about how to end the Ukraine war focus on territory, with Russia demanding Ukraine cede all of eastern Ukraine's Donbas region. Kyiv rejects any deal that would include giving up land it currently holds.
In his comments on Thursday , Putin said any discussion on territory in eastern Ukraine had to consider what he said was the fact that the area was "historically Russia n land."
And residents there, he claimed, had voted to be a part of Russia in referendums staged seven months after Moscow launched its full-scale invasion.
"Firstly, my attitude on this matter is that this is not their territory. It’s the territory of historical Russia ," Putin said.

title: Two Georgian Citizens Illegally Detained in 2024 Near Tskhinvali Occupation Line Released to Tbilisi
body: Two Georgian citizens who were detained on September 16, 2024, near Mejvriskhevi, a village in Gori municipality adjacent to the Tskhinvali occupation line, have been released and returned to the Tbilisi-controlled territory, the State Security Service of Georgia (SSSG) said on October 22. The agency reported the releases after two years in custody on the same day as the 135th meeting of the Incident Prevention and Response Mechanism (IPRM), which addresses the security incidents on the ground and brings together the representatives of Georgia’s central government and de facto authorities of Tskhinvali/South Ossetia, was held in Ergneti, a village near the Tskhinvali occupation line. “All relevant instruments available to the central government were used to release Georgian citizens from illegal detention, including the ‘hotline’ mechanism managed by the EU Monitoring Mission in Georgia (EUMM),” the SSSG said, adding that they “continue to work actively toward the release of all Georgian citizens held in illegal detention in the occupied territories.” In line with its practice, the agency did not disclose the individuals’ identities or publish any photos of their release. According to the SSSG, “the issue of the Georgian citizens’ unconditional release from illegal detention was regularly discussed within the frameworks of the Incident Prevention and Response Mechanism (IPRM) and the Geneva International Discussions.” SSSG’s latest annual report states that 34 cases of illegal detention were recorded around the occupied Tskhinvali region in 2025. title: SH Defence, Naval Group ink MoU on modular naval solutions
body:
Danish naval equipment supplier SH Defence and French shipbuilder Naval Group have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to explore cooperation on modular capabilities for naval operations.
The agreement establishes a framework for the two companies to explore opportunities in mission modularity, containerized mission solutions, and launch and recovery systems supporting unmanned systems and diving operations.
The cooperation will focus on solutions that allow naval platforms to adapt to changing mission requirements by integrating different capabilities. These include systems for deploying and recovering unmanned platforms, as well as equipment supporting diving operations.
Modular mission systems allow navies to configure vessels for different operational tasks by integrating mission-specific equipment. Containerized solutions can support this approach by allowing capabilities to be installed, removed, or exchanged as requirements change.
The MoU provides a basis for SH Defence and Naval Group to combine their expertise and explore modular solutions for future naval requirements. The companies have not disclosed specific projects, contract values, or delivery timelines.
To remind, Naval Group recently partnered with PhotonFirst to test the use of fibre-optic sensors on the structures of surface vessels and submarines.

title: Opinion| The nation hears the silence, but waits for its envoys to speak
body: South Sudan has seemingly slipped from the radar of international donors. This neglect represents more than a moral shortcoming. It poses a strategic risk that requires South Sudanese diplomats in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to act with urgency and determination. Funding for South Sudan’s humanitarian appeal remains persistently inadequate. In Western capitals, the conversation has evolved from helping build the world’s newest nation to containing an endless emergency. This exhaustion has resulted in drastic reductions in food assistance, medical care, and schooling. The World Food Programme has been compelled to make heart-breaking decisions, reducing food allocations for refugees and other vulnerable groups, pushing millions toward the edge of starvation. This is precisely where South Sudan’s diplomatic corps must take action. The days of sitting back and waiting are finished. Issuing statements from Juba bemoaning insufficient funding accomplishes unknown. South Sudanese ambassadors in Washington, London, Brussels, Beijing, and the Gulf states need to transform themselves from passive observers into energetic champions of their people’s cause. They must approach the international donor community with a coordinated, clear, and compelling approach. To begin with, diplomats need to tackle donor fatigue directly. They should openly recognise the legitimate worries about transparency and accountability that have long dogged aid efforts in South Sudan. By offering a transparent, verifiable framework for how money is spent and safeguarded, diplomats can restore the confidence needed to release held-back funds. The message should be unmistakable. Putting money into South Sudan isn’t throwing it away. It’s a vital investment in regional peace and security. South Sudanese representatives abroad must capitalise on their geopolitical connections. South Sudan isn’t standing alone. It maintains strategic partnerships throughout the region and beyond, with allies who have real stakes in its stability. Diplomats should present the humanitarian emergency not merely as a question of conscience, but as a matter of security. An unstable South Sudan poses a threat to the entire Horn of Africa, with possible consequences for migration patterns and commerce. This case needs to be made vigorously within the halls of the United Nations and the European Union. What’s more, diplomatic missions should actively pursue relationships with unconventional donors. While Western nations may be preoccupied, rising economies and regional powers might be ready to step into the gap. South Sudanese ambassadors need to broaden their scope, looking for partnerships that extend past traditional charity toward long-term development, infrastructure projects, and agricultural ventures. The international community’s silence is striking, but it doesn’t have to last forever. Determined diplomacy can fill the opening. Millions of South Sudanese lives depend on it. They cannot afford to have their representatives sit back. The moment has arrived for South Sudan’s diplomats to become the most passionate advocates for their people’s survival. They must pound on every door, insist on a voice at every negotiating table, and remind the world that South Sudan, however young, exists and matters. International donors may have lost sight of it, but South Sudan’s diplomats must make certain the world never forgets. The writer is a South Sudanese journalist and a student at the University of Juba, pursuing a Master’s Degree in International Relations. title: Governor Rimbasa, officials inspect Yambio Ebola unit to test readiness
body: Western Equatoria State Caretaker Governor Badagbu Daniel Rimbasa on Thursday led a high-level delegation to inspect an Ebola isolation unit in Yambio to assess the facility’s readiness to receive and manage suspected cases. The inspection took place at the Infectious Disease Unit (IDU), also known as the Ebola Treatment Unit (ETU), where health workers conducted a simulation exercise to assess emergency response procedures and identify areas requiring improvement. The delegation included State Health Minister Nama Bukulu, security officials, government representatives, health partners and a team from the National Public Health Institute in Juba. The exercise focused on the facility’s capacity to screen patients, isolate suspected cases, prevent infection and ensure that health workers are prepared to respond safely if an Ebola case is reported. Speaking during the visit, Governor Rimbasa said the government was working with health authorities, security agencies and humanitarian partners to strengthen preparedness and protect communities from the risk of Ebola. “We have taken drastic measures as the Government of Western Equatoria State to control the entry of the dangerous Ebola through our state. There is political will to increase our surveillance and also to visit the readiness in case we have a case,” Governor Rimbasa said during the inspection. “I called all officials, including security organs, so that we can have concerted efforts in place to prevent Ebola from entering South Sudan through Western Equatoria because we are just a few kilometers from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).” He commended the Ministry of Health and its partners for their efforts to strengthen disease prevention and emergency response capacity in Western Equatoria. For her part, Nama Bukulu, the state’s health minister, said authorities were assessing the isolation unit’s readiness, including its facilities, documentation and response procedures. “We have come to this center to check how prepared the facility is to receive a confirmed case,” she said. “We are also carrying out a simulation exercise that is supposed to check on our surveillance.” Bukulu said the facility has separate male and female sections and a designated red zone for patient isolation and green zones to support health workers, to support infection prevention and patient management. Meanwhile, Dr. Nomi Poni, the facility manager of the Infectious Disease Unit and acting team leader for the International Medical Corps (IMC) in Western Equatoria State, said the facility has a capacity of 28 beds across four wards. “This Infectious Disease Unit is where we will treat Ebola patients if we receive any. You have seen government officials and partners here because we are doing a simulation exercise to test our readiness,” she said. “Since the outbreak of Ebola in DRC, we have not received any cases in South Sudan, so this delegation from Juba came to test our readiness.” Other facilities include a pharmacy, an ambulance parking area, staff accommodation and space for psychosocial support. The International Medical Corps manages the facility in collaboration with health authorities and supporting partners, including the World Health Organization (WHO) and UNICEF. The exercise is part of ongoing efforts to strengthen Western Equatoria’s capacity to detect, investigate and respond to suspected Ebola cases and protect the wider population. The post Governor Rimbasa, officials inspect Yambio Ebola unit to test readiness appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Abdulaziz Abdulaziz: Why Tinubu deserves a second term
body: Senior Special Assistant to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu on Media and Public Enlightenment, Abdulaziz Abdulaziz, has said the president deserves a second term in 2027 to consolidate ongoing reforms and translate them into greater prosperity for Nigerians. Abdulaziz said the administration had recorded significant achievements in infrastructure, education, healthcare and economic reforms, arguing that Nigerians should give Tinubu another opportunity to complete ongoing projects and deliver more tangible benefits to citizens. He spoke at the inauguration of the Kano State executive and local government coordinators of Arewa for Asiwaju (A4A), a support group campaigning for the president’s re-election. According to him, the group was established to counter what it considers misinformation about the administration’s performance, particularly in Northern Nigeria, by taking evidence of its achievements to the grassroots. “People will tell you that Tinubu has not done anything for the North, but the evidence suggests otherwise,” he said. He explained that A4A intended to promote evidence-based campaigning and equip voters with information to make informed decisions ahead of the 2027 general elections. Abdulaziz said the administration had invested in infrastructure and introduced reforms aimed at placing the country on a path of sustainable growth, adding that the next term should focus on converting the gains of the reforms into improved living conditions. “The next term is about consolidating the reforms, but also translating them into more impactful results, especially for the poor, for people to have prosperity,” he said. He described the proposed campaign slogan, “From Reform to Prosperity,” as a reflection of the administration’s intended direction for a second term. The presidential aide also cited the ongoing Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano expressway project as evidence of the administration’s infrastructure drive, pointing to the commissioning of a section of the road by the president, represented by Kano State Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf. He argued that the quality of the road infrastructure demonstrated how resources freed up by the removal of the petrol subsidy were being channelled into development projects. On education, Abdulaziz highlighted the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), saying the programme was helping students from low-income families remain in school by providing loans for tuition and upkeep. He said the administration’s second term would focus more on improving household prosperity, including access to affordable transportation, food and other basic necessities. Speaking specifically on Kano, Abdulaziz said the state stood to benefit from the completion of major infrastructure projects, particularly the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano (AKK) gas pipeline project. He said pipeline installation had been completed and that a power substation was expected to be established in Kano, adding that the project included plans for a power generation plant with a capacity of about 700 megawatts. According to him, re-electing Tinubu would help ensure the completion of ongoing projects and create opportunities for Kano to attract further federal investments. He also urged Kano residents to support the president, arguing that the state’s political influence and voting strength could give it a stronger voice in negotiations for federal development projects. Earlier, the Kano State Coordinator of Arewa for Asiwaju, Abdullahi Tijjani Muhammad Gwarzo, called on the newly inaugurated executives and local government coordinators to strengthen the group’s grassroots structures and work towards Tinubu’s re-election. Gwarzo expressed appreciation to the organisation’s national leadership, led by its Board of Trustees Chairman, former Kano State Governor Ibrahim Shekarau, and Director-General, former Jigawa State Governor Muhammad Badaru Abubakar, for their support. He also acknowledged the guidance and support of Kano State Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf and other stakeholders involved in the inauguration. He said A4A’s mission extended beyond political mobilisation to promoting national unity, inclusiveness, fairness and shared prosperity. “As we approach the 2027 general elections, we must work collectively and responsibly in support of the APC presidential candidate, His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, and all other candidates of our great party,” he said. Gwarzo urged the newly inaugurated officials to demonstrate discipline, integrity and commitment to their responsibilities, while strengthening collaboration with party stakeholders and expanding engagement at the grassroots. He further called on members to ensure that their political activities remained peaceful, lawful and respectful of democratic principles. “An appointment is not merely a title; it is a call to service,” he said, urging the coordinators to place collective interests above personal ambitions. He expressed confidence that unity and sustained mobilisation would help the organisation achieve its objectives ahead of the 2027 elections.

title: NITDA to journalists: Use AI to verify information
body: The Director-General of the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA), Kashifu Inuwa Abdullahi, tasked journalists to use artificial intelligence to authenticate stories before amplifying it. Abdullahi said this is important because people no longer believe in what they see or read because artificial intelligence can manufacture convincing falsehoods that can be hard to separate from the truth. He said the same technology that used to distort reality can be used to address those challenges as well. “Today in an AI age, it is very difficult to believe what we see. So, looking at that, today everything can be a fact, and that makes us doubt every other thing we see. “For us, the greatest contribution AI can give to the newsroom is not generating faster breaking news. But if we can use AI to get people to believe what they see. “So I believe you are going to use AI in your newsroom for verification, for amplifying authenticity, for letting people trust what they see. We want to see you using AI to verify everything. “We believe your team is going to use the AI responsibly and ethically to propagate trust in the country,” he said.

title: US Senator Blumenthal opens probe into Ukraine Starshield restrictions
body:
U.S. Democratic Senator Richard Blumenthal said on Oct. 22 he had launched an inquiry into sudden restrictions of Starshield satellite services in Ukraine that hampered the country's ability to intercept Russian drones.
Starshield is the militarized version of the Starlink system, operated by Elon Musk 's SpaceX company and widely used by the Ukrainian military.
Kyiv said that overnight on Oct. 14, SpaceX implemented restrictions on Starshield operations in Ukraine, capping its speed limit at 161 kilometers per hour (kph) and curbing Ukrainian interceptors' ability to down Russian jet-powered drones.
"This decision to limit critical technology for a key ally... (puts) Ukrainian forces at risk and their people in peril," Blumenthal wrote in a letter addressed to U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
The move also "raises serious questions about who controls critical capabilities the U.S. government has spent billions of dollars to procure," the senator continued.
Neither Musk nor the Trump administration publicly claimed responsibility for the slowdown, but the Wall Street Journal (WSJ) reported on Oct. 21 that the order came from the SpaceX founder.
The outlet separately wrote a day later that Trump called Musk to lift the restrictions. However, a Ukrainian official told the Kyiv Independent that the 161 kph limit is still in place.
Blumenthal, who sits on the Senate's Subcommittee on Investigations, asked the Pentagon to clarify who ordered the restrictions and to provide information on the U.S. military's own reliance on Starlink.
The pro-Ukraine lawmaker also stressed that the reports "raise further questions about the respective roles of (the Pentagon), the White House, and SpaceX in controlling and modifying the service."
"If the Pentagon cannot say plainly who has the authority to degrade a military communications network, our partners cannot rely on it, and our adversaries will look for ways to exploit that uncertainty."
Blumenthal asked Hegseth to provide information by Nov. 5. As the Democrats lack a majority in the Senate, they do not hold the subpoena power.
The Democratic Party aims to wrest control of both chambers of Congress from the Republicans during the upcoming midterm elections on Nov. 3.
