title: Two Finnish firms progress satellite plans for Ukraine
body:
Ukraine is urgently seeking alternatives to Elon Musk's Starlink internet service which recently capped its connection speed in the country.
Finnish space tech firm Iceye and networking giant Nokia are partnering with Ukraine's defence ministry to develop satellite communications in the war-torn country.
Ukraine is looking to reduce its dependence on the United States-based satellite internet service provider Starlink, owned by multi-billionaire Elon Musk 's firm SpaceX.
A letter of intent about the firms' cooperation with Ukraine was signed on Thursday in Kyiv, during Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo 's (NCP) visit to the country.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the agreement is important for the country's defence and resilience, the Kyiv Independent reported.
Musk has recently capped the speed of Starlink services in Ukraine. The embattled country has used Starlink for military communications and operating drones — but hampered network speeds reduce Ukraine's capabilities on the battlefield.
However on Thursday, US President Donald Trump said that Musk had restored Starlink service in Ukraine — while at the same time declining to comment on reports that he had discussed the matter with the billionaire.
According to US and Ukrainian officials interviewed by the Wall Street Journal , the Starlink system began to function better after the reported discussion.
However, according to the Kyiv Independent, speed restrictions on Starlink's military version, Starshield, still haven't been lifted, despite reports that either Musk or Trump had ordered the restrictions — introduced just over a week ago — to be removed.
Ukraine needs secure, independent and powerful satellite communication systems that the country controls itself, Iceye chief executive Rafal Modrzewski said in a press release.
"We have a proven track record of delivering sovereign missions at speed to help build that capability. Iceye has proudly supported Ukraine since 2022, and we remain committed to continuing that support today," the CEO and co-founder said.
Iceye's and Nokia's cooperation was announced earlier this month .
At the time, Professor Jaan Praks from Aalto University told Yle that Iceye has a firm grasp on today's geopolitical realities.
According to Praks, Europe urgently needs its own, sovereign satellite system.
"Iceye knows what European states need, perhaps better than anyone else—perhaps even better than the really big satellite manufacturers like Airbus and others," Praks said earlier this month.
Praks is a space technology researcher, and Iceye's roots trace back to his research group at Aalto University.
Iceye was founded in Otaniemi, Espoo, in 2014 and now has more than 1,500 employees with operations in around ten countries. The firm operates around 80 satellites that transmit Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images of the Earth.
In its early days, Iceye's focus was on mapping storm and flood damage in real time as well as monitoring effects of climate change, but today its operations are increasingly security-focused.
The militaries of Finland, Poland and the Netherlands, among others, have made deals with Iceye, which had a turnover of over 250 million euros in 2025.
SpaceX has a network of over 10,000 Starlink satellites — far more than any European entity.
According to Marko Höyhtyä , research professor at the VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland and satellite comms expert, it's unlikely anyone could access that kind of performance at the same price from any other operator — but other factors weigh in favour of a European solution.
"Price is hardly the decisive argument, especially not at this early stage. Other factors weigh more heavily, such as independence from the US and similar considerations," Höyhtyä told Yle earlier this month.

title: The 10 highest-rated movies of the 2020s so far, according to Letterboxd
body: Letterboxd has become an increasingly influential measure of a film's popularity, offering an alternative to traditional critics' reviews and box-office figures. Launched in 2011, the film-focused social platform allows users to rate movies with up to five stars, write reviews and create lists. Its popularity has surged from about 1.8 million members in 2020 to more than 28 million by April 2026, with particularly strong appeal among Gen-Z. Unlike Rotten Tomatoes , which measures the percentage of critics who give a film a positive review, Letterboxd uses a weighted average of members' ratings. Its rankings offer an insight into audience enthusiasm, with independent films and documentaries competing alongside Hollywood blockbusters. Based on a combined ranking of narrative features and documentaries compiled on October 17, these are the 10 highest-rated films released since 2020, each with at least 25,000 Letterboxd ratings. Their Rotten Tomatoes critics' scores are included for comparison. 1. You Can See Everything (2026) Letterboxd score: 4.7/5 Rotten Tomatoes: 98% Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim's documentary follows Elizabeth Holmes , the disgraced founder of blood-testing company Theranos, during the final weeks before her imprisonment for fraud. Given access to Holmes and her family, the filmmakers explore her claims of innocence while questioning the nature of truth and manipulation. Released in October, the nearly three-hour film briefly achieved a 4.8-star Letterboxd score, becoming the platform's highest-rated release. You Can See Everything also earned $15 million during its North American opening weekend, the biggest documentary debut in more than two decades. The film has received five Critics Choice Documentary Award nominations, including Best Documentary Feature. 2. No Other Land (2024) Letterboxd score: 4.6/5 Rotten Tomatoes: 100% Palestinian filmmakers Basel Adra and Hamdan Ballal join Israeli filmmakers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor to document the destruction of Palestinian communities in Masafer Yatta in the occupied West Bank. Filmed over several years, the documentary follows Adra's efforts to record demolitions and displacement, alongside his developing friendship with Abraham. Despite struggling to secure a US distributor, the film won Best Documentary Feature at the 2025 Academy Awards, becoming the first Palestinian film to win an Oscar. During his acceptance speech, Adra spoke of his hopes that his newborn daughter would not experience the displacement and violence his community faces. Read The National 's review of the film here . 3. Naza (2026) Letterboxd score: 4.5/5 Rotten Tomatoes: 100% Oscar-winning filmmakers Abraham and Szor follow up No Other Land with this documentary that examines Israeli military operations in Gaza through anonymous testimonies from intelligence and military personnel. Filmed on rooftops in Tel Aviv, the film investigates how acceptable levels of civilian casualties are calculated during air strikes. Its title comes from an Israeli military term used to count expected civilian deaths. Produced by The Guardian and JW Films, with Jonathan Glazer as executive producer, Naza won the Special Jury Prize at the 2026 Venice International Film Festival after receiving a 25-minute standing ovation . The film subsequently secured theatrical distribution in 56 territories, including the Middle East , with plans for free global streaming. Read The National 's review of the film here . 4. The Voice of Hind Rajab (2025) Letterboxd score: 4.4/5 Rotten Tomatoes: 93% Tunisian filmmaker Kaouther Ben Hania reconstructs the final hours of five-year-old Palestinian girl Hind Rajab , who was trapped in a car under Israeli fire in Gaza in January 2024. Combining real recordings of Hind's emergency calls with dramatised scenes, the film follows Palestine Red Crescent Society workers attempting to organise her rescue. It won the Silver Lion Grand Jury Prize at the 2025 Venice International Film Festival and received an Oscar nomination. The film has also remained central to calls for accountability. In August 2026, Ben Hania and Palestinian actor Motaz Malhees questioned whether an Israeli military investigation into Hind's killing would deliver justice. Read The National 's review of the film here . 5. La Bola Negra (2026) Letterboxd score: 4.4/5 Rotten Tomatoes: 86% Spanish filmmakers Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi explore identity, relationships and personal struggles across generations in this drama inspired by an unfinished work by poet and playwright Federico Garcia Lorca. Spanning three periods of Spanish history, the film follows three interconnected lives shaped by longing, loss and inheritance. Its ensemble cast includes Penelope Cruz, Glenn Close, Miguel Bernardeau and singer Guitarricadelafuente. La Bola Negra shared the Best Director prize at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival before winning the People's Choice Award at Toronto and an audience award at San Sebastian. It was also selected as Spain's submission for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards. 6. Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse (2023) Letterboxd score: 4.4/5 Rotten Tomatoes: 95% Miles Morales returns in this animated sequel, travelling between dimensions after encountering a team of Spider-People responsible for protecting the multiverse. His journey brings him into conflict with Miguel O'Hara, whose determination to preserve the established order threatens Miles's future. Directed by Joaquim Dos Santos, Kemp Powers and Justin K Thompson, the film expands on the distinctive animation of 2018's Into the Spider-Verse , combining multiple artistic styles. It won seven Annie Awards in 2024, including Best Animated Feature, and received an Academy Award nomination for Best Animated Feature, losing to Hayao Miyazaki's The Boy and the Heron . Read The National 's review of the film here . 7. Dune: Part Two (2024) Letterboxd score: 4.4/5 Rotten Tomatoes: 92% Denis Villeneuve's science-fiction epic continues Paul Atreides's journey on the desert planet Arrakis as he joins the Fremen and seeks revenge against those responsible for his family's downfall. Timothee Chalamet reprises his role as Paul, alongside Zendaya as Chani, with Rebecca Ferguson, Javier Bardem, Florence Pugh and Austin Butler completing the ensemble. Adapted from Frank Herbert's novel, the film explores political power, religious prophecy and the consequences of revenge. Dune: Part Two earned more than $700 million worldwide and won two Academy Awards in 2025, for Best Sound and Best Visual Effects. It was also nominated for Best Picture. Read The National 's review of the film here . 8. How to Make Millions Before Grandma Dies (2024) Letterboxd score: 4.4/5 Rotten Tomatoes: 98% Thai filmmaker Pat Boonnitipat's family drama follows M, a young man who moves in with his terminally ill grandmother after learning of her cancer diagnosis. Initially hoping to secure an inheritance, he gradually develops a deeper understanding of family responsibility and the sacrifices involved in caring for someone. Starring Putthipong Assaratanakul and Usha Seamkhum, the film became a major box office success across South-East Asia, attracting attention for its portrayal of ageing and family relationships. It won the Audience Award at the 2024 New York Asian Film Festival and became the first Thai film shortlisted for the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film. 9. Chainsaw Man – The Movie: Reze Arc (2025) Letterboxd score: 4.4/5 Rotten Tomatoes: 96% Based on Tatsuki Fujimoto's manga, Chainsaw Man – The Movie: Reze Arc continues the story of Denji, a young devil hunter who can transform parts of his body into chainsaws. His life takes an unexpected turn when he meets Reze, a mysterious girl who offers the possibility of romance and an ordinary existence. Their developing relationship soon draws him into another violent confrontation with supernatural enemies. Directed by Tatsuya Yoshihara and produced by animation studio Mappa, the film earned acclaim for its energetic action sequences and distinctive animation. It also became an international box-office hit, following the success of the original television series. 10. Monster (2023) Letterboxd score: 4.4/5 Rotten Tomatoes: 97% Japanese filmmaker Hirokazu Kore-eda examines a troubling incident at a school through the perspectives of a mother, a teacher and two young boys, gradually revealing how misunderstandings can distort the truth. The story begins when single mother Saori notices unusual changes in her son Minato's behaviour and suspects a teacher is responsible. As events unfold from different viewpoints, the film explores childhood, prejudice and the difficulty of understanding others. Written by Yuji Sakamoto, Monster premiered at the 2023 Cannes Film Festival, where it won Best Screenplay. It also features one of the final film scores composed by Ryuichi Sakamoto , who died in March that year.

title: Military horses could carry loads in the field again
body: Exercise COPPER HORSE found that Military Working Horses may be able to support a limited range of field tasks under controlled training conditions, with further development needed on equipment, load carriage and operating endurance, according to an answer given in Parliament. Ben Obese-Jecty, the Conservative member for Huntingdon, asked the Secretary of State for Defence what findings were made on the feasibility of the operational use of horses during Exercise Copper Horse. Louise Sandher-Jones, the Minister for the Armed Forces, said: “Exercise COPPER HORSE found that Military Working Horses may be able to support a limited range of field tasks under controlled training conditions. It also identified areas requiring further development, including equipment, load carriage and operating endurance before any judgement can be made on potential operational use.” Britain’s forces keep around five hundred horses, almost all of them in ceremonial roles with the Household Cavalry Mounted Regiment in London, the King’s Troop Royal Horse Artillery at Woolwich, and the Defence Animal Training Regiment at Melton Mowbray, which trains horses and military working dogs. A horse can carry around a fifth of its body weight, and United States special forces operated on horseback in northern Afghanistan in 2001, and the French, Italian, Austrian and Swiss armies retain mules or horses for mountain logistics. We reported recently that the British Army has been experimenting with the use of horses for reconnaissance, patrol and security tasks in terrain where military vehicles may struggle to operate, according to imagery released by the Ministry of Defence. Soldiers and Military Working Horses from the Household Cavalry Mounted Regiment took part in a mounted combat capability experiment on the Barossa training area at Sandhurst, exploring how mounted troops could support battlefield activity beyond the Regiment’s familiar ceremonial duties. The training was conducted across difficult terrain and focused on environments where conventional vehicles could face restrictions, giving soldiers an opportunity to examine how horses might provide an alternative means of moving personnel during reconnaissance and security operations. The post Military horses could carry loads in the field again first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Russian attacks leave nearly 105,000 customers without power in Volyn region, one person injured
body:
According to Ukrinform, acting head of the Volyn Regional Military Administration Roman Romaniuk reported this on Telegram .
He said the region had been attacked by more than ten jet-powered Shahed-type UAVs overnight.
"Attacks on energy facilities have left nearly 105,000 customers without electricity. Facilities in the Lutsk and Kovel districts were among those affected," the post said.
According to Romaniuk, one person was injured in the Russian attacks and a house was damaged in the Lutsk district.
There are also partial restrictions on water supply in Lutsk, and emergency repair crews are working in an enhanced capacity.

title: 5 European Leaders Floated as Potential Negotiators With Putin
body:
Five European leaders, including Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and Finnish President Alexander Stubb, are being considered as potential negotiators with Russian President Vladimir Putin as Europe seeks a bigger role in efforts to end Russia’s war against Ukraine.
Other names under consideration include Czech President Petr Pavel, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre, The Telegraph reported on Friday, Oct. 23, citing diplomatic sources.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
European diplomats have approached potential candidates about the role, the report says.
The debate comes as US President Donald Trump pursues direct engagement with Putin, raising fears in European capitals that Washington and Moscow could shape a peace deal while leaving Ukraine’s European allies on the sidelines.
“There first needs to be a consensus that we need to negotiate with the Russians,” a source familiar with the discussions told The Telegraph. “Secondly, there needs to be a consensus on what that position is.”
Trump’s efforts to broker a deal have made little progress, largely because Moscow has refused to abandon its maximalist territorial demands in Ukraine.
On Oct. 21, Trump’s envoy Steve Witkoff met Putin in St. Petersburg . The Kremlin subsequently said Russia was prepared in principle to resume trilateral talks with Ukraine and the US in November.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has also confirmed that trilateral talks with the US and Russia could take place by early November , although no date has been set.
The planned talks come as Washington faces criticism for pursuing economic cooperation with Moscow alongside peace negotiations. Witkoff has confirmed US Treasury discussions with Putin’s economic envoy , Kirill Dmitriev, on potential trade and economic ties.
Europe has yet to agree on a negotiator. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul faced criticism over his bid to lead the effort, while European Council President António Costa turned down the role at a recent EU leaders’ meeting.
One source told The Telegraph that a group of leaders may be more viable than appointing a single negotiator, as it could reduce competition between countries and the risk of individual candidates being vetoed.
The question of a European envoy is not new. In June, Meloni backed Stubb as a potential representative in negotiations between Ukraine and Russia.
Stubb has played a prominent role in European efforts to support Ukraine during the diplomatic process and maintains a close relationship with Trump. He joined Zelensky and Witkoff for talks in Oslo on Oct. 20.
The Finnish president has also argued that pressure on Moscow is necessary to bring it to the negotiating table. In August, he said Ukraine’s long-range strikes inside Russia could help push Moscow toward peace talks.
Pavel, a former head of NATO’s Military Committee, has also emerged as a potential candidate because of his military background and experience with NATO-Russia relations.
Europe needs to appoint someone or a group authorized to speak on its behalf, Pavel told the Axel Springer Global Reporters Network , of which The Telegraph is a member .
“President Putin disregards the European Union as an authority,” Pavel said, adding that Moscow has stopped engaging with several senior European officials and leaders.
Pavel has argued that negotiations could help prevent further escalation between Russia and the West. He has also suggested that the prospect of renewed trade and business ties could encourage Moscow to negotiate, while sanctions relief should depend on Russia agreeing to a ceasefire and a peace process.
Putin said in May that he would “personally” prefer Gerhard Schroeder, who served as German chancellor from 1998 to 2005, to help restart dialogue between Russia and Europe.
The proposal was met with skepticism in Berlin. German government sources told AFP that officials had “taken note” of Putin’s comments but viewed them as part of “a series of bogus offers” from Moscow.
Schroeder has remained close to Putin since leaving office and held senior positions linked to Russian energy interests, including roles involving the Nord Stream gas pipelines and Russian oil company Rosneft.
He gave up his Rosneft board position in 2022 but has never publicly condemned Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
His potential appointment has divided Germany’s Social Democratic Party, which Schroeder belongs to.
Michael Roth, a former SPD lawmaker who chaired the Bundestag’s foreign affairs committee, told Tagesspiegel that a mediator “cannot be Putin’s buddy.”
Any candidate must first be acceptable to Ukraine, Roth said. “Neither Moscow nor we can decide that on Kyiv’s behalf.”
Other SPD politicians have been more open to the proposal. The party’s foreign affairs spokesman in parliament, Adis Ahmetovic, told Der Spiegel that it should be “carefully considered” with European partners.
EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said on May 11 that Russia should not influence the EU’s choice of negotiator.
“If we give the right to Russia to appoint a negotiator on our behalf, that would not be very wise,” she said .
Kallas described Schroeder as a “high-level lobbyist for Russian state-owned companies,” arguing that Putin wanted someone who would effectively be “sitting on both sides of the table.”
She also warned that Russia was seeking to expand its influence in Europe, citing Russian participation in sports organizations and at the Venice Biennale.
“Our adversaries are not sleeping,” Kallas said.
For now, Europe has no agreed negotiator and no unified position on when direct talks should begin.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: ASELSAN building on African momentum at AFRIDEX 2026
body:
ASELSAN will use the inaugural Africa International Defence Exhibition (Afridex) 2026 in Lagos to consolidate a growing African presence built on local industrial partnerships and a battle-proven portfolio spanning air defence, electronic warfare, electro-optics and precision-guided munitions that can address evolving regional security challenges across Africa.
The 26-29 October exhibition is positioned as a pan-African platform for defence cooperation, capability development and procurement dialogue. For ASELSAN, Nigeria is not simply another exhibition venue. It is the location of its permanent Abuja office, opened last year as its operational base for West Africa, and a market where the company is actively pursuing local partnerships, including potential shipyard cooperation.
ASELSAN’s participation follows a high-profile presence at the Aerospace and Defence (AAD) 2026 exhibition in Pretoria, where the company hosted more than 30 delegations from dozens of countries and met South African Defence Minister Angie Motshekga. That South African engagement demonstrated ASELSAN’s ability to integrate its systems onto regional platforms. At AAD 2026, its ASELFLIR-500 electro-optical system was displayed on the Paramount Mwari intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR) and light-attack aircraft, for example.
Afridex extends that approach into West Africa, where the security environment is shaped by insurgency, porous borders, unmanned aerial system (UAS) threats, maritime insecurity and the need for affordable, sustainable capability. The exhibition’s programme is structured around land, maritime, air, space and cyber domains, aligning closely with ASELSAN’s multi-domain product base.
The timing is favourable. Nigerian President Bola Tinubu visited Türkiye in January 2026 for talks with President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, while ASELSAN President & CEO Ahmet Akyol has made regular visits to Nigeria. The Nigerian Air Force’s acquisition of six T-129 attack helicopters from Turkish Aerospace Industries has also created a broader entry point for Turkish defence suppliers. These helicopters are fitted with ASELSAN electro-optical gimbals and helmet-mounted displays, for example.
A flagship element of ASELSAN’s Afridex offering is Steel Dome, the company’s multi-layered integrated air-defence ecosystem. Steel Dome links radars, electro-optical sensors, command-and-control nodes and missile and gun effectors into a unified network. Its principal advantage is the creation of a real-time air picture across low-, medium- and high-altitude threat vectors. For African militaries, this offers decision-makers broader situational awareness and coordinated coverage against aircraft, helicopters, cruise missiles, drones and other aerial threats.
Counter-unmanned aerial system capability is one of ASELSAN’s most marketable offerings in Africa. Its İHTAR is a mobile or stationary counter-drone system intended for critical infrastructure and base protection. It combines radar detection, electro-optical tracking and active radio-frequency directional or omnidirectional jamming to neutralise micro- and mini-UAV threats.
The KORKUT 25 mm system is optimised for armoured units and mechanised formations, providing point defence against drones, low-flying air targets and lightly armoured ground targets. The KORKUT 35 mm twin-barrel system, meanwhile, uses ATOM 35 mm airburst ammunition to deliver cost-effective defence.
Together, these systems reflect ASELSAN’s view that drone defence cannot depend on one technology. Detection, electronic attack and kinetic effects must be combined according to the threat, terrain and protected asset.
ASELSAN is also highlighting its Laser Guidance Kits for conventional unguided bombs. The kits deliver high circular error probable accuracy, reducing collateral damage in complex operating environments. This capability complements the company’s broader airborne portfolio, including the TOLUN precision-guided munition family and the ASELFLIR-500 electro-optical targeting system.
On the ground, ASELSAN is promoting modernisation and life-extension packages for legacy land platforms, including self-propelled howitzers and main battle tanks. Its main battle tank upgrades include C4I systems, thermal imaging and sighting units, 360-degree situational-awareness sensors, active protection systems, laser-warning receivers and remote weapon stations.
ASELSAN’s tactical communications portfolio completes the offering. Its software-defined radio family covers HF, VHF and UHF bands and supports encrypted voice, high-speed data and video across airborne, naval, vehicular and dismounted platforms. The radios incorporate electronic counter-countermeasures, including frequency hopping and advanced TRANSEC/COMSEC encryption. ASELSAN also offers mission-critical and public-safety communications for military police, internal security forces and emergency responders.
ASELSAN’s African strategy is broader than equipment sales. Africa is a key growth market both for demand and for long-term strategic partnerships. That message resonates at Afridex, which is designed to connect governments, armed forces, policymakers, manufacturers and technology providers in a formal environment supporting procurement pathways and partnership formation. In West Africa, the Abuja office gives ASELSAN a permanent channel into Nigerian security institutions and regional customers amid growing Turkish-Nigerian defence ties and a portfolio matched to counter-insurgency, border security, counter-drone operations and ISR requirements.

title: Kambolov Appoints Members of De Facto Government in Occupied Tskhinvali
body: Marat Kambolov appointed Soslan Margiev as de facto “prime minister” of the occupied Tskhinvali/South Ossetia on October 22, culminating a series of appointments in the region’s executive branch after Kambolov was declared a winner in the region’s early “presidential vote” in September. Kambolov signed a relevant “decree” after the de facto parliament unanimously approved Margiev’s candidacy on the same day. According to the region’s so-called “constitution,” the “president” appoints the “head of government” with the consent of “parliament,” while the “president” can independently appoint and dismiss members of the “government” and heads of executive bodies. Margiev was born on June 20, 1982, in Tskhinvali. He worked in the Russian judicial system for more than 20 years, including serving as chairman of the Lobnya City Court in the Moscow Region from 2022 to 2026. He also previously served as deputy head of the Anti-Corruption Division of the Judicial Department under the Supreme Court of Russia. Also on October 22, the region’s “parliament” unanimously approved the nomination of Emilia Gagieva for the position of head of the region’s “Central Election Commission” for a second consecutive term. Earlier, on October 19, Kambolov appointed Ekaterina Tolstikova, a native of Russia, as first deputy “chairman of the government” of the region. Other Appointments Following his “election,” Kambolov has made a number of other appointments to the region’s de facto executive branch. Radion Gabaraev became the “minister of internal affairs,” Yuri Yarovitsky was appointed “minister of defense,” Vladimir Pukhaev was appointed “minister of civil defense, emergency situations, and disaster relief,” and Akhsar Dzhioev was appointed “minister of foreign affairs.” On September 23, Kambolov signed a decree appointing Erislav Zasseev as “minister of agriculture.” The agency was subsequently reorganized into the “Ministry of Agriculture and Food.” Kambolov also appointed Inna Dzudtsova as “minister of finance,” Oleg Glagolev as “minister of labor and social protection,” Alena Kochieva as “minister of land and property relations,” and Igor Tasoev as “minister of culture.” On October 22, Kambolov dismissed Yuri Kadiya from his post as head of the region’s “State Security Committee” (KGB) and appointed Evgeny Romanov in his place. In separate decrees, Kambolov appointed the heads of government agencies. Aslan Basiev was appointed head of the “Customs Service,” Mairbeg Guchmazov was appointed head of the “Veterinary and Phytosanitary Surveillance Service,” Rita Dzutsati was appointed head of the “Registration, Cadastre, and Cartography Service,” and Marina Kochieva was appointed head of the “Service for Supervision in the Sphere of Consumer Protection and Human Well-Being.” Tskhinvali ‘Elections’ and Russia ‘Treaty’ Appointments follow Tskhinvali’s early so-called “ presidential vote ” in September, widely condemned by Tbilisi and the West as “null and void,” which led to the “election” of Marat Kambolov, a North Ossetian-born long-time Russian official with no prior links to Tskhinvali, as the occupied region’s new de facto leader. The early vote was called following the June resignation of former de facto president Alan Gagloev, who moved to Russia to serve as Putin’s adviser. Kambolov, a North Ossetian-born former Russian official with no prior links to the region, who had been appointed the region’s “prime minister” a week before Gagloev’s resignation, assumed the role of an interim leader. The recent changes and the subsequent early “vote” follow the so-called “Treaty on Deepening Allied Cooperation” signed between Tskhinvali and Moscow on May 9, which, among others, allows “citizens” of one side to “hold state and municipal positions” in the other. title: NAIMOS to extend river protection operations to two more water bodies by year-end
body: The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) plans to extend its river protection operations to two more major water bodies before the end of 2026 as it intensifies efforts to combat illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey. NAIMOS Director of Operations, Colonel S.K. Appiah, announced this during the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources’ Progress Series media briefing, where he outlined the Secretariat’s operations and achievements between June 13 and September 30, 2026, and its next enforcement priorities. He said Operation Water Shield, which began on the River Birim before extending to the Ankobra, would be complemented by Operation Green Shield, a sustained intervention targeting illegal mining in the Atiwa Forest Reserve. Col. Appiah said the strategy was not only to clear illegal miners but also to prevent their return through sustained patrols, intelligence-led operations, and a planned dedicated riverine unit in collaboration with the Ghana Navy. Hundreds arrested, more than 100 excavators seized Responding to questions about arrests and seized equipment, Col. Appiah said hundreds of suspected illegal miners had been arrested during the period under review and handed over to the police and other relevant authorities. He said some suspects were facing court proceedings, others were remanded, and some were granted bail. NAIMOS also seized more than 100 excavators, which have been secured at designated holding areas across the regions. Col. Appiah said the Secretariat was documenting the machines’ chassis numbers and GPS locations to support legal processes aimed at securing their confiscation by the state. Strategy to sustain gains Addressing concerns about the risk of illegal miners returning after enforcement teams leave cleared areas, Col. Appiah said the military could not remain permanently in every affected community. He explained that NAIMOS was working to clear and stabilise illegal mining hotspots before gradually transferring routine monitoring and protection responsibilities to relevant security agencies, the Forestry Commission and local communities. The Secretariat is also strengthening collaboration with Blue Water Guards and other intelligence agencies to improve information-sharing and coordinate enforcement. Col. Appiah said the operations were being carefully planned to secure lasting results and prevent illegal miners from returning once enforcement teams withdrew.

title: Shot putters Salehi, Hadidi win gold, silver at 2026 Nagoya
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 23 (MNA) – Iranian athletes Elham Salehi and Shahla Hadidi won gold and silver medals in the women’s shot put F53/F54 event at the 2026 Asian Para Games in Nagoya on Friday.
Salehi secured the gold medal to lead an Iranian one-two finish, while compatriot Hadidi claimed silver, further boosting Iran’s medal tally at the continental competition.
Iraqi athlete Malak Ali completed the podium, earning the bronze medal with a throw of 4.98 meters.
The result marked a successful outing for the Iranian delegation in the women’s shot put, with Salehi and Hadidi demonstrating their competitive strength against athletes from across Asia. Their performances added to Iran’s achievements at the Games, which bring together leading para-athletes from across the continent to compete for medals in a wide range of sports.

title: Debunking "Faster than Rust": Malicious Benchmarks in Tov
body:
Tov is a programming language that claims to perform significantly better than Rust. This blog post debunks tricks used in their unfair benchmarks.
Tov is a new programming language marketed to be "[a] programming language for coding agents. It reads like TypeScript and builds native binaries that beat Rust's."
Benchmarks in their Git repository show that they perform better than Rust, in some cases over 10× better. However, they also briefly mentioned the internals of Tov:
A sane engineer would immediately doubt the correctness of their benchmarks. Rust has pretty much the same performance as C, and if Tov transpiles to C, saying Tov beats Rust is mostly equivalent to saying C beats C . That's contradiction right there. Let's ignore the stats for axum , maybe tokio has some overhead, like maybe ; but clearly there's no way you get 1.6× faster than Rust in strings . You have to be lying. That's what a sane engineer would normally think.
In this blog post, we check 3 of their "inflated" benchmarks: bigint_fib , dispatch , and map_insert . We show that these benchmarks are maliciously crafted to slow Rust down . We have also benchmarked the improved Rust programs with their Tov programs to show that Rust has equivalent or better performance than Tov .
cargo build --release was used to compile the Rust programs, and tov build (which defaults to -O3 ) was used to compile the Tov programs. Here are our setups:
This was the Rust code used in Tov's benchmark. Their benchmarking results showed that Rust used 501 ms · 4.5 MB, while Tov used 168 ms · 3.1 MB. However, we cannot reproduce their results on any of our setups :
Rust was given a very large disadvantage: dynamic dispatching at Vec<Box<dyn Shape>> . We've created an improved version that does not use dynamic dispatching:
We also used arrays instead of vectors because arrays were used in the C version. Here are the results:
We believe Tov's developers intentionally used dynamic dispatching in order to slow down the performance significantly and create misleading results. The program / code between the original Rust version and the Tov version was highly inequivalent. Their benchmark and its results should be deemed invalid.
We believe Tov developers deliberately chose std::collections::HashMap , which is a hash map known to be slow since it is made to be resilient to HashDoS attacks. Usually in real-world situations where HashDoS is not a concern, the ahash library is used. Tov developers chose to use external libraries like num_bigint to their advantage while ignoring popular libraries like ahash that are commonly used and make more sense in this case.
The point of Rust is not to write simple code and get the fastest binary; it shines in getting near-metal performance from the code you have written. You have a program in Tov that runs slow? Good luck speeding your code up. You have a program in Rust that runs slow? Rewrite the part of the code that causes the slowdown.
Code in JavaScript or TypeScript are not supposed to perform well. JavaScript is single-threaded. The name implies it's a scripting language. It doesn't make sense to write programs using tools meant for running scripts in a browser if performance matters.
Tov failed not because their transpiler isn't good enough, but rather due to its design. Tov's main website is reflecting its design flaw — it is impossible to get faster than Rust and C in any meaningful way, especially if Tov transpiles to C.
Tov's idea of shipping JavaScript programs as native binaries is not new. If you are interested, I recommend Porffor . Porffor compiles your JavaScript code to a native binary, and it passes over 95% of all tests in the official ECMAScript conformance suite. It's also available in Terra, by the way. Note that Porffor and Tov are not affiliated with Fyra Labs.

title: 'We had a plan B, C and D': UAE retailers pledge to keep food prices stable amid Iran war disruption
body: Food industry leaders in the UAE have pledged to keep prices in check and shelves well stocked, as they look to curb the effects of the Iran war . The conflict, which began on February 28, has caused widespread disruption across the region. The effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz , where commercial ships have been attacked by Iran, has hit supply chains and fuelled an increase in the cost of food, transport, insurance and energy around the world. Shamim Sainulabdeen, director of private labels at Lulu Group International, which operates more than 100 outlets in the UAE, said the retailer would follow government guidelines and refrain from increasing the price of staples, commodities and essential goods. "We are a responsible retailer, so we are absorbing some costs. The government insists on keeping the price stable for our fast-moving staples," he said. The supermarket company has chartered vessels to speed up deliveries, instead of having orders shipped with those of other companies. The Dubai Statistic Centre's latest consumer price index showed food inflation rose to 8.05 per cent in September, up from 7.39 per cent a month earlier. In a study by consultancy Redseer this year, 78 per cent of respondents in the UAE noted higher grocery prices and 51 per cent identified food inflation as their main concern. Planning ahead For producers, keeping ingredients and farm supplies on the move has been central to easing the pressure on prices during challenging times. Tareq Al Hosani, chairman of Al Ain Farms Group, said the company had contingency plans in place before the war broke out. They included using Fujairah port, working with suppliers and contacts in Saudi Arabia and other neighbouring countries and using air freight. Strategic reserves of feed and other supplies provided a further buffer for production. "We always had a plan B, plan C and a plan D to continue to be able to serve our market," he said. Mr Al Hosani said the company had taken on additional costs to minimise the impact on the public. Customer loyalty and growth in sales helped the company maintain profitability while limiting price changes, he added. "We are trying to swallow as much as we can from that cost variation and we are trying to put the minimum on the clients because you know this is only a transition," he said. "It's only a short period and we owe it to our clients who put their trust in us." Conflict drives inflation Nagham Hassan, a Middle East market analyst for investment platform etoro, said the conflict had accelerated the rate of global inflation. She said people were favouring more affordable options, as they look to reduce discretionary spending. "Both Lulu and Spinney's stated that private label sales increased, and usually private label is a more economic option than the other brands that are out there," she said. More people are making trips to supermarkets, but are spending less each time, Ms Hassan added. The UN Trade and Development agency has previously warned that higher energy, freight and insurance costs linked to the disruption in the strait could increase food costs and put pressure on household budgets. UAE protects consumers In April, the UAE government launched the Essential Goods Prices Platform, overseen by the Ministry of Economy and Tourism, to monitor price changes on 8,343 products at 525 shops operated by 13 major retailers. The tool was expanded in August after recording 143,000 visits in the first four months. The government took action to protect customers from unjustified price increases after a surge in demand for essentials in the early weeks of the war. The ministry carried out more than 7,000 inspections of retailers in the two weeks after the conflict broke out. It said at the time that it was “intensifying monitoring efforts” to ensure price stability, particularly for nine essential goods – cooking oil, eggs, dairy products, rice, sugar, poultry, legumes, bread and wheat. The price of those items cannot be raised without approval from the ministry and a national committee set up to assess food costs.

title: Ukrainian, Norwegian defense ministers discuss urgent increase in interceptor missile stocks
body:
According to Ukrinform, the Ukrainian Defense Ministry reported this on Facebook .
"The parties discussed options for an urgent increase in stocks, with Ukraine counting on Norway's support," the ministry said.
During the call, the ministers also focused on a project to integrate additional missiles into NASAMS air defense systems operated by Ukraine.
Countering jet-powered drones was another topic of discussion.
"Aircraft are one of the most effective means of countering jet-powered Shaheds. Therefore, it is necessary to maintain a steady supply of ammunition for F-16 aircraft and increase its volume. Man-portable air defense systems are also an important component of protecting specific facilities. To strengthen its air defense, Ukraine needs additional systems and missiles for them and is counting on Norway's support," Khmara said.
He also thanked Norway for its leadership and significant contribution to strengthening Ukraine's defense capabilities.

title: Zamfara community fights back
body: Residents of Birnin Tudu community in Gummi Local Government Area of Zamfara State said they killed more than 30 bandits during a three-day confrontation after armed men invaded the community. The residents said the attackers, who reportedly arrived in their hundreds on motorcycles, surrounded the village and opened fire. Speaking to Daily Trust on condition of anonymity, a resident said the attackers took the community by surprise after locals had relaxed their usual security vigilance. “What happened in Birnin Tudu over the last three days was alarming. The bandits unexpectedly surrounded our village. We have always remained vigilant and defended ourselves, but this time, we thought everything was under control,” he said. Security operatives guard Tinubu’s billboards ahead campaign launch Ogun govt mulls relocation of communities over gas leak The resident said the attackers arrived at about 10am on Tuesday when some villagers had gone to their farms to harvest crops. “Before we realised what was happening, the bandits had surrounded the village from all directions. They were conveying three people on each motorcycle. There were more than 100 motorcycles, and I personally counted 71 from where I was hiding,” he said. According to him, the attackers entered the community, shooting sporadically, breaking into shops and looting goods. He said the residents decided to confront them rather than flee their homes. “We thank God that some of our people were ready to defend the community. We confronted them because we realised that fleeing our homes and becoming IDPs would be a disgrace to us,” he said. The resident said the confrontation resulted in the deaths of three villagers, while three others sustained fractures and another person suffered a gunshot wound. He added that the bandits returned for a second confrontation while residents were distributing batteries for torch lights. “We confronted them again and eventually chased them out of the village towards the eastern part. They were in their hundreds and were all armed,” he said. He added that the attackers succeeded in taking cattle rustled from neighbouring communities but did not steal any livestock from Birnin Tudu. Another resident, who also spoke on condition of anonymity, said the attackers operated in three groups. He said the first group comprised more than 71 motorcycles, with three people riding on each, while the second group moved with the rustled cattle. A third group followed behind. The resident said the attackers used communication devices to contact their colleagues scattered in the surrounding bushes, asking them to regroup. He claimed that the villagers initially counted 11 bandits killed during the confrontation but were prevented by the assailants from recovering more weapons when another group of armed men launched a fresh attack. “We killed 11 bandits, and while we were trying to seize their rifles, another group attacked us again. That prevented us from recovering more weapons that we could have used to defend ourselves,” he said. The resident further disclosed that the community received intelligence on Thursday morning that the bandits were approaching from the western side, prompting villagers and local vigilantes to prepare for another confrontation. He said the residents also received reports that the attackers had rustled cattle from Sabon Garin Kaddagi village and were moving towards a forest known as Kwartaga. According to him, local vigilantes in the area confirmed sighting the bandits and reportedly lay in ambush to prevent them from entering the community. The resident said subsequent information indicated that the number of bandits killed in the clashes had risen to more than 30. He added that, apart from the three villagers killed inside Birnin Tudu, another person was reportedly killed outside the community, while one other death was reported in Dantsullutu. The resident also recounted the account of a villager who allegedly escaped from the bandits’ captivity and returned home. According to him, the escapee said he overheard a bandit leader reprimanding his men over the attack on Birnin Tudu, claiming that more than 30 of their colleagues had been killed. The resident said the captive escaped after being ordered to help push a motorcycle belonging to one of the bandits. After the motorcycle started, he reportedly moved away, ran into tall crops and eventually made his way home. The residents also dismissed reports that the community had been attacked by a bandit leader identified as Gwaska because it refused to allow him to mine gold in the area. “That report is completely false. We are still in our community, and no bandit leader can force us to abandon our homes. We are determined to confront them and defend ourselves,” one resident said. He added that people remained in the village and had resolved not to flee despite the attacks. When contacted, the spokesperson for the Zamfara State Police Command, DSP Yazid Abubakar, confirmed the incident and said the command had intensified security measures to protect the community. “The incident occurred, and we have intensified efforts to ensure that the community receives adequate police support,” Abubakar said. Daily Trust gathered that Zamfara State has two villages bearing Birnin Tudu, one in Anka LGA and the other one in Gummi LGA. One of the village heads of Birnin Tudu of Anka LGA told Daily Trust that nothing has happened in the village. The Zamfara Police Command also debunked the media reports on an attack on Birnin Tudu in Anka LGA for not mining gold for a bandit Kingpin. “Nothing of such has happened in Birnin Tudu village in Anka LGA and the village was not attacked,” Yazid confirmed. Vigilantes seek security support The vigilante commander in Birnin Tudu village in Gummi LGA, Bello Abubakar, popularly known as Bello Karo Birnin Tudu, has called on security agencies and the local government council to provide additional security support and equipment following the three-day confrontation with bandits. Abubakar said the villagers had received intelligence about the movement of a large group of bandits towards their community since Monday, but the attackers did not strike until Tuesday morning, when most residents had gone to their farms. “We had privileged information about the movement of the bandits since Monday. We learnt that a large group of them was moving towards our village across the river, but they did not attack until Tuesday morning, when most of our people had gone to their farms,” he said. The vigilante commander recalled that fewer than 10 villagers were available to guard the community when they received information that the bandits were approaching. He further explained that the villagers suspected that an informant had leaked their plans and the location of their ambush to the bandits, forcing the attackers to change their direction of movement. According to him, the bandits entered the village through the eastern side, avoiding the villagers’ blockade, before splitting into two groups. One group moved towards Koga village, while the other headed for Hishi village, he added. Abubakar said the movement of the attackers allowed the villagers to regroup and block all the entrances to their community. “Whenever we hear gunshots, we rush to that location to reinforce our people,” he said. He recalled that the bandits had last attacked the community about two years ago, when the villagers claimed to have killed more than 15 of them. “They attacked us about two years ago, and we killed more than 15 of them. Their corpses were later found in the bushes of neighbouring villages, and we did not lose anybody on our side,” he said. The vigilante commander appealed to security agencies to come to the community’s aid by deploying security personnel and providing an armoured vehicle to support the villagers. “We know there will be a reprisal and we are ready to confront them. However, we need the government to support us with an armoured vehicle and security personnel to strengthen our capacity,” he said. He also appealed to the chairman of Gummi Local Government Area, Aminu Falale, to provide additional equipment to support the villagers, saying they had exhausted much of their resources during the three-day confrontation. “We need more ammunition, gunpowder, torchlights and guns. Our equipment has run low because we spent three days confronting the bandits,” he pleaded. When contacted, the local government chairman, Falale declined to comment on the issue over the telephone, insisting that the reporter meet him in person. “I cannot speak to you over the telephone. Just find time to come and meet me physically for a proper introduction,” Falale said. He, however, ended the call after our correspondent requested an appointment. Efforts to reach the member of the Zamfara State House of Assembly representing the constituency, Adamu Aliyu Gazura, were unsuccessful as his telephone numbers were not reachable. Retired military officer calls for reinforcement Meanwhile, a retired military officer and security expert, Bello Muhammad Bakyasuwa Maradun, has urged the state government to urgently strengthen security in Birnin Tudu. Maradun, a former commandant of Anti-Thuggery in Zamfara, warned that the community could face reprisals and called on the government to deploy additional security personnel to protect residents and prevent further violence. He commended the villagers for their courage and determination to defend their community, describing their resistance as a demonstration of their resolve to protect their lives, dignity and rights amid persistent insecurity. The retired officer said the residents’ ability to confront the armed men for three consecutive days highlighted the importance of community participation in addressing insecurity. He, however, stressed that the government must not leave the villagers to defend themselves without adequate protection and support from security agencies. Maradun also called for stronger community-based security arrangements, including intelligence-sharing, surveillance equipment and other lawful measures to enable residents to protect themselves. He said any provision of weapons to community members must comply with the law and be subject to appropriate supervision to prevent the proliferation of arms and further insecurity. According to him, the development could weaken the ability of bandits to intimidate rural communities if residents’ determination was sustained and supported by effective security operations. He added that the experience could encourage other communities to cooperate more closely with security agencies in confronting criminal activities. However, the security expert cautioned that the reported killings of bandits should not be taken as evidence that the armed groups had been defeated. He stressed that the possibility of retaliation made immediate security intervention necessary. He urged the government and security agencies to translate the villagers’ courage and sacrifice into concrete measures to protect lives, restore public confidence and ensure lasting peace in Zamfara State.

title: N3.5bn Revenue Hangs as Abuja Estate Residents Fight for Cof O
body: Residents of Prince and Princess of Estate are crying out to the Department of Lands, FCT Administration to compel the developers of the estate, Prince & Princess Properties Limited, to provide the necessary documents required for issuance of Certificates of Occupancy(CofO). The residents said they had applied for Cof O since 2015, attended several meetings and exchanged correspondences with FCT Administration, but the developers of the estate had refused to provide the Lands Department of Administration with the required documents needed to process the title document. The action of the developers has cost the FCT Administration about N3.5 billion revenue that would have accrued to it the form of charges and fees for processing the title document. According to one of the Executive Members of the Prince & Princess Estate Residents Association, “We have done everything necessary to process our Cof Os with AGIS (Abuja geographic information system), which is a unit in the Lands Department. We have met all conditions and are ready to pay the N3.5 million processing fee per building, but the developers of the estate – Prince & Princess Properties Limited – are deliberately withholding critical information from the FCT Administration, thus denying the government of the needed revenue.” He added: “The over 1,100 home owners in this estate are therefore asking the FCT Minister, Nyesom Wike, to compel the developers to provide the document to AGIS so that the process can move forward and/or give an executive waiver for the issuance of the certificate of occupancy. According to a letter dated October 25, 2025, written by the Lands Dept to the developer, the developer is to provide the following documents: Land use and site development plan; Building plan;Engineering infrastructure design; A-built survey plan;3D Aerial photo of the estate and List of beneficiaries (house owners). House owners in the estate are particularly exasperated that the developers have deliberately caused the delay in issuance of the title document by refusing to provide these documents to AGIS because of their persona interest, thus denying government of the needed revenue. Another homeowner in the estate lamented, saying: “It is quite inconceivable that the developers would block the FCT from earning its legitimate revenue from our estate. This is against the agreement the developers had with the FCT Administration before the land for this estate was allocated to them.” The FCT Administration had put up an advertisement in The Sun newspaper, inviting all estate developers in the city to ‘’submit necessary documents…for commencement of preparation of certificate of occupancy to beneficiaries/off takers’’. Two weeks after the publication of the advert, Owelle Prince C.N. Ukachuwku, Chairman/CEO of Prince & Princess Properties Limited, was said to have issued a letter to the residents, requesting for proof of payments; receipts of payments and allocation letter in order to commence “preparation to perfect documentation and ownership of plots and houses by individuals in the estate.” It was gathered despite the residents’ compliance with this directive, the process has not moved forward. Since then, the estate’s residents association has written several letters to FCT Minister, Nyesom Wike; the developers and Hon. Michael Chinda, Senior Special Assistant to the Minister of FCT, pleading for the process to move forward. In one of such letters dated July 19, 2024, the residents association wrote to the FCT Minister about the ‘’various illegal activities of the agents of Prince and Princess Estate Limited (the developer)’’. The letter noted, among other things, that the developer has ‘’refused/failed to provide the requirements for the issuance of CofO as recently communicated to them by the FCDA, thereby leaving the interests of house owners in jeopardy with regards to the recent efforts of the Minister on the issuance of the Cof O.” Prince and Princess Estate is one of the foremost gated communities in Abuja, with several homes and over 7,000 residents.

title: New B-series uncrewed surface vessels emerge in US market
body:
Red Cat, a US-based provider of advanced all-domain drone and robotic solutions for defense and national security, has introduced its B-Series portfolio of uncrewed surface vessels (USVs) through its Blue Ops maritime division.
The B-Series establishes a unified naming convention for Blue Ops’ growing family of U.S.-designed and built autonomous maritime systems, with designations reflecting vessel length in feet, which is the traditional American methodology for naval and commercial shipbuilding. Building on its flagship B-26, Blue Ops is expanding its portfolio to support tactical reconnaissance, one-way attack, persistent maritime defense and logistics missions.
The portfolio includes the B-26 (formerly Variant 7); the B-18, an 18-foot USV designed for tactical and one-way attack missions; and the B-39, a 39-foot vessel already in low-rate production.
Developed with US Navy requirements in mind, including deployment from littoral combat ships, the B-18 is designed for tactical reconnaissance, shipboard launch and recovery, and one-way attack missions, according to the company.
With its modular architecture, flexible payload integration and advanced autonomous capabilities, the B-39 is designed to support persistent maritime surveillance, integrated defense systems and extended operations in demanding naval environments.
“The Navy doesn't need examples of what autonomous vessels might deliver years from now. It needs affordable, reliable systems that perform in real-world conditions and are available today,” said Barry Hinckley , President of Blue Ops.
“That's exactly what we're building at Blue Ops. From one-way attack and tactical reconnaissance to maritime defense and logistics, our B-Series vessels are designed to meet immediate operational needs. Combined with Red Cat's aerial assets, we're delivering a complete family of systems that gives U.S. and allied forces the capabilities and flexibility to operate across air and sea.”
Since Red Cat launched Blue Ops in 2025, the division has expanded its U.S. manufacturing capabilities in Valdosta, Georgia, advanced the B-26 into full-rate production and accelerated the availability of additional maritime platforms.
Together with Red Cat's aerial portfolio, the B-Series is expected to strengthen the company's ability to deliver domestically manufactured autonomous systems for modern multi-domain operations.

title: Should state have right to ban political parties? Tbilisi street poll – Video
body: Ban on Georgian opposition Should the state have the right to ban political parties? Tbilisi residents answered reporters’ questions. Context The Constitutional Court of Georgia began examining a lawsuit filed by the ruling Georgian Dream party on 21 October, seeking to ban five opposition parties. The lawsuit was signed by 88 Georgian Dream MPs, who claim that the parties violated Article 23 of the Constitution, which prohibits the establishment and activities of political parties aiming to overthrow or forcibly change the country’s constitutional order. The proposed ban on opposition parties is no ordinary constitutional case. The court’s ruling could determine what kind of country Georgia ultimately becomes. The case has therefore attracted widespread attention. Georgia’s party ban: Court to begin hearing government case against opposition on 21 October Court begins hearing case to ban opposition parties in Georgia: first-day developments Scenes from the protests in Georgia: video and photos How respondents reacted to the question Most Tbilisi residents interviewed by reporters said that banning political parties was unacceptable in a country that claims to be a democracy. They stressed the importance of a multiparty system and people’s right to choose. Many said the current developments reminded them of a slide towards dictatorship, drawing comparisons with Russia, North Korea and even the Soviet Union. One respondent echoed claims made on Georgian pro-government propaganda channels that the opposition had attempted to set fire to parliament and stage a coup, and should therefore be banned. Another respondent said that banning political parties could be open to discussion, but only if the process was fair and transparent. Many passers-by declined to comment and tried to avoid appearing on camera. This was hardly surprising, given that people approached on the street generally tend to avoid politically sensitive questions.

title: Oleksandr Levchenko: Financing Ukraine’s Recovery Must Combine Capital, Risk Management, and Responsible AI
body:
Oleksandr Levchenko is a Candidate of Economic Sciences and a certified bank auditor who previously worked in banking inspection at the National Bank of Ukraine (NBU). Since January 2026, he has served as a Lead Research Fellow (on a voluntary basis) at S.A. Podolynsky Institute of Physical Economics, Private Enterprise located in Kyiv, Ukraine.
He has authored two copyright-registered methodologies and co-authored published research on explainable artificial intelligence (AI), regulatory compliance, and virtual assets. His work connects recovery financing with risk management and digital resilience.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Iryna Skoryk: What did banking inspection teach you about financing Ukraine’s recovery?
Oleksandr Levchenko: Banking inspection and audit taught me that a compliant report is not proof of a resilient institution. Economic cybernetics shaped my analytical approach. Studying financial services at Napier University in Edinburgh added practical context. On-site inspections, including information-security reviews, reinforced the need for verifiable data and an audit trail. Recovery financing needs that discipline: investors must know how risks are assessed and controlled, using comparable data and predictable rules.
Which of your dissertation findings have been used in practice?
I developed a method for assessing the efficiency of leasing transactions from the lessor’s perspective using an integrated risk indicator. It incorporates risk, uncertainty, and market instability into the assessment rather than adding them as a note after calculating returns.
ULF-FINANS LLC applied that approach. The Ukrainian Union of Lessors used elements of my proposed financial and credit framework, while Banking University used results in teaching and research methodology. These documents establish practical use, not a measured increase in profit or reduction in losses. Nor does the use of those earlier results establish implementation of my newer methodologies.
What do PRISM-Lease and DFR-PRISM add, and what remains to be tested?
I developed both methodologies to address fragmented assessment and registered copyright in the works this year. PRISM-Lease integrates prudential compliance, risk management, and internal control in leasing companies.
DFR-PRISM addresses digital financial resilience and cyber risks in non-bank financial institutions, linking service disruptions, data risks, and provider dependencies to financial and governance consequences.
The aim is to make interconnected risks visible and support a timely management response, rather than examine each indicator in isolation. Copyright registration establishes authorship, not effectiveness – neither is an implemented product, and both still require independent validation and pilot testing.
Testing must also establish whether specialists understand the signals and can act on them.
What did your Aug. 31 compliance study show?
In our article published Aug. 31, my co-authors and I compared public NBU data with regulatory requirements. Our approach connects financial capacity, digital controls, legal obligations, governance, and professional competence.
Digital tools support reliable data and monitoring – legal mechanisms translate requirements into internal responsibilities.
Common control principles are useful, but the indicators, depth of review, and response procedures must fit the business model. An insurer, finance company, and credit union cannot be assessed adequately through identical checklists.
What did you contribute to the US auto lease study, and what did the tests show?
Our collaborative study of explainable AI, published in August, used public US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) data on six families of auto lease securitizations.
My contribution covered methodology, data preparation and curation, software implementation, formal analysis, visualization, and project administration.
We examined transitions to at least 30 days past due in the following month, not lifetime default. We separated time periods, tested contracts excluded from training, and assessed transfer to previously unseen issuers.
At equal review capacity, X-LEASE did not outperform the unconstrained model in detecting delinquency in our test. We analyzed explanations for both models: a more concentrated explanation did not establish greater fairness or auditability.
The findings support early-warning monitoring with human review under the conditions studied, not automatic adverse decisions or claims of universal transferability.
How would regulatory whitelists reduce wrongful payment blocks without weakening safeguards?
In our joint publication, we proposed validating the legal basis, recipient, and payment details of mandatory payments before blocking them.
This is an additional verification layer, not a privilege for recipients or an exemption from sanctions and anti-money-laundering controls. Conflicting signals require authorized human review.
The framework remains conceptual: it aims to reduce false-positive blocks without missing more dangerous transactions, but we have not tested its effectiveness on proprietary bank transaction data.
What does your Conceptual Prudential Compatibility Index (CPCI) establish – and what does it not?
In our joint work, CPCI distinguishes an asset’s tradability from its suitability to back an insurer’s or pension fund’s obligations. It assigns categories using documentary evidence on liquidity, value stability, and valuation reliability, then separately examines regulatory admissibility for the instrument, jurisdiction, institution, and intended use.
Legal prohibitions cannot be offset by attractive returns. CPCI helps identify gaps in the evidence – it is an ordinal framework, not an externally validated quantitative risk model, a price forecast, or a substitute for applicable law.
What did you propose to the NBU, and what would you pilot next?
I submitted my proposals on responsible AI to the NBU on July 13. They called for limited agent permissions, auditable actions, independent review proportionate to risk, and a tested safe-shutdown procedure. Customers must also have a genuine path to review and correction.
The NBU acknowledged receipt that day – this was not approval of the recommendations.
I would next seek independent pilot testing of an integrated early-warning system combining prudential, digital, and model risks, operating alongside existing procedures without automatically affecting customer decisions.
The views expressed in this opinion article are the author’s and not necessarily those of Kyiv Post.
Iryna Skoryk is a journalist, culture and art researcher, and management specialist based in the United States. She writes for Kyiv Post on finance, corporate governance, insurance, culture, art and the creative industries.

title: Netanyahu orders Hebron sealed off, full West Bank closure after Hamas terror attack
body: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the city of Hebron to be cordoned off and for the entire West Bank to be blocked from entry and exit starting on Friday morning, after five people were wounded in a terror attack in the area carried out by Hamas terrorists."I have instructed the IDF and security forces to immediately impose a closure on the city of Hebron and prepare for a full lockdown of all of Judea and Samaria, beginning today," Netanyahu said, adding that the IDF would be carrying out extensive waves of arrests."We will pursue Hamas terrorists and those who send them, wherever they are and at any time," Netanyahu said. "You have nowhere to hide."Two soldiers were killed, and three were lightly injured in the attack, according to the IDF. The military had announced earlier that morning that two terrorists involved in the attack had been killed. The IDF and the Shin Bet are investigating whether the two terrorists were part of a small self-contained cell or whether their vast ammunition shows that they were connected to a larger terror cell.There were no other terrorists involved.  Netanyahu also said that the military would be applying the methods used in refugee camps, with the IDF going house-to-house and dismantling the terror infrastructure.The prime minister explained that the model would be used in Hebron, while it could be expanded to other cities in the future if it shows that it's an effective way to fight terrorism in the area."We also wish to make another promise: the Defense Minister and I have overseen the planning of a very extensive IDF operation in Judea and Samaria -- on a scale not seen since the Six-Day War. The IDF is prepared to carry it out; we will determine the timing, but it is coming," he added.What happened in the Hamas-backed attack near Hebron?The two Palestinian terrorists were traveling in a car with an M4 machine gun and a pistol toward the Yehuda junction.IDF sources estimated that they intended to go past the junction to carry out a larger attack on Route 35, which has many civilians.However, when they saw how many soldiers were present at the Yehuda junction checkpoint, they realized they would not get through and decided to attack the soldiers there. There were initially around four soldiers on site.Magen David Adom said that five people had been wounded in the attack, with two in critical condition, one moderate, and two mild. The mildly and moderately wounded people were evacuated to the hospital.The two critically wounded people are receiving medical care, MDA said in a statement."We brought a man in his 20s into the ambulance. He was unconscious, suffering from gunshot wounds, and in extremely serious condition. We provided him with medical treatment," said MDA emergency medical technician Zuriel Edri."We evacuated additional wounded people to MDA ambulances that had arrived at the scene and immediately began transporting them to hospitals. Another person in extremely serious condition was treated by IDF medical personnel in a mobile intensive care unit."The company commander, deputy battalion commander, a nearby deputy battalion 101 commander, and their various soldiers came to reinforce the soldiers who were initially taken by surprise.The reinforcement forces eventually overwhelmed and killed the two terrorists, Hamouda and Firas Jua'ba. According to Army Radio, the pair were from the same family in Hebron, both aged 27, and both married with two children each.Next, the IDF said that it had surrounded and cut off the Hebron and Chalchul areas to avoid copycat attacks and to arrest all potentially connected nearby Palestinians.In addition, the IDF announced it would map out the houses of the two terrorists for sealing off and for eventual demolition, following the relevant legal proceedings.The IDF also said that it would be checking all cars in the Jebin, Nablus, and Jericho areas to reduce the likelihood of copycat attackers."This was a serious attack," said IDF Chief of Staff Lt.-Gen. Eyal Zamir in a statement. "The soldiers' swift actions prevented an even more serious attack and further harm to civilians and security forces. A large quantity of ammunition was found in the vehicle used by the terrorists to reach the scene of the attack, which was intended to be used to carry out an attack on a larger scale."The soldiers who killed the two terrorists were part of the Ari Battalion from the IDF Search and Rescue Brigade. Lt.-Col. L., the battalion's commander, commended the soldiers for their actions."The two terrorists were neutralized by the battalion's combat soldiers, who acted with professionalism and were optimally deployed across the area as part of the effort to protect the residents of the State of Israel," L. said."Even during their very first operational deployment, the battalion's soldiers demonstrated the importance of their mission and their operational readiness. Maintaining a high state of alert and operational vigilance, the soldiers engaged the enemy, acting with determination and speed to thwart the threat - all while ensuring no civilians were harmed - and successfully accomplished their mission."Terror in the West Bank: 'The terrorist has been shooting for more than 20 minutes now!'In a video recorded at the scene, a soldier can be heard saying that the terrorists had been actively shooting for over 20 minutes."The terrorist keeps shooting. There are still exchanges of fire with that son of a b***h terrorist. Our forces still haven't managed to get the wounded out," the person said in the video. "The terrorist has been shooting for more than 20 minutes now."תיעוד: חילופי אש בין כוחות צה"ל למחבלים שביצעו את הפיגוע סמוך לצומת יהודה @HGoldich https://t.co/pJlwXd1pa5— כאן חדשות (@kann_news) October 23, 2026During the attack, several people used an armored ambulance that was nearby the scene for cover from the fire."Open the door, quickly!" one person at the scene shouted as the wounded were being evacuated."It's open," the paramedic replied."Get them in quickly (the wounded); we're getting out of here, come on! 442, get a paramedic out here now! Get him in quickly, get him in quickly!"

title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1702: Ukraine says Poland paused military aid package over Lviv vote honoring WWII nationalists

Now Starlink could help Russia take the ground back . The operation retook 277 square kilometers north of Lyman. The drones that now hold that line lose their Starshield link above about 160 km/h. Ukraine’s answer to Russia’s jet Shaheds: a jet drone named Bars, built to strike Russia and now turned around to hunt them . Zelenskyy says it has the best hit rate of any Ukrainian interceptor against the jet drones, about 30%, but the small jet engines it needs may be in short supply. Progress on a sore point for Ukraine and Poland: remains of over 40 Ukrainians killed by Polish WWII units found in Łasków . The find is the first in years from Ukraine’s searches in Poland, coming as Warsaw keeps pressing Kyiv over how it remembers the UPA. Military Russia kept sneaking troops through gas pipes behind Ukrainian lines. Now Ukraine has gone more than 15 km underground to do the same to Russia . Ukrainian OSINT analyst: Russia’s Yandex data center in Sasovo burned out inside, though its roof shows almost no significant holes .
