title: Mohamed Salah on song for Trabzonspor in Europa Conference League
body: Egyptian star Mohamed Salah had a day to remember as he celebrated his 150th appearance in Uefa competitions with a goal and an assist as Trabzonspor defeated Scottish side Hearts 2-0 in the Europa Conference League. The Scottish visitors came close when Malachi Fagan-Walcott hit the post, but the hosts went ahead with Salah converting from the penalty spot after a Tomas Bent Magnusson foul. The Egypt international then set up Dju Franculino for a classy finish shortly before the hour. It was the club's 200th continental goal and even though Trabzonspor were reduced to 10 men in added time following Sidny Lopes Cabral's red card, they held on to victory. Salah has been in sensational form for the Turkish side. Earlier this month, Salah set a new Turkish Super Lig record as he became the fastest player to register 10 goal contributions. The Egyptian provided an assist in Trabzonspor's win over Samsunspor – his third assist of the campaign. With seven goals since his summer move from Liverpool , Salah reached double figures in goal contributions in only seven games for his new club. Salah has since increased his tally to eight goals in the Super Lig. An incredible night under the lights 💡 Marco Rose's full post-match interview is now available on AFCBTV 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/lPdIvrJur7 — AFC Bournemouth 🍒 (@afcbournemouth) October 22, 2026 Meanwhile, Bournemouth pulled off a sensational 3-0 home victory over 10-man AC Milan, making it three wins from opening three games in the Europa League. Justin Kluivert and Marcus Tavernier converted first-half penalties to put Bournemouth in control. Milan goalkeeper and captain Mike Maignan received a red card early on for a foul on Tyler Adams and his side never recovered from that point. Amine Adli scored in the 84th minute to make it 3-0. “It means a lot. We came off two victories, so that gave us a good feeling for this game,” Kluivert told TNT Sports. “We trust ourselves. It doesn't matter who we play against. We know what we're capable of, and I think we showed that today.”

title: Iran to sue US over illegal naval blockade: senior MP
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 23 (MNA) – A senior Iranian lawmaker has said that Tehran will sue the United States over its illegal naval blocakade in internatinal legal bodies.
Esmaeil Kowsari, a member of Iranian parliament's National Security and Foreign Policy Commission, said in an interview with Mehr that Iran will lodge a complaint against the US over its illegall blockade.
He said that the Foreign Ministry and Judiciary in Iran have the prime duty in that regard.
Kowasari also noted that the international bodies have the legal juricdication to sue the US over Iran's blockade but they have not lived up to their commitments.
The seniro lawmaker called on the Iranian Judiciary to document the negative impact of the US criminal blocalde on the livlihood and health of Iranians in order to sue the aggressor over that.

title: GIZ gives grinding machines to smallholder farmers, Yei River, Magwi
body: The Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH, through its project Improved Living Conditions and Psychosocial Support (ILiPS), on Tuesday handed over 12 cereal grinding machines to 12 beneficiary farmer groups in Yei River and Magwi counties. A press statement extended to Radio Tamazuj said each farmer group consists of 25 members, with 60 percent of the selected members being female. GIZ South Sudan implements the project on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ). “The initiative aims to support beneficiaries in establishing and strengthening small-scale income-generating activities by improving access to cereal-processing equipment,” the statement reads in part. “The machines are expected to reduce the time and effort required to process cereals, increase productivity and the value of the resulting products, and create opportunities for beneficiaries to earn a sustainable income.” The handover ceremony brought together representatives of GIZ South Sudan, implementing partners, local authorities, communities, and beneficiary groups. The equipment was formally handed over to the beneficiaries, who were encouraged to take responsibility, maintain the machines, and use them for their intended purpose. Speaking at the handover, Ramson Duku, Agricultural Advisor, emphasized the importance of the equipment in promoting self-reliance and strengthening household livelihoods. “This support is intended to provide beneficiaries with practical tools that can contribute to increased household income and improved resilience,” he said. “We encourage beneficiaries to take ownership of the equipment, maintain it properly, and use it sustainably for the benefit of their families and communities.” The beneficiaries expressed their appreciation for the support, noting that the cereal-grinding machines would help increase productivity, reduce processing costs, and create opportunities to generate income. The project will provide follow-up support to promote effective and sustainable use of the equipment, GIZ said. The handover of the grinding mills is part of GIZ South Sudan’s broader efforts to strengthen agricultural extension services and promote climate-smart farming practices among smallholder farmers in Yei and Magwi counties. GIZ takes an integrated approach: the handover of machinery is accompanied by training and technical support for beneficiaries. The ILiPS project is implemented by GIZ South Sudan on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ). It supports returnees, internally displaced persons, and host communities to increase agricultural production and improve food security. The project also provides cereal value-addition machines to improve access to processing and income-generating opportunities. In addition, it aims to strengthen community members’ access to psychosocial support services and raise awareness of the importance of psychosocial well-being. The Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH is a German federal enterprise that supports international cooperation for sustainable development. In South Sudan, GIZ works with local institutions, communities, and development partners to support initiatives that strengthen agricultural development, food and nutrition security, livelihoods, natural resource management, access to water, and community resilience. The post GIZ gives grinding machines to smallholder farmers, Yei River, Magwi appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: A Prisoner Release From Hell: the Potentially Catastrophic Human Cost of Trump’s Deal
body:
On October 21, 75-year-old American Stephen Hubbard gained his freedom after more than four years in Russian captivity. That’s the good news.
The bad news is, through no fault of his own, Mr. Hubbard’s release is being turned into political cover for policies that could condemn untold numbers of Ukrainians to murder, torture and imprisonment.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The release of Mr. Hubbard is now being used by US President Donald Trump as a diplomatic trophy to justify the isolation and abandonment of Ukraine for an American realignment with Putin’s Russia.
This comes during a week in which the president has pushed regime change in Ukraine, falsified an energy ceasefire, restricted life-saving information sharing with Kyiv, and scorned Congressional law and intent by defying federal statute through his efforts to suspend oil sanctions and purchase diesel from the Kremlin, thus funding the Russian war machine.
The danger Trump and his envoy Steve Witkoff are creating to real human lives cannot be overstated. With the release of Hubbard, both men have given Putin a form of cover and absolution for war crimes past, present and future. They have taken an occasion for celebrating one American’s freedom and turned it into an exercise in rehabilitating his torturer.
Moscow is taking cues from Trump. They have dramatically escalated their strikes on civilians and energy infrastructure in their effort to depopulate cities and crush the Ukrainian spirit. The result is that Ukraine’s president is noticeably worn down, and her people are in their most vulnerable position since the beginning of the full-scale invasion.
On Oct. 19, 2026, Trump told reporters, “Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine. They haven’t been doing much” – the same day a Russian drone strike on a park in Nova Vodolaha killed a one-year-old girl in her stroller and fatally wounded her mother.
Now the White House is presenting the world with a macabre fiction: that a man recognized by many as perhaps the greatest war criminal of the 21st century should be celebrated as “a humanitarian.”
It was just a month ago on Sept. 5, that Trump’s envoy to the Kremlin, real estate developer Steve Witkoff, addressed Putin in Moscow:
“When we retire, we’ll have all these incredible stories and incredible memories, and yours will be right at the top of it all.”
During a week where Putin ordered missile strikes targeting civilians which ended the lives of infants and mothers, Witkoff looked Putin in the eyes and said:
“You are a humanitarian also, sir, and I salute that. I commend you.”
When pressed by reporters about Witkoff’s encomium of Putin, both Trump and Vice President JD Vance came to his defense.
The obsequious comment jolted the international community working on behalf of a free Ukraine. It also drew sharp criticism from members of the president’s own party.
“Another embarrassment,” Representative Don Bacon (R-Neb.) wrote on X.
Outgoing Republican Senator Thom Tillis, an outspoken opponent of Trump’s Russia appeasement strategy, had particularly choice words publish on X Oct. 21:
“WTF, Steve? Look up the definition of ‘humanitarian.’ What an embarrassing and outrageous thing to say. You should go back to Ukraine and ask the families of the children Putin has kidnapped and murdered whether they agree your friend Putin is a ‘humanitarian.’”
Right-wing commentator Laura Loomer said:
“If [Putin] is such a humanitarian how come the private jet they flew Stephen Hubbard back on did not have the other eight American hostages who are being held hostage right now by Vladimir Putin in Russia.”
Not mentioned by Witkoff in his dialogue with Putin was the context of Mr. Hubbard’s imprisonment. Nor did the Witkoff acknowledge that Russia is a signatory to and legally bound by the Fourth Geneva Convention which classifies torture, inhumane treatment, and unlawful confinement of protected civilians as grave breaches constituting war crimes.
The release of Mr. Hubbard emerges against a backdrop of a horror show of heinous crimes committed by Russians against civilians in 2022 in the town of Izyum, in Ukraine’s Kharkiv region.
Like Bucha, the name Izyum has become synonymous with Russian atrocities. Putin’s forces occupied Izyum from early April until Sept. 10, 2022, subjecting residents to arbitrary detention, beatings, rapes, electric shocks, executions and other torture documented by human-rights investigators.
Body being exhumed from mass grave site in Izyum, Sept. 23, 2022 (Photo by Stephan Korshak)
Body being exhumed from mass grave site in Izyum, Sept. 23, 2022 (Photo by Stephan Korshak)
On Sept. 15, days after liberation, Ukrainian authorities announced the discovery of a vast burial site in a nearby pine forest. Investigators recovered 447 bodies between Sept. 16 and 23, including women and children. Some had their hands bound or ropes around their necks; others bore gunshot wounds, knife wounds, broken limbs and burns. According to regional prosecutors, at least 30 bodies showed visible signs of torture.
Mr. Hubbard was a 71-year-old retired school teacher. Investigators told ABC News that Russian soldiers seized Hubbard from his home in April 2022, then took him to a detention and torture site in nearby Balakliya where he was abused.
Russia falsely alleged that the 71-year-old man was a mercenary. They wanted an American prisoner with whom they could blackmail the United States for such a day like the one provided by Trump and Witkoff.
A closed Moscow trial resulted in a sentence of six years and ten months in October 2024. His family disputed the mercenary accusation and the credibility of his reported confession. The United States designated him wrongfully detained.
Eyewitnesses reported how Hubbard was repeatedly tortured in prison by Putin’s men. Former fellow prisoner Ihor Shyshko, interviewed by AFP, said guards repeatedly beat Hubbard with sticks and truncheons, kicked him, attacked him with dogs, deprived him of food, and forced him to crawl through corridors.
Shyshko separately told ABC that prisoners experienced electric shocks, freezing conditions and starvation rations. He recalled Hubbard becoming unable to walk properly, with severely damaged knees, and believed his American nationality brought harsher treatment. Russia denied US diplomats access to Hubbard.
According to Trump nothing, something, everything, but actually nothing.
The president’s incoherent explanations were punctuated by unhinged personal attacks and volleys of gaslighting aimed at reporters seeking straightforward answers.
“We gave nothing in exchange, which is very rare,” Trump boasted.
He added: “And we’re getting him back because of me.”
Next, he insisted that imposing sanctions on Russia would have prevented Hubbard’s release: Washington had given Moscow nothing, but lifting sanctions and funding Russia was essential to bringing the American home.
CNN’s Kaitlan Collins pressed the obvious question : Did that not mean Russia had received something in exchange? Trump resorted to bullying:
“You don’t know what you’re talking about. You’re a dummy… You’re a low-IQ person.”
ABC News correspondent Karen Travers followed up, asking how waiving sanctions to secure Hubbard’s release could amount to giving Russia nothing. Trump’s response to the obvious contradiction he had created was: “Are you a stupid person?”
Trump then introduced another justification: “Russia has had very little input into Iran.” He suggested that Moscow’s supposed restraint should also count in its favor when considering sanctions.
That characterization clashes with statements made by Trump’s administration officials who acknowledged Russian assistance to Iran with the targeting of American servicemen, as well as other support for Iranian attacks on American targets in the Gulf.
In 1938, US Ambassador Joseph Davies returned from a meeting with Soviet dictator Joseph Stalin and wrote admiringly: “His demeanor is kindly, his manner almost deprecatingly simple,” adding: “He gave me the impression of being sincerely modest.”
The backlash became especially public with the 1943 film adaptation of his book, “Mission to Moscow,” which defended Soviet purge trials and portrayed Stalin sympathetically. Journalist and anti-Stalinist Suzanne La Follette, later a founding editor of National Review, condemned it as “the first instance in our country of totalitarian propaganda for mass consumption.” Critics nicknamed it “Submission to Moscow.”
Eighty-eight years later, an American envoy is again mistaking a Kremlin dictator’s cunning cordiality for humanity.
Recall that Witkoff played a role in the January 2025 release of hostages held by Hamas. At the time, he made it clear that Hamas “does not appear to be acting in good faith.”
Would Witkoff have called Hamas “humanitarian” for releasing a hostage it had brutalized? Unlikely. Yet he bestows sycophantic praise on Putin for freeing an American hostage who was illegally taken prisoner and brutalized by Russia.
Yes, a prisoner has been freed from his Russian torturers. Thank God.
The tragedy is that Hubbard finds himself an unwitting pawn in a game of international brinkmanship, in which the president of the United States and the leader of the Russian Federation are united in an effort to use him to provide both men with a “win.”
Trump is desperate for a deal, any deal. He has determined that undermining Ukrainian national security and aligning with Russia is the critical path to a fast win.
Trump’s motivations appear clear. He hopes to distract the public and avoid imminent catastrophe at the midterms by casting Ukraine as the scapegoat for the oil crisis created by his war in Iran, and Russia as the savior who will win the day. He wants to brag that he has negotiated a prisoner release. Importantly, he wants to create a strategic realignment between the United States and Russia before the Democrats take over Congress following the midterms and his administration becomes the subject of perpetual investigations and potential impeachment hearings.
Back in Moscow, an overjoyed Putin finds himself allied with the White House against Kyiv. He hopes to leverage the relationship to save his oil refineries from attack, give himself carte blanche to target Ukrainian energy infrastructure and civilians, secure American funding for his war machine through diesel sales, force regime change in Kyiv, and pressure Ukraine to surrender sovereign territory.
And the reality is that Putin will read every concession as permission to demand more. He will interpret every American threat against Kyiv as evidence that his campaign of continued violence is working.
The views expressed in this opinion article are the author’s and not necessarily those of Kyiv Post.
DW Phillips is a filmmaker, attorney and journalist who is director for Ukraine Story, a foundation for documentary reporting. He covered the story of Ukrainian athletes from the Paris 2024 Olympics, and is presently working an episodic series for streaming, Ukraine Story Anthology, which presents the humanity and hope of the people of Ukraine in wartime, including the stories of war orphans, soldiers, religious leaders and everyday Ukrainians. DW has served as a presidential appointee, and specialized in constitutional and civil rights issues as an attorney. He lives in Texas, USA.

title: Opinion| Awarding Constituency No. 1 to Abyei and the dangerous rewriting of boundaries
body: The recent presidential decree awarding Constituency No. 1 to the Abyei Special Administrative Area has created a shockwave across Twic County in Warrap State. It is a decision that contradicts administrative reality, electoral history, and the fragile peace between two communities whose identities and political statuses are fundamentally different. It quietly rewrites boundaries and risks reopening a conflict that has not yet healed. To understand the gravity of this decree, we must begin with clarity. Twic County is a fully recognized county of Warrap State, part of the sovereign territory of South Sudan. Its people voted in the 2011 referendum. Its borders are defined. Its constituencies existed when Southern Sudan was a region within Sudan before separation, and they continued to exist for more than a decade after independence. Abyei, by contrast, is a Special Administrative Area whose final status remains unresolved between Sudan and South Sudan. Abyei did not vote in the 2011 referendum. Abyei is governed under a joint arrangement because it is politically suspended between two nations. Abyei is not part of Warrap State. Abyei is not a county of South Sudan. Abyei does not share Twic County’s administrative certainty or citizenship history. These two communities do not share the same political identity, the same administrative status, or the same electoral destiny. Yet the decree forces them into one constituency. This is the contradiction at the heart of the problem. The decree places Twic County’s polling areas—the whole of Ajak Kuac Payam, Anyiel, Majak Kool, Aweng, Aneet, Athoony, Akok, Nyin Deng Ayuel, Madau, Mading-Jonthian, etc. (just to mention a few)—inside Abyei’s constituency. These areas are not Abyei. They have never been Abyei. They are Twic County territories. But Abyei Administration claims them, and that claim triggered the 2022 Twic–Abyei conflict, a conflict that killed people, displaced families, and left deep scars that have not healed. The conflict is still unresolved. The borders are still contested. The communities remain tense. Now, by awarding Constituency No. 1 to Abyei, the decree quietly suggests that these Twic areas belong to Abyei. It gives political weight to a territorial claim that has already caused bloodshed. It tells Abyei: “These areas are yours.” It tells Twic: “Your land can be reassigned without your consent.” This is not an administrative adjustment. It is a political provocation. Twic County residents have already made their position clear: they will not accept Abyei residents voting inside Twic territory. This is not defiance; it is self-defence. Allowing Abyei voters into Twic polling stations would be interpreted as surrendering land. It would create confrontation at the ballot box. It would turn election day into a flashpoint. It would undermine the sovereignty of Twic County and the integrity of Warrap State. The decree does not calm tensions; it inflames them. Every other administrative area in South Sudan—Greater Pibor, Ruweng, Panriang—is assigned its own constituency, separate from any state. Abyei must be treated the same way. Abyei is not a payam of Twic County. Abyei is not a county of Warrap State. Abyei is not under South Sudan’s full administrative jurisdiction. It is a special territory awaiting a referendum. Awarding it Twic’s Constituency No. 1 is not only illogical—it is unlawful. Before the decree, the eastern part of Twic County had two constituencies—No. 1 and No. 2—giving Twic County four constituencies in Warrap State. Removing Constituency No. 1 without replacement reduces Warrap’s representation, disrupts the state’s constituency sequence, and breaks the national pattern where every state begins its numbering at 1. Warrap State now begins at 2, because 1 has been taken away and handed to a territory that is not even part of the state. This is a contradiction that cannot stand. South Sudan is preparing for its first general elections. These elections must be peaceful, credible, and grounded in administrative truth. They cannot be built on contradictions, territorial confusion, or decisions that reignite conflict. Constituency No. 1 must be restored to Twic County. Abyei must be assigned its own constituency, reflecting its special status. The boundaries of Warrap State must be respected. The identities of both communities must be acknowledged. Anything less is an invitation to instability. South Sudan deserves better. Twic County deserves clarity. Abyei deserves consistency. And the nation deserves an electoral map that does not turn polling stations into battlegrounds. The decree must be corrected—not for politics, but for peace. The writer, Morris Yoll, is an advocate for truth, reconciliation, and territorial integrity and can be reached via myoll2002@yahoo.com . title: Clocks fall back this weekend, despite Finland's opposition
body:
The European Parliament voted in favour of ending seasonal time changes in 2019, but the practice continues.
Summer time will officially end this weekend when clocks in Finland are wound back by one hour to Eastern European Time (EET) at 4am on Sunday, 25 October.
Finland has observed the daylight saving tradition since 1981, with the switch between summer and winter time becoming a unified practice within the European Union.
Clocks are changed in all EU member states at the same time on the same date, as this is important for international rail and air traffic, among other considerations. The early hours of Sunday morning have been chosen as the best moment to change clocks because it will lead to the least amount of disruption.
However, there has been a growing movement of opposition to the biannual changing of the continent's clocks over recent years — including within the EU.
In 2018, the European Commission proposed that the practice be abandoned, and in 2019 the European Parliament voted in favour of ending seasonal time changes.
The proposal has since become entangled in red tape, as the Council of the EU cannot take a stand on the issue until all member states have submitted their positions. Finland is in favour of abandoning clock changes.
The EU Commissioner for Sustainable Transport and Tourism, Apóstolos Tzitzikostas , ordered a report into the practice earlier this year, with the study expected to be completed by the end of 2026.
Once the report is compiled, the European Commission will begin exploring further measures, according to a press release from Finland's Ministry of Transport and Communications.

title: Abu Dhabi’s NMDC awarded projects worth $763m by Saudi Aramco
body: Abu Dhabi’s NMDC Energy has been awarded new projects worth Dh2.8 billion ($763 million) by Saudi Aramco to complete offshore engineering, procurement and construction-related works. Completion of the projects is expected to take between 18 and 23 months, NMDC Energy said in a statement on Friday to the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange (ADX), where its shares are traded. It did not provide further details. The new deals add to the Dh2.2 billion in projects secured by the company in the second quarter of this year. The company's project backlog stood at Dh3.3 billion at the end of June. NMDC Energy, a majority-owned subsidiary of NMDC Group, offers end-to-end solutions including engineering, procurement, pipe laying, project management, fabrication, installation and commissioning. The company raised Dh3.22 billion from an initial public offering in 2024 and reported a net profit of Dh251 million for the first half of this year, with revenue reaching Dh9.5 billion. Chief executive Ahmed Al Dhaheri told The National last year that NMDC Energy was aiming to strengthen its collaboration with Chinese companies and looking for opportunities in Iraq, North Africa and Nigeria as part of its global expansion plan. The company was seeking contracts to serve offshore and onshore segments of the energy industry in Iraq, with mostly offshore jobs in Nigeria, he said.

title: AMA Ghana promotes literary tourism at 10th Pa Gya! Festival
body: AMA Ghana has promoted literary tourism at the 10th anniversary of the Pa Gya! Literary Festival, bringing students and literature enthusiasts together to explore the link between books and Ghana’s tourism heritage. The session, titled Tour on Pages with AMA Ghana , used reading and interactive discussions to demonstrate how literature can inspire people, particularly young readers, to discover Ghana’s historical landmarks, cultural traditions and tourism destinations. The event, organised by Adwinsa Publications Ghana Limited and the Ghana Library Authority in partnership with the festival, was held at 1.30 pm at the Foundation for Contemporary Arts, W. E. B. Du Bois Memorial Centre, Cantonments, Accra. It attracted participants from basic schools, senior high schools and the general public. The discussion featured Dr Nii Ayi Solomon, a tourism consultant, poet and playwright; Nana Akua Asante, co-founder and CEO of Kids in Tourism Ghana; and Ursula Abena Brago, who represented Mr Ziblim Alhassan, Executive Director of the Ghana Library Authority. With AMA Ghana serving as the book of focus, participants explored the potential of books to function as gateways to tourism discovery, connecting readers with the country’s history, cultural identity, natural attractions and heritage sites. The session highlighted the importance of making reading more relevant to everyday life by linking literary engagement with practical experiences and opportunities to learn about Ghana. It also reinforced the role of literature in nurturing national pride and encouraging young people to appreciate the country’s cultural and historical assets. By bringing tourism into the reading experience, Tour on Pages with AMA Ghana demonstrated how books can go beyond the classroom to become tools for cultural education, heritage appreciation and domestic tourism promotion. The initiative formed part of activities marking the 10th anniversary of the Pa Gya! Literary Festival, one of Ghana’s prominent international literary gatherings, which continues to provide a platform for celebrating literature and encouraging conversations around books, creativity and cultural expression. AMA Ghana is the book around which the session was organised, although further details about its author, publication and contents would help provide readers with a fuller understanding of the work and its role in promoting literary tourism.

title: Russian forces attack gas station in Sumy, injuring two employees
body:

title: War update: 165 clashes on front lines over past day
body:
The General Staff of the Ukrainian Armed Forces said this in an operational update as of 08:00 on Friday, October 23, Ukrinform reports.
According to the General Staff, Russian forces carried out three missile strikes and 76 airstrikes yesterday, dropping 239 guided aerial bombs.
The invaders also deployed 10,313 kamikaze drones and shelled settlements and Ukrainian forces' positions 2,781 times.
Russian troops used artillery to shell Mala Korchakivka, Nova Sich, Ulanove, Yunakivka, Shalyhyne, Luzhky and Vyntorivka in the Sumy region. Airstrikes targeted areas near Luzhky and Khotin.
Over the past day, Ukrainian aircraft, missile forces and artillery struck three Russian targets: two troop concentration areas and one drone command post.
In the Northern Slobozhanshchyna sector, Russian troops launched two attacks near Ulanove and Korchakivka.
In the Southern Slobozhanshchyna sector, Ukrainian defenders repelled 14 Russian attacks. Russian forces attempted to advance near Kovalivka, Anyshchyne, Izbytske, Radkivka and Vilkhuvatka.
In the Kupiansk sector, Russian troops launched one attack near Petropavlivka.
In the Lyman sector, Ukrainian defenders repelled five Russian attacks near Katerynivka, Kolodiazi and Lyman. Russian attempts to advance in this section of the front were halted.
In the Sloviansk sector, Russian troops launched one attack near Mykolaivka.
In the Kramatorsk sector, Russian forces conducted no assault operations over the past day.
In the Kostiantynivka sector, Russian troops launched 11 attacks, conducting assault operations near Druzhkivka, Novoselivka, Kostiantynivka, Dovha Balka and Pavlivka.
In the Pokrovsk sector, Ukrainian defenders halted 15 Russian attacks. Russian forces attacked near Serhiivka, Molodetske and Novopavlivka and also launched assaults toward Kucheriv Yar, Svitle, Sofiivka, Vilne, Novyi Donbas and Myrne.
In the Oleksandrivka sector, Russian forces conducted no active offensive operations.
In the Huliaipole sector, Ukrainian forces repelled 12 Russian attacks near Charivne, Ternuvate, Verkhnia Tersa, Kosivtseve, Vozdvyzhivka, Kopani, Novoselivka and Bilohiria.
In the Orikhiv sector, Ukrainian defenders repelled one Russian attack near Lukianivske.
In the Dnipro River sector, Russian forces took no active action.
The situation on the Volyn and Polissia axes has not changed significantly. No signs of Russian forces forming offensive groupings have been detected.

title: Video: Millions fall in puppy love with Finland's slow-TV livestream
body:
The latest season of Yle's Pentulive (Puppy live) is attracting attention from around the world.
More than 10 million people around the world have so far tuned into the latest season of Yle's Pentulive (Puppy live) series.
The slow-TV show, now in its sixth season, follows a mother dog and her litter for a period of around eight weeks from the puppies' birth until they move to their new homes.
"It's a whole roller-coaster of emotions," Pentulive's producer Jyri Loikkanen told Yle News. "From the excitement of this life-or-death situation when the puppies are born, to observing how they start to grow day by day, to the heartbreaking, bittersweet moment when they leave for their new homes."
This year's stars are mother Hilkka and her litter of Lagotto Romagnolo pups.
The cameras began rolling on 6 October, a few days before Hilkka's due date, and the six puppies (four males and two girls) were born in the early hours of Saturday 10 October.
Since then, while Hilkka has been busy with feeding and the puppies have been napping for up to 20 hours a day, millions of viewers have been tuning in.
Finland's fascination with the fluffy furballs has also made headlines around the world on outlets from the US news network CNN to the UK's Daily Mail .
The Puppy Live format has even been bought by a public broadcaster in the Netherlands.
Yle's science journalist Pirjo Koskinen , who came up with the idea for Puppy Live, believes that the huge popularity of the series in Finland reflects the nation's relationship with its canine friends.
"I think we see dogs more and more as family members nowadays in Finland, and people want to be more aware of animal welfare, of dog welfare," Koskinen said. "So I see Puppy Live as an information campaign as much as a cuteness campaign."

title: South African police investigate killing of foreign national by crowd
body: South African police said on Thursday they were investigating the killing of ​a foreign national by a crowd ‌of about 50 people in the city of Durban. The South African Police Service said in a post ​on X that the victim, thought ​to be in his late 30s or ⁠early 40s, was beaten by the ​crowd and declared dead at the scene A group ​of people had been marching in central Durban when two men appeared to break away and approach ​the victim, after which he was assaulted ​by about 50 people, police said Police did not give ‌the ⁠victim’s nationality and said the motive for the killing was unknown The incident follows months of anti-migrant protests in South Africa, some ​of which have ​turned ⁠violent and drawn international criticism, prompting thousands of migrants from elsewhere ​in Africa to flee affected communities Earlier ​this ⁠month, anti-migrant protests in Durban and Johannesburg’s Soweto township turned violent, with foreign-owned businesses looted and ⁠vehicles ​set alight after demonstrations against ​the processing of asylum applications at a refugee reception ​centre.

title: Oil prices exceed $114 a barrel amid escalated war on Iran
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 23 (MNA) – Oil prices continued continued to rise to above $114 bpd amid persistent concerns over disruptions to global energy markets as a result of continued US and Zioinst regime aggression on Iran.
Brent crude briefly climbed to $114 a barrel. Around five months ago, in mid-May, the benchmark had risen above $114 and reached $112 a few days later. It had not returned to these price levels since then.
The latest surge in oil prices comes as economic analysts warn that prices above $110 a barrel could intensify pressure on the U.S. economy. U.S. crude oil prices have also climbed above $100 a barrel, raising concerns about higher energy costs and mounting inflationary pressures.

title: Protests, the cost of living and a widening wealth gap
body: Protesters in several countries in Europe and Asia are voicing anger over the cost of living, public services and their prospects. France has had the largest demonstrations, with more than 500,000 people marching at the weekend and outbreaks of looting and rioting. There is no single, unifying motivation for the broader international protests, but underlying them is undoubtedly the rising cost of living. This global inflation is exacerbated in the minds of some protesters by a widening wealth gap, and our chart of the week points to how broad that gulf really is. UBS’s Global Wealth Report 2026 estimates that 58 million adults, 1.5 per cent of the world’s total, are worth more than $1 million each and hold 48.4 per cent of global wealth. At the other end, 1.62 billion adults, or 42.1 per cent, have less than $10,000 each; together, they hold just 0.6 per cent of the world’s wealth. The pressure on household budgets is another part of the picture. The attached charts show how much consumer prices have risen since 2000. In France, a basket of products costing $100 in 2000 cost $151 in 2025. In Serbia, it rose to $1,054. Iran and Turkey are higher still, so the comparison uses a logarithmic scale. title: No leaders in history have been more criminal than US ones
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 23 (MNA) – Brigadier General Mohammad Akraminia, spokesperson for Iran’s Army, criticized US officials’ remarks about Iran, describing American leaders as among the most criminal figures in history.
In a post on the social media platform X, Akraminia referred to US Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s remarks about targeting commercial vessels, saying that the United States had also carried out attacks during negotiations that, according to him, killed civilians and sailors.
The Iranian Army spokesperson cited the deaths of 168 children and several athletes in attacks involving prohibited bombs. He also referred to the killing of 104 sailors and an attack on a wedding ceremony.
Akraminia concluded by questioning whether history, dating back to ancient times, had ever seen criminals comparable to the current US leadership.

title: General Staff: Russia has lost 1,574,620 troops in Ukraine since Feb. 24, 2022
body:
Russia has lost 1,574,620 troops in Ukraine since the beginning of its full-scale invasion on Feb. 24, 2022, the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reported on Oct. 23.
The number includes 1,830 casualties that Russian forces suffered over the past day.
According to the report , Russia has also lost 12,439 tanks, 25,597 armored combat vehicles, 166,088 vehicles and fuel tanks, 51,501 artillery systems, 2,230 multiple-launch rocket systems, 1,720 air defense systems, 449 aircraft, 356 helicopters, 3,003 unmanned ground vehicles, 35 ships and boats, and two submarines.
Ukraine's General Staff has not revealed its own losses during the full-scale invasion, citing operational secrecy.
Independent Western think-tank reports agree that the Russian casualties significantly surpass Ukraine's losses, with the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) estimating the ratio to be "roughly 2.5:1 or 2:1."
A January 2026 CSIS report said Ukraine has likely suffered between 500,000 and 600,000 casualties from February 2022 to December 2025, of which between 100,000 and 140,000 are thought to be killed in action.
While Ukrainian officials rarely disclose the figure, President Volodymyr Zelensky told France TV on Feb. 4 that at least 55,000 Ukrainian soldiers have been killed in action since the beginning of the full-scale war, in addition to significant numbers who are missing in action.
The intensity of Russian drone attacks and the fighting has made it extremely difficult for Ukraine to retrieve the bodies of fallen soldiers, which are needed for DNA confirmation.

title: Araghchi slams Macron’s flip-flop on Iran nuclear program
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 23 (MNA) – Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has criticized French President Emmanuel Macron over his shifting positions on Iran’s peaceful nuclear program, urging him to “get your story straight.”
In a post on X on Thursday night, Araghchi recalled Macron’s firm stance before the US Congress in 2018, just before then-President Donald Trump withdrew the United States from the nuclear agreement. At the time, Macron declared that “France won’t leave the JCPOA, because we signed it.”
Today, however, Macron claims he has always opposed “any form of nuclear activity” in Iran, a position Araghchi described as inconsistent with the French leader’s earlier public commitments.

title: F1 power rankings and US GP predictions: Verstappen eyes hat-trick while Antonelli has title in grasp
body: Formula One heads to Austin this weekend with Max Verstappen looking for a hat-trick of wins while Kimi Antonelli is within touching distance of a first world championship. Circuit of the Americas combines fast flowing corners with heavy braking zones and a long back straight. It asks a great deal of both car and driver. This weekend, track temperatures are expected to climb above 55°C which puts tyre wear firmly in the spotlight. The drivers who manage their rubber best should be the ones fighting at the front. Our power rankings measure who will arrive in Austin in the best shape. We take into account recent form, raw speed, how much each driver extracts from their car, momentum and how well their strengths might suit the Circuit of the Americas. Here are our top 10 rankings and predictions for the race. Kimi's Austin mission is as follows... 😮‍💨 Here is how he could claim the Drivers' Championship this weekend! 👀 #F1 #USGP pic.twitter.com/cTS7HSRKbV — Formula 1 (@F1) October 21, 2026 10. Nico Hulkenberg (Audi) Form: Bahrain P11, Singapore P8. Championship: P14 Singapore was Hulkenberg’s most productive weekend of the season. He took P7 in the sprint and P8 in the race where he spent the closing laps resisting a much quicker George Russell. Audi believes recent work on the car is beginning to pay off, although Hulkenberg was quick to temper expectations. The Circuit of the Americas will tell us if their progress is genuine and worthy of excitement. 9. Oscar Piastri (McLaren) Form: Bahrain P6, Singapore P5. Championship: P7 Successive top six finishes have steadied him after a difficult period. He should have left Singapore with more but the McLarens collided on the final lap of the sprint which ended his race and led to internal talks within the team. McLaren chief executive Zak Brown believes Piastri is recovering his confidence and the driver looks like himself again. McLaren is bringing small floor changes to Austin alongside work aimed at improving braking, something that ought to help the Australian in Texas. 8. Isack Hadjar (Red Bull) Form: Bahrain P5, Singapore P10. Championship: P8 Hadjar’s Singapore result deserves an asterisk. His weekend was wrecked by a succession of technical problems, including power-unit and gearbox issues. He eventually started from the pit lane and yet he still recovered to P10. Laurent Mekies admitted Red Bull “owe him one” after failing to give the French-Algerian driver a proper chance to show his pace. RB22 car has progressed immensely well so Hadjar ought to have a good weekend. Admiring the COTA scenery 😍💨 #F1 #USGP pic.twitter.com/OXjQusBKlM — Formula 1 (@F1) October 22, 2026 7. Liam Lawson (Racing Bulls) Form: Bahrain P7, Singapore P7. Championship: P9 Lawson is now one of the most dependable drivers on the grid. Two successive P7 finishes and P5 in Singapore’s Sprint race, Lawson is collecting points. With his 2027 future still undecided, the New Zealander is making his case on track. He has now finished ahead of Lindblad in 10 of their 14 Grands Prix together. Can he keep his seat? 6. Lando Norris (McLaren) Form: Bahrain P9, Singapore P4. Championship: P6 Singapore dented Norris ’ momentum after the Sprint clash with Oscar Piastri cost McLaren points and promoted internal talks. His pace is still strong but questions must be asked about his decision making. McLaren has drawn a line under the crash but the British river will head to Austin with a lot to prove. 5. George Russell (Mercedes) Form: Bahrain DNF, Singapore P9. Championship: P2 Russell continues in his unlucky streak. He was heading towards taking P3 in Sepang when his engine failed and he was forced to retire. That forced him into a huge power-unit penalty in Singapore where he started 19th and recovered to P9. Reliability issues continue to haunt the driver and Toto Wolff admitted, “Malaysia and Singapore were difficult weekends for us and we have worked hard to understand where we fell short.” Both Mercedes drivers will be driving the latest specification cars and Russell will hope lady luck will be on his side in Texas. Six winners in 2026. Six still left in the fight. Can anyone hunt down Kimi? 🎯 #F1 #USGP pic.twitter.com/LwnEKW0ScR — Formula 1 (@F1) October 19, 2026 4. Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari) Form: Bahrain P3, Singapore P6. Championship: P3 He finished second in the Sprint and qualified P3 for the Singapore GP but Sunday didn’t go as planned. Hamilton missed Ferrari’s pit entry under the virtual safety car, stayed out and endured until his ageing tyres surrendered three positions late on. “Sorry, boys. I let you down today with that strategy. My call, and I lost us valuable points.” Ferrari brings a new floor to Austin designed to give the SF-26 car a wider operating window. Hamilton’s five victories at this track should stand him in good stead. 3. Charles Leclerc (Ferrari) Form: Bahrain P4, Singapore P2. Championship: P5 Leclerc finally escaped his run of fourth places with a superb second in Singapore. He attacked Verstappen at the start and briefly looked capable of truly challenging before the Red Bull pulled clear. It was a throwback to 2022 but the truth is, as Leclerc admitted, the Ferrari lacks the pace. Ferrari’s new upgrade is the last big one of the season and the new floor should help the team generate more consistent aerodynamic load allowing for better balance. 2. Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes) Form: Bahrain P2, Singapore P3. Championship: P1 Despite Mercedes’ problems, Antonelli always finds a way of fighting at the top. He battled braking problems throughout a difficult Singapore race but he recovered well on fresh tyres to pass Norris and Hamilton for P3. Antonelli now has 14 podiums from 17 races and leads Russell by 102 points. Victory in Texas could give him the chance to seal the title this weekend if other results go his way. Verstappen wins Bahrain GP – in pictures 1. Max Verstappen (Red Bull) Form: Bahrain P1, Singapore P1. Championship : P4 Verstappen has gone from chasing his first victory of the season to looking like the favourite for every upcoming race. He followed his win in Malaysia with a clean-sweep in Singapore , taking Sprint pole and victory before repeating the feat in the GP. It was his first win at Marina Bay in 10 attempts. Red Bull’s progress is now clear, and the car now looks to be the best on the grid. Verstappen has always done well in this circuit and will be gunning for a third successive victory to stop Antonelli winning the championship. Austin podium prediction: 1. Max Verstappen Two consecutive victories, it’s virtually impossible to stop the Dutchman when he finds momentum. He has now looked competitive across several circuit types and he knows how to win in the Circuit of the Americas 2. Kimi Antonelli He could win it all in Texas and the youngster will be challenging himself to win this race. The team now understands its latest upgrade better and will hope to avoid any reliability issues. 3. Charles Leclerc After managing a strong result in Singapore, the latest upgrade should help Leclerc to challenge once again. He won in Austin in 2024 and will hope to manage at least a podium finish this Sunday.

title: Google Cloud Launches Agent Compute Engine: A MicroVM per AI Agent
body:
Google Cloud has announced Agent Compute Engine , a compute service built specifically for AI agents. Google Agent Compute Engine gives each agent its own hardware-isolated microVM. The sandbox holds zero credentials. The service already powers Gemini as an agent for work tasks. Google unveiled it this week at AGNTCon + MCPCon. Customer preview is targeted for the coming months. The pitch: VM-grade isolation with container-like speed and density. TL;DR Unit: One hardware-isolated microVM per agent session, with its own guest kernel, root access and Hyperdisk. Runs on: Google-managed hosts using Titan silicon and the Titanium IPU. Open-source sibling Agent Substrate runs on any Kubernetes cluster. Performance: Idle agents are checkpointed to zero active resources and resumed from snapshots. Google gives no ACE boot or density numbers. Best: Agent Substrate hit 500 activations/s at under 500 ms suspend/resume across 200,000 agents. Worst: No published boot time, density, pricing or preview date for Agent Compute Engine itself. What is Google Agent Compute Engine? Agent Compute Engine is a Google Cloud service that runs each AI agent inside a dedicated microVM. Per the technical post , it powers Gemini, Antigravity, and internal evaluation and RL pipelines. Google splits every agent into 2 parts. The harness, or ‘brain,’ calls the model. The sandbox, or ‘hands,’ runs code, shell commands and browsers. The harness runs fully outside the sandbox and dispatches explicit commands into it. How does the microVM isolation work? Each session runs in a single-tenant microVM behind a Cloud Hypervisor boundary . Hosts are stateless appliances with a read-only root filesystem enforced by dm-verity. Titanium holds attestation keys outside the guest. The networking design is the unusual part: MicroVMs have no standard network interface, no default gateway and no direct VPC access. All traffic crosses a virtio-vsock boundary to a local proxy, then to an external gateway. Guests get only a session-scoped SPIFFE certificate and a short-lived identity token. Agent Gateway swaps in the real backend credential in flight, after policy checks. Google assumes an attacker controls everything inside the sandbox. A prompt-injected agent finds no secrets to steal. What are the Four Agent Identities? Google defines 4 identities for every agent workload: User identity: authenticates the overall task only. Delegated on-behalf-of identity: a scoped grant stored in a central authorization service, never on the node. Agent Workload Identity: a short-lived SPIFFE identity, the only one used for sandbox traffic. Agent Workforce Identity: an agent’s own account and resources. The workload identity is useless for direct API calls if exfiltrated. It only identifies which sandbox sent a packet. How does it keep idle agents cheap? Google team found agents spend most of their time waiting on models or users. So the sandbox signals when a tool call finishes. The host checkpoints the idle microVM to zero active resources. It resumes on the next call. Density comes from copy-on-write memory sharing . Pre-warmed snapshot images are mapped with DAX, so microVMs on a host share base OS and library pages. Only each agent’s modified pages consume private memory. Harnesses also get cloning, snapshot/forking, rewind and rollback. Storage is split 3 ways: disposable scratch overlays, shared read-only volumes, and persistent user workspaces on Hyperdisk .
